title: feat(pypi): pin packages to private uv indexes with indexes and sources
body:
Pins individual `pypi:` packages to a private uv index with new `indexes` and `sources` tool options, as requested in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15780.

`registry_url` swaps the index for a `pypi:` tool's whole dependency graph, so there was no way to take one package, such as a private `with` dependency, from a private index while everything else stays on PyPI. The new `indexes` and `sources` tool options do that, mirroring uv's `tool.uv.index` and `tool.uv.sources`:

```toml
[tools."pypi:zensical"]
version = "0.1.1"
with = ["my-zensical-theme==1.2.3"]
indexes = [{ name = "private", url = "https://pypi.example.com/simple/", explicit = true }]
sources = { my-zensical-theme = { index = "private" } }
```

`mise lock` writes both into the tool's synthetic uv project, so uv resolves `my-zensical-theme` from `private` and everything else from the default index. `mise install` replays the same project from the sidecar. With `explicit = true`, uv uses the index only for pinned packages.

## Behavior and limits

- Needs uv and a dependency graph. uv has no CLI flag for sources, so a tool that sets these is never installed version-only; `mise install` creates the graph when the lockfile is enabled.
- Rejected with `uvx = false`, `uvx_args` or `pipx_args`.
- Index URLs cannot carry credentials or a query string, since the lockfile records them. Credentials go through uv's `UV_INDEX_<NAME>_USERNAME` and `_PASSWORD` variables.
- A source must name a defined index, and its package must be the tool or one of its `with` or `expose` requirements.
- A pinned `with` package's Python requirement is not looked up on the registry, so its name is never sent there. For a package with a narrower Python range than the tool, set `python`.
- Both options are recorded in `mise.lock`, and a changed pair no longer matches an existing graph.

Not included: the optional reusable named indexes under `[settings.pypi]` from the discussion.

## Validation

- New e2e `test_pypi_lock_index_sources` covers locking, replaying with `--locked`, a changed-options lock, and each rejected configuration. It uses a new fixture flag that makes the private index host `mise-lock-extra`.
- `test_pypi_lock`, `test_pypi_lock_registry_index`, `test_schema_ajv`, the `mise-config` tests and the schema conformance test pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace` fails at origin/main too, on an unrelated lint in `crates/mise-ui`; no warnings in the touched files.

title: fix(deps): prefer the distribution's package manager over brew for plugin system dependencies
body:
On Linux hosts whose native manager sorts after `brew` alphabetically (AlmaLinux, Fedora, Arch, openSUSE), a plugin's `systemDependencies` were installed with mise's built-in Homebrew instead of `dnf`, `pacman` or `zypper`, whenever the dependency had both hints:

```
$ MISE_SYSTEM_DEPS=warn mise use tmux      # AlmaLinux 9
mise WARN  install with: sudo dnf install -y gcc
mise WARN  install with: brew install make ncurses libevent bison
```

Libraries that brew installs live under `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`, which the system `pkg-config` and compiler do not search, so the build could still fail after mise reported the dependencies as installed.

`pick_manager` now tries the distribution's own managers (`apk`, `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `zypper`) before any other manager. The rest keep their order, so brew is still used when the native manager has no entry for a dependency or when the host has none. title: fix(exec): keep tool bins ahead of inherited PATH entries
body:
`mise x -- npm` could run Node's bundled npm instead of the pinned npm tool when the caller's PATH already contained the npm tool's bin directory.

```toml
[tools]
node = "26.13.1"
npm = "12.2.2"   # npm:npm
```

With the npm tool's bin on PATH but no mise activation state (for example a child of an activated shell with `__MISE_DIFF` and friends removed), `mise x -- npm --version` printed 11.20.0, Node's bundled npm. `mise x -- sh -c 'npm --version'` printed 12.2.2.

Cause: `exec_program` searches mise-added directories before inherited ones so wrapper scripts on the inherited PATH can't shadow real tool binaries. It told them apart by whether a directory was in the caller's PATH, so a tool bin the caller already had counted as inherited and ranked after Node's bin. #15564 fixed the same ranking for `env._.path`. Every directory mise puts ahead of the inherited PATH (tool bins, the uv venv, tool-added paths, appended `_.path` entries) now ranks as mise-added too, so the lookup matches the PATH the child gets.  The list comes from the same environment build that prepares the child env, so nothing runs twice.

Testing: new e2e `test_exec_inherited_tool_path_order` fails without the fix and passes with it. `test_exec_inherited_path_order`, `test_exec_venv_path_order`, `test_exec_wrapper_recursion`, `test_exec_wrapper_recursion_with_shims` and `test_exec_shim_recursion` pass. `cargo clippy -p mise` could not run to completion here: it stops on an existing `unnecessary_lazy_evaluations` error in `crates/mise-ui`, which this PR doesn't touch. The Windows `exec_program` shares the call site and takes the same extended list; it wasn't compiled here.

title: fix(prune): keep the current commit of an npm git source tracking HEAD
body:
Fixes #15754

## Problem

A tool installed from a git source that tracks the default branch (`npm:git+ssh://…` with `version = "latest"`) leaves one install per commit. `mise prune` listed all of them as prunable, including the commit `latest` currently resolves to:

```
mise prune --dry-run
npm:git+ssh://…@<sha> is prunable: … is required at latest by ~/mise.toml
```

so it could not be used to clean up old revisions without removing the active one.

## Fix

Prune resolves tracked configs offline, where `latest` for a git source stays the literal string and matches no commit-named install. Prune now asks the remote what HEAD points at. If that commit is installed it is kept and older commits are listed. If the remote can't be reached, or HEAD isn't installed, every install of the tool is kept, so the active one is never removed by mistake.

## Testing

- `test_npm_git` e2e: install `latest`, advance the remote, install again, and check that only the old commit is prunable; an explicit pin to an older commit does not displace `latest`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Prune now performs cached remote resolution for rolling `latest` git sources; failures are conservative (keep all installs), but wrong HEAD resolution could still misclassify what to delete.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise prune`** no longer marks the commit that **`latest`** currently resolves to on a git-backed npm source as prunable when a config still tracks **`latest`**. Offline prune used to treat **`latest`** as a literal version string, so none of the per-commit installs matched and older SHAs—including the active HEAD—could be listed for removal.
> 
> Prune now resolves **`latest`** via **`rolling_head`**, with per-source caching for the process so many tracked configs don’t each hit the remote. If the resolved commit is installed, only that install is protected for that config; older commits stay prunable. If lookup fails or that commit isn’t installed, **every** install of the tool is kept so the active revision isn’t deleted by mistake.
> 
> E2E coverage in **`test_npm_git`** exercises advancing the remote after **`mise use @latest`**, checking dry-run prune, and verifying an explicit older pin doesn’t replace **`latest`**’s protection.
>

title: fix(backend): make bin.install files executable in brew formulas
body:
Formulas in third-party taps that install a downloaded binary (like `ampcode/tap/ampcode`) used to leave the file non-executable, so `mise install brew:ampcode/tap/ampcode` reported success but `amp --version` failed with "permission denied".

```toml
[tools]
"brew:ampcode/tap/ampcode" = "latest"
```

`bin.install "amp"` moved the download into the keg and kept its `0644` mode. Homebrew makes files installed into `bin` executable, and mise now does the same: regular files that a formula installs into `bin` or `sbin` are set to `0755` (executable, still writable so a later `inreplace` works). `shim_bin_install_makes_files_executable` runs a formula that installs `0644` sources into `bin`, `sbin` and `pkgshare` (with an `inreplace` after `bin.install`), then checks the modes. It fails with `0644` without the change.

title: feat(http): add filter_bins option
body:
Fixes #15773.

## Problem

Tools installed with the `http:` backend and an explicit `bin_path` put that whole directory on `PATH` and into the shims. `cursor-agent` sets `bin_path = "dist-package"`, a private directory that holds Cursor's own `node`, `rg`, helper binaries and `.node` addons. With `cursor-agent` and `node = "lts"` in a global config, `node` resolved to Cursor's bundled Node (v24.22.1) instead of mise's, and Vitest workers failed with `node: bad option: --no-webstorage`. The registry's `bins = ["cursor-agent"]` is metadata only and does not limit what is exposed.

## Fix

The http backend now takes `filter_bins`, matching the option the github backend already has. mise links only the named executables into a `.mise-bins` directory, searching `bin_path`, `bin/` and the install root, and puts only that directory on `PATH`.

```toml
[tools."http:my-tool"]
version = "1.0.0"
url = "https://example.com/my-tool-1.0.0.tar.gz"
bin_path = "dist"
filter_bins = ["my-tool"]
```

`filter_bins` is part of the extraction cache key, so tools that share an extraction never see each other's `.mise-bins`. The `cursor-agent` registry entry now sets `filter_bins = ["cursor-agent"]`, so only `cursor-agent` is exposed; the launcher resolves its own directory with `realpath`, so the link works from anywhere.

Includes the schema, docs and an e2e test (`test_http_filter_bins`) that installs an archive with a bundled `node` and `rg` and checks they stay off `PATH`.

## Verification

- `mise run test:e2e test_http_filter_bins test_http_rename_exe test_http_caching` passes.
- `mise run lint-fix` passes.
- `cargo clippy` stops on `crates/mise-ui/src/text_install_progress.rs:101` (`unnecessary_lazy_evaluations`) with the local toolchain, and the same error appears on `origin/main`. I could not get a clean clippy run through the rest of the workspace here.
- Not verified against the live cursor.com download.

title: fix(brew): define HOMEBREW_PREFIX and friends in the source build shim
body:
Source builds of formulae from third-party taps no longer fail with `uninitialized constant Formula::HOMEBREW_PREFIX`.

Tap helpers read Homebrew's global constants directly. For example, `gromgit/fuse` has `HOMEBREW_PREFIX.to_s != "/usr/local"` in `require/formula-patch.rb`. The brew build shim exported `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` and `HOMEBREW_CELLAR` only as environment variables, so installing `sshfs-mac` failed at the start of `install`:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"brew:gromgit/fuse/sshfs-mac" = "latest"
```

```console
$ mise bootstrap packages apply
Error: build failed: uninitialized constant Formula::HOMEBREW_PREFIX
```

The shim now defines `HOMEBREW_PREFIX`, `HOMEBREW_CELLAR`, `HOMEBREW_REPOSITORY` and `HOMEBREW_LIBRARY` as Ruby constants, with the same values mise uses elsewhere.

This does not address the issue's second complaint that mise builds from source even though the tap has an `arm64_tahoe` bottle. That is a separate bottle-selection question.

Fixes #15777

title: fix(ls): keep tools that share a version in --all-sources
body:
`mise ls --all-sources` dropped a tool whenever another tool had the same version string. With `aqua:suzuki-shunsuke/pinact = "5.0.2"` in one project and `packslip:github.com/suzuki-shunsuke/pinact = "5.0.2"` in another, only the aqua row was listed.

The rows were deduplicated on the version alone. They are now deduplicated on the tool and the version, so one tool pinned by several configs still collapses to one row (#8042) while different tools that share a version each keep theirs.

The e2e test gives `dummy` and `cargo:mise-test-other` the same version and checks that both are listed; it fails without the fix.

Fixes #15763

title: feat(task): offer one spelling per task in completion, chosen by the typed prefix
body:
## Summary

In a monorepo, `mise run <TAB>` offered three spellings of the same root task (`test`, `:test`, `//:test`). Completion now picks the spelling from what has been typed:

- `mise run <TAB>`: the shortest name (`test`); tasks in other config roots keep their `//apps/web:build` path, since they have no shorter spelling
- `mise run :<TAB>`: names qualified for the current config root (`:test`)
- `mise run //<TAB>`: absolute monorepo paths (`//:test`)

All spellings still run; only the suggestions change. `mise run <TAB>` is answered from the mounted `mise tasks --usage` spec and the named `task` completer; both now receive the typed word through a new hidden `--complete-word` flag on `mise tasks`, and offer only the spelling that fits. The other spellings stay hidden aliases, so a task's own arguments still complete.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15776

## Test plan

- New assertions in `e2e/tasks/test_task_ls_complete_monorepo` for the three prefixes
- `test_task_completion_control_chars` and `test_task_experimental_gates` still pass

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes shell completion and task usage-spec generation across monorepos and alias resolution; behavior is well covered by new e2e tests but affects a frequently used UX path.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Task completion** now suggests a single spelling per task based on what the user has already typed, instead of listing every equivalent form (`test`, `:test`, `//:test`) at once. Bare `mise run <TAB>` shows the shortest name; leading `:` or `/`/`//` narrows to root-qualified or absolute monorepo paths. Other spellings remain **hidden aliases** so task flags and arguments still complete after selection.
> 
> This is driven by a new hidden **`--complete-word`** on `mise tasks` / `mise tasks ls`, wired through shell completion (`mise.usage.kdl`, task completers) and **`tell_task_mounts_the_word`** for `mise tasks --usage` mounts. **`completion_names`** / usage-spec generation in **`tasks/ls.rs`** implement prefix logic and filter aliases that collide with another task’s **name** so the named task keeps its flags and usage.
> 
> New e2e coverage includes monorepo prefix behavior, alias/name collisions, and qualified `//apps/web:build`-style completion.

title: fix(ruby): install precompiled previews published as pre-releases
body:
Fixes #15764.

`ruby = "4.1.0-preview1"` failed with `no precompiled ruby found` even though jdx/ruby publishes `4.1.0-preview1-1` builds, so mise fell back to compiling with ruby-build (or failed outright with `ruby.compile = false`, where `mise ls-remote ruby 4.1` also printed nothing). jdx/ruby flags Ruby previews as GitHub pre-releases, and the precompiled lookup dropped every pre-release.

```toml
[tools]
ruby = "4.1.0-preview1"
```

Now the precompiled install and the `ruby.compile = false` version listing both include pre-release-flagged releases, so the preview installs from the jdx/ruby build with GitHub attestation checks intact (no `precompiled_url` workaround needed).

- `ruby.rs`: `retain_precompiled_versions` lists releases including pre-releases.
- `ruby_lock.rs`: the asset lookup uses a new `get_release_including_prereleases_with_build_revision_status`. The existing function is unchanged, so rubyinstaller2 keeps its behavior.
- Unit test for a pre-release-flagged build revision.

Not run: an end-to-end install against jdx/ruby. Unit tests pass; local clippy fails only on an unrelated `mise-ui` lint from the newer toolchain.

> **Overview**

> 
> Release selection logic is factored into shared helper `pick_release_with_build_revision_status`, with a new **`get_release_including_prereleases_with_build_revision_status`** that lists releases including pre-releases. The original **`get_release_with_build_revision_status`** still uses stable-only listings so other tools (e.g. rubyinstaller2) are unchanged.

body:
`npm:` installs failed on images without `ca-certificates` (for example `node:24-slim`) now that `npm.provenance` is on by default. mise's own clients fall back to the bundled Mozilla roots, but the provenance check's TUF client did not:

```
docker run --rm node:24-slim sh -c 'npm i -g @jdxcode/mise@2026.11.1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && cd /tmp && mise use -g npm:@fission-ai/openspec@1.16.0'

title: fix(lock): point aqua SLSA downgrades at the signer options
body:
`mise lock` refuses to update an `aqua:` tool whose lock entry records SLSA provenance when the registry recipe declares SLSA without a signer identity and issuer (for example `aqua:fluxcd/flux2`), because mise can no longer verify it. The error said to fix the recipe or use another backend, but not that the signer can be supplied as tool options.

```text
mise ERROR lockfile generation would downgrade recorded provenance; previous files were preserved: recorded slsa but the new entry has no provenance. If the registry recipe no longer provides what mise needs to verify it, fix the recipe or lock the tool through another backend, or set slsa_signer_identity and slsa_signer_issuer in the tool options so the SLSA provenance can be verified and recorded again (flux2@2.10.0 on linux-x64, aqua:fluxcd/flux2)

The hint only appears for an `aqua:` backend where the old entry recorded SLSA and the new one has none. The downgrade protection itself is unchanged.

title: fix(install): reject a named tool excluded by its os option
body:
## Problem

A tool scoped to another platform with the `os` tool option is skipped by a bare `mise install`, but naming it bypassed that filter and reached the backend, which failed with a release-asset error that mentioned neither the `os` option nor the platform:

```toml
[tools]
"github:owner/repo" = { version = "latest", os = ["macos"] }
```

```
$ mise install github:owner/repo
mise ERROR Failed to install github:owner/repo@latest: No matching asset found for platform linux-x64
```

`mise x <tool>` failed the same way because it installs first.

## Fix

`mise install <tool>` now checks `is_os_supported()` on the requested tools and exits non-zero before touching the backend:

```
github:owner/repo is not available on linux: its `os` option lists macos
```

`--dry-run` fails the same way instead of reporting a would-install.

Fixes #15819

Co-authored-by: Z. Bornheimer (issue author; their fork patch showed the same approach)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes install/exec request resolution and error paths for named tools, but behavior is narrowly scoped to OS filtering with new e2e tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Named installs and `mise x` now honor tool `os` restrictions** before any backend work. Previously, a bare `mise install` skipped OS-excluded tools, but explicitly naming one could still hit the backend and fail with an opaque asset error.
> 
> Install and exec run **`check_named_os`** on named tools: they read the relevant config (including highest-precedence / monorepo union), compare against an **`os` override on the CLI** when present, and **`reject_os_excluded`** when every matching request is excluded—returning a clear message that names the tool, current platform, and configured `os` list. Partially supported multi-version config still installs only OS-valid rows. **`get_requested_tool_versions`** filters excluded config rows for normal args while treating explicit `[os=...]` args separately. **`ToolRequest::os`** is now public for this plumbing.
> 
> Adds e2e coverage in `test_install_os_unsupported_tool` for dry-run, exec, explicit versions, local config precedence, and OS overrides.

title: chore(deps): ignore unmaintained chrono advisories in cargo-deny
body:
The daily `cargo deny check advisories` run on `main` fails because RustSec now flags `chrono` (RUSTSEC-2026-0543), `chrono-tz` (-0555), `chrono-tz-build` (-0559) and `humantime` (-0542) as unmaintained. There is no safe upgrade for any of them, and they arrive transitively through `built`, `expr-lang`, `tera` and `rattler`, so this adds each to the `deny.toml` ignore list with a reason. `cargo deny check advisories` passes locally.

Fixes #15809.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Config-only change to cargo-deny ignores; no runtime code or dependency version bumps, only acknowledged transitive unmaintained-crate noise.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds four RustSec **unmaintained** advisories to the `[advisories].ignore` list in `deny.toml` so **`cargo deny check advisories`** (and the main CI workflow that runs it) can pass again after the advisory database started flagging them.
> 
> The new ignores are **`humantime`** (via `rattler` / `rattler_repodata_gateway`), **`chrono`** (via `built`, `expr-lang`, `tera`), **`chrono-tz`**, and **`chrono-tz-build`** (build dep of `chrono-tz` via `tera`). Each entry documents that there is **no safe upgrade** and names the transitive path, matching the pattern used for other ignored advisories in the same file.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>Stranger6667/jsonschema (jsonschema)</summary>

### [`v0.61.1`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0611---2026-11-10)

##### Added

- `PatternCache` and `ValidationOptions::with_pattern_cache` to compile each regex once across validator builds.

##### Fixed

- `dereference` following `$ref` in keywords that hold data, such as `const` and `examples`. [#​1858](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/issues/1858)
- `pattern` over one character class under a large bounded count, such as `^.{0,404600}$`, failing with a regex engine error on the empty string when the size limit was raised to compile it.

##### Performance

- `pattern` and `patternProperties` with a large bounded count over one character class, such as `^.{0,262144}$` or `[^\p{C}]{1,2048}`, build without unrolling the count and fit the default size limit.
- `pattern` and `patternProperties` match anchored character-class patterns such as `^[a-z0-9-]+$` without a regex engine.

### [`v0.61.0`](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#0610---2026-11-08)

##### Added

- `Evaluation::root()` and `OutputUnit` for walking evaluation output units without serializing them.

##### Fixed

- `.` in `pattern` and `patternProperties` matched `\r`, U+2028 and U+2029 (it should reject every line terminator).
- `evaluate()` reported a missing single `required` name beside `additionalProperties: false` at `/additionalProperties` (it should be `/required`).
- Numeric keywords misjudging whole floats past 2^53. [#​1825](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/issues/1825)
- Building a validator with an explicit draft retrieving the schema's `$schema` URI.
- `format: "date-time"`, `"date"` and `"time"` accepting `+`, `,`, `-`, `.` or `/` where RFC 3339 requires a digit. [#​1829](https://redirect.github.com/Stranger6667/jsonschema/issues/1829)
- `$ref` pointers through a numeric object key (`#/responses/200`) skipping the references under their target.
- `oneOf` / `anyOf` rejecting valid instances when a `$ref` inside a branch sits under an `$id`.
- `unevaluatedItems` treated every element as evaluated beside a non-schema `items` value (it should evaluate none).

##### Performance

- Building validators up to 15% faster on

### [`v5.2.7`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v5.2.7): : Retry failed mise downloads with backoff and show the HTTP status

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.6...v5.2.7)

When the action can't download mise, the log now shows the HTTP status and host for each failed attempt. Retries wait longer between attempts, so a short GitHub outage is less likely to fail the job.

#### Fixed

- **Download failures now show what went wrong, and brief outages are retried for longer.** Before this release, a failed mise download logged only `The process '/usr/bin/curl' failed with exit code 22` and retried five times with a fixed 2-second wait. From that message you couldn't tell a rate limit from a missing asset or a server error. Each failed attempt now logs the HTTP status and the host that answered:

  ```text
  Download attempt 1/6 failed: Could not download github.com/…/mise-v2026.10.21-linux-x64.tar.zst (HTTP 503 from github.com). Retrying in 3.4 seconds.
  ```

  The wait between attempts doubles from about 2s up to a 30s cap, with random jitter, so the five retries cover roughly a minute. Only transient failures are retried: connection errors and timeouts, and HTTP 408, 429 and 5xx responses. A 404, any other 4xx, or a local file-write error fails at once. The log shows only the host and file name of each URL, never signed query strings or curl/wget stderr. Partial files are deleted before the next attempt. wget now runs with `--tries=1`, so its own 20-retry default no longer stacks on top of the action's retries. This applies to every download the action makes: the release archive, checksums and the packslip bundle. Checksum and signature verification are unchanged, and there are no new inputs. ([#​722](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/722) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), fixes [#​721](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/issues/721))

- packslip, which the action uses to verify downloaded mise releases, is updated from 1.11.0 to 1.11.2. This version includes upstream hardening of its verifier checks. ([#​726](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mis

title: feat(task): skip git-ignored files in sources with !@gitignore
body:
A task whose `sources` glob covers a directory also counts the files git ignores in it, such as installed dependencies, build output and editor caches. Writing one of those files made the task run again. Because these files differ between checkouts, cached results rarely matched from one machine to the next. Until now the only workaround was a `!` exclusion for every ignored path, kept in step with the `.gitignore` files by hand.

`sources` now accepts a `!@gitignore` entry. It drops the files git ignores from what the entries before it matched. Like a `!` pattern it is evaluated in order, so a later entry can add an ignored path back. That matters when one task's ignored output is another task's input:

```toml
[tasks.build]
sources = ["pkg/**", "!@gitignore", "pkg/dist/**"]
outputs = { auto = true }
run = "npm run build"
```

With `out/` and `dist/` in `.gitignore`, writing `pkg/out/generated.js` no longer makes `build` stale. A change under `pkg/dist/` still does.

- A file git tracks stays a source even when an ignore rule matches it, as in git itself.
- mise reads only the repository's own rules: every `.gitignore` in the work tree and `.git/info/exclude`. Your global `core.excludesFile` is left out, so the same files count as sources on every machine. `core.ignoreCase` is honoured.
- Inside a submodule or other nested repository, that repository's tracked files and rules apply, as in git.
- Files inside `.git` are always dropped. Outside a git work tree the entry drops nothing. Sources outside the task directory (`../shared/**`) are filtered too.
- The entry applies everywhere `sources` does: freshness checks, the artifact cache key and audit, `mise run --affected`, monorepo `global_inputs` and input groups, and `task_source_files()`. `mise watch` drops the entry because watchexec already applies VCS ignores, unless a task sets `watch.no_vcs_ignore`.
- mise still walks ignored directories to find their files. To skip walking a large directory, keep a `!**/node_modules/**` entry as well.

## Implementation

`build_source_matcher` now returns a `SourceMatcher` that splits `sources` at each `!@gitignore` and checks the segments from last to first. The git checks use gix for repository discovery and the index (to find tracked files), and `ignore::gitignore` for the per-directory rules. Each directory's rules are read once and then reused. Matchers whose `sources` have no `!@gitignore` behave exactly as before and never open the repository.

## Tests

- Unit tests cover the ignore rules (nested `.gitignore`, `info/exclude`, negation, a rule that cannot re-include a file below an ignored directory, tracked files, `.git`, paths outside the work tree, nested repositories, non-UTF-8 names) and the ordering of the entry, including sources outside the task directory.
- New e2e test `e2e/tasks/test_task_run_sources_gitignore` covers freshness, re-inclusion, a force-added tracked file and `task_source_files()`.

Closes discussion https://github.com/jdx/

title: fix(shim): skip rustup checks for unrelated tools on inactive shims
body:
Fixes #15789.

When `rust` is in the config, running a shim that is not active in the current directory (so it falls back to a system binary) ran `rustup show profile` and `rustup component list --installed` twice per call. Something polling `jq` through an inactive shim kept deleting `rustup-init` during `mise up`. #13705 only covered the active-shim path.

Looking up a provider for the shim ran the backend-specific satisfaction check on every configured tool. It now runs only for tools that could provide the shim's binary (a name match, a registry provider, or a lazy tool); everything else uses the install-marker check.

```sh
cd /tmp && MISE_DEBUG=1 ~/.local/share/mise/shims/rg --version   # rg inactive here, rust = "latest" globally
```

Before: four `rustup` lines in the debug output. After: none. The new e2e test counts `show profile` and `component list` calls across an inactive shim run with a fake rustup.

## Test plan

- `mise run test:e2e test_rust_inactive_shim_no_rustup test_rust_external_provider test_rust_system_fallback test_hook_not_found_auto_install test_exec_shim_recursion`
- Reproduced the original behavior on v2026.11.8 in Docker.

--- e2e/core/test_rust_inactive_shim_no_rustup (+71/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,71 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# An inactive shim falls back to a system binary. Resolving it must not run
+# the rust backend's rustup checks (`rustup show profile`, `rustup component
+# list`) for tools unrelated to the shim: they spawn rustup on every call.
+
+unset CARGO_HOME RUSTUP_HOME MISE_CARGO_HOME MISE_RUSTUP_HOME
+
+ORIGINAL_PATH=$PATH
+PREFIX="$PWD/provider"
+STATE="$PREFIX/state"
+mkdir -p "$PREFIX/bin" "$STATE" "$PWD/home/active" "$PWD/home/inactive" "$PWD/system"
+
+# A fake rustup proxy that logs every call.
+cat >"$PREFIX/bin/rustup-init" <<PROXY
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+case "\$(basename "\$0")" in
+rustup)
+	echo "\$*" >>"$STATE/rustup.log"
+	case "\${1:-} \${2:-}" in
+	"--version ") echo "rustup 1.0.0 (fake)" ;;
+	"show profile") echo minimal ;;
+	"toolchain install") mkdir -p "$STATE/toolchains/\$3" ;;
+	"component list" | "target list") ;;
+	esac
+	;;
+rustc | cargo)
+	if [[ ! -d "$STATE/toolchains/\$RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN" ]]; then
+		echo "error: toolchain '\$RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN' is not installed" >&2
+		exit 1
+	fi
+	echo "\$(basename "\$0") \$RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN (fake)"
+	;;
+esac
+PROXY
+chmod +x "$PREFIX/bin/rustup-init"
+for command in rustup cargo rustc; do
+  ln -s rustup-init "$PREFIX/bin/$command"
+done
+
+# A system binary the shim falls back to.
+cat >"$PWD/system/dummy" <<'EOF2'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "system dummy"
+EOF2
+chmod +x "$PWD/system/dummy"
+
+export HOME="$PWD/home"
+export PATH="$MISE_DATA_DIR/shims:$PWD/system:$PREFIX/bin:$ORIGINAL_PATH"
+export MISE_OFFLINE=1
+
+cat >"$HOME/mise.toml" <<EOF2
+[tools]
+rust = "1.2.3"
+EOF2
+cat >"$HOME/active/mise.toml" <<EOF2
+[tools]
+dummy = "1.0.0"
+EOF2
+
+mise trust "$HOME/mise.toml"
+mise trust "$HOME/active/mise.toml"
+(cd "$HOME/active" && mise install)
+mise reshim
+
+# The shim is inactive here: dummy is installed but not configured.
+cd "$HOME/inactive" || exit 1
+: >"$STATE/rustup.log"
+assert_contains "$MISE_DATA_DIR/shims/dummy" "system dummy"
+# grep -c prints 0 on no match but exits 1, so mask the status.
+assert "grep -c -e ^show.profile -e ^component.list $STATE/rustup.log || true" "0"

title: feat(settings): set one task.lock_pools entry and read it from MISE_TASK_LOCK_POOLS
body:
Sizing a task lock pool is awkward: `mise settings set task.lock_pools.cpu 8` fails with `Unknown setting`, and the only accepted form, `mise settings set task.lock_pools '{"cpu":"8"}'`, replaces the whole map and drops other pools. There is also no environment variable, so a run that ignores config files (`MISE_IGNORED_CONFIG_PATHS`) can't pass a pool size.

## What changes

```sh
mise settings set task.lock_pools.cpu 8      # sets one pool, keeps `gpu`
mise settings unset task.lock_pools.cpu      # removes one pool
MISE_TASK_LOCK_POOLS=cpu=8,gpu=1 mise run test
MISE_TASK_LOCK_POOLS='{"cpu":"8"}' mise run test
```

- `settings set` and `settings unset` accept a dotted key into any map setting (`IndexMap`), such as `task.lock_pools` or `url_replacements`, and touch only that entry.
- `MISE_TASK_LOCK_POOLS` takes `NAME=SLOTS` pairs separated by commas, or a JSON object.

Reported in [discussion 15717](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15717#discussioncomment-19665660).

## Testing

New e2e test `test_settings_map_entry` covers set, overwrite, unset, an unknown key and both env spellings. `test_settings_set` and `test_settings_unset` still pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.325.*

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CLI and env parsing for optional task lock-pool configuration only; no auth or core runtime paths beyond settings load.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Map settings** (`task.lock_pools`, `url_replacements`, and other `IndexMap` settings) now accept dotted keys in `mise settings set` and `unset`, so you can change one entry without replacing the whole map. Entry names can include dots (e.g. URL keys).
> 
> **`task.lock_pools`** can be driven from **`MISE_TASK_LOCK_POOLS`**, parsed as comma-separated `NAME=SLOTS` pairs or a JSON object, via new `parse_lock_pools` in the settings crate. Metadata, schema, and docs describe the env format.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>aubepkg/aube (aube)</summary>

### [`v2.10.1`](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/releases/tag/v2.10.1): : Workspace update, remove, audit and SBOM fixes; more reliable downloads

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/v2.10.0...v2.10.1)

v2.10.1 fixes several workspace bugs in `aube update`, `aube remove`, `aube audit` and `aube sbom`, closes more pnpm compatibility gaps, and makes network access more reliable on VPN/split-DNS setups and unstable connections.

##### Changed

- **Smaller, faster store compression on APFS** ([#​1930](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1930), [@​jdalton](https://redirect.github.com/jdalton)): on macOS, aube now tries LZFSE before LZVN and compresses blocks in parallel. On three ARM64 native addons (Oxlint, Rolldown, Lightning CSS), this used 5% less disk space, compressed 23% faster, and used up to 6.4 MB less memory. Decoding of zstd-packed napi addons is now bounded. File contents and store keys do not change.
- **System CA store is authoritative** ([#​1932](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1932), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): aube no longer adds its bundled Mozilla root certificates on top of the OS trust store. A CA that an OS update or enterprise policy removes is now also distrusted by aube. On Linux and other Unix systems, aube uses the bundled roots only when it cannot load any system roots, for example in a minimal container without `ca-certificates`. It then prints `WARN_AUBE_BUNDLED_ROOTS_FALLBACK`. `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `cafile` and `ca` work as before.

##### Fixed

##### Workspaces

- **`aube remove` with a shared lockfile** ([#​1952](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1952), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): removals now go through the workspace install. Before, removing a dependency from a member with a `workspace:` dependency failed with `no version of lib matches range workspace:*` after `package.json` had already been rewritten. Removing from other members wrote a stray member lockfile, and removing a root dependency re-resolved every member's locked versions.
- **`workspace:` links after `aube update`** ([#​1969](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1969), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx), with [@​ruandre](https://redirect.github.com/ruandre)): a member's `workspace:` dependency was written relative to the workspace root, which left its `node_modules` symlink broken. The path also grew longer with each update. This affected both `aube-lock.yaml` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`

title: feat(lock): show each entry's provenance in --check
body:
`mise lock --check` said whether a lockfile was complete, but not what each entry was verified with. A lockfile can pass the check with nothing but a checksum, or with a recorded signature or attestation, and the output looked the same (raised in discussion #15748).

The check now lists each platform entry with the provenance type recorded when the lockfile was generated (`minisign`, `cosign`, `slsa` or `github-attestations`), `checksum only`, or `none`. That is what `mise lock` verified. When an entry records both a checksum and provenance, a locked install may check only the checksum unless [`locked_verify_provenance`](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/settings.html#locked_verify_provenance) is set.

```console
$ mise lock --check
✓ ~/src/app/mise.lock is up to date (2 tool versions, 4 platform entries)
  jq@1.7.1 for linux-x64: checksum only
  jq@1.7.1 for macos-arm64: checksum only
  gh@2.62.0 for linux-x64: github-attestations
  gh@2.62.0 for macos-arm64: github-attestations
```

When there are problems, the same lines appear under the problem count, so an entry with no checksum, or one the check cannot find, shows as `none`:

```console
$ mise lock --check
✗ ~/src/app/mise.lock has 2 problems
  yq@4.44.1 for linux-x64: none
  yq@4.44.1 for macos-arm64: checksum only
mise ERROR ~/src/app/mise.lock would fail a locked install:
  - jq@1.6 is not in the lockfile
  - No lockfile checksum found for yq@4.44.1 on platform linux-x64 (https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.44.1/yq_linux_amd64) (--locked mode)
hint: run `mise lock` to update the lockfile
```

`--json` gains a `provenance` field on each platform entry, with the same values. Problems that belong to a whole tool (such as a version missing from the lockfile) have `provenance: null`.

This is display only. The check does not fail because of an entry's provenance, and no new setting is added.

### Testing

- `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_check` now asserts `checksum only` for a complete entry, `github-attestations` for an entry that records it (human and `--json`), `none` after the checksum is removed, and `none` for a per-platform `asset_pattern` entry that is missing from the lockfile.

Thanks to jmoreno11 for raising this in #15748.

title: feat(lock): add --check
body:
Nothing told you that `mise.lock` had fallen behind `mise.toml` until `mise install --locked` failed. That happens, for example, when an update bot bumps `node = "24"` to `node = "26"` in `mise.toml` and leaves the lockfile alone. `mise lock --check` turns that into a CI failure on the pull request itself. It reads only the lockfile and runs in offline mode, so it never writes anything, skips the deferred cleanup of tools due for removal, and makes no network requests (raised in discussion #15746).

It covers every configured tool, plus the tools that tasks declare and the tool stubs the lockfile lists, on each platform `mise lock` would lock. It fails and lists each problem that `mise install --locked` would reject:

- a request with no matching locked version (the config was bumped but the lockfile was not)

title: fix(lock): make --dry-run report what would change
body:
`mise lock --dry-run` printed a ✓ for every configured tool and platform. Its output was the same whether the lockfile was missing, stale or already complete, so it could not tell you whether running `mise lock` would change anything (raised in discussion #15746).

A dry run now resolves every tool on every platform the way `mise lock` does, into a copy of the lockfile, and compares the result with the file on disk. Each platform entry is shown as one of:

- a new entry, when the tool is not in the lockfile yet
- a version change, with the version it replaces
- a new platform, for a locked version that lacks this platform
- the fields that would be filled, changed or removed, such as `checksum filled` or `url changed` (a changed SLSA provenance URL counts)
- an entry that would be removed, for example when a tool's `os` option no longer allows the platform. Platforms the lockfile stores outside the ones being locked are listed too, but only when generation would drop or change them.
- unchanged

Nothing is written:

```console
$ mise lock --dry-run --platform linux-x64,macos-arm64
→ Dry run - would update:
  ~ jq@1.7.1 for linux-x64 (checksum filled)
  + jq@1.7.1 for macos-arm64 (new platform)
  + yq@4.44.1 for linux-x64 (new entry)
  + yq@4.44.1 for macos-arm64 (new entry)
→ 4 of 4 platform entries would change
```

When nothing would change, the header reads `Dry run - already up to date` and every line says `unchanged`.

### Behavior changes

- A dry run now makes the same network requests as `mise lock`, and for some backends it may download artifacts to compute checksums. It used to resolve nothing.
- A dry run now fails where `mise lock` would. One example is a version that cannot be resolved for a platform it was locked for.
- `--json` output is unchanged. It still reports only version-level changes (`old_versions` / `new_versions`), so `mise lock --bump --dry-run --json` keeps working for update bots.
- A version that `mise lock` would prune is left to the existing prune line rather than listed per platform.
- A tool that cannot be resolved for a platform is listed once per option variant it was configured with.
- The report does not cover changes to dependency-graph sidecars or request bindings. Those are only computed while the lockfile is written.

### Testing

- New e2e test `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_dry_run_changes` covers a new entry, unchanged, a new platform, a filled checksum and a version change, and checks that the lockfile stays byte-for-byte the same.
- Unit tests cover the per-entry comparison, including option variants of one version reported once each, removed entries, untargeted platforms, stale versions, unresolved option variants, and an SLSA URL change.
- The existing lock and lockfile e2e tests that run `--dry-run` still pass.

Thanks to jmoreno11 for raising this in #15746.

title: feat(backend): add enable_backends allowlist
body:
`disable_backends` is a denylist, so locking a project down to a few backends means naming every other one, and the list silently goes stale when mise adds a backend. The new `enable_backends` setting is an allowlist that fails closed: only the backends you list resolve or install.

```toml
[settings]
enable_backends = ["core", "aqua", "github"]
```

With this setting:

- `node`, `python` and the other core tools keep working, because they use the `core` backend.
- A registry shorthand skips to its next allowed backend, the same way it skips disabled backends today. `fnox` lists `packslip:github.com/jdx/fnox` before `github:jdx/fnox`, so it installs from `github:jdx/fnox`.
- An identifier whose backend isn't listed fails, and the error names the setting:

  ```console
  $ mise install gem:rake
  mise ERROR Failed to install gem:rake@latest: backend gem is not listed in enable_backends
  ```

- A shorthand with no allowed backend says which setting ruled them all out:

  ```console
  $ MISE_ENABLE_BACKENDS=aqua mise install fnox
  mise ERROR Failed to install fnox@latest: fnox is in the mise tool registry but none of its backends (packslip:github.com/jdx/fnox, github:jdx/fnox) are supported in the current configuration for version latest (enable_backends allows only aqua)
  ```

`disable_backends` still applies on top of the list. The default is an empty list, which allows every backend, and so does `MISE_ENABLE_BACKENDS=` with nothing after it. `pypi` and `pipx` count as the same backend, and a vfox backend plugin is allowed by its plugin name, matching how `disable_backends` treats them.

The setting checks the backend each tool is configured with. It does not check tools a backend runs itself, such as the `node` that the `npm` backend uses.

The idea comes from @jmoreno11 in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15747.

## Implementation

Every place that honors `disable_backends` now goes through one check in `src/backend/mod.rs`: install, install-into and ls-remote, registry backend selection, plugin precedence over the registry, lockfile backend discovery, `mise search`, the tool catalog and `mise doctor`. `mise install-into` called the backend directly and skipped this check, so it now runs the check too, for `disable_backends` as well. When no backend can serve the request, `install-into` used to panic on an empty version list; it now prints the same error as `mise install`. `mise search` previously compared homepage URLs against `disable_backends`, so that filter never matched. It now filters by backend name.

## Validation

- New e2e test `e2e/backend/test_enable_backends`: an allowed backend (`aqua:`) installs; `gem:` and a core tool are refused with errors naming the setting, including through `install-into`; `fnox` falls back to `github:` and installs; `disable_backends` overrides an allowed backend; an empty value allows everything. `test_disable_backends` and `test_ls_remote_disable_backends` still pass.
- Unit tests cover the all

title: feat(backend): add a per-tool libc option to packslip and github
body:
On Linux, packslip and github tools now take a `libc` option. It picks the glibc or musl build for that tool only. Until now the only way to get a musl build was to set the global `libc` setting (`MISE_LIBC`), and that changes every tool. The aqua backend already has this option.

The case that prompted this is in [discussion #15750](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15750): fnox's glibc build needs libudev, which wasn't on the user's machine. The musl build runs without it:

```toml
[tools]
fnox = { version = "latest", libc = "musl" }            # registry entry, installed through packslip
"github:jdx/fnox" = { version = "latest", libc = "musl" }
```

How it behaves:

- **Values:** `glibc` or `gnu`, and `musl`. Any other value is an error.
- **Strict choice:** with the option set, mise never falls back to the other libc.
  - packslip skips its gnu→musl fallback and its `glibc_min` floor fallback, and errors if the release has no build for the libc you asked for.
  - github, gitlab and forgejo refuse assets built for the other libc. Assets that don't name a libc still qualify.
- **Precedence:**
  - The option overrides the `libc` setting for that tool.
  - A platform that names its libc (such as `linux-x64-musl`) keeps that libc. A lockfile entry is keyed by platform, so a gnu build can't be locked under a musl platform. This matches aqua.
- **Lockfile:** the option is written to the tool's lockfile entry, as aqua does. If you change it, run `mise install --force` to replace an install that already exists.
- **ARM and provenance:** github-family asset matching now reads the ARM suffixes `gnueabi`, `gnueabihf`, `musleabi` and `musleabihf` as a libc, so the option can refuse the other libc's ARM build. Provenance files are also ranked by libc on Linux, so a musl build gets the musl provenance. Provenance follows the libc the installed archive names, whether `libc`, `asset_pattern` or a platform `url` picked it. Both apply with or without the option: on an ARM glibc host, an asset that names `gnueabihf` now outranks one that names `musleabihf`.
- **Defaults:** otherwise nothing changes without the option. Default packslip installs still choose the full fnox archive, not the `lite` variant.

Docs for the option are under `libc` in the packslip and github backend pages. The JSON schema accepts the key for both backends.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover artifact and asset selection, strict refusal, the `glibc_min` fallback, validation, and lockfile options.
- The new e2e test `e2e/backend/test_packslip_libc` checks fnox 1.48.0 through both packslip and `github:jdx/fnox`:
  - The default config locks the gnu build. `libc = "musl"` locks the musl build for x64 and arm64 and records `libc = "musl"`.
  - On Linux x64 it installs the musl build and runs it.
  - An invalid value fails.

title: fix(lock): leave tool_config.locked lockfiles alone after installs
body:
A config root that sets `[tool_config] locked = true` asks for the same guarantee as the global `locked` setting, scoped to its own tools: the lockfile is the source of truth and only an explicit `mise lock` changes it. Installs didn't respect that. After `mise install`, `mise exec` or a lazy install, mise still ran its lockfile pass over the root's lockfile: it refreshed recorded entries, added platforms from `lockfile_platforms` and pruned entries of tools that left the config. Only unrecorded version pins were held back (#15428). The global `locked` setting skips this pass entirely.

```toml [mise.toml]
[tool_config]
locked = true

[tools]
node = "24"
```

```sh
MISE_LOCKFILE_PLATFORMS=windows-x64 mise install
# before: mise.lock gains platforms.windows-x64 entries
# after:  mise.lock is unchanged
```

Now installs, `mise use`, `mise unuse`, `mise prune` and the other install paths leave a lockfile alone when every config that writes it sets `tool_config.locked`. `mise lock` still records new versions and platforms and prunes removed tools, and `mise upgrade` still moves to newer versions. A monorepo lockfile is left alone only when every config root that writes it sets `tool_config.locked`, including sibling packages the install didn't start from. A shared lockfile with at least one unlocked writer keeps the #15428 behavior: the pass runs, but unrecorded pins of the locked configs are held back.

**Behavior change:** before, an install in a locked root pruned stale entries of tools removed from the config. Now they stay until the next `mise lock`, as in global locked mode.

Fixes the problem raised in discussion #15749.

### Validation

- `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_generate_tool_config_locked_install` now asserts that `mise.lock` is byte-identical after an install with an unrecorded pin, with an extra platform configured, and with a stale entry. It also checks that `mise lock` then prunes the stale entry and that an unlocked root still prunes on install. I checked by hand that the platform case adds `platforms.windows-x64` without `tool_config.locked`, so the assertion isn't vacuous.
- New `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_monorepo_tool_config_locked`: an install from one package leaves a shared lockfile alone when every root is locked, and still prunes once one package is unlocked. It fails without the sibling lookup.
- New `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_merge_monorepo_tool_config_locked` covers the same sibling case in the deprecated merge mode, using an extra platform as the signal. It fails without the fix.
- The other tool_config.locked, monorepo, locked-mode, locked-scopes, request-precedence and upgrade-prune lockfile e2e tests pass. Clippy is clean on stable with `--workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`.

title: feat(bootstrap): enable services without starting or stopping them
body:
`[bootstrap.services]` could only say `state = "running"` or `state = "stopped"`, so every entry also started or stopped the unit. That's a problem for a unit that should only take over later. Two examples are a login manager, which would switch away from the console you are provisioning from, and a graphical-session service when no session is running yet.

`state = "unchanged"` now manages only whether the unit starts at boot or login. mise never starts, stops, reloads or restarts it:

```toml
[bootstrap.services.greetd]
state = "unchanged"
enabled = true
```

mise runs `systemctl enable greetd.service` (after `unmask`) when the unit isn't enabled yet. Once it is enabled, the entry is up to date whether greetd is running or not. A managed file that `notify`s the service doesn't reload or restart it either.

What the new state works with:

- **System units:** supported.
- **Existing user units** (`scope = "user"` with no `command` or `builtin`): supported.
- **User services mise defines** with `command` or `builtin`: rejected. mise writes and launches those itself, and on macOS loading a LaunchAgent that runs at login starts it right away, so mise can't promise to leave its state alone.
- **`masked = true`:** rejected, because masking stops the unit.

`state` still defaults to `"running"`, so existing configs behave the same.

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15745

Co-authored-by: Vantesh <121645908+Vantesh@users.noreply.github.com>

### Validation

- New unit test covering plan and commands for enabled/disabled × active/inactive/failed, notifications, and the masked rejection.
- e2e: `test_bootstrap_services` (rejection for defined user services), `test_schema_bootstrap_services`, `test_schema_ajv`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets` is clean on stable. Beta flags a lint in `mise-ui` that also fails on `main`.

> 
> **Overview**
> Bootstrap service entries can now use **`state = "unchanged"`** so mise only **`enable`**s or **`disable`**s a unit (after **unmask**) and never **start**, **stop**, **reload**, or **restart** it. Convergence ignores the runtime active state, and file **notify** / **on_change** no longer triggers lifecycle commands for that state.

title: fix(shim): keep shims pointing at mise after a shim-triggered install
body:
Fixes #15742

On macOS, running a tool shim when no `mise` is on `PATH` (for example `ssh host '~/.local/share/mise/shims/kimi …'`, which gets `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`) could break every shim at once. If the shim auto-installed a new version, the reshim that followed rewrote every shim as a symlink to the shim that was run:

```text
$ readlink ~/.local/share/mise/shims/jq
/Users/me/.local/share/mise/shims/jq
$ jq --version
zsh: too many levels of symbolic links: jq
```

Shims now keep pointing at mise (`/opt/homebrew/bin/mise` in the issue's reproduction), and `mise reshim --force` is no longer needed to recover.

### Cause

macOS reports the path a process was launched through as `current_exe()`. When mise runs as a shim, that path is the shim, and `MISE_BIN` used it as-is. Running that path again runs the tool, not mise, because mise chooses what to do from its argv0. Reshim fell back to `MISE_BIN` when it found no `mise` on `PATH`. Other places that start mise from `MISE_BIN` have the same problem: `__MISE_BIN` for asdf plugin scripts, `mise watch`, `run_at`, and `self-update`. Two of them had already been patched one at a time: task hooks in #14550, and `tool update`.

### Change

- **`MISE_BIN` never names a tool shim.** When the running executable's file name isn't a mise name, mise follows the shim's link one step. That finds the mise the last reshim chose, usually a launcher that survives upgrades (`/opt/homebrew/bin/mise`), not the versioned file behind it (`…/Cellar/mise/<version>/bin/mise`), which `brew cleanup` deletes. It resolves all the way only when that one step doesn't end at mise. Paths already named mise are unchanged, which covers every non-shim launch, and Linux, where `current_exe()` is already the real binary.
- **Shims are never written pointing at something that isn't mise.** If the only candidate still names a tool (for example a Windows hardlink shim with no mise on `PATH`), reshim warns and leaves the existing shims alone instead of turning every one into a loop:
  ```text
  mise WARN  not writing shims: …/jq is not the mise executable; put mise on PATH and run `mise reshim`
  ```
- `running_mise_bin()` (hooks and watch_files) and `mise tool update` now rely on `MISE_BIN` instead of resolving the shim themselves.

### Testing

- Unit tests for the resolution: a shim linking to the launcher, a relative link, a link through an intermediate file not named mise, and paths that should be left as they are.
- New e2e test `test_reshim_from_shim_without_mise_on_path`. It reproduces the bug on Linux by setting `__MISE_BIN` to a shim and removing mise from `PATH`, and it checks the warning path.
- Existing reshim and shim e2e tests and the shims/hooks/tool_update unit tests pass. I couldn't test on macOS or Windows.

title: fix(install): refresh installed versions after waiting on an install lock
body:
Concurrent `mise install` processes that share a data dir and install `node = "lts"` could fail an `npm:` tool with:

```
failed: tool 'npm:typescript@latest' requires configured install dependency 'node@lts', but its selected version is not installed
```

The failing process waits on the other's install lock, logs `node ⇢ already installed`, then fails the dependency check. This now re-reads the installed versions once the lock is held, so the dependency resolves to the node the other process just installed.

Fixes #15752

## Cause

The offline resolve of a prefix like `lts` or `26` reads the installed versions from a per-process memo. The memo can be built while the other process is still installing, and nothing refreshed it after the lock wait. This matches why an exact `node = "26.13.0"` passed: it never consults the list. This is read from the code, not from a trace of a failing run.

## Testing

- `cargo check -p mise` passes.
- I reproduced the failure once with 2026.11.6 (two projects, fresh data dir). It is timing-dependent and did not recur in ~20 more runs, so I could not confirm the fix by repeating it, and there is no deterministic test.

title: fix(java): pick the newest build in ls, runtime symlinks, lockfile and outdated
body:
With two Temurin builds installed, such as `temurin-25.0.4+7.0.LTS` and `temurin-25.0.4+101.0.LTS`, several commands still treated `+7` as newer than `+101`. `Versioning` ignores everything after `+`, so the two tie, and the string tie-break sorts `101` before `7`. #14876 fixed this for `mise current` and `mise exec` only.

Now the same numeric build tie-break is used everywhere:

- `installs/java/` links (`temurin-25`, `temurin-latest`, `latest`, ...) point at `+101`, so `java = "latest"` resolves to the newest build.
- `mise ls` lists `+101` above `+7`.
- Lockfile entry selection prefers the newest build.
- `mise outdated` reports `+7` as outdated when `+101` is available (with `java = "temurin-25.0.4"` pinned it previously said everything was up to date). Only numeric build segments decide this, so `1.0.0+one` vs `1.0.0+two` is still not outdated.

The ordering helper that #14876 added privately to `install_state.rs` moved to `mise_util::semver` (`version_sort_key`, `build_metadata_is_older`), and all call sites share it. It only breaks ties between versions that are identical before the `+`, so no version scheme is assumed.

Validated with unit tests for the helper plus the existing `mise-util` semver and `mise` lib tests for sort_versions, outdated, lockfile and runtime_symlinks. Clippy was clean for the touched code, apart from existing lints in files this PR doesn't touch.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14872 (reported by javabrett, whose branch proposed this shape)

title: fix(lock): name the tool and provenance in the downgrade error
body:
## Summary

When `mise lock` refuses to write a lockfile because an entry would lose recorded provenance or change its signer, the error now says which tool, version, platform and backend it was, and what the old and new entries record:

```
mise ERROR lockfile generation would downgrade recorded provenance; previous files were preserved: recorded slsa but the new entry has no provenance. If the registry recipe no longer provides what mise needs to verify it, fix the recipe or lock the tool through another backend (flux2@2.10.0 on linux-x64, aqua:fluxcd/flux2)
```

Each failing check describes itself: primary provenance, signer and `attested_by`, or an additional artifact's URL with its old and new provenance. The recipe hint appears only on the primary provenance failure. Before, the message gave no hint of which of a project's tools blocked the update.

The downgrade protection itself is unchanged.

Refs #15744 (the diagnostic request only; the underlying cause is that the aqua flux2 recipe declares `slsa_provenance` without a signer identity, so mise can no longer record SLSA for it and must be fixed upstream in aquaproj/aqua-registry).

## Test plan

- `cargo test --lib lockfile::generate` passes.

title: feat(task): select dependencies by tag with { tag = ... }
body:
`--tag` (#15406) selects tasks from the command line, but a task's `depends` still had to name every task it needed, or lean on name groups like `lint:*`. A dependency table can now select by tag instead:

```toml
[tasks.clippy]
tags = "lint"
run = "cargo clippy"

[tasks.shellcheck]
tags = "lint"
run = "shellcheck scripts/*.sh"

[tasks.ci]
depends = [{ tag = "lint" }, { tag = ["test", "slow"] }]
```

`mise run ci` runs `clippy` and `shellcheck` whatever they are named, so role selection can move out of task names and into tags.

- `tag` takes one tag or a list, and selects tasks that have any of them.
- With a `task` as well, only the matching tasks that have the tag are kept, like `mise run --tag lint 'check:*'`.
- It works in `depends`, `depends_post` and `wait_for`.
- A tag that selects no task is an error, as for a name, unless `optional = true`.
- A task never depends on itself, so a task tagged `lint` can sit in a `{ tag = "lint" }` list.
- `mise tasks validate` does not flag a tag entry as a missing dependency.

Suggested by slikts in [#15406](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15406#issuecomment-6894335162). The string form (`depends = ["tag:lint"]`) is left out on purpose: `:` is already the task namespace separator. Tags match tasks in the loaded configs only (no other monorepo projects), and a remote task counts only when its tags are in its `mise.toml` entry, not its `#MISE` header.

title: fix(brew): accept installer script casks from taps
body:
`mise bootstrap` failed for any tap cask that declares `installer script:`, such as `xykong/tap/flux-markdown`, with:

```
brew-cask: installer metadata must be an array
```

On macOS that error also stopped every other `brew-cask:` package in the same run from installing.

Casks from Homebrew's API publish `installer` as an array, but casks evaluated from a tap's Ruby emit a single object, and the parser only accepted the array. It now accepts both shapes, so the cask installs normally.

Artifact parse errors now name the cask, for example `brew-cask:flux-markdown: installer metadata must be an array or object`, so a failure in a long bootstrap run can be traced.

title: fix(vfox): let plugins call async functions inside pcall
body:
Installing `vfox:version-fox/vfox-python` fails with a Lua error. vfox-python 0.6.4, published 2026-11-14, wraps its version-index requests in `pcall`. Embedded Lua 5.1's `pcall` cannot be yielded across, and `http.get` suspends the plugin's coroutine while it waits. Every install then fails:

```
$ mise i vfox:version-fox/vfox-python@3.12.0
mise ERROR Failed to install vfox:version-fox/vfox-python@3.12.0: runtime error: ...util.lua:1836:
Could not list Python versions. pyenv: attempt to yield across metamethod/C-call boundary;
uv-build: attempt to yield across metamethod/C-call boundary
```

The same would hit any plugin that puts `http.get`, `http.download_file` or another async call inside `pcall`.

Plugins now get a `pcall` that runs the protected function in its own coroutine and passes its yields up. Results and errors behave as with the built-in `pcall`.

`xpcall` is unchanged. A message handler needs the stack at the point of the error, which a coroutine would discard.

This also unblocks `release` on the open release PR: `e2e-linux-2` fails on `test_vfox_python_slow`, which only runs with `TEST_ALL=1`, so main never exercised it.

## Testing

- Unit tests cover the old `pcall` failing on an async call, and the new one returning results, nesting, catching errors after a yield, and matching the old `pcall` without yields.
- `TEST_ALL=1 mise run test:e2e test_vfox_python_slow` passes on this branch. It failed on the release PR with the error above; I did not re-run it on main locally.
- `cargo clippy -p vfox --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: fix(dotfiles): warn about keys no dotfile entry or bootstrap hook reads
body:
A `[dotfiles]` entry, a `[dotfile_groups.<name>.entries]` entry, or a `[bootstrap.hooks]` table silently ignored any key mise doesn't read. Packages take `env = "work"` to install only in an environment, so the same key on a dotfile or hook looked like it worked — but the entry applied, and the hook ran, on every machine ([discussion #15148](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15148)).

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/edit.conf/id" = { block = "text", env = "work" }

[bootstrap.hooks.post-packages]
run = "echo HOOK_RAN"
env = "work"
```

Now each such key warns once:

```
mise WARN  [dotfiles]."~/.config/edit.conf/id": unknown key "env", ignoring it
mise WARN  [bootstrap.hooks.post-packages]: unknown key "env", ignoring it
```

The entry or hook still applies as before, so a config written for a newer mise keeps loading.

This adds no new selector. To gate a whole-file entry on an environment, use `variants = [{ profile = "work" }]`. For edits, hooks, or anything else that belongs to a combination of environments, give the combination its own config file (`mise.ssh-work.toml`, selected with `MISE_ENV=ssh,work,ssh-work`). The dotfiles docs now say so.

## Validation

- New e2e test `test_dotfiles_unknown_keys`: whole-file, edit, group, and hook entries with an unknown key warn and still apply. Known keys don't warn.
- `cargo test -p mise -p mise-oci -p mise-system` passes, including the schema conformance test.
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: perf(config): trim eager work in hook-env
body:
Profiling `hook-env` (discussion #15722) found work that runs on every `cd` or every prompt even when nothing needs it. This trims it without changing behaviour.

- **Lockfile warning:** `warn_outdated_lockfiles` no longer reads the clock up front. Reading it makes jiff build the system time-zone database (about 10% of a full run), and the date is only needed for a lockfile in an old format.
- **Plugin shorthands:** `Config::shorthands()` builds the asdf/vfox map on first use instead of on every config load. Only `get_repo_url` and `plugins ls`/`ls-remote` read it.
- **Registry platforms:** `backend_matches_platform` returns early for an empty platform list and compares `os-arch` without formatting a string.
- **Prompt fast path:** `config_search_dir_mtimes` expands `conf.d/*` style patterns with `read_dir` per component instead of `glob()` on an absolute path, which re-stats every prefix from `/` on each call.

The chrono-tz duplicate and the `perf` task's PIE build from the same discussion are not part of this PR.

Tests: `cargo test --lib` for lockfile, registry, hook_env, config and plugins (748 passed), including a new test that `glob_in_dir` matches `glob::glob` on a directory with metacharacters in its name. `cargo +1.95 clippy -p mise --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Thanks to @FalkWoldmann for the profile.

title: fix(dotfiles): refuse whole-file keys on block and line edits
body:
A `[dotfiles]` block or line edit with `variants` was silently misread. Without a matching selector the edit applied anyway; with one, the entry was also parsed as a whole-file entry keyed by the edit path, so `mise dot apply` and `mise bootstrap` failed with "sources do not exist".

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/t.conf/id" = { block = "text", variants = [{ profile = "work" }] }
```

Now `variants` (and every other whole-file-only key) on a block or line edit warns like a merge edit already does and the entry is ignored:

```
[dotfiles]."~/.config/t.conf/id": variants applies to whole-file entries, not block or line edits, ignoring entry
```

Honoring the selector on edits would be a feature of its own; this only fixes the misparse and the silence.

- A table with `block`, `line`, `template`, `comment` or `position` is never a whole-file entry.
- The edit parser rejects all whole-file keys on such a table, not just `permissions` and `dot_prefix`.
- `mise dot pull` validation refuses the same keys.

Fixes #15726

## Testing

Unit tests for both classifiers and an e2e test, `test_dotfiles_edit_variants`. `cargo test -p mise -p mise-oci -p mise-system` passes. Clippy could not run here (missing `lua51`).

title: fix(bootstrap): skip brew-cask entries with unsupported artifacts on linux
body:
Fixes #15728.

On Linux, one shared `[bootstrap.packages]` list with a cask that ships an AppImage (for example `brew-cask:helium-browser`) made `mise bootstrap packages status` print only `unsupported artifact type app_image`, and `apply` exit 1 after installing the other packages. title: fix(bootstrap): pull the global config before loading it on --update
body:
`mise bootstrap --update` now fast-forwards the global config checkout even when the commit it already has does not parse. Before, a machine that pulled a config commit with a TOML typo could not pick up the follow-up fix: `--update` failed on the broken file before it ran `git pull`, and every other mise command failed on it too.

```
$ mise bootstrap --update --yes
mise::config::parse_error
  × Invalid TOML in config file
   ╭─[~/.config/mise/config.toml:1:5]
 1 │ [env
```

The pull is wrapped in a history scope, and opening that scope loads the config of the checkout to work out which files are tracked. `--update` now checks that config first: when it fails to load, the pull runs without the history record but under the same operation lock, so it cannot overlap another history operation (the reason is logged under `MISE_DEBUG=1`), then bootstrap reruns from the fixed commit as before. When the config loads, the scope opens and records the pull exactly as it did, and any error opening it, such as a lock timeout, still stops the update.

Fixes #15727. The `--from <url> --update` case mentioned in the issue goes through a different path and is not covered here.

## Test plan

- `e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_update_config_checkout` gains a case: a checkout on a commit that does not parse (`mise env` fails), upstream has the fix, `mise bootstrap --update` pulls it and runs the fixed config.
- `cargo clippy` reports one failure in `crates/mise-ui`, which also fails on `origin/main`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.325.*

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes bootstrap update ordering and history locking when config is unloadable; scope is skipped in that branch, so behavior diverges from the normal journaled path but lock semantics stay aligned.

> **Overview**
> **`mise bootstrap --update`** can fast-forward the global config checkout even when the **current** checkout commit has **invalid TOML** that prevents any command from loading config. Previously, opening the history `OperationScope` required reading that broken config first, so the pull never ran and machines could not pick up a fixing commit upstream.
> 
> The update path now **probes config load** before opening a scope. When config loads, behavior is unchanged: scope + journal on success/failure. When load fails, it acquires a new **`hold_operation_lock()`** guard (same wait/contention rules as a scope, no history record, released on drop) and runs **`git pull --ff-only`** under that lock only.

title: fix(zig): record minisign provenance at lock time
body:
`mise lock --bump` no longer fails for zig with "lockfile generation would downgrade recorded provenance" when the existing entry has `provenance = "minisign"`.

Every zig archive is minisign-verified when it is installed, but the lock-time resolution left `provenance` empty. The lockfile ratchet read that as a downgrade from the old `minisign` entry. A fresh `mise install` of zig also never wrote `provenance = "minisign"` to `mise.lock`. Lock-time resolution now records `minisign` for every resolved zig entry (release index, numbered fallback and nightly), matching what install enforces.

```toml
# mise.lock
[[tools.zig]]
version = "0.17.0"
backend = "core:zig"

[tools.zig."platforms.macos-arm64"]
provenance = "minisign"
```

```
MISE_LOCKFILE_PLATFORMS=macos-arm64 mise lock --bump
```

Fixes #15721

Not tested beyond `cargo check --lib` and `cargo fmt`; resolution needs the network, so there is no unit test.

title: feat(task): let a lock hold several slots with `task.lock_pools` and `count`
body:
## What changes

A task `lock` can now be shared by several runs at once. Until now a lock admitted one holder, so a resource that is limited rather than unique, such as the CPU cores or memory of a machine, could only be guarded by making every heavy task wait for the one before it.

Declare how many slots a lock has once per machine, and let each task take the share it needs:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings.task.lock_pools]
cpu = "8"
```

```toml
[tasks.lint]
run = "..."
lock = "cpu"                                    # one slot

[tasks.test]
run = "..."
lock = [{ name = "cpu", count = 4 }, "test-db"] # four slots
```

`lint` and `test` runs from any worktree start together while their shares fit in the 8 slots, and a run that does not fit waits and says who holds the pool:

```text
[test] waiting for lock cpu (4 of 8 slots), held by test in ~/src/app-pr-7 (pid 5120, for 4m01s), test in ~/src/app-pr-9 (pid 5302, for 40s)
```

## Details

- A lock is a pool of slot files under `task-locks/`, held with the same OS file lock as before, so a task that dies frees its slots.
- A task takes `count` free slots, all or none, under a short admission lock for the pool that is never held while waiting. A task that does not fit leaves room for a smaller one that does, and gives up its `--jobs` slot while it waits, as it does for any lock.
- A name without `task.lock_pools` has one slot, so every existing `lock = "name"` behaves as before. A `count` above the pool's slots takes all of them.
- `MISE_TASK_LOCKS` lists the slots held, for example `cpu,cpu:1,cpu:2`, so a task can pick a per-slot resource such as a test database or a port.
- A nested task shares the slots its parent holds. One that needs more than its parent holds fails with a message instead of risking two parents each waiting for what the other holds.
- Waiting tasks are not queued, so a steady stream of small tasks can keep a large one waiting. The docs say so.

Capacity lives in a setting rather than on each task so tasks cannot disagree on it. Values are strings because the setting is a string map.

Follows the discussions in jdx/mise#15717 and jdx/mise#15715, and builds on the prototype in davdroman's `feat/task-lock-slots` branch.

## Tests

Unit tests for the all-or-none admission, count capping and nested slots; `e2e/tasks/test_task_lock_pools` for separate `mise run` processes, a nested run and `--jobs` inside one run; the existing lock e2e tests pass.

title: fix(task): do not cache a pass when a source changed during the run
body:
A cached task no longer records a pass when one of its sources changed while it ran. Previously the pass was stored under the key computed before the run, so a later run on the earlier content restored a result produced from different content.

Reproduction from the issue: edit `input.txt` while `mise run check` sleeps, then restore the old content and run again. The second run printed `sources up-to-date, skipping` and replayed `checked: new`. Now the first run warns and stores nothing:

```
[check] input.txt changed while the task ran; not caching
```

The task's own result is reported as before. The check compares each source's mtime and ctime (Unix) with the time the key's inputs were first read, rather than hashing again, so it also catches a file that was written and then restored during the run. A source that was removed counts as changed. It guards both the artifact store and the freshness pointer that raw/interactive tasks write. The task reports no cache key in that case, so dependents are not cached on top of an uncertain result.

Before accepting a pass the sources are also re-selected, so a file that starts matching a glob during the run counts as a change; if that rescan fails, nothing is cached. A file that matches only briefly and is removed again before the rescan is not detected.

On platforms without ctime (Windows) only mtime is compared. A source edited in the same instant as the start can be missed, or on coarse-timestamp filesystems a recent edit can cause a skipped cache write; both err toward not caching.

Fixes #15712

title: fix(task): scan the cache once when clearing several tasks
body:
`mise cache clear --task '<pattern>'` now reads the task cache once for all matched tasks instead of twice per task. Clearing many tasks no longer slows down with the size of the cache.

Reproduction from the issue: with 4,000 entries in the cache, `mise cache clear --task 'u*'` (20 tasks, nothing to delete) took about 2.3 s, against 145 ms to list the same tasks with `mise cache task`. It now costs about one pass over the cache, like the listing.

The clear lists every matched task's entries with `task_cache_entries_for`, then finds the partial writes of all of them in one more directory pass. Behavior is unchanged: a manifest shared by several tasks is removed once, entries whose owner cannot be verified are still skipped with the same warning, and each task's freshness pointer is removed. `clear_task_cache` stays as a one-task wrapper.

The e2e test now also checks that clearing one task of a pattern leaves the other's entries alone.

title: feat(task): render templates in lock names
body:
A task's `lock = "name"` is shared by every task on the machine that names it, so two unrelated projects that both lock `package-lock.json` made each other wait. Lock names now render templates, so a project can scope a shared name to itself:

```toml
[tasks.w]
lock = "package-lock.json-{{ config_root | hash(len=8) }}"
run = "npm version --no-git-tag-version {{arg(name='version')}}"
```

Two projects running `mise run w` at once no longer queue behind each other; two runs in the same project still do. Worktrees of one repository have different `config_root`s, so they get separate locks too. `mise tasks info` shows the rendered name.

A name that renders empty, or with a comma or control character, is an error. A scope that other tasks can share by name across a repository's worktrees would need a separate `scope` option, which this doesn't add.

Refs #15706
