title: fix(completions): complete the next task after `:::`
body:
## Problem

`:::` starts the next task in `mise run`, but completion did not follow it. Words after `:::` were completed as more arguments of the first task:

```console
$ mise __complete_word__ --shell bash --line "mise run a f1 ::: "
files
$ mise __complete_word__ --shell bash --line "mise run a f1 ::: b -"
-h
--fast
--help
```

Tasks are subcommands mounted under `run`, and usage checks `restart_token` only on the innermost parsed command, which by then is the first task.

## Fix

When a `mise run` (or `mise tasks run`, or naked `mise <task>`) line has a `:::` before the cursor, complete the words after the last `:::` as a fresh `mise run` line. `mise run a f1 ::: <Tab>` now offers task names, and `mise run a f1 ::: b -<Tab>` offers only `b`'s flags. Other commands keep `:::` as an ordinary word.

## Not fixed

The second half of #15610 remains: `mise run b extra -<Tab>` still offers `b`'s flags although `mise run` refuses `extra`. Dropping the hidden `[ARGS]` catch-all and setting `unknown_flags=error` on `run` did not change it, so it looks like it needs a change in usage.

Refs #15610

title: fix(bootstrap): build brew formulae from source in a clean environment
body:
## Summary

`mise bootstrap packages apply` built brew formulae from source with the caller's whole environment, so toolchain variables from the user's shell leaked into the build. For example, mise exports `GOROOT` for its managed Go (`go.set_goroot`), and a Go formula then failed with `compile: version "go1.27.3" does not match go tool version "go1.27.4"`. A stray `CC`, `GOFLAGS`, `CARGO_HOME` or `PYTHONPATH` broke builds the same way.

The source build now starts from a clean environment, like `brew` does when it re-execs under `env -i`. Only a small allowlist is inherited: `HOME`, `USER`, `LOGNAME`, `SHELL`, `TERM`, `TMPDIR`, `LANG`/`LC_*`, proxy variables, CA bundle variables (`SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR`, ...), `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and `HOMEBREW_*`.

Behavior change: a `CC` or `CFLAGS` exported in your shell no longer steers a formula's source build, which matches `brew`.

## Testing

- Unit test that `GOROOT`/`CC`/`GOFLAGS`/`PYTHONPATH` are dropped while `HOME`, proxy, `LC_*` and `HOMEBREW_*` are kept.
- The source-build e2e now exports a nonexistent `CC` and must still build `hello`.
- Not run locally: `mise-sigstore` currently fails to compile in this checkout, so CI is the first run.

Fixes discussion #15611

title: fix(bootstrap): refuse to archive a home directory or oversized source in bootstrap remote
body:
`mise bootstrap remote` archives the source directory, which defaults to the current directory. Run from a home directory, it tarred everything in it with no output, so the command looked hung after printing the staging-directory ssh call. It would also have uploaded `~/.ssh` and similar to the remote host. Reported in [discussion 15554](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15554).

Before archiving, mise now:

- refuses a source that is `$HOME` or `/`
- stops when the source holds more than 512 MiB or 100,000 files after excludes, listing the largest top-level entries
- prints `archiving <dir>` so a slow archive is not silent

```
$ cd ~ && mise bootstrap remote --host example
Error: refusing to send /home/me to the remote host: it is not a project directory and would include credentials such as ~/.ssh. Run from your project, pass --source <DIR>, or pass --yes to send it anyway
```

`--yes` skips the checks for a project that really is that large. The limits are not configurable otherwise.

Tests: unit tests for the home/root refusal, the size limit and `exclude` handling; `test_bootstrap_remote` covers the home refusal and the `--yes` bypass. The size-limit e2e is not covered because it would need a 512 MiB fixture.

Local clippy fails on lints in files this PR does not touch (newer local toolchain); `remote.rs` has no findings.

title: fix(uninstall): remove the alias links of the last uninstalled version
body:
## Summary

`mise uninstall` left `~/.local/share/mise/installs/<tool>/` behind after the last version was removed. The folder held only dangling alias links (`latest`, `global`, `5`, `5.1`):

```console
$ mise uninstall --all cheat
$ ls -A ~/.local/share/mise/installs/cheat
5  5.1  global  latest
```

Now the links and the empty folder are removed together with the last version.

Fixes jdx/mise#15595.

## Cause

The empty-folder cleanup counts subdirectories, and a link whose target is gone does not count, so the folder looked empty. It deleted `.mise.backend.toml` but not the links. Without that file the tool no longer counts as installed, so the runtime-symlink rebuild never visited the folder again.

The cleanup now drops dangling runtime links first.

## Test

`e2e/cli/test_uninstall` asserts the tool folder is gone after the last version is uninstalled. Also checked by hand with `cheat@5` on macOS.

title: fix(doctor): stop warning about the backend a packageManager checksum forces
body:
`mise doctor` no longer warns that the registry recommends a different backend for `yarn`, `npm`, `pnpm` or `bun` when the tool was installed through a `packageManager` checksum.

With `"packageManager": "yarn@4.16.0+sha512.…"` in `package.json`, mise installs Yarn with `http:yarn`, the backend that publishes the checksummed artifact. `mise doctor` then reported:

```
tool 'yarn' installed with backend 'http:yarn'
but registry now recommends 'vfox:jdx/vfox-yarn'.
To migrate: mise backends switch yarn
```

The advice could not clear the warning: the next install from that `package.json` forces the checksum backend and records it again. `npm` (`npm:npm` against `aqua:npm/cli`), `pnpm` and `bun` behaved the same way.

Doctor now skips tools whose recorded backend is one a checksum forces, using the same `recorded_by_checksum_backend` check the install manifest reader already uses to treat those records as non-explicit.

Fixes #15603.

title: fix(pipx): run an installed github git source with no releases offline
body:
Fixes the failure reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15596: with `MISE_OFFLINE=1`, `mise x` could not run an already-installed `pipx:git+https://github.com/...` tool.

## Problem

A github.com git source whose repo has no GitHub releases has no version list to resolve `latest` from, so mise installs it under a literal `latest` directory. The installed-version lookup deliberately skips a directory named `latest`, so offline mise found no installed version, logged `no versions found`, and ran the command without the tool on PATH:

```
$ MISE_OFFLINE=1 mise x -- srun-refresh
mise WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for pipx:git+https://github.com/1208nn/NetKeeper4srun.git: ... no versions found
mise ERROR "srun-refresh" couldn't exec process: No such file or directory
```

with a config of:

```toml
[tools]
"pipx:git+https://github.com/1208nn/NetKeeper4srun.git" = "latest"
```

## Fix

When offline, and the backend reports an unresolved `latest` (`unresolved_latest_version`), mise now uses the literal `latest` install if it exists. Online behavior is unchanged: a remote listing still wins when one is available.

## Validation

- Reproduced the error above with the reporter's repo, then confirmed the same command runs the tool with this change.
- New e2e test `test_pipx_git_no_releases_offline` installs that repo and runs it with `MISE_OFFLINE=1`. It depends on that third-party repo staying release-less.

title: chore(ci): run cargo-deny advisories only when dependencies change
body:
`cargo deny check` ran every category on every PR, with the advisory DB wiped first. A new RustSec advisory against any transitive dependency turned every open PR red, including PRs that never touched `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`. Recent `deny.toml` commits (#15416, #15352, #15012, #14939) are all "ignore RUSTSEC-xxxx" fixes made to unblock unrelated PRs.

## Changes

- PR `lint` runs `cargo deny check bans licenses sources` always. These only change when the dependency graph does.
- `cargo deny check advisories` runs on a PR only when it changes `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml` or `deny.toml` (and always on pushes), so the PR that introduces a vulnerable dependency owns the failure.
- New `deny-advisories.yml` runs the advisories check daily against `main`. On failure it opens (or comments on) one tracking issue, emails via Resend using the existing `RESEND_API_KEY` / `NOTIFY_EMAIL` secrets, and fails the run.

A new advisory is now an issue and an email, not a red check on unrelated PRs.

## Testing

zizmor passes on the new workflow. Not yet run end to end: trigger `deny-advisories` once with `workflow_dispatch` after merging.

> **Low Risk**
> CI and tooling workflow changes only; no application runtime or security logic in the product itself.
> 
> **Overview**
> **PR lint** no longer runs full `cargo deny check` on every run. It always checks **bans, licenses, and sources** via `mise x -- cargo-deny`, and runs **`check advisories` only when the PR touches `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, or `deny.toml`** (non-PR runs still treat deps as changed so advisories run on push). `cargo-deny` is added as a **lazy** tool in `mise.toml`/`mise.lock` instead of installing it in the lint job.

>

title: feat(dotfiles): warn when a copy target was edited since mise wrote it
body:
`mise dot apply` now warns before it overwrites a `copy` target you edited since mise last wrote it, the way it already does for templates. This matters for copies under `/etc` or other files that applications rewrite, where a local edit was easy to lose silently.

```
$ mise dot apply --dry-run
cp ~/src ~/.copied (edited since mise last wrote it)

$ mise dot apply --yes
mise WARN files: ~/.copied was edited since mise last wrote it; applying overwrites the edit. Move it into ~/src to keep it
```

- `--dry-run` and the confirmation list mark edited files. Directory copies in a group show `(N edited since mise last wrote them)` in `--dry-run` and mark each file in the confirmation list.
- A single-file `copy` entry now records a digest of what it wrote. Files deployed by a dotfile group are compared with the digest the group already records for `--prune`.
- Quiet when mise has no record (a target that predates the entry), and when the target already matches the source.
- Directory copies outside a group have no per-file record, so they are not checked.

Added `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_copy_edited_warning`; the related dotfiles e2e tests pass. Clippy and the crate's unit tests could not run locally (no `lua51` for `mlua-sys`), so CI covers those.

Co-authored-by: nahoj, who proposed this in discussion 15592.

> Changes apply-path behavior and state capture for copy entries (digest persistence and pre-apply warnings); mistakes could miss warnings or false-positive, but overwrites remain explicit and logic mirrors existing template handling.
> 
> **Overview**
> `mise dot apply` now treats **copy** targets like templates when detecting local edits: after a single-file copy it persists a SHA256 digest in per-target state, merges in digests from dotfile **group** deploy records, and compares current files before overwrite.
> 
> **Dry-run**, confirmation prompts, and apply now annotate or warn with *edited since mise last wrote it* when a recorded copy diverges from what mise wrote and no longer matches the source. Copies with no history, targets that already match the source, and directory copies outside a group (no per-file record) stay silent. Group moves keep per-file records so edits are still detected when an entry switches groups.

title: fix(sandbox): allow `./` relative paths on macOS
body:
On macOS, a task sandbox with a relative path that starts with `./` blocked everything it was meant to allow:

```toml
[tasks.build]
run = "bash -c 'pwd'"
allow_read = ["./"]   # or ["./sub"], or "./dist" in allow_write
```

`allow_read = ["./"]` failed with `getcwd: cannot access parent directories: Operation not permitted`, and `["./sub"]` made `cat sub/x` fail with "Operation not permitted". `{{config_root}}` and absolute paths were unaffected. Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15590.

mise joined the relative path onto the cwd, giving `<cwd>/./sub`, and then canonicalized it. `Path` equality ignores `.` components, so the canonical path compared equal and the `./` spelling went into the Seatbelt profile as `(subpath "<cwd>/./sub")`. Seatbelt matches against the canonical path, so the rule never matched. Dropping the `.` components after the join fixes it.

I could not reproduce the `{{cwd}}` failure from the discussion; it worked here.

Verified by running the repro tasks against a debug build (`./`, `./sub`, and `dir = "sub"` with `./` all pass now) and with a new unit test.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core sandbox path normalization on macOS; incorrect handling could widen or narrow file access, though scope is limited to allow-list resolution and is covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes macOS task sandboxes where **relative allow-list paths** like `./`, `./sub`, or `./dist` were effectively ignored, so reads/writes that should be permitted still failed with “Operation not permitted”.
> 
> `SandboxConfig::resolve_paths` now **strips redundant `.` components** after resolving paths against the cwd, so rules emitted to the Seatbelt profile use canonical spellings that match how the kernel checks paths (instead of literals such as `<cwd>/./sub`). **Trailing-slash / `/.` directory intent** is preserved: existing files that are not directories still get a trailing `/` so directory-only rules stay strict; missing directory paths drop the suffix so allowances apply once the path is created.
> 
> Two **Unix unit tests** lock in normalization for `./` paths and trailing-slash behavior.

title: fix(task): complete bare root task names in a monorepo
body:
With `monorepo_root = true`, `mise run te<TAB>` did not offer a root task named `test`, even though `mise run test` runs it. Only `//:test` and `:test` completed, so the shell found nothing extending `te` (aliases were the one exception).

```toml
monorepo_root = true

[tasks.test]
run = "echo test"
```

Before: `mise __complete_word__ --shell zsh --line 'mise run test'` offered no `test`. After: it offers `test` next to `:test` and `//:test`, which still complete. Bare names are offered only for tasks of the current config root (inside `apps/web`, `build` completes but the root's tasks do not), since those are the names the resolver accepts.

Fixes #15591

title: fix(bootstrap): keep the brew rack lock out of the Cellar so uninstalled formulae disappear
body:
Fixes #15593.

`mise bootstrap` left an empty `.mise-staging.lock` in every formula's Cellar rack (`/opt/homebrew/Cellar/<name>/`). Homebrew treats a rack directory as an installed formula, so after `brew uninstall qpdf` the rack still held the lock file and the formula stayed in the list:

```console
$ brew uninstall qpdf
$ brew list --versions qpdf
qpdf
$ brew uninstall qpdf
Error: No such keg: /opt/homebrew/Cellar/qpdf
```

The same happened to dependencies removed by `brew autoremove`.

Now the staging lock is taken at `<prefix>/var/homebrew/locks/mise-staging-<name>.lock`, next to the existing `mise-bootstrap.lock`, so nothing is left in the Cellar. The next time mise stages a formula it also deletes leftover `<rack>/.mise-staging.lock` files from earlier versions and removes the racks they left empty. Racks that still hold a keg keep it and only lose the lock file.

Tested with new unit tests for the lock location and the legacy cleanup (`cargo test -p mise -p mise-system-packages --lib -- brew::pour brew::maintenance`). I did not run this against a real Homebrew prefix on macOS.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes concurrency and filesystem layout around Cellar staging locks; incorrect cleanup could remove racks or leave stale Homebrew state, though locking and keg-preservation checks limit exposure.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves Homebrew formula **staging rack locks** from `<Cellar>/<name>/.mise-staging.lock` to `<prefix>/var/homebrew/locks/mise-staging-<name>.lock`, so uninstalled formulae are no longer left visible to `brew list` because an empty rack still exists.
> 
> Adds a **one-time legacy sweep** that deletes old in-rack lock files, removes empty racks when safe, and coordinates with the new external lock so concurrent staging is not interrupted. The sweep runs when staging a bottle and on **real (non–dry-run) installs even when nothing needs pouring**, so cleanup does not wait for the next pour. **Dry runs** skip that install-time sweep.

## Problem

`mise run --quiet` and `--silent` hid mise's own messages, but when a task declared `daemons = [...]`, the supervisor's startup log lines still printed:

```
• [shop/db] LOG:  starting PostgreSQL 17.11 ...
• [shop/db] LOG:  database system is ready to accept connections
✔ pitchfork: [shop/db] started on port 5432
```

## Fix

When `quiet` or `silent` is set, the implicit daemon start now passes `--quiet` to `pitchfork start`, which suppresses those lines. Without either flag nothing changes.

`mise daemons start -q` already hid them, because unknown flags go straight to pitchfork. The docs now mention both.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15587.

## Testing

`cargo check --all-features` passes. I did not add an e2e test.

> 
> **`mise daemons start`** maps global or trailing **`--silent`** to pitchfork’s **`--quiet`** (pitchfork has no **`--silent`**). Task-driven starts in **`daemons/tasks`** honor the same hush state from the run flags, settings, and task output mode.

title: feat(vfox): let tool plugins that download nothing install in locked mode
body:
A vfox tool plugin that downloads nothing, such as [mise-xcode](https://github.com/Nozbe/mise-xcode), which selects an Xcode already on the system, could not be installed with `mise install --locked`. Locked mode required a lockfile URL for every vfox tool plugin, and `mise lock` can't record one when `PreInstall` returns no `url`:

```
mise ERROR Failed to install vfox:nodl@1.0.0: No lockfile URL found for nodl@1.0.0 on platform linux-arm64 (--locked mode)
```

A plugin can now declare in `metadata.lua` that it downloads nothing:

```lua
PLUGIN = {
  name = "xcode",
  version = "0.1.0",
  downloads = false,
}
```

For such a plugin, `mise install --locked` installs the locked version without a lockfile URL, as it already does for asdf plugins, and `mise lock` records the version only. If the plugin's `PreInstall` returns a `url` anyway, the install stops with an error, so the flag can't be used to skip the check for a real download.

Plugins that don't set `downloads` behave as before. A metadata read failure also keeps today's requirement. The field is documented in the `metadata.lua` table in `docs/plugin-lua-modules.md`.

Plugins that download on some platforms only are not covered; the flag is static.

Added e2e `test_vfox_no_download_locked`: locked install succeeds with the flag, fails without it, and a `url` from a `downloads = false` plugin is rejected. Clippy and `mise run lint-fix` are clean.

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15581

title: fix(install): read the idiomatic version file of a plugin installed in the same run
body:
Fixes #15580.

`mise install` and `mise lock` read idiomatic version files (such as `.xcode-version`) through the plugin that declares them. When that plugin came from `[plugins]` and wasn't installed yet, the first `mise install` cloned it but never read the version file. It printed "all tools are installed" and exited 0, and only the second run installed the tool. `mise lock` reported "No tools configured to lock" on a fresh machine. This hit CI hardest, where every run starts without the plugin.

```toml
[plugins]
xcode = "https://github.com/Nozbe/mise-xcode#51cf7df04ec240f86b6c6865ec23fd5a8101f036"

[settings]
idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["xcode"]
```

With an `.xcode-version` file next to it, a single `mise install` now installs `xcode`, and `mise lock` locks it.

The config reads the idiomatic filenames when it loads, and an uninstalled unprefixed plugin counts as an asdf plugin with none. Bare `mise install` (non-monorepo) and `mise lock` now install the missing `[plugins]` entries first and reload the config if any were installed. `--dry-run` installs nothing and so reloads nothing.

Not covered: `mise install --monorepo` and `mise install TOOL@VERSION` keep their current behavior.

Validation: new e2e `test_plugins_idiomatic_first_install` (a local vfox plugin with `legacyFilenames`, one `mise install` and one `mise lock`) passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from an existing unused-dependency warning in `mise-util`. I did not confirm the test fails without the fix, or run the issue's Docker repro.

> 
> **Overview**
> **Bare `mise install` and `mise lock` now install missing `[plugins]` entries and reload config before resolving tools**, so idiomatic version files (e.g. `.xcode-version`) declared by those plugins are recognized on the first run instead of requiring a second command.
>

This runs for unscoped, non-monorepo `mise install` and for `mise lock` except `--sidecars`. Scoped installs (`mise install TOOL@VERSION`) and `--monorepo` install are unchanged.
>

title: ci: run untrusted macOS jobs on macos-latest
body:
Renovate PRs (and other untrusted PRs) have been failing `test-ci` because `untrusted / unit-macos` is cancelled the instant it starts: no runner is assigned, no steps run and there is no log. In the last 60 `test` runs, every untrusted `unit-macos` job was cancelled this way (all five were renovate PRs, e.g. #15579) and none ever ran. Reruns are cancelled the same way.

This moves the untrusted macOS jobs from the `macos-14` label to `macos-latest`:

- `unit-macos` in `test-impl.yml`
- the untrusted `build-tarball` runner in `release.yml`
- the comments in `test-impl.yml` that name the runner

Trusted runs stay on Namespace and are unchanged.

## Not verified

The root cause is not confirmed. Trusted PRs run on Namespace, so they never exercise this path, and this PR is trusted too. The real check is the next renovate or fork PR after merge. If `unit-macos` is still cancelled at start, the cause is not the `macos-14` label.

`macos-latest` can move to a newer macOS image later, so the test environment may shift with it.

title: fix(exec): stop a detached tool process from holding the caller's stdout pipe on Windows
body:
## Problem

On Windows, a process a tool starts detached with `stdio: 'ignore'` kept the caller's stdout pipe open when the tool ran under `mise x` or a shim. In PowerShell, `$out = mise x node@22 -- node -e <detached spawn>` returned only when the detached process exited (20s in the report), while running `node` directly returned at once. This hit Nx's daemon through pnpm, for example.

## Fix

mise passed the tool extra inheritable copies of the caller's stdin/stdout/stderr, and the tool handed them on to the detached process. mise now clears the inherit flag on its own standard handles right before spawning the tool, and `mise exec` spawns with `std::process::Command` instead of `duct`, which kept its own inheritable duplicates while the child started. The Node IPC shim path is left alone because it must forward the parent's handles.

On a Windows machine, the example above went from about 20s to 0.13s under `mise x` and 0.20s under a shim.

Adds an e2e-win test that covers both `mise x` and a shim.

Fixes #15582.

> **Overview**
> Fixes **#15582** on Windows where `mise exec` or a shim could keep the caller's stdout pipe open until a **detached** child exited (e.g. Node with `stdio: 'ignore'`), making PowerShell captures block for ~20s.

> Before spawning the real tool, **`disinherit_std_handles()`** clears the inherit flag on mise/shim's own stdin/stdout/stderr so stray handles are not passed through to grandchildren, while `Command` still gives the child proper duplicated stdio. title: fix(dotfiles): close large history operations by sending the commit message on stdin
body:
## Problem

`mise dot` history gets stuck after a large `mise dot apply`. The operation's checkpoint message lists every affected path (2,749 in the report), and it was passed to `git commit-tree` as a single `-m` argument. That exceeds Linux's per-argument limit (128 KiB), so spawning git failed with `Argument list too long (os error 7)`. The pending operation was kept and retried on every `save`/`sync`, failing the same way each time, so nothing was ever published.

## Fix

`commit_tree` now sends the message on stdin, as `commit_tree_as` already does, with a trailing newline added so the commit text matches what `-m` produced. Machines already stuck close their pending operation on the next `save`, with no manual editing of the pending file.

A regression test commits a 200 KiB message.

Fixes #15571

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.317.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Single plumbing call path change with a focused test; behavior is preserved except that oversized messages now succeed instead of failing at spawn.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`HistoryRepo::commit_tree`** no longer passes the commit message to `git commit-tree` as `-m`, because huge checkpoint text (e.g. every path from a large `mise dot apply`) can exceed the OS per-argument cap (~128 KiB) and leave history stuck in a retry loop. The message is written on **stdin** instead (same pattern as `commit_tree_as`), with a trailing newline so stored commit text still matches `-m` behavior.
> 
> A regression test commits a **200 KiB** message to lock this in.
>

title: test(dotnet): stop the channel alias test failing for a day after a new release
body:
`core/test_dotnet_channel_aliases` failed in CI for about a day after Microsoft shipped a new .NET channel. Today `mise latest dotnet@sts` resolved to the new 11.0 channel, whose only stable SDK (11.0.100, released the same day) the default 24h `minimum_release_age` hides. Every other 11.0 version is a preview or RC, so `latest` printed nothing, `trusted / e2e` failed, and so did every PR's `test-ci` aggregate.

The alias behaves correctly: `sts` means the current Standard Term Support channel, and the cutoff holds back a release that new. The test only checks that the alias resolves to an SDK version in a supported channel, so it now sets `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0s` and no longer depends on how old the newest release is. This also removes the same one-day flake after every future LTS or STS release.

Testing: `mise run test:e2e test_dotnet_channel_aliases` passes locally against the new 11.0 channel.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: Anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.317.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Test-only change; no production behavior modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Sets **`MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0s`** in `e2e/core/test_dotnet_channel_aliases` so `mise latest dotnet@lts` / `dotnet@sts` still resolve right after Microsoft ships a new channel. Without it, the default minimum age hides the only stable SDK on day one, `latest` goes empty, and the alias shape assertions flake for about a day on every new LTS/STS release.
> 
> Adds a short comment explaining that the test validates alias/channel resolution, not the release-age cutoff.

title: fix(task): let the task's usage spec decide whether -h asks for help
body:
`mise run <task> -h <value>` printed the task's help and exited 0 even when the task's usage spec disables help and declares its own `-h` flag, so the task never ran and there was no way to pass that flag. Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15532.

```toml
[tasks.dh]
usage = '''
disable_help #true
flag "-h --host <host>"
'''
run = 'echo "host=$usage_host"'

[tasks.hv]
usage = 'flag "--pat <pat>" allow_hyphen_values=#true'
run = 'echo "pat=$usage_pat"'
```

| command | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| `mise run dh -h x` | task help, exit 0 | `host=x` |
| `mise run hv --pat -h` | task help | `pat=-h` |
| `mise run hv --help` | task help | task help (unchanged) |

mise looked for `-h`/`--help` anywhere in the task's arguments without consulting the spec. It now asks usage's parser, so `-h`/`--help` is a help request only where the spec takes it as one: not when the spec sets `disable_help` or `disable_help_flag`, not when a declared flag owns the word, and not as a flag's value. Tasks that do not opt out keep printing help (#7893), as do tasks without a usage spec and `raw_args` tasks.

The check reads only the words: no `choices run=` command runs and environment values and defaults are not validated, so it adds no external calls.

The same early scan in the `usage bash/zsh/fish` wrapper was fixed in jdx/usage#1637. This change needs no usage release, since `Parser::explain_refused` is already public in the usage-lib mise uses.

Tested with the new `e2e/tasks/test_task_help_spec_decides` plus the existing help, raw_args, double-dash and args-position e2e tests, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.317.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes early-exit behavior for `mise run` when `-h`/`--help` appear in task args; mistakes in `asks_for_help` could suppress help or run tasks unexpectedly, but impact is localized and covered by e2e tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise run`** no longer treats every `-h` / `--help` in task arguments as a help request. When a task has a **usage** spec (including one that only sets `disable_help` or `disable_help_flag`), mise consults the usage parser via new **`asks_for_help`** so help is shown only when the spec maps those tokens to built-in help—not when they are a declared flag, a flag value (e.g. `allow_hyphen_values`), or should be forwarded to the task.
> 
> Tasks without a usage spec still get the basic task info help path; **`raw_args`** tasks are unchanged. A new e2e script **`test_task_help_spec_decides`** locks in disable-help, custom `-h`, hyphen values, and default help behavior.
>

title: fix(bootstrap): evaluate and build brew tap formulae from a tap checkout
body:
Formulae from a third-party tap that start with `require_relative` could not be evaluated or built. mise loaded the formula from its text, so the include resolved against whatever directory mise ran in (or failed outright, because the evaluation sandbox cannot read it). Homebrew loads the formula by its path inside the tap, so the include finds the tap's own files.

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"brew:gromgit/fuse/sshfs-mac" = "latest"
```

Before, from `~`:

```
Formula/sshfs-mac.rb:1:in 'Kernel#require_relative': Operation not permitted - getcwd (Errno::EPERM)
mise ERROR failed to resolve Homebrew tap formula 'gromgit/fuse/sshfs-mac'; ...
```

and the source build failed the same way, because only the formula file was copied into mise's cache, without the tap's `require/` directory.

Now, when a tap formula contains `require_relative`, mise downloads the tap at the pinned commit once (through the GitHub API, so a private tap uses your token; cached under `system-brew/tap/`) and:

- **Evaluates metadata** with the formula's absolute path inside that checkout. The sandbox still blocks every other read; it gains read access to that one directory.
- **Builds from source** by loading the formula from the checkout. Its checksum is still verified against the metadata first.

Formulae that do not use `require_relative` keep the existing single-file fetch, so they pay no extra download. Only GitHub taps are supported, as before.

Tests: an evaluation test with a `require/` directory beside `Formula/` (it needs a Ruby on PATH, as the neighbouring tap tests do), plus validation tests for the checkout download. `cargo test --workspace --lib -- brew::` passes (479 tests) and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The sandboxed evaluation test was skipped on my machine because my only Ruby is installed under `$HOME`, which the sandbox cannot execute; I ran its logic unsandboxed instead, so CI is its first sandboxed run. I did not run a real `sshfs-mac` build, and the tarball download itself is untested.

Fixes #15543

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-317_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Adds network downloads and sandbox path allowances for tap builds, but scope is limited to formulae containing `require_relative` and still pins checksums/commits.
> 
> **Overview**
> Third-party Homebrew tap formulae that use **`require_relative`** now work for **metadata evaluation** and **source builds**. mise detects those formulae, downloads a **pinned GitHub tap tarball** (cached under `system-brew/tap/`), and loads the `.rb` from that checkout so relative includes resolve like Homebrew.
> 
> **Metadata:** The Ruby shim evaluates the formula using **`MISE_BREW_SOURCE_FILE`** and the process **`current_dir`** set to the checkout; the sandbox gains read access only to that directory.
>

title: fix(task): resolve a monorepo project's own task templates from sibling projects
body:
A task template defined in a monorepo project's own `mise.toml` could not be used by that project's tasks when mise ran from a sibling project, or when a path such as `//foo:foo_task` was run from another project.

```toml
# foo/mise.toml
[task_templates.example]
env = { GREETING = "hello" }

[tasks.foo_task]
extends = "example"
run = "echo foo $GREETING"
```

Before, from `bar/`:

```
$ mise run //foo:foo_task
mise ERROR Task 'foo_task' extends template 'example' which was not found. Available templates: (none)
```

Now it prints `foo hello`. Running from the monorepo root already worked. Any task run from `bar/` that loaded `foo`'s tasks (for example `mise run :bar_task`) hit the same error, so the workaround of declaring an empty `[task_templates.example]` in the root config is no longer needed.

mise now layers a project's own config files (up to the monorepo root) over the templates collected for the current directory when it loads that project's tasks. Precedence is unchanged: the project's templates beat its ancestors' and global ones.

Reported in discussion 15531.

## Validation

Added `e2e/tasks/test_task_monorepo_project_template` (passes): runs `foo_task` from the root and from `bar/`, and checks `mise tasks ls --all`. I did not run the wider e2e or unit suites.

> 
> **Overview**
> **Monorepo tasks that extend templates defined only in a subproject's `mise.toml` now resolve those templates when mise runs from a sibling project or via paths like `//foo:foo_task`.** Previously the loader only had templates from the current working directory's config chain, so `extends = "example"` failed outside the owning project.
>

+/// Layer the templates a monorepo project's own config files define over `base`.

+/// not include a sibling project's. Without this, a task in `/foo` that extends a template

+fn with_project_templates(
+    base: &TaskDefinitions,
+    project_dir: &Path,
+    project_configs: &ConfigMap,

+        .templates
+        .extend(collect_task_definitions(&overrides, None).templates);

title: fix(doctor): report a malformed package.json that mise skips as a version file
body:
When `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools` includes a tool and the project's `package.json` can't be parsed (a trailing comma, or `devEngines.runtime` written as a string), mise skips the file for that tool and says nothing. The tool then resolves with no version and nothing explains why.

`mise doctor` now reports it:

```
1 warning found:

1. package.json is not valid, so mise ignores the versions it declares: <parse error>
```

A valid `package.json`, or one with no `devEngines`, produces no warning. Only `package.json` files mise has loaded as version files are checked.

I did not add a warning on normal commands. `package.json` belongs to npm and other tools, may be mid-edit, and runs through `hook-env` on every prompt, so a runtime warning would be noisy. `mise doctor` is where people look when a version isn't picked up.

`idiomatic_version` and its `package_json` module are now `pub` so the doctor code in the binary can call the new `problem()` helper.

Fixes #15541

Tested with a unit test and a new e2e test (`test_doctor_malformed_package_json`) covering a malformed and a valid file. I did not run the wider doctor e2e tests or check `doctor -J`.

title: fix(dotfiles): refuse to overwrite edited copies without a terminal
body:
## Problem

With no terminal attached (a script, `ssh` without `-t`, an agent shell), `mise dot apply` skipped its confirmation and replaced `copy` targets that had been edited locally. Untracked files are not journaled, so `mise dot undo` reported "nothing to undo" and the edit was gone.

```sh
mise dot apply 2>&1 | cat   # edited ~/dst/x.conf overwritten silently, exit 0
```

## Change

Without `--yes` and without a terminal, `mise dot apply` now fails and names `--yes` when a `copy` target (a file, or a file inside a directory copy) would be replaced with different content that no tracked history keeps, including a file mise never wrote:

```text
files: applying would overwrite ~/dst/x.conf and nothing keeps the current content, but there was nobody to ask; run `mise dot diff` to review it, then pass --yes to proceed non-interactively
```

Copies that already match the source, new targets, and tracked files apply without asking, as before. With a terminal the existing prompt is unchanged. This follows the #14071 rule that irreversible operations fail without a TTY and name `--yes`. The Conflicts section of the dotfiles docs now says so.

Fixes #15528

## Test

New e2e `test_dotfiles_copy_non_tty`; the 158 non-slow dotfiles e2e tests pass.

> 
> **Overview**
> **Non-interactive `mise dot apply` now aborts** instead of silently replacing `copy` targets whose current content isn't recoverable via history or undo. Before applying (when there's no `--yes`/`MISE_YES` and stderr isn't attached to a terminal), the planner walks copy operations and flags paths where content would be lost: differing file bytes, symlink→file replacement, or `--force` directory removals where not every nested file is tracked.
> 
> The failure message lists up to five targets and directs users to `mise dot diff` and **`--yes`** to proceed. **Unchanged behavior:** identical content, new targets, mode-only repairs, and history-tracked paths still apply without prompting; interactive TTY flows keep the existing confirmation prompt.

title: fix(exec): keep env._.path ahead of tool bins when the caller's PATH already has it
body:
`mise x -- <tool>` could run a tool's bundled binary instead of the one a project put on PATH with `env._.path`, whenever the shell's PATH already contained that directory.

```toml
[tools]
node = "26.13.0"

[env]
_.path = ["override/bin"]   # contains a pinned npm
```

With `override/bin` already on the caller's PATH, `mise x -- npm` ran Node's bundled npm, while `mise x -- sh -c npm` ran the override, because the child PATH had the right order but mise's lookup of the program did not. Now both run `override/bin/npm`.

Cause: to stop wrapper scripts on the inherited PATH from being found before real tool binaries, `exec_program` searches mise-added directories before inherited ones. Entries produced by templated post-env directives are not included either, only those the config declares directly.

title: fix(config): run pnpm's install script when a packageManager checksum is set
body:
## Summary

With `idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["pnpm"]`, a `packageManager` field that carries a checksum made every `pnpm` run print this to a terminal:

```
pnpm is running through Node.js because the script that installs its native binary was skipped.
Reinstall pnpm with its build scripts allowed to run the binary directly.
```

A checksum installs pnpm through the `npm:pnpm` backend so the download can be verified, and that backend skips lifecycle scripts. pnpm 12 installs its native binary from an install script, so it fell back to Node.js. Without a checksum the aqua backend installs the binary directly, so there was no warning.

mise now approves builds for that install, as it already does for bun. The checksum is still verified.

`allow_builds = ["pnpm"]` is not enough here: aube ignores a per-package approval for the archive a checksum installs from, so the script never ran. Only `allow_builds = true` took effect. pnpm's only dependencies are its platform binaries.

## Test plan

- Unit test checks that a pnpm checksum request sets `allow_builds`.
- New e2e `cli/test_idiomatic_pnpm_checksum` installs `pnpm@12.15.0` with the checksum from the issue and checks `pnpm --version` prints no warning under a PTY. It fails without the fix.

Fixes #15529

title: fix(bootstrap): expand $HOMEBREW_PREFIX in brew-cask completion commands
body:
Installing a cask whose completions are generated through a wrapper command failed. The `ngrok` cask runs its own binary via `/usr/bin/env`, and its metadata names that binary with a `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX` placeholder in the arguments:

```
mise brew-cask:ngrok                   ✗ failed
mise ERROR brew-cask: failed to generate bash completions from /usr/bin/env: env: $HOMEBREW_PREFIX/Caskroom/ngrok/3.39.13,msmi2kd3cjc,a/ngrok: No such file or directory
```

mise already expanded the placeholder in the executable and in artifact targets, but passed the arguments through literally. It now expands `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX` in the arguments too. A path into the cask's own Caskroom version directory is redirected to the staging directory where the cask is held until installation finishes, so `mise bootstrap packages apply brew-cask:ngrok` can run the staged binary.

Tests: added a unit test for the argument expansion using the ngrok metadata shape. `cargo test --workspace --lib -- brew::cask` passes (365 tests). I did not run a real ngrok install.

title: fix(daemons): name the other checkout when a named port collides
body:
Named daemon ports (`ports.app = { auto = true, base = 5173 }`) were never part of what mise compares across checkouts, so a collision on one of them failed with pitchfork's message about whoever holds the port, usually Docker, instead of naming the other checkout. Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15533.

## Before

With `ports.app` and `ports.db` on a custom daemon, starting a second worktree that landed on the same slot as a running one:

```
pitchfork ERROR Daemon example-244-e02f25d92806ea0b/stack failed to start
✗ pitchfork: [...] port 5174 is already in use on 127.0.0.1 by process 'com.docker.backend' (PID: 37254)
```

The documented warning naming the daemon and port only fired for the primary `port`, and `mise env` gave no hint that a worktree on slot 259 resolves `app` to 5432, the port the primary checkout uses for `db`.

## After

- Named ports are recorded in the daemon's claims, so starting a daemon checks all of its ports against daemons other checkouts are running. The error now reads, for example, `daemon stack (ports.app) would use port 5174, in use by stack (ports.app) running in /…/example-116. Stop it, or declare the daemon again in a gitignored mise.local.toml with that port fixed (ports.<name> = <n>) …`. The start-failure hint for an automatic port that is taken also covers named ports.
- On load, mise warns when a linked worktree's slot moves one of a custom daemon's automatic ports onto the number the primary checkout uses for another of its automatic ports (`app` at 5173 and `db` at 5432 in a worktree on slot 259). It is a warning, not an error, because only that worktree is affected.

Not changed: how slots are chosen, and `mise.local.toml` still replaces a whole daemon declaration. The warning covers custom `run`/`task` daemons; presets and container daemons get the cross-checkout check but not the primary-collision warning.

## Testing

Unit tests cover recording and carrying named claims, and the slot-259 case (and that other slots and the primary are clear). Ran `cargo test -p mise -p mise-daemons --lib -- ports claim collision worktree` (102 passed) and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`. The cross-checkout start error needs a running pitchfork and was not exercised end to end.

title: fix(bootstrap): ignore brew-cask Caskroom directories Homebrew has no record of
body:
`bootstrap.packages` entries for casks whose installer creates its own directory in the Caskroom failed outright. With the `miniconda` cask, the conda root is installed to `Caskroom/miniconda/base`, next to the version directory, and mise counted it as a second installed version:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"brew-cask:miniconda" = "latest"
```

```
mise ERROR brew-cask:miniconda: Homebrew metadata exists with multiple Caskroom versions (base, py312_25.1.1-2); repair it with Homebrew
```

Because that error aborted the run, `mise bootstrap packages status` and `apply` failed for every other package while the cask was declared.

mise now counts only Caskroom directories that have a matching `.metadata/<version>` record, which is how Homebrew itself decides what is installed. `miniconda` reads as one installed version, and a real second version (one with a metadata record) still produces the "multiple Caskroom versions" error.

Tests: added a miniconda-shaped regression test and updated the existing Caskroom fixtures to include the `.metadata/<version>` records Homebrew writes. `cargo test --workspace --lib -- brew::cask` passes (365 tests). I did not run this against a real miniconda install.

title: fix(skills): expand a leading ~ in skills.dir
body:
Setting `skills.dir` to a path starting with `~` linked skills into a directory literally named `~` instead of the home directory:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings.skills]
dir = "~/.claude/skills"

`skills.dir` is now a `Path` setting, its docs mention the `~` form, and `skills_target` expands it. Because the expanded path is absolute, the check that spots a project and the home directory sharing one skills directory also matches it.

title: fix(dotfiles): skip unchanged files when applying a directory copy
body:
Fixes #15527.

## Problem

When a directory `copy` dotfile entry (or group) has one changed file, `mise dot apply` rewrote every file in the tree. Unchanged files got a new mtime and counted as written, so every `[history.reload]` glob under the target fired. That is costly for reload commands like `update-initramfs -u` or `udevadm control --reload`. The confirmation plan already skipped matching files, so the plan and the apply disagreed.

## Fix

The directory copy now skips an existing file whose content and mode already match its source, using the same check the plan uses. The file keeps its mtime and is not recorded as written.

```toml
[dotfile_groups.sys]
root = "sys"
target = "~/dst"
mode = "copy"

[history.reload]
"~/dst/a/**" = "echo RELOAD a"
"~/dst/b/**" = "echo RELOAD b"
```

Changing only `sys/a/x.conf` now runs only `RELOAD a`; `dst/b/y.conf` is untouched.

## Testing

Added a case to `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_apply_reload`: change one of two files, backdate the other, and assert only one reload runs and the other file's mtime is unchanged.

Not changed: a single-file `copy` entry goes through a different path (`replace_recorded`) that also rewrites on every apply. That was not part of this report.

title: fix(task): use the project root for env of file tasks in subdirectories
body:
File tasks grouped in a subdirectory of the task directory (for example `mise-tasks/sub/nested`) resolved `{{ config_root }}` and relative `_.file` paths in their `env` against the subdirectory instead of the project directory. `description`, `dir` and `MISE_CONFIG_ROOT` already pointed at the project, so a nested task saw two different roots.

Before, with `.env` in the project and a different `.env` in `mise-tasks/sub/`:

```console
$ mise run sub:nested   # env = {ROOT="{{config_root}}", _={file=".env"}}
root=<project>/mise-tasks/sub where=sub
```

After:

```console
root=<project> where=project
```

The same applies to `.mise-tasks`, `mise/tasks`, `.mise/tasks` and `.config/mise/tasks`. The root is now the nearest enclosing task directory's project, for any non-config file. Project configs (`mise.toml`, `config.toml`, `mise*.toml`) are excluded, so a `mise.toml` in a project under a directory named `tasks` keeps its own directory as its root.

Fixes the report in discussion #15546.

Validated with new unit tests for `config_root()` and the e2e test `test_task_nested_file_task_config_root`. No other e2e tests were run.

title: fix(lock): send the forge token when hashing private release assets
body:
`mise lock` failed with `401 Unauthorized` for `gitlab:` tools on a private or self-managed GitLab project, even though `mise install` downloaded the same asset fine. Closes #15550.

A GitLab release has no digest, so lock downloads the asset to hash it. On a private project the browser URL returns an HTML login page, so lock switched to the API asset URL and requested it with no `Authorization` header. The install path sends the forge token; the lock path did not. Private GitHub, GitHub Enterprise and Forgejo assets without a digest hit the same gap.

```toml
[tools]
"gitlab:mygroup/mytool" = { version = "2.2.3", api_url = "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4" }
```

Before: `mise lock` -> `401 Unauthorized` on `.../api/v4/projects/46/packages/generic/...`. After: the checksum download sends the GitLab token and the lockfile is written. No credentials are persisted.

The headers are resolved for the API asset URL when the platform entry is built, and are only sent when lock actually picks that URL. If the browser URL is reachable, no token goes to it.

Not covered: `additional_asset_patterns` artifacts are still hashed without headers.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes authenticated HTTP during lockfile generation for private forges, but mirrors install-time header logic and does not persist credentials in the lockfile.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`mise lock`** failing with **401** on private GitLab/GitHub/Forgejo releases that have no upstream digest: lock must download the asset to compute a checksum, but that path did not send the same forge **Authorization** headers **`mise install`** already uses.

> New tests cover both URL-selection paths. **`additional_asset_patterns`** still hash without headers (unchanged limitation).

### [`v2.10.0`](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/releases/tag/v2.10.0): : npm shim workspace flags, workspace-wide audit, and lockfile compatibility fixes

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/v2.9.0...v2.10.0)

The npm shim now handles npm's `--workspace`/`--workspaces`, `--audit`, and `--fund` flags. `aube audit` now checks every workspace package, and this release fixes several lockfile, resolver, and registry bugs.

##### Added

- **`--no-include-workspace-root`** ([#​1917](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1917), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): this hidden global flag leaves the workspace root out of recursive selections unless a selector names it directly. It overrides `includeWorkspaceRoot: true` and `--include-workspace-root`.
  ```sh
  aube -r --no-include-workspace-root run build
  ```

##### Fixed

- **npm `--workspace`/`--workspaces` in the npm shim** ([#​1916](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1916), [#​1917](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1917), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): the npm shim now translates these flags for `run`, `test`, `start`, `stop`, `restart`, and `exec`. Before, the flags reached the root script as arguments. A root script that called `npm run build --workspaces` then ran itself again and again. Like npm, `--workspaces` now skips the root unless you also pass `--include-workspace-root`. Arguments after `--` are passed through unchanged.
  ```text
  npm run build --workspaces     ->  aube -r --no-include-workspace-root run build
  npm run build -w @scope/child  ->  aube --filter @scope/child run build
  npm run build -w packages/child ->  aube --filter ./packages/child run build
  ```
- **npm `--audit`/`--fund` flags** ([#​1908](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1908), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): for `install`, `add`, `ci`, and `remove` and their aliases, the npm shim now drops `--audit`, `--no-audit`, `--fund`, `--no-fund`, and their `=<bool>` forms. Before, tools that pass these flags, such as the shadcn CLI, failed with `unknown option '--no-audit'`.

title: fix(install): leave read-only system global links alone
body:
A non-root `mise install` no longer fails when the user's global config selects a different version of a tool than the administrator's system config.

Before, with the system installs dir read-only and a user global config of `lychee = "0.24.1"` while the admin had set `0.24.2`, running `mise install dyff@1.12.0` exited 1:

```text
mise ERROR failed to rebuild runtime symlinks
failed to rebuild runtime symlinks for lychee in <system>/installs/lychee: not running as root and system_packages.sudo is disabled.
```

The `global` link added in 2026.10.8 is computed from the merged global and system config, so one user's config tried to retarget (or, when their pick was not in the system dir, remove) the link in a shared directory they cannot write. A shared install dir the user cannot write now keeps its existing `global` link; the administrator's own `mise install --system` still manages it.

Fixes #15520

## Testing

New e2e `test_install_system_global_link_read_only` (skipped as root); it fails on main and passes here.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes install-time runtime symlink behavior for shared/system directories and version pinning; incorrect logic could leave stale `global` links or still touch dirs users cannot write.
> 
> **Overview**
> Non-root **`mise install`** no longer errors when rebuild would retarget the **`global`** symlink in a **read-only shared/system installs directory** because the user's global config picks a different tool version than the administrator's system config.
> 
> **Shared install directories** now drive **`global`** from **`ConfigScope::SystemOnly`** (system config only), not the invoking user's global config. User-owned install dirs still use global-only scope.
> 
> When a shared dir is **not writable** and cannot be updated via **`system_packages.sudo`**, symlink rebuild **leaves the existing `global` target** instead of attempting a change that would fail the install. Additional logic preserves the administrator's link when the system-selected version is missing in that dir or only resolves outside it, and adds **`pin_in_dir`** to point at a version present in the shared tree.
> 
> **`ToolsetBuilder`** gains **`ConfigScope::SystemOnly`** so system config can be loaded in isolation. Regression coverage: e2e **`test_install_system_global_link_read_only`** (non-root).

title: feat(shim): one-line no-version error and opt-in shims.fallback_to_installed
body:
A shim run where no config selects its tool now fails with one line that names the fix, and a new opt-in setting makes it run the latest installed version instead.

## Why

In 1,312 Claude Code sessions on one machine since 2026-10-05, agents hit `No version is set for shim` 151 times in 89 sessions (most often `rg` 15, `cargo-deny` 14, `luau-lsp` 12, `fnox` 11, `actionlint` 9, `ruby` 9), and 149 of the 151 ran in a Claude Code worktree. Each hit cost a request and a retry with `mise x --`.

## Behavior

Before, a multi-line message listing a `mise use -g` line for every installed version. Now:

```
$ rtx-tiny
mise ERROR No version is set for shim: rtx-tiny. Run `mise use -g tiny@3.1.0` to set a default, or `mise x tiny@3.1.0 -- rtx-tiny` to run it once.
```

The version is the backend's own latest installed version (`Backend::latest_installed_version`), not a semver sort. `--verbose` adds the full list of installed versions.

New setting `shims.fallback_to_installed` (`MISE_SHIMS_FALLBACK_TO_INSTALLED`, default `false`):

```sh
mise settings shims.fallback_to_installed=true
```

With it on, the shim runs that same latest installed version (debug-logged). It only applies to a tool no config mentions; a configured tool whose version is missing or lacks the executable still fails as before, so a pinned version is never swapped.

## Alternatives considered

- **Fallback on by default**: rejected, it runs a version nobody chose and changes behavior for everyone. The one-line error already removes most of the retry cost.
- **Fallback to the global config / `mise use -g` automatically**: rejected, it writes config as a side effect.
- **Fallback to a pinned "default version" setting**: more control, but more surface; "latest installed" is enough for the measured cases. Can be added later.
- **Also fall back when a configured version is missing**: rejected, that is the case where silently running something else is most surprising.

## Testing

New e2e `test_shims_fallback_to_installed` (error text, `--verbose`, opt-in, configured tool not substituted) and two unit tests. `test_shim_active_version_lacks_bin`, `test_shims_fallback`, `test_shims_system_fallback` still pass; `mise run lint-fix` and `cargo clippy -p mise --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean. Docs: settings entry, `docs/dev-tools/shims.md`, `docs/errors.md`; `schema/mise.json` regenerated.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

 :::
 
+## Run an installed version when none is configured {#fallback-to-installed}
+
+A shim run in a directory where no config file selects its tool fails with
+`No version is set for shim`, and names the `mise use -g` and `mise x` commands
+that fix it, using an installed version. Set
+[`shims.fallback_to_installed`](/configuration/settings.html#shims.fallback_to_installed)
+to run the latest installed version instead:
+
+```sh
+mise settings shims.fallback_to_installed=true
+```
+
+It is off by default because the version it runs is one nobody chose. It never
+replaces a tool a config file does select: a pinned version that is missing
+still fails, as does a command named like a configured tool. It applies to Unix

title: fix(ui): keep demand's bright base16 colors bright
body:
Prompt descriptions, placeholders and error markers lose their bright-black/bright-red look with the base16 theme since demand 2.4.2 (#15516). They come out as plain black and red, which is hard to read on dark terminals, and `trusted / windows-unit` fails on `main` because of it.

demand 2.4.2 builds its base16 theme from named colors and marks the bright ones `intense` itself. mise's `name_ansi_colors` only knew the older `Ansi256(8..=15)` form: it found none, computed `intense = false`, and cleared the flag demand had set. It now keeps an `intense` flag that is already set, so it works with both demand versions.

Validation: `cargo test --workspace --lib -p mise-ui theme` passes against demand 2.4.2 (8 tests, including `base16_uses_named_colors_not_ansi256`, which is what fails on Windows CI). I did not rerun the failing Windows job.

title: fix(version): hide the update notice and hints from coding agents
body:
An agent running `mise version`, `mise -v` or `mise doctor` was told `mise WARN  mise version <N> available` and `To update, run mise self-update`. An agent can't act on that, and the lines stay in its context for the rest of the session. In a measurement of 1,312 Claude Code sessions since 2026-10-05, the notice reached an agent in 72 of them.

mise already detects agents (`mise-agent-env`, exposed as `env::AI_AGENT`, which also drives table truncation and progress style). With this change, when an agent is detected:

```console
$ mise version                      # a person: unchanged
2026.11.5 linux-x64 (...)
mise WARN  mise version 2026.12.0 available
mise WARN  To update, run mise self-update

$ CLAUDECODE=1 mise version         # an agent
2026.11.5 linux-x64 (...)
```

- The new-version notice and its self-update / packager instructions are not printed (`show_latest`, same gate as `disable_update_warning`).
- All `hint!` output is off under an agent (`hint_enabled` / `hint_would_display`). Hints already required both stdout and stderr to be a TTY, so this only affects an agent on a pty.
- `mise version --json` and the `warnings` entry in `mise doctor` / `doctor --json` are unchanged: those are explicit queries, not unprompted notices.

## Notices I looked at

Left alone, because an agent can act on them: deprecation warnings (`deprecated_at!`), trust errors, config errors and every other `warn!`/`error!`.

Hidden by the `hint!` change (all start with `hint`, all are for a person): `auto_update`, `optimized_mise_binary`, `optimized_mise_homebrew`, `python_compile`/`python_multi`/`python_precompiled`, `ruby_compile`/`ruby_precompiled`, `skills`, `raw_redactions`/`interactive_redactions`, `task_secrets_stdin`, `fnox_daemon_protocol`, `upgrade_auto_prune`, `system_packages_missing` and `tools_missing` (installed but missing / not activated). `tools_missing` is the one an agent could conceivably use; say so if you'd rather keep it.

Not touched: the stderr line in `mise doctor` is hidden but its entry in the doctor warnings list stays.

## Relation to #15403

None in code. #15403 (merged) adds an opt-in `summary` task output and deliberately doesn't select it for agents. This PR only touches the version notice and hints, not task output, so the two don't overlap or conflict. Making `summary` the default for agents would be a separate change.

## Validation

`mise run test:e2e test_version_update_hint` passes. It now asserts the notice and self-update line are absent under `AI_AGENT=test` and `CLAUDECODE=1`, `--json` still reports the version, and the notice is present with `AI_AGENT=0`. Clippy and the full suite were not run.

title: feat(task): show run history in tasks info and tasks ls --json
body:
A tool that already reads a task's definition can't tell how long the task usually takes. #15408 records every task run, but the numbers are only in `mise tasks history`, so an agent or script has to make a second call per task to decide whether to start a slow check.

`mise tasks info <task> --json` and each entry of `mise tasks ls --json` now carry a `history` field with the same summary as `mise tasks history --summary --json`:

```console
$ mise tasks info test --json | jq .history
{
  "task": "test",
  "runs": 10,
  "failures": 2,
  "median_ms": 62040,
  "last_ms": 58300,
  "last_status": "failed",
  "last_started_at": "2026-11-09T14:02:11Z"
}
```

`history` is `null` for a task that has never run, or when `task.history` is off and nothing was recorded.

## Behavior

- No new storage or settings. It reads the files #15408 writes, takes no lock, and treats a missing or unreadable file as no history.
- `tasks ls --json` reads the project's history once, not once per task.
- Text output is unchanged.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e test_task_history` covers the field in `tasks info` and `tasks ls`, including `null` for a task that never recorded a run.
- `cargo clippy -p mise --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Docs: the "See how long tasks take" section of `docs/tasks/running-tasks.md` describes the field. No settings or CLI help changed, so nothing needed regenerating.

title: docs: add a coding agents page with a Claude Code hook
body:
Coding agents run each command in a non-interactive shell, so `mise activate` in an rc file never applies and they have to wrap commands in `mise x --` or rely on shims. This adds a "Coding agents" docs page with a one-line Claude Code `SessionStart` hook that puts the current project's tools and `[env]` on the agent's PATH, plus notes on Codex, other agents and worktrees. No code changes.

```json
"command": "[ -n \"$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE\" ] && echo 'eval \"$(mise hook-env -s bash)\"' >> \"$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE\"; true"
```

## Why

Measured over 1,312 Claude Code sessions on jdx's machine since 2026-10-05:

- agents ran `mise x` / `mise exec` 2,772 times just to reach project tools
- `No version is set for shim` appeared 151 times in 89 sessions (lines starting with the error); 149 of them ran in a Claude Code worktree

jdx's own settings carry a homemade fix (a hook appending a line that sources `~/.zshenv` to `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`).

## What already existed

Shims, `mise activate --shims`, `mise env`, `mise hook-env`, and `mise exec`. Nothing agent-specific beyond the `mise-agent-env` detector, which only changes output behavior. I found no open issue or PR covering this.

## Alternatives considered

- **`mise env -s bash >> $CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`**: also works and is documented as the fixed-environment option, but it is evaluated once in the session's start directory and does not follow `cd`.
- **Shims on PATH**: documented as the fallback; they fail with `No version is set for shim` when the current directory's config does not select the tool.
- **New `mise env` format or command**: not needed, since `hook-env` in an env file is already one line, so docs are enough.

I chose `hook-env` because it re-evaluates before each command, tracks `cd`, and costs about 40 ms per call (5 runs in 0.2 s).

## Testing

In a scratch project with `[env] FOO` and `_.path = ["{{config_root}}/bin"]`, using mise 2026.11.0 in `env -i` bash and zsh:

- the sourced `hook-env` line makes the project tool and `FOO` available, drops them after `cd` to an unrelated directory, and restores them on return
- the static `mise env -s bash` variant sets both but keeps them after `cd`
- the hook command, run with `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` set, writes exactly the one line

Not tested: running Claude Code itself (I relied on its documented behavior of sourcing the file before each Bash command) and Codex. The page says so for Codex.

`hk run check --safe` (oxfmt, render-llms, markdownlint) and `mise run docs:build` pass.

+---
+description: "Put a project's mise tools and environment variables on the PATH of a coding agent's non-interactive shell, with a tested Claude Code hook."
+socialDescription: "Give coding agents a project's mise tools without wrapping every command in mise x."
+---
+
+# Coding agents
+
+A coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex runs each command in a
+non-interactive shell. `mise activate` in your `.zshrc` or `.bashrc` never runs
+there, so the agent does not get the project's tools or `[env]` unless it wraps
+the command in [`mise x --`](/cli/exec.html) or the shell finds
+[shims](/dev-tools/shims.html) on `PATH`.
+
+Both work, but they have costs. Wrapping every command is noisy and agents
+forget to do it. Shims resolve a tool from the directory the command runs in, so
+a tool that the current directory's config does not select fails with
+`No version is set for shim`.
+
+mise has no agent-specific mode. The pieces it already has are enough:
+`mise hook-env` is what `mise activate` runs before each
+prompt, and it works without a prompt. Running it before each command gives the
+agent the same `PATH` and variables that an activated interactive shell has.
+
+## Claude Code {#claude-code}
+
+Claude Code sources the file named by `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` before each Bash
+command it runs. Only `SessionStart`, `Setup`, `CwdChanged` and `FileChanged`
+hooks can write to it. Add this to
+`~/.claude/settings.json`, or to a project's `.claude/settings.json`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "hooks": {
+    "SessionStart": [
+      {
+        "hooks": [
+          {
+            "type": "command",
+            "command": "[ -n \"$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE\" ] && echo 'eval \"$(mise hook-env -s bash)\"' >> \"$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE\"; true"
+          }
+        ]
+      }
+    ]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The hook appends one line:
+
+```sh
+eval "$(mise hook-env -s bash)"
+```
+
+Use `-s zsh` if Claude Code runs commands in zsh. The line runs before every
+command, so it follows the directory the agent is in when a command starts:
+after the agent runs `cd subproject`, its next command gets that project's
+tools, and leaving removes them. It does not refresh in the middle of one
+command, so in `cd subproject && node --version` the `node` is still the
+parent project's. When nothing changed since the last command, `hook-env`
+prints nothing and costs a few milliseconds.
+
+The line must be able to find `mise`. The installer can leave `~/.local/bin` off
+the `PATH` of a shell that does not run `mise activate`, which includes the
+agent's. If `command -v mise` fails there, write the absolute path into the
+hook instead, for example `eval "$(~/.local/bin/mise hook-env -s bash)"`.
+
+If you prefer a fixed environment for the whole session, write the output of
+[`mise env`](/cli/env.html) once instead. It is evaluated at session start, in
+the directory the session started in, and does not follow `cd`:
+
+```sh
+mise env -s bash >> "$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE"
+```
+
+Either way, the agent can then run `node`, `cargo` or `python` directly, and
+the project's `[env]` variables are set.
+
+mise does not install missing tools on its own here. Run
+[`mise install`](/cli/install.html) in the project first, or have the agent do
+so. A config that mise does not [trust](/cli/trust.html) is not loaded.
+
+## Codex {#codex}
+
+Codex runs commands through your login shell by default, so the tools in your
+login profile apply. Add [shims to your login profile](/dev-tools/shims.html#how-to-add-mise-shims-to-path)
+and run `mise install` in the project. Shims are weaker than the Claude Code
+setup: they put a project's `[env]` variables only on the tool they launch and
+its children, so `echo "$FOO"` in the shell still sees nothing, and a tool the
+current directory's config does not select fails with `No version is set for
+shim`. Check
+Codex's own documentation for how it selects the shell, because mise cannot
+change that. This setup has not been tested here the way the Claude Code hook
+has.
+
+## Other agents
+
+Any agent that sources a file before each command, or lets you point its shell
+at an rc file, can use the same line. A command that only runs once at session
+start is not enough on its own, because it changes just that process and its
+children, and later commands do not inherit it. That is why the Claude Code
+hook writes to a file instead of running `hook-env` itself. If the agent offers
+neither, the fallback is [shims on `PATH`](/ide-integration.html#adding-shims-to-path-default-shell)
+in the login profile, with the limits described above.
+
+## Worktrees {#worktrees}
+
+Agents often work in a git worktree, such as `.claude/worktrees/<name>`. The
+`hook-env` line needs nothing per worktree, because it reads the config of
+whichever directory the command runs in. Shims are the likelier trap here: a
+worktree is often where `No version is set for shim` appears, since the shim
+resolves tools from the worktree's own config.
+
+Installed tools live in mise's data directory, not in the worktree, so a new
+worktree does not reinstall them.
+
+## Related
+
+- [AI assistants (MCP)](/mcp.html) lets an assistant read a project's tasks and
+  config and run tasks through `mise mcp`.
+- [Shims](/dev-tools/shims.html) explains the trade-offs between shims and
+  `PATH` activation.

title: fix(upgrade): keep registry options out of mise.toml on --bump
body:
`mise upgrade --bump` and `mise use` no longer write a registry entry's own options into `mise.toml`.

Reported in discussion #15513: with `jactionlint = "2.4.0"` in `mise.toml`, `mise upgrade --bump jactionlint` rewrote the line as

```toml
jactionlint = { version = "2.5.0", workflow = "release.yaml" }
```

`workflow` is the packslip signer policy from the registry entry. The user never set it, and the registry applies it on its own. The rewrite skipped the "same as the registry defaults, so write a bare version" shortcut because that check only knew inline `[k=v]` registry options, not the structured `options = {...}` table packslip entries use (#14947). Any registry tool with such a table was affected.

Now the line stays `jactionlint = "2.5.0"`. An option the file already spells out (for example an explicit `workflow = "release.yaml"`) is kept.

`mise.lock` is unchanged: packslip's lock options are `variant`, `ignore_requirements` and `trust`, and never included `workflow`. Whether a locked entry should pin the signer is a separate question and not part of this fix.

Validation: new `e2e/cli/test_upgrade_bump_registry_options` (fails before the fix), related upgrade/use e2e tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, `mise run lint-fix`.

Closes nothing; answers discussion #15513.

> 
> **Overview**

title: fix(bootstrap): read snap list in the C locale
body:
`mise bootstrap` no longer tries to reinstall snaps that are already installed when the system language is not English.

`snap list` was run with `LC_ALL=C`, but snap ignores `LC_ALL` for its translations and reads `LC_MESSAGES` and `LANG`. With `LANG=fr_FR.UTF-8` the header comes out as `Nom Version Révision …`, so `parse_snap_list` (which looks for a line starting with `Name `) found no installed snaps:

```console
$ mise bootstrap
snap: install whatsie? Yes
mise $ sudo snap install whatsie
le snap "whatsie" est déjà installé, voir « snap help refresh »
```

Now `snap list` also gets `LC_MESSAGES=C`, so the header is always English. Only snap is affected; the other managers use glibc/gettext tools, where `LC_ALL=C` is honored.

Validation: `cargo test --workspace --lib -p mise-system-packages snap` passes (23 tests). I did not reproduce under a French locale with a real snapd.

Fixes #15515. Thanks to @nahoj for the report and the diagnosis.

Co-authored-by: nahoj <469017+nahoj@users.noreply.github.com>

That keeps the **`Name …`** table header English so **`parse_snap_list`** still sees installed snaps when the user’s locale is not English—fixing mistaken reinstall attempts during **`mise bootstrap`**.

title: fix(config): keep boolean and numeric tool options unquoted when rewriting a tool
body:
Rewriting a tool entry in `mise.toml` (`mise upgrade --bump`, `mise use`) quoted boolean and numeric backend options, so `uvx = true` came back as `uvx = "true"` ([discussion 15514](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15514)).

Before:

```toml
"pipx:commit-check/commit-check" = { version = "2.19.4", uvx = true }
```

after `mise upgrade --bump`:

```toml
"pipx:commit-check/commit-check" = { version = "v2.20.0", uvx = "true" }
```

Backend options are stored as strings, and the writer emitted them as such. Now, when the entry already holds a boolean, integer or float for an option whose stored value spells the same thing, that original value is written back. A string the user wrote (`name = "true"`) stays a string. Options newly added from the command line are unchanged.

The `v` in `v2.20.0` is not changed here: `owner/repo` pipx packages are installed from git, and `v2.20.0` is the real tag.

Covered by a new `replace_versions` unit test; the existing `replace_versions` tests pass and clippy is clean.

> **Low Risk**
> Localized to TOML config serialization during tool version replacement; behavior is additive preservation with extensive unit tests and no auth or runtime install changes.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a regression where rewriting tool entries in `mise.toml` (e.g. `mise use`, `mise upgrade --bump`) serialized backend options as strings, turning booleans and numbers like `uvx = true` into `uvx = "true"`.
> 
> **`replace_versions` and `update_explicit_tool_options`** now read existing boolean, integer, and float option values from the document before writing, and reuse those scalars when the stored backend value is logically the same (while leaving intentional strings such as `name = "true"` quoted). For tool version arrays, scalars are matched per entry by unique version or by index when counts match or versions repeat.
>

title: perf(task): avoid repeated realpath calls resolving the task config cascade
body:
## Summary
- After installing, `mise upgrade` scans every tracked config to decide which old versions are safe to remove (`mise prune` runs the same scan). With ~930 tracked configs that scan took 12-13s in a release build, and nothing was printed, so `mise up` looked hung.
- Profiling the release binary showed ~97% of the scan inside `cascaded_task_config_for_dir`. It runs once per directory and checked **every** config file's root with `file::same_file` and `file::path_starts_with_resolved`, which both call `realpath`. `task_tool_requests` calls it twice per tracked config (task includes and excludes), so ~900 configs means over a million `realpath` calls (about 10s of system time on macOS).
- Resolve through the existing `desymlink_path_cached` instead, and apply the cheap root check before `is_global_config`. The selection logic is unchanged: a root is kept if it is not the directory itself (lexically or after resolving) and the directory is under it (lexically or after resolving).

## Measurements
`mise prune --dry-run` (same scan), release build, ~930 tracked configs, macOS:
- before (installed 2026.11.4): real 12.4-13.0s, user 4.1s, **sys 9.8s**
- after: real 2.3-4.4s, user 2.6s, **sys 1.2s**

Debug build, same machine: sys 11s -> 2s, user 19s -> 14s.

The scan is still quadratic in the number of tracked configs; computing the sorted roots once per config set rather than once per directory would remove the rest, but this keeps the change small.

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run test:e2e`: test_task_config_dir_inheritance, test_task_config_precedence, test_task_excludes, test_task_config_includes_templates, test_task_global_config_dedup, test_task_global_config_root, test_task_includes_glob, test_task_artifact_cache_input_groups, test_task_config_shell, test_task_monorepo_aliases, test_task_info_monorepo, and the cli/test_prune* tests (38 of 40 pass)
- [ ] `cli/test_prune_tool_stub` (GNU `touch -d`) and `cli/test_prune_snapshot_keeps_secrets_out` (GNU `stat -c`) fail on macOS; unrelated

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Performance-only refactor of root filtering with preserved selection rules and broad task-config e2e coverage; worst case is incorrect task include/exclude inheritance if path equivalence checks diverge.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`cascaded_task_config_for_dir`** no longer resolves every config root with **`same_file`** / **`path_starts_with_resolved`** on each pass. It resolves the target directory once via **`desymlink_path_cached`**, compares roots with cached resolutions and lexical **`starts_with`** where appropriate, and defers the **`is_global_config`** filter until after the cheaper checks.
> 
> This targets the hot path during **`mise prune`** / **`mise upgrade`** scans over hundreds of tracked configs (each directory × every root), cutting repeated **`realpath`** work without changing which roots participate in task config cascading.
> 
>
