title: fix(install): clean up after a failed install
body:
A failed install no longer leaves files behind in two cases.

**A repo that is not a plugin.** Running `mise use -g gurgeous/tennis` treats the repo as an asdf plugin and clones it into `~/.local/share/mise/plugins/gurgeous-tennis`. The repo has no `bin/list-all`, so the install fails, but the whole clone (about 8 MB of source) stayed in the plugins directory. mise now removes the clone and says why:

```
gurgeous-tennis is not an asdf or vfox plugin: it has no bin/list-all or metadata.lua. To install a tool from a GitHub repo's releases, use the github: backend
```

Reported in [discussion 15508](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15508).

**The per-version cache directory.** A failed install removed the install and download directories but left `~/.cache/mise/<tool>/<version>`. It is now removed too, but only once the install directory itself is gone. Nothing can resume from it, because it is wiped at the start of every install attempt. `always_keep_install` skips it, as it skips the rest of the cleanup.

New e2e test `test_plugin_install_not_a_plugin`; `test_aqua_failed_install_cleanup` now also asserts the cache directory is gone. The cache assertion fails without the fix.

title: fix(env): stop an undefined env field from listing every environment variable name
body:
An undefined `{{ env.X }}` in a template no longer prints the name of every environment variable.

Before, a typo like this in `mise.toml`:

```toml
[env]
X = "{{ env.NOPE }}"
```

failed with `Field `NOPE` is not defined. Available fields: COLORTERM, EDITOR, HOME, … (78 names)`. That is about 2 KB per error, it buries the actual message, and it puts the names of variables such as `*_TOKEN` and `*_KEY` into terminal output, CI logs and bug reports. In an activated shell `mise hook-env` runs at every prompt, so the list was printed after every command.

Now the error is:

```
Field `NOPE` is not defined in `env`. For an optional variable use `get_env(name="NOPE", default="")` or `env.NOPE | default(value="")`.
 --> __tera_one_off:1:8
```

Other objects keep tera's list (`{{ vars.nope }}` still says `Available fields: a`), since it helps there.

tera does not say which object a missing field was looked up on, so the list is compared with the keys of `env` in the context and replaced only when they match. This applies to every template mise renders, including tasks.

Closes #15502 (discussion).

## Test plan

- unit test `test_undefined_env_field_does_not_list_env_names`
- e2e test `env/test_env_undefined_field`

title: feat(bootstrap): add soft_resource_limits and hard_resource_limits to launchd agents
body:
launchd starts LaunchAgents with a 256 open-file soft limit, so a server declared in `[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents]` that holds many connections runs out of descriptors under load. The only workaround was wrapping the program in `/bin/sh -c "ulimit -n 10240; exec ..."`.

Agents now accept `soft_resource_limits` and `hard_resource_limits`, written to the plist as `SoftResourceLimits` and `HardResourceLimits`:

```toml
[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents.proxy]
program = "~/.local/bin/proxy"
keep_alive = true
soft_resource_limits = { number_of_files = 10240 }
hard_resource_limits = { number_of_files = 65536 }
```

The keys are launchd's nine limits in snake case (`core`, `cpu`, `data`, `file_size`, `memory_lock`, `number_of_files`, `number_of_processes`, `resident_set_size`, `stack`), and only the ones you set are written. An empty table, or a soft limit above the hard limit for the same key, is an error: setrlimit refuses that and launchd only logs it, so the agent would otherwise start with default limits.

This is the implementation from @disintegrator's branch on their fork (commit 99aa60501, authorship preserved), plus a small docs trim. `[services]` user services are unchanged.

Fixes #15507

title: feat(bootstrap): pick one package manager for unprefixed bootstrap.packages keys
body:
`[bootstrap.packages]` can now share one config across machines that use different package managers. A key without a `manager:` prefix installs through exactly one manager instead of needing a declaration per distribution.

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
git = "latest"
fish = "latest"
openssl = { names = { apt = "libssl-dev", dnf = "openssl-devel" } }
```

On Ubuntu `git` uses apt even though the built-in Homebrew manager also runs there. On Fedora it uses dnf, on macOS brew, on Windows winget.

- mise picks the first manager that is available and allowed by `system_packages.managers`. The default order is `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `zypper`, `apk`, `brew`, `winget`, `scoop`, `choco`.
- The new `system_packages.prefer` setting replaces that order, for example `["apt", "dnf", "pacman", "brew"]`. The list names the only candidates.
- The choice depends only on which managers are available, never on what their repositories contain. An install failure is an error and does not switch managers.
- The new `names` entry option gives the package name per manager. A manager not listed uses the key.
- Prefixed keys such as `"apt:git"` behave as before. `"latest"` keeps its meaning: any installed version satisfies it, and upgrades stay a separate command.
- If no candidate is available, mise warns and skips the entry. `MISE_DEBUG=1` logs the selected manager and the reason.

`status` lists an unprefixed key that no manager can take as `skipped` (manager `-`, or `unprefixed` in `--json`). If two unprefixed keys resolve to one package with a different state or version, mise warns and keeps the one that installs it. Not in this PR: a per-package preference override (use an explicit prefix), and a fallback when a package is missing from a repository.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14802

title: fix(activate): complete mise subcommands in Nushell when activation is on
body:
With `mise activate nu` set up, pressing Tab after `mise ` in Nushell offered file paths instead of mise subcommands, even after installing the completion script with `mise completion nu --install`. Only `^mise <Tab>` worked, and `^` skips the activation wrapper.

`mise activate nu` defines `mise` as a Nushell command. Nushell consults the external completer that `mise completion nu` installs only for external commands, so it never sees `mise <Tab>`. The wrapper now carries a completer of its own, backed by the same `mise __complete_word__ --shell nu` protocol the completion script uses:

```nu
def "nu-complete mise" [context: string] { ... }
export def --env --wrapped main [command?: string@"nu-complete mise", --help, ...rest: string@"nu-complete mise"] { ... }
```

After this change, activation alone completes `mise` subcommands and arguments, with descriptions. Before Nushell 0.116, a wrapped command offers no flags (`mise install --<Tab>` shows only `--help`); on 0.116 they complete too, and `^mise` plus the completion script covers older versions. Where mise says a path belongs (and offers no candidates), the completer returns `null` so Nushell falls back to file completion. `mise completion nu --install` is still needed for `^mise` and, before 0.116, for flags; the Nushell section of the shell setup docs says so.

Fixes #15500.

## Testing

- Loaded the generated completer in Nushell 0.115.1 against a real mise: `mise ins` completes to `install`, `install-into` and `installs`; `mise install ` and `mise x -- ` return candidate tables. This also caught that `char --unicode 1` is invalid, so the marker is written as `"\u{1}"`.
- Updated the `hook_init` snapshot (`cargo test --lib shell::nushell` passes) and added e2e assertions to `test_completion_nu`, including a block that runs the completer under Nushell when `nu` is on PATH; I did not run the e2e test here.
- Also drove Tab through Nushell 0.116.1's completion engine in a pty: `mise ins` and `mise install --` both complete. If the mise executable can no longer run, the completer returns `null` and Nushell falls back to files.
- Not tested on Windows, the reporter's platform.

title: feat(daemons): add named ports to custom daemons
body:
Follows up https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15496.

A `run` or `task` daemon can now name more than one port, the way presets and containers already can. Before, `ports.<name>` on a custom daemon was forwarded to pitchfork and silently ignored, so a Docker Compose stack that publishes several ports needed one placeholder daemon per port.

```toml
[daemons.stack]
run = "docker compose up"
ports.app = { auto = true, base = 8080 }
ports.db = { auto = true, base = 5432 }
ports.admin = 9000

[env]
APP_PORT = "{{ env.STACK_APP_PORT }}"
DB_PORT = "{{ env.STACK_DB_PORT }}"
```

The primary checkout gets `8080` and `5432`. Each linked worktree adds the same slot to both, so `mise env` and `mise exec` give every checkout its own ports before anything starts. Variables are `<DAEMON>_<NAME>_PORT`; a fixed integer is used as written.

- An allocated port needs its own `base`, since a custom daemon has no preset default. Leaving it out is an error naming the key.
- The slot comes from the daemon's `port = { auto = true }` if set, otherwise from the project root, as for presets.
- Named ports join the existing collision checks and the daemon's expected ports.
- Presets, containers and daemons without `ports` behave as before.

Not included: an `[env]` template function for ports with no daemon. It would skip the collision check that daemon registration provides.

Tested with a unit test, the `test_daemons_named_ports` e2e (primary, linked worktree, missing `base`), the schema conformance test, and clippy.

title: feat(task): add mise run --multi to pick several tasks from a menu
body:
`mise run` with no task opens a picker, but it can only run one task. To run a handful, you had to type them out with `:::`. `mise run --multi` opens the same picker as a checklist:

```sh
mise run --multi          # check tasks, Enter runs them
mise run --multi --all    # list tasks from every project in the monorepo
```

Space checks a task, `/` filters, and Enter runs the checked tasks as if they were named with `:::` (parallel unless one depends on another, with `-j` and the other `mise run` settings applying as usual). At least one task must be checked. Without a terminal it fails with `--multi requires an interactive terminal`. It conflicts with a task name and with `--affected`, like `--all`.

This is a flag on `mise run` rather than a new top-level command, so a project task named `select` (or anything else) keeps working.

Based on the proof of concept in discussion #15474 by @AdrianDC, who is credited as co-author.

Tested with a new e2e test (`test_task_run_multi`) that drives the checklist through a pty, plus clippy with `-D warnings`.

title: fix(packslip): find releases past unrelated ones in busy monorepos
body:
`packslip:` could not install or resolve releases in a monorepo that publishes several components, because release discovery stopped at the first stable release it saw, even when that release belonged to an unrelated component.

```sh
mise install packslip:github.com/tuist/tuist@4.215.0
# before: github.com/tuist/tuist has no release 4.215.0 carrying packslip.sigstore.json
# after:  installs 4.215.0
```

4.215.0 sat on page 4 of the repository's release listing, past the unrelated releases the listing stopped at. `latest` was affected too: the newest release was too young for the minimum release age, and the older eligible ones were never fetched.

- A pinned version is now looked up by its exact tag (`4.215.0`, then `v4.215.0`) instead of searching the recent-release listing. Other tag prefixes fall back to the asset-filtered catalog.
- Asset-filtered discovery (used for `latest`) reads up to the same 10-page budget as the release mirror rather than stopping at the first stable release. GitHub's anonymous API rejects results past the first 1000.
- Cached listings that may have been truncated are invalidated.
- Manifest verification and minimum-release-age checks are unchanged.

Regression tests cover a matching release on page 4 that discovery must keep, a pinned lookup of a release absent from the recent listing (bare, `v`-prefixed and custom-prefixed tags), draft exclusion and the page-budget boundary. `mise-util` github tests and the packslip tests pass, and clippy and fmt are clean.

Fixes #15469. Based on the patch and analysis by @pepicrft in that issue.

title: perf(task): skip directories that no source or output can come from
body:
Task freshness checks no longer read directories that can't hold a source or an output. In a pnpm monorepo, `sources = ["packages/*/src/**/*"]` made every `mise run` read each `packages/*/node_modules` tree (the reporter measured about 3 million files walked for 2,783 real ones), and a `!**/node_modules/**` entry never shortened the walk.

```toml
[tasks.build]
sources = ["packages/*/src/**/*"]           # no longer enters packages/*/node_modules
# or
sources = ["**/*.ts", "!**/node_modules/**"] # no longer enters node_modules at all
outputs = ["dist", "!dist/.vite"]           # no longer enters dist/.vite
```

The files mise selects are unchanged; only the directories it reads shrink.

- A directory is skipped when its name fails the pattern component at its depth, for the components before the first `**`. This restores the behavior before 2026.9.2.
- A directory is skipped when a `!` entry excludes everything below it and no later entry could include something there again. In `sources` only entries ending in `/**` qualify (`!**/node_modules` excludes just the paths it matches). In `outputs` every `!` entry qualifies, since each already covers its subtree.
- Entries the pruner can't read with certainty (character classes, escapes) never skip a directory.
- A pattern whose matches all sit in skipped directories still counts as matched, so "output matched no files" results don't change.

Applies to the sources freshness check, the output hash and mtime checks, and the artifact cache (output roots and the archive it writes). `task_source_files()` and the post-run "output exists" check still walk without pruning, to keep the "no source resolved" warning unchanged.

Tested with unit tests for the pruner rules and walkers, a new e2e test using an unreadable `node_modules` directory, the existing task e2e tests (30 pass), and clippy. I did not time the issue's repro.

Fixes #15466. Thanks to @2chanhaeng for the report and the fork branch this follows.

title: feat(dot): add history.lock_wait to wait longer for a running history operation
body:
A mutating `mise dot` command waits 30 seconds for the history operation lock, then fails with `another history operation is running`. A script that needs its own checkpoint (with a description, label or task id) had to retry in a shell loop, because the watcher records an unlabeled change but not the checkpoint the command asked for.

The new `history.lock_wait` setting (env `MISE_HISTORY_LOCK_WAIT`, default `30s`) sets how long a command waits:

```sh
MISE_HISTORY_LOCK_WAIT=5m mise dot save --description "before upgrade" # waits up to 5 minutes
MISE_HISTORY_LOCK_WAIT=0 mise dot save                                # fails at once if the lock is held
```

- Values above `1h` count as `1h`; an unparseable value warns and keeps the default 30s.
- The command still takes the lock itself, so it does not poll and then race the watcher.
- `mise dot watch` and `mise dot recover` never wait, whatever the setting says. They already pass a zero wait explicitly, so an exported `MISE_HISTORY_LOCK_WAIT` cannot stall the watcher.
- Applies to every operation that waits on the lock, including the end-of-run wait of a bootstrap that starts tracking, and `bootstrap --adopt --replace-history`.

Based on the idea and branch by @zachbornheimer in discussion #15473, who is co-author. This takes a setting instead of a `--lock-wait` flag, so no process-global state and no CLI page regeneration are needed.

Validation: new e2e `test_dotfiles_lock_wait` (a hook holds the lock; `0` fails, `60s` succeeds once it is released, a bad value warns) passes; a unit test covers parsing and the 1h cap; workspace clippy with `-D warnings` is clean. Other dotfiles e2e tests were not run.

title: fix(backend): install tools without command wrappers on PATH
body:
`mise install cargo:<crate>` failed for anyone whose config wraps cargo with mbx (what `mbx setup` writes):

```toml
[wrappers.cargo]
command = "mbx"
env = { MBX_CARGO_SHIM_MODE = "1" }
```

mise put the `command-wrappers/bin` dir on PATH for the `cargo install` it runs, so mbx took over and exited with `could not find the real Cargo after excluding ...`. Ordinary `cargo` calls through the wrapper were fine.

Installs now run without command wrappers on PATH, so `cargo install` reaches the real cargo. Running `cargo`, `mise exec` and `mise run` still go through wrappers. The change is in `Toolset::env_with_path_without_tools`, which the cargo, npm, pipx and aube backends build their install environment from. Preinstall hooks and `dependency_env` use it too, so they also run without wrappers.

Fixes jdx/mr-boxington#919.

## Testing

New e2e `test_cargo_install_ignores_wrappers` wraps cargo with a command that always fails and checks that the install still succeeds. `test_command_wrappers` and `test_command_wrappers_install_provider` still pass. I did not confirm the new test fails without the fix.

title: fix(ui): keep prompt options readable on light terminals
body:
Interactive prompts, such as the `mise run` task picker, were hard to read on a light terminal. Unselected options came out as pale grey on white.

The default `color_theme` was `auto`, which picks `base16` only when `COLORFGBG` reports a light background. Many terminals, including GNOME Terminal and other VTE-based ones, don't set it, so they fell back to the `charm` theme's near-white grey options. And `base16` itself drew unselected options in ANSI white, which light themes show as pale grey.

The default `color_theme` is now `base16`, built from the terminal's named colors (not 256-color values) so it follows the terminal's palette. Unselected options and their markers, and prompt help text, use the terminal's own text color. Titles, the cursor and checked options keep their roles and colors.

```toml
[settings]
color_theme = "auto"   # the previous default: base16 on a detected light background, else charm
```

- **Visible change on dark terminals:** the default prompt look moves from `charm` to `base16` (cyan titles, yellow cursor, green checked options). Set `color_theme = "charm"` (or `"auto"`) to keep the old look.
- **`auto` is unchanged:** it still detects a light background from `COLORFGBG`, and uses the improved `base16` there. `default` and an unknown value mean `base16`.
- **Task output prefixes:** the issue also asked for the dim and bright task-prefix colors to be dropped. I left those alone, since they come from the terminal's palette.
- **Tests:** unit tests cover theme selection, no `Ansi256` colors in `base16`, and the default text color for unselected options and help keys. Clippy with `-D warnings` passes.
- **Not verified:** I haven't looked at it on a real light terminal.
- **Upstream:** the same `base16` fix for the `demand` crate is in jdx/demand#270. Until it ships, mise applies it on top of demand's `base16` in `mise-ui`.

Fixes #15472

title: fix(http): keep staging directory names under NAME_MAX for long cache keys
body:
Fixes #15483.

## Problem

Installing Yarn 2+ from a `package.json` whose `packageManager` carries a Corepack checksum (`yarn@4.10.3+sha512...`) fails with `File name too long (os error 63)` whenever mise's process ID has 5 or more digits, which is common on workstations:

```sh
cat > package.json <<'JSON'
{"name":"repro","packageManager":"yarn@4.10.3+sha512.c38cafb5c7bb273f3926d04e55e1d8c9dfa7d9c3ea1f36a4868fa028b9e5f72298f0b7f401ad5eb921749eb012eb1c3bb74bf7503df3ee43fd600d14a018266f"}
JSON
MISE_IDIOMATIC_VERSION_FILE_ENABLE_TOOLS=yarn mise install yarn
```

## Cause

The `http:` backend's cache key for this install is 226 bytes (three 64-char hashes plus labels). The staging directory was named by appending a prefix, the pid and a 13-digit millisecond timestamp to that key, which reaches 256 bytes with a 5-digit pid and exceeds the 255-byte `NAME_MAX` on ext4 and APFS.

## Fix

Staging directory names now embed a hash of the cache key instead of the key itself, so they are a fixed ~100 bytes. This covers both the install-path and cache extraction sites. Finished install and cache directory names are unchanged, so nothing already installed is re-extracted.

A regression test checks the staging name stays under the limit for a 226-byte key.

> **Overview**
> Fixes **filesystem `NAME_MAX` (255-byte) failures** when the HTTP backend builds very long cache keys (e.g. Yarn via Corepack checksums) and then creates staging directories by appending pid and timestamp to the full key.
>

title: fix(deps): update rmcp to 3.9.0 for RUSTSEC-2026-0462
body:
## Problem

`cargo deny check` now fails on every PR's lint job: `rmcp` 3.8.0 is affected by [RUSTSEC-2026-0462](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0462). Its built-in Streamable HTTP clients read response bodies into memory with no size limit. mise only uses rmcp's stdio server (`mise mcp`), not those clients, so it is not exploitable here, but the advisory check blocks merging.

## Change

`cargo update -p rmcp --precise 3.9.0` (`Cargo.toml` already allows `"3"`). Only the `rmcp` and `rmcp-macros` lock entries change, plus rmcp's new `sha2` dependency. I dropped the unrelated `windows-sys` reshuffling `cargo update` also produced.

`cargo deny check` passes and `cargo check --locked -p mise` builds.

title: fix(brew): accept zap :not_required in tap cask metadata
body:
Casks that declare `zap :not_required`, such as Entire's, no longer fail to preview or install when mise has to evaluate the tap's Ruby source.

```sh
mise bootstrap packages apply --dry-run brew-cask:entireio/tap/entire
# before: wrong number of arguments (given 1, expected 0) (ArgumentError)
#         from Casks/entire.rb:44:in 'block in <main>'
```

The tap metadata shim only accepted keyword directives for `zap`. It now also accepts the positional `:not_required` exemption and records it as an empty zap list, the same as Homebrew's JSON. Keyword directives such as `zap trash: ...` are unchanged, and any other positional argument still raises.

A new test evaluates both `zap :not_required` and `zap trash: ...` through the shim.

Fixes #15471

Thanks to @cdenihan for the report and the proposed fix.

title: fix(env): quote values in `mise env --dotenv` so they read back unchanged
body:
`mise env --dotenv > .env` wrote every value raw, so a value containing ` #` was cut short when the file was read back, and a value with a newline made the whole file fail to parse.

With this config:

```toml
[env]
HASH = "a #b"
ML = "line1\nline2"
```

`mise env --dotenv` used to print:

```
HASH=a #b
ML=line1
line2
```

It now prints:

```
HASH="a #b"
ML="line1\nline2"
```

Values that are already safe unquoted (such as `FOO=bar`) are unchanged. Quoting comes from the existing `mise_dotenv::render_var`, which is the inverse of the parser `_.file` uses. A variable name the dotenv syntax cannot represent now produces an error instead of a broken file.

The e2e test writes `mise env --dotenv` to a file, loads it with `_.file`, and checks each value against `mise env --json`.

Literal `$` in a value is double-quoted with the dollar escaped, because `_.file` expands dollar references. The output is quoted for mise's own dotenv syntax; tools that do not interpret quotes, such as Docker `--env-file`, receive it literally, and the `--dotenv` help now says so.

Fixes #15484

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2-1-317.*

> **Low Risk**
> Output-format fix for `mise env --dotenv` with clearer errors; low risk aside from consumers expecting unquoted raw values.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise env --dotenv`** no longer prints raw `KEY=value` lines. It now renders assignments with **`mise_dotenv::render_var_for_substitution`**, which quotes and escapes values (including `#`, newlines, quotes, backslashes, and **`$`**) so loading the file via **`_.file`** returns the same values. Plain safe values like `FOO=bar` stay unquoted.
> 
> The dotenv crate gains **`render_value_for_substitution`** / **`render_var_for_substitution`** on top of the existing render helpers: values containing **`$`** are forced into quoted form with escaped dollars so mise’s substitution reader does not expand references. Rendering is done for all entries before anything is printed, so an invalid key or value fails with an error instead of a partial file.

> Help text for **`--dotenv`** notes that quoting targets mise’s parser; tools such as Docker **`--env-file`** may see literal quotes. E2e coverage checks dotenv → **`_.file`** round-trip for tricky values and literal **`$`** when shell expansion is off.

title: feat(upgrade): show progress while checking tracked configs
body:
## Summary
- After installing, `mise upgrade` resolves every config tracked on the machine to decide which old versions are safe to uninstall. With hundreds of tracked configs this takes a while and printed nothing, so the command looked hung.
- Add a `checking tracked configs` progress line around that step.

## Test plan
- [x] `mise run test:e2e test_upgrade_progress_summary test_lockfile_upgrade_prune test_upgrade_latest_stale test_upgrade_parallel_failure`
- [ ] `cli/test_upgrade` fails locally at its `ubi:bazelbuild/buildtools` GitHub install step, and also fails on main; the new progress line prints correctly before that point

Related: the pause itself is addressed by the vfox legacy-filenames cache PR.

+# `mise dot files` shows what is tracked in a directory
+
+This release adds `mise dot files` to show which files in a directory are tracked, and a `status.show_env_ignore` setting to hide variables from the status line. It also lets dot commands accept relative paths, stops warning when you save dotfiles by hand, and fixes downloads that failed because `~/.netrc` held a stale login.
+
+## Added
+
+- **`mise dot files`.** Lists the files and subdirectories in a directory and shows the state of each one, so you no longer have to work out how `[dotfiles]` entries, their `exclude`/`include` lists and `[history] exclude` apply. The possible states are:
+  - `tracked`: saved to history. The row shows the entry that covers it and whether it autosaves.
+  - `excluded`: covered by an entry, but a rule leaves it out. The row names the rule.
+  - `omitted`: selected, but capture skips it, for example a file that looks like a credential.
+  - `untracked`: no entry covers it.
+  - `partial`: a directory that isn't tracked itself but contains tracked files.
+  - `local`: a path kept in local-only history (`mode = "track-local"`).
+
+  `PATH` defaults to the current directory and can be a relative path or a single file. `-r`/`--recursive` lists every file below the directory, `--tracked` and `--untracked` filter the rows, and `--json` prints one object per row. The command uses the same exclusion check as `mise dot save`, so the two always agree. [#15456](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15456) (@jdx, @farangkao)
+
+  ```console
+  $ mise dot files ~/.config
+  untracked  cache/
+  partial    foot/   1 file tracked below
+  tracked    hypr/   1 file · ~/.config/hypr (track, autosave)
+  untracked  mise/
+  ```
+
+- **`status.show_env_ignore`.** With `status.show_env` on, mise lists every variable it sets each time you enter a directory, including variables that never change. This new setting takes variable names or shell globs to leave out of that line. You can also set it with `MISE_STATUS_MESSAGE_SHOW_ENV_IGNORE` as a comma-separated list. Changes to config files and paths are still shown. mise warns about malformed patterns and ignores them. [#15454](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15454) (@jdx)
+
+  ```toml
+  [settings.status]
+  show_env = true
+  show_env_ignore = ["GO*", "DENO_INSTALL_ROOT"]
+  ```
+
+  With this config, `mise +DENO_INSTALL_ROOT +GOBIN +GOROOT +LUA_INIT` becomes `mise +LUA_INIT`.
+
+## Fixed
+
+- **Relative paths in `mise dot` commands.** `mise dot track config.toml` used to fail with `target must be absolute or start with ~/`. `track`, `untrack`, `add` and `edit` now resolve relative paths from the current directory the way a shell does, including `..` after a symlinked directory. A path inside your home directory is saved in its `~/` form. Exclude and include rules are still relative globs. [#15455](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15455) (@jdx, @farangkao)
+- **No warning when saving dotfiles by hand.** If you haven't set up the `history-watch` service, `mise dot track` now prints an info message about saving with `mise dot save` instead of a warning, so `--quiet` hides it. `mise dot status` now lists automatic capture as `manual`, without a warning or a suggested next step. mise still warns if the watcher is set up but not running, or if captures fail. [#15455](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15455) (@jdx, @farangkao)
+- **401 errors caused by stale `~/.netrc` credentials.** Some downloads failed with `401 Unauthorized` even though the server would serve the file without logging in. For example, `mise install glab` failed against gitlab.com when `~/.netrc` held a login that gitlab.com no longer accepted. If the only credentials came from netrc and the server returns 401, mise now retries once without them. Later retries of the same download also leave them out. Requests that carry their own `Authorization` header (such as forge tokens) and requests redirected to another host are not retried this way. [#15451](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15451) (@jdx)
+
+**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.11.4...v2026.11.5

title: fix(core): include the cutoff's own day for date-only release ages on rust channels
body:
A date-only `minimum_release_age` no longer makes `rust@beta` or `rust@nightly` resolve one day too old.

```sh
mise install -n rust@beta --minimum-release-age 2026-11-09
```

With a beta manifest dated `2026-11-09`, this used to resolve to `beta-2026-11-08`. A date-only cutoff means the end of that UTC day (`2026-11-09T23:59:59Z`), so the build dated that day is inside it, as it would be for a numbered release. It now resolves to `beta-2026-11-09`. If the current build is newer, the fallback search for a dated manifest also starts at the cutoff's own day instead of the day before.

Mid-day cutoffs such as `30d` or an RFC 3339 timestamp are unchanged: they still require a build from an earlier day, since a same-day build may have been published after the cutoff.

Fixes #15480

> 
> **Overview**
> **Date-only** `minimum_release_age` values (e.g. `2026-11-09`) now treat the cutoff as the **end of that UTC day**, so `rust@beta` / `rust@nightly` can resolve to a channel build dated **on** the cutoff day instead of always picking the previous day.
> 
> The rust plugin adds small helpers (`cutoff_day`, `channel_build_within_cutoff`, `cutoff_search_dates`) and wires them into `channel_for_cutoff`: eligibility checks and dated-manifest fallback both respect whether the cutoff includes its own day. **Mid-day** cutoffs (durations, RFC 3339 timestamps) still exclude same-day builds. Unit tests cover the new boundary behavior.

title: fix(github): fall back to the API asset endpoint after one probe retry on 5xx
body:
## Problem

When `github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/...` answers 5xx, mise only switches to the `api.github.com/.../releases/assets/<id>` endpoint after the reachability HEAD has used the whole `http_retries` budget on the browser URL. With `http_retries = 12` that is about 2.3 minutes per file. During the 2026-11-09 GitHub edge incident the API endpoint kept serving the same files with 200, so CI jobs spent minutes per aqua/github/packslip tool before falling back.

## Change

`pick_reachable_asset_url` now allows its probe one retry before using the API asset endpoint. The download itself still gets the full `http_retries` budget. A 404 or HTML login page already fell back at once and is unchanged.

```sh
MISE_HTTP_RETRIES=12 \
MISE_URL_REPLACEMENTS='{"https://github.com/":"http://127.0.0.1:18733/github.com/"}' \
mise install --locked flyctl   # server answers 504 to everything
```

Before: the HEAD retries 12 times before the API URL is tried. After: two HEADs, then the API URL.

## Not in this PR

- packslip's tarball and completion-file fetches still spend the full budget on the browser URL once the probe has picked it.
- `core:python` and `core:bun` still have no API fallback or `url_api` in the lockfile.

Part of #15481 (partial fix).

> **Low Risk**

> **Overview**
> GitHub release **browser download** reachability checks no longer burn the full **`http_retries`** budget on repeated **5xx** responses before switching to the **API asset** URL.
> 
> `head_without_netrc` now takes a **`max_retries`** cap; `pick_reachable_asset_url` passes **`PROBE_RETRIES = 1`**, so the HEAD probe gets at most **one retry** (two attempts) while the actual download still uses the configured retry count. **404** and **HTML login** handling is unchanged.

title: fix(task): keep other tasks working when one TOML task's usage fails to load
body:
One TOML task whose `usage` cannot be loaded no longer breaks the rest of the project. Reported in discussion #15462.

Before, a task such as

```toml
[tasks.good]
usage = 'flag "--good"'
run = 'echo good'

[tasks.bad]
usage = 'include file="{{ config_root }}/missing.kdl"'
raw_args = true
run = 'echo bad "$@"'
```

made `mise tasks --usage` and `mise generate task-docs` exit with an error, made shell completion of every task fall back to files, and `mise run bad x` failed even though `raw_args = true` never uses the spec. The same happened for a spec that does not parse, an undefined Tera variable, or `$VAR` in an include path.

Now it behaves like a file task with a broken `#USAGE`:

- `mise tasks --usage`, completion and `mise generate task-docs` warn about `bad`, use an empty spec for it, and keep working for every other task.
- A task that bypasses the usage parser (`raw_args = true`, or `--help`/`-h` passed through) runs even when its spec is broken, with a warning.
- `mise tasks validate` still fails on the broken spec.

Tested with the new e2e `test_task_usage_broken_toml` plus `test_task_ls_usage`, `test_task_usage`, `test_task_usage_cmd` and `test_task_validate`; clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(task): make MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD the directory mise was started in
body:
`MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD` is documented as the directory where you ran mise, but a task run through `--cd` / `-C` or `MISE_CD` saw the `--cd` target instead:

```bash
cd caller
mise -C ../project run show   # MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD was .../project, now .../caller
```

Tasks (TOML and file tasks) now get the directory mise was started in, before `--cd` or `MISE_CD` moved it. The task's own working directory and config discovery are unchanged. Without `--cd` nothing changes.

Hooks and `watch_files` also set `MISE_ORIGINAL_CWD` from the same cached value and are not touched here.

Adds `e2e/tasks/test_task_original_cwd_cd`, covering `-C` before and after `run`, `MISE_CD`, a file task, and no `--cd`; it passes.

Fixes #15463

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrows task env to an existing cached startup path; behavior without `--cd` is unchanged and covered by e2e.
> 
> **Overview**

title: feat(npm): install from an https tarball URL such as a pkg.pr.new preview
body:
The npm backend can now install from an `https://` tarball URL, so a preview build such as a [pkg.pr.new](https://pkg.pr.new) package can be installed like any other tool. Until now these URLs failed as a tool name (`invalid package name`) and as a version.

```toml
[tools."npm:https://pkg.pr.new/kjanat/actionlint/@kjanat/actionlint@343"]
version = "latest"
allow_exotic_deps = ["@kjanat-actionlint/actionlint-linux-x64"]
```

```sh
mise use 'npm:https://pkg.pr.new/kjanat/actionlint/@kjanat/actionlint@343'
```

## Behavior

- The whole URL is the tool name, including any `@` in its path, so the CLI no longer reads `343` as a version.
- A tarball has no version list, so `latest` means what the URL serves now. The version is a prefix of the tarball's SHA-256, and `mise up` fetches the URL again and updates when a new push changed the content.
- Installing downloads the tarball once, checks it against the version, and installs that file. A push between the check and the install cannot change what is installed, and a pinned version fails with a message pointing at `mise up` if the URL has changed.
- The package keeps the name in its own `package.json`. Because aube resolves a downloaded archive's `optionalDependencies` (it skips them for a URL root), pkg.pr.new's per-platform packages install. Those URL dependencies still need `allow_exotic_deps` with embedded aube or `aube_cli`; the docs recommend naming them rather than `true`.
- Only `https://` is accepted, and the `checksum` option is not supported.
- **`mise.lock` records the version but no dependency graph.** The graph aube writes for a URL root lacks the tarball's platform packages and would give a broken install, so lockfile-enabled projects still install a tarball URL, with the digest as its locked version.
- A task declares one as `tools = { "npm:https://…" = "latest" }`; its request is built from the URL and version separately, so `@latest` is not glued onto the URL.

The URL is declared in the tool name, the way git sources are, so it does not conflict with #14896 rejecting URLs in the version field.

## Testing

Unit tests cover URL detection, aliasing and validation, the CLI argument split for the pkg.pr.new form, and refusal of `http://` and `checksum`. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint-fix` pass.

I also ran a debug build against the real `kjanat/actionlint@343` preview: `mise ls-remote`, `mise use`, `mise install` (also with `lockfile = true` and `--locked`) and a task using the string form work and `mise x -- actionlint -version` runs the platform binary; a stale pinned version fails with the `mise up` message; `mise lock` records the version with no graph. There is no e2e test: the source must be `https://` and the e2e harness has no local HTTPS server.

Proposed in [discussion 15458](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15458) by @kjanat.

title: fix(backend): find the dated rust install when checking cargo install dependencies
body:
Fixes #15459.

With an explicit `minimum_release_age`, `cargo:` tools failed to install on a fresh machine because `core:rust` installs `stable` as a dated version (`1.99.1`) while the install dependency check kept looking for `rust@stable`:

```toml
[settings]
minimum_release_age = "7d"
[tools]
"core:rust" = "stable"
"cargo:cargo-binstall" = "latest"
```

```
mise ✗ cargo:cargo-binstall@1.26.2  failed: tool 'cargo:cargo-binstall@latest' requires configured install
dependency 'rust@stable', but its selected version is not installed
```

The dependency check resolves offline, and offline resolution skipped the release-age channel mapping entirely, so `stable` never became the dated install. Offline resolution now still maps a channel the backend can pin without the network (`rust@stable` → `latest`, which then finds the installed dated version). Lookups that need the network (`beta`, `nightly`) stay skipped offline.

Added `e2e/backend/test_cargo_rust_stable_release_age`, which fails with the error above on main and passes with this change.

title: feat(dot): add `mise dot files` to show what is tracked in a directory
body:
Until now, answering "is this file tracked?" meant reading `[dotfiles]` in your config and working out how each entry's `exclude`/`include` lists and `[history] exclude` applied. `mise dot files` answers it from the directory instead: it lists a directory's files and subdirectories and shows the state of each one.

```
$ mise dot files ~/.config
untracked  cache/
partial    foot/   1 file tracked below
tracked    hypr/   1 file · ~/.config/hypr (track, autosave)
untracked  mise/

$ mise dot files -r ~/.config
tracked    foot/foot.ini      ~/.config/foot/foot.ini (track, manual save)
tracked    hypr/bindings.lua  ~/.config/hypr (track, autosave)
excluded   hypr/monitors.lua  excluded by the entry's exclude list
untracked  mise/config.toml
```

The states:

- `tracked`: saved to history, with the entry that covers it and whether it autosaves.
- `excluded`: covered by an entry, but a rule leaves it out. The row names that rule: `[history] exclude`, the entry's `exclude` list, an `include` list that doesn't select it, a nested repository, or a `.git` directory.
- `omitted`: selected, but a capture skips it (for example a credential-like file), with the reason.
- `untracked`: no entry covers it.
- `partial`: a directory that isn't tracked itself (or is excluded) but holds tracked files.

A symlink is listed as the link itself, as history saves it. A path kept in local-only history (`mode = "track-local"`) is one `local` row, because that history applies its own rules: `-r` does not descend into it, a directory holding one is `partial`, and naming the path directly (or `mise dot --local files`) lists it from that history.

Options:

- `PATH` is optional and defaults to the current directory. A relative path is read from the current directory, and a single file works too.
- `-r`/`--recursive` lists every file below the directory (skipping `.git`). An unreadable subdirectory is reported and skipped.
- `--tracked` and `--untracked` split the output, like chezmoi's `managed`/`unmanaged`. A `partial` or `local` row goes under `--tracked`, so `--untracked` finds what holds nothing tracked.
- `--json` gives one object per row.

`mise dot ls` stays an alias of `mise dot status`, as before.

The listing asks the same exclusion check a capture uses: that check now returns which rule dropped a path rather than just yes or no. So `mise dot files` can't call a file excluded that `mise dot save` would save, or the other way round.

Requested in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13022#discussioncomment-19454828.

**Validation:** a new e2e test, `test_dotfiles_files_listing`, covers the states, relative paths, filters, recursion, symlinks, local-only paths and unreadable subdirectories. The existing exclude, include, rooted-pattern, nested-repository and track-preview e2e tests and the `history::tracked` unit tests pass, and clippy is clean.

title: fix(dot): accept relative targets and stop warning about manual saving
body:
Two small fixes for people who use `mise dot` without the automatic history watcher, reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13022#discussioncomment-19454828.

### Saving by hand is no longer a warning

Saving with `mise dot save` is a supported way to work, but every `mise dot track` printed a WARN, and `mise dot status` flagged automatic capture with ⚠ plus a "declare history-watch" next step. There was no way to turn either off.

A watcher that was never declared is now treated as a choice, not a fault:

```console
$ mise dot track ~/.zshrc
mise dotfiles: tracking ~/.zshrc (…)
mise history: edits are saved when you run `mise dot save` (or `mise dot watch --once`); to save them automatically, add a `[bootstrap.services.mise-history]` table with `builtin = "history-watch"` to your global config and run `mise bootstrap`
```

The line is logged at info level (so `--quiet` hides it), and `mise dot status` shows:

```text
Automatic capture
  manual: edits are saved when you run `mise dot save` (…).
```

There's no ⚠ and no next step. A watcher that is declared but not running, one that is running but not watching this store, and failing captures still warn, because in those cases edits are not being saved even though you asked for it.

### Relative targets

`mise dot track config.toml` used to fail with `target must be absolute or start with ~/`. `track`, `untrack`, `add` and `edit` now resolve a relative target from the current directory, the same way a shell would (`..` after a symlinked directory goes to the link's real parent), and declare it under its `~/` name when it is inside your home directory:

```console
$ cd ~/.config/mise
$ mise dot track config.toml      # declares "~/.config/mise/config.toml"
$ cd conf.d && mise dot untrack ..
```

Exclude and include rules such as `mise dot exclude 'sessions/**'` stay relative globs, as before.

### Testing

- New e2e `test_dotfiles_relative_target` covers track, untrack, `..`, add, edit, an exclude glob, and a target outside home. The existing dotfiles e2e tests were updated for the new wording.
- Added a unit test for the path resolution. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: feat(status): add status.show_env_ignore to hide variables from show_env
body:
## Summary

`status.show_env` prints every variable mise sets in each new shell, including ones that never change (`+GOBIN +GOROOT ...`). The new `status.show_env_ignore` setting lists variable names or shell globs to leave out, so the line only flags variables you don't expect.

```toml
[settings.status]
show_env = true
show_env_ignore = ["GO*", "DENO_INSTALL_ROOT"]
```

With that, `mise +DENO_INSTALL_ROOT +GOBIN +GOROOT +LUA_INIT` becomes `mise +LUA_INIT`. It can also be set with `MISE_STATUS_MESSAGE_SHOW_ENV_IGNORE` (comma-separated). Config files and paths that start or stop applying are still listed.

Closes discussion https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15452

## Test plan

- `mise run test:e2e test_status` (new case covers glob and exact-name matching)

Configure in TOML or via **`MISE_STATUS_MESSAGE_SHOW_ENV_IGNORE`** (comma-separated list).

+# zip:: includes for config and tasks
+
+Config and task includes can now load from `zip::` archives over HTTP(S). This release also fixes shim tab completion, `[tool_alias]` handling in `enable_tools`/`disable_tools` and `mise prune`, `mise dot sync` conflicts, and ufw firewall rule matching in `mise bootstrap`.
+
+## Added
+
+- **`zip::` includes for config and tasks.** Before, `include` and `task_config.includes` accepted local paths, `git::` and `oci::` sources. They now also accept a zip archive served over HTTP or HTTPS. mise downloads and unpacks the archive, then loads it the same way as an `oci::` artifact. For `task_config.includes` it loads executable file tasks and `.toml` task files. For `include` it loads the `mise.toml` at the archive root. Zip entries don't reliably carry file permissions, so mise makes non-TOML files that start with a shebang executable. [#15439](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15439) (@jdx)
+  - Only HTTP and HTTPS URLs are accepted. Any other scheme fails with an error.
+  - Task includes are still experimental, like the other remote sources.
+  - A URL doesn't pin specific contents. mise refreshes a zip config include the way it refreshes a branch (`fetch_remote_versions_cache`), and paranoid mode rejects zip config includes.
+
+  ```toml
+  # replace <URL> with the archive's HTTP(S) URL
+  include = ["zip::<URL of platform-config.zip>"]
+
+  [task_config]
+  includes = ["zip::<URL of shared-tasks-1.0.0.zip>"]
+  ```
+
+## Fixed
+
+- **Tab completion through shims.** Completing a command for a tool run through a mise shim (such as `aube` or `pitchfork`) showed mise's own subcommands instead of the tool's. mise now answers completion requests only when it is invoked as `mise`. Under a shim name, the request goes to the real tool. mise also skips version resolution, auto-install and auto-update while answering these requests. [#15429](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15429) (@jdx)
+- **Tool aliases in `enable_tools` and `disable_tools`.** If a tool was declared by its full backend ID, filtering by its `[tool_alias]` name did the wrong thing. `MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS=myjq` excluded the tool instead of selecting it, and `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS=myjq` had no effect. An alias now matches the same tool as its full ID in both filters, including aliases with inline options. An explicit enable list still overrides `disable_tools`. If you disable an aliased python, `_.python.venv` is turned off too. Based on a fix by @zeitlinger. [#15437](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15437) (@jdx)
+- **`mise prune` and project tool aliases.** When run from another directory, `mise prune` resolved a tracked project's `[tools]` entries against the current directory's config. Tools named through the project's own `[tool_alias]` caused "not found in mise tool registry" warnings, and mise couldn't tell whether those installs were still in use. These entries now resolve through the project's aliases, as well as the aliases in its parent and global configs. [#15438](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15438) (@jdx)
+- **`mise dot sync` with exclusions added on two machines.** When two machines each added their own `mise dot exclude` globs, sync failed with "enrollment conflict in exclusions". mise now merges the lists in this order: the shared base, then this machine's additions, then the other machine's. The same applies to an enrolled path's own `exclude` and `include` lists. A removal or a `!glob` added on both sides is still a conflict, because glob order matters. The error message now says how to recover. [#15449](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15449) (@jdx)
+- **ufw rules with a source or destination CIDR.** A `[[bootstrap.linux.firewall.rules]]` entry with a `source` or `destination` CIDR and no port never converged. mise read `10.42.0.0/16` as a port and a protocol, so `mise bootstrap plan --detailed-exitcode` kept reporting the rule. Firewall commands also now run with `LC_ALL=C`, so inspection no longer fails under non-English locales such as `de_DE.UTF-8`. [#15450](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15450) (@jdx)
+- **Fedora 45 COPR builds.** Releases are now built for Fedora 45 (x86_64 and aarch64) in the `jdxcode/mise` COPR repo. Before, Fedora 45 users were stuck on 2026.8.5. [#15441](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15441) (@jdx)
+
+## Documentation
+
+- The shell setup docs now say that fish 4.9.3 loads mise completions on its own, so you can skip `mise completion fish --install` there. [#15442](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15442) (@jdx)
+
+**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.11.3...v2026.11.4

title: fix(http): retry without netrc credentials after a 401
body:
Fixes #15445

`mise install glab` (the `gitlab:gitlab-org/cli` backend) could fail with `401 Unauthorized` on a public gitlab.com project when `~/.netrc` held a login gitlab.com no longer accepts. mise applies netrc credentials as a fallback to any request without its own `Authorization` header, and gitlab.com's package registry answers 401 to a rejected login even though it would serve the file anonymously.

mise now retries a request once without netrc credentials when netrc alone supplied the `Authorization` header and the server answered 401:

```
DEBUG GET https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases/v1.128.0/downloads/glab_1.128.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz 401 Unauthorized
DEBUG GET https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/cli/-/releases/v1.128.0/downloads/glab_1.128.0_linux_amd64.tar.gz retrying without netrc credentials after 401
```

The retry does not apply when the caller passed its own `Authorization` header (forge tokens) or when a URL replacement moved the request to a different host, whose netrc login is intentional.

I could not reproduce the reporter's exact 401 with fake credentials (gitlab.com accepts invalid Basic logins), so this is based on the log: netrc was the only credential on the failing `checksums.txt` requests. Validation: new e2e test `test_netrc_401_retry` (a local server that rejects any `Authorization` header) and the existing `test_netrc` pass.

> **Medium Risk**
> Touches authentication and download retry paths in the shared HTTP client; behavior is narrowly scoped to netrc-only 401s but affects all downloads that use netrc fallback.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes installs failing with **401** when `~/.netrc` supplies a stale login for a host that would still serve the resource anonymously (e.g. public GitLab release assets).
> 
> HTTP downloads now carry a shared **netrc retry state** on `DownloadLimits` / `AttemptOutcome`, wired through `send_once_with_https_fallback_allow_416`. If **only netrc** added `Authorization` and the server returns **401** on the same origin (with normal status checking), mise **logs and retries once without netrc**, and flips shared state so **later retry attempts in the same download** do not resend the rejected credentials. Caller-supplied auth, `allow_error_status`, and responses after cross-origin redirects are unchanged.
>

title: fix(bootstrap): match ufw rules with a source CIDR and ignore the locale
body:
A `[[bootstrap.linux.firewall.rules]]` entry with a `source` or `destination` CIDR and no port never converged: `mise bootstrap plan --detailed-exitcode` kept reporting it as unknown after every apply.

```toml
[[bootstrap.linux.firewall.rules]]
name = "k3s-pods"
source = "10.42.0.0/16"
interface = "cni0"
```

mise read the CIDR in `from 10.42.0.0/16` as port `10.42.0.0` and protocol `16`. It now skips values that follow `from` or `to` when looking for `port/proto`, so these rules match.

ufw output is also parsed as English text, so inspection failed under locales such as `de_DE.UTF-8`. Firewall commands now run with `LC_ALL=C`.

Fixes #15447

Tests: added a unit test for CIDR source and destination rules; `cargo test -p mise-system -p mise --lib firewall` passes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches firewall inspection and apply paths: parsing logic and global locale for external commands; low blast radius but wrong edge cases could still mis-detect rules or affect non-UFW tools sharing these helpers.
> 
> **Overview**
> **UFW rule matching** no longer treats CIDR strings after `from`/`to` (e.g. `10.42.0.0/16`) as compact `port/proto` tokens; only `/` in other positions is used for that fallback, so rules with source/destination networks and no port converge correctly.
> 
> **Firewall subprocess helpers** (`command_output_path`, `run_with_stdin`) now build commands via `c_locale_command`, which sets `LC_ALL=C` and drops `LANGUAGE`, so `ufw`/`firewall-cmd`/similar output stays English and parsing does not break under translated locales.
> 
> Unit tests cover CIDR-only and CIDR-with-port UFW lines plus the C-locale command environment.

body:
`mise dot sync` no longer fails with "enrollment conflict in exclusions" when two machines each added their own `mise dot exclude` globs.

Previously the manifest's `exclude` list was merged as one opaque field, so base `[a]`, local `[a, y]` and remote `[a, x]` aborted the sync and paused sharing. Now, when both sides only appended to the base, the result is the base followed by local's additions and then remote's (`[a, y, x]`).

The same merge applies to an enrolled path's own `exclude` and `include` lists when all three sides state one.

Globs apply in order and the last match wins, so the merge stays conservative: a `!glob` added on a diverged side, or a removal on a diverged side, is still a conflict. The error now says what to run to recover (`mise dot exclude`, `mise dot save`, sync again).

Fixes #15446

## Testing

`independent_exclusion_additions_are_merged` and `independent_entry_exclusion_additions_are_merged` cover disjoint additions, a shared addition, a diverged `!glob` and a removal versus an addition. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches dotfile sync conflict resolution for exclusion semantics; incorrect merging could change which files are tracked or excluded across machines.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise dot sync`** no longer aborts when two machines each append different **`exclude`** (or per-enrollment **`exclude`/`include`**) globs on top of the same base manifest.
> 
> Manifest merge now routes top-level **`exclude`** and enrollment glob lists through **`merge_exclusions`** / **`merge_entry_globs`** instead of strict three-way equality. When local and remote both only extend the base list, the merged result is base → local additions → remote additions (deduped), preserving glob order semantics (“last match wins”).
> 
> The merge stays **conservative**: divergent removals, reordering, **`!glob`** additions, or missing optional lists on only some sides still surface an enrollment conflict, with clearer guidance to reconcile **`.mise-history/manifest.json`**.

title: docs: note that fish 4.9.3 loads mise completions itself
body:
The shell setup page tells every fish user to run `mise completion fish --install`. fish 4.9.3 ships a built-in loader that runs `mise completion fish | source` the first time `mise` is completed, so there the install step does nothing useful. I confirmed the loader is embedded in the 4.9.3 binary; I did not test other fish versions.

This adds a short note to the Completions section of `docs/shell-setup.md`: on fish 4.9.3 you can skip `--install`, earlier versions may not have the loader, and other shells or distributions may provide their own. No behavior changes.

title: fix(copr): build releases for fedora 45
body:
Fedora 45 users of the `jdxcode/mise` COPR repo get a very old `2026.8.5-1`, while Fedora 43, 44 and rawhide get the latest release. The release script's default chroot list (`DEFAULT_CHROOTS` in `packaging/copr/build-copr.sh`) never included `fedora-45`, so no release build has been submitted for it.

This adds `fedora-45-aarch64` and `fedora-45-x86_64` to the defaults, so every release publishes to F45 alongside the other Fedora chroots.

Existing F45 users stay on 2026.8.5 until a build is submitted. After merge, running the `copr-publish` workflow once with `chroots: "fedora-45-x86_64 fedora-45-aarch64"` backfills the latest version. The `fedora-45` chroots must also be enabled in the COPR project settings; that is not checked here.

Until then, F45 users can replace `$releasever` with `fedora-44` in `/etc/yum.repos.d/_copr:copr.fedorainfracloud.org:jdxcode:mise.repo`.

Fixes #15369

title: feat(task): support zip:: includes for config and tasks
body:
Config and task includes accepted local paths, `git::` and `oci::`, but not a zip archive, even though plugin installs do. A team that publishes shared tasks or a base config as a `.zip` on a release page or file server can now include it directly.

```toml
include = ["zip::https://example.com/platform-config.zip"]  # mise.toml at the archive root

[task_config]
includes = ["zip::https://example.com/shared-tasks-1.0.0.zip"]
```

mise downloads the archive, unpacks it into a directory and loads it exactly like an `oci::` artifact: executable file tasks and `.toml` task files for `task_config.includes`, and the root `mise.toml` for `include`. Non-TOML files that start with a shebang are made executable, since zip entries here are not trusted to carry modes.

- Only http(s) URLs are accepted; anything else fails with a clear message.
- Task includes stay experimental, like the other remote sources.
- A URL names no content, so a config zip is refreshed like a branch (`fetch_remote_versions_cache`) and paranoid mode rejects it.

Closes #15431

## Test plan

- unit tests for the provider (prefix match, URL validation, download and unpack against a mock server)
- new e2e `test_task_zip_include`: task include, config include, paranoid rejection, non-http rejection

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Downloads and unpacks remote zip archives into local task/config includes, affecting discovery and environment; risk is moderated by http(s)-only URLs, caching semantics, and paranoid-mode rejection for unpinned content.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`zip::http(s)` remote includes** alongside existing `git::` and `oci::`, for both **`include` config merging** and **`task_config.includes` task discovery**.
> 
> A new **`RemoteTaskZip` provider** downloads/unzips HTTP(S) archives, normalizes unpacked files (reuses OCI’s shebang→executable handling), and **caches by full URL** (or bypasses with `task.remote_no_cache`). **Paranoid mode rejects `zip::` config includes** because they’re inherently **mutable pins**, and **non-http(s) `zip::` references fail fast**.
> 
> Docs/schema comments are updated to describe behavior, limits, and caching; **unit tests** cover the provider and a new **e2e** verifies task runs, env merge from zip `mise.toml`, paranoid failure, and invalid schemes.

title: fix(prune): resolve a project's tool_alias for its [tools] entries
body:
`mise prune` run from outside a project warned about, and could not account for, a tool that the project names through its own `[tool_alias]`:

```toml
[tool_alias]
jq-local = "github:jqlang/jq[version_prefix=jq-]"

[tools]
jq-local = "1.8.2"
```

```
$ mise -C elsewhere prune --dry-run
WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for jq-local: [project/mise.toml] jq-local@1.8.2: jq-local not found in mise tool registry
```

The project's `[tools]` were resolved against the config of the current directory, which has no such alias. `[tools]` entries now resolve through the tracked project's `[tool_alias]` (and those of its parent and global configs), the same way its task tools already do after #15427. The request keeps the alias name, which names the install directory, and takes the alias's backend and options; options written in `[tools]` win over the alias's.

Version aliases (`[tool_alias.x.versions]`) are not touched here.

Fixes #15432

## Test plan
- New `e2e/cli/test_prune_tool_alias` covers an installed and an uninstalled aliased tool. It fails without the fix with the warning above and passes with it.
- `test_prune_task_tools` and `test_prune_tracked_config_invalid_version` still pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from a pre-existing unused-dependency warning.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes prune's resolution of tracked configs when aliases are involved; wrong routing could misclassify installs as unused or alter warnings, though scope is limited to alias-aware request building.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fix:** Running `mise prune` from another directory no longer tries to resolve a tracked project's `[tools]` names against the *current* directory. Those entries are now routed through that project's own `[tool_alias]` (and the same layered config sources as tasks: globals and roots above the project), keeping the alias as the install name and the alias's backend/options, with **`[tools]` options overriding** the alias.
> 
> **Implementation:** Config code splits out **`project_config_layers`** and **`project_tool_aliases`**, generalizes **`aliased_tool_request`** (explicit version, written opts, `ToolSource`; registry backend choice can follow the version), and adds **`route_project_tool_aliases`**, which the prune path calls on successfully parsed **tracked** config tool request sets.
> 
> **Tests:** New **`e2e/cli/test_prune_tool_alias`** covers no spurious "Failed to resolve" for aliased tools, correct dry-run output for installed vs stray versions, and that **per-version** tool options on aliased entries are preserved.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1dbc0105ffbe1401ad9ce26e4c62b3cce459c5fd. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo.

title: fix(config): honor tool aliases in enable and disable filters
body:
`MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS` / `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS` (`enable_tools` / `disable_tools`) ignored `[tool_alias]` names when the tool is declared under its full backend ID:

```toml
[tool_alias]
myjq = "aqua:jqlang/jq"

[tools]
"aqua:jqlang/jq" = "1.7.1"
```

`MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS=myjq` used to exclude jq instead of selecting it, and `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS=myjq` did not exclude it. Now the alias identifies the same tool as its full ID in both filters. An explicit enable allowlist still overrides `disable_tools`.

Search, the interactive tool picker, and early backend discovery are unchanged; they run before project aliases are loaded.

Based on the fix by @zeitlinger in discussion #15433 (commit e055fd30ef).

> **Medium Risk**
> Core tool inclusion/exclusion and python venv gating changed; mis-resolved aliases could incorrectly hide or keep tools on PATH.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Tool allow/deny lists now treat `[tool_alias]` names as the backend they point to**, so `MISE_ENABLE_TOOLS` / `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS` (and `enable_tools` / `disable_tools`) match fully-qualified tools when the filter uses an alias, including aliases with inline options. An explicit allowlist still overrides `disable_tools`; an empty allowlist still blocks everything.

> **Implementation:** `tool_enabled_for_backend` / `tool_enabled_for_backend_in` replace the old registry `tool_enabled` for these checks, resolving alias targets from config and comparing normalized full backend IDs (options stripped). `ToolRequestSetBuilder` keeps filter sets as short strings consistent with that logic. **`_.python.venv` uses the same path** via `python_venv_enabled` so disabling an aliased python turns off `VIRTUAL_ENV` like disabling `python` directly.

@@ -0,0 +1,54 @@
+# Task history, saved task logs, and source-based --affected outside monorepos
+
+This release adds three task features: `mise tasks history` shows how long past runs took, the opt-in `task.logs` setting saves each task's last output, and `mise run --affected` now works in any project by matching changed files against each task's `sources`. It also fixes problems with `upgrade --bump`, GitHub asset detection, locked lockfiles, Windows npm installs, `prune` and hung asdf plugins.
+
+## Added
+
+- **`mise run --affected` outside a monorepo.** Before, `--affected` worked only at a monorepo root and failed anywhere else. Outside a monorepo it now runs only the matching tasks affected by changed files. A task is affected when a changed file matches its `sources`, or when the config file or `file` script that defines it changed. Matching uses the same rules as the up-to-date check, including `!` exclusions and paths relative to the task's directory.
+  - Tasks with no `sources`, and tasks whose sources use `{{usage.*}}`, run whenever anything changed. When nothing changed, nothing runs.
+  - Global tasks are left out. Dependencies of a selected task still run, subject to the up-to-date check.
+  - The existing `--affected-base`, `--affected-head`, `--affected-committed`, `--affected-uncommitted` and `--affected-untracked` options decide which changes count. `--affected-explain` prints why each task was selected or skipped, and `--affected-json` reports the reasons (`changed-source`, `task-config`, `task-file`, `no-sources`, `argument-sources`).
+  - Monorepo project selection is unchanged.
+
+  [#15407](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15407) (@jdx)
+
+  ```toml
+  [tasks."test:unit"]
+  run = "cargo test"
+  sources = ["src/**"]
+
+  [tasks."test:docs"]
+  run = "markdownlint docs"
+  sources = ["docs/**"]
+  ```
+  ```sh
+  mise run --affected --affected-explain 'test:*'
+  ```
+
+- **`mise tasks history`.** mise now records when each task run started, how long it took, its redacted arguments, its exit code and its status (`ok`, `failed`, `cached`, `skipped` or `cancelled`). `mise tasks history [TASK]` lists past runs. `--summary` shows each task's run count, failure count, median duration of successful runs, and last duration and status. `--json` prints the records as JSON. Recording is on by default and keeps the last 20 runs per task. You can change the limit with `task.history_limit`, or turn recording off with `task.history = false`. Dry runs and tasks that only have `depends` are not recorded, and a recording error never fails a run. [#15408](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15408) (@jdx)
+
+  ```console
+  $ mise tasks history --summary
+  hello      3  0  89.0ms  88.0ms  ok
+  test:unit  3  0  -       1.0ms   skipped
+  ```
+
+- **Saved task output with `mise tasks log`.** When the new `task.logs` setting (or `MISE_TASK_LOGS=1`) is on, mise keeps the full output of each task's last run. `mise tasks log NAME` prints it, and `--path` prints where the file is. This gets back output that the `replacing`, `timed`, `silent` and `summary` styles hide or shorten. When a task fails under one of those styles, mise prints a `full output: <path>` line. Logs are stored in `$MISE_STATE_DIR/task-logs/` with owner-only permissions and are redacted the same way as terminal output. Each log keeps the newest 4 MiB. Output that mise doesn't pipe is not logged: `raw` and `interactive` tasks, and the default `interleave` mode when it has nothing to redact. The setting is off by default. [#15409](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15409) (@jdx)
+
+  ```toml
+  [settings]
+  task.logs = true
+  ```
+
+  The same PR changes every piped output style: lines longer than 1 MiB now arrive in pieces, so mise no longer holds a whole long line in memory. The pieces are split so that secrets and URL credentials are still fully redacted.
+
+## Fixed
+
+- `mise upgrade --bump` no longer rewrites a two-part prefix such as `{ prefix = "1.23" }` to the unresolvable `prefix:prefix:1.1`. It now bumps to the correct version, for example `prefix:1.26`. [#15426](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15426) (@jdx, @kjanat)
+- When choosing a release asset automatically, the `github:` backend now skips Python wheels (`.whl`) and Ruby gems (`.gem`), as it already does for `.deb` and `.rpm`. Before, a `manylinux` wheel could be picked over the native binary. An explicit `asset_pattern` can still select these files. If an `asset_pattern` looks like a regular expression and matches nothing, the GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo error now explains that `asset_pattern` is a glob and suggests `matching_regex`. [#15423](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15423) (@jdx)
+- With `tool_config.locked = true` and `lockfile_mode = "generate"`, installing or running one tool no longer writes another tool's unrecorded version into `mise.lock`. Before, this let the next run accept a pin nobody had reviewed. The lockfile now stays unchanged, and only `mise lock` records new versions. [#15428](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15428) (@jdx, @mikomiel)
+- On Windows, `npm:` tools installed with aube are now reinstalled when a cache restore turned their dependency links into file symlinks. Before, `mise install` reported "already installed" while Node failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. [#15425](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15425) (@jdx, @Diapolo10)
+- When run from outside a project, `mise prune` and `mise upgrade` no longer delete installs of task tools that the project names through its `[tool_alias]`. The "not found in mise tool registry" warning for these tools is also gone. [#15427](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15427) (@jdx)
+- `fetch_remote_versions_timeout` now stops an asdf plugin's `bin/list-all` that hangs. mise kills the script's process group and fails with `timed out after ...` and a hint about the setting. Before, mise waited until the script exited and held the version lock the whole time. `ruby-install --update` now follows the same timeout. `bin/list-all` now runs with stdin closed, so a script that reads stdin gets EOF. [#15424](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15424) (@jdx, @karngyan)
+
+**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/v2026.11.2...v2026.11.3

title: fix(completion): forward a shim's completion request to its tool
body:
Tab completion for a tool run through a mise shim (`aube`, `pitchfork`, ...) offered mise's own commands instead of the tool's ([usage discussion 1623](https://github.com/jdx/usage/discussions/1623)).

A shim is the mise binary under another name. mise answered the hidden `__complete_word__` request before shim handling ran, so the shim answered for mise:

```
$ ~/.local/share/mise/shims/aube __complete_word__ --shell fish --line "aube ins"
install        Install the tools in your config, or specific tool versions
install-into   Install a tool version into a directory outside mise
installs       [experimental] Inspect and choose identity-layout installations
```

The real `aube` binary answers `install` and `install-clean` for the same line. With this change mise answers the completion request only when invoked as mise itself. Under any other name the request continues into shim handling, which already forwards it to the tool behind the shim, so the shim now returns the tool's candidates. `mise __complete_word__ ...` is unchanged.

Checked with a debug build: as `mise`, `ins` still completes to `install`, `install-into` and `install-dev`; as a differently named symlink, the request now reaches shim handling instead of returning mise's list. I did not run it against a real installed aube or pitchfork shim, and the new e2e test asserts only that a non-mise name no longer returns mise's commands.

title: fix(lock): keep tool_config.locked pins out of the lockfile after an install
body:
Fixes #15417.

With `tool_config.locked = true` and the default `lockfile_mode = "generate"`, installing or running one tool could write a different tool's unrecorded pin into `mise.lock`. The next run then accepted that pin, so the lockfile stopped being the reviewed contract.

```toml
[tool_config]
locked = true

[tools]
"http:fixture-a" = { version = "1.0.0", ... }
"http:fixture-b" = { version = "2.0.0", ... } # only 1.0.0 is in mise.lock
```

Before: `mise exec -- fixture-b` failed with "not in the lockfile", but it first installed `fixture-a`, and that install regenerated the lockfile and added `fixture-b` 2.0.0. Running the same command again succeeded.

After: the lockfile stays byte-identical and both attempts fail. Only an explicit `mise lock` records the new version.

After an install, lockfile generation now withholds tools whose config sets `tool_config.locked` and whose resolved version the lockfile does not record yet, and keeps the entries it already has for them (they are not pruned as unselected). Entries that are already recorded are still refreshed. `mise lock` itself is unchanged.

The e2e test fails without the change and passes with it.

title: fix(prune): resolve a project's tool_alias for its task tools
body:
`mise prune` (and `mise upgrade`) run from outside a project deleted the install of a tool that the project only uses in a task, when the tool was named through the project's `[tool_alias]`:

```toml
[tool_alias]
llvm = "github:llvm/llvm-project[version_prefix=llvmorg-,matching=LLVM-]"

[tasks.bundle]
run = "clang --version"
tools.llvm = "23.1.2"
```

```
WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for llvm: llvm@23.1.2: llvm not found in mise tool registry
```

The task tool was resolved against the config of the current directory, which has no such alias, so the version dropped out of the set of needed versions and prune removed it. Task tools now resolve through the tracked project's `[tool_alias]`, the same way its `[tools]` entries do, so the install is kept and the warning is gone.

Version aliases (`[tool_alias.x.versions]`) for task tools are not touched here.

Fixes #15420

## Test plan
- `e2e/cli/test_prune_task_tools` gains an aliased task tool; it fails without the fix (the warning and the pruned version) and passes with it.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from a pre-existing unused-dependency warning.

title: fix(upgrade): stop --bump doubling prefix: on two-part prefix requests
body:
`mise upgrade --bump` no longer rewrites a two-part `prefix` request to a version that cannot resolve.

With this config and 1.26.2 released:

```toml
[tools]
cargo-binstall = { prefix = "1.23" }
```

`mise upgrade --bump` proposed `prefix:prefix:1.1` and failed with `no versions found for cargo-binstall`. It now bumps to `prefix:1.26`. One-part prefixes such as `{ prefix = "27" }` already worked and behave the same.

The bump split the `prefix:`-marked display form (`prefix:1.23`) at its first dot, which produced a bogus vendor prefix of `prefix:1.`. It now splits the version the user wrote. Requests that are not `prefix` requests are unchanged.

Fixes #15419. Thanks to @kjanat for the report and the root-cause trace.

Adds `e2e/cli/test_upgrade_bump_prefix_request`.

title: fix(npm): reinstall aube trees whose dependency links were restored as file symlinks on Windows
body:
## Problem

On Windows CI, an npm tool installed by mise's embedded aube can still fail at run time after a cache restore, even with the junction check from #14418:

```
mise install --locked   ->  cspell@10.4.0 · already installed
cspell lint ...         ->  Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'picomatch'
```

This is the reopened report on #14417 (mise 2026.11.1).

## Cause

Reproduced on a Windows machine: install `cspell@10.4.0`, archive the mise data dir with Git for Windows' `tar.exe` (what `mise-action` does), delete it, and restore it.

- With `tar`'s default symlink mode the links are dropped, and #14418's check catches that.
- With native symlinks (`MSYS=winsymlinks:native`, where the restore succeeds as it did on the reporter's runner), aube's directory junction comes back as a **file** symlink that points at the right directory. Win32 opens through it, so `picomatch/package.json` looks present and the health check passes, but node does not follow a file symlink as a directory, so the package cannot be resolved. `mise install` says "already installed" and never repairs it.

## Fix

On Windows, a dependency that is a file symlink now counts as missing, so the tree is treated as not installed and `mise install` reinstalls it from the lockfile (a package directory is never a file symlink, so healthy trees are unaffected). Unix is unchanged.

## Validation

- Reproduced the failure above on Windows; confirmed the restored link reports `is_symlink_file` and that the previous check returned healthy for it.
- The existing `virtual_store_entry_without_dependency_links_is_detected` test and clippy pass on Linux. A new Windows-only test covers the file-symlink case (it skips itself when the runner cannot create symlinks); it has not been run on Windows, nor has the patched binary been run there.

Fixes #14417
