title: fix(lock): keep the locks/ sidecar layout for a symlinked global config dir
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3013/changes/mise/1126
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When `~/.config/mise` is a symlink into a dotfiles repo (for example `~/dotfiles/mise`), `mise lock --global` now keeps writing npm and Python sidecars to `locks/`, as it did before 2026.10.19, instead of `.mise/locks/`.

#14961 chose the sidecar layout from the canonical directory so the location no longer depended on how the config dir was reached. A side effect was that a link target not named `mise` under a `.config` dir fell through to the project layout, so the canonical global path `~/.config/mise` got `.mise/locks/`.

The layout still comes from the canonical directory, so it is the same from any working directory. A directory that canonicalizes to the same place as `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` now counts as the global config dir and uses `locks/`.

```
$ ls -l ~/.config/mise
~/.config/mise -> ~/dotfiles/mise
$ mise lock --global      # before: aube = { path = ".mise/locks/npm-cowsay/1.6.0", ... }
                          # now:    aube = { path = "locks/npm-cowsay/1.6.0", ... }
```

A lockfile already written with `.mise/locks/` pointers is rewritten to `locks/` on the next `mise lock --global`. The old `.mise/locks/` copy is not removed and can be deleted by hand.

Extends the symlinked-config-dir e2e test to assert the `locks/` pointer, and adds a unit test for the link, its target, and a non-global directory.

Closes https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15109

title: fix(node): keep a packageManager checksum from pinning later installs to npm
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3011/changes/mise/1125
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `packageManager` entry with a checksum made every later install of the same tool use the npm backend, even for a newer version with no checksum.

For example, after installing a project that declares `"packageManager": "pnpm@11.7.0+sha512.…"`, a second project declaring just `"packageManager": "pnpm@12.15.0"` also installed `npm:pnpm` instead of the registry's `aqua:pnpm/pnpm`. pnpm 12 then printed:

```
pnpm is running through Node.js because the script that installs its native binary was skipped.
```

The checksum has to install from npm (or `http:yarn` for Yarn 2+), because only that artifact is the one corepack's checksum covers. mise therefore forces that backend for the request. It also recorded the backend in `installs/pnpm/.mise.backend.toml` as `explicit_backend = true`, as if the user had written `npm:pnpm`. From then on every `pnpm` request followed the manifest instead of the registry. Deleting `installs/pnpm` was the only way out.

A backend forced for one request is now pinned for that request but written to the manifest as non-explicit, so later requests for the tool follow the registry again. A checksummed install still uses npm, and the `checksum` option is stored as before. The same applies to `npm`, `bun` and `yarn` checksums.

Installs already affected recover too: a manifest an earlier mise wrote for a checksum backend (`pnpm` → `npm:pnpm`, `explicit_backend = true`) is read as the registry's choice again, and the next install rewrites it. This reading is temporary and guarded by `remove_by!`.

Tested with the reproduction from the discussion: after the checksummed pnpm 11 install the manifest reads `explicit_backend = false`, and pnpm 12.15.0 installs from `aqua:pnpm/pnpm` as the native binary without the warning. `e2e/core/test_package_manager_checksum_slow` now asserts both, and fails without the fix. A unit test covers all five forced backends.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15121.

body:
Follow-up to #13391 and #13832. A gem `source` without RubyGems' JSON versions API could only install a pinned version: `latest`, prefixes, `mise outdated` and `mise upgrade` all failed there, and every bump meant editing the pin. GitHub Packages is the common case. When `api/v1/versions/<gem>.json` is a 404, mise now reads the source's compact index (`info/<gem>`) instead. That is the file Bundler installs from, so any registry Bundler can use serves it, GitHub Packages included, and it takes the same credential as the install.

```toml
[tools]
"gem:internal-cli" = { version = "latest", source = "https://rubygems.pkg.github.com/acme" }
```

```console
$ mise ls-remote gem:internal-cli
0.0.2
0.1.0
2.3.1
```

- Each version appears once even when the index lists several platform builds, and versions are sorted in RubyGems' own order, since the index is in publish order and a backport would otherwise read as the latest.
- Release dates come from the index's `created_at:` field where a registry includes it (rubygems.org does). GitHub Packages does not, so release-age settings such as `minimum_release_age` have no dates for its versions.
- GitHub Packages answers a missing or under-scoped token with a bare 401, which `gem install` reports as "Could not find a valid gem". Listing and installing from it now add a message naming the `read:packages` scope and `gh auth refresh -s read:packages`.
- Sources with the JSON API, and installs with no `source`, are unchanged.

Tested with a new e2e test against a registry that serves only the compact index, unit tests for the index parser and version order, and by hand against a real private GitHub Packages org.

--- e2e/backend/test_gem_compact_index (+76/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# A `source` registry without RubyGems' JSON versions API, as GitHub Packages
+# is, lists versions from its compact index (`info/<gem>`), the file Bundler
+# installs from. Listing never shells out to `gem`, so this needs no Ruby.
+
+TOKEN="ghp_e2eSECRET"
+
+# A fake registry with only the compact index. It records each request's path
+# and Authorization header.
+cat >registry.py <<'PYTHON'
+import os
+import threading
+import time
+from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
+from pathlib import Path
+
+info = b"""---
+1.0.0 |checksum:aa
+2.2.0 thor:>= 1.2|checksum:bb
+2.2.0-x86_64-linux thor:>= 1.2|checksum:cc
+2.3.1 |checksum:dd
+"""
+
+
+class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def log_message(self, *args):
+        pass
+
+    def do_GET(self):
+        auth = self.headers.get("Authorization") or "none"
+        with open("requests.log", "a") as log:
+            log.write(f"{self.path} {auth}\n")
+        if self.path != "/acme/info/internal-cli":
+            self.send_error(404)
+            return
+        self.send_response(200)
+        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
+        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(info)))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(info)
+
+
+def exit_with_test():
+    parent = os.getppid()
+    while os.getppid() == parent:
+        time.sleep(0.5)
+    os._exit(0)
+
+
+threading.Thread(target=exit_with_test, daemon=True).start()
+server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
+Path("registry.port").write_text(str(server.server_port))
+server.serve_forever()
+PYTHON
+
+python3 registry.py &
+registry_pid=$!
+wait_for_file registry.port "gem registry port" 30 "$registry_pid"
+port="$(cat registry.port)"
+
+cat >mise.toml <<EOF
+[tools]
+"gem:internal-cli" = { version = "latest", source = "http://${TOKEN}@127.0.0.1:${port}/acme" }
+EOF
+
+# Each version once, oldest first, and a prefix resolves against them.
+assert "mise ls-remote gem:internal-cli" "1.0.0
+2.2.0
+2.3.1"
+assert "mise latest gem:internal-cli@2.2" "2.2.0"
+
+# The JSON API first, then the compact index, both with the credential
+# (base64 of `ghp_e2eSECRET:`).
+assert "cat requests.log" "/acme/api/v1/versions/internal-cli.json Basic Z2hwX2UyZVNFQ1JFVDo=
+/acme/info/internal-cli Basic Z2hwX2UyZVNFQ1JFVDo="

title: registry: install Danger Swift libraries alongside its executable
body:
Configure `danger-swift` to use its [official installer](https://github.com/danger/swift/blob/3.21.2/Scripts/install.sh#L26-L43), installing `libDanger` and Swift modules alongside the executable through mise's existing `install_command` option. Projects can use `danger-swift = "3.22.1"` without repeating installer options; Node and Danger JS remain explicit dependencies.

Follow-up to [#11286](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11286) and [discussion #3540](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/3540). The original was [reverted](https://github.com/jdx/mise/commit/4c32d0fac60f83a07c3284f08d7e750c9f049b81) because Ubuntu 26.04 used an Ubuntu 24.04 Swift toolchain requiring a different libxml ABI; its installer then reported success without an executable ([maintainer's explanation](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11286#issuecomment-5087097291)). [#11369](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/11369) restored the generic installer with executable verification, deferring Danger integration.

Swift now supplies native Ubuntu 26.04 toolchains ([downloads](https://www.swift.org/install/linux/ubuntu/26_04/), [release metadata](https://www.swift.org/api/v1/install/releases.json)). Restore the original source-installation approach and Danger regression test, retaining its versions, fixture and assertions. Apply its `CFFIXED_USER_HOME` override on Linux too: [Foundation otherwise prefers the account home](https://github.com/swiftlang/swift-corelibs-foundation/blob/swift-6.4.1-RELEASE/Sources/CoreFoundation/CFPlatform.c#L356-L397), causing library lookup to miss the isolated test install. Remove the obsolete libxml alias. No backend code changes are needed.

On macOS, Danger’s installer and Dangerfile execution can use different Swift compilers, producing incompatible modules. The installer now uses the compiler selected by `xcrun`, and the regression test keeps mise-managed Swift active to verify this configuration.

[Verification](https://github.com/Mostafa-Ashraf97/mise/actions/runs/40715790686): macOS 26 Intel and Ubuntu 26.04 passed the complete Swift E2E, including real Dangerfile execution. Ubuntu also passed a second run pinned to native Swift 6.4.1 without a libxml alias. The updated regression also passed locally on macOS ARM64 with mise Swift 6.4.1 active alongside Xcode Swift 6.4.

The regression pins Danger Swift 3.22.1. [3.23.1 identifies itself as 3.23.0](https://github.com/danger/swift/blob/3.23.1/Sources/Runner/main.swift#L6), breaking its versioned mise library lookup; that existing release bug and custom-prefix lookup remain separate. Source installation retains existing custom-installer restrictions.

title: fix(backend): name the program when a command can't be found
body:
When a backend ran a command whose program isn't on `PATH`, mise failed with an error that never named the program:

```
mise ERROR Failed to install cargo:Mossop/stacks@branch:main: failed to execute command: cargo install --git=https://github.com/Mossop/stacks.git --branch=main --locked --root ...: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

"No such file or directory" reads like a file the command needed, so the report in jdx/mise#15118 gave no hint whether the program or something else was missing. This affects every backend that shells out (`cargo`, `go`, `gem`, `pipx`, ...). It does not change the behavior behind that report: the reporter had `~/.cargo/bin` on `PATH` only through a `_.path = { ..., tools = true }` entry, which mise resolves after tools load (see [Use values that tools set](https://mise.jdx.dev/environments/index.html#lazy-eval)), so `cargo` wasn't on the install's `PATH`. The new wording makes that failure read as a missing `cargo`.

The error now names the program:

```
failed to execute command: cargo install --git=... --root ...: `cargo` not found: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

The program is only named once a lookup on the command's `PATH` confirms it is absent. If the working directory is what's missing, or a script exists but its interpreter doesn't, the error is left as it was, so the new wording is never wrong about the cause.

This only changes the wording of the error. The existing "cargo may be required but was not found" warning and its `mise use rust@latest` hint are unchanged.

Validation: new unit tests in `mise-util` cover a missing program (sync, async and raw mode), a missing working directory and a script with a missing interpreter. I reproduced the original error with the released 2026.10.21 binary and no `cargo` on `PATH`, and confirmed the same command runs normally with a stub `cargo` on `PATH`. I did not rebuild the full `mise` binary to re-run that repro against the change.

title: fix(shell): convert MANPATH to POSIX form when activating under MSYS2/Cygwin
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3007/changes/mise/1123
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Under MSYS2, Git Bash and Cygwin, `eval "$(mise activate zsh)"` (or bash/fish) put `PATH` in POSIX form but exported `MANPATH` as a native Windows list, so `man` could not use it:

```
# before
MANPATH=C:\Work\tools\mise\installs\usage\7.1.2\.mise-packslip\man;C:\Work\tools\msys2\usr\share\man;...

# after
MANPATH=/c/Work/tools/mise/installs/usage/7.1.2/.mise-packslip/man:/usr/share/man:...
```

`MANPATH` is now converted the same way `PATH` is: entries are mapped to the active runtime's POSIX paths and joined with `:`. Unlike `PATH`, empty entries are kept, because an empty `MANPATH` component tells `man` to retain its platform defaults (packslip relies on this).

Applies to bash and zsh (`set_env`) and fish (`set -gx MANPATH`). It only takes effect when mise detects a MSYS2/Cygwin parent; other platforms and shells are unchanged.

Tested with a unit test of the list mapping (including an empty entry). I have not run this on Windows, and there is no new `e2e-win` test.

Fixes #15107

title: fix(uninstall): don't remove 3.4.12 when asked to uninstall 3.4.1
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3006/changes/mise/1122
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise uninstall <tool> <version>` matched the version as a raw string prefix, so asking to remove a version that was not installed could remove a different one:

```
$ mise ls --installed ruby
ruby  3.4.12
$ mise uninstall ruby 3.4.1
mise WARN  ruby@3.4.1 is not installed
✓ removed 1 tool: ruby@3.4.12
```

Uninstall now uses the same version matching as the rest of mise: a query matches a version that equals it or continues it after a separator (`.`, `-`, `+`). `3.4.1` still matches `3.4.1`, `3.4.1.2` and `3.4.1-rc1`, and `3.4` still selects every `3.4.x`, but `3.4.1` no longer matches `3.4.12`. This is string matching only; it makes no assumption that versions are semver, so date, tag and vendor-prefixed versions behave as they do everywhere else.

With the fix, the example above only prints the `is not installed` warning and leaves `3.4.12` in place. When several installed versions are only string-prefix siblings, `mise uninstall ruby@3.4.1` no longer reports "multiple tools specified".

Adds an e2e case to `cli/test_uninstall` that installs `dummy@1.1.1` and `dummy@1.1.12`, checks that uninstalling `1.1.1` leaves `1.1.12`, and that repeating it only warns. It fails on `main` and passes here.

Fixes #15110.

title: docs(secrets): note that fnox daemon reads need fnox 1.43.0
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3005/changes/mise/1121
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Since the fnox-client 1.43.0 bump in #15043, mise reads cached secrets only from a daemon started by **fnox 1.43.0 or newer**. fnox 1.43.0 moved its daemon to protocol 7, and the protocol is part of the socket path. A daemon from fnox 1.39–1.42 still runs, but mise no longer finds it: `mise run` falls back to the fnox CLI, and `mise secrets ls` reports `daemon: not running`. Secrets still resolve, just without the daemon's cache.

```text
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise run deploy        # fnox 1.42 daemon running
DEBUG secrets: fnox daemon not used (Absent); using the fnox CLI

$ mise use fnox@1.43                  # restart the daemon on the new protocol
$ mise secrets ls
fnox · profile dev · ~/src/app (mise.toml) · fnox 1.43.0 · daemon: running (protocol 7)
```

The CLI path still works with fnox 1.39.0 or newer. To get daemon cache hits again, upgrade fnox to 1.43.0 or newer.

## Changes

- Docs: the fnox page now says daemon reads need fnox 1.43.0, and that an older fnox's daemon counts as not running. The `mise secrets ls` examples show protocol 7.
- e2e: `test_mise_secrets_fnox_daemon` now pins fnox 1.43.0 and expects protocol 7. It still pinned 1.39.0, so it has failed on every release run since #15043, including the 2026.10.22 release PR (#15045).
- The test drops its `_slow` suffix. It runs in about 7s, and the suffix kept it off every PR except release PRs, which is why #15043 merged green.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e secrets/test_mise_secrets_fnox_daemon` passes locally with fnox 1.43.0: the first run resolves through the CLI, the second is a daemon hit, and `mise secrets ls` reports `daemon: running (protocol 7)`.
- `cargo test --lib status_line_names_the_protocol` passes.

title: fix(ls): show uninstalled lazy tools as lazy instead of missing
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3004/changes/mise/1120
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A lazy tool that hasn't been installed yet is waiting for its first run, but mise showed it as if something were wrong. `mise ls` marked it as a red, struck-through `(missing)`, and every bare `mise upgrade` listed it among the tools it resolved, even though the upgrade leaves it alone. With a distribution's defaults, such as Omarchy's 31 lazy tools, that looks like a pile of broken or forced installs on every update.

Now `mise ls` marks it `(lazy)`, dimmed, the same label `mise doctor` and `mise outdated` already use:

```
dummy        1.0.0         /etc/mise/config.toml  1.0.0
needs-dummy  1.0.0 (lazy)  /etc/mise/config.toml  1.0.0
```

and a bare `mise upgrade` lists only the tools it actually looks up:

```
mise by @jdx – resolving 1 tool
mise ✓ dummy  1ms
```

Once a lazy tool is installed, both commands show it like any other tool. A tool that isn't lazy and isn't installed is still `(missing)`, as is a lazy declaration that can't install on first use because safe mode refuses it, it has no commands to shim, or `shims.exclude` removes all of them. In `mise ls --json`, an uninstalled lazy tool still has `"installed": false`, and `mise ls --missing` still includes it.

A new e2e test covers both commands; its `(lazy)` and upgrade assertions fail without the change. The existing lazy, `ls` and upgrade e2e tests pass.

title: fix(prune): keep only the running version of a tool started through a moved link
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3002/changes/mise/1119
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When a tool is configured as `latest` (or a prefix such as `20`), mise puts its runtime link (`installs/claude/latest`) on `PATH`. So a launcher that finds the tool on `PATH` starts it through that link. Every upgrade retargets the link, and after that `mise prune` and deferred upgrade pruning could no longer tell which version a long-running process started from. They kept **every** version of the tool for as long as the process ran.

On a machine that always has an agent session open, such as Claude Code with `auto_update = "4h"`, that meant old versions were never cleaned up. Omarchy ran into exactly this (omacom/omarchy#16852): each claude session pinned all of its installed versions, even though the process only ran one.

Now, when the path through the moved link is the process's own executable, mise uses the executable's real location to work out the version. Only that version is kept, and the others become prunable again. For example, take a claude session started as `installs/claude/latest/claude` while `latest` pointed at 2.1.309, followed by two upgrades. `mise ls --prunable` used to list no claude versions while the session ran. It now lists the versions that nothing else uses, and keeps 2.1.309 for the session.

A command-line path that only goes through the link to a script, such as `sh installs/tool/latest/bin/tool.sh`, still keeps every version. In that case the executable is the interpreter, which tells nothing about the script's version. This works with both the legacy and the identity install layouts. The `upgrade.auto_prune` docs now say what counts as running from a version.

## Validation

- New unit tests start a copied binary through a `latest` link, retarget the link, and check that only the binary's own version counts as running, in both install layouts. The first test fails without the fix.
- `test_prune_running_process` and `test_upgrade_no_prune` e2e pass, and so does clippy on CI's toolchain.

The claude example was not reproduced with a live session. The unit tests cover the same launch shape.

title: feat(bootstrap): print a hook's description or one line instead of its whole script
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/3000/changes/mise/1118
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap` printed the whole rendered script before every hook, so a hook that only checks a condition filled the output on every run, even when it did nothing. Quieting it with `-q` also hid every other info message.

A hook table can now set `description`, and mise prints it instead of the script:

```toml
[bootstrap.hooks.final]
description = "Remove the root copy of pam_reattach if Homebrew removed the module"
run = '''
copy=/usr/local/lib/pam/pam_reattach.so
if [ ! -e /opt/homebrew/lib/pam/pam_reattach.so ] && [ -e "$copy" ]; then
  sudo rm -f "$copy"
fi
'''
```

```text
mise bootstrap: final hooks
mise Remove the root copy of pam_reattach if Homebrew removed the module
```

Without a `description`, mise prints `$` and the first line of the command, cut to the terminal width, as it does for tasks (`truncate = false` and agent/CI runs print it uncut). The description sits on the first command of a `run` array and applies to the whole table, so later commands in it run without a header.

`--verbose` prints the full script, and so does `--dry-run`, which shows what a real run would execute.

A remote host's own config and a shared config that both have a hook for the same phase are merged into one list of commands, which prints without descriptions. The docs say so.

Unknown keys in a hook table are still ignored without a warning, so a typo like `run_window` stays silent. That tolerance is deliberate (a hook from a newer mise must still load), so this PR leaves it alone.

Tests: unit tests for parsing and the header line, plus an e2e case in `test_bootstrap` covering the description, the truncated line, `--verbose` and `--dry-run`.

Implements [the proposal in discussion 15104](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15104).

title: fix(lock): install pipx tools when only the current platform is locked
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2978/changes/mise/1111
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise install pipx:<tool>` no longer fails with `missing lockfile entry` when `lockfile_platforms` lists only the current platform.

With `lockfile_mode = "generate"` (the default) and a lockfile used on a single machine, the tool installed but the command exited 1 and the lockfile was left unchanged:

```toml
[tools]
python = "3.14"
uv = "latest"
"pipx:yamllint" = "1.38.0"

[settings]
lockfile = true
lockfile_platforms = ["macos-arm64"]
```

```console
$ mise lock --global
$ MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=generate mise install pipx:yamllint
mise ERROR missing lockfile entry for pipx:yamllint@1.38.0
previous lockfiles were preserved
```

The same install now succeeds. This is the pipx counterpart of #14994, which was fixed for npm tools.

## Cause

While installing, mise prepares lockfile entries for the platforms other than the host, since the installer owns the host artifact. When the host is the only target, nothing is left to prepare, so the candidate lockfile has no entry for the tool. The uv dependency graph step then tried to attach a graph to that missing entry and failed. The npm path already skipped tools with no target platform; the pipx path did not. It now uses the same `tools_on_platforms` filter that `mise lock` uses.

## Testing

New e2e test `backend/test_pypi_lock_current_platform_only` limits `lockfile_platforms` to the host, then runs `MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=generate mise install --force pipx:mise-lock-cli`. Without the fix it fails with the error above; with it, it passes. `mise run lint-fix` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

Fixes #15090

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved lockfile generation for platform-specific configurations by limiting dependency resolution to tools supported by the selected platforms.

* **Tests**

author: jdx
diff:
--- e2e/backend/test_pypi_lock_current_platform_only (+32/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+# With lockfile_platforms limited to the host, `mise install` in generate mode
+# has no foreign platform to prepare. It must not try to attach a uv graph to a

title: feat(shell): add --all to `mise shell --unset`
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2976/changes/mise/1109
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise shell node@20` overrides a tool version for the current shell by setting `MISE_NODE_VERSION`. Until now the only way to undo several of those overrides was `mise shell --unset <tool>` once per tool. `mise shell --unset --all` now removes them all at once:

```
$ mise shell java@temurin-25 node@20
$ mise shell --unset --all
$ java -version   # back to what mise.toml requests
```

Details:

- `--all` only works together with `--unset`. `mise shell --all` fails with `--all can only be used with --unset`, and combining `--all` with tool arguments is rejected.
- It removes every `MISE_<TOOL>_VERSION` in the shell, including aliased spellings such as `MISE_NODEJS_VERSION`. That includes variables you exported by hand rather than through `mise shell`; the flag's help text says so.
- A bare `mise shell --unset` with no tools still errors, so nothing is removed unless you ask for `--all`.

Validation: new e2e test `e2e/cli/test_shell_unset_all` (sets two tools through `mise shell` and one by hand, runs `--unset --all`, checks all three are gone, plus the error cases); existing `test_shell_no_version` still passes; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint` are clean. The usage spec and man page were regenerated; `docs/cli/shell.md` was edited by hand to match, because `render:usage` wipes `docs/cli` when it fails in a worktree.

Closes #15084

title: feat(dotfiles): set permissions on a file a merge entry creates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2975/changes/mise/1108
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `merge` dotfiles entry can seed a config file with defaults, but it could not give that file a mode. From discussion #14884: keep a template for local API tokens in Git, have `mise dot apply` create the file once, and fill the tokens in locally. With `merge = "missing"` that worked except the file was created with the default mode, which is not what you want for a token.

`merge` entries now take `permissions`:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/mise/conf.d/private.local.toml/seed" = { source = "templates/private.toml", merge = "missing", permissions = "0600" }
```

- The mode is set only when apply **creates** the target. A file that already exists keeps its mode, because the application or user that writes it owns the file. Nothing reports mode drift for a merge entry.
- The first apply creates the file from the source at `0600`. Later applies add only the keys it lacks, so a token you type stays, and a deleted file is created again.
- To keep an existing file's mode too, add a permissions-only entry for the same path.
- Merge entries for one file that declare different modes are refused, so the mode never depends on apply order. `permissions` is ignored with a warning on Windows, as for other entries.
- Block and line edits still reject `permissions`, since they never create their file's mode.

Merge covers JSON, TOML and YAML targets. For files in other formats, such as `.netrc` or `.env`, #15080 adds `create_if_missing` instead.

Tested with unit tests for parsing, a new e2e test (`test_dotfiles_merge_permissions`: create at the mode, an edited file and mode kept, recreate after delete, conflicting modes, a bad mode, block edits rejecting the key), a schema e2e test, and `schema_matches_parser`. Clippy and lint pass.

title: chore(deps): stop lock file maintenance from downgrading crates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2973/changes/mise/1107
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Weekly `lock file maintenance` PRs have been downgrading the AWS SDK and other crates, and the next "update rust crates" PR then bumps them back. That happened twice on 2026-10-27 (#15043 and #15062 lowered `aws-sdk-s3` to 1.122.0; #15050 and #15065 restored 1.155.0), and the open #15085 would lower it again. This is internal-only: it changes no mise behavior, but it stops the lockfile churn.

## Cause

The workspace uses `resolver = "3"`, so cargo picks dependency versions whose `rust-version` fits the *lowest* `rust-version` declared by any workspace member. `crates/mise-agent-env` declared `1.88` while the root crate and the other crates that set one declare `1.95`. A full re-resolve (what Renovate's lock file maintenance does) therefore fell back to versions that build on 1.88:

| crate | before (needs) | after fallback (needs) |
|---|---|---|
| `aws-sdk-s3` | 1.155.0 (1.94.1) | 1.122.0 (1.88) |
| `aws-smithy-runtime` | 1.16.2 (1.94.1) | 1.10.0 (1.88) |
| `uuid` | 1.28.0 (1.89) | 1.26.1 (1.85) |
| `lru` | 0.18.5 | 0.16.4 |

A targeted `cargo update -p` isn't limited that way, which is why the follow-up bumps worked.

## Change

Raise `mise-agent-env`'s `rust-version` from 1.88 to 1.95 to match the rest of the workspace. The crate had declared 1.88 in #13627 because it uses let chains; 1.95 is a superset, but anyone building `mise-agent-env` on its own with Rust 1.88–1.94 will now be refused by cargo.

## Validation

Regenerating the lockfile from scratch (`rm Cargo.lock && cargo generate-lockfile`) with cargo 1.100.0-beta.7:

- before: `aws-sdk-s3` 1.122.0, `uuid` 1.26.1, `lru` 0.16.4
- after: `aws-sdk-s3` 1.155.0, `aws-smithy-runtime` 1.16.2, `uuid` 1.29.0, `lru` 0.18.5

`cargo check -p mise-agent-env` passes. `Cargo.lock` itself is unchanged by this PR. #15085 should be closed or rebased after this merges so Renovate regenerates it.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/packslip</summary>

### [`v1.9.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/packslip/releases/tag/v1.9.1): : Stop trusting compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/packslip/compare/v1.9.0...v1.9.1)

packslip now ships an updated TLS trust store and certificate verifier. The private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised, and this release stops trusting them. The manifest format and verification rules have not changed.

##### Fixed

- Moved the bundled TLS trust material to the patched releases: `rustls-webpki` 0.103.16 and `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.10. Browsers already block the compromised eMudhra intermediates ([details](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/)), and the packslip CLI and the `jdx/packslip` Action now reject HTTPS connections that chain through them too. Connections that relied on those certificates will now fail. If you use packslip as a library, the change only applies to your own build once you run `cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-root-certs`. [#​246](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/packslip/issues/246) ([@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/packslip/compare/v1.9.0...v1.9.1>

</details>

title: feat: add --no-global and --project scope flags, deprecate --local
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2967/changes/mise/1104
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`--local` means two different things in mise. On `ls`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and `tasks ls` it means "everything except global config", parent directories included. On `settings`, and on the new `uninstall --local`, it means the nearest project config. So `mise ls --local` does not preview what `mise uninstall --local` removes.

This stacks on #15079 and renames that PR's flag before it ships.

```console
$ cd ~/work/app            # ~/work/mise.toml also exists
$ mise ls --no-global      # app's config and ~/work's, not the global config
$ mise ls --project        # app's config only
$ mise uninstall --project # removes the versions app's config names, after asking
```

## What changes

- **`mise uninstall --project`** replaces `mise uninstall --local` from #15079. Nothing released uses the old name, so there is no alias.
- **`mise ls --project`** lists the versions the nearest project's config files request. It uses the same file selection as `uninstall --project`, so it shows what that command works from. A version that a later file in the directory overrides is not listed, as with `--no-global`, while `uninstall --project` still removes it and lists it before asking. `MISE_<TOOL>_VERSION` is ignored.
- **`--no-global`** on `ls`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and `tasks ls` does what `--local` did there: only tools or tasks from non-global config. On `ls`, `outdated` and `upgrade` it conflicts with `--global` and `--local`. On `tasks ls`, where `-g` and `-l` already override each other (the later flag wins), `--no-global` follows the same rule.
- **`--local` is deprecated** on those four commands in favor of `--no-global`. The flag help and docs say so now, and it keeps working. mise starts warning on 2027.1.0:

  ```text
  mise WARN  deprecated [cli.ls.local]: `mise ls --local` is deprecated. Use `mise ls --no-global` instead. This will be removed in mise 2027.7.0.
  ```

  `settings --local` and `lock --local` are unchanged.

## Timeline

| When | What happens |
|---|---|
| Now (2026.10) | `--no-global` and `--project` ship. `--local` works as before, without a warning. |
| 2027.1.0 | `--local` starts warning. |
| 2027.7.0 | `--local` is removed from `ls`, `outdated`, `upgrade` and `tasks ls`. It fails as an unknown flag. |

The three silent months are the compatibility window: `--no-global` is new, so older mise versions reject it, and warning people to switch before it is widely available would send them to a flag their other machines do not have. The six months of warning is shorter than the 12-month default, on purpose. `--local` is not coming back: it would read as `mise.local.toml`, which `mise lock --local` and `mise dot --local` already mean, and `--project` and `--no-global` cover both scopes it could take.

## Things to know

- **Merge with #15079.** If #15079 shipped alone, `uninstall --local` would ship and then need

title: feat(dotfiles): add create_if_missing to seed a file once
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2966/changes/mise/1103
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`copy`, `template`, and inline `content` dotfile entries overwrite their target on every apply, so a file that is meant to be filled in on the machine can't be managed. The motivating case, from discussion #14884: keep a template for local API tokens in Git, have `mise dot apply` put it in place once, and then type the tokens into the destination without the next apply wiping them.

`create_if_missing = true` makes the entry write the target only while nothing exists there:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/mise/conf.d/private.local.toml" = { source = "templates/private.toml", mode = "copy", permissions = "0600", create_if_missing = true }
```

- Nothing at the target: the source is copied and `permissions` is set.
- Anything but a directory at the target, a symlink included: it is left exactly as it is, content and permissions both. `mise dot status` reports it as applied and `mise dot diff` shows nothing, so your edits are never drift.
- The target is deleted: the next apply creates it again.

Details:

- A template is not rendered while its target exists, so `exec()` in it does not run.
- A directory at the target is still a conflict that needs `--force`.
- The key works on `[dotfiles]` entries and on `[dotfile_groups.<name>.entries]`. It needs a file source with `mode = "copy"` or `"template"`, or inline `content`. mise warns and ignores an entry that combines it with a directory source, `symlink`, `symlink-each`, `absent`, `track`, or a permissions-only entry (a directory source with `mode = "copy"` fails the apply with an error naming the key).
- `mise dot unapply` keeps a seeded file you have since edited unless you pass `--force`, like any other copy whose content no longer matches.
- `[bootstrap.files]` is unchanged; this covers `[dotfiles]` only.

`merge = "missing"` is the closest thing available today, but it cannot set permissions, and a key deleted locally is filled back in. The name follows the discussion's suggestion (`create_if_missing` rather than `copy_once`, since the file is recreated when deleted).

Tested with a new e2e test (`test_dotfiles_create_if_missing`: copy, template, inline content, group entry, symlink, directory, deleted target, invalid combinations), a schema e2e test, and a unit test of the validation rules. Clippy, `schema_matches_parser`, and lint pass.

title: feat(uninstall): add --local to remove a project's installed tools
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2964/changes/mise/1102
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise uninstall --local` removes the installed versions that the current project's config requests, so you can tear a project down to a clean state and reinstall it. Previously this took `mise ls --current | awk ... | xargs mise uninstall`, and `--current` also picks up inherited and global tools.

```console
$ cd ~/work/app
$ mise uninstall --local --yes
mise dummy@1.1.0 is requested by ~/work/app/mise.toml
mise ✓ dummy@1.1.0  210ms
```

Without `--yes` it asks before removing anything.

## What "local" means

The project is the nearest directory, starting at the working directory and moving up, that has a mise config file. Every config file in that directory counts: `mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `conf.d` fragments, `.tool-versions` and idiomatic version files. Configs in parent directories and global or system configs do not, so running it in `~/work/app` does not remove what `~/work/mise.toml` requests.

This is narrower than `mise ls --local`, which lists every non-global config source including parent directories. I left `ls --local` alone; aligning it would be a separate behavior change.

## Things to know

- Installs are shared by every project. Another project that uses the same version has to install it again, and the help text says so.
- It lists each version with the file that requests it, then asks for confirmation. `--yes` skips the question, `--dry-run` and `--dry-run-code` list without removing, and with nobody to ask it fails instead of removing.
- It conflicts with `--all` and explicit tool arguments.
- If the nearest config requests nothing that is installed, it says so and exits 0. With no config file in or above the working directory it errors.
- It only removes installed versions; it does not edit `mise.toml`. `mise unuse` does both.

Requested in [Discussion #10930](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10930).

## Validation

New e2e test `e2e/cli/test_uninstall_local` covers nearest-root selection (a parent's `.tool-versions` stays untouched, then is the local config when run from the parent), dry runs, the refusal without a terminal, `--yes`, the nothing-to-do case and the flag conflicts. `test_uninstall` and `test_install_layout_uninstall` still pass, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(github): ask for fewer releases when api.github.com times out listing them
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2963/changes/mise/1101
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Listing the releases of a repository whose releases each carry hundreds of assets no longer fails when api.github.com times out on a page of 100.

For example, `github:be5invis/Iosevka` has about 450 assets per release. When mise-versions can't answer, mise asks GitHub for `releases?per_page=100`, which GitHub answers with a 504, so resolving the tool errors:

```
mise ERROR HTTP status server error (504 Gateway Timeout) for url
  (https://api.github.com/repos/be5invis/Iosevka/releases?per_page=100)
```

GitHub serves a smaller page of the same list (`per_page=30` answers in about 7 s). On a 5xx for the first page, mise now asks again with `per_page=30`, then `per_page=10`, before giving up. Later pages follow GitHub's `Link` header, which keeps the smaller size. Other errors, such as a 404, are not retried with a smaller page, and nothing changes for repositories GitHub answers normally.

Resolving a bare `latest` already goes through `/releases/latest` first (one small request); the full list is only needed when that shortcut can't answer, or for a prefix or filter. I couldn't reproduce `latest` skipping the shortcut for this repository (mise-versions and GitHub both answered `/releases/latest` quickly), so this PR fixes the listing that fails once it is needed rather than changing the shortcut. If the reporter still sees the list being requested for a plain `latest`, a `MISE_DEBUG=1` log would show why.

## Validation

- New unit tests: a 504 on `per_page=100` followed by a 200 on `per_page=30` returns the releases; a 404 is not retried with a smaller page.
- `cargo clippy -p mise-util --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Not verified against the live Iosevka list from a built mise.

Fixes #15075

title: feat(dotfiles): merge into JSONC files such as VS Code's settings.json
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2962/changes/mise/1100
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

VS Code's `settings.json` allows comments and trailing commas, so a `merge` dotfiles entry failed on it as invalid JSON. A merge entry can now edit JSONC.

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/Code/User/settings.json/shared" = { source = "vscode/shared.json", merge = true, format = "jsonc" }
```

With a target like:

```jsonc
{
  // my theme
  "workbench.colorTheme": "Dark+", // keep
}
```

applying sets the keys in `vscode/shared.json` and leaves comments, indentation, trailing commas and every key the source doesn't own as written. The source may also contain comments.

- A `.jsonc` target is detected by extension. For a file like `settings.json`, set the new `format` key (`"json"`, `"jsonc"`, `"toml"` or `"yaml"`); an unknown value skips the entry with a warning.
- A plain `.json` target without `format` is still strict JSON, so existing setups behave the same.
- JSONC means comments and trailing commas only. Single-quoted strings, unquoted keys and other JSON5 syntax are rejected.
- A merge source that fails to parse now reports the file and the parse error (`invalid merge source /path/shared.json: failed to parse the JSON source: ...`) instead of a bare `invalid merge source`.

Adds the `jsonc-parser` crate (MIT) to `mise-util` for in-place editing.

Closes the request in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15070.

Validated with unit tests for the JSONC merge, the `test_dotfiles_merge_jsonc` and `test_dotfiles_merge_edits` e2e tests, the `mise-config` schema tests, and workspace clippy.

Co-authored-by: TimonLukas <18093957+TimonLukas@users.noreply.github.com>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.308.*


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Dotfile merges support JSONC, preserving existing comments and trailing commas while combining settings.
  * Specify `json`, `jsonc`, `toml`, or `yaml` when a target’s extension does not identify the format; `.jsonc` targets are detected automatically.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Unsupported explicit formats and `format` settings on non-merge entries are rejected. Errors for file-based merge sources include the source file path.

title: fix(release): include shell completions in Debian packages
body:
Debian packages from the mise APT repository omit shell completions, so installing mise through apt does not install its completion scripts. Include Bash, Zsh, and Fish completions in both the amd64 and arm64 packages built with fpm, using the same system paths as the Ubuntu PPA packages.

Validation: scoped hk checks (ShellCheck and shfmt), Bash syntax validation, and checks that both architecture commands map all three existing completion files to their expected paths passed. A full Debian package build was not run because Docker is not running locally.

title: feat(vars): add --json and --json-extended to mise vars
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2959/changes/mise/1097
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise vars` only printed a table, so scripts that needed the vars and where they come from had to scrape it. It now takes `--json` (`-J`) and `--json-extended`, matching `mise env` and `mise settings ls`:

```console
$ mise vars --json
{
  "greeting": "hello",
  "secret": "[redacted]"
}

$ mise vars --json-extended
{
  "greeting": {
    "value": "hello",
    "source": "~/project/mise.toml"
  },
  "secret": {
    "value": "[redacted]",
    "source": "~/project/mise.toml"
  }
}
```

Both flags work on `mise vars` and `mise vars ls`. Values hidden with `redact` stay `[redacted]`, as in the table. The flags are mutually exclusive, and both conflict with `--no-header`.

Co-authored-by: Artem Klevtsov <603798+artemklevtsov@users.noreply.github.com>

Closes discussion https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15059

## Testing

New e2e test `config/test_vars_json` covers both flags, the `ls` form, `-J`, redaction and the `--no-header` conflict; it passes. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint` are clean. Generated docs are limited to the vars pages, since usage 7.1.3 rewrites unrelated pages that the CI version leaves alone.

title: fix(version): never report a latest version older than the running one in version --json
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2958/changes/mise/1096
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise version --json` could report a `latest` older than the version you are running, which breaks scripts that compare the two to decide whether to update.

`latest` is the newest release that has passed the `minimum_release_age` gate (24h by default). A build newer than that, such as a fresh release or a nightly, therefore saw an older release as `latest`:

```json
{
  "version": "2026.10.21 linux-x64 (2026-10-27)",
  "latest": "2026.10.19"
}
```

Now, when the running version is newer than the newest eligible release, `latest` reports the running version (`"latest": "2026.10.21"`), meaning there is nothing newer to update to. `latest` is unchanged when it is equal to or newer than the running version, and is still `null` when the lookup fails. Plain `mise version` already warned only when a newer release existed, so its output is unchanged.

Added a unit test, `latest_is_never_older_than_current`, covering older, equal, newer and missing `latest` values.

Fixes #15061

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * JSON version output now reports the current version when a parseable latest-release value is older, preventing the displayed latest version from falling behind.
  * Equal or newer latest-release values remain unchanged. Missing or unparseable values are also left as provided, so the adjustment applies only when the latest version can be compared and is older.
  * This behavior also applies when a minimum release age makes the latest eligible release older than the running version.

title: registry: fix docuum and android-sdk test expectations
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2957/changes/mise/1095
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `test-tool` registry tests for `docuum` and `android-sdk` currently fail on every run, which turns the `test-tool` matrix jobs red on unrelated PRs (for example #15064).

- `docuum`: 0.27.3 prints `Docuum 0.27.3`, but the test expected lowercase `docuum {{version}}`. The test now expects `Docuum {{version}}`.
- `android-sdk`: `sdkmanager` is deprecated and now prints a warning before `1.1.16717390 (Android CLI)`, so the old `.0` expectation no longer matches. The test now runs `android --version` (the replacement binary, which prints only `1.1.16717390`), and `android` is added to `bins`.

I confirmed both outputs locally by installing the tools and running the commands. This does not touch `gcloud`, which fails separately with `module 'python' not found`.

title: fix(config): stop warning about a version-file link to a sibling version file
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2953/changes/mise/1091
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A project that keeps `.nvmrc` as a link to the `.node-version` beside it no longer gets a `not reading …/.nvmrc` warning. The warning repeated for every tracked project and worktree, in commands such as `mise bootstrap`.

```sh
echo 22 > .node-version
ln -s .node-version .nvmrc
mise current node
```

Before: `mise WARN  not reading …/.nvmrc: it is a symlink to a file of another name…`, then `22`. Since #15006 the node version was already read from `.node-version`, but the warning stayed.
After: `22`, with no warning.

mise still never reads a version file that is a link to a file of another name, so a link such as `.nvmrc -> .env` cannot turn a local secret into a "version". Only the warning changes, and only when the link stays in its own directory and ends at a recognized version file (an idiomatic filename of an enabled tool, or a tool-versions filename such as `.tool-versions`). That file is read under its own name, so the warning has nothing left to tell the user. A link to any other file, or one that leaves the directory, still warns.

## Test plan

- `mise run test:e2e test_linked_version_file test_task_monorepo_linked_version_file`: `.nvmrc -> .node-version` and `versions.toml -> .tool-versions` are silent and still resolve; `.nvmrc -> .env` still warns and never prints its text.
- Unit test `a_link_to_a_sibling_version_file_is_told_apart_from_other_links`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Related: #15006. Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/15051

title: feat(http): add ipv4_only setting for hosts that fail over IPv6
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2952/changes/mise/1090
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On a dual-stack machine where one host answers wrongly over IPv6, mise had no way to avoid it. In #15047, `dl.google.com` returns `404 Not Found` over IPv6 and 200 over IPv4, so `mise install go` fails. The Sigstore TUF trust root fails to load the same way, so `uv` and `tree-sitter` fail attestation verification (`timestamp.json not found`). The reporter's only fix was `precedence ::ffff:0:0/96 100` in `/etc/gai.conf`.

This adds an `ipv4_only` setting that makes mise connect over IPv4 only:

```toml
[settings]
ipv4_only = true
```

or `MISE_IPV4_ONLY=1`. The default is `false`, so nothing changes unless it is set.

It covers the connections mise makes with its own HTTP client: downloads, version lookups, GitHub API calls, attestation verification, vfox plugins and the GitHub relay. Programs mise runs, such as `git`, `npm` or a tool's installer, still follow the system resolver, and so does the package manager embedded in the `npm:` backend (aube builds its own clients); the setting's docs point to `gai.conf` for those. A host with no IPv4 address cannot be reached while it is on.

Implementation: every client is built through `mise_tls::build_client`, which now binds the unspecified IPv4 address when the flag is set, and `load()` in `src/config/settings.rs` pushes the setting into it. The sigstore library builds its own HTTP client for the default TUF fetch, so `select_tuf_config` and `github_tuf_trusted_root` now hand it mise's client when `ipv4_only` is on. Clients built before settings load or reload keep their address family.

Testing: a `mise-tls` unit test checks that an IPv4-only client cannot reach a listener on `[::1]` while a default client can. An e2e test serves a version list over `[::1]` only and over `127.0.0.1`, and checks that `MISE_IPV4_ONLY=1` makes the IPv6 host fail and the IPv4 host succeed, while the IPv6 host works without it. Clippy is clean and the `mise-sigstore` trust tests pass. I did not reproduce the Google/Sigstore IPv6 failures themselves; they depend on the reporter's network.

Fixes #15047

title: fix(packslip): log versions held back by minimum_release_age at debug level
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2950/changes/mise/1089
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `minimum_release_age` set, resolving a packslip tool printed a warning for every recent version the delay held back. A version held back by the delay is what the user asked for, so these are no longer warnings.

Before, with `minimum_release_age = "3d"` and `hk = "latest"`:

```text
$ mise latest hk
mise WARN  packslip:github.com/jdx/hk: skipping 2.9.0: verified release time is after the allowed cutoff
mise WARN  packslip:github.com/jdx/hk: skipping 2.8.2: verified release time is after the allowed cutoff
2.8.1
```

After, the same command prints only `2.8.1`. The skipped versions still appear with `MISE_DEBUG=1`. This matches other backends, such as uv, which do not warn about versions the delay holds back.

This applies to any release-age cutoff, including one set with `--before`, since each is a cutoff the user chose. Other reasons a packslip version is skipped (no compatible artifact, unmet requirements) still warn. #14835 already silenced the message for an installed version; this covers the versions that are not installed.

Validated with `cargo check`. No new e2e test: reproducing a held-back release needs a live packslip release inside the cooling window.

Fixes discussion #15052.

title: fix(gem): quote paths in generated wrapper scripts
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2949/changes/mise/1088
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The bash wrapper that mise writes into `bin/` for each installed gem executable interpolated the executable path unquoted:

```bash
GEM_HOME="/path/libexec" exec /path/libexec/bin/tool "$@"
```

If the install directory or the executable's name contained a space or a shell metacharacter, bash split or parsed the path instead of running it. For example, with `MISE_DATA_DIR="/home/my user/.local/share/mise"` the wrapper tried to exec `/home/my` and failed.

Both `GEM_HOME` and the executable path are now always single-quoted (with embedded single quotes escaped), so they are passed as a single, unexpanded word. Spaces, `;`, `$(...)`, and brace patterns like `{1,2}` in a path are all safe.

## Testing

A new unit test generates the wrapper for install directories and an executable name containing spaces, `;`, `$(...)`, braces, and single quotes, runs it, and checks that the right executable ran with `GEM_HOME` and arguments intact and that nothing else was executed. `cargo clippy --lib --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

title: fix(config): treat an empty system_packages.elevate_with as "never elevate"
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2947/changes/mise/1086
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Setting `system_packages.elevate_with = ""` used to be ignored: mise fell back to the first of `sudo`, `run0` or `doas` on `PATH`. On a host with no root to get, such as Termux, `mise bootstrap packages` then failed trying to run `sudo`. The only workaround was a placeholder like `elevate_with = "env"`.

An explicitly empty value now means "never elevate". mise runs package manager commands as the current user, with nothing in front:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings]
system_packages.elevate_with = ""
```

```console
$ mise bootstrap packages apply --dry-run
snap install hello
```

`MISE_SYSTEM_PACKAGES_ELEVATE_WITH=""` behaves the same. An unset value is unchanged and still picks an elevator from `PATH`. There is no `sudo -n` probe, no "requires a password" error and no manual-command hint when it is empty, and the brew cask shim is told elevation is denied because it can only call `sudo`.

If `system_packages.sudo = false` is also set, the empty `elevate_with` wins and commands run directly rather than failing.

Validation: new e2e `test_system_elevate_with_empty` uses a fake `snap` and a `sudo` that fails if called, and checks that `apply` runs `snap` directly. `test_system_snap` and `test_elevate_with_global_only` still pass, and workspace clippy is clean.

Fixes #15044

title: fix(aqua): stop warning "invalid aqua tool" for custom registry packages
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2945/changes/mise/1085
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Packages from a custom aqua registry whose name has no `owner/repo` shape, such as the `proxy-3p-beads` entry in #15037, made mise print a warning on essentially every command that touched them, dozens of times per run, even though the tool resolved and installed fine:

```
mise WARN  invalid aqua tool: proxy-3p-beads
```

A bare name that is not in mise's own registry can legitimately be defined by a custom registry in `aqua.registries`. Which registry defines it can only be decided by an async lookup, so the check made when the backend is constructed could not tell a valid custom package from a typo. It warned for both.

The warning is removed. A name that no registry defines still fails with `package not found: <name>` the first time the package is looked up, so a typo is still reported, once and as an error.

```toml
[settings]
aqua.registries = ["registry.yaml"]

[tools]
"aqua:my-bare-tool" = "1.0.0"   # defined in registry.yaml, bare name
```

Before, `mise ls` printed `invalid aqua tool: my-bare-tool` repeatedly. Now it lists the tool with no warning.

## Validation

- New e2e `backend/test_aqua_custom_registry_bare_name` uses a local custom registry with a bare-named `http` package and asserts `mise ls` lists it without the warning. It passes on this branch; mise 2026.10.11 prints the warning five times on the same config.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean apart from an existing `junction` manifest warning in `mise-util`.

Fixes #15037

### Release Notes

</details>

<details>
<summary>houseabsolute/ubi (ubi)</summary>

### [`v0.13.0`](https://redirect.github.com/houseabsolute/ubi/blob/HEAD/Changes.md#0130---2026-10-21)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/houseabsolute/ubi/compare/v0.12.0...v0.13.0)

- The `ubi` crate no longer declares a minimum supported Rust version (MSRV). It was 1.88. The crate
  is now only tested with the current stable Rust release.
- Fixed a bug where a token env var set to the empty string, like `GITHUB_TOKEN=`, was treated as a
  token. This made `ubi` send an `Authorization: Bearer ` header, which the forge rejects, instead
  of simply making an unauthenticated request. An empty token is now treated as not being set at
  all, whether it comes from an env var or is passed to `UbiBuilder::token`.
- Updated to the latest rustls-webpki and webpki-root-certs crates to remove support for the
  compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates.

</details>

### [`v5.2.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/releases/tag/v5.2.1): : Require the signed packslip for mise 2026.9.3 and later

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.0...v5.2.1)

The action now refuses to install mise 2026.9.3 or later if the release's signed packslip is missing. This closes a gap where verification could be downgraded to the weaker checksum check.

##### Fixed

- **A missing packslip no longer weakens the check on recent mise releases.** v5.2.0 started checking the mise binary against the release's signed `packslip.sigstore.json`. If that file wasn't found, though, the action quietly fell back to the minisign-signed `SHASUMS256` checksums. Anyone who could hide the file could force the weaker check. Every mise release from 2026.9.3 on includes a packslip, so for those versions a missing bundle now stops the install with an error like this:
  ```
  mise v2026.10.11 must ship a signed packslip, but https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/download/v2026.10.11/packslip.sigstore.json was not found
  ```
  Releases before 2026.9.3 don't include a packslip, so they're still checked against the signed checksums. A version string that isn't three dot-separated numbers also requires a packslip. If you set the `sha256` input, it still takes precedence over both checks. A packslip that fails verification still never falls back to the checksums. ([#​695](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/mise-action/pull/695) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/mise-action/compare/v5.2.0...v5.2.1>

title: fix: hide the Windows console for prompt-started tool updates
body:
On Windows, a shell prompt with an `auto_update` tool whose check was due opened a visible Windows Terminal window titled with the `mise.exe` path. One window per due tool, each up for as long as its update ran, so with several opted-in tools a series of windows flashed up every `tool_update.check_duration` (the reporter saw 13 queued from a single prompt).

```toml
# global config
[tools]
"aqua:junegunn/fzf" = { version = "latest", auto_update = true }

[tool_update]
check_duration = "6h"
```

The hook starts `mise __tool-update <tool> --id <id> --background` detached with `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, so that process has no console. It then starts the actual update pass through `Tick::start`, which called `windows_job::spawn(&mut command, 0)`, adding only `CREATE_SUSPENDED`. Windows gives a console program started by a process with no console a new console of its own, which Windows 11 opens in Windows Terminal; the child is not `--watch`, so `hide_if_unattended` never applied and the window stayed up until the pass ended.

`Tick::start` now passes `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, which `windows_job::spawn`'s doc comment already expects callers that need it to pass, so the pass gets a console with no window and everything the pass starts (hooks, downloads, nested mise) inherits it and stays hidden too. The flag changes only the console the child gets, not the std handles it inherits, so wherever a service's output went is unchanged.

This covers both `Tick::start` callers: the prompt-started `--background` path (the reported bug) and the `tool-update` service's `--due` path, including a watcher that itself has no console. Interactive paths are unchanged: `mise __tool-update <tool>` run by a shim or `mise x`, and `mise upgrade --global`, still run in the caller's console so progress and errors stay visible. Unix behavior is unchanged.

Validation: `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass on macOS. The change is Windows-only (`cfg(windows)`), so its compilation and unit checks rely on the Windows CI jobs (`build-windows`, `windows-lint`, `windows-unit`, `windows-e2e`); I have not watched the window disappear on a Windows 11 machine.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14997 (converted from issue #14995).

title: fix(packslip): read a repository's release list from mise-versions first
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2928/changes/mise/1077
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing a `packslip:github.com/owner/repo` tool from a hosted CI runner could fail with an error starting `fetching the release list of packslip:github.com/jdx/hk`, because `raw.githubusercontent.com` answered 429.

mise reads a repository's optional signed release list from `raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/HEAD/.well-known/packslip.json` on every resolution. Nearly every repository has no such file (all 13 `packslip:github.com/…` registry entries return 404 today), but raw rate-limits by source IP and GitHub-hosted runners share IPs, so an unrelated job's traffic can fail the install. A 404 is "no list", but a 429 is an error.

mise now asks mise-versions first, via the `packslip-list` route added in jdx/mise-versions#401. It answers either "this repository has no list" or the list's exact text, and mise verifies the text as before; the mirror is only trusted about presence. mise still reads the file from GitHub, with the user's token, when:

- mise-versions is rate limited, down or times out (the `429`/`5xx` fallback the other mirrored lookups use),
- it does not serve the repository (a private one answers `404`),
- `use_versions_host` is off, or
- a `url_replacements` rule reroutes the raw URL, which makes the replacement the source.

A list or its absence reaches mise within about ten minutes of a change on the default branch, since mise-versions keeps its answer at the edge for that long. A pinned list that goes missing still fails closed.

The route is live (jdx/mise-versions#401 is merged and deployed). Against it, `mise install hk@latest` from a fresh data directory makes one request to the mirror, gets `present: false`, and never asks raw.githubusercontent.com.

Tested with unit tests against a mock mise-versions (absent list never asks raw, exact text from the mirror, `429`/`503`/`404` fall back to raw, a `url_replacements` rule bypasses the mirror) and the existing 109 packslip tests. Dropping the `url_replacements` check makes its test fail.

title: fix(pypi): fall back to version-only locks when a uv graph can't install
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2926/changes/mise/1076
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` on a `pypi:` tool could write a dependency graph that `mise install` then could not replay, because installs run `uv sync --frozen --no-build`. A package like `zstandard` with no wheel for the active interpreter made the next `mise install` fail, and a win32-only sdist-only dependency made `mise lock` itself fail.

`mise lock` now dry-runs the same `uv sync --frozen --no-build` against the freshly resolved graph before accepting it. If the graph can't be installed, or can't be resolved at all, it warns and keeps a version-only entry instead of failing or writing a broken graph:

```
mise pypi:omnigent dependency graph unavailable; keeping a version-only lock entry: ...
```

Fixes #15029

title: fix(lock): degrade to version-only for pypi tools with uvx_args during a lock sweep
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2925/changes/mise/1075
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` with no tool arguments (for example `mise lock --global --bump`) aborted and wrote nothing as soon as one `pypi:`/`pipx:` tool set `uvx_args` or `pipx_args`, even though `mise install` handles the same tool by warning and falling back to version-only resolution.

Now a sweep warns (`dependency graph skipped because uvx_args or pipx_args are configured`), drops the tool's uv graph, and locks it version-only while the rest completes. Naming the tool explicitly (`mise lock pipx:foo`) stays strict and still errors.

Fixes #15028

title: fix(ci): stop ci overrides from killing tests on the shared macOS profile
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2921/changes/mise/1073
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Outside contributors' PRs run `unit-macos` on a shared `macos-14` runner with the `ci-shared` nextest profile, which is supposed to report slow tests without killing them. It still killed one: on #14996 (a Renovate bump unrelated to aqua), `aqua::aqua_registry_wrapper::tests::parses_bundled_registry_from_local_source` hit its 4s ceiling on both attempts and failed the job.

`ci-shared` inherits the per-test `[[profile.ci.overrides]]` from `ci`, and those set `terminate-after`. The comment above `ci-shared` said nextest does not inherit overrides; that is wrong. I confirmed it locally by shrinking that test's override to 1ms and running `--profile ci-shared`: the test was terminated.

This adds a catch-all `[[profile.ci-shared.overrides]]` (`all()`, 1s period, no `terminate-after`), which takes precedence over the inherited ones, and fixes the comment. With the same 1ms override in place, the test now passes and is reported as slow. The trusted `ci` profile is unchanged and keeps its strict ceilings.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

* **Tests**
  * Automated test runs now report slow tests without terminating them based on the slow-test threshold. An overall job timeout remains in place to limit test runs that hang indefinitely. This update affects CI test execution only; it does not change application behavior or add user-facing features.

--- .config/nextest.toml (+6/-2)
@@ -78,9 +78,13 @@ slow-timeout = { period = "1s", terminate-after = 3 }
 # This profile keeps the reporting but drops `terminate-after`, so a slow test is
 # logged and not killed. The period is the trusted ceiling (250ms x 4), which
 # makes the first SLOW line mark exactly the tests that would have failed there.
-# Per-test overrides are deliberately not repeated: nextest does not inherit
-# `overrides`, and without `terminate-after` they would only shift log lines.
+# nextest does inherit `overrides` from `ci`, so the catch-all override below is
+# what keeps those per-test ceilings from killing tests on this profile.
 # A genuine hang is still bounded by the job's `timeout-minutes`.
 [profile.ci-shared]
 inherits = "ci"
 slow-timeout = { period = "1s" }
+
+[[profile.ci-shared.overrides]]
+filter = 'all()'
+slow-timeout = { period = "1s" }

title: feat(dotfiles): set up from a dotfiles checkout or Stow packages with less config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2918/changes/mise/1072
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Setting up machines from your own dotfiles gets simpler: share the whole global config directory, keep mise's config inside a dotfiles checkout, and deploy Stow-style packages without a table for each. Along the way this fixes `--force` destroying source files when a Stow-folded link was in the way, and `--adopt --dry-run` previewing only part of the config.

**Track the whole config directory.** The setup tutorial and the dotfiles overview told you to track `~/.config/mise/config.toml`. That left `config.<env>.toml`, `conf.d/` fragments, and `miserc.toml` behind on the first machine. The docs now track the directory:

```sh
mise dot track ~/.config/mise
mise dot origin set https://github.com/you/setup.git --sync sync
# on another machine
mise bootstrap --adopt you/setup
```

Files ending in `.local.toml` stay on each machine, so each machine can still pick its environments in `miserc.local.toml`. `from-repository.md` now points readers who want to share their own setup to this path first.

**Keep mise's config in your own dotfiles checkout.** The new `--config-dir` flag for `mise bootstrap --from` links mise's config directory to a directory inside the checkout, then bootstraps from it. The repository can keep mise's config beside every other application's:

```text
~/.dotfiles/
├── .zshrc
└── .config/
    ├── kitty/kitty.conf
    └── mise/
        ├── config.toml        # deploys ~/.config/kitty and ~/.zshrc
        ├── config.work.toml
        ├── miserc.toml
        └── conf.d/
```

```toml
# ~/.dotfiles/.config/mise/config.toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/kitty" = { mode = "symlink" }
"~/.zshrc" = {}
```

```sh
mise bootstrap --from https://github.com/you/dotfiles.git --from-dir ~/.dotfiles --config-dir .config/mise
```

That links `~/.config/mise` to `~/.dotfiles/.config/mise` (or wherever `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`/`MISE_CONFIG_DIR` put mise's config directory) and runs the bootstrap from it, so `config.toml`, `config.<env>.toml`, `conf.d/`, and `miserc.toml` are global config from the first run on, and the repository's `miserc.toml` selects the environment. `{{ mise_config_dir }}` is `~/.config/mise` on that run and every later one. The config directory must be missing, empty, or already that link; anything else is refused and left alone, as `--adopt` requires. Later runs need only `git -C ~/.dotfiles pull && mise bootstrap`, and `mise use -g` and `mise dot add` write into the checkout through the link. `--dry-run` creates no link and previews from the directory directly.

Before this, the docs' "Global config in another directory" recipe mounted the whole repository under `~/.config/mise/conf.d/` and set `write_targets.dotfiles`. A conf.d folder only reads `mise*.toml`, so `miserc.toml`, `config.<env>.toml`, and nested `conf.d/` in the repository had no effect. That recipe still works, but the section now documents `--config-dir` i

title: fix(config): keep root tool inheritance for monorepo children when "." is a config root
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2913/changes/mise/1070
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `monorepo.config_roots = [".", "child"]`, a child with no tool overrides lost its inheritance from the monorepo root config. `mise install --monorepo --locked` then also tried to install a version pinned only by a global config, and failed:

```text
mise ERROR Failed to install core:ruby@3.3.12: ruby@3.3.12 is not in the lockfile
```

The cause was that the monorepo union dropped the config of every declared root from the shared base hierarchy, including `.`, which is an ancestor of `child`. The child therefore fell back to the global request. Each declared root now loads its own full hierarchy (ancestor directories, then global and system config), exactly as if mise ran there, so siblings' overrides never leak and intermediate ancestors are honored.

Added `e2e/cli/test_ls_monorepo_root_inheritance`: with a global `tiny = "1.0.0"`, a root pin of `2.1.0`, an empty `child`, and a `sibling` overriding to `3.1.0`, `mise ls --current --monorepo` now reports only `2.1.0` and `3.1.0`. It also covers running from an undeclared directory and an intermediate ancestor config above a nested root. The existing monorepo install and lockfile e2e tests also pass.

Fixes #15007

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

diff:
--- e2e/cli/test_ls_monorepo_root_inheritance (+60/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,60 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+export MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1
+
+rm -rf "$MISE_DATA_DIR/plugins/tiny"
+ln -s "$ROOT/test/data/plugins/tiny" "$MISE_DATA_DIR/plugins/tiny"
+
+# a global request that the repository overrides must not leak into the union
+mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/mise"
+cat >"$HOME/.config/mise/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+tiny = "1.0.0"
+TOML
+
+mkdir -p monorepo/child monorepo/sibling
+cat >monorepo/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+monorepo_root = true
+
+[monorepo]
+config_roots = [".", "child", "sibling"]
+
+[tools]
+tiny = "2.1.0"
+TOML
+touch monorepo/child/mise.toml
+cat >monorepo/sibling/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+tiny = "3.1.0"
+TOML
+
+# the empty child inherits the root's pin, not the global one; the sibling's
+# override still contributes its own version
+assert "cd monorepo && mise ls --current --monorepo tiny --json | jq -r '[.[].version] | sort | join(\",\")'" "2.1.0,3.1.0"
+
+# an undeclared directory under the root is not an ancestor of child, so its
+# config must not leak into child's hierarchy
+mkdir -p monorepo/scratch
+cat >monorepo/scratch/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]

title: ci(release): leave room to retry a hung tarball build
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2912/changes/mise/1069
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The release PR's `build-tarball-linux-x64` job (run 40331469497) hung during the PGO instrumented build and never recovered. Its log is silent from 13:50, right after `Compiling mise-oci`, until 16:08. The release run then failed on `build-tarball-linux: cancelled`.

Two things stopped the retry from rescuing it:

- The retry action's per-attempt timeout was 140 minutes inside a 150-minute job, so a hung first attempt left about 10 minutes for the second. The second attempt (3 allowed) had just started merging profile data when the job limit cancelled it.
- The timeout kills the `cross` client but not its docker container. The container kept compiling and held cargo's target-directory lock, so attempt 2 logged `Blocking waiting for file lock on artifact directory` for 6m37s.

This is a one-off hang, not a slowdown: `linux-x64` took 79–84 minutes on the last four green release PR runs I could read.

## Changes

- `release.yml`: per-attempt timeout 140 → 120 minutes (about 40% above the normal ~82 minutes) and job limit 150 → 300 minutes, so a hang costs less runner time and still leaves room for a full retry.
- `build-tarball.sh`: kill any cross containers left over from an earlier attempt before building. The runner only runs this one job, so any `cross-rs/*` or `cross-custom*` container still up is stale.

The cleanup is untested against a real hang. I only checked the image filter against sample `docker ps` output and ran `bash -n`, `shellcheck` and `shfmt`.

title: fix(config): use the sub-project lockfile for idiomatic files in monorepo task runs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2911/changes/mise/1068
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `MISE_LOCKED=1`, `mise run //app:t` from a monorepo root looked up an idiomatic version file such as `app/.node-version` in the root `mise.lock` instead of `app/mise.lock`. mise warned that the version was not in the lockfile and ran the task without mise's node on `PATH`. The same task run from `app/` worked.

The root run doesn't load `app/mise.toml`, so the lockfile lookup only saw the root config and treated it as the owner of `app/.node-version`. The lookup now also finds the nearest base `mise.toml` between the version file and the monorepo root, even when it isn't loaded, and uses its lockfile when it is deeper than the loaded match.

Before:

```text
$ MISE_LOCKED=1 mise run //app:t
mise WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for node: [.../app/.node-version] node@24.21.0: node@24.21.0 is not in the lockfile
```

After: the task runs with `node@24.21.0` from `app/mise.lock` and prints no warning.

The same applies to other idiomatic files such as `rust-toolchain.toml`, which take the same code path. I only tested `.node-version`.

Added `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_monorepo_idiomatic_task`, which fails without the change and passes with it. `test_lockfile_monorepo` and `test_lock_monorepo_dot_config_root` still pass, and clippy is clean.

Fixes #15014
