title: feat(dotfiles): warn when apply overwrites an edited template target
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2910/changes/mise/1067
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise dot apply` silently overwrites a rendered `template` target you edited by hand, so the edit is lost unless you notice first. mise already records a digest of what it last wrote to each template target, so it can tell an edit from its own output.

`apply` now warns before overwriting such a target:

```text
mise files: ~/.private.sh was edited since mise last wrote it; applying overwrites the edit. Move it into ~/src/private.sh to keep it
```

The overwrite itself is unchanged: templates still apply without `--force`, as documented, so unattended runs are not blocked.

The warning stays quiet when:
- the source changed but the target is untouched (the usual case),
- mise has no record for the target (first apply, pre-existing file, lost state).

Tested with a new e2e test (`test_dotfiles_template_edited_warning`) covering the quiet and warning cases.

Second half of discussion #15017; the first half (refusing `mise dot add` on a template) is #15019.

https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2909/changes/mise/1066

`mise dot add ~/.private.sh` on a `mode = "template"` entry used to copy the rendered target over the template source. title: chore(deps): ignore zstd-safe 7 advisories from zstd 0.13 dependents
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2903/changes/mise/1064
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`cargo deny check` in the `lint` job now fails on every PR, including the `chore: release` PR, because RustSec published three advisories against `zstd-safe` 7.x: RUSTSEC-2026-0391, RUSTSEC-2026-0398 and RUSTSEC-2026-0403. The lint job re-fetches the advisory database on each run, so unrelated PRs went red.

This adds the three IDs to the `deny.toml` ignore list.

## Why ignore rather than upgrade

- mise's own `zstd` is 0.14 (`zstd-safe` 8.2, patched). The 7.3.0 copy is only reachable through `zstd` 0.13, used by `decmpfs` (via aube-store), `rattler_*` and `ubi`.
- `zstd` 0.13 pins `zstd-safe` 7.x, so `cargo update -p zstd-safe` can't reach the fix. Aube already uses `zstd` 0.14, so nothing changes there; the old copy comes from the third-party `decmpfs`.
- The advisories cover the streaming writer, the seekable decoder and legacy frames. The `read::Decoder` and bulk APIs are not affected.

I couldn't confirm which `zstd` APIs rattler, ubi and decmpfs call, so the ignore reasons say they use the read and bulk APIs as an assumption. The ignores should come out once those crates move to `zstd` 0.14.

Verified with `cargo deny check advisories` (cargo-deny 0.20.2): `advisories ok`.

title: fix(lock): refresh platform entries whose URL belongs to another release
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2902/changes/mise/1063
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With the default `lockfile_mode = "generate"`, `mise lock <tool>` left a tool's platform entries untouched after its `version` in `mise.lock` was rewritten (the way Renovate bumps a lock-only change). It reported success, but the `url` and `checksum` still pointed at the old release, and `mise install --locked` then refused the lockfile.

```sh
mise lock lefthook@2.1.17 -p macos-arm64
sed -i 's/^version = "2.1.17"/version = "2.2.2"/' mise.lock
mise lock lefthook -p macos-arm64   # before: url still .../download/v2.1.17/...
```

`mise lock` now treats an entry whose URL provably names a different release than its `version` as stale and re-resolves it, so the example above ends with a `v2.2.2` URL and checksum. It uses the same URL/version check `mise install --locked` already applies. URLs with no release number are still reused as before.

Fixes #15009

Tested with a new unit test and the existing `lockfile::` unit tests. I did not run the full lefthook repro end to end.

title: fix(config): keep a skipped version-file link from hiding the file it points at
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2901/changes/mise/1062
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #15005

Since 2026.10.19, mise skips an idiomatic version file that is a symlink to a file of another name (`.nvmrc -> .node-version`). That skip is intended. But skipping `.nvmrc` also hid the `.node-version` it points at, so the directory resolved no Node at all:

```sh
echo 24.22.1 > .node-version
ln -s .node-version .nvmrc
mise ls --current node   # warns about .nvmrc, then resolves the global Node
```

Config discovery dropped files that resolve to the same real path as duplicates. `.nvmrc` is found first and claimed the real `.node-version`, so the real `.node-version` was discarded as its duplicate, and `.nvmrc` then parsed to nothing. A version file that loading skips for linking to another name no longer takes part in that dedupe, so `.node-version` is read and `.nvmrc` still gets the warning.

Whether a path is a version file is decided the way loading decides it: a tool-versions filename (including `MISE_OVERRIDE_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAMES`, even one ending in `.toml`), or a filename discovery searched for as idiomatic. The link check itself is unchanged, so a link to `~/.netrc` or a local `.env` is still never read.

Based on the approach and tests from #15011 by @jjb.

## Test plan

- `mise run test:e2e test_linked_version_file`: a regular `.node-version`, both files linked to `client/.node-version`, `versions.toml -> .tool-versions`, and a custom TOML config name that is still one config
- `mise run test:e2e test_task_monorepo_linked_version_file`: the same through a monorepo config root's own idiomatic settings
- unit: `skipped_version_file_link_is_told_apart_from_mise_toml`

title: docs(templates): list the settings that render templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2896/changes/mise/1061
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The [templates page](https://mise.jdx.dev/templates.html#where-templates-are-rendered) says `mise.toml` renders "string values in most sections", which suggests any setting can be a template. Most settings can't: a template in their value is used literally. Only a few path settings, which have to resolve against the file that sets them, are rendered:

- `dotfiles.root`
- `write_targets` paths
- `age.key_file`, `age.identity_files` and `age.ssh_identity_files`

This adds a `[settings]` row to the "Where templates are rendered" table and a short "Templates in settings" section that lists them and explains their context. They render while mise reads settings, so they get the same limited context as `.miserc.toml` (plus `config_source`), and a relative result resolves against the file's config root:

```toml
[settings]
dotfiles.root = "{{ mise_config_dir }}/home"
```

The `dotfiles.root` template support is from #14969 and is not in a release yet.

Asked about in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14945#discussioncomment-19190822.

Validation: markdownlint, oxfmt and `render-llms` pass; `mise run docs:build` succeeds and the new links and anchors resolve in the built site; `schema_matches_parser` passes with the new TOML example.

title: fix(lock): let mise lock add tools missing from the lockfile under tool_config.locked
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2895/changes/mise/1060
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` failed for any tool that was not yet in the lockfile when `tool_config.locked = true` was set, which is the state Renovate leaves a repo in when it bumps a tool and runs `mise lock <tool>`:

```toml
[tool_config]
locked = true

[tools]
claude-code = "2.1.300"
```

```
$ mise lock
mise ERROR claude-code@2.1.300 is not in the lockfile
hint: Run `mise lock` to update the lockfile, or disable `tool_config.locked`
```

The error told users to run the command that was failing. `mise lock` now writes the entry (`Lockfile ready at mise.lock`), and `mise install` under `tool_config.locked` then installs exactly what the lockfile says.

## Cause

Since `lockfile_mode = "generate"` became the default, `mise lock` resolves each tool through its existing lock entry. With `tool_config.locked = true` a tool with no entry fails that lookup with `NotInLockfile`. `mise lock` only cleared the lookup in `merge` mode.

## Fix

In generate mode `mise lock` still prefers an existing lock entry, so pinned versions are kept. If that lookup fails with `NotInLockfile`, it retries once without the lock lookup, since creating the entry is the command's purpose. Other resolution errors are unchanged.

## Testing

Added `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_generate_tool_config_locked`: `mise install` is rejected before locking, `mise lock tiny` succeeds, and `mise.lock` gains the entry. `test_lockfile_tool_config_locked` still passes, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean for this change.

Fixes #14987

title: fix(vfox): send PreInstall headers when locking downloads artifacts
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2894/changes/mise/1059
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14998.

`mise lock`, and the automatic locking `mise install` does when a `mise.lock` exists, downloaded a vfox plugin's artifact without the `headers` its `PreInstall` hook returns. For private artifact repositories that failed with a 401, even though a plain install of the same tool worked.

Now the lock download sends the plugin's headers, with the same rules as an install: they go only to the origin of the plugin's `url`, never to a rewritten mirror or a cross-origin redirect. They are not written to `mise.lock`.

- `Vfox::download_to` is the install download split out of `Vfox::download`.
- `PlatformInfo.download_headers` is a new `serde(skip)` field filled by the vfox backend's `resolve_lock_info`.
- `artifact_checksum` uses the headers when present.

Recording the hook's declared `sha256` to skip the download is not part of this change.

Tests: new `test_download_to_sends_plugin_headers`; vfox download tests and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

title: fix(bootstrap): stage cask apps in a hidden directory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2890/changes/mise/1058
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14986.

After `mise bootstrap` installed a cask app, launchers such as Raycast could list it as `Nani.mise-tmp-<hash>` instead of `Nani`. The cask installer copied the bundle into the appdir as `/Applications/Nani.mise-tmp-<hash>` before renaming it into place, and a launcher that indexed it during that window kept the staging name.

The copy now lives at `/Applications/.mise-tmp-<hash>/Nani.app` — a hidden directory in the same parent, with the final bundle name — and is renamed into `/Applications/Nani.app` from there. The staging directory is opened without following symlinks and renames go through its descriptor. It is removed after activation.

Not changed: when replacing an existing app, the old bundle is still moved aside to `Name.mise-old-<hash>` briefly.

Not verified against Raycast itself (macOS-only); unit tests for the swap/activation paths pass on Linux.

title: fix(dot): retry git write-tree when Windows refuses a loose object write
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2887/changes/mise/1057
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise dot` snapshots could fail on Windows when two compositions ran at the same time. `git write-tree` died with `unable to write file .../objects/a2/88ce…: Permission denied`, because both processes were writing the same loose object and Windows will not let git replace a file another process holds open. CI hit it as a failure of `history::shadow::tests::concurrent_composition_keeps_every_overlay` on `windows-unit`.

`compose` now retries `write-tree` up to five times, with a short backoff, when git reports `Permission denied`. The other process has written the object by then, so the retry finds it in place. Any other error is returned at once.

I could not reproduce the race on Linux, so this is verified by the existing `history::shadow` tests (22 pass) and clippy, not by a Windows run.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-308_agent.*

title: registry: add tuios (aqua:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios)
body:
Hi! I'm the author of [tuios](https://github.com/Gaurav-Gosain/tuios), a terminal window manager with tiling panes, workspaces, sessions that survive restarts, and an inbox for coding agents. This adds a `tuios` shorthand so people can install it with:

```sh
mise use tuios
tuios --version   # tuios version 0.10.1 [pure-Go backend]
```

## Backend

- `aqua:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios` first. The aqua registry already has a recipe for it with checksums.
- `github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios` as the fallback. Each release also ships `tuios-web`, `tuios-ghostty`, `sketch`, `tml` and `tplot` archives, so I set `matching = "tuios_"` to keep only the tuios archives. There is no Windows arm64 build, and without a pattern autodetection picked the FreeBSD arm64 archive there, so windows-arm64 gets the x86_64 archive like aqua does.
- No packslip manifests and no artifact attestations yet, so no `attestations_since`.

The tuios archive holds only the `tuios` binary (plus license files), so `bins = ["tuios"]`.

## Testing

On Linux x86-64 with the mise 2026.10.19 release binary and empty data, config and cache directories:

```
$ mise use -g github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios@latest
mise by @jdx – installing 1 tool
mise ✓ github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios@0.10.1  1.9s  tuios_0.10.1_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
mise ████████████████ 1/1 · installed 1 tool in 1.9s
mise <global config> tools: github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios@0.10.1

$ mise exec github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios -- tuios --version
tuios version 0.10.1 [pure-Go backend]
Commit: f8b7820aa685b28295af46e1f32fb20b0d8461dc
Built: 2026-10-17T18:18:08Z
By: goreleaser
```

`latest` resolves to 0.10.1 here because 0.11.0 came out yesterday and the default `minimum_release_age` hides it. With `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0`, `github:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios@0.11.0` installs and prints `tuios version 0.11.0`.

`mise exec aqua:Gaurav-Gosain/tuios@latest -- tuios --version` installs `tuios_0.10.1_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz` and prints the same version.

`mise lock` for linux-x64, linux-arm64, macos-x64, macos-arm64, windows-x64 and windows-arm64 resolves the right `tuios_*` archive for every platform on both backends.

With a debug build of this branch:

```
$ mise test-tool tuios
mise by @jdx – installing 1 tool
mise ✓ tuios@0.11.0  3.5s  tuios_0.11.0_Linux_x86_64.tar.gz
mise ████████████████ 1/1 · installed 1 tool in 3.5s
mise $ tuios --version
tuios version 0.11.0 [pure-Go backend]
Commit: 3638a6f2093edfa7396b6233515786de4dbda683
Built: 2026-10-25T11:22:02Z
By: goreleaser
mise tuios: OK
```

title: feat(bootstrap): add `--force` to remove casks prune cannot prove unchanged
body:
`mise bootstrap packages prune --manager brew-cask` only removes a cask when mise can prove it is unchanged since install. Self-updating apps such as OrbStack, casks with install steps such as AeroSpace, and casks installed before mise recorded prune metadata never meet that bar. Once you delete their `brew-cask:` entry there is no way to remove them through mise, and because mise installs casks without Homebrew's metadata, `brew uninstall --cask` reports them as not installed either.

`prune` now accepts `--force` for `brew-cask`. Without it, prune names the casks that `--force` would remove:

```
$ mise bootstrap packages prune --manager brew-cask
mise WARN  brew-cask:orbstack: skipped: install lifecycle actions may have untracked side effects
mise WARN  brew-cask:raycast: skipped: receipt predates safe prune metadata; upgrade or reinstall first
mise brew-cask: to remove orbstack, raycast anyway, run again with --force
mise brew-cask: nothing to prune

$ mise bootstrap packages prune --manager brew-cask --force --dry-run
mise WARN  brew-cask:orbstack: forcing removal: install lifecycle actions may have untracked side effects
mise WARN  brew-cask:raycast: forcing removal: receipt predates safe prune metadata; upgrade or reinstall first
remove brew-cask:orbstack@2.2.3,20963
remove brew-cask:raycast@1.104.24
```

`--force` relaxes only the "provably unchanged" requirement, not ownership. A forced prune removes the apps, fonts, binary links and completion links the receipt recorded, provided each is still in its install location and each link still points where mise left it, and then removes the Caskroom directory. A link that now points somewhere else is kept with a warning, and so are targets recorded by a cask's own install scripts, because mise cannot tell what they are. Anything those scripts created outside the receipt, such as a privileged helper or launch agent, also stays. `--force` still skips casks Homebrew owns, casks with no mise receipt (or a pre-schema-2 receipt without a target inventory), interrupted installs, and targets shared with another cask, and it re-checks Homebrew ownership and the receipt just before removing anything.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added `--force` to `mise bootstrap packages prune` for mise-installed Homebrew casks that cannot be verified as unchanged. The option is available only with the `brew-cask` manager.
  * Forced pruning removes recorded files that remain in their expected locations, along with the cask directory. Files created by install scripts and links that now point elsewhere are left in place.
  * Homebrew-owned casks, shared files, casks without a mise receipt, and interrupted installs remain protected. Use `--dry-run` to preview planned removals.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: feat(github): add version_regex to list only matching release tags
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2848/changes/mise/1054
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Some repositories publish GitHub releases that aren't versions of the tool. Turning on `prerelease` then lists them alongside real versions, and `latest` can resolve to one with nothing installable for the platform. For example, indexable-inc/blaze has a `nightly` prerelease with the builds and a `pgo-profiles` prerelease that holds only `.profdata` files. With `prerelease = true`, `latest` is `pgo-profiles`, and installing it fails. `version_prefix` doesn't help, because the tags share no prefix.

The `github`, `gitlab` and `forgejo` backends now take a `version_regex` tool option. It is a regular expression that a release tag must match to be listed:

```toml
[tools]
"github:indexable-inc/blaze" = { version = "latest", prerelease = true, version_regex = '^(v\d+\.\d+\.\d+|nightly)$' }
```

```console
$ mise ls-remote 'github:indexable-inc/blaze[prerelease=true]'
nightly
pgo-profiles
$ mise ls-remote 'github:indexable-inc/blaze[prerelease=true,version_regex=^(v\d+\.\d+\.\d+|nightly)$]'
nightly
```

The option only filters. Listed tags become versions the same way as before (by stripping `version_prefix` or a leading `v`), so installing a listed version looks its tag up unchanged. When both options are set, a tag has to start with `version_prefix` and match `version_regex`. The filter applies to the full listing, to GitHub's and Forgejo's `/releases/latest` shortcut, and to the versions-host tag lookup. Installing never uses a tag the pattern excludes. In a repository with both `1.2.3` and `v1.2.3`, `version_regex = '^\d'` installs from the `1.2.3` release, even though mise would otherwise try `v1.2.3` first. `version_regex` is also part of the version-list cache key, the same as `version_prefix`. An invalid pattern is an error (`invalid version_regex "(": regex parse error: …`), not an empty list.

## `blaze` registry entry

This PR also adds `blaze` to the registry. It was merged into this branch from #14981. `mise use blaze` installs [indexable-inc/blaze](https://github.com/indexable-inc/blaze) (formerly ra-jit), an incremental Rust build daemon. It uses GitHub releases on Linux x64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64, with `prerelease = true` and `version_regex = '^(v\d+\.\d+\.\d+|nightly)$'`. blaze has no tagged release yet, so today `latest` is the `nightly` prerelease. Once blaze publishes `vX.Y.Z` releases, those are listed too.

Caveats:

- jdx chose to submit this below the usual popularity bar.
- `nightly` is rebuilt in place, so a lockfile checksum for it goes stale. The current nightly predates the rename: it ships `ra-jit`, `ra-jit-rustc` and `cargo-ra-jit`, and no `blaze` or `cargo-blaze`.
- The tool test runs `ra-jit --help` and expects `usage: ra-jit`. The nightly prints `ra-jit 0.0.0` for `--version`, which doesn't name a version mise can compare. Both the nightly and blaze's main branch print that usage line.
- Wit

title: fix(dot): resolve a relative dot add --source from the current directory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2847/changes/mise/1053
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise dot add --source <relative path>` resolved the path three different ways: it moved the file relative to the current directory, created the symlink with the literal relative text (so it resolved relative to the link's own directory), and wrote the entry verbatim (so the loader read it relative to the config file's directory). The documented `mise dot add --source dotfiles/gitconfig ~/.gitconfig` left a broken link, and from a subdirectory the entry pointed at a source that didn't exist, so every later `mise dot apply` failed.

A relative `--source` now starts from the current directory, like any path on the command line. The link points at that resolved file, and the entry records it relative to the config file's directory when it lies inside it, so the config stays portable:

```sh
cd ~/project/sub
mise dot add --local --yes --source rel ~/.rel
readlink ~/.rel   # ~/project/sub/rel  (was: rel)
```

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.rel" = { source = "sub/rel" }  # was: "rel", which resolved to ~/project/rel
```

A relative source outside the config file's directory is written as an absolute (`~/…`) path. An absolute `--source` is unchanged. The `--source` help and the managed-dotfiles docs now say which directory a relative path starts from.

Validation: new `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_add_relative_source` covers the project root, a subdirectory, a source outside the config directory, and `relative_symlinks`; the existing `dot add`/track/groups e2e tests and clippy pass.

Fixes #14982

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.308.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Relative paths provided when adding a dotfiles source now resolve from the current directory. Sources inside the selected configuration directory are recorded relative to it; sources outside are recorded as absolute paths.
  * Paths that pass through symlinked directories are resolved consistently, including when navigating to a parent directory with `..`.
* **Documentation**

title: registry: add blaze (github:indexable-inc/blaze)
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2845/changes/mise/1052
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Adds `blaze`, the incremental Rust build daemon from [indexable-inc/blaze](https://github.com/indexable-inc/blaze) (formerly ra-jit). It keeps a project compiled in memory and recompiles only the functions an edit changed. The entry installs the GitHub release archive for Linux x64, Linux arm64 and macOS arm64, which are the targets blaze's `release.yaml` builds. All of blaze's programs sit in one directory because they find each other there, and the github backend keeps them together.

```toml
[tools]
blaze = "nightly"   # works today
# blaze = "latest"  # works after blaze's first v* release
```

## Caveats

- **The popularity bar is not met.** This is submitted at jdx's request anyway. The numbers are below.
- **Only the nightly build installs today.** blaze has no tagged release yet. The repository's only releases are the `nightly` and `pgo-profiles` pre-releases. So `mise ls-remote blaze` prints nothing, `mise use blaze` (latest) fails with `no versions found for blaze`, and `mise test-tool blaze` fails the same way. The CI `validate-new-tools` job will fail until blaze publishes a `v*` release. Its `release.yaml` makes non-prerelease `vX.Y.Z` releases, with `blaze-vX.Y.Z-<target>.tar.gz` archives and `SHA256SUMS`, and those should match this entry without changes.
- **`blaze@nightly` is a moving tag.** It installs because mise fetches the named tag directly. It is rebuilt in place, so a locked checksum for it goes stale. The current nightly archive predates the rename: it contains `ra-jit`, `ra-jit-rustc` and `cargo-ra-jit`, and no `blaze` or `cargo-blaze`.
- I did not use `prerelease = true`. With it, `latest` resolves to `pgo-profiles`, which is a profile-data release, not a build.
- **No crates.io fallback.** `cargo:ra-jit@0.1.0` builds from source on Linux x64 with Rust 1.99.0 (1m51s) and `ra-jit --version` prints `ra-jit 0.1.0`. I left it out for four reasons: it is a tier-4 backend, it needs a Rust 1.99.0 toolchain on `PATH`, the 0.1.0 crate has no `blaze`/`cargo-blaze` binaries, and mise would only reach it on Windows or Intel macOS, where it is untested. `cargo:cargo-blaze` 0.0.1 is only a wrapper that runs `cargo ra-jit`, so it can't stand alone.

## Testing

All on Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.39), using a debug build of this branch with an empty `MISE_DATA_DIR`/`MISE_CACHE_DIR`:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `mise use blaze@nightly` | installs `ra-jit-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` in 5.2s; `mise x -- ra-jit --version` prints `ra-jit 0.0.0` |
| `mise ls-remote blaze` | empty (no tagged release) |
| `mise use blaze` / `mise test-tool blaze` | `no versions found for blaze` |

I did not test macOS arm64 or Linux arm64.

The test runs `ra-jit --version`. On blaze's main branch that prints `blaze <version> (<commit>)`, so it should pass on a tagged release.

## Popularity

- GitHub: 398 stars, 15 forks. The rep

title: feat(bootstrap): manage existing systemd user units from bootstrap.services
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2844/changes/mise/1051
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.services]` could start and enable units a package installed, but only system units. A systemd *user* unit such as `gnome-keyring-daemon` had to be redefined as a `dev.mise.*` service or driven with a separate `systemctl --user`. Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14938.

`scope = "user"` with no `command` and no `builtin` now manages the unit that already exists:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"pacman:gnome-keyring" = "latest"

[bootstrap.services.gnome-keyring-daemon]
scope = "user"
state = "running"
enabled = true
```

mise runs `systemctl --user` against `gnome-keyring-daemon.service` (no root, no `dev.mise.*` unit written). `state`, `enabled`, and `masked` behave as they do for system services, and sockets/timers work with a suffix.

## Behavior

- Linux only. Elsewhere the entry errors, pointing at `command`.
- Options that define a service (`command`, `builtin`, `description`, `restart`, `environment`, `working_directory`, `requires_tools`, `state = "absent"`) are rejected in this mode with an explanatory error.
- Fails closed like system units: a missing unit or unavailable user manager reports `unknown` and apply refuses.
- Managed-file `notify` still reaches system services only.
- A privileged plan is never allowed to carry a user unit, so `--user` cannot be pointed at root's manager.

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Moving a symlinked dotfiles repo to `mise dot track` hit three dead ends, reported in discussion #14933:

- `mise dot origin set` against the existing remote fails with "local and origin histories are unrelated" and advises pushing "the local history", but nothing says where that is. It is a separate bare repo under the state directory, not the `~/dev/dotfiles` checkout.
- `mise dot track` on a file with a `symlink`/`copy`/`template` entry writes the tracking entry to `conf.d/dotfiles-tracking.toml` and leaves the original entry alone. That is deliberate, but the output never says so.
- Nothing in the docs explains that a symlink-managed repo and tracked history are different repositories.

## Changes

`mise dot status` prints the local history repository under Repository (and as `history_repo` in `--json`):

```
Repository
  git@github.com:me/dotfiles.git
  Branch: main · Mode: manual
  Local history: ~/.local/state/mise/history/repo.git
```

The unrelated-histories error and the docs now point at that line.

`mise dot track` explains a split entry:

```
dotfiles: ~/.bashrc is also declared with mode = "copy" in ~/.config/mise/config.toml, which was left as it is. To track it from that entry instead, replace it with { mode = "track" } (dropping source, content, and manifest) and remove the entry from ~/.config/mise/conf.d/dotfiles-tracking.toml
```

A new "Move from a symlinked dotfiles repository" section in the sync docs covers replacing symlinks with copies, replacing the entry with a tracking entry, and publishing the local history to a `mise-history` branch of the existing remote.

The report that `mise dot track ~/.config/mise/config.toml` says "already tracked" with no entry in sight did not reproduce: the entry is written to `config.toml` and the message names that file. It needs the reporter's `mise dot paths` output.

title: fix(config): warn about an ignored write_targets only when a write uses it
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2826/changes/mise/1046
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap --adopt` clones global config into the config directory mise reads it from, and `mise bootstrap --from` runs a repository once without making it global config. Someone who wants their dotfiles sources and mise config together in `~/.dotfiles` (as in [discussion 14945](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14945)) had no documented way to do that, and the setup that works printed a misleading warning on its first run.

## Keep global config in a dotfiles repository

A new "Global config in another directory" section in [Bootstrap from a repository](https://mise.jdx.dev/bootstrap/from-repository.html#global-config-elsewhere) shows a repository that links itself into `~/.config/mise/conf.d/` as a [conf.d folder](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html#conf-d-folders), so it loads as global config from then on:

```toml
# ~/.dotfiles/mise.toml
[settings]
write_targets.dotfiles = "mise.toml"

[dotfiles]
"~/.config/mise/conf.d/dotfiles" = { source = ".", mode = "symlink" }
"~/.zshrc" = {}
```

```sh
mise bootstrap --from https://github.com/you/dotfiles.git --from-dir ~/.dotfiles   # new machine
git -C ~/.dotfiles pull && mise bootstrap                                          # later updates
```

After the first run, `mise dot add ~/.gitconfig` saves the source to `~/.dotfiles/.gitconfig` and the entry to the repository's `mise.toml`.

## `write_targets` warning only when a write uses it

`write_targets.*` set in a project config is ignored, because it only applies from global config. mise used to warn about that every time such a file loaded, so the first `mise bootstrap --from` above printed:

```text
mise WARN  write_targets.dotfiles in non-global config /home/me/.dotfiles/mise.toml is ignored for security reasons
```

even though bootstrap writes no global config. Now mise stays quiet while loading and warns only when `mise use --global`, `mise bootstrap packages use/import --global`, or `mise dot add` would have used the ignored value, naming the file it writes instead:

```text
mise WARN  write_targets.dotfiles in ~/.dotfiles/mise.toml is ignored because it only applies from global config; writing to ~/.config/mise/config.toml
```

Other global-only settings keep their load-time warning.

## Validation

- e2e `test_global_section_write_targets` gains a case: a project `write_targets.dotfiles` prints nothing on `mise config ls`, warns on `mise dot add`, and the entry lands in global config. A new unit test checks the strip records the ignored key.
- Checked by hand in a throwaway `HOME` with a debug build: loading the repository and `mise bootstrap` print no warning; `mise dot add` before the link warns; after the link it writes to the repository's `mise.toml` from inside and outside `~/.dotfiles`. The `--from` clone itself was not run.
- Lint, clippy, `mise run docs:build`, and `schema_matches_parser` pass.

title: security(config): make elevate_with a global-only setting
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2825/changes/mise/1045
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

`system_packages.elevate_with` names the program mise runs in place of `sudo` when it elevates. It is now `global_only`, so only global config and `MISE_SYSTEM_PACKAGES_ELEVATE_WITH` can set it, like the shell-args and credential-command settings.

```toml
# a project's mise.toml
[settings]
system_packages.elevate_with = "./attack/sudo"   # now ignored, with the usual warning
```

This is hardening, not a fix for an untrusted-repo hole. A project's `[settings]` are already ignored until the config is trusted (#14538, v2026.10.13), and a trusted project can already run code through `[env]`, `[hooks]` and `[tools]`. Nothing legitimately sets a privilege wrapper per project, so there is no reason to let a project choose it.

Other settings that name a build repository, patch or `make` command, such as `ruby.ruby_build_repo` and `python.pyenv_repo`, stay settable from trusted projects on purpose; existing e2e tests rely on that.

## Testing

- Unit test `test_command_selecting_settings_are_global_only` pins `elevate_with` and the four shell-args keys.
- e2e `config/test_elevate_with_global_only` checks that a trusted project file cannot set it and that global config and the environment still can.

title: fix(oci): write aliased tools by their resolved backend in the image config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2824/changes/mise/1044
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise oci build` writes `/etc/mise/config.toml` into the image keyed by the tool names from your config. If a tool's backend came from `[tool_alias]`, the image got the bare alias name, but the alias table isn't in the image, so the name no longer resolves:

```toml
# host mise.toml
[tool_alias]
goose = "aqua:pressly/goose"

[tools]
goose = "latest"

$ mise which goose
mise WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for goose: ... goose not found in mise tool registry
mise ERROR goose is not a mise bin. Perhaps you need to install it first.
```

Such tools are now written as their resolved backend, so the image config is self-contained:

```toml
[tools]
"aqua:pressly/goose" = "3.29.0"
```

Tools that don't use an alias are written exactly as before, so existing images and layer digests are unchanged.

Fixes the report in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14941.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2820/changes/mise/1041
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise oci` printed a `WARN ... has an absolute target outside the tool's install dir; it will be dangling inside the container` for every absolute symlink in a `[bootstrap.packages]` layer. With `apt:buildah`, that is the whole `/etc/alternatives/*` set:

```

The warnings were wrong. A system package layer is a rootfs overlay extracted at `/`, so `/usr/sbin/arptables-nft` is already the correct in-image path and the link resolves fine. The layer builder was passing these links through the tool-relocation logic, which assumes the tree moves under `/mise` and could also have rewritten a target relative to the temporary build directory.

System package layers now keep symlink targets exactly as the package installed them. Tool layers are unchanged and still warn about, or rebase, links that really would dangle.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2819/changes/mise/1040

Filters on `version` in a tool's `url` now work. `{{ version | replace(from='--4--foobar', to='') }}` previously left the version unchanged, and `{{ version | split(pat='') }}` split the characters of the text `{{ version }}`.

```toml
[tools."http:foo"]
version = "1.2.3--4--foobar"
url = "https://example.com/tool-{{ version | replace(from='--4--foobar', to='') }}.tgz"
# now downloads https://example.com/tool-1.2.3.tgz
```

Because the version is unknown when the config loads, mise renders it as the placeholder text `{{ version }}` and fills it in at install time. A filter therefore ran on that placeholder text. Any `{{ ... }}` expression that uses `version` beyond a bare `{{ version }}` is now kept as written at config load and rendered at install time with the real version. This applies to every tool option, not only `http`.

An expression that mixes `version` with `env` or `vars` is now rendered entirely at install time, so it no longer sees them.

Adds a unit test, an e2e test (`backend/test_http_version_filter`), and a docs note.

title: fix(task): stop sibling tasks run through Git Bash when a task fails on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2818/changes/mise/1039
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On Windows, when a task fails during `mise run`, mise now stops sibling tasks that run through Git Bash instead of waiting for them to finish.

```toml
[tasks.fail]
run = "exit 1"

[tasks.slow]
shell = "bash -c"
run = "sleep 10; echo done"
```

```
mise run fail ::: slow
```

Before, `fail` exited at once but the run took about 10 s, because `sleep.exe` kept running and holding the output pipe open. After, it finishes in about 0.15 s and no `sleep.exe` is left behind. Linux already behaved this way.

## Cause

mise stopped a task with `taskkill /F /T`, which follows parent PIDs. Git Bash (Cygwin/MSYS2) emulates `fork`, so `sleep.exe` does not hang off `bash.exe` in the Windows process tree and `/T` missed it.

## Change

Each command now starts suspended, joins a job object, and then runs. Killing a task terminates its job, which holds every process the command started whatever its parent chain looks like. The job only records membership: when a command finishes normally, anything it deliberately left running keeps running, as before. If a command cannot join a job (for example mise already runs in a job that forbids nesting), it runs outside one and is stopped with `taskkill` as before. This also applies to Ctrl-C and timeouts, which share the same kill path.

`windows_job` gains `Job::tracking`, `Job::assign` and `resume`, the pieces `spawn` was already built from.

## Validation

Run on the Windows CI box:
- Reproduced on main: 10.1 s. With this change: 0.15 s, no `sleep.exe` left over.
- New Pester test `e2e-win/task_fail_fast_git_bash.Tests.ps1` passes. It runs `sleep 20` through Git Bash, so it would take 20 s without the fix.
- An ordinary task's output, a task's non-zero exit code, and a `timeout` task (stopped after 2.1 s) behave as before.
- `cargo clippy -p mise-util --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on Windows, and `cargo check -p mise-util` passes on Linux.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14950.

title: fix(http): accept # comment lines in netrc files
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2816/changes/mise/1037
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise ignored the whole `~/.netrc` when the file had a comment line. Tools such as StepSecurity add marker comments to `~/.netrc`:

```
#stepsecurity-package-config-credential-dmg-begin
machine example.com
  login user
  password secret
#stepsecurity-package-config-credential-dmg-end
```

Before this change, every mise command that loaded netrc printed this warning and then sent no netrc credentials for any host:

```
mise WARN  Failed to parse netrc file /Users/me/.netrc: Illegal format in 1:50 token: #stepsecurity-package-config-credential-dmg-begin
```

Now mise skips lines whose first non-space character is `#`, as curl and Python's `netrc` module do, so the other entries load and their credentials are sent. A `#` in the middle of a line is kept, because it can be part of a password.

The cause was `netrc-rs` 0.1.2, which has no comment support and no release with it. This replaces it with [`netrc-jdx`](https://github.com/jdx/netrc-jdx), a small fork of that parser that accepts comments. It also drops `netrc-rs` from the lockfile. This supersedes the earlier approach in #14956, which pre-stripped comments before calling `netrc-rs`.

Limitation: a `macdef` body ends at the next blank line, and mise does not use macros.

## Validation

- A unit test parses a netrc that has marker comments and a password with `#` in it; `netrc-jdx` has its own tests for comments, `default`, `account`, `macdef` and malformed input.
- A new case in `e2e/config/test_netrc` checks that a netrc with comment lines gives no parse warning and that mise sends an `Authorization` header to the local test server. I did not run the e2e test locally; CI will.

title: fix(lock): keep npm sidecars in one place for a symlinked config dir
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2814/changes/mise/1035
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When `~/.config/mise` is a symlink into a dotfiles repo, `mise lock --global` wrote the npm sidecar graph to `.mise/locks/...` from one working directory and `locks/...` from another, flipping the `aube = { path = ... }` pointer and leaving duplicate sidecar directories behind.

`sidecar_root` chose between the `locks/` and `.mise/locks/` layouts from the unresolved directory name, so `~/.config/mise` counted as the global config dir while the same directory reached as `repo/mise` did not. It now picks the layout from the canonicalized directory, so the sidecar location is the same however the config dir is reached. The root is still built under the path it was given.

```
$ mise -C repo lock --global      # aube = { path = ".mise/locks/npm-cowsay/1.6.0", ... }
$ mise -C elsewhere lock --global # before: path = "locks/npm-cowsay/1.6.0"; now unchanged
```

Adds an e2e test with a symlinked config dir; it fails without the change.

Fixes #14942

title: fix(npm): skip the aube tree health walk in repeated hook-env runs on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2813/changes/mise/1034
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

On Windows, `mise hook-env` could block the shell for seconds when an `npm:` tool with a large `node_modules` was installed (#14952 measured ~1.9s in `toolset_env::env` for a ~28k-file tool, on every prompt and `cd`).

The cause is the Windows-only junction check added in #14418. To decide whether an aube install is healthy, it reads every virtual-store entry and parses each package's `package.json`. Its result was cached only inside the running process, and `hook-env` is a new process every time, so the full walk repeated on every prompt.

Now a self-contained verdict is also written to `<state>/npm-tree-health/`, keyed by the install path and the modification times of `node_modules/.mise` / `.aube`. Later processes skip the walk while those are unchanged; a reinstall or uninstall invalidates it. The marker lives in the state dir, not the install dir, so a CI cache that restores only installs (the case #14418 targets) still gets re-checked once. Linux and macOS behavior is unchanged.

## Testing

- New unit test `aube_health_marker_tracks_virtual_store_changes`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.
- Could not reproduce the slowdown on Linux (the walk is gated on Windows); not run on Windows.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2812/changes/mise/1033
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` no longer resolves or reports tools for platforms their `os` option excludes. With `lockfile_platforms = ["linux-x64", "macos-arm64"]` and `ttyd = { version = "1.7.7", os = ["linux"] }`, it used to warn `ttyd@1.7.7 is not available for macos-arm64; it will not install there`, and `mise lock --dry-run` listed ttyd as a planned update for macos-arm64. body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2811/changes/mise/1032
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes the remaining half of #14706: `[bootstrap.compose]` projects with a service using `network_mode: service:X` (or `ipc`, `pid`, `volumes_from`) still report `update` forever on 2026.10.18, even though compose considers everything up to date.

#14729 pins those references to container ids before asking compose for the desired config hash, but it took the ids from `compose ps`, which truncates them to 12 characters. Compose stamps the `config-hash` label from the full 64-character id, so the hashes could never match.

mise now takes the full id from the `docker inspect` it already runs to read the labels (`{{.Id}} {{json .Config.Labels}}`), so no extra engine call is added.

The e2e fake `ps` returns short ids and the fake engine now returns a different, full id from `inspect`; the test fails unless the override pins the full one. The previous fake used the same id on both sides, which is why it couldn't catch this.

Reported by @thurstonsand.

title: docs(use): explain that a bare tool reuses the newest installed version
body:
`mise use <tool>` without a version writes `latest` to the config, but when some version of the tool is already installed, mise resolves that request to the newest *installed* version instead of the newest release. Only an explicit `<tool>@latest` fetches the newest release. This is intentional (it's what `e2e/cli/test_use_latest` asserts, from #3169), but the argument help only said "Without a version, mise requests `latest`", which made the behaviour look like a bug, especially with `--pin`:

```console
$ mise install hk@2.1.0
$ mise latest hk
2.8.1
$ mise use --pin hk          # writes hk = "2.1.0"
$ mise use --pin hk@latest   # writes hk = "2.8.1"
```

This PR only rewords the `<TOOL@VERSION>` help in `src/cli/use.rs` to say that a bare tool reuses the newest installed version and that `@latest` installs the newest release unless the `locked` setting is on (then the lockfile still decides), then regenerates `docs/cli/use.md`, `mise.usage.kdl` and the man page. No behaviour changes.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2808/changes/mise/1030

### 🚀 Features

- **(bootstrap)** let Homebrew upgrade casks mise installs by @jdx in [#14929](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14929)
- **(bootstrap)** manage existing systemd user units from bootstrap.services by @jdx in [#14980](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14980)
- **(bootstrap)** install Windows packages with Chocolatey by @jdx in [#14978](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14978)
- **(bootstrap)** support launchd launch events by @deecewan in [#14992](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14992)
- **(completion)** add nushell support to mise completion by @jdx in [#14999](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14999)
- **(dotfiles)** render templates in dotfiles.root by @jdx in [#14969](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14969)
- **(github)** add version_regex to list only matching release tags by @jdx in [#14984](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14984)

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

- **(backends)** name --global in the switch warning for global lock entries by @jdx in [#14976](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14976)
- **(bootstrap)** find a just-installed git outside startup PATH by @pmmmwh in [#14919](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14919)
- **(bootstrap)** pin full container ids when hashing compose service references by @jdx in [#14958](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14958)
- **(bootstrap)** stage cask apps in a hidden directory by @jdx in [#15001](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15001)
- **(config)** warn about an ignored write_targets only when a write uses it by @jdx in [#14973](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14973)
- **(doctor)** accept any registry-listed backend for an explicit install by @jdx in [#14965](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14965)
- **(doctor)** color mise doctor project output by @jdx in [#14970](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14970)
- **(dot)** show the local history path in status and explain split track entries by @jdx in [#14979](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14979)
- **(dot)** resolve a relative dot add --source from the current directory by @jdx in [#14983](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14983)
- **(dot)** retry git write-tree when Windows refuses a loose object write by @jdx in [#15000](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/15000)
- **(env)** avoid sops CLI recursion through mise shims by @shuaiyafei in [#14801](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14801)
- **(hook-env)** install error hooks before the hook-env fast path by @jdx in [#14963](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14963)
- **(http)** accept # comment lines in netrc files by @jdx in [#14964](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14964)
- **(http)** apply Tera filters to {{ version }} in tool option templates by @jdx in [#14967](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14967)
- **(lock)** keep npm sidecars in one place for a symlinked config dir by @jdx in [#14961](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14961)
- **(lock)** skip platforms excluded by a tool's os option

title: test: pin java relock e2e to a fully published Temurin line
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2807/changes/mise/1029
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`core/test_java_shorthand_vendor_slow` locked java `17` and expected the newest Temurin 17 build to resolve on every platform. On 2026-10-22 Adoptium published Temurin 17.0.21+9 with only linux-x64 and mac-aarch64 binaries, so `mise lock --bump java` refused to replace the locked 17.0.2 entries for windows-x64, linux-arm64 and macos-x64. That failed `e2e-linux-7` and `trusted / e2e` on the 2026.10.19 release PR (#14892), and left `test-ci` and `release` red.

mise's behavior is correct here; the test just shouldn't depend on whichever upstream build is newest. The bump step now uses a `java = "17.0.20"` request, a line published for all platforms. The final vendor-switch section uses `java = "17.0.2"` for both the OpenJDK and Temurin locks, so it still checks that an uninstalled OpenJDK entry is replaced under the same request; Temurin's 17.0.2+8 is fixed metadata that upstream releases can't change. The other OpenJDK steps keep `java = "17"`. The assertions are unchanged apart from the expected "not in the lockfile" message naming `java@17.0.2`.

Validated by running `TEST_ALL=1 mise run test:e2e core/test_java_shorthand_vendor_slow` locally while Temurin 17.0.21+9 was still partial; it passes.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-308_agent.*

* **Tests**
  * Expanded automated coverage for Java lockfile updates, including version validation and handling of a vendor mismatch during locked installation.

--- e2e/core/test_java_shorthand_vendor_slow (+11/-1)

+# Bump against a pinned patch line: a newest Temurin build that Adoptium has only

+cat <<TOML >mise.toml

+java = "17.0.20"

-assert_fail "mise install --locked" "java@17 is not in the lockfile"

title: chore(deps): ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0387 in cargo-deny
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2806/changes/mise/1028
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`cargo deny check` now fails `lint` on every branch because of RUSTSEC-2026-0387, a constant-time advisory against `crypto-bigint` 0.5.5.

The crate comes from `pgp` (through `cx448` and `elliptic-curve` 0.13). The patched release is 0.7.6, which `pgp` cannot take because it pins 0.5, so `cargo update -p crypto-bigint` does nothing. mise only uses `pgp` to verify signatures over public data, so this adds an ignore entry with that reason, like the other transitive advisories in `deny.toml`.

## Test plan

- `cargo deny check advisories` passes with cargo-deny 0.19.6.

+                    # A literal suffix test, not `string match "*.$extension"`: the extension is
+                    # a name the binary sent, and a `*` or `?` in it should not widen the filter.
+                    set -l suffix ".$extension"
+                    set -l tail (string sub -s -(string length -- "$suffix") -- "$value")
+                    if test "$tail" = "$suffix"
                         printf '%s\n' $candidate
                         break
                     end

title: fix(shim): keep command wrappers in place during a concurrent reshim
body:
Every mise process on a machine execs command wrappers from one shared directory, `command-wrappers/bin`. A forced reshim, or one that found no wrapper wanted, removed that whole directory and recreated it without a lock. A process that exec'd a wrapper in that window failed with ENOENT, for example a git hook running `cargo` through an mbx wrapper while another project reshimmed. Polling a wrapper during 40 forced reshims found it missing 126 times in 30646 polls.

Now:

- A reshim takes the wrapper directory's lock, which bootstrap shim writers already take, and never removes the directory while a wrapper is wanted.
- Each wrapper is staged in a hidden directory inside it and renamed into place, so on Unix a concurrent exec finds either the old wrapper or the new one. Windows keeps its remove-then-rename fallback, which leaves the same brief gap it had before.
- Only unwanted wrappers are deleted, and the directory is removed only once it is empty. Bootstrap writers take the lock before creating the directory, so that removal cannot race them.
- A staging directory left by a reshim that died mid-publish is removed by the next reshim, so it cannot keep the directory, and with it the PATH entry, alive.

`e2e/cli/test_command_wrappers_reshim_race` polls the wrapper during 10 forced reshims and requires zero misses (304679 polls, 0 misses locally, about 4s), then checks that a stale staging directory is swept. Clippy (`--workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`) and the `test_command_wrappers*`, `test_shims*`, `test_reshim*` and `test_exec_wrapper*` e2e tests pass.

Related: #14277 and #14355, a different wrapper bug fixed on the same code path.

title: feat(bootstrap): let Homebrew upgrade casks mise installs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2797/changes/mise/1026
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Casks that mise installs are invisible to Homebrew: `brew upgrade` and `brew outdated` skip them and `brew doctor` reports their Caskroom folder as having no valid metadata. For a cask without auto-updates, such as `1password-cli` or a font, only `mise bootstrap packages upgrade` upgrades it.

This adds an opt-in for people who keep Homebrew:

```toml
[bootstrap.brew]
homebrew_metadata = true
```

After mise installs a `brew-cask` package, it writes `.metadata/<version>/<timestamp>/Casks/<token>.json` (containing `{}`, as Homebrew writes for a cask loaded from its API). Homebrew then counts the cask as installed, and mise's existing ownership rule leaves it to Homebrew from then on. The default is unchanged, and a failed metadata write only warns because the install itself has finished.

It does not write `INSTALL_RECEIPT.json`: Homebrew builds a default receipt from the current cask definition when it is absent.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14928

## Test plan

- `written_homebrew_metadata_hands_the_cask_to_homebrew` checks the path, the Homebrew timestamp format, and that `homebrew_installed_version` sees the cask afterwards.
- `test_brew_cask_homebrew_metadata_option_reaches_package_request` checks the setting reaches the package request.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the schema and docs conformance tests, pass. Not run against a real Homebrew on macOS.

title: fix(python): stop uv_venv_auto from fork-bombing through python shims
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2794/changes/mise/1025
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source"`, mise could fork-bomb the machine when a project had no `.venv`, a `.python-version` that uv hadn't installed, and a python that was installed in mise but not active in that directory. mise ran a bare `uv venv`, uv probed mise's own `python`/`python3` shims, and each probe started a mise that ran `uv venv` again. With any vfox tool installed the recursion never terminated.

Now the `uv venv` (or `python -m venv`) child that mise spawns carries `__MISE_CREATING_VENV=1`. A mise started inside it sees the variable and skips venv creation, so the shim probes return normally and the tree is finite.

This stops the runaway but not its cause: with no active mise python, mise still runs a bare `uv venv`, so uv picks its own interpreter.

Fixes the report in discussion #14926.

## Validation

- New e2e test `core/test_python_uv_venv_reentrant`: with the guard variable set no `.venv` is created; without it the venv is created as before. Passes.
- Not run: the discussion's docker repro, clippy, the other venv e2e tests.

title: fix(task): quote and escape header values written by tasks add --file
body:
`mise tasks add --file` writes a file task whose `#MISE` header it builds by pasting each value between hand-written quotes. `--dir` was not quoted at all, and quotes or backslashes in a description, alias or glob were not escaped. The header is invalid TOML, so the next `mise run` or `mise tasks` fails while loading the project's tasks:

```console
$ mise tasks add --file build --dir src -- make
$ mise run build
Error:
   0: failed to parse task header TOML "dir=src": TOML parse error at line 1, column 5
```

`--description 'Build "app"'` failed the same way (`#MISE description="Build "app""`).

The header values are now written with `toml_edit`, the same way the command already writes a `[tasks.<name>]` table, so they are quoted and escaped:

```sh
#MISE description='Build "app"'
#MISE dir="src"
```

Header lines with simple values (for example `#MISE depends=["test", "render"]`) are unchanged.

`e2e/tasks/test_task_add` now adds a file task with `--dir` and a quoted description, checks the header, and runs the task in that directory. It fails before this change and passes after it.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.301.*

title: security(backend): reject SLSA provenance built from another tag
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2790/changes/mise/1024
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

SLSA provenance made with a reusable workflow such as `slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator` is signed with the same identity for every release of a tool. mise checked the signer and the repository the workflow ran in, but not which release the workflow built. A mirror or compromised download host could serve an older release's genuine artifact and provenance as a newer version, and the provenance verified.

mise now also checks the git ref in the provenance's Fulcio certificate (the ref the signed workflow run built) against the tag of the version being installed or locked. Provenance built from another tag, or from a branch, is rejected:

```
SLSA provenance was built from refs/tags/v3.9.0, expected refs/tags/v3.10.0
```

Where the tag comes from depends on the backend. Versions are not assumed to follow any scheme, and mise does not guess at `v` prefixes:

- **`github:`** uses the tag of the release the asset came from, as long as that tag spells the version being installed (the same way the backend lists versions). If it doesn't, mise skips the check and logs a debug line.
- **`aqua:`** uses the recipe's `slsa_provenance.source_tag`, or else the version's release tag (what aqua templates as `{{.Version}}`, including any `version_prefix`). This matches the `--source-tag` that aqua passes to slsa-verifier. A version counts as a tag when the release asset was found under it, or when it was listed, locked, or made by `version_prefix`. A version whose download URL merely resolved doesn't count. A locked GitHub URL's tag must map back to the version being installed. When no tag is known, mise skips the check and logs a debug line. A `source_tag` of `-` turns the check off, which is how the registry marks tools built from a branch.
- **vfox plugins** can set a new `slsa_source_tag` attestation field to the tag the version's release was built from. Without it, mise doesn't check the ref.

```lua
attestation = {
    slsa_provenance_path = provenance_path,
    slsa_signer_identity = "https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/.github/workflows/generator_generic_slsa3.yml@refs/tags/v2.1.0",
    slsa_signer_issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com",
    slsa_source_repository = "your-org/example",
    slsa_source_tag = "v" .. ctx.version,
}
```

**Compatibility:** a `github:` tool that sets `slsa_signer_identity` but builds its releases from a branch instead of a tag no longer passes SLSA verification. The github backend docs now say so.

## Tests

- Unit tests use the sops v3.9.0 provenance fixture. Offered as v3.10.0 it is rejected, and offered as v3.9.0 it verifies. These run in mise-util through the full verification path, and in mise-sigstore through the DSSE path with the embedded trust root. With the check disabled, the rejection tests fail.
- Unit tests cover the github backend's tag mapping and aqua

title: fix(upgrade): don't downgrade date-versioned tools with leading zeros
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2761/changes/mise/1023
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14921

With `minimum_release_age` set, `mise upgrade yt-dlp` replaced a manually installed `2026.10.21` with the older `2026.08.19`:

```
Upgraded 1 tool:
  yt-dlp 2026.10.21 → 2026.08.19
```

Date versions with a leading zero (`2026.08.19`) are rejected by both the SemVer and `versions` parsers, so the comparison fell back to `current != latest` and treated any difference as outdated. Purely numeric dotted versions are now compared component by component before that fallback.

title: fix(bootstrap): find a just-installed git outside startup PATH
body:
`mise bootstrap --from <url>` offers to install git when the machine has none.

However, on a fresh macOS machine, due to how `mise_util::env::PATH` is captured once per process, and how `/opt/homebrew/bin` is not by default on system `PATH`, the run still tails with "installed git with brew, but git is still not on PATH" when the install is successful, as the re-check can still only see `/usr/bin/git` which is a stub to `xcrun` (a Linux machine with no distro package manager falling back to Homebrew would fail the same way too).

This only happens (on Unix) for Homebrew as it is the only one that does not require the prefix to be on `PATH` - `apt`, `dnf`, `pacman`, `zypper` and `apk` all require their CLI on `PATH` and installs into `/usr/bin`, which is on `PATH`.

This PR changes the post-install re-check to also look in the directory the chosen manager installs into, and prepends that directory to `PATH` inherited by child processes, so clone instead runs via the freshly installed copy of `git`.

For Windows, `winget` can still fail this way, because its installers extend `PATH` for new shells through the registry rather than the current environment, and mise has no way to read that. The failure message now says a new shell is needed instead of leaving it unexplained.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5; version: 2.1.310.*

* **Improvements**

title: feat(lsp): send semantic tokens for tasks, tools, env vars and templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1021
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14914

Editors color `mise.toml` with a plain TOML grammar, so a task name, a tool and an env var all look like any other key, and a `{{ }}` template inside a string is just string text. `mise lsp` knows what each key is, so it now sends `textDocument/semanticTokens/full` and `/range` and lets the editor color them.

| What | Token |
|---|---|
| `[tasks.X]`, `[task_templates.X]` headers | `function` + `declaration` |
| task names in `depends`, `depends_post`, `wait_for`, `extends`, `run = [{ task = "..." }]` | `function` |
| keys of `[tools]` and a task's `tools` | `type` |
| keys of `[env]` and a task's `env` | `variable` |
| keys of `[vars]` | `variable` + `readonly` |
| the `_` of `_.path`, `_.file`, `_.source`, ... | `keyword` |
| `{{ }}`, `{% %}`, `{# #}` in any string, `run` scripts included | `macro` |
| keys the schema marks deprecated | `deprecated` modifier |

A template in a multi-line string is sent one token per line. A file that does not parse returns `null`, so the client keeps the colors it has. Clients that prefer their own highlighting can turn it off with `initializationOptions`: `{"semanticTokens": false}`.

Tested with unit tests for each token kind, multi-line encoding, ranges, and the switch; `cargo test -p mise-lsp` and clippy with `-D warnings` pass. Not tried in a real editor.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

title: security: keep credentials out of install paths, lockfiles, logs and redirects
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2755/changes/mise/1020
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Credentials could end up where they shouldn't:
- tokens in tool URLs and `url_replacements` showed up in install directory names, Sigstore cache directories and error messages;
- http header tokens and templated credentials were written into install manifests and `mise.lock`;
- query-string tokens were sent to redirect targets in the `Referer` header;
- `mise doctor`, `mise settings` and `mise tool` printed age keys and Forgejo tokens;
- a shebang task's temporary script, which can contain templated secrets, was world-readable;
- OCI registry credentials went to a blob redirect host.

This PR strips or redacts credentials in all of those places.

## What changes

- **Shared redaction**: a common `strip_url_credentials` removes URL credentials (it keeps the user of an `ssh://git@` URL), and `redact_output` applies the logger's redaction to text printed outside the logger, such as the verbose error report and `mise doctor`.
- **Install directories and caches**: install directory names and Sigstore TUF cache directory names no longer contain URL credentials, or query parameters with credential-like names such as `?private_token=`. Other query parameters, such as `?ref=`, are kept.
- **Manifests and `mise.lock`**: install manifests no longer store http `headers` values, and lockfile options are stripped of credentials. The stripping also runs when `mise.lock` is read, so entries written with a token still match and are rewritten without it. A tool configured with credentials in its URL matches its credential-free lock entry, so it isn't pruned as stale or duplicated by a partial `mise lock <tool>`. npm credential options are masked as whole shell words, so `--_password="a b"` and `--_authToken="npm_"suffix` leave nothing behind.
- **HTTP**: every client built by mise sends no `Referer`, so a query-string token can't follow a redirect. Debug and error URLs hide query values but keep parameter names and the `page`, `per_page` and `limit` numbers.
- **`mise lock` output**: the progress, `--dry-run` and config-bump lines and the `--json` report show tools without URL credentials.
- **Doctor, settings and `mise tool`**: age keys, Forgejo tokens and credentials in tool options are redacted, in text and JSON output. `mise doctor project` redacts its check names, messages, hints and errors. `mise tool` redacts the backend, description and version list, and shows `[redacted]` for options and `install_env` entries with secret-shaped names such as `api_token` or `NPM_TOKEN`. `mise settings get sops.age_key` prints `[redacted]`.
- **Task scripts**: shebang task temp scripts are created readable only by the owner.
- **Task output redaction**: secret values that contain a newline are redacted line by line, so multi-line secrets no longer leak.
- **OCI**: registry credentials aren't sent to a blob redirect on another host, and a `401` from such

title: security(config): keep untrusted repo content from hanging or crashing hook-env
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2754/changes/mise/1019
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Simply `cd`-ing into an untrusted repository could hang or crash the shell prompt, or make mise echo the contents of files outside the repo. Ways it could happen:
- a `mise.toml` linked to `/dev/zero`;
- a symlink loop in a task directory;
- a non-UTF-8 directory name;
- a malformed `rust-toolchain.toml`;
- an aqua version with multibyte characters;
- a lockfile path or `.miserc.toml` filename that expands as a glob;
- an oversized session variable.

This PR makes config loading and `hook-env` robust against these inputs.

## What changes

- **Regular files only**: config files, `mise.lock`, task `file =` targets and git pointer files are read only when they are regular files. A config linked to a device or FIFO is skipped.
- **Task directory walk**: stops with an error after 100,000 entries, so a symlink maze can't hang task discovery.
- **"Did you mean" suggestions**: cached per name, skipped for names over 100 bytes, and limited to 20 distinct names per process.
- **`__MISE_SESSION`**: `hook-env` errors instead of exporting a variable over 128 KiB, which would stop every later command from starting.
- **Non-UTF-8 paths**: template contexts, trust record names and `--json` output handle them instead of panicking.
- **aqua**: `split_version_prefix` splits on character boundaries, and malformed `version_constraint` values are treated as unmatched instead of panicking.
- **`rust-toolchain.toml`**: a field of the wrong type is an error naming the field, not a panic.
- **Literal paths, not globs**: the Gemfile `ruby file:` watch, the lockfile watch path and `override_*_filenames` (rooted at their directory) are matched literally.
- **TOML parse errors**: they no longer quote a project file reached through a symlink, so a repo can't make mise print a file from elsewhere on disk. The error gives the file, line and column only; the parser's message is withheld too, since a value error such as `invalid type: string "…"` quotes the value. Projects that themselves sit behind a link, like macOS `/tmp`, still get the excerpt.
- **pypi**: sdist filenames in a simple index are parsed in linear time, so a crafted index can't stall `mise ls`.

- **Version files linked to another file**: a `.tool-versions` or idiomatic version file (such as `.node-version`) that is a symlink to a file with a different name is skipped with a warning that doesn't show its contents, and mise won't write `.tool-versions` back through such a link. A repo can no longer make mise read, print or overwrite something like `~/.netrc`. A same-name link, such as a shared `.tool-versions`, still works.
- **Config size limit**: `mise.toml`, `.tool-versions`, idiomatic version files, `mise.lock`, `.miserc.toml` and task TOML files larger than 16 MiB are refused with an error. A command that edits a config (`mise use`, `mise set`, …) fails instead of saving when the file can

title: security(http): bound response, download and archive sizes and slow response bodies
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2753/changes/mise/1018
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A small hostile download could make mise use gigabytes of memory or disk, or hang. Examples:
- a compressed HTTP response read fully into memory;
- an archive that expands thousands of times;
- a zip whose entries overlap;
- a tar with huge sparse members;
- a server that trickles a JSON reply forever.

This PR adds size and time limits to the places that read untrusted data.

## What changes

- **HTTP responses read into memory**: capped at 128 MiB after decompression in the shared client, for every getter and for callers that read bodies themselves. Separate clients get their own limits:
  - OCI blobs are capped at the size their descriptor declares;
  - attestation responses and the bundles they link to share a 16 MiB budget;
  - vfox `http.get`/`try_get` are capped at 128 MiB, and vfox downloads stream to disk;
  - remote cache blobs are capped at the size their digest records.
- **Downloads stored as sent**: downloads use a client with transfer decoding off, so a file is saved exactly as the server sent it and can't inflate during the download. Remote task files are capped at 128 MiB and packslip manifests at 4 MiB.
- **Self-update**: all response decoders are off. The release reply is capped at 16 MiB, the packslip at 4 MiB and the archive at 512 MiB. The Windows shim update uses the same client.
- **Archive extraction**: unpacking fails once the output is both over 256 MiB and over 100 times the download size. This is controlled by a new global-only setting, `extract_max_ratio` (`0` turns the check off). Zip archives are checked against the sizes in their central directory, so they are still decompressed only once.
- **SLSA archive content check**: stops after hashing 100 times the archive's size (at least 256 MiB), which stops overlapping zip entries and huge sparse tar members.
- **Choosing whether to strip a top-level directory**: archive reading now stops at the second top-level name instead of reading every entry, for tar, zip and 7z.
- **Slow responses**: reading a response body that mise parses is now bounded by `http_download_timeout`.

## Compatibility

- A tool archive that legitimately expands more than 100× and to over 256 MiB needs `extract_max_ratio` raised, or set to `0`.
- If a server compresses a download despite being asked not to, the file is saved compressed as received. For a `.tar.gz` mislabeled as gzip-encoded, that's the correct file.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. The exception is the attestation-client test, which was checked by reading the code. Unit tests pass for mise-util, vfox, mise-sigstore, mise-cache-core and self-update, and for the mise library apart from one test that needs write access to `/usr/local/share/mise` and can't run in this sandbox. The new e2e test `test_task_remote_http_encoded_body` and five existing remote-task and HTTP e2e tests

title: security(github): send forge tokens only to their API host and harden release caches
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2746/changes/mise/1017
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Forge API tokens, release caches and mise-versions pins had several weak spots:
- the GitHub token went to any host serving `/api/v3`;
- release caches could be shared between look-alike repositories;
- a download that failed its pinned checksum could be reused;
- a URL spelled in uppercase passed a pin check;
- `bootstrap --adopt` could pick a local directory over the GitHub repo;
- the GitHub relay capability was visible in the process list.

This PR fixes each of those.

## What changes

- **GitHub token**: the token goes only to a GitHub API host over https, or to the origin of the configured `api_url`. Before, any host serving `/api/v3` got it, including a URL in a remote task file or an `spm:` package name from an untrusted repository.
- **Remote task files in safe mode**: they are no longer fetched from project config, which matches how safe mode already treats remote includes. Safe mode lists those tasks from their TOML only.
- **`spm:` URL names**: naming a package by URL on a host other than github.com or gitlab.com needs trust, and safe mode no longer derives an API host from the name.
- **Release cache keys**: GitHub, Forgejo and GitLab release caches include a hash of the exact repository and tag, so look-alike repositories no longer share an entry. The npm, pipx and aqua latest-version caches are keyed by package.
- **mise-versions pins**: URLs from mise-versions are rebuilt in one standard form before they are compared, and the GitHub-API check parses the URL instead of comparing a string prefix. A digest from mise-versions can no longer serve a kept download from the cache. Asset IDs read from `mise.lock` are confirmed with GitHub before use, including aqua's private-repo path.
- **Download cache**: a download that fails its pinned checksum is not kept, and a cached file is checked against the pin before it is reused after a 304. A pinned checksum reuses a kept file only for a URL it was downloaded from.
- **mise-versions checksums in `mise.lock`**: when `mise lock` takes a checksum from mise-versions without downloading the file, it records `checksum_source = "mise-versions"`. That checksum is compared after a real download but is never used to serve a kept file.
- **GitHub Enterprise**: a new global-only setting, `github.enterprise_hosts` (`MISE_GITHUB_ENTERPRISE_HOSTS`), lists hosts that receive the GitHub token on `/api/v3` URLs over https. Project config can't set it.
- **Task `global` flag**: a task is global only when it's loaded from global config. A project's `[tasks.x]` table or `#MISE global=true` header no longer sets it.
- **Self-update**: the release index and the Windows shim download send a configured `self_update.api_url` token only to that API's origin.
- **`mise bootstrap --adopt`**: a bare `OWNER/REPO` that also exists as a path in the current directory is refused. Write a local path as `./
