title: security(packslip): pin signers by repository ID and stop release-age backdating
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2745/changes/mise/1016
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

packslip's signer pins could be redirected by a repository rename or by a file in the working directory, and its `workflow` pins never checked the repository ID. Separately, `minimum_release_age` could be dodged by a backdated GitLab release, or by a packslip bundle with no transparency-log time. This PR closes those gaps and fixes several packslip performance and robustness bugs.

## What changes

### Signer pins

- **Renames**: a pin that has no repository ID, such as one set by `identity`, `identity_prefix` or `pubkey`, holds by name and never follows a rename. After a real rename, run `mise packslip forget <tool>` once. Merging pins keeps a repository ID even when only the old-name pin held it, and a pin that follows a rename no longer leaves the old name open to a new owner.
- **`workflow` pins**: these are checked against the pinned repository ID like other forge pins. Registry shorthands that set `workflow` (hk, fnox, usage and others) still install. They now record repository IDs, so `mise lock` adds `repository_ids` to existing entries once.
- **`pubkey`**: a value that parses as a key line is used as a key, and is not first looked up as a file in the working directory.

### Release age

- **GitLab**: releases are dated by the later of `created_at` and `released_at`, so a backdated `released_at` can't make a new release look old.
- **packslip**: a bundle's own published date only counts when `allow_unlogged` is set. Otherwise a bundle with no log time is treated as too new.
- **Cutoff search**: instead of looking up one date per version (one Go proxy request per too-new version, and now aqua `github_tag` packages too), the cutoff steps back and then bisects.

### Safe mode and robustness

- **`requires.bin`**: resolving a version no longer starts commands named in a manifest. At install, the `--version` probe runs in the command's own directory, not the project.
- **Performance**: completion resource selection and the `requires.libs` `ldconfig -p` call run once instead of once per bin or library.
- **Nested skill directories**: deeply nested skill directories no longer overflow the stack.

## Compatibility

- After a repository rename, a packslip tool whose pin (or `mise.lock` entry) has no repository ID needs `mise packslip forget <tool>`, or its lock entry removed, before it installs again.
- If a backend's version order isn't chronological, the release-age cutoff may settle on an older eligible version.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. One exception is the version-resolution half of the `requires.bin` change: reverting it breaks compilation rather than a test. mise-util and mise unit tests pass, apart from one that needs write access to `/usr/local/share/mise` and can't run in the sandbox. title: security(task): close sandbox escapes in --allow-write, --deny-net and --deny-write, and OCI whiteouts
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1015
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's task and exec sandbox (`--deny-net`, `--deny-write`, `--allow-write`) could be escaped or silently weakened, and an OCI base image could delete files on the build host. This PR closes those gaps.

## What changes

- **`--allow-write` and symlinks**: an allowed path is refused when a symlink inside the project leads outside it (the project is matched by device and inode, so a differently-cased path on a case-insensitive volume is caught too), so a repository can't plant `./out -> ~/.ssh` and have the sandbox grant write access there. The error says to name the target directly. Your home directory is never treated as a project, so allowed paths like `~/.npm` that point to another disk still work.
- **`--deny-net`**: the seccomp filter now allows only Unix and netlink sockets, and it blocks io_uring and x32 system-call aliases on x86_64. Before, AF_SMC or other socket families, io_uring and x32 `socket()` calls all bypassed it.
- **`--deny-write` on older kernels**: on kernels whose Landlock can't block `truncate(2)` (Linux before 6.2), write restrictions now refuse to run with a clear error instead of silently allowing truncation. `mise run` checks this before starting the task.
- **Env-only sandboxes**: while a task runs under `deny_env`/`allow_env`, `mise run` marks itself non-dumpable, so a sandboxed task running as the same user can't read the withheld variables from `/proc/<mise pid>/environ` or attach to mise with ptrace. `mise exec` replaces itself with the command, so it holds nothing to read. The shell that started mise and commands running as root aren't covered. Add `--deny-write` or `--deny-all` for untrusted commands.
- **Empty `allow_write`**: an allow list whose entries are all empty, or render to nothing, now blocks every write instead of turning the sandbox off.
- **macOS**: `mise exec` and tasks start `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec` instead of looking it up on the command's PATH, which tool bin directories could shadow.
- **OCI builds**: base-image whiteout files no longer delete through a symlink the layer planted, and the malformed whiteout `.wh..` is rejected. The apt cleanup step checks every directory down to `var/cache/apt/archives`, like the apk cleanup.

## Compatibility

- Programs that need io_uring no longer run under `--deny-net`.
- On Linux before 6.2 (for example stock Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04 kernels), `--deny-write`/`allow_write` sandboxes now fail to start.
- A project symlink that points outside the project, such as `./target -> /cache`, can no longer be used as an allowed path. Name the target instead.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it, except the old-kernel check: this kernel is 7.2, so only its "truncate is required" logic could be exercised. mise-util, mise-oci and the task/sandbox unit tests pass, as do the e2e tests `test_task_sandbox_symlink_escape`, `test_task_san

title: ci: retry snapcraft upload on transient store errors
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1013
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The v2026.10.18 snap shipped for amd64 but not arm64: the Snap Store closed the connection during the arm64 upload (`RemoteDisconnected: Remote end closed connection without response`). `snapcore/action-publish` can't retry, and re-running by hand only works while the 1-day build artifacts still exist.

This replaces the action with a plain `snapcraft upload ... --release stable` step that retries up to 3 times (10s, 20s backoff). Re-uploading the same snap is safe because the store deduplicates by hash. The step installs snapcraft the same way the action did (`snap install --classic snapcraft`), and no new third-party action is added.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*
author: jdx
diff:
--- .github/workflows/snapcraft-publish.yml (+17/-4)
@@ -96,9 +96,22 @@ jobs:
           fi
           echo "path=${snaps[0]}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 
-      - uses: snapcore/action-publish@214b86e5ca036ead1668c79afb81e550e6c54d40 # v1.2.0
+      # Not snapcore/action-publish: it cannot retry, and the Snap Store
+      # occasionally drops the connection mid-upload.

           SNAPCRAFT_STORE_CREDENTIALS: ${{ secrets.SNAPCRAFT_STORE_CREDENTIALS }}

+              sleep "$((attempt * 10))"
+            fi
+          done
+          echo "::error::snapcraft upload failed after 3 attempts"
+          exit 1

title: security(backend): make SLSA, attestation and signed-checksum checks fail closed
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2740/changes/mise/1012
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Several provenance checks in the github and aqua backends and in `mise lock` could be satisfied by the wrong file, or skipped without failing:
- a release could present the artifact itself as its SLSA provenance;
- `mise lock` pinned aqua releases without the checks the recipe declares;
- a SHA-512 signed checksum file was not compared with the artifact;
- an SLSA signer pin passed when the provenance was missing;
- a lockfile merge kept old provenance next to a new checksum.

This PR closes each of those.

## What changes

- **SLSA provenance download (github)**: the provenance file downloads into its own temporary directory under a fixed name, at install and at lock time, so it can never overwrite or stand in for the selected asset.
- **SLSA signer pins (github)**: when a `github:` tool sets both `slsa_signer_*` options, a release with no provenance, or with empty or unreadable provenance, fails `mise install` and `mise lock`. GitHub attestations still satisfy the pin. Tools without those options behave as before.
- **aqua at lock time**: when no GitHub attestation exists, `mise lock` checks the next mechanism the recipe declares (cosign, minisign or SLSA), as install already did.
- **Signed checksum files with another algorithm**: when the signed checksum file uses a different hash than the recorded one (for example SHA-512), the artifact is hashed against the signed digest at lock time.
- **aqua `attestations_since`**: the registry's `attestations_since` cutoff now applies to `aqua:` backends as it already does to `github:`. For an aqua tool whose recipe declares GitHub attestations, a release at or after the cutoff that has no attestation fails install and lock. Earlier releases, tools with no cutoff and users who turned attestations off are unaffected. Version comparison is the existing `github:` one, and a version that can't be compared is never required.
- **Lockfile merges**: a merge no longer keeps old provenance next to a changed checksum, and `mise lock` refuses an entry whose checksum changed while its provenance got weaker, including a replacement uploaded under a new file name.

## Compatibility

- A lockfile entry with a checksum but no provenance installs on the checksum alone, even when the `slsa_signer_*` options are set. Re-run `mise lock` to record provenance, or set `locked_verify_provenance` to verify on every install.
- mise releases without this change reject `attestations_since` on `aqua:` entries, and would drop the whole floating registry. No registry entry uses it yet, and `docs/contributing/registry.md` says to wait until those releases are out of use.

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it, including the new e2e test `test_aqua_registry_attestations_since`. The provenance, SLSA, cosign and attestation e2e tests pass, as do the registry, aqua, github and lockfile uni

title: security(lockfile): stop lockfiles, tool stubs and the task cache from reaching outside the repo
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1011
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise.lock`, `mise lock` and remote task caching trusted the content of a repository more than they should have. A committed symlink could make mise delete or overwrite files outside the repo, or copy files from outside it into lock sidecars. An untrusted lockfile could switch a tool's backend or download URL. `mise lock` read tool stubs before checking trust. A remote task cache entry could restore files outside the task's declared outputs.

## What changes

- **Symlinks around lockfiles**: sidecar cleanup, writes and reads under `.mise/locks` no longer follow a symlink between the lockfile's directory and the sidecar, including a committed `.mise` or `.mise/locks` link. mise writes through a `mise.lock` symlink that leaves its directory only for the global or system lockfile, or, outside safe mode, for a lockfile owned by a trusted config.
- **Untrusted lockfiles**: an untrusted project's lockfile still pins versions and checksums. Entries that switch to a different backend or add inline options are ignored. The rest lose their download URLs, conda packages and `uv`/`aube` graphs, so mise resolves those itself.
- **`mise lock` and tool stubs**: `mise lock` asks for trust before reading the tool stubs it lists (each stub is checked in paranoid mode), and before resolving task tools that carry options. A stub's full path is canonicalized, so a symlinked stub can't reach a file outside the project.
- **`.miserc.toml` paths**: `env` names containing a path separator are ignored, as are override filenames that are absolute or contain `..`. Monorepo lockfile migration only reads sources inside the monorepo. `MISE_ENV`, `-E` and `MISE_OVERRIDE_*` that you set yourself are unchanged.
- **Backend dependency cycles**: a dependency cycle in a lockfile no longer overflows the stack.
- **Remote task cache**: a cached symlink's target may use `..` only before its first named component. Restores never write through a symlink the cache entry staged, and refuse any root or file the task's `outputs` don't select. Such an entry counts as a cache miss and the task runs.

## Compatibility

`mise lock` and installs in an untrusted clone keep the lockfile's versions and checksums, but re-resolve download URLs and dependency graphs instead of taking them from the lockfile.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. About 60 existing lock, lockfile, tool-stub, trust and task-cache e2e tests pass along with the new ones. Unit tests pass apart from one that needs write access to `/usr/local/share/mise` and can't run in the sandbox. clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check` pass.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1010
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `pypi:` tool whose source is a private GitHub repository over `git+ssh://` failed to list versions without a `GITHUB_TOKEN`, even though the user's SSH key can read the repository:

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/<owner>/<private-repo>.git" = "latest"
```

```text
mise ERROR GitHub repository <owner>/<private-repo> not found (404 from mise-versions.jdx.dev, ...)
```

mise now falls back to `git ls-remote --tags` over SSH when the versions host and the GitHub API can't list an `ssh://` github.com source, so the SSH agent provides the access. HTTPS sources keep the existing error. The fallback lists tags rather than GitHub releases, as the non-github.com path already does.

Closes discussion #14894.

title: security(backend): tighten SLSA signer and GitHub attestation checks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1009
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise checks GitHub attestations and SLSA provenance before installing some tools. This PR tightens what those checks accept and fixes three robustness bugs in the attestation client.

## What changes

- **SLSA signer source repository**: when the signer is a GitHub workflow, the signing run must come from the repository that holds that workflow or from the tool's own repository. Before, any run of a shared reusable workflow such as slsa-github-generator passed, whoever ran it. Projects that build in a separate repository keep working. The github backend uses the tool's repository and aqua uses `source_uri`. vfox plugins can set a new optional `slsa_source_repository` field in PreInstall.
- **Attestation repository**: attestations returned by the GitHub API must name the repository that was asked for, which matters when the API is reached through a mirror. A renamed repository is still accepted when GitHub confirms the rename. When `url_replacements` reroutes the API, that rename lookup is not trusted.
- **Tokens and URL replacements**: when `url_replacements` moves an attestation request to a different host, mise no longer sends the GitHub token there.
- **Rekor inclusion**: the transparency-log check is skipped only for GitHub's own log-less Sigstore instance. Public-good bundles that carry only a timestamp and no Rekor entry are rejected.
- **Bug fixes**: bundle fetches stop at the `per_page` limit, so an install can't hang on an endless list. A malformed `bundle_url` returns an error instead of panicking.

## Compatibility

- A repository renamed or transferred after a release was signed still passes SLSA verification when api.github.com confirms the rename; a `url_replacements` mirror cannot confirm it. vfox plugins set `slsa_source_repository` themselves.
- A cross-host `http://` mirror for attestation requests now receives an unauthenticated request instead of failing the install.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. mise-sigstore, mise-util, vfox and the backend unit tests pass. The lockfile provenance, aqua SLSA, aqua attestation, github registry attestation, and python and ruby attestation e2e tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(config): stop treating help, shims, hooks and config writes as consent to trust
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2734/changes/mise/1008
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Several commands treated running them as consent to trust the project, even when you never asked mise to trust anything. A command that only printed help could trust the project. So could a shim run, a task hook, a config write or an MCP call. After that, the project's `[env]`, hooks and tasks ran on every later prompt. This PR narrows that implicit trust to the cases where you actually chose to run the project's code.

## What changes

- **`mise trust` on the command line**: a command whose first argument is `trust` no longer skips the trust check for every config it loads. Shims ignore their argv for this check.
- **`mise run --help` / `mise watch --help`**: printing help no longer trusts the project. Neither does the bare `help` task.
- **Shims and hooks**: running a tool through a shim (including asdf plugin shims) no longer implies trust. The `mise run` that task hooks and `watch_files` tasks start requires explicit trust, so a hook from a trusted global config can't silently trust the project it fires in.
- **Config writes**: `mise set`, `mise unset`, `mise tasks add` and other commands that save a config used to mark the whole directory trusted afterwards, including sibling configs mise never checked. They now ask before trusting an untrusted sibling, and fail without a terminal. In safe mode they record no trust at all.
- **Monorepo marker**: the `.monorepo` marker only counts while its root is itself trusted, which also defuses markers already on disk. It is only written for a trusted root, and CI leaves it alone.
- **MCP server**: `run_task` refuses untrusted file tasks, and refuses a task name shaped like a file path (`./`, `../`, `~/`, absolute, drive or UNC paths). The `mise run` it starts looks names up only as tasks, never as script paths, so a file created after the check can't be run in a task's place. `install_tool` refuses inline tool options such as `postinstall`.
- **`mise bootstrap`**: picks the `bootstrap` task the same way `mise run bootstrap` does, so a task merely aliased to `bootstrap` doesn't count. It refuses only when that task itself, or a task it reaches through `depends`, `depends_post` or its `run` entries, comes from untrusted config. Your own global `bootstrap` still runs inside an untrusted repo, as long as it doesn't reach that repo's tasks.
- **Explicit-trust runs**: when a task hook or MCP child starts `mise run`, it refuses if the tasks reach any task from untrusted config. That includes inline tasks in a tasks-only parent `mise.toml`. The check follows dependencies only when they would run, so `MISE_TASK_SKIP_DEPENDS=1` is honored. A `run` entry with templated arguments is checked by the executor once rendered, before any of its tools are installed.
- **Task overlays**: a task counts as trusted only if every config file that adds to it is trusted, not just the file that defines it. An

title: security(config): tie trust to the right files for worktrees, symlinks and config dirs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2733/changes/mise/1007
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Trust is supposed to follow the files you actually trusted. Several layouts let a cloned repository borrow trust it was never given, or switch off paranoid mode:
- a forged git worktree pointing at a trusted checkout;
- a symlink to your global config;
- a clone named `.mise`;
- a project `.miserc.toml` that hid the global config;
- `mise trust --ignore` steered onto the global config.

This PR ties trust to the right files again.

## What changes

- **Git worktrees**: a worktree shares its main checkout's trust only if the repository's own `worktrees/<name>/gitdir` record points back at it. A symlinked main checkout no longer passes trust along, which also fixes a stack overflow on a self-referencing link.
- **Config directories**: a `mise/`, `.mise/` or `.config/` directory that is its own git checkout is treated as a separate project, with its own trust. A git-managed `~/.config` or mise config directory is exempt.
- **Global config symlinks**: a project symlink to the global config, including one in `conf.d`, no longer moves the global config's root into the project.
- **`.miserc.toml`**: a project `.miserc.toml` can no longer hide global or system config.
- **`mise trust --ignore`**: never picks or accepts the global config. Ignoring `~/mise.toml` no longer drops the global config too.
- **Paranoid mode (`config` category)**:
  - idiomatic version files such as `.nvmrc` need trust, and `mise trust`, `mise untrust` and `mise trust --ignore` can find them;
  - each local task file needs its own trust, even next to a trusted `mise.toml`;
  - a local `aqua.registries` file named by a project config needs its own content-bound trust. Files named by global or system config stay exempt.
- **Override files**: `config.override.toml` keeps the global config root when `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` points elsewhere.
- **Remote git includes pinned to a commit SHA**: mise checks out that commit and fails unless `HEAD` matches it. A branch or tag named like the SHA can no longer replace it.
- **git errors**: non-UTF-8 output from git is reported instead of panicking.

## Compatibility

- A worktree moved by hand needs `git worktree repair` before it shares trust again.
- A user's own `~/.miserc.toml` can no longer ignore the global config.
- Pinning a remote include to an annotated tag's object ID now errors; pin the commit SHA instead.
- In paranoid mode, run `mise trust <file>` once for each existing task file.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. About 50 related trust, paranoid, miserc and global-config e2e tests pass, along with the new ones. `cargo test --bin mise` and the mise-util git tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(backend): validate versions and names that become paths or URL segments
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1006
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tool versions and names from config files or remote version lists become path components and URL segments. Values such as `..`, `../../x`, a percent-encoded `%2e%2e`, or a name with `/` could point an install, a shim or a plugin lookup outside the directory it belonged in. This PR validates those values where they are turned into paths.

## What changes

- **Resolved versions**: the version a request resolves to, whether from a release API, a version list or `mise.lock`, must follow the same rules as a requested version, and must not be empty or `.`. At install time it also may not contain whitespace, `; & | < > ( )` or `% # ?`. That stricter check runs only at install time, so offline `ls` and `hook-env` still load.
- **Download URLs**: bun, erlang and Forgejo encode the version as a single URL path segment. aqua builds its URLs from path segments and refuses versions containing `% # ? \` or a `.`/`..` segment. The version and ref validators also refuse a percent-encoded `..`.
- **vfox backend plugins**: plugin names must be plain directory names, both in tool keys and in `[plugins]` entries.
- **reshim**: the tool name is kebab-cased before mise looks under `plugins/` for shims, and the generated shim script quotes its target.
- **`mise generate task-stubs`**: stops before writing anything if a task name would put a stub outside the stub directory.
- **cargo native binstall**: bin names, and the `.crate` file name built from the crates.io response, must be plain file names.

## Compatibility

- A remote version containing quotes, `$`, `\`, a leading `-` or `..` now fails with "invalid tool version" instead of installing.
- The undocumented `owner/repo:tool` form no longer resolves to a backend plugin.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it: 13 unit tests, plus the new e2e tests `test_resolved_version_path_safety`, `test_backend_plugin_name_path` and `test_generate_task_stubs_escape`. Related forgejo, backend-plugin, reshim, bun and erlang e2e tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(config): close safe-mode gaps for lazy tools, deps, S3, bin_path and templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/-/trails/2730/changes/mise/1004
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Safe mode (`MISE_SAFE=1`) is meant to let you run mise inside an untrusted project without that project's config running code or reading secrets. Several project settings still got through. This PR closes them.

## What changes in safe mode

- **Lazy tools**: a project's lazy tools get no shims and are not installed on first use. A project `[tool_alias]` can no longer make a global tool lazy.
- **`[deps]`**: a project's `[deps]` is ignored. Providers from global and system config still run.
- **Rust**: `mr_boxington` only takes effect when the trusted rust entry sets it itself. A bare `rust@<version>` argument no longer turns it on.
- **S3**: every S3 request is refused, including for s3 tools from global config, the same trade-off asdf already makes. Versions already pinned in the lockfile still resolve.
- **spm**: `install_command` is refused, like `postinstall` and `install_env`.
- **`path:` versions**: a project's `path:` versions, and `[tool_alias]` entries that point at `path:`, are ignored.
- **Templates**: project templates, including a project `.miserc.toml`, see an empty `env`. In every config, `get_env()`, the `hash_file`, `file_size`, `last_modified` and `canonicalize` filters, and the `dir`, `file` and `exists` tests are unavailable. Global and system config keep `env`, including for `[deps]` providers, `[wrappers]`, `[bootstrap]` and `[dotfiles]` templates.
- **Forge tokens**: GitHub, GitLab and Forgejo tokens aren't sent to a host that a project `api_url` names, unless global config names the same host. The public forges are not affected.
- **netrc**: in safe mode, mise records every host named by a project tool's `url`, `checksum_url`, `version_list_url`, `version_date_url` or `api_url` (platform-specific keys included). No request to those hosts gets netrc credentials, on any code path. If one of those hosts is templated, netrc is withheld everywhere. Work for tools declared in global or system config keeps its netrc credentials.
- **`[tool_alias]`**: a project alias for a tool that the global config declares is ignored.

## What changes in every mode

- **Project `.miserc.toml` templates**: a project `.miserc.toml` still never needs trust. Its templates now see an empty `env` and are limited, so they can't leak secrets or hang mise:
  - at most 16 KiB;
  - only `if`/`elif`/`else` statements, so no loops;
  - only the `arch()`, `os()`, `os_family()`, `libc()`, `avx2()` and `num_cpus()` functions;
  - only filters and tests that neither grow their input much nor touch the filesystem.

  A file outside these limits is left unrendered, with a warning. Global and system `.miserc.toml` files keep the full template language and `env`.
- **`bin_path`**: must stay inside the tool's install directory everywhere it is used. For http tools it is checked before anything is downloaded, and the extraction cache key uses a

title: security(install): enforce pinned checksums and node signatures instead of falling back
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1005
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Several installers let a download host get around a checksum or signature that should have been enforced: either by answering 404, or because the installer preferred the host's own checksum. With this PR, a pinned or published checksum is checked, and a missing signature fails the install instead of being skipped.

## What changes

- **node**
  - A missing `SHASUMS256.txt.sig` now fails `mise install` and `mise lock` instead of skipping GPG verification. The unofficial-builds host, which signs nothing and serves the musl builds, is exempt.
  - `mise lock` verifies the signature before recording checksums. If verification fails it warns and records the entry without a checksum, so the next install verifies the signature itself.
  - If `mise.lock` pins the prebuilt archive and the host answers 404, the install fails and points at `mise lock node`, instead of quietly compiling the source tarball.
- **erlang**: the checksum `mise.lock` pins wins over the one builds.hex.pm publishes for the same artifact.
- **npm**: when a checksum is pinned, the root package in the aube lock graph must match the tarball that passed that checksum.
- **spm**: when `mise.lock` pins a bundle checksum for this platform, a missing or altered artifact bundle fails the install instead of falling back to a source build.
- **http**: the `mise.lock` checksum is checked before unpacking, as the s3 backend already does.
- **bun and deno**: installs without a lock entry check the archive against the publisher's sha256.
- **GPG**: verification work is capped at one attempt per trusted key and subkey, so a `.sig` file full of bogus signatures can't stall an install.

## Compatibility

Node mirrors that don't copy the `.sig` files, and a few early releases that never had one (for example 4.0.0 and 5.12.0), now need `node.gpg_verify = false`. The error message says so.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it: unit tests, plus 7 new or extended e2e tests. Related node, npm, erlang lockfile and tool-stub e2e tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`. Not tested end to end:
- deno, which shares bun's code path;
- the npm call site, which would need a fake registry serving tarballs;
- erlang on macOS and Windows.

title: security(completion): stop shell completion from running untrusted task code
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1003
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Pressing TAB in an untrusted repository could run code from that repository. Task argument completers (`complete run=`, `choices run=`, `mount`) ran without a trust check, and a task file whose name contained Tera syntax was rendered with `exec()` available. Typed words were pasted unquoted into mise's own `sh -c` completers, and control characters in task names could forge zsh completion output. The fish and PowerShell emitters also quoted some values with rules those shells don't use.

## What changes

- **Completion commands need trust.** Shell completion only runs `complete run=`, `complete delegate=`, `choices run=` and `mount` for tasks from trusted config. Task names, help, flags and static choices still complete in untrusted projects, and the dynamic completers come back after `mise trust`. In safe mode they stay off even for trusted project tasks.
- **mise's own completers quote their input.** The five built-in completers that interpolate typed words now shell-quote them and put `--` before them.
- **Control characters**: completion candidates containing control characters are dropped, and control characters in descriptions become spaces, including in `mise tasks ls --complete`.
- **Task file names**: a script discovered in a task directory is used by its literal path, so a file name is never rendered as a template. `file = "{{ config_root }}/…"` in TOML still renders.
- **fish**: all output, including the `-C` script `mise exec -- fish` builds, now uses fish's own single-quote rules.
- **PowerShell**: the typographic single quotes U+2018 to U+201B are doubled too, since PowerShell treats them as quote characters.

## Compatibility

Dynamic task completions now need trust in two cases:
- a project that has only a `mise-tasks/` directory and no config file needs `mise trust .`;
- tasks that a global config includes from a directory outside `~/.config/mise/tasks` need that directory to be trusted.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. Awkward values were round-tripped through real fish and pwsh. `cargo test --bin mise` passes, as do the 4 new and 17 related existing e2e tests, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(hooks): render hook commands once and keep templates out of written versions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1002
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Hook commands were rendered by Tera twice: once when the config loaded, and again just before the hook ran. Whatever the first pass substituted was then evaluated as template source. So with a hook like

```toml
[hooks]
cd = "echo now in {{ cwd | quote }}"
```

a directory whose name contained `{{ exec(command=...) }}` ran that command when you `cd`ed into it. Hooks are now rendered once, when they load.

This PR also closes two related ways untrusted template text ended up in `mise.toml`.

## What changes

- **Hooks**: commands are rendered once, at load. `{% raw %}…{% endraw %}` in a hook command now prints literally instead of being rendered on a second pass.
- **Hook working directory**: a project's `enter`, `leave` and `[[watch_files]]` `run` commands now start in the project root instead of the shell's current directory, so entering through a subdirectory that contains its own `bin/` or `scripts/` can't change which script runs. `cd` hooks and hooks from the global config still run in the shell's directory. Use `$MISE_PROJECT_ROOT` where a hook needs the root explicitly.
- **Writing versions**: `mise use`, `mise upgrade --bump` and every other writer refuse to write a version containing `{{`, `{%` or `{#` into `mise.toml` or `.tool-versions`. A remote version list can no longer plant a template in your config.
- **Option templates**: when mise rewrites a tool entry, an option whose current value matches what its template renders to is written back as the template. Secrets rendered from `{{ env.X }}` no longer end up in the file.
- **Tera filters**: `hash_file` and `last_modified` return a render error instead of panicking on a missing file or a pre-1970 modification time.

## Limitations

- A rewritten tool entry renders its option templates a second time, so an `exec()` in a tool option runs again.
- Templates whose output changes on every call, or that fail to render, are still written rendered.
- `.tool-versions` files that use templates are still rendered as a whole when read.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it: the new e2e tests `test_hooks_render_once`, `test_upgrade_bump_template_version` and `test_use_keeps_option_templates`, plus unit tests. Existing hook, `use` and `upgrade` e2e tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(backend): keep untrusted values out of subprocess arguments and the project directory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1001
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Values from an untrusted project could reach the command lines of tools mise runs, and some of those tools ran inside the project directory, where the repo's own files could change what they do. This PR keeps those values in their place and starts build tools and VCS lookups outside the project.

## What changes

- **git version lookups** (npm, pipx, spinel and go git sources, the history-sync relay check, and `git credential fill`) now run from `$HOME` (or `/` if it is missing). They drop an inherited `GIT_DIR` and put `--` before the remote. A repo's `.git/config` (for example `core.sshCommand`) no longer applies, and a remote starting with `-` is no longer read as an option.
- **Build tools** (ruby-build, python-build, `cargo install`/`binstall`, `gem install` and ruby's default gems) run in the tool's install directory instead of the user's directory. ruby and python versions containing a path separator are refused. ruby-install still runs in the user's directory, because its `--patch` paths are relative to it.
- **rustup**: the `rustup --version` probe pins the toolchain, as the cargo and rustc probes already did, so a project `rust-toolchain.toml` cannot pick which `rustc` runs.
- **asdf**: `exec-env` is refused in safe mode.
- **npm**: the package name passed to `npm view` comes after `--`, and npm runs in its own metadata directory. Versions returned by the registry must pass an allowlist, so a version that is really a package spec (a URL, a path, `x.tgz`) is rejected.
- **conda**: match specs are built from a parsed name and version. Version globs such as `3.12.*` still work. A version can no longer inject bracketed options such as `[url=…]`.
- **package.json**: the suffix after `+` in `packageManager` must be `<algorithm>.<hex digest>`, otherwise the declaration is ignored. Tool options from version files read without trust (`package.json`, `rust-toolchain.toml`) are refused if they contain template syntax. The `packageManager` checksum is now applied when `devEngines` names the same version without one.

## Compatibility

- A relative `go.repo` setting now resolves from `$HOME`, not the current directory.
- A `packageManager` value with a non-hex checksum is now ignored.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. Unit tests pass (549 in the mise library, 824 in mise-util), as do 25 e2e tests in the affected areas, clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

title: security(backend): keep archive contents and release asset names inside the install directory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/1000
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise now refuses to install a tool whose release metadata or archive would write files outside the tool's install directory.

Before this change, a release asset name containing `../` or `/` could place the download outside the download directory. That covered the github, gitlab and forgejo asset lists, SLSA provenance files and spm artifact bundles. A symlink inside a tool archive could also point outside the install directory, and later steps (chmod, bin linking, packslip file copies) followed it. aqua registry `files[].src`/`link` and spm `info.json` paths were joined unchecked as well.

## What changes

- Release asset names must be plain file names. Anything else fails with an error naming the asset.
- After extraction, archives installed by the github, http, aqua, cargo-binstall and packslip backends must not contain symlinks that resolve outside the install directory. vfox now applies its existing check to tarballs, not just zips, and to the Lua `archiver.decompress` helper.
- aqua registry `src`, `name` and `link` values must stay inside the install directory. A leading `./` is still accepted.
- spm artifact bundles must name a plain executable that resolves inside the extracted bundle.
- SLSA content checks treat a zip entry as a symlink before checking whether it is a directory, the same order extraction uses. A symlink named like a directory is no longer counted as verified content.

## Compatibility

A tool archive that ships a symlink pointing outside its own directory now fails to install through the backends above. Brew casks and aqua dmg/pkg installs are deliberately not checked, because they legitimately ship links such as `Applications -> /Applications`.

## Validation

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it: unit tests, plus the new e2e tests `test_github_asset_name_traversal` and `test_archive_symlink_outside_install`. Existing github, http, aqua, packslip, spm, vfox and cargo-binstall e2e tests pass, as do clippy with `-D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.308.*

title: fix(lock): rebuild lockfiles completely by default
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/999
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes a gap where `mise install` records a lockfile entry only for the platform it ran on. With the default `lockfile_mode = "merge"`, a `mise.lock` committed from one machine has no entries for other platforms, so `mise install --locked` on another platform fails with a missing entry. This came up in [discussion 14885](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14885).

`lockfile_mode = "generate"` already rebuilds the whole lockfile from the current requests, reuses unchanged entries, and locks the other platforms during installs. It has been an opt-in trial since 2026.9.5. This PR makes it the default and removes the build-time gate that required a decision by December 2026.

```toml
# mise.toml: the previous behavior stays available
[settings]
lockfile_mode = "merge"   # or MISE_LOCKFILE_MODE=merge
```

- Neither mode creates a lockfile. Run `mise lock` or set `lockfile = true`, as before.
- No lockfile format migration is needed in either direction.
- Docs and `schema/mise.json` are updated, and the "trial" wording is removed.
- This does not make `mise install` read-only when a lockfile exists; `generate` still writes the file.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p mise-settings` and the `lockfile_mode` unit test pass.
- e2e: `test_lockfile_monorepo`, `test_settings_invalid_choice`, `test_lockfile_runtime_scope`, `test_lockfile_global_preserve_unreferenced` and `test_lockfile_pipx_selected_python` pass. `test_lockfile_generate_platform_options` failed locally while removing `/usr/local/share/mise/installs/jq/1.6`; it sets `generate` explicitly, so I don't believe this change causes it, but I did not check it against `main`. Clippy and the full suite were not run.

* **New Features**

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/996
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [aube](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube) | dependencies | patch | `2.8.1` → `2.8.2` |
| [aube-registry](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube) | dependencies | patch | `2.8.1` → `2.8.2` |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>aubepkg/aube (aube)</summary>

### [`v2.8.2`](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/releases/tag/v2.8.2): : Smaller lockfile diffs for yarn.lock v1 and package-lock.json, plus no more 5-minute cap on slow tarball downloads

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/v2.8.1...v2.8.2)

v2.8.2 brings aube's rewrites of Yarn Classic, npm and pnpm lockfiles closer to each tool's own output. It also stops large tarball downloads from failing after 5 minutes while data is still arriving, and fixes several install and resolution differences from pnpm.

##### Fixed

##### Lockfiles

- **Yarn Classic `yarn.lock`** ([#​1802](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1802)): re-resolving no longer rewrites every entry. aube now keeps `resolved` URLs, including the `#sha1` fragment, and quotes keys only where Yarn does. Block headers list only the ranges that consumers declare, and blocks are sorted the way Yarn sorts them. As a result, bumping one dependency changes only that package's entries:
  ```diff
  -"accepts@1.3.8", "accepts@~1.3.8":
  +accepts@~1.3.8:
     version "1.3.8"
  +  resolved "https://registry.yarnpkg.com/accepts/-/accepts-1.3.8.tgz#0bf0be125b67014adcb0b0921e62db7bffe16b2e"
  ```
- **npm `package-lock.json`** ([#​1814](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1814)): `aube add` and other rewrites leave unchanged entries byte-identical to npm's output.
  - Keys are now sorted the way npm sorts them, so `"dev": true` no longer moves.
  - `funding` values are kept exactly as written, including `type` and arrays with more than one URL.
  - New entries still record funding only as `{"url": …}`.

title: fix(task): apply extended template usage to file tasks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/995
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A file task that `extends` a task template ignored the template's `usage` spec, so `mise file_task -h` printed "This task does not accept any arguments" and the template's flags were rejected, while the same template worked for TOML tasks.

```toml
[task_templates.template]
usage = '''
flag "-t --test" help="template flag"
'''
```

```sh
#!/bin/sh
#MISE extends="template"
```

Before: `mise file_task -h` shows no flags. After: it lists `-t --test`, and `mise run file_task -t` sets `usage_test`. The template's spec comes first, followed by the script's own `#USAGE` lines, matching how TOML tasks compose them.

Adds an e2e case to `test_task_templates`.

Fixes #14882

title: feat(config): expose mise_config_dir to templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/993
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Templates can now use `{{ mise_config_dir }}`, the config directory mise itself resolves (`MISE_CONFIG_DIR`, else `xdg_config_home` + `/mise`). Before, a dotfiles variant that links into `conf.d` had to copy that rule into every `target`, and the copy renders `/conf.d/...` when `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` is set but empty, where mise falls back to the default.

```toml
[dotfiles."git-tools"]
source = "git"
mode = "symlink"
variants = [{ default = true, target = "{{ mise_config_dir }}/conf.d/git-tools" }]
```

The variable is available everywhere `xdg_config_home` is: config templates, `.miserc.toml`, and settings paths. Documented in the templates reference and the dotfiles guide.

Closes discussion #14881. Tested with a unit test that the variable renders `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`.

title: fix(uninstall): remove installs whose directories deny their owner writes
body:
`mise uninstall` failed with `Permission denied (os error 13)` when an installed tool's
directories deny their owner write access, and left the whole installation in place:

```console
$ mise uninstall http:ethos@9.9.9
mise ERROR failed to uninstall http:ethos@9.9.9
mise ERROR failed to remove: ~/data/installs/http-ethos/9.9.9
mise ERROR Permission denied (os error 13)
```

Archives can carry such directories on purpose. An `http:` tool that ships an immutable
`0555` runtime tree installs fine, because extraction applies directory modes after the
contents, but nothing can then be unlinked from those directories, so the version could not
be uninstalled or reinstalled. Go's read-only module cache has the same shape.

When removing a directory tree fails with a permission error, mise now gives the owner read,
write and search access to every directory in that tree and removes it once more. Like
`remove_all_at`, the walk opens each directory relative to its parent's descriptor with
`O_NOFOLLOW` and changes it through its own descriptor, so neither a link in the tree nor one
swapped in during the walk can redirect the change to a directory outside it. Any other error,
or a tree the owner cannot open or change, is reported as before. The change is in
`remove_all`, so uninstalling, reinstalling over an existing version and cleaning up a failed
install all benefit. Windows is unchanged.

Tests: a `mise-util` unit test removes a `0555` tree that contains a link into a sealed
directory outside it, and checks that the outside directory keeps its mode and contents;
`e2e/cli/test_uninstall_read_only` uninstalls a tool whose installation was made read-only; it
runs as a non-root user, because root would remove the tree without the fix. The
`mise-daemons` prune test that used a `0o500` directory as an entry `remove_all` cannot delete
now uses a directory its owner cannot read, which `remove_all` still cannot delete.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Uninstall now succeeds when directories within an installation have had their write permissions removed, including nested directories in read-only installation trees.
  * Removing an installation that contains a link to an external directory leaves the linked directory and its contents untouched. External directory permissions are also preserved during removal.
  * These fixes apply to non-root uninstall operations when the affected directories remain accessible enough for their permissions to be restored.

title: fix(task): accept mise tasks list as an alias for ls
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/992
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise tasks list` failed with `Task not found: list`, even though every other `ls` subcommand (`mise ls`, `config`, `settings`, `plugins`, `vars`, `secrets`, ...) also answers to `list`. Reported in discussion jdx/mise#14833.

The cause is that `mise tasks` takes an optional task name, so `list` was parsed as "show the task named `list`". Now `mise tasks list` and `mise task list` behave like `ls`, flags included:

```console
$ mise tasks list
Name   Description
hello  Say hello with optional name and greeting

$ mise tasks list --name-only
hello
```

A task named `list` still wins. If one is defined, `mise tasks list` shows that task, as it did before, so nothing that works today changes. Because this is a fallback rather than a clap alias, `list` does not appear in `--help` or the generated CLI docs.

Added `e2e/tasks/test_task_ls_list_alias` covering both cases; it passes along with the existing `tasks/` e2e tests and clippy with `-D warnings`.

title: fix(github): page when mise-versions lists no releases for a repo
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/991
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise ls-remote github:caarlos0/svu` printed "No versions found" and `mise install` of `"github:caarlos0/svu" = "3"` failed with a 404, even though the repository has 41 releases. mise-versions had baked an empty `releases.json` (`"releases":[],"truncated":false`) for it, and mise read that as "this repository has no releases" instead of paging.

mise now treats an empty whole-list answer from mise-versions as no answer and falls back to the paged endpoints, which still list every release. A repository that really has none gets the same empty result, one request later.

The empty file itself is fixed in jdx/mise-versions (stored lists are no longer replaced by an empty read). This change protects clients against any bad list that has already been baked.

title: fix(java): pick the newest build when installed versions differ only after `+`
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/990
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With two builds of the same Temurin release installed, `java = "latest"` could resolve to the older one:

```
$ mise ls java
java  temurin-25.0.4+101.0.LTS
java  temurin-25.0.4+7.0.LTS    mise.toml  latest   # older build wins
```

Installed versions are ordered with `Versioning`, which ignores everything after `+`, so `+7` and `+101` compared equal. The string tie-break then put `+101` before `+7`, and `latest` takes the last entry. Remote listings were not affected; the Java plugin already ranks build numbers numerically there.

Installed-version ordering now falls back to comparing the build metadata segment by segment, numerically where a segment is a number, before the plain-string tie-break. Versions without a `+` sort as before.

Fixes the ordering problem raised in discussion #14872. The mise-java side (Temurin is the only vendor emitting a semver-derived version) is unchanged.

## Test plan

- Added `sort_versions_orders_build_metadata_numerically` (`+7`, `+36`, `+101` sort in that order).
- `cargo test --lib install_state` passes. I did not run an end-to-end `mise ls java` against real installs.

title: perf(config): check trusted_config_paths after cheaper trust rules
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/989
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise now skips the `trusted_config_paths` lookup for configs that are already trusted by other means, which speeds up every prompt for users with entries on slow mounts.

Reported in [discussion 14864](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14864): on macOS, `trusted_config_paths = ["/home/me/proj"]` costs ~17–20ms per entry on every `hook-env`, because `/home` is an autofs mount and mise canonicalizes each entry on each check. The old order paid that for every config, even one trusted by a plain `mise trust` record or the global config, before looking at those cheaper rules.

`trusted_config_paths` can only turn "not trusted" into "trusted", so it now runs last, after the ignore list, global config, monorepo marker, trust record and worktree rules. Behavior is unchanged: a path in `trusted_config_paths` still overrides `mise trust --ignore`, and still trusts without a content hash in paranoid mode.

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings]
trusted_config_paths = ["/home/me/work"]  # no longer looked up for configs trusted by record
```

Two more changes cover configs trusted only by a `trusted_config_paths` entry (the reporter's likely case):

- The entries are compared as written first. A canonical path has no symlinks, so an entry that is a prefix of it is a real directory and matches with no filesystem call. `~/work` expands to a canonical path, so this is the common hit.
- When no entry matches as written, each entry is resolved once per process, including entries that don't exist. Before, a nonexistent `/home/me/proj` was retried (a fresh autofs lookup) for every config checked.

An entry that doesn't match as written still needs one lookup per process, and so does a config that matches none. The `trusted_config_paths` docs now say so and suggest `~/...` instead of `/home/...` on macOS.

Not measured on autofs (no autofs available here). Existing e2e tests `test_trusted_config_paths_override_ignore`, `test_local_settings_trust_controls` and `test_paranoid_env_file_trust` pass.

title: fix(prune): keep a selected Python reached through a minor-version link
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/988
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes the `mise prune` failure reported in discussion #14865.

With a tool such as `"pypi:beets" = { version = "latest", python = "3.14" }`, `mise install` records the interpreter in the environment's receipt through the `python/3.14` minor-version link, while the receipt's identity can name a different patch than the directory that link resolves to. `mise prune` then aborted the whole run:

```
mise ERROR cannot safely prune: Python receipt .../pypi-beets/2.14.1~uv~…/.mise-uv/python.json points to an unknown mise Python installation .../installs/python/3.14/bin/python
```

Now, when the receipt's recorded version doesn't match an install, prune keeps whichever mise Python installation the interpreter path actually resolves into (identity-layout or legacy `python/<version>`), so the environment stays working and prune proceeds. Receipts that point outside mise's Python installs still fail closed.

I could not reproduce the exact state from the discussion with a fresh install, so I forced it: I edited a receipt to record `core:python:3.14.7` while its path went through `python/3.14` (→ 3.14.9). `mise prune` succeeded with this change; the new unit test covers the link-resolution helper. This was checked on Linux only; the reporter is on macOS.

title: fix(gitlab): ignore expired glab OAuth2 tokens instead of sending them
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/987
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14868

`mise use -g gitlab:gitlab-org/cli@latest` failed with `401 Unauthorized` when the glab OAuth2 token in `config.yml` had expired. mise warned that the token was expired but still sent it, and gitlab.com rejects a stale token even for public release lookups, so tools like `glab` itself could not be installed.

mise now ignores an expired glab OAuth2 token and falls through to the next token source. If there is none, the request goes out unauthenticated, which works for public projects. The warning now says the token is being ignored and still suggests `glab api user` to refresh it:

```
WARN  glab OAuth2 token for gitlab.com expired at 2026-09-14T17:14:22+07:00, ignoring it. Run a glab command (e.g. `glab api user`) to refresh it.
```

Expiry dates in glab's older, non-RFC3339 format are not detected, so those tokens are still used as before.

If the same host also has a valid token in another section of glab's config (e.g. `logins`), that token is kept; only the expired one is dropped.

Validation: `gitlab` unit tests in `mise-util` pass, including a new one for the valid-token-survives case.

title: fix(dotfiles): report a saved enrollment under a symlinked parent instead of failing capture
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/986
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A single saved dotfile enrollment that sits under a symlinked parent no longer stops automatic capture for every other tracked path.

## Problem

`mise dot status` could report "Automatic capture has failed N times in a row" while all entries showed as tracked. Each capture re-read the saved enrollment manifest through `Manifest::tracking()`, which returns an error for the first entry whose path now runs through a symlink, for example `~/.claude/skills/entire-trails/SKILL.md` enrolled back when `entire-trails` was a real directory and later replaced by a link to `~/.agents/skills/entire-trails`:

```
cannot track ~/.claude/skills/entire-trails/SKILL.md through symlinked parent ~/.claude/skills/entire-trails; explicitly track the link itself and its real target instead
```

Saved enrollments are kept until untracked, so the one stale entry failed every capture, and nothing was saved.

## Fix

Live capture now reads the manifest with `Manifest::tracking_lenient()`. An entry under a symlinked parent is left out of the capture set and recorded in `invalid` with the same message, so it shows up as omitted in the checkpoint coverage and still blocks publishing until it is untracked. Replay and sync keep the strict `tracking()`.

I reproduced this from reading the code and your report rather than from a failing machine; the new assertions in `enrollment_rejects_alias_parents_but_allows_links_and_real_targets` cover the lenient read.

title: fix(http): extract zip archives that contain read-only files on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/985
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing `http:flutter` on Windows failed during extraction:

```
mise install flutter@latest
Error: Failed to install http:flutter@latest: Access is denied. (os error 5)
```

The Flutter SDK zip contains a git checkout, and its `.git/objects` files (for example `commit-graph`) are read-only. After unzipping, mise resets every extracted file's mtime to now. On Windows that needs a write handle, which a read-only file refuses. Installs of any zip with read-only entries failed the same way.

Now mise sets the times through a handle opened with only the right to write attributes, which a read-only file allows, so the file stays read-only throughout. Other platforms are unchanged.

Validated on a Windows 11 host: the new `test_reset_dir_mtime_to_now_handles_read_only_files` passes with the fix and fails at `set_file_times` without it. I did not extract the real Flutter zip.

Fixes #14867. Also reported in discussion #14767.

title: fix(unuse): prune only the named version and say why one is kept
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/984
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise unuse` (alias `rm`/`remove`) took a version argument but then pruned *every* unused version of that tool, and said nothing when the version you named was kept. With node 24.20.0, 24.22.1, 26.8.1 and 26.8.2 installed:

```
$ mise rm node@24.20.0
remove core:node@26.8.1 ? No      # not what I asked for
```

24.20.0 itself stayed because another tracked config still required it, with no hint why.

Now `mise unuse tool@version` prunes only the installed version(s) that argument stands for, and says why one stays:

```
$ mise rm node@24.20.0
node@24.20.0 is kept: required by ~/GitRepos/abcdef/mise.toml
```

- Naming a tool without a version (`mise unuse node`) still prunes all of its unused versions, as before.
- A request like `node@20` still prunes the installed version it resolves to.
- `--no-prune` and `mise uninstall` are unchanged.

The `unuse` help text now describes this. I added `e2e/cli/test_unuse_scoped_prune`; it and the existing prune/uninstall e2e tests pass. `test_unuse` itself fails in this sandbox on its first `mise ls` (a system `jq` shows up) before reaching any changed code, so I could not run it here.

Fixes #14855

title: docs(dotfiles): explain what add --no-apply, dot diff, and exclude do
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/983
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to the feedback in [discussion #14827](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14827#discussioncomment-19126585). Three behaviors there were confusing, and the docs now state each one.

- **`mise dot add --no-apply`** leaves the live file alone but still writes the source. If the source already exists with different contents, `add` overwrites it with the live file, and asks first only in a terminal. The page now says so, and notes that `--dry-run` prints a `cp` line for every existing target, so it does not show which sources would actually change.
- **`mise dot diff`** reads every entry in `[dotfiles]`, not only ones made with `mise dot add`. It reports `files: all files are applied` (or `edits: all edits are applied` for edit entries) when nothing would change, and skips `track` entries (use `mise dot history diff` for those).
- **`exclude`** is a per-entry field set in the config. `mise dot exclude` is a separate global rule for tracked paths.

Docs only: `docs/dotfiles/managed.md`. I reproduced the `--no-apply` source overwrite with a debug build in a scratch `$HOME` (copy and symlink modes, existing source, non-interactive). I did not run `docs:build`, since the docs dependencies are not installed here; the focused `hk` check (Prettier, markdownlint, oxfmt) passes.

title: fix(lock): keep a .config root's monorepo lockfile next to its config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/981
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `monorepo_root = true` and `[monorepo] lockfile = true`, a root config in `.config/mise.toml` sent the shared lockfile to `<root>/mise.lock`. That left the existing `.config/mise.lock` behind, unread, and moved the lockfile out of `.config/`.

The shared monorepo lockfile now lives in the lockfile directory of the config that declares `monorepo_root = true`, so it is where that config's lockfile lives without monorepo mode:

```
.config/mise.toml          # monorepo_root = true, lockfile = true
.config/mise.lock          # now written here (was ./mise.lock)
apps/foo/mise.toml         # its tools are locked in .config/mise.lock
```

Roots using `mise.toml`, `mise/config.toml` or `.mise/config.toml` are unchanged. The migration of subproject lockfiles targets the same directory.

Added `e2e/lockfile/test_lock_monorepo_dot_config_root`; it and `test_lock_sidecars_monorepo` pass, and clippy is clean. Not covered: merging a stale root `.config/mise.lock` into a different location, which is no longer needed for this layout.

Fixes #14844

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes monorepo lockfile placement and migration/stub path logic; wrong paths could break installs or lock merges, but behavior is scoped to monorepo + lockfile mode with tests added.
> 
> **Overview**
> When the monorepo root config lives under **`.config/`** (e.g. `.config/mise.toml`), the shared lockfile is now written **next to that config** (`.config/mise.lock`) instead of at the repository root. Descendant app configs still contribute to that single lockfile.
> 
> Implementation tracks each monorepo root’s lockfile directory via `monorepo_lockfile_dir()` (populated when resolving the monorepo lockfile root), and lockfile path resolution, migration targets, and legacy discovery use that directory rather than the monorepo filesystem root.
> 
> **Stub paths** are rebased when merging subproject lockfiles, and `tool_stub_reference` builds relative paths with `..` so stubs under sibling projects still resolve when the lockfile sits in `.config/`.
> 
> Adds an e2e scenario for `.config` monorepo roots (including migrating an existing root `mise.lock`) and a unit test for cross-directory stub references.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+export MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1
+export MISE_LOCKFILE=1
+
+# A root config in .config/ keeps its lockfile there in monorepo mode, and
+# descendant configs share it instead of writing <root>/mise.lock.
+mkdir -p monorepo/.config monorepo/apps/foo
+cat >monorepo/.config/mise.toml <<'EOT2'
+monorepo_root = true
+
+[monorepo]
+lockfile = true
+config_roots = ["apps/*"]
+
+[tools]
+"npm:cowsay" = "1.6.0"
+EOT2
+cat >monorepo/apps/foo/mise.toml <<'EOT2'
+[tools]
+"npm:is-odd" = "3.0.1"
+EOT2
+
+mise -C monorepo lock
+assert_succeed "test -f monorepo/.config/mise.lock"
+assert_fail "test -e monorepo/mise.lock"
+assert_contains "cat monorepo/.config/mise.lock" "npm:is-odd"
+

title: fix(task): let an empty run_windows skip the task on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/980
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`run_windows = []` now skips a task's `run` on Windows. Before, an empty list was treated like a missing key, so the task ran its `run` command on Windows anyway.

```toml
[tasks.enable-linger]
run = "loginctl enable-linger"
run_windows = []   # nothing runs on Windows
```

Previously the only workaround was `run_windows = ""`, which shows up as running an empty command.

An explicit `run_windows` (even empty) is now tracked separately from an absent one, and a task template's `run_windows` no longer overrides a local empty list.

Fixes #14840

Config parsing uses `deserialize_opt_arr` and `Option<Vec<RunEntry>>` so an omitted `run_windows` stays distinct from an explicit empty list; runtime tasks carry `run_windows_declared` and `Task::run()` selects the Windows list when that flag is set or the list is non-empty.
> 
> Template merge, TOML overlays, and `mise tasks validate` were updated so a local empty `run_windows` is not overwritten by a template, overlays preserve the declaration, and tasks with `run` plus declared empty `run_windows` are not flagged as having no executable content. title: fix(bootstrap): match only an exact bootstrap task
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/979
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap` no longer fails when the config has a namespaced task such as `system:bootstrap` but no task named `bootstrap`.

Before, with this config:

```toml
[tasks."system:bootstrap"]
run = "echo hi"
```

`mise bootstrap` logged ``running `bootstrap` task`` and then failed with `no task bootstrap found`. The check used a fuzzy task match that also matches namespaced tasks ending in `:bootstrap`, while the run step requests the exact name. Now the phase runs only for a task named exactly `bootstrap` (or aliased to it); otherwise it is skipped and bootstrap continues to the final hook.

Fixes #14836

I did not change the special task's name or add namespaced lifecycle tasks, which the issue also suggests.

title: fix(prune): resolve symlinked Python path in pypi receipts
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/978
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise prune` no longer aborts with `cannot safely prune: Python receipt … points to an unknown mise Python installation` when a pypi tool's receipt reaches mise's own Python through a minor-version symlink.

```sh
mise install python@3.14
mise use -g "pypi:cowsay[python=3.14]"
mise prune --dry-run   # before: aborts; after: runs
```

The receipt can record the interpreter as `installs/python/3.14/bin/python` (`3.14 -> ./3.14.9`), while the identity names `3.14.9`. `prune` compared the two with `Path::starts_with`, which does not follow symlinks, so the match failed and the whole prune bailed. `prune` now also resolves the receipt path's directory and accepts a match on either the recorded or the resolved path, so existing receipts keep working.

I did not change where the symlinked path gets written into the receipt; existing receipts like this are handled at prune time.

Validation: new unit test `resolve_receipt_python_follows_the_minor_version_symlink`. I did not run the reproducer above end to end.

Discussion: jdx/mise#14841

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes prune’s safety logic for retaining interpreters referenced by uv receipts; incorrect matching could prune needed Python or retain too much, though behavior is narrowed with explicit fail-closed rules and tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`mise prune`** aborting when a **pypi/pipx** `.mise-uv/python.json` receipt points at mise Python via a **minor-version symlink** (e.g. `python/3.14/bin/python` while the runtime identity is `3.14.9`). Matching no longer relies only on `Path::starts_with`, which ignores symlinks.
> 
> Prune now **resolves the receipt interpreter path** (`resolve_receipt_python`) and uses **`receipt_python_in_dir`** to treat a match on either the recorded or resolved path, including when the install tree is reached through symlinked directories. Identity-layout installs can also match when the install name equals the receipt version and the resolved path lives under that dir; legacy `installs/python/<version>` checks use the same helper.
> 
> The matcher is **conservative** when the `python/3.14` link has moved to a newer patch: a receipt tied to an older patch through that link must not count as living in the old install dir. Missing paths are left unchanged instead of failing resolution.
> 
> Adds a **Unix unit test** for symlinked minor-version paths and the “link moved on” case.

title: feat(dotfiles): render templates in a variant's target
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/977
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A dotfiles variant's `target` can now be a template, so a shared config can link into a location that differs between machines, such as a custom `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` or `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`. Previously the entry was ignored with `variant target must be absolute or start with ~/`, because the check ran on the unrendered string.

```toml
[dotfiles.examplectl]
source = "dotfiles/examplectl"
mode = "symlink"
variants = [{ default = true, target = "{{ xdg_config_home }}/examplectl" }]
```

With `XDG_CONFIG_HOME=~/custom-config`, this links `~/custom-config/examplectl` to the source. Only the variant `target` is rendered; the table key stays a stable logical name for overrides between config files.

- The template has the context every config file gets (`env`, `xdg_config_home`, `config_root`, ...). `exec()` is not available, and neither is `vars`, because the file resolution path has no `Config` to take a per-file context from.
- The absolute-or-`~/` check now runs on the rendered path when a variant is selected; a template that fails to render, or renders to a relative path, ignores the entry with that reason.
- Targets without template syntax behave as before.

Closes the idea in discussion #14843.

## Validation

- New e2e `test_dotfiles_variant_target_template` (custom `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` link, relative render rejected); existing `test_dotfiles_destination_variants` still passes.
- Clippy was not run locally (`mlua-sys` build script fails in this sandbox); CI covers it.

title: fix(oci): package the rust toolchain in mise oci build
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/976
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise oci build` images that include `rust` had no `cargo` or `rustc`, and the first `mise run` inside the container downloaded rustup-init and the whole toolchain again ([discussion #14848](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14848)).

rustup installs into `~/.cargo` and `~/.rustup`, not mise's install directory. The rust tool layer held only a symlink to the build host's `~/.cargo/bin`, which dangled in the image.

## What changes

```toml
[tools]
rust = { version = "stable", profile = "default", components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"] }

[oci]
mount_point = "/home/ubuntu/.mise"
```

With this config the image now has:

- `/home/ubuntu/.mise/rust/cargo/bin`: the `rustup` binary, with `cargo`, `rustc`, `rustfmt` and the other proxies as symlinks to it.
- `/home/ubuntu/.mise/rust/rustup`: rustup's `settings.toml` and the directory of each toolchain the toolset uses (including a `nightly` alias for a dated nightly).
- `CARGO_HOME` and `RUSTUP_HOME` set to those two directories, and `PATH` entries for the proxies.
- The install symlink `installs/rust/<version>` pointing at the in-image `cargo/bin`, so mise in the container sees rust as installed and does not run rustup-init.

The build host's registry caches, other toolchains and `cargo install` binaries are not copied. These homes go into one extra layer after the tool layers; the rust tool layer is now only the symlink and uses a new relocation key, so layers pushed by older versions are never reused.

## Limits

- If rust comes from a rustup mise does not manage (for example a system package's rustup on `PATH`), the build now fails with a message to install rust through mise or set `CARGO_HOME` and `RUSTUP_HOME`. Previously it produced a broken image.
- All rust versions in the toolset must share the same cargo and rustup homes.
- The homes layer is rebuilt on every build and is not reused from a registry or the local layer cache.

## Validation

- Built an image with `rust = { version = "1.90.0", profile = "minimal" }` and `mount_point = "/home/ubuntu/.mise"`, then extracted its layers at the same paths. With the image's env, `cargo -V` printed `cargo 1.90.0`. With the image's data and cargo/rustup dirs, `mise ls` showed rust as installed and `mise x -- cargo -V` ran without any download. The minimal toolchain layer is about 210 MB compressed.
- Added unit tests for the new layer builder. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Not tested: running the image in a container runtime, a non-root `USER`, or a slow e2e test.

title: fix(install): run [hooks].postinstall against the just-installed version
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/975
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

During `mise upgrade`, a project-level `[hooks].postinstall` hook ran against the version being replaced when a tool used a fuzzy request such as `latest` or `1`. The runtime symlink (`installs/<tool>/latest`) is only re-pointed after the hooks run, so the hook's `PATH` resolved to the old install. Tool-level `postinstall` already avoided this (#10415).

The hook now runs against a copy of the toolset in which the just-installed versions are locked, so `PATH` points at the exact install listed in `MISE_INSTALLED_TOOLS`.

```toml
[tools]
"aqua:jqlang/jq" = "latest"

[hooks]
postinstall = 'jq --version'  # now prints the upgraded version
```

Adds `e2e/config/test_hooks_postinstall_upgrade_path`, which fails without the change (hook PATH contains `installs/dummy/1/bin`) and passes with it. `test_hooks_installed_tools` still passes.

Fixes #14842

title: fix(lock): accept PEP 691 +html content types from PyPI simple indexes
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/974
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` for a `pipx:`/`pypi:` tool no longer fails on PyPI simple indexes that answer with the PEP 691 HTML media type, such as Azure Artifacts.

Before, the request succeeded (`200 OK`, valid PEP 503 HTML) but `mise lock` then bailed:

```text
$ mise lock pipx:my-package
Error:
   0: failed to lock pipx:my-package
   1: Got non-HTML text from https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/<org>/<project>/_packaging/<feed>/pypi/simple/my-package/
```

The feed returns `content-type: application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+html; api-version=7.2-preview.1`, and the lock path only accepted an exact `text/html`. Version listing already accepted any `+html` type, so `mise install` and `mise ls-remote` worked. `get_html_with_headers` now accepts `text/html` or a media type ending in `+html`, matching version listing. `text/plain` and other types are still rejected. The same helper fetches the JRuby listing, which is plain HTML and unaffected.

Added a test that serves `application/vnd.pypi.simple.v1+html; api-version=7.2-preview.1`; the existing rejection test still passes (`cargo test -p mise-util get_html`). I have not run this against a real Azure Artifacts feed.

title: fix(remote-source): validate git ref in remote git sources
body:
### Problem
`RemoteSource::parse_git_repo` validates that an explicit `?ref=` query parameter is not empty, does not start with `-`, and is not `"HEAD"`.

However, `parse_git_with` (which handles `RemoteSource::parse_git_ssh` and `parse_git_https` for remote git sources with inner paths) captured the `ref` query parameter with `(?P<ref>[^?&]+)` and accepted any string without validation. If an untrusted source or config specifies a ref beginning with `-` (such as `--upload-pack=...`), the flag can be passed downstream to git operations, leading to CLI option injection.

### Fix
- Validate that `git_ref` does not start with `-`, is not empty, and is not `"HEAD"` in `parse_git_with`, matching `parse_git_repo`.
- Add regression test `rejects_git_sources_with_unsafe_refs` in `crates/mise-util/src/remote_source.rs`.
