title: feat(dotfiles): erase a tracked path from history with `mise dot history purge`
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/969
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What

`mise dot track` saves a file immediately, and `untrack`, `rollback` and `undo` only append checkpoints, so a secret tracked by mistake stays readable in history ([discussion jdx/mise#14827](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14827)). The only fix was a manual `git update-ref` recipe that also dropped later checkpoints of other files.

`mise dot history purge <path>` rewrites the history without the path:

```console
$ mise dot untrack ~/.aws/credentials
$ mise dot history purge ~/.aws/credentials
2 of 9 checkpoints hold this path:
  remove  4  secret changed
  rewrite 2  tracked ~/.aws/credentials
Erase these versions from history? This cannot be undone [y/N]
```

- A checkpoint that changed only the path is removed. Every other checkpoint keeps its message, date, label and **numeric ID** (only commit hashes change), and checkpoint references in operation records and annotations are remapped, so `history`, `rollback` and `undo` keep working.
- `--dry-run` lists what would change; `--yes` skips the prompt (non-interactive use without it fails). Replaced objects are pruned afterwards; `--keep-objects` leaves them and `--backup` keeps the old history under `refs/mise/purge-backup/` (which still holds the secret).
- **Local-only:** mise never force-pushes, so the command refuses if any saved version of the path is reachable from the origin, pointing at the manual recipe (docs updated to link both ways). Published commits are never rewritten.
- It takes the operation and store locks, and refuses with unfinished operations. Stop the watcher first; if the file is still tracked the next save records it again.

## Notes for review

- Rewrite is in `crates/mise-system/src/history/purge.rs`: tree filtering (including `home@variant` roots and the manifest's permission entries), original author/committer dates preserved, drop of annotations on dropped checkpoints, and a rebuilt index keyed by the new hashes.
- Local-only (`track-local`) histories are handled through the existing `route_local`.
- Not covered: path names may remain in operation records of other checkpoints; local recovery journals of rewritten checkpoints are rebuilt from commits (same as any index rebuild).
- Backup defaults to off because the point is erasure; flag if you'd rather default it on.

## Validation

New e2e `test_dotfiles_history_purge` (preview changes nothing, secret absent from all objects, IDs/descriptions survive, `undo` works afterwards, origin refusal, local-only path still purgeable) and unit tests pass; `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint-fix` are clean. Not run on Windows. Docs overlap with the open docs PR jdx/mise#14829; the sections should merge cleanly but may need a rebase.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/968
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes the \`curl https://mise.run | sh\` failure for users whose \`~/.config/curlrc\` sets \`write-out\` (e.g. \`write-out = "\n"\`).

`download_file` returns the cache path on stdout, and the caller captures it with `cache_file=$(download_file ...)`. curl's `write-out` output went to the same stdout, so the path gained a leading newline and the later `cd "$(dirname "$cache_file")"` failed with a confusing "no such directory" error even though the directory existed.

The curl download now redirects its stdout to stderr (`curl -#fLo "$file" "$url" >&2`). With `-o` curl writes nothing useful to stdout, and the progress bar already goes to stderr, so behavior is otherwise unchanged. Other curlrc settings (proxy, CA) are still honored, which `curl -q` would not do.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14826

title: fix(pipx): find uv's Windows launcher for console scripts ending in .py
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/965
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14823.

On Windows, installing a uv-locked `pipx:` tool whose console script name ends in `.py` failed after the package installed. For example, `pipx:clang-format@23.1.3` declares `clang-format-diff.py`, and mise tried to copy `Scripts\clang-format-diff.py.exe`, which doesn't exist:

```
failed copy: ...\.venv\Scripts\clang-format-diff.py.exe -> ...\bin\clang-format-diff.py.exe: The system cannot find the file specified.
```

uv drops a trailing `.py` from the entry point name before adding `.exe`, so the launcher is `clang-format-diff.exe`. mise now checks the venv's `Scripts` directory for both `name.py.exe` (pip's naming) and `name.exe` (uv's naming) and exposes whichever exists. Behavior on other platforms and for names without `.py` is unchanged.

Validation: `cargo check` passes. Not tested on Windows and no new test added.

> **Low Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Windows **pipx/uv-lock** installs that fail when copying console scripts whose entry point names end in `.py` (e.g. `clang-format-diff.py`).
> 
> **`DISCOVER_SCRIPTS`** no longer assumes every Windows launcher is `{entry.name}.exe`. For console/GUI entry points on Windows it probes the venv `Scripts` folder for **`name.exe`** (uv, which strips a trailing `.py`) and **`name.py.exe`** (pip) and records whichever file exists, defaulting to the first candidate if neither is present. title: fix(e2e): reap background watch process and retry isolated dir cleanup
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/964
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

`cli/test_watch_ignore` could fail a CI run even though every assertion passed. The harness's cleanup then died with:

```
rm: cannot remove '.../home/.local/share/mise/.fake-asdf': Directory not empty
```

The test backgrounds `mise watch` and sends SIGINT without waiting for it, so mise (or the watchexec it spawned) could still be writing under the isolated data dir while `remove_isolated_env` ran `rm -rf`. This is how #14822 (an unrelated registry PR) got a red `e2e` job.

## Fix

- `e2e/cli/test_watch_ignore`: use a stub `watchexec` that exits immediately, so `mise watch` runs in the foreground and nothing is left running (killing only `mise watch` would orphan the real watchexec and its nested `mise run`).
- `e2e/run_test`: `remove_isolated_env` retries `rm -rf` a few times so any other test with a straggling process doesn't flake on teardown.

No user-facing change; test-harness only. Not run locally (no built binary in this worktree); lint (shfmt/shellcheck) passes.

It prepends a **`$HOME/bin/watchexec` stub** that exits immediately so `mise watch` runs in the foreground, then asserts the debug `$ watchexec ...` line and forwarded flags via `assert_contains`.

diff:
--- e2e/cli/test_watch_ignore (+15/-16)
@@ -4,29 +4,28 @@
 # parsed by `mise watch` but must be forwarded onto the watchexec command line
 # it builds. We assert on the `$ watchexec ...` line that mise logs (with
 # MISE_DEBUG=1) right before spawning watchexec.
+#
+# watchexec is a stub that exits immediately, so `mise watch` runs to completion
+# in the foreground. A real watchexec never exits on its own, and killing
+# `mise watch` would orphan it (and its nested `mise run`) to write into the
+# isolated dir during teardown.
+
+mkdir -p "$HOME/bin"
+cat >"$HOME/bin/watchexec" <<'STUB'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+exit 0
+STUB
+chmod +x "$HOME/bin/watchexec"
+export PATH="$HOME/bin:$PATH"
 
-mise use -g watchexec@latest
 mise tasks add example -- echo 'running example'
 
 echo 'spec/**/*.rb' >.mise-watch-ignore
 
 output_file=.watch_ignore_output
-rm -f "${output_file}"
-
-MISE_DEBUG=1 mise watch --ignore 'spec/**/*.rb' --ignore-file .mise-watch-ignore --print-events example >"${output_file}" 2>&1 &
-PID_TO_KILL=$!
-
-# Wait for the constructed watchexec command line to be logged. Anchor on the
-# exact `$ watchexec ` debug prefix (debug!("$ watchexec {}", ...)) so unrelated
-# output mentioning "watchexec" (e.g. tool-resolution logs) can't satisfy the
-# loop early and kill the process before the command line is flushed.
-for _ in $(seq 1 40); do
-  grep -Fq '$ watchexec ' "${output_file}" && break
-  sleep 0.5
-done
-
-kill -SIGINT "$PID_TO_KILL" 2>/dev/null || true
+MISE_DEBUG=1 mise watch --ignore 'spec/**/*.rb' --ignore-file .mise-watch-ignore --print-events example >"${output_file}" 2>&1
 
+assert_contains "cat ${output_file}" '$ watchexec '
 assert_contains "cat ${output_file}" "--ignore spec/**/*.rb"
 assert_contains "cat ${output_file}" "--ignore-file .mise-watch-ignore"
 assert_contains "cat ${output_file}" "--print-events"
--- e2e/run_test (+12/-2)
@@ -69,12 +69,22 @@ create_isolated_env() {
 
 remove_isolated_env() {
   if [[ ${MISE_E2E_INSIDE_DOCKER:-0} == 1 ]]; then
-    rm -rf "$TEST_ISOLATED_DIR"
+    rm_rf_retry "$TEST_ISOLATED_DIR"
   else
-    rm -rf "$TEST_ISOLATED_DIR" &
+    rm_rf_retry "$TEST_ISOLATED_DIR" &
   fi
 }
 
+# A straggling process from the test can still be writing into the tree while it
+# is removed, making rm fail with "Directory not empty". Retry a few times.
+rm_rf_retry() {
+  for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
+    rm -rf "$1" 2>/dev/null && return 0
+    sleep 1
+  done
+  rm -rf "$1"
+}

title: ci: retry windows-lint once and print diagnostics when it fails
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/962
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `windows-lint` job now retries its Clippy step once, and if the job still fails it prints runner diagnostics, so a rare transient failure on the self-hosted Windows runner no longer needs a manual re-run and, if it recurs, leaves evidence of the cause.

## Why

On 2026-10-21, `trusted / windows-lint` failed once on the self-hosted runner `jdx-win-ci-3`:

```
could not execute process ...mbx-rustc.exe ... --crate-name regex_lite ...: The directory name is invalid. (os error 267)
```

`aws-lc-sys` MSVC probe errors followed. Across the last 250 runs of `test.yml` this job failed once in about 120 completed self-hosted runs. Read-only checks on the runner ruled out two causes: the `regex-lite-0.1.9` registry source directory (created 2026-10-01, never recreated) and the shared `mbx` shim directory in the error path (created 2026-10-17) were both stable. All three runner instances were busy at the time (two `windows-unit`, one `windows-lint`) and share `W:\cargo` and `W:\mbx-cache`. Which directory was invalid is still unknown.

## What changes

Only `.github/workflows/test-impl.yml`, only the `windows-lint` job:

- **Retry:** "Run Clippy on Windows" is wrapped in `nick-fields/retry` exactly like `windows-unit`'s `cargo test` (same pinned SHA, `max_attempts: 2`, `retry_wait_seconds: 30`, same `mbx`/`cargo` selection). `timeout_minutes: 17` per attempt keeps two attempts plus the wait inside the job's 40-minute limit. The Clippy flags are unchanged.
- **Diagnostics:** a new `if: failure()` step (PowerShell, `continue-on-error: true`, read-only) prints the runner name, current directory, whether `$env:GITHUB_WORKSPACE` exists, a listing of the workspace root, `cargo`/`rustc`/`mbx*`/`cl`/`link` processes, and free disk space on the workspace drive. It works on the self-hosted runner and `windows-latest`.

## Validation

`mise run lint-fix` passes, including `jactionlint` and `oxfmt` on the workflow. The retry wrapper and the diagnostics step can only be exercised by CI itself, on a real Windows runner and only when Clippy actually fails; the diagnostics output has not been seen yet.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.304.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> 
> **Overview**
> The **`windows-lint`** job now runs **Clippy** through **`nick-fields/retry`** (two attempts, 30s between, 17-minute timeout per attempt), matching the existing **`windows-unit`** pattern, so rare transient self-hosted failures (e.g. Windows os error 267) can recover without a manual re-run. title: fix(generate): end install-script and task-stubs files with a newline
body:
`mise generate install-script --write` and `mise generate task-stubs` write files without a trailing newline. Because these files are meant to be committed, end-of-file checks in formatters and linters (hk, pre-commit's `end-of-file-fixer`, editorconfig) flag them. If such a tool adds the newline, the next regeneration removes it again.

Before:

```console
$ mise generate install-script --write bin/mise
$ tail -c 12 bin/mise | od -c
0000000    L   _   P   A   T   H   "       "   $   @   "
```

After:

```console
$ mise generate install-script --write bin/mise
$ tail -c 12 bin/mise | od -c
0000000    _   P   A   T   H   "       "   $   @   "  \n
```

Task stubs now end with a newline as well. `mise generate install-script` without `--write` prints the same output as before, with no extra blank line at the end.

Existing task stubs keep working. Before overwriting a stub, `mise generate task-stubs` checks that the file is one it generated, and that check now ignores the trailing newline. Stubs written by earlier versions (no trailing newline) and stubs that a formatter has since given a trailing newline both regenerate instead of being refused as "not a generated task stub".

The `.cmd` launcher written by `--windows` already ended with a newline and is unchanged.

Tested with new e2e assertions on the last byte of `bin/mise`, of a task stub, and of the stdout output, plus a unit test for the stub comparison. The existing e2e case that regenerates a stub without a trailing newline still passes.

title: fix(lock): prefer the nearest lockfile when an unowned request is ambiguous
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/961
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise install aube@latest`, or any install dependency that resolves `aube@latest` (such as `npm:ajv-cli`), failed when nested mise configs pinned the tool to different versions:

```
mise ERROR Failed to install aube@latest: lockfile contains multiple resolutions for aube@latest with the same options
```

This hit checkouts nested under another mise checkout (a parent `mise.lock` pinning aube 2.7.0, a child pinning 2.8.1). A request with no owning config reads every lockfile merged together, and both pins matched.

Now, when the merged read is ambiguous, mise falls back to the lockfiles in precedence order and the nearest one that decides the request wins. The ambiguity error remains only if no single lockfile decides it. Requests owned by a config still read only that config's lockfile, as before.

## Validation

- Unit test for the nearest-lockfile selection.
- New e2e `lockfile/test_lockfile_nested_ambiguous_latest`: parent pins `tiny` 1.0.0, child pins 1.0.1, and `mise install tiny@latest` from the child now picks 1.0.1. The same setup fails with the error above on 2026.10.11.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint-fix` pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-304_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core lockfile resolution for unowned `latest` installs in nested configs; wrong precedence could pick the wrong version, though behavior for single-config and owned requests is unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes nested lockfile ambiguity** for installs like `mise install tiny@latest` when parent and child `mise.lock` pin the same tool to different versions. Those requests have no owning config, so mise merges every lockfile and used to fail with “multiple resolutions.”
> 
> **`get_locked_version`** now tracks when resolution uses the merged lockfile view. If that lookup returns `AmbiguousRequestBinding`, it **retries** by walking lockfiles in **nearest-config-first** order via new **`nearest_lockfile_decision`**, using the first lockfile that yields a single clear pin (ambiguous lockfiles are skipped). Config-owned requests still use only that config’s lockfile.
> 
> Adds a **unit test** for precedence/fallback behavior and an **e2e** case: child directory installs `tiny@latest` and gets **1.0.1** from the child lock, not the parent’s 1.0.0.
>

title: fix(http): fall back to bundled root certificates when the system store is empty
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.com/gh/jdx/mise/trails/960
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With the official release binaries (rustls), mise refused to start its HTTP client when the system certificate store had no roots, so every download failed with `No CA certificates were loaded from the system`. That happens in minimal or distroless containers without `ca-certificates`, and when `SSL_CERT_FILE` names a missing file. mise now warns once and retries with Mozilla's bundled root certificates, the same roots the npm backend already trusts:

```text
mise WARN  no CA certificates could be loaded from the system, so mise is trusting its bundled Mozilla roots. Install ca-certificates, or check SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR
```

The fallback only applies when nothing loads. Roots that do load are never supplemented, so `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` keep replacing the system store, for example to pin mise to a private CA. It covers the shared HTTP client (downloads, version lookups) and `mise self-update`, on Linux and other Unix targets except macOS, in rustls builds. The default `native-tls` build and macOS/Windows are unchanged, because their verifiers have no empty-store failure to recover from.

This PR also adds an FAQ entry, "How does mise handle TLS certificates?", and a note in the packaging docs. They cover which trust store each build uses, that `SSL_CERT_FILE` replaces the system store on Linux, and the new fallback.

Not covered by the fallback: the vfox, cache, sigstore, gix and rattler clients build their own reqwest clients, so they still fail on an empty store.

## Validation

Release feature set (`--no-default-features --features rustls-native-roots,self_update,vfox/vendored-lua`) on Linux, running `mise install` against a public site and a local HTTPS server signed by a throwaway CA:

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| public site, `SSL_CERT_DIR=<empty dir>` | warns, TLS succeeds with the bundled roots |
| public site, `SSL_CERT_FILE=<missing file>` | warns, TLS succeeds with the bundled roots |
| private CA server, `SSL_CERT_FILE=<private CA>` | TLS succeeds, no warning |
| public site, `SSL_CERT_FILE=<private CA only>` | `UnknownIssuer`, so the replace behavior is unchanged |
| public site, default store | TLS succeeds, no warning |

Before the change, the first two cases failed with `No CA certificates were loaded from the system`. I ran clippy with `-D warnings` on `mise-util` (rustls and default features) and on the release feature set, plus the focused hk checks. There is no automated test for the empty-store case, because the e2e harness builds with default `native-tls`, where the fallback isn't compiled in. macOS, Windows and the `native-tls` build were not tested.

+//! Trust roots for HTTPS clients.
+//!
+//! With rustls, reqwest verifies certificates against the operating system's
+//! trust store and refuses to build a client when that store has no roots, for
+//! example in a minimal container without `ca-certificates`, or when
+//! `SSL_CERT_FILE` points at a missing file. [`build_client`] retries such a
+//! build with Mozilla's root certificates. Roots that load from the system are
+//! never supplemented, so `SSL_CERT_FILE` and `SSL_CERT_DIR` keep replacing the
+//! system store.
+
+use reqwest::{Client, ClientBuilder};
+
+/// Builds the client `make` describes. If that fails, builds it again with
+/// Mozilla's root certificates added and returns the original error when the
+/// second build fails too.
+///
+/// `make` runs once per attempt because [`ClientBuilder`] cannot be cloned.
+pub fn build_client(make: impl Fn() -> ClientBuilder) -> reqwest::Result<Client> {
+    match make().build() {
+        Ok(client) => Ok(client),
+        Err(err) => with_bundled_roots(make, err),
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(all(
+    any(feature = "rustls", feature = "rustls-native-roots"),
+    unix,
+    not(target_os = "android"),
+    not(target_vendor = "apple")
+))]
+fn with_bundled_roots(
+    make: impl Fn() -> ClientBuilder,
+    err: reqwest::Error,
+) -> reqwest::Result<Client> {
+    static WARN: std::sync::Once = std::sync::Once::new();
+    let roots = webpki_root_certs::TLS_SERVER_ROOT_CERTS
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|cert| reqwest::Certificate::from_der(cert.as_ref()).ok());
+    match make().tls_certs_merge(roots).build() {
+        Ok(client) => {
+            WARN.call_once(|| {
+                log::warn!(
+                    "no CA certificates could be loaded from the system, so mise is trusting its bundled Mozilla roots. Install ca-certificates, or check SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR"
+                );
+            });
+            Ok(client)
+        }
+        Err(_) => Err(err),
+    }
+}

+/// from, or this build does not use rustls.

+    unix,
+    not(target_os = "android"),
+    not(target_vendor = "apple")
+)))]
+fn with_bundled_roots(
+    _make: impl Fn() -> ClientBuilder,
+    err: reqwest::Error,
+) -> reqwest::Result<Client> {
+    Err(err)
+}

title: fix(dotfiles): keep entries declared in an unselected env config tracked
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/959
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Moving a \`mode = \"track\"\` entry into \`config.<env>.toml\` made every machine that does not select that env publish a removal of it from the shared history. A machine that does select the env then re-added it, so the entry flapped in history and \`mise dot status\` on that machine could list it as tracked while it was not captured (#14814).

```toml
# config.desktop.toml, selected only on machine A
[dotfiles]
"~/.yabairc" = { mode = "track" }
```

**Before:** machine B (no \`desktop\` env) saw the entry vanish from its declarations and treated that as an explicit untrack, publishing the removal.

**After:** when a previously declared entry disappears, mise checks the global config directory's \`config.<env>.toml\` / \`mise.<env>.toml\` files for environments not selected here. If one still declares the path as \`track\`, the entry stays enrolled. Deleting the declaration everywhere still untracks it.

Not addressed: \`mise dot status\` does not yet report an entry that is declared but not captured (the second ask in #14814). Only \`[dotfiles]\` in the global config directory is scanned, not \`[dotfile_groups]\`.

Verified with a unit test on the reconcile step and clippy. No e2e test added for the two-machine flow.

Fixes #14814

title: feat(lsp): complete and describe tools
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/958
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lsp` now completes tool names under `[tools]` from mise's registry and shows a tool's description and backends on hover.

**Stacked on #14811** (`feat(lsp): flag unknown task references and rewrite deprecated keys`, branch `claude/lsp-task-diagnostics`, itself stacked on #14808). Retarget this PR's base to `main` once #14811 merges. This is the last of the three.

## Before / after

```toml
[tools]
no
```

Before: nothing completed under `[tools]`, and hovering `node` showed only the generic schema text.

After: `no|` offers `node`, `nomad`, `notation`, ... each with its registry description. Hovering `nodejs` (an alias works too) shows:

> **node** _tool_
>
> Node.js runtime
>
> Backends: `core:node`

The same applies to `[tasks.<name>.tools]`, inline `tools = { ... }` and `[tools.no|` headers.

## How it works

`mise_lsp::Options` gets a `registry: Vec<RegistryEntry>` (short name, description, aliases, backends, deprecation message). `mise lsp` fills it from the registry `mise registry` reads (`src/registry.rs`): the baked-in one, or the cached floating one when `registry_floating` is on. Tools that `enable_tools`/`disable_tools` filter out and tools without a backend are left out, as in `mise registry`; deprecated tools are not offered. An empty list switches the feature off. The `mise-lsp` crate still has no workspace dependencies.

The server stays offline: no version resolution, no network, no templates rendered. Resolved and latest versions and inlay hints are not part of this PR. Tool completion and hover follow the existing `completion` and `hover` switches.

Docs: `docs/ide-integration.md` and the `mise lsp` help (rendered).

## Testing

Unit tests for the registry lookup, completion in every tool table shape, and hover; a session test for completion and hover; and a smoke test of `target/debug/mise lsp` against the real registry (`no` completes to `node`, `nomad`, ...).

## Remaining ideas (not built in this stack)

From the follow-up wish list on #14744, left for later: Tera completion and hover, `usage` and `#MISE` header support, `.tool-versions` files, inlay hints with resolved versions, document links, monorepo `//path:task` references, and cross-file rename.

title: feat(lsp): flag unknown task references and rewrite deprecated keys
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/957
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lsp` now flags task references that point at nothing, flags dependency cycles, and offers a one-click rewrite of a deprecated key to its replacement when the schema names it.

**Stacked on #14808** (`feat(lsp): complete, define, and rename tasks`, branch `claude/lsp-tasks`). Retarget this PR's base to `main` once #14808 merges. PR 3 is stacked on this one.

## Before / after

```toml
[tasks.build]
run = "cargo build"

[tasks.test]
depends = ["bild"]      # after: warning `unknown task `bild`; did you mean `build`?` + quick fix

[tasks.a]
depends = ["b"]         # after: error `dependency cycle: a -> b -> a`
[tasks.b]
depends = ["a"]

env_path = ["bin"]      # after: quick fix "Replace with `env._.path`"
```

Before, none of these were reported, and the deprecated key only got a warning with no fix.

## What it does

- `unknown-task` (warning): a name in `depends`, `depends_post`, `wait_for` or `run = [{ task = "..." }]` that no task defines, and an `extends` template that no `[task_templates]` entry defines. The "did you mean" suggestion is a quick fix that replaces just the name.
- `task-cycle` (error): each `depends` that is part of a cycle among the tasks the file defines, with the cycle in the message.
- A quick fix for a `deprecated-key` when its schema description names the replacement (`Deprecated alias for \`task.output\``, `use env._.path instead`, ...).

## Staying quiet when it cannot know

`unknown-task` follows what `mise tasks validate` checks, and skips what only mise can resolve: patterns (`lint:*`), monorepo references (`//app:build`, `:build`) and `optional = true` dependencies. Aliases count as names. File tasks (scripts in `mise-tasks/` and the other task directories, and in directories `includes` names) and the user's and system's configs count as defined. When tasks can come from somewhere the server does not read (a glob or `git::`/`oci::` entry in `includes`, or a `task_config.dir`) nothing is reported.

The deprecated-key rewrite is only offered when it can be done from schema data without guessing: the replacement is a key the schema declares and does not deprecate, nothing is already there, the value is accepted by the schema in its new place, and the edited text parses to exactly the document with that value moved. `env_path`, `env_file` and the deprecated `task_*` settings qualify (tested against `schema/mise.json`); descriptions without a named key, such as hook `script`, get no fix.

The server stays offline and never renders templates.

Docs: `docs/ide-integration.md` and the `mise lsp` help (rendered).

## Testing

Unit tests for the diagnostics, the skip rules, file tasks, cycles (chain, self, none), and the replacement rules (including the real schema), plus session tests for the quick fixes and diagnostics.

title: fix(schema): declare dotfile_groups entry keys and lint the schema with Tombi
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/956
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14803

Editors that validate strictly against `schema/mise.json` (Tombi, for example) flagged valid keys in `[dotfile_groups.<name>.entries]`, because the schema declared those entries as an open `object` with no properties:

```toml
[dotfile_groups.common.entries]
"~/.ssh/config" = { mode = "copy", permissions = "0600" }
# in strict mode, `dotfile_groups.common.entries."~/.ssh/config"` does not allow "mode" key.
```

Group entries now have a declared schema (`DotfileGroupEntryTableDecl`): the whole-file keys of a `[dotfiles]` entry, with the same descriptions and key-combination rules. It leaves out `block`, `line`, `template`, `comment`, `position` and `merge`, which a group rejects. Editors get validation and completion for these entries, and unknown keys are now reported.

- A mise-system test checks the declared keys match what the group entry parser reads.
- CI now lints `schema/tombi-fixtures/*.toml` with `tombi lint --error-on-warnings` (an `hk` step), pointing at the checkout's generated schema. The fixture reproduces the issue and fails on the previous schema.

Not run: the full `mise run lint` stops on an existing `unused dependency openssl` warning in `Cargo.toml`, unrelated to this change.

title: fix(aqua): make the baked registry encoding deterministic
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/955
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's `build.rs` no longer writes different bytes for the baked aqua registry on every run. Two builds of the same commit used to differ in 659 of 2333 `aqua_standard_registry_packages/*.rkyv` files, so the compiled-in registry, and the binary containing it, was not reproducible, and build caches keyed on the build script's output disagreed with the files on disk.

`AquaPackage` kept its `replacements` and `vars` values in `std::collections::HashMap`, and rkyv serializes a map in iteration order. std seeds that order randomly in each process. The fields are now `BTreeMap`, so the encoding is stable. The public `AquaPackage::with_var_values` still takes a `HashMap` and converts it.

How I found it: the `trusted / windows-lint` job on the self-hosted Windows runner kept failing with `mbx[error]: compilation result was discarded: compiler input changed after discovery: ...\aqua_standard_registry_packages\6684d9455c61a47e.rkyv`, preceded by `build-script result was not stored: local action key already has a different result`. The failure was intermittent and depended on which sibling job had populated the shared cache first. That points at the build script producing different output for the same inputs, which this PR fixes at the source.

Verification: I built the `mise` build script twice into separate target directories on the same commit. Before: 659 of 2333 files differed. After: 0 of 2333 differ. A new unit test in `crates/aqua-registry/src/codec.rs` encodes the same package with its map filled in different insertion orders and requires identical bytes. `cargo test -p aqua-registry` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

Not verified: that this stops the Windows CI failure. I could not reproduce that failure outside CI, so I'll watch `windows-lint` on later runs.

> **Medium Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Makes baked aqua registry **rkyv** output stable across builds by storing package **`replacements`**, internal **`var_values`**, and checksum **`replacements`** in **`BTreeMap`** instead of **`HashMap`**, since rkyv serializes maps in iteration order and `HashMap` order varies per process.

title: feat(lsp): complete, define, and rename tasks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/954
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lsp` now understands tasks. In `mise.toml`, a task name in `depends`, `depends_post`, `wait_for` or `run = [{ task = "..." }]` completes, shows the task's description and command on hover, jumps to its `[tasks.<name>]`, and can be renamed together with every reference to it in the file.

Follow-up to #14744, which is merged. This is the first of three `mise lsp` PRs. They are stacked: PR 2 is based on this branch and PR 3 on PR 2. Retarget each PR's base to `main` once the one below it merges.

## Before / after

```toml
[tasks.build]
description = "compile"
run = "cargo build"

[tasks.test]
depends = ["bu"]
```

Before: nothing completed inside `depends`, and `build` was just a string.

After:
- Completing at `"bu|"` offers `build` (with its description).
- Hovering `"build"` shows `**build** _task_`, `compile`, and the `cargo build` command.
- Go to definition on `"build"` lands on `[tasks.build]`, in another file when that is where it lives.
- Rename on `build` to `compile` rewrites `[tasks.build]`, `[tasks.build.env]`, dotted spellings and every reference, and keeps arguments (`"build --release"` becomes `"compile --release"`).

## What it reads

The open document (from the editor buffer), the configs in the directories above it, and the TOML files their `[task_config] includes` name (a file, or a directory of TOML files), read the way `includes.rs` already reads configs. Globs, `git::`/`oci::` includes and file tasks (scripts) are not read. The server stays offline and never renders templates.

## Notes

- `extends` names a task template (`[task_templates.<name>]`), not a task, so it completes, jumps and renames within templates.
- A task is found by its name or an `alias`.
- Rename is refused rather than half done: after computing the edits the server re-parses the result and checks it equals the original document with only the rename applied. It also refuses when the task is defined in another file, when the name is an alias, or when the new name exists. It also refuses when another config or include file refers to the task, since the server edits only the open file.
- New `initializationOptions` switches `definition`, `references` and `rename` (default on); each capability is advertised only while on. Task completion and hover follow the existing `completion` and `hover` switches.

Docs: `docs/ide-integration.md` and the `mise lsp` help (rendered).

## Testing

Unit tests in `crates/mise-lsp` cover the index, reference shapes, completion, rename edge cases, and whole-session tests for hover, definition (same and other file), references, rename and the capability switches.

title: fix(brew): tolerate custom Requirement classes in tap formulae
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/953
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14804.

A tap formula that declares its own platform check no longer breaks `mise bootstrap packages apply` when the tap has no published API metadata and mise has to evaluate the Ruby formula:

```ruby
class SplashMacOSRequirement < Requirement
  fatal true
  satisfy(build_env: false) { OS.mac? && MacOS.full_version >= "26.4" }
end

class Splash < Formula
  depends_on SplashMacOSRequirement
end
```

Before, this failed with `uninitialized constant Requirement` and nothing was installed. Now the formula resolves.

- Adds a `Requirement` base class to the metadata shim and the build shim. Its class-level DSL (`fatal`, `satisfy`, ...) is a no-op.
- `depends_on SomeRequirement` is no longer recorded as a formula dependency.
- Custom requirements are **not enforced**: their `satisfy` blocks use Homebrew internals such as `MacOS`, so they are never evaluated. Enforcing them would be a separate change.

I ran the metadata shim directly under Ruby 4.0.7 and it resolves the formula above. The new Rust test (`tolerates_custom_requirement_classes`) did not run here because `mise-sigstore` fails to compile in this sandbox, so CI is its first run.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Custom platform requirements are skipped rather than evaluated, so packages may install on hosts that Homebrew would reject; behavior is logged but not blocking.
> 
> **Overview**
> Third-party Homebrew tap formulae that define custom **`Requirement`** subclasses (e.g. `depends_on SplashMacOSRequirement`) no longer abort metadata evaluation with **`uninitialized constant Requirement`**.
> 
> The metadata and build Ruby shims now define a stub **`Requirement`** base class so subclass bodies can load; class-level DSL calls are no-ops and **`satisfy`** blocks are never run. **`depends_on`** treats a **Class** argument as a platform requirement, not a formula: it is omitted from dependency lists, collected as **`unsupported_requirements`** in the JSON output, and the Rust tap loader strips that field and emits a **warn** that the requirement is not enforced. A regression test covers a formula with a custom requirement plus a normal **`libfoo`** dependency.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 54a4348bc31df0223932e35140b4ad6d6fe7d59b. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(env): avoid sops CLI recursion through mise shims
body:
With `sops.rops = false`, a missing configured `sops` version can make environment decryption fall back to mise's own `sops` shim on `PATH`. The shim re-enters mise and loads the same encrypted environment again. This can also happen with an inherited shim from a different `MISE_DATA_DIR`.

Internal executable lookup now skips mise's dispatch directories and candidates that are the running mise binary, including symlinks and hard links on Unix and Windows. It continues searching for a directly spawnable executable on `PATH`, rejecting directories and Windows interpreter-only scripts such as `.ps1` and `.vbs`. Configured installed tools still take precedence, executable-name ordering stays the same, and a missing executable retains the existing strict error or non-strict skip behavior. The file-identity check is shared with the existing npm lookup and uses the existing `same-file` dependency.

For example, if a project requests an uninstalled SOPS version and `PATH` contains a mise shim followed by a standalone `sops`, decryption now uses the standalone executable. If only the shim is available, strict mode reports `sops command not found` instead of invoking the shim. The SOPS documentation explains this lookup behavior.

Fixes #14799.

### Validation

- All **922 backend unit tests** and **8 SOPS-related unit tests** pass on macOS arm64 with Rust 1.97.0. The lookup tests cover dispatch directories, inherited symlink and hard-link shims, real executable fallbacks, and missing-CLI behavior without executing a shim.
- Both relevant E2E scripts pass through `mise run test:e2e`: `test_sops_cli_shim` and `test_sops_cli_without_age`. They cover configured-tool priority, real PATH fallback, strict/non-strict missing-CLI behavior, and lookup without a configured version. The fixture PATH excludes host-installed SOPS.
- Workspace/all-features/all-targets Clippy passes with warnings denied. Changed-file hk checks and normal pre-commit checks pass.

Windows-only regressions cover interpreter-only extensions and a bare shebang script before a native `.cmd` fallback; these cases have not run locally and require native Windows CI. The E2E uses local SOPS stubs and does not exercise a live KMS provider. The unchanged documentation passed its build and link checks on the previous PR head.

title: fix(lockfile): keep the Python a pipx tool selects
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/948
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Recreates #14788 by @AllDmeat (credited as co-author). Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14787.

When a pipx tool selects its own Python (`python = "3.12"` on the tool, from #14479), `mise lock` writes that Python next to the project's Python. Other commands that rewrite `mise.lock` then lose one of the two entries:

```toml
[tools]
python = "3.13"
"pipx:yamllint" = { version = "1.38.0", python = "3.12" }
```

- `mise use` / `mise up -l` drop the selected Python, and `mise install --locked` then fails with `python@3.12 is not in the lockfile`.
- `mise lock pipx:yamllint` drops the project's Python.
- `mise lock python` drops the selected Python.

With this change all three keep both entries. A full `mise lock` behaves as before.

## How

- When a lockfile is rewritten, entries bound to Python requests that a current pipx tool (or tool stub) selects are kept, unless this update locked the same request itself. These runtimes are private, so installs never return them and the merge cannot see them. Removing the pipx tool still drops its Python.
- A filtered `mise lock` prunes stale versions only of the tools it names.
- `mise lock python` also resolves the Pythons that the configured pipx tools and stubs select.
- A malformed `python` option on one tool is logged at debug level instead of failing an unrelated lockfile rewrite.

## Testing

- New e2e test `lockfile/test_lockfile_pipx_selected_python` covers `mise use`, `mise lock pipx:yamllint`, `mise lock python` and tool stubs. It fails without the fix and passes with it.
- New unit test `test_preserve_selected_python_entries_keeps_only_unlocked_selections`; `cargo test --lib lockfile::` passes. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

> Changes lockfile merge and filtered `mise lock` behavior for Python and pipx tools; mistakes could leave stale or duplicate Python entries, though coverage is added for the main scenarios.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes lockfile rewrites dropping **two Python entries** when a pipx tool pins its own interpreter (`python = "3.12"`) alongside the project Python (`python = "3.13"`). Partial updates—`mise use`, filtered `mise lock pipx:…`, `mise lock python`, tool stubs, and task tools—now keep both specifiers instead of leaving `mise install --locked` without the selected runtime.
> 
> **Lockfile merge** (`lockfile.rs`): while updating a lockfile, pipx-selected Python requests are derived from configured tools and on-disk tool stubs; existing Python rows that match those requests (version specifier + options) are **preserved** unless this pass already locked that request. +#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# The Python a pipx tool selects with `python = "..."` is locked next to the
+# project's python. Updating another tool or a filtered `mise lock` must keep it.
+export MISE_LOCKFILE=1
+export MISE_PYTHON_GITHUB_ATTESTATIONS=0
+# Without uv the lock needs no interpreter for the dependency graph.
+export MISE_PYPI_UVX=0
+
+cat <<'EOF' >mise.toml
+[tools]
+python = "3.13"
+"pipx:yamllint" = { version = "1.38.0", python = "3.12" }
+dummy = "1.0.0"
+EOF
+touch mise.lock
+
+mise lock
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.13"]'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+cp mise.lock mise.lock.full
+
+echo "=== mise use keeps the selected python ==="
+mise use dummy@1.1.0
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.13"]'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+
+echo "=== mise lock pipx:yamllint keeps the project python ==="
+cp mise.lock.full mise.lock
+mise lock pipx:yamllint
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.13"]'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+
+echo "=== mise lock python keeps the selected python ==="
+cp mise.lock.full mise.lock
+mise lock python
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.13"]'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+
+echo "=== mise lock python adds a missing selected python ==="
+cp mise.toml mise.toml.full
+grep -v 'pipx:yamllint' mise.toml.full >mise.toml
+rm mise.lock
+touch mise.lock
+mise lock
+assert_not_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+cp mise.toml.full mise.toml
+mise lock python
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.13"]'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'specifiers = ["3.12"]'
+
+echo "=== a tool stub's selected python survives too ==="
+cat <<'EOF2' >mise.toml
+[tools]
+python = "3.13"
+EOF2
+mkdir -p bin

### [`v1.1.2`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/releases/tag/v1.1.2): : comment-release-fixes now actually runs the no-common-ancestor fix

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/compare/v1.1.1...v1.1.2)

v1.1.2 makes `comment-release-fixes` actually run the "no common ancestor" fix that v1.1.1 announced.

##### Fixed

- **`comment-release-fixes`: the v1.1.1 ancestry fix now takes effect.** The reusable workflow runs its shared script from a fixed commit of `jdx/workflows`. In v1.1.1, that pinned commit was still from before [#​12](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/issues/12), so the workflow kept failing with `No common ancestor` / `cannot safely establish release ancestry` whenever an earlier release tag shared no history with the new release. The pin now points to the merge of [#​12](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/issues/12). Release tags with no common ancestor are skipped, and the workflow uses the closest earlier release that is an ancestor. ([#​14](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/issues/14) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

  To upgrade, change your `uses: jdx/workflows/.github/workflows/comment-release-fixes.yml@<sha> # v1.1.2` pin to the v1.1.2 commit. Pinning to v1.1.1 doesn't fix the error. If the job failed for a release, run the workflow again with `workflow_dispatch` to post its comments.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/workflows/compare/v1.1.1...v1.1.2>

### [`v1.1.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/releases/tag/v1.1.1): : comment-release-fixes no longer aborts on tags from unrelated history

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/workflows/compare/v1.1.0...v1.1.1)

`comment-release-fixes` now ignores earlier release tags that share no history with the new release, so it can still find the correct base release.

##### Fixed

- **`comment-release-fixes`: release tags with no common ancestor are skipped.** Some repositories have published releases from a separate history, for example after the repository was rewritten. Because a tag with no common ancestor can't be an earlier release of the target, the workflow now skips it and uses the closest release that is an ancestor. title: feat(upgrade): write resolved versions on bare --bump when pin is set
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/945
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `pin` on (`MISE_PIN=1`), `mise upgrade --bump` now writes exact versions for every non-exact request in `mise.toml`, so `latest` and `20` become the resolved version. Previously `pin` only affected `mise use` and named selectors like `mise upgrade node@3 --bump`; a bare `--bump` kept each request's precision, so `latest` stayed `latest`.

```toml
# mise.toml before
[tools]
node = "latest"
python = "3.12"
```

```sh
MISE_PIN=1 mise upgrade --bump
```

```toml
# mise.toml after
[tools]
node = "24.14.0"
python = "3.12.8"
```

This applies whether or not the tool was outdated, so an up-to-date `latest` is also rewritten. `--dry-run` reports `Would bump ...`. Without `pin`, behavior is unchanged: requests keep their precision, and exact versions are untouched. Requests like `node@latest` named on the command line behave as before.

Motivated by https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14790, where the author wanted to turn `latest` into the installed version.

Behavior change for existing `pin` users: their next bare `--bump` will turn `"22"` into `"22.1.0"`, which matches what `pin` is documented to mean.

Tests: new `e2e/cli/test_upgrade_bump_pin` covers `latest` and `20`, with and without pin, and dry-run. The existing upgrade e2e tests still pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how `mise.toml` is rewritten for users with `pin` enabled on `upgrade --bump`, though scope is limited to config persistence and documented edge-case skips.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise upgrade --bump`** gains a **`--pin`** flag (requires **`--bump`**) that rewrites config entries to the **resolved** version instead of preserving request shape (`latest` / `20` → `24.14.0`). The existing **`pin`** setting / **`MISE_PIN=1`** now applies the same behavior on a **bare** `mise upgrade --bump`, including when tools are already up to date; without pin, precision-keeping bump behavior is unchanged.
> 
> Implementation walks writable, single-entry config requests, skips non-numeric channel strings (except `latest`), multi-platform tool blocks, and non-persistable sources; it suppresses the normal precision bump preview when a pin rewrite applies, and drops pin updates for tools deselected in **`--interactive`** mode. Docs, usage KDL, man page, and **`pin`** setting text are updated; **`e2e/cli/test_upgrade_bump_pin`** covers pin setting, **`--pin`**, dry-run, exact versions, outdated bumps, and edge cases.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# With the `pin` setting on, a bare `--bump` writes exact versions for requests
+# that are not exact (`latest`, `20`), whether or not they are outdated. Without
+# it, the specificity of the request is kept.
+
+PLUGIN_DIR="$MISE_DATA_DIR/plugins/pintest"
+mkdir -p "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin"
+
+cat <<'LISTALL' >"$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/list-all"
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "19.0.0 20.0.0 20.5.0 20.5.3"
+LISTALL
+chmod +x "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/list-all"
+
+cat <<'INSTALL' >"$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/install"
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+mkdir -p "$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH"
+touch "$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH/version-$ASDF_INSTALL_VERSION"
+INSTALL
+chmod +x "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/install"
+
+for request in latest 20; do
+  cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pintest = "$request"
+CONFIG
+  mise uninstall --all pintest 2>/dev/null || true
+  mise install pintest@20.5.3
+
+  # without pin the request is left alone
+  before=$(cat mise.toml)
+  mise upgrade --bump
+  assert "cat mise.toml" "$before"
+
+  # a dry run reports the change without writing it
+  assert_contains "MISE_PIN=1 mise upgrade --bump --dry-run 2>&1" "Would bump pintest@20.5.3"
+  assert "cat mise.toml" "$before"
+
+  MISE_PIN=1 mise upgrade --bump
+  assert "cat mise.toml" '[tools]
+pintest = "20.5.3"'
+done
+
+# --pin does the same as the setting
+cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pintest = "latest"
+CONFIG
+mise uninstall --all pintest 2>/dev/null || true
+mise install pintest@20.5.3
+mise upgrade --bump --pin
+assert "cat mise.toml" '[tools]
+pintest = "20.5.3"'
+
+# a configured exact version is untouched
+mise upgrade --bump
+assert "cat mise.toml" '[tools]
+pintest = "20.5.3"'
+
+# an outdated request is upgraded and pinned to the version installed
+cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pintest = "latest"
+CONFIG
+mise uninstall --all pintest 2>/dev/null || true
+mise install pintest@20.5.0
+mise upgrade --bump --pin
+assert "cat mise.toml" '[tools]
+pintest = "20.5.3"'
+assert_contains "mise ls --current pintest" "20.5.3"
+
+# a named tool is pinned on its own
+cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pintest = "latest"
+CONFIG
+mise upgrade pintest --bump --pin
+assert "cat mise.toml" '[tools]
+pintest = "20.5.3"'
+
+# deselected or multi-platform entries are not rewritten
+cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pintest = [{ version = "latest", os = ["linux"] }, { version = "latest", os = ["macos"] }]
+CONFIG
+before=$(cat mise.toml)
+mise upgrade --bump --pin
+assert "cat mise.toml" "$before"
+
+# a request that names no version is left alone, it is not "latest"
+PLUGIN_DIR="$MISE_DATA_DIR/plugins/pinchannel"
+mkdir -p "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin"
+cat <<'LISTALL' >"$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/list-all"
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "1.0.0 2.0.0 nightly"
+LISTALL
+chmod +x "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/list-all"
+cat <<'INSTALL' >"$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/install"
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+mkdir -p "$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH"
+touch "$ASDF_INSTALL_PATH/version-$ASDF_INSTALL_VERSION"
+INSTALL
+chmod +x "$PLUGIN_DIR/bin/install"
+cat <<CONFIG >mise.toml
+[tools]
+pinchannel = "nightly"
+CONFIG
+mise install pinchannel@nightly
+before=$(cat mise.toml)
+mise upgrade --bump --pin
+assert "cat mise.toml" "$before"

title: fix(github): skip .netrc credentials on the asset reachability HEAD
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/943
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14785

With a \`.netrc\` entry for \`github.com\` (e.g. Bitrise's git-clone step) and a lockfile \`url_api\`, mise's reachability HEAD on the browser download URL carried Basic auth. github.com then redirects to a presigned URL that returns 401 for HEAD, so mise treated the asset as unreachable and fell back to an anonymous \`api.github.com\` download, which 403s on shared CI IPs.

The reachability probe now sends HEAD without \`.netrc\` credentials, so it behaves the same as with no \`.netrc\` and downloads from the browser URL.

I did not add an e2e/unit test; verified that it compiles and passes clippy.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes HTTP credential application for a specific HEAD path; behavior for normal GET/downloads and URL-replacement mirrors is intentionally preserved but touches shared retry/netrc logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes GitHub release asset URL selection when a **`.netrc`** entry supplies credentials for **`github.com`** (common on CI). The reachability **HEAD** on the browser download URL no longer sends those netrc credentials, so GitHub does not redirect to a presigned URL that fails **HEAD** and mis-reports the asset as unreachable.
> 
> **`HTTP.head_without_netrc`** implements this via a **`netrc_replacement_only`** retry/send option: netrc is skipped for the original host but still applies after a **URL replacement** moves the request to another host (private mirror auth unchanged). **`pick_reachable_asset_url`** now uses that helper instead of **`HTTP.head`**.
>

title: fix(deps): update webpki-root-certs and rustls-webpki for eMudhra CA revocation
body:
The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised ([details](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/)). Browsers have blocked them, but mise's embedded npm backend (aube) bundles its own root list via `webpki-root-certs`, so it still trusted them.

Bumps in `Cargo.lock` to the patched releases:

- `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 → 0.103.16
- `webpki-root-certs` 1.0.9 → 1.0.10

Lockfile-only. The default `native-tls` build and the `rustls` feature read the OS trust store, so they're fixed by OS updates.

> Touches embedded TLS root trust for the npm backend; scope is limited to lockfile patches but incorrect or incomplete CA removal would leave compromised roots trusted.

> **Overview**
> **Lockfile-only** dependency bumps so mise’s embedded npm path (via `aube-util`’s bundled `webpki-root-certs`) no longer trusts CAs revoked after the eMudhra intermediate key compromise.
> 
> Updates **`webpki-root-certs`** `1.0.9` → `1.0.10` and **`rustls-webpki`** `0.103.15` → `0.103.16`. The diff also reflects transitive **`windows-sys`** `0.52.0` → `0.59.0` on several crates pulled in by those releases. Builds that use the OS trust store (`native-tls` / `rustls` feature) are unchanged here and rely on platform updates instead.

title: fix(config): keep tracked .tool-versions recognized under a filename override
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/940
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14775

With \`MISE_OVERRIDE_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAMES=.combined-tool-versions\`, commands that load tracked configs (\`mise ls --prunable\`, \`mise prune\`, \`mise upgrade\`) warned \`unknown config file type\` for every tracked \`.tool-versions\`, and skipped them, so \`mise prune\` could treat those projects' versions as unused.

Tracked files now fall back to recognizing the builtin \`.tool-versions\` name regardless of the override, so they load without warnings and their versions stay protected.

```sh
MISE_OVERRIDE_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAMES=.combined-tool-versions mise prune --dry-run
```

Added e2e test \`test_prune_tracked_tool_versions_override\`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to tracked-config type detection when a filename override is active; reduces incorrect prune behavior without touching auth or global config resolution.
> 
> **Overview**
> When **`MISE_OVERRIDE_TOOL_VERSIONS_FILENAMES`** is set, tracked **`.tool-versions`** paths were no longer classified during **`load_tracked_config_files`**, which produced **unknown config file type** warnings and let **`mise prune`** (and similar commands) treat those projects’ pinned versions as unused.
> 
> **Tracked config loading** now falls back to **`ToolVersions`** for paths whose basename is **`.tool-versions`**, even if the override hides that name from normal filename detection, so tracked pins stay loaded and protected.
> 
> An **e2e** script asserts **`mise prune --dry-run`** under the override emits no tracked-config errors and only prunes versions not referenced by the tracked file.

title: fix(task): rehash same-size source edits that restore mtime in content-hash mode
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/939
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14746.

With `task.source_freshness_hash_contents = true`, a task source edited to a same-size value while keeping its old mtime (`rsync -a`, `cp -p`, `touch -r`, `os.utime`) was treated as unchanged. A cached task kept returning its earlier success even though the input had changed.

The per-file content-hash cache reused a stored hash whenever size and mtime matched. It now also compares the file's ctime on Unix, which can't be set from userspace, so the file is rehashed and the task re-runs. Cache files written by older versions are rehashed once. Windows behavior is unchanged.

Added a unit test that edits a file to the same size, restores its mtime, and checks the aggregate hash changes. I didn't run the reporter's full Python repro end to end.

> **Low Risk**

> **Overview**
> Fixes stale task skips when **`task.source_freshness_hash_contents`** is enabled: a same-length source edit with **mtime restored** (`cp -p`, `rsync -a`, `touch -r`) no longer reuses a cached blake3 hash.
> 
> The per-file **content-hash cache** in `task_source_checker.rs` now treats **size, mtime, and Unix ctime** as the stat key before skipping a re-read. **ctime** is included because it typically cannot be forged from userspace when size and mtime are copied back. title: feat(vfox): add RUNTIME.cacheDirPath for plugins
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/937
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Backend plugins now get `RUNTIME.cacheDirPath`, a directory under mise's cache that belongs to the plugin, so a plugin that serves many tools can keep a large shared download in one place.

```lua
function PLUGIN:BackendListVersions(ctx)
    local index = RUNTIME.cacheDirPath .. "/01-index.tar"
    -- download once, then extend it with a Range request on later runs
end
```

- The path is `$MISE_CACHE_DIR/plugins/<plugin-name>`. mise creates it before running a hook, and every hook of the plugin sees the same path.
- It survives reinstalling the plugin, unlike `pluginDirPath`.
- `mise cache clear` already deletes the whole cache directory, so it covers this too. Plugins must cope with it being missing.
- It is `nil` where there is no cache directory configured.

I did not change `mise cache prune`.

Closes discussion #14757.

title: feat(doctor): let a project check depend on another check
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/935
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Adds `depends` to `[doctor.checks.*]` so a check that only makes sense after another one passes is reported as `blocked` instead of as a second, misleading failure.

```toml
[doctor.checks."examplectl:auth"]
run = "examplectl auth status"
hint = "examplectl auth login"

[doctor.checks."examplectl:project"]
depends = ["examplectl:auth"]
run = 'test -n "$(examplectl config get project)"'
hint = "examplectl config set project <name>"
```

When not logged in, `mise doctor project` now prints:

```
FAIL examplectl:auth: examplectl:auth
  Command exited with exit status: 1
  examplectl auth login
BLOCKED examplectl:project: examplectl:project
  Blocked: dependency examplectl:auth did not pass
```

The blocked check's command does not run and its hint is not shown, so the report points at the first step to fix.

- `depends` takes a check name or a list of names.
- A dependency that ends in `fail`, `error`, `skipped` (excluded by `os`) or `blocked` blocks its dependents.
- New `blocked` status in text and `--json` output. It does not fail the run by itself; the failing dependency already does (exit 1).
- An unknown dependency or a cycle is reported as a config error and no check runs.
- Checks without `depends` run in parallel as before. Dependents wait for their dependencies, and `jobs` cannot deadlock the wait because checks are admitted in dependency order.

Docs, JSON schema and e2e coverage (blocked, passing dependency, cycle, unknown name) are included.

Closes discussion #14761.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`depends`** to `[doctor.checks.*]` so a check can wait for other checks to pass before running. If a dependency fails, errors, is skipped by `os`, or is blocked, dependents are reported as **`blocked`** (command not run, hint hidden) instead of producing a second misleading failure.
> 
> `mise doctor project` now topologically orders checks, validates unknown names and cycles up front (no checks run on config error), and uses watch channels so dependents wait without holding **`jobs`** permits—only the actual shell command acquires concurrency limits. Text and `--json` output include the new **`blocked`** status; exit code behavior is unchanged (still driven by `fail`/`error`, not `blocked` alone).

title: fix(env): keep pre-activation PATH entries when the shell deduplicates PATH
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/934
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14760

`exec()` in an `[env]` value (and other commands mise spawns with the pristine environment) could fail to find a command in a directory listed in `_.path` when that directory was already on `PATH` before activation and the shell deduplicates `PATH`, e.g. zsh with `typeset -U path PATH`:

```toml
[env]
_.path = ["/opt/homebrew/bin"]   # also added by ~/.zshrc
FOUND = "{{ exec(command='command -v examplectl || echo not found') }}"
```

Before: `FOUND` was `not found` with `typeset -U path PATH`, but worked without it.
After: `FOUND` resolves the command either way.

## Cause

When mise reconstructs the pre-activation environment, it removes each directory it added to `PATH` once. If the shell keeps duplicates, `PATH` has mise's copy and the original, so removing one leaves the original. With deduplication there is a single entry, and removing it also drops the pre-activation one.

## Fix

A directory that appears in `__MISE_ORIG_PATH` and occurs only once in the current `PATH` is now kept, since that single copy must be the pre-activation entry. Shells that keep duplicates behave as before. With a deduplicating shell, the surviving entry sits at its position in the activated `PATH` rather than its original position, which only affects lookup order for spawned commands.

## Testing

Added a unit test covering both the deduplicated and duplicated `PATH` cases (`cargo test -p mise-util pristine`). Clippy on `mise-util` is clean. I did not run the zsh reproduction script from the discussion.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core PATH reversal used by `PRISTINE_ENV` and spawned commands; logic is narrow but incorrect PATH handling could break command lookup in activated shells.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **pristine environment** reconstruction so `exec()` and other subprocesses that use `PRISTINE_ENV` can still resolve binaries on directories that were already on `PATH` before mise activation when the shell deduplicates `PATH` (e.g. zsh `typeset -U path`).
> 
> `get_pristine_env` still strips each mise-added directory from `PATH` once, but now **preserves** a path entry when it appears in `__MISE_ORIG_PATH` and occurs only once in the current `PATH`—treating that lone copy as the pre-activation entry rather than mise’s add. Shells that keep duplicate entries behave as before (only mise’s copy is removed).
> 
> Adds regression tests for deduplicated vs duplicated `PATH` layouts.

https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/933

`[doctor.checks.*]` commands and messages can now use the same templates as the rest of the config, so a check can reuse a value from `[vars]` instead of hard-coding it or exporting it through `[env]`.

```toml
[vars.repos_dir]
prompt = "Where should repositories be cloned?"
default = "{{ env.HOME }}/src"

[doctor.checks."project-a:env"]
description = "project-a has a .env file"
run = 'test -f {{ vars.repos_dir | quote }}/project-a/.env'
hint = "cp {{ vars.repos_dir }}/project-a/.env.example {{ vars.repos_dir }}/project-a/.env"
```

Before, `run` was passed to the shell verbatim (failing with exit 127) and `hint` printed `{{ vars.repos_dir }}` literally. Now `run`, `description` and `hint` are rendered with the declaring config file's template context, as hooks are. `dir` is still not rendered. A template error reports `ERROR` for that check only (naming the file); other checks still run, and checks skipped by `os` are not rendered. Existing literal `{{`/`{%` in these fields now parse as templates.

Docs updated; new e2e `test_doctor_project_templates` covers a passing check, a failing check, and a rendered hint and description.

title: feat(bootstrap): accept a shell name in bootstrap.user.login_shell
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/932
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.user].login_shell` previously required an absolute path, so a config shared across machines had to know where each system installs the shell. It now also accepts a bare shell name:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"brew:fish" = "latest"

[bootstrap.user]
login_shell = "fish"
```

mise resolves the name when it checks or applies the setting, after `bootstrap.packages` has installed the shell. It searches `PATH` (never the mise shims directory), then common package-manager locations (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin`, `~/.linuxbrew/bin`, `/usr/bin`, `/bin`), and uses the first executable it finds. The resolved path goes through the existing idempotent `/etc/shells` and `chsh` handling.

- If no executable is found, `mise bootstrap user apply` fails without touching `/etc/shells` or the account, `status` reports `not installed` (and `--missing` exits 1), and `apply --dry-run` says the path is resolved after installation.
- `mise bootstrap user status` shows the resolved path; `--json` has a new `resolved` field.
- Absolute paths behave as before. A relative path containing a slash (e.g. `bin/fish`) is still ignored with a warning, now worded "must be an absolute path or a bare shell name".

Docs are updated in `docs/bootstrap/shell.md`.

Closes discussion https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14765.

## Validation

`mise run test:e2e test_system_login_shell` passes, extended to cover unresolved, resolved, dry-run and apply. Unit tests and clippy were not run locally because the `mlua-sys` build needs `lua51.pc`.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how login shells are validated and applied (`chsh`, `/etc/shells`, sudo); mistakes could still affect the wrong user under `sudo`, but unresolved names fail closed without modifying system state.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`[bootstrap.user].login_shell`** can now be a **bare executable name** (e.g. `fish`) in addition to an absolute path or template. Relative paths with a separator (e.g. `bin/zsh`) are still rejected; schema, docs, and validation messages reflect the new rules.

> Resolution happens at **status/apply** time via `LoginShellRequest::resolve()`: search `PATH` (excluding mise shims), then common package-manager bins (including the target user’s `~/.linuxbrew/bin` under `sudo`). The resolved path drives `/etc/shells` and `chsh`; if nothing is found, status reports **not installed** / `--missing`, JSON includes **`resolved`**, dry-run notes deferred resolution, and **apply fails without changing the account or shells file**. title: fix(pipx): don't pick a case-insensitive `Python` match as the interpreter on macOS
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/931
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On macOS (case-insensitive APFS), \`pipx:\` installs failed when \`aqua:aws/aws-cli\` was in the toolset. aws-cli's pkg payload directory is on PATH and contains an executable-bit \`Python\` shared library, so mise's lookup for \`python\` resolved to it and handed it to uv as \`--python\`:

\`\`\`
uv tool install debugpy==1.8.22 --python .../aws-cli.pkg/Payload/aws-cli/python
error: Querying Python at \`.../aws-cli/python\` failed ... cannot execute binary file
\`\`\`

Spawnable lookups of a tool's binaries (used by pipx to find a mise-managed Python) now require the directory entry to match the requested name's case exactly on macOS. \`python\` no longer matches \`Python\`. Plain \`mise which\`, Linux and Windows behavior are unchanged.

This does not stop the dylib from shadowing \`python\` in the shell when \`aqua:aws/aws-cli\` is written out in full; the \`aws-cli\` registry shorthand already sets \`symlink_bins = true\`, which avoids that.

Tested with a new macOS unit test (\`which_in_dirs_spawnable_ignores_case_insensitive_match\`) and \`cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings\`.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14763

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> **Low Risk**
> Narrow, platform-specific guard on spawnable PATH resolution with fail-open behavior when `read_dir` errors; non-spawnable and non-macOS paths unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **pipx** (and other spawnable PATH lookups) on macOS when a case-insensitive volume would open the wrong file—for example `python` resolving to aws-cli’s executable `Python` dylib.

title: docs(dotfiles): clarify permissions-only group entries and pruning
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/930
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A group entry that sets only `permissions` does not inherit the group's `mode`: it deploys nothing and only adjusts an existing target. Removing a redundant `mode = "copy"` from such an entry therefore leaves the previously deployed file orphaned, and `--prune` removes it.

The group docs now state this exception under Group entries and under Deselect and remove groups, and show `{ mode = "copy", permissions = "0600" }` as the way to deploy and set permissions.

Fixes #14764

title: fix(release): sign Windows binaries in a separate workflow run
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/929
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tag releases could not sign the Windows binaries. SignPath rejected both signing jobs of run 39418030068 with "at least one job that had an impact on the artifact creation was executed on a non-github-hosted runner". It validates every job of the run it signs, and the release run builds Linux and macOS on Namespace runners, so the check could never pass.

## What changes

The Windows build and SignPath signing move to a new `release-windows.yml` workflow.

- **Tag releases:** a `sign-windows` job in `release.yml` dispatches `release-windows.yml` on the tag, so it runs as its own run containing only GitHub-hosted jobs. It waits for that run, downloads the signed zips, and re-uploads them as `tarball-<target>`, so the `release` job is unchanged. The job has a 120-minute timeout because the production policy can wait on a manual approval in SignPath.
- **Release PR dry run:** `release.yml` calls the same workflow in-run through `workflow_call`. Nothing is signed there, so the self-hosted Windows runner is still allowed for x64.
- **`release` job:** it requires that exactly one of `build-windows` (dry run) and `sign-windows` (tag) succeeded.

The dispatched run is found by a `request_id` (`<run_id>-<run_attempt>`) in its run name, so "re-run failed jobs" dispatches a fresh one.

## Validation

`jactionlint` passes on both workflows. I haven't run this end to end, and it can't be exercised before a tag push. I'd re-run the `v2026.10.16` release, or `workflow_dispatch` on a tag, to confirm.

> **Medium Risk**

> **Fixes tag releases where SignPath rejected Windows signing** because the main `release` workflow runs Linux/macOS builds on Namespace (non–GitHub-hosted) runners, and SignPath requires every job in the signing run to use GitHub-hosted runners.

> Windows packaging and Authenticode signing move into a new **`release-windows.yml`** workflow (build matrix, unsigned zip naming, SignPath on tags). **`release.yml`** no longer runs those jobs inline:
> 
> - **Release PR dry runs** call `release-windows.yml` via `workflow_call` as `build-windows` (non-tag only), so unsigned Windows zips still build in the same run—including optional self-hosted x64 when allowed.
> - **Tag releases** use a new `sign-windows` job that **`workflow_dispatch`es** `release-windows.yml` with a `request_id` run name, waits for completion, downloads `tarball-*-pc-windows-msvc` artifacts from that run, and re-uploads them so the `release` job keeps the same artifac
