diff:
--- .github/workflows/release-windows.yml (+144/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+name: release-windows
+
+# Builds and Authenticode-signs the Windows release zips.
+#
+# SignPath Foundation validates every job of the workflow run it signs and rejects the run if any
+# job ran on a non-GitHub-hosted runner. The rest of the release builds on Namespace runners, so a
+# real release dispatches this workflow as a run of its own (see `sign-windows` in release.yml) and
+# downloads the signed zips from it. The release PR's dry run calls it in-run instead: nothing is
+# signed there, so the self-hosted Windows runner is allowed.
+run-name: release-windows ${{ inputs.request_id }}
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      request_id:
+        description: "Identifies the release run that dispatched this workflow"
+        type: string
+        required: true
+  workflow_call:
+    inputs:
+      request_id:
+        type: string
+        required: false
+        default: ""
+    secrets:
+      MISE_GH_TOKEN:
+        required: false
+      SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN:
+        required: false
+
+concurrency:
+  group: release-windows-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ inputs.request_id }}
+  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
+  DRY_RUN: ${{ startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && '0' || '1' }}
+  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
+  GITHUB_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MISE_GH_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+  GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MISE_GH_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+  GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.MISE_GH_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+jobs:
+  build-tarball-windows:
+    name: build-tarball-windows-${{matrix.arch}}
+    # Each arch builds on a native runner. Cross-compiling arm64 on the x64 runner
+    # with fat LTO and panic=unwind ran past the 150-minute timeout.
+    # The release PR's dry run builds x64 on the shared trusted self-hosted runner (repository variable
+    # WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED=true; unset falls back to the hosted runner). A real release always builds on
+    # a GitHub-hosted runner, because SignPath Foundation requires every job of a run it signs to run
+    # on GitHub-hosted runners.
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.arch == 'x64' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && (github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'jdx' || github.event.pull_request.user.login == 'mise-en-dev') && vars.WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED == 'true' && fromJSON('["self-hosted", "jdx-win-trusted-v1"]') || matrix.runner }}
+    # Matches the Linux tarball job. Fat LTO's link varied from ~65 minutes to
+    # past this timeout on windows-latest depending on memory pressure, so
+    # scripts/build-tarball.ps1 builds with thin LTO on hosted runners and with
+    # the profile's fat LTO on the self-hosted runner, which has the RAM for it.
+    timeout-minutes: 150
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - arch: arm64
+            target: aarch64-pc-windows-msvc
+            runner: windows-11-arm
+          - arch: x64
+            target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
+            runner: windows-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - run: rustup target add ${{matrix.target}}
+      - run: scripts/build-tarball.ps1 ${{matrix.target}}
+        env:
+          OS: windows
+          ARCH: ${{matrix.arch}}
+      - name: Smoke-test vfox Lua errors
+        run: scripts/smoke-test-vfox-lua-error.ps1 dist/mise/bin/mise.exe
+      # The release job globs artifacts/*/mise-<version>-<platform>.zip, so the unsigned zip must not
+      # share the final name.
+      - name: Mark zip as unsigned
+        shell: pwsh
+        run: |
+          foreach ($zip in @(Get-ChildItem dist/*.zip)) {
+            Rename-Item $zip.FullName "unsigned-$($zip.Name)"
+          }
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: unsigned-tarball-${{matrix.target}}
+          path: dist/*.zip
+          if-no-files-found: error
+  # Authenticode-signs mise.exe and mise-shim.exe with SignPath Foundation. Only tag runs submit a
+  # signing request; dry runs pass the unsigned zip through under the name the release job expects.
+  sign-windows:
+    needs: [build-tarball-windows]
+    name: sign-windows-${{matrix.target}}
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 90
+    strategy:
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        target: [aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
+        with:
+          name: unsigned-tarball-${{matrix.target}}
+          path: dist
+      - name: Upload unsigned zip for SignPath
+        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
+        id: upload-unsigned
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: signpath-unsigned-${{matrix.target}}
+          path: dist/unsigned-*.zip
+          if-no-files-found: error
+      - name: Sign with SignPath
+        if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
+        uses: signpath/github-action-submit-signing-request@f6d04783b4569d051e0c80105fe66e82819d0092 # v3
+        with:
+          api-token: ${{ secrets.SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN }}
+          organization-id: ${{ vars.SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID }}
+          project-slug: mise
+          signing-policy-slug: ${{ vars.SIGNPATH_SIGNING_POLICY || 'release-signing' }}
+          github-artifact-id: ${{ steps.upload-unsigned.outputs.artifact-id }}
+          wait-for-completion: true
+          # The production policy requires a manual approval in SignPath.
+          wait-for-completion-timeout-in-seconds: 3600
+          output-artifact-directory: signed
+      - name: Restore the release zip name
+        run: |
+          src=dist
+          if [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/v* ]]; then src=signed; fi
+          mkdir final
+          for f in "$src"/unsigned-*.zip; do
+            cp "$f" "final/$(basename "$f" | sed 's/^unsigned-//')"
+          done
+      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
+        with:
+          name: tarball-${{matrix.target}}
+          path: final/*.zip
+          if-no-files-found: error

title: fix(aqua): handle unterminated string literals in template lexer
body:
### Problem
When lexing Aqua registry templates in `crates/aqua-registry/src/template.rs`, a string literal that begins with `"` but lacks an unescaped closing quote causes `lex()` to spin indefinitely in its `while !code.is_empty()` loop because `code` is never advanced.

Additionally, checking `code.chars().nth(end) != Some('\\')` indexed into character positions rather than byte offsets from `match_indices`, and did not account for escaped backslashes preceding the quote (e.g. `\\"` vs `\"`).

### Fix
- Ensure `lex()` bails with `"unterminated string literal"` when no matching unescaped closing quote is found instead of spinning indefinitely.
- Accurately count preceding backslashes byte-wise to determine quote escaping.
- Add regression test `test_render_unterminated_string_fails` in `crates/aqua-registry/src/template/tests.rs`.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of escaped quotation marks and backslashes in template strings.
  * Closing quotes are now identified correctly, including after multiple backslashes.
  * Unterminated string literals now return a clear error instead of being parsed incorrectly.
  * Unicode and escaped characters are preserved correctly during template processing.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for unterminated strings, Unicode content, escaped quotes, and backslash combinations.

title: feat(lsp): add mise lsp, a language server for mise.toml
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/922
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Editors can now get mise-aware help in `mise.toml` from mise itself. `mise lsp` runs a Language Server Protocol server over stdin/stdout, so any editor with an LSP client (Neovim, Helix, Emacs, Zed, VS Code, ...) can use it without a separate TOML extension or a TypeScript copy of mise's schema that drifts. Requested in [#14743](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14743).

```lua
vim.lsp.config("mise", { cmd = { "mise", "lsp" }, filetypes = { "toml" }, root_markers = { "mise.toml" } })
vim.lsp.enable("mise")
```

## What it does

- **Diagnostics**: TOML syntax errors, unknown keys with a suggestion (`unknown key \`colr\`; did you mean \`color\`?`), values of the wrong type, and deprecated keys.
- **Completion**: keys for the table the cursor is in (including `[headers]` and dotted keys) and values with a fixed set (booleans, enums).
- **Hover**: the key's type and description.
- **Quick fixes**: replace an unknown key with the suggested one. Diagnostics carry a `code` and the suggestion for clients.
- **Formatting**: the same output as `mise fmt`.

Inline tables complete too, and keys a table already has are not offered again. Diagnostics for the parts of a file you did not edit stay while it has a syntax error. A client can turn off `formatting`, `hover` or `completion` with `initializationOptions` when another TOML server covers them.

It answers only for files mise loads as configs (`mise.toml`, `.mise.toml`, `mise.<env>.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `mise/config.toml`, `conf.d/*.toml`) and ignores `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, other TOML, and files that `[task_config] includes` lists, so it can be attached to the TOML language safely. Configs are only parsed, never rendered, so opening an untrusted file runs nothing.

## How it works

The logic lives in a new `mise-lsp` crate that has no dependency on mise. `mise lsp` hands it `schema/mise.json` (generated from the types mise parses config with) and the `mise fmt` formatter, so answers track the installed mise. The crate name is reserved on crates.io with `0.0.0`, trusted publishing is configured for `jdx/mise` via `release-plz.yml`, and `xtasks/release-plz` publishes it before `mise`.

Not included yet: tool/version completion, go-to-definition, quick fixes, and which-files-does-mise-read discovery from the discussion; those are follow-ups.

title: feat(config): resolve relative and templated write_targets paths
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/921
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`settings.write_targets.*` only accepted absolute or `~/` paths, so dotfiles shared between machines with different `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` had to hardcode the config directory. Settings aren't templated and these keys have no env var, so there was no workaround.

Targets now resolve like other path settings (`settings.age.*`, `aqua.registries`): templates are rendered, and a relative result is joined to the `config_root` of the settings file that declares it. For a global file `config_root` is `$HOME`, so the portable spelling uses the template for the file's own directory:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/conf.d/settings.toml
[settings.write_targets]
tools = "{{ config_source | dirname }}/tools.toml"   # -> ~/.config/mise/conf.d/tools.toml
```

This works with any `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` / `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. The existing check still applies: the resolved path must be a global config file mise loads. A template that fails to render logs a warning and `mise use --global` fails with "must resolve to an absolute path" instead of writing to the default file.

Implementation: the path rendering from `resolve_age_paths` moved into a shared `settings_path_resolver`, and `write_targets` is resolved per file before settings layers merge (the declaring file is unknown afterwards).

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14739

Portable layouts can use **`{{ config_source | dirname }}/tools.toml`** instead of hardcoding `MISE_CONFIG_DIR`.

title: fix(daemons): resolve file tasks without their script extension
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/920
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[daemons.<name>] task = "worker"` failed with `daemon srv runs unknown task "worker"` when the task was a file task such as `.mise/tasks/worker.sh`, even though `mise run worker` and `mise task worker` resolve it. Users had to write `task = "worker.sh"`.

The daemon task validator did an exact key lookup on the task map. It now matches task names the same way `mise run` does, so `worker` finds `worker.sh`, and an unknown name still errors.

```toml
[daemons.srv]
task = "worker"   # .mise/tasks/worker.sh
```

Tested with a new case in `e2e/cli/test_daemons`.

Fixes #14740

title: ci(release): sign Windows release binaries with SignPath
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/919
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Windows releases of mise are currently unsigned, so SmartScreen and antivirus tools flag `mise.exe` and `mise-shim.exe`. mise was accepted into the SignPath Foundation program; this wires its Authenticode signing into the release workflow.

On `v*` tag runs, a new `sign-windows` job takes each Windows zip (x64 and arm64), has SignPath sign `mise.exe` and `mise-shim.exe` inside it, and republishes the signed zip as `tarball-<target>`, so downstream release jobs are unchanged. Release PR dry runs skip signing and pass the unsigned zip through.

- `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` is the config to paste into the SignPath project.
- The signing policy slug comes from the repo variable `SIGNPATH_SIGNING_POLICY`, falling back to `release-signing`. It is set to `test-signing` (self-signed certificate) until SignPath imports the production certificate; delete the variable then.
- Real-release x64 Windows builds now run on a GitHub-hosted runner, because SignPath Foundation requires every job of a signed run to be GitHub-hosted. They build with thin LTO (as arm64 already does) instead of the self-hosted runner's fat LTO. The PR dry run still uses the trusted self-hosted runner, and `WINDOWS_RELEASE_SELF_HOSTED` / `jdx-win-release-v1` are no longer used.
- Needs the `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` secret and `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` variable (both set).

Not yet exercised: signing only runs on a tag, so the first release is the real test.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes the release supply chain for Windows (new external signing step and runner selection on tags); misconfiguration of SignPath secrets or artifact naming could block or ship unsigned releases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **SignPath Foundation Authenticode signing** for Windows release zips on `v*` tag runs, so published `mise.exe` and `mise-shim.exe` are signed. Release PR dry runs still ship **unsigned** zips with the same artifact names the `release` job already expects.
> 
> The Windows build job now uploads **`unsigned-tarball-*`** artifacts (zips renamed with an `unsigned-` prefix). A new **`sign-windows`** job (x64 + arm64) downloads those zips, submits them to SignPath only on tags (with up to 1h wait for policy approval), then re-uploads **`tarball-<target>`** with the final zip names. The **`release`** job depends on **`sign-windows`** instead of the raw Windows build.
> 
> **Runner policy changes:** tag/manual release x64 builds always use **GitHub-hosted** runners (SignPath requires hosted jobs in signed runs). The trusted self-hosted x64 path remains only for in-repo release PR dry runs when `WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED=true`. **`WINDOWS_RELEASE_SELF_HOSTED`** / **`jdx-win-release-v1`** are dropped.
>

title: fix(self-update): update mise-shim.exe beside the real mise.exe, not a link to it
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/918
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise self-update` on Windows now keeps the `mise-shim.exe` link that winget creates and updates the real `mise-shim.exe` instead.

When mise is started through a link such as `%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\mise.exe`, self-update wrote the new `mise-shim.exe` next to that link. That replaced the `mise-shim.exe` link in `Links` with a plain copy and left the shim in the winget package directory on the old version. `mise reshim` then kept warning that the shim was older than mise, because it looks for the shim beside the real `mise.exe`.

Self-update now resolves `mise.exe` to its real path before choosing where to write `mise-shim.exe`. This matches how `mise reshim` already finds the shim.

Not tested on Windows: the changed function is `cfg(windows)`, so I only checked that the workspace still builds on Linux.

Fixes discussion #14736.

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Windows-only path resolution in post-update shim refresh; canonicalize failure keeps the old behavior via fallback.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Windows self-update** when `mise` is launched via a **WinGet link** (e.g. `%LocalAppData%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\mise.exe`). Previously, refreshing `mise-shim.exe` used the parent of `MISE_BIN`, so the new shim landed beside the link, replaced the link’s `mise-shim.exe` with a plain file, and left the real shim in the package directory outdated—triggering stale-shim warnings on `mise reshim`.
> 
> Self-update now **`dunce::canonicalize`s `MISE_BIN`** (falling back to the original path if that fails) and writes `mise-shim.exe` next to the **resolved** `mise.exe`, aligned with where reshimming expects the shim to live.
>

title: fix(env): start _.file find_up at the config root
body:
Fixes the confusion in #14711: `find_up = true` on `env._.file` silently changed where the search starts. Every other relative path in a config resolves against the config root, but `find_up` started at the current directory.

Now a relative `find_up` path starts at the config root and walks up through its parents, which suits a monorepo whose root `.env` applies to every package:

```toml
# mise.toml
[env]
_.file = { path = ".env", find_up = true }
```

An absolute path starts at its own directory and searches that directory and each parent for the file name. A global config that wants to search from wherever mise runs says so explicitly with `cwd`:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[env]
_.file = { path = "{{cwd}}/.env", find_up = true }
```

## Compatibility

`find_up` shipped in v2026.10.12 (and the multi-name `path` list in v2026.10.14). A global config with a relative `find_up` entry used to search from the current directory; it now searches from `~`, so it stops finding project files. Add `{{cwd}}/` in front of the path to keep the old behavior. The `env_file` setting still discovers dotenv files up from the current directory and is unchanged.

## Validation

- e2e: `env/test_env_file_find_up`, `env/test_env_file_find_up_group`, `config/test_paranoid_categories`, `config/test_paranoid_env_file_trust`, plus a new `env/test_env_file_find_up_hook_env` that activates bash, changes directories, and edits a loaded file.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p mise-config` pass.

title: feat(pypi): read private index passwords from a keyring for lock and version listing
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/916
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` and `latest` version listing now work against a PyPI index that authenticates through a keyring, such as Azure Artifacts with `artifacts-keyring`. Before, `mise install` succeeded because uv read the password from its keyring provider, but mise's own index requests sent no credentials and failed with `401 Unauthorized` (discussion #14724).

Set the new `pypi.keyring_provider` to `subprocess` and write the registry URL with a username and no password:

```toml
[settings.pypi]
keyring_provider = "subprocess"
registry_url = "https://VssSessionToken@pkgs.dev.azure.com/org/project/_packaging/feed/pypi/simple/{}/"
```

When the URL has a username but no password, mise runs `keyring get <url> <username>`, the same lookup uv's `keyring-provider = "subprocess"` makes. It sends the printed password as HTTP Basic credentials when it lists versions and when `mise lock` reads a release's `requires-python`. The password is never written to the lockfile or the version cache.

- `pypi.keyring_provider` accepts `disabled` (the default) or `subprocess`; env var `MISE_PYPI_KEYRING_PROVIDER`.
- The `keyring` executable must be on `PATH`. If it is missing or has no entry, mise sends the request without credentials, so the 401 is unchanged.
- URLs that already carry a password, and netrc credentials, behave as before.

The lookup lives in the pypi backend rather than the shared HTTP client, so no other backend is affected. `get_html_with_headers` is added to the client so the simple-index HTML request can carry the header.

Tested with a new e2e test (`test_pipx_keyring_provider`) that runs a local simple index requiring Basic auth and a fake `keyring` script. It checks that the request returns 401 without the setting, returns versions with it, and returns 401 again when the keyring has no entry. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint` pass. Not tested against a real Azure Artifacts feed or on Windows.

Closes nothing directly; follows up discussion #14724.

title: feat(vfox): let backend plugins report version aliases
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/915
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Backend plugins can now return an `aliases` table from `BackendListVersions`, so a registry's moving names resolve to real versions. This follows discussion jdx/mise#14714.

Before, `"mise-ghcup:ghc" = "recommended"` passed the literal string to the plugin. It installed into `installs/.../recommended`, never followed the tag when it moved, and `mise ls` and the lockfile showed `recommended` instead of a version.

```lua
return {
  versions = { "9.8.4", "9.10.3", "9.14.1" },
  aliases = { recommended = "9.10.3" },
}
```

With that, `ghc@recommended` resolves to `9.10.3`, installs into `9.10.3/`, and the lockfile records `9.10.3`.

- Config-defined aliases still win; the vfox backend implements `resolve_dynamic_alias`, which is asked last.
- Aliases are cached like the version list, and offline an expired cache still answers.
- Only names that don't start with a digit, aren't `latest`/`system`, and contain no `:` are looked up, so pinned versions cost nothing extra.
- `aliases` is a top-level optional field, so older mise ignores it and plugins can adopt it right away.

Documented in the backend plugin guide, with unit tests and an e2e test (`e2e/backend/test_vfox_backend_aliases`).

Co-authored-by the discussion author, cprecioso.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/914
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With the embedded aube installer, `allow_builds = ["re2"]` also ran the install scripts of every package on aube's bundled trusted-dependencies list (368 packages, a snapshot of pnpm's list), such as `dtrace-provider`. The docs say "Approve specific packages with `allow_builds`", so the list should approve exactly what it names.

```toml
"npm:renovate" = { version = "44.161.2", allow_builds = ["re2"] }
```

For a package list, mise now writes `useDefaultTrustedDependencies = false` into the install's aube config, so only `re2` builds. `allow_builds = true` and the no-option default are unchanged.

It needs aube 2.8.0, which adds that setting, so this also bumps the embedded aube crates. A new e2e (`test_npm_allow_builds_exact`) checks that node-pty, which is on aube's trust list, no longer builds when `allow_builds` names a different package.

Fixes #14707

title: fix(vfox): keep symlinks when extracting zip archives
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/913
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Zip archives downloaded by a tool plugin (`PreInstall` returning a `.zip` url) lost their symlinks: entries like `bin/npm -> ../lib/node_modules/npm/bin/npm-cli.js` were written as regular files containing the link target, so the installed tool failed with `No such file or directory`. The `http:` backend and tarballs were not affected.

vfox now extracts zips with `ZipArchive::extract`, the same call the `http:` backend uses. Symlinks are created, and links that resolve outside the install directory are still rejected, so the protection from #14577 is kept.

Adds a unit test that extracts a zip containing a symlink and checks the link survives.

Fixes #14719

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes archive extraction and symlink validation on the install path; mistakes could break installs or weaken zip slip protections, though behavior is covered by targeted Unix tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **ZIP installs from vfox plugins now keep symlinks** instead of turning them into plain files with the link target as contents (e.g. `bin/npm` → `../lib/...`), which broke tools that rely on those links.
> 
> Extraction for `.zip` archives switches from `xx::archive::unzip` to the `zip` crate’s `ZipArchive::extract`, aligned with the `http:` backend behavior. After the usual top-level directory strip, **`ensure_symlinks_stay_within`** re-validates every symlink (including chains and paths through linked dirs) so nothing resolves outside the install tree; failed installs are rolled back by deleting the partial install directory.

title: fix(bootstrap): pin compose service references before hashing
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/912
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.compose]` projects no longer report drift forever when a service uses a `service:` reference.

With this compose file, `mise bootstrap compose status` planned an `update` on every run even though compose considered everything up to date:

```yaml
services:
  vpn:
    image: busybox
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
  app:
    image: busybox
    command: ["sleep", "infinity"]
    network_mode: service:vpn
```

`compose config --hash` hashes `network_mode: service:vpn` as written, but when compose creates the container it first resolves the reference to `container:<vpn id>` and stamps the hash of that. The two sides could never match. The same applies to `ipc: service:`, `pid: service:` and `volumes_from`.

mise now reads `compose config --format json`, and for any service using such a reference writes a temporary override file that pins it to the running container's id before asking compose for the desired hash. Projects that don't use service references take the same path as before (plus one extra `config` call).

Pinning needs an explicit `files` list: passing the override as `--file` turns off compose's own file discovery (`COMPOSE_FILE`, `.env`, override files), and mise doesn't re-implement that. Projects without `files` hash as before, and the docs say so.

Fixes #14706

## Testing

- unit test for the override generation
- `e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_compose` (fake compose now answers `config --format json`)
- not run against a real docker engine

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes compose drift detection and inspection command ordering for running projects; incorrect pinning could hide real config changes or still mis-detect when `files` is unset or `volumes_from` is used.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes false **update** drift in `[bootstrap.compose]` when services use **`network_mode` / `ipc` / `pid: service:…`** references. Compose hashes those fields after resolving them to **`container:<id>`**, while `compose config --hash` used the unresolved `service:` form, so mise could never see a converged project.
> 
> Desired hashes are now computed via **`desired_config_hashes`**: after loading running containers (including **one-off** flags and **names** for replica selection), mise may emit a **temporary override** that pins `service:` refs to the same container ids Compose uses, then runs **`config --hash`** with that override. Pinning only runs when **`files`** is set explicitly, because an extra `--file` disables Compose’s own file discovery; without `files`, behavior stays the old hash path (and docs note ongoing drift). **`volumes_from`** service refs are still not pin-able.
> 
> Adds a unit test for override generation, extends compose **e2e*

title: feat(plugins): accept vfox-backend: for packslip plugin sources
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/910
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

vfox backend plugins can now be installed from a signed packslip archive, using the `vfox-backend:` prefix. Previously `mise plugins install vfox-backend:foo 'packslip:owner/repo#1.0.0'` failed with `packslip plugin sources require the vfox plugin type`, while the same entry in `[plugins]` resolved to the backend type and then hit a similar rejection.

```sh
mise plugins install vfox-backend:my-backend 'packslip:your-org/my-backend#1.0.0'
```

```toml
[plugins]
"vfox-backend:my-backend" = "packslip:your-org/my-backend#1.0.0"
```

The CLI and `[plugins]` now agree. An explicit `asdf:` or `package:` prefix is still rejected, and the error now says "vfox or vfox-backend".

The archive contract is unchanged: a backend plugin's archive still declares `extensions.mise.plugin = "vfox"`, since that names the archive format. mise tells a backend plugin apart by `hooks/backend_install.lua`. Both docs pages say so.

Closes discussion #14718.

## Validation

- `test_plugins_packslip` and `test_plugins_packslip_unprefixed` pass. The unprefixed test now covers the `vfox-backend:` prefix on the CLI and in `[plugins]`.
- The signed fixture is a tool plugin, not a backend, so the e2e covers prefix acceptance only. A signed backend fixture can't be produced locally.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(dotfiles): don't warn on an entry with only enabled = false
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/909
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Turning off an inherited `[dotfiles]` entry with only `enabled = false` printed a warning on every command that read `[dotfiles]`, even though the entry was disabled correctly:

```toml
# config.toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/foo" = {}

# config.local.toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/foo" = { enabled = false }
```

```console
$ mise dot status
mise WARN  [dotfiles]: "~/.config".foo: no recognized operation (block, source, or line), ignoring entry
```

The edit parser only treated a table as a whole-file entry when it was empty or held a whole-file key like `mode` or `source`, so `{ enabled = false }` was read as a block/line edit of `~/.config` with id `foo`. A table whose only key is `enabled` is now a whole-file entry, matching the reference's description of `enabled = false`. Other tables with no recognized operation, such as a misspelled `line`, still warn.

Note: edit entries (`path/id`) have no `enabled` handling, so an `enabled`-only table under an edit key is now ignored silently instead of warned about.

Reported in jdx/mise#14721 (thanks @ponko2). Added a unit test; the `mise-system` edits tests pass.

Co-authored-by: ponko2 <901860+ponko2@users.noreply.github.com>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.299.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow parser change in dotfiles edit classification with a unit test; no auth, security, or data-path impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes spurious `[dotfiles]` warnings when a local config disables an inherited whole-file entry with only `{ enabled = false }`.
> 
> The edit-entry classifier in `edit_entry_from_toml` now treats a table whose sole key is `enabled` as a **whole-file** override (same as an empty table or one with `mode`/`source`), so it is skipped by the edit parser instead of being misread as a `path/id` block/line edit and failing with “no recognized operation”. Invalid edit tables (e.g. a typo like `line`) still warn as before.
> 
> A unit test asserts that `enabled = false` alone is not parsed as an edit.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 46b15e3fe8fa4037d8aef9dab179379d2eb9b219. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(ci): stop render:help failing when markdown-magic scans target/
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/908
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `lint` job in CI intermittently fails in `mise run render` with an error like this:

```
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '.../target/debug/deps/serde_derive-....rcgu.o'
```

([failing run](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/39244920002/job/118037781515))

`render:help` ran `md-magic` (markdown-magic) with its default `**/**.md` glob, which walks the whole tree including `target/`. When a cargo step in the same job deleted an object file mid-walk, `lstat` threw and the job failed.

No markdown file in the repo contains a markdown-magic block, so the step does nothing. Running `md-magic` locally reports `Files with transforms: 0` and changes no files. This PR removes the step from `render:help`. It also removes the `wait_for = ["render:usage"]` that existed only so markdown-magic would not scan `docs/cli` while it was being replaced.

`render:help` now only runs `mise render-help`. The failing job can't be re-run until its run finishes, so CI on this PR is the check.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Build-task-only change; drops a no-op doc step and does not alter runtime or release behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes intermittent CI failures in `mise run render` by simplifying the **`render:help`** task.
> 
> **`render:help`** now only runs `mise render-help` (README / `cli_commands.ts` generation). The **`markdown-magic`** (`md-magic`) step is removed because it scanned `**/**.md` across the repo (including `target/`) and could race with Cargo deleting build artifacts, and no repo markdown uses markdown-magic blocks anyway.
> 
> The **`wait_for = ["render:usage"]`** guard is also removed; it existed only to avoid `md-magic` walking `docs/cli` while `render:usage` was replacing that directory.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 1b2d5b59310353f8e10e54e320ba2678398cd7c3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: fix(docs): render mise.toml editor hover card code as inline pills
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/907
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

Hover cards and autocomplete info popups in the mise.toml editor on the docs site showed every inline `code` span (the key path, `value`, `default`, `required`, ...) as a full-width block with large left padding. They now render as small inline pills, as intended.

The editor sits inside a code block, so VitePress's `.vp-doc [class*='language-'] code` rule (block display, 24px padding, full width) was overriding the card's own `code` styles. The card styles are now scoped under `.mise-toml-editor` and set `display: inline` explicitly.

Not rendered locally (docs dependencies aren't installed in this worktree), so worth a look at the preview on a page with a hover-enabled mise.toml block.

title: feat(config): add read_json, read_yaml and read_toml template functions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/902
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tool versions are often already recorded in another file, such as `Pulumi.yaml`, `package.json` or `pyproject.toml`, and today the same version has to be copied into `mise.toml` and kept in sync by hand. `read_json()`, `read_yaml()` and `read_toml()` parse a file and return its contents as a value, so a template can pick one entry out of it:

```toml
[tools]
node = "{{ read_json(path='package.json')['volta']['node'] }}"
pnpm = "{{ read_json(path='package.json')['packageManager'] | split(pat='@') | last }}"
pulumi = "{{ read_yaml(path='Pulumi.yaml')['requiredPulumiVersion'] }}"
mytool = "{{ read_toml(path='pyproject.toml')['tool']['mytool']['version'] }}"
```

Behavior:

- Relative paths resolve from the config file's directory, like `read_file()`.
- A file that cannot be read or parsed fails with an error naming the function and file, instead of passing raw text through.
- A key that is not there is a render error; `| default(value="...")` gives a fallback.
- TOML dates are strings. YAML reads like the rest of mise, so `yes` and `on` stay strings; quote versions such as `"3.270.0"` because an unquoted `3.270` is a number and renders as `3.27`.
- Like `read_file()`, they need a trusted config and are refused in safe mode, in `.miserc.toml` and in OCI dotfile templates.

Tera does not parse `.key` directly after a call, so use brackets, or bind the result with `set` to use `.key` on it. The bracket form needs the default Tera v2 engine; the deprecated `tera_v1` setting only gets the functions, not that syntax.

Based on the request in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14704. This takes the object-returning approach instead of the proposed `json_query`/`yaml_query`/`toml_query` filters, so no second path language is needed.

Tested with unit tests (including safe mode) and an e2e test that renders the examples above.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.299.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Templates gain new host file read/parse paths; risk is mitigated by the same trust, safe-mode, OCI, and `.miserc.toml` restrictions as `read_file()`.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`read_json`**, **`read_yaml`**, and **`read_toml`** Tera functions so templates can load structured config from disk (relative to the config file) and index into the parsed value with brackets or `set` + dot notation, instead of duplicating versions in `mise.toml`.
> 
> Implementation mirrors **`read_file`**: shared **`read_structured`** parsing (JSON/YAML via mise YAML, TOML with datetimes as strings), **`track_tera_file`**, and registration on both Tera v1/v2. The new functions are **disabled in safe mode**, **blocked in OCI dotfile rendering** (same message as `read_file`), and documented alongside existing trust/safe-mode rules. Unit tests

title: fix(http): retry the install rename on Windows when antivirus holds the files
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/901
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14702

`mise install` of a very large archive over `http:` (for example `http:flutter`, a ~1.9 GB zip) on a Windows runner could fail with `Access is denied. (os error 5)` right after extraction. Since the http backend started extracting straight into the install directory, the final move into place was a bare `std::fs::rename`, which fails while antivirus is still scanning the freshly written files and had no retry.

The http backend now moves the extracted directory with `file::rename`, which retries transient `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` / `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` and adds the source and destination paths to the error. The Windows retry window grows from about 1.5s to about a minute (20 attempts, backoff capped at 5s), which only costs time when the rename is already failing.

Not verified on Windows; I could not reproduce the runner's antivirus behavior locally.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are scoped to Windows rename retries and HTTP backend finalization; successful renames behave the same, with longer waits only when rename already fails.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Windows HTTP installs** can fail right after extracting very large archives when antivirus still holds file locks during the final directory rename. This PR routes those moves through `file::rename` instead of `std::fs::rename`, so transient `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` / `ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION` are retried with richer errors (paths included).
> 
> The Windows retry policy in `do_rename` is widened: **20 attempts** (was 5) with exponential backoff **capped at 5 seconds** per wait (~one minute total vs ~1.5s before), aimed at multi‑GB extractions like Flutter. The HTTP backend uses this for both cache promotion and install-path finalization after extraction.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d45e5fb64635d70466b47e21dd55fb568ff65ca0. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(config): apply the default minimum_release_age to every backend
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/900
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The 24h `minimum_release_age` default only applied to backends that report release dates (aqua, cargo, core, forgejo, gem, github, gitlab, go, npm, packslip, pypi, spm, ubi). Tools from asdf, vfox, conda, dotnet, http and s3 got no cutoff at all, even when they could be dated.

Now the default applies to every backend:

```toml
# mise.toml: no minimum_release_age configured
[tools]
"conda:ffmpeg" = "latest"   # was: newest version immediately; now: held back 24h
```

A backend can only hold back versions it knows a date for. When `mise install`, `mise upgrade` or `mise use` is about to install a version that has none (see the stacked #14694), mise warns once and names the escape hatch:

```
WARN  asdf:tiny@3.1.0 has no release date, so the ... cutoff cannot be checked and it is allowed (exclude it with minimum_release_age_excludes to silence this)
```

So a tool is either held back or flagged, never silently unprotected. Exclude a tool or backend with `minimum_release_age_excludes`, or turn the delay off with `minimum_release_age = "0s"`.

**Stacked on #14694.** Merge after it, and ideally after the backends that gain dates (#14691, #14692, #14693, #14695, #14696, #14697).

Behavior to know about: a brand-new tool whose only version is under 24h old now resolves to "no versions found", as it already does on aqua and github.

Refs #14689

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default version resolution and install warnings for every backend type; tools on backends that rarely expose release dates may see new warnings or “no versions” when only very fresh releases exist.
> 
> **Overview**
> Extends the built-in **24h `minimum_release_age`** so it applies to **all backends** (asdf, vfox, conda, `http:`, etc.), not only the previous whitelist. Opt out per tool via **`minimum_release_age_excludes`**, or globally with **`minimum_release_age = "0s"`**.
> 
> Cutoff enforcement is unchanged in spirit: only versions with known release dates are held back. Versions without dates still resolve, but **`mise install` / upgrade / use** can emit a **one-time warning** that the cutoff could not be verified, with clearer text when the date lookup failed and a pointer to exclusions. **Exact version pins** the user named are not flagged; **`latest`** and rolling channels still are.
> 
> Resolution logic in **`src/backend/mod.rs`** is tightened so partial listings and the latest-stable fast path still respect the cutoff (on-demand date fetch for undated stable picks, undated plugin stable choices kept rather than forcing a full-list fallback). Docs and **`settings.toml`** now describe “every backend” and the undated-version behavior.

title: feat(backend): serve every backend's version list from the versions host
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/899
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## What changes

Version lists for `npm:`, `pipx:`, `cargo:`, `gem:`, `go:`, `dotnet:` and `spm:` tools, and for http/s3 tools with a `version_list_url`, can now come from [mise-versions](https://mise-versions.jdx.dev) like every other registry tool. Before, an allowlist kept them on their own source. That allowlist came from a stale hosted Flutter list (#9245). The host cache TTL is now the tool's `minimum_release_age` less an hour (1–24h), so a stale list cannot hide anything the cutoff would not already hide.

This keeps the sources consistent and lets mise-versions' first-seen `created_at` stamps give dates to backends that return none (http, vfox). See #14689.

## When the host is still skipped

A source you redirect lists other versions than the public one, so mise lists from it directly:

| Backend | Redirect that skips the host |
| --- | --- |
| npm | registry from `.npmrc` / `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`, including scoped registries; any registry under `npm.shell_out` |
| pipx | `pypi.registry_url` / `pipx.registry_url` |
| go | `GOPROXY`, `GOPRIVATE` or `GONOPROXY` other than the default |
| cargo | `cargo.registry_name` |
| gem | a `source` tool option, or a primary `gem sources` entry other than rubygems.org |
| conda | always (versions depend on the platform, which the host's one list cannot describe) |
| dotnet | `dotnet.registry_url` |
| s3 | `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` / `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` |
| http, s3, spm, all | local listing tool options (`version_list_url`, `api_url`, `endpoint`, ...) |

The existing guards stay: registry-default backend only, no local listing option overrides, no custom aqua registry, and `use_versions_host`. Skipping is traced (`MISE_TRACE=1`): "local context affects remote version listing".

Set `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0` (or `use_versions_host = false`) to list from the source for everything.

## Other changes

- `conda` still lists from its channel, but through the shared cache (keyed by channel and platform) instead of bypassing it.
- Go and pipx always had a cache context, which blocked the host even for the default source. They now have one only for a non-default source.
- `versions_host_tool` / `versions_host_skip_reason` no longer take listing options.

## Host data

Every registry tool except `aws-cli`, `chromedriver`, `sui`, `tiny` and `vim` has a list on the host; jdx/mise-versions#389 restores those, and until then they fall back to their own source.

## Tests

Unit tests cover each formerly excluded backend type using the host by default and the redirected-source contexts; `e2e/cli/test_ls_remote_versions_host_redirected_source` checks a redirected PyPI index bypasses the host. `test_conda*`, `test_gem_source` and the versions-host cache e2e tests pass. `backend/test_npm` could not run here (no `npm`).

title: registry: add release dates to dart, flutter, nim, julia and other http tools
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/898
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Ten http-backed registry tools listed versions without release dates, so `minimum_release_age` could not hold any of their releases back (#14689). They now report a `created_at` per version, using the `version_date_expr` / `version_date_url` / `version_date_next_expr` options from #14696 (this PR is stacked on it).

`mise ls-remote --json <tool>` was checked for each:

| Tool | Date source | Undated versions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dart | GCS `VERSION` object `timeCreated`, two pages | 0 of 180 |
| flutter | `release_date` in the manifest already used for versions | 0 of 195 |
| nomad-pack, sentinel, tfc-agent | HashiCorp releases API `timestamp_created`, paged 20 at a time | 0 |
| nim | build date in each release's nightlies download path on install.html | 0 of 41 |
| julia | `last-modified` in versions.json | 104 of 109 |
| android-cli | `Date` of the apt repo's Release file (never earlier than the build it lists) | 0 |
| cursor-agent (also `cursor-cli`) | the build date every version starts with | 0 |
| twg | `publishedAt` in manifest.json | 0 |

Julia's versions.json only started recording `last-modified` in August 2026, so releases before that, and prereleases, stay undated; every release since is dated.

Not dateable from what these upstreams publish:

- `oc`, `openshift-install`: the mirror's directory index shows no date for version folders (`datetime=""`), and the release controller and Cincinnati graph carry none. Dating them would take one request per version (about 1,200).
- `grok`: only `https://x.ai/cli/stable` (a bare version) is published, and the bucket cannot be listed anonymously.
- `muse`: the channel document and manifest carry no date.

Old mise clients read the floating registry too; they ignore the new options (checked with 2026.10.11).

Tested with `mise run test:e2e cli/test_registry cli/test_registry_floating`.

title: fix(core): date more ruby, python and rust versions so minimum_release_age applies
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/897
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Part of #14689. `minimum_release_age` keeps any version that has no release date, so every undated ruby, python or rust version silently bypassed the cooldown. This gives those versions real dates, and makes `rust@stable` honor the cooldown.

With the mise-versions host off (`MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0`), `ls-remote --json` undated counts go from:

| tool | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ruby | 640 of 699 | 261 of 699 |
| python | 40 of 1095 | 0 of 1095 |
| rust | 4 of 161 | 0 of 161 |

**rust**: `stable` now resolves to the newest stable release that is old enough.

```
$ mise install -n rust@stable --minimum-release-age 30d
mise rust@1.98.1   ⇢ would install      # 1.99.1 without the cutoff
```

`nightly-YYYY-MM-DD` is dated from its own name. `stable`, `beta` and `nightly` carry no release date of their own, so each takes the date of the build its channel manifest points at right now. Under an explicit cutoff in the past (not the built-in 24h default, and not `--minimum-release-age 0s`), each channel resolves to what it pointed at then:

```
$ mise install -n rust@beta --minimum-release-age 30d
mise rust@beta-2026-09-18   ⇢ would install
$ mise install -n rust@nightly --minimum-release-age 30d
mise rust@nightly-2026-09-19   ⇢ would install
```

`beta` and `nightly` take the newest dated build that exists (up to 90 and 30 days back) from a day before the cutoff's day (the current build, pinned by date, when it is already old enough), and error if none does. This needs the network, so offline resolution leaves the channel as written, and so does prefer-offline for `beta` and `nightly` in a config file (a command-line request still applies the cutoff). This adds a `Backend::channel_for_cutoff` hook (default `None`) used in `ToolVersion::resolve`, so it touches `src/backend/mod.rs` and `src/toolset/tool_version.rs`.

**python**: `3.13.0`, `3.14.5`, `3.15.0` and the pypy definitions had no date because `git log --diff-filter=A` does not count a definition git detects as a rename or copy (`3.15.0` is a rename of `3.15.0rc3`). `--no-renames` fixes it.

**ruby**: MRI versions without a ruby/ruby GitHub release now use ruby-lang.org's release index. jruby uses Maven Central's `jruby-dist` listing (every release back to 1.7). truffleruby and `truffleruby+graalvm` use oracle/truffleruby's GitHub releases.

Still undated, because nothing publishes a date for them: rolling `-dev` definitions, rubinius, mruby, picoruby, ree, and some very old MRI patch levels (1.8.x/1.9.x).

Unit tests cover the ruby-lang index, Maven listing and truffleruby tag parsing, rust channel dating, and python's rename case against a real temporary git repo. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(http): read release dates for http versions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/896
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`http:` tools could not carry release dates, so every version an http tool listed was undated, and `minimum_release_age` never held any of them back (#14689). Two new options let an http tool say when each version was published.

```toml
[tools."http:my-tool"]
version = "latest"
url = "https://example.com/releases/my-tool-v{{ version }}.tar.gz"
version_list_url = "https://example.com/releases.json"
version_expr = 'map(fromJSON(body).releases, { #.version })'
version_date_expr = 'map(fromJSON(body).releases, { [#.version, #.published_at] })'
```

With that, `mise ls-remote --json http:my-tool` reports a `created_at` for each version, and the cooldown applies to them.

- `version_date_expr` is an expr-lang expression that sees `body` (the `version_list_url` response), `bodies` and `versions`, and returns `[version, date]` pairs or a map of version to date. Dates may be RFC 3339, `YYYY-MM-DD`, or an HTTP date such as a `Last-Modified` value (normalized to RFC 3339). Versions it leaves out stay undated; dates mise cannot read are skipped with a warning.
- `version_date_url` fetches the dates from a different URL than the version list. For listings that come in pages (GCS object listings, the HashiCorp releases API), `version_date_next_expr` sees each page as `body` and its address as `url` and returns the next page's address, or `nil` after the last. `bodies` holds every page. The next page must be on the same host, because the request `headers` follow every request, and mise stops after 100 pages.

Existing configs behave as before: without `version_date_expr` nothing changes. `version_date_url` or `version_date_next_expr` without `version_date_expr` is an error rather than a silent no-op. The s3 backend is untouched.

The registry entries that can use this follow in a stacked PR.

Tested with unit tests for the expression shapes and date forms, and `e2e/backend/test_http_version_dates` (dates from the list body, from a paged second document, the cross-host refusal, and the orphan-option error). Documented in the http backend page; `schema/mise.json` regenerated with `mise run render:schema`. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(vfox): let plugins report release dates for minimum_release_age
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/895
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Part of jdx/mise#14689. `minimum_release_age` and `--before` can only hide a version mise knows the release date of, and a vfox plugin had no way to report one. Every vfox-backed registry tool therefore bypassed the cooldown silently. This adds the plugin contract; plugins can adopt it separately.

A tool plugin's `Available` hook can now return `created_at` (RFC 3339) on each entry:

```lua
function PLUGIN:Available(ctx)
  return {
    { version = "3.0.0", created_at = "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z" },
    { version = "2.0.0", created_at = "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z" },
  }
end
```

A backend plugin's `BackendListVersions` hook can return the same table form in `versions`. Plain strings still work, and a list can mix both, so existing plugins are unaffected.

```lua
return { versions = { "0.9.0", { version = "1.0.0", created_at = "2025-06-01T00:00:00Z" } } }
```

With `minimum_release_age = "30d"` or `mise ls-remote --before 2026-01-01`, dated versions newer than the cutoff are hidden. A missing date, or one that is not an absolute RFC 3339 timestamp, leaves that version undated (with a trace message) rather than failing the listing. Undated versions are still never hidden, as before.

## Plugins

The plugin changes live upstream, not in this PR: 30 `jdx/vfox-*` repos now return `created_at` where their source exposes a release date. mise's vendored copies pick them up on the next sync. Version sets and ordering are unchanged, and a failed date lookup leaves versions undated instead of failing the listing. Coverage is partial for bpkg, chezscheme, clojure, v, scala 2.x and yarn Berry tags not on npm.

No usable per-version date exists for ag, aapt2, android-sdk, chicken, chromedriver, gcc-arm-none-eabi and mysql, and tiny is a hard-coded list.

## Changes

- `crates/vfox`: `AvailableVersion.created_at`, and a new public `BackendVersion { version, created_at }`. `Vfox::backend_list_versions` now returns `Vec<BackendVersion>` instead of `Vec<String>`; mise is the only caller.
- `src/backend/vfox.rs`: maps both hooks into `VersionInfo.created_at`.
- Docs: tool and backend plugin development pages, plus the Lua type stubs.

## Tests

- Lua unit tests for both hooks (date present, absent, plain strings, mixed entries).
- `e2e/backend/test_vfox_release_dates`: a tool plugin and a backend plugin where a cutoff hides the too-new version and keeps invalid or undated ones.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise --cd crates/vfox run lint` pass.

title: fix(backend): warn when minimum_release_age cannot check a version's date
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/894
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With `minimum_release_age` set, a backend that returns no release date for a version lets that version through the cutoff, and nothing says so. For example, `mise upgrade --bump` picked an `aws-cli` version inside a `14d` cooldown because aqua lists tag-only repositories without dates.

Now `mise install`, `mise upgrade` and `mise use` print a one-time warning when the version they are about to install was picked without a release date:

```
WARN  aqua:aws/aws-cli@2.38.1 has no release date, so the 2026-10-05T... cutoff cannot be checked and it is allowed
```

The warning is deliberately not printed by `mise env`, `mise ls`, `mise outdated` or `mise ls-remote`, which can run on every shell prompt: resolution only records the undated pick, and the install path prints it.

Behavior is otherwise unchanged: undated versions are still allowed (many backends cannot date anything, and excluding them would break those tools). This only makes the gap visible. The backends that return no dates are being fixed separately; the warning then only appears for tools that remain undated.

Refs #14689

title: fix(conda): report release dates so minimum_release_age applies
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/893
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`conda:` tools (vim, ffmpeg, postgres, redis, sqlite, and the other registry tools that use conda) returned no release dates, so `minimum_release_age` could not hide any of their versions: every version looked old enough and a brand-new release was installable immediately. Part of jdx/mise#14689.

`mise ls-remote --json conda:vim` now reports `created_at` for each version:

```json
{"version":"9.2.1054","created_at":"2026-09-10T18:21:11.21Z"}
```

Each version has many builds and platform records in the channel's repodata, each with its own date. The channel's `indexed_timestamp` (when the channel first listed the package) is preferred over the builder-supplied build `timestamp`, and the earliest date across a version's records is used, since that is when the version first became available, which is the date a cooldown should judge (later builds are rebuilds of an already-released version). Records without a timestamp stay undated, as before.

Tests: unit tests cover earliest-wins and undated records, and that `minimum_release_age` filtering hides a too-new conda version. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean, and `ls-remote --json` was checked live for `conda:vim` and `conda:ffmpeg`.

title: fix(core): date dotnet, deno and erlang versions for minimum_release_age
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/892
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`minimum_release_age` keeps undated versions (`filter_by_date`), so tools whose version list carries no dates silently bypass the cooldown (#14689). The core dotnet, deno and erlang plugins listed no dates at all. They now do:

- **dotnet**: each SDK takes the `release-date` of the release entry in Microsoft's releases index that first shipped it (runtime-only entries repeat earlier SDKs, so the earliest date wins).
- **deno**: the version list still comes from deno.com, dated from the GitHub releases of `denoland/deno`.
- **erlang** (default kerl path): the version list still comes from `kerl list releases all`, dated from the GitHub releases of `erlang/otp` (`OTP-x.y` tags). The `erlang_compile=false` path was already dated.

Release listings go through the existing GitHub helpers, so with the versions host enabled (default) this is one cached request per tool and every version is dated. Checked live with `mise ls-remote --json`: dotnet 591/591, deno 324/324, erlang 547/547 dated.

Limitation: with `use_versions_host = false`, the direct GitHub API returns only the newest releases unless `MISE_LIST_ALL_VERSIONS` is set. Older versions (225 of 324 for deno, 447 of 547 for erlang, all more than a year old) stay undated. If GitHub can't be reached, a warning is logged and versions stay undated rather than failing `ls-remote`.

Tests cover the parsing and that a cutoff hides a too-new version for each plugin.

title: fix(aqua): date github_tag versions so minimum_release_age applies
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/891
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`minimum_release_age` did not apply to aqua packages that take their versions from git tags (`version_source: github_tag`), such as `aws/aws-cli`, `cockroachdb/cockroach`, `docker/cli` and `apache/tomcat`. Their versions had no release date, and an undated version counts as old enough, so a version released minutes ago was installable under any cutoff. Part of jdx/mise#14689.

```sh
mise ls-remote --json aqua:aws/aws-cli
# before: no created_at on any version
# after:  {"version": "2.38.1", "created_at": "2026-10-14T18:10:16Z", ...}
```

mise now takes the dates mise-versions already has for the tags, at the same request cost as the undated listing. A tag without a date from mise-versions is dated on demand: when a cutoff hides the version resolution is about to pick, mise looks up that one tag's commit date.

I did not reuse `github::list_tags_with_dates`: it fetches one commit per tag, which is about 3,500 requests for aws-cli. Single-tag lookups cost one request per version the cutoff actually hides.

Checked with a build from this branch: `aqua:aws/aws-cli`, `aqua:docker/cli` and `aqua:cockroachdb/cockroach` list every version with a date. Aqua packages that use releases are untouched. Install-time tag resolution still reads names only.

They now show a short description, taken from the matching bootstrap docs page and checked against the code that reads the key.

The keys covered are the entries and fields of:

- `[bootstrap.files]`, `[bootstrap.directories]`, `[bootstrap.services]`, `[bootstrap.compose]`, `[bootstrap.repos]`, `[bootstrap.remote.hosts]`, `[bootstrap.groups]` and `[bootstrap.users]`

For example, an editor now explains these keys:

```toml
[bootstrap.files."/etc/example.conf"]
source = "./files/example.conf" # file to copy the content from; a relative path resolves from the declaring config's directory and ~/ from your home directory

title: docs(config): turn the mise.toml reference into a key explorer
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/888
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The [mise.toml reference](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/reference.html) put 1,076 keys in one long column of nested lists, written as dotted paths like `tasks.<name>.depends`. It was hard to see the overall structure or find your way back out of a deep key. About 20% of keys also had no description, including `tasks.<name>.depends`, `sources`, `outputs`, `env._.file` and the `[hooks]` events.

### A key explorer

The page is now a two-pane explorer:

- **Left:** a tree of every key, grouped by topic (Tools, Environment, Tasks, Hooks and shell, Config file, Project services, Machine setup, and Deprecated at the end), with a key count on each branch. Type to filter, press `/` to focus the filter, and use the arrow keys to move through the tree. The site sidebar is hidden on this page, so the tree is the only left column.
- **Right:** the selected key, with breadcrumbs, type, default, choices, a link to the guide for its section, its child keys as a table, and a `mise.toml` snippet showing where the key goes. For `tasks.<name>.depends` the snippet is:

title: docs: record the landing-page showreel against current mise so its cache fills
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/886
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The landing-page showreel has never made it into the docs cache. Since #14077 and #13910, every run of the docs workflow on main spent about 45 minutes recording on a Namespace runner, failed to record, rendered nothing and still finished green with only a warning: "the showreel was not rendered … the site builds without one" (runs [39144125367](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/39144125367) and [39144813214](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/39144813214)). The cache plumbing itself worked; there was just never a render to keep, so the next run missed again.

## Why recording failed

- #14077 stopped `mise dot track`, `mise dot rollback` and `mise bootstrap --adopt` from asking for confirmation. The recipe still waited for `y/n/enter submit`.
- #13910 made `mise skills sync` print `~/work/api/...` instead of `/home/you/work/api/...`.
- `mise dot rollback` now says `rolled back ~/.zshrc to checkpoint 1; recorded as checkpoint 4, with checkpoint 3 …`, which the recipe anchored as a whole line.

## Changes

- `showreel-capture/steps.json` no longer waits on the removed prompts and matches the current output.
- The reel's scenes (`track`, `bootstrap`) play the take without those prompts. The services prompt in `mise bootstrap` stays on camera. The committed reference captures are re-recorded with mise 2026.10.13.
- `mise use hk@…` now writes `hk = { version = "2.2.0", workflow = "release.yml" }`, which is wider than the card and was folded away with its row. Cards can now keep a named wide row, with its tail faded off the edge like the terminal pane, and packslip's card keeps hk's.
- Install time-lapses now slow down just enough that no elapsed-time text stands still for more than 0.1 s. A fresh recording had a 350 ms gap between two frames, which failed the existing timing test. The render step runs that test against fresh captures, so it could fail the same way on any recording.

## Validation

Recorded all 19 captures locally in Docker (about 4 minutes) and ran `mise run docs:showreel-test` with `SHOWREEL_REQUIRE_CAPTURES=1` and `SHOWREEL_REQUIRE_CHROMIUM=1`: 189 pass, 0 fail. I have not rendered the video (no ffmpeg here), so the hk card's faded row has not been looked at in a rendered frame; the tests check the handoff frames. A render on main after merge is the first full check.

title: ci(release): publish releases staged before install.ps1 existed
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/885
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `publish-version` run for v2026.10.14 failed on an `aws s3api head-object` 404, so `VERSION`, `releases.tsv` and the public installers were never updated for that release.

`publish-version` checks out `main` so recovery works for older tags. v2026.10.14 was built from a release commit that predates #14660, so it never staged `install.ps1`, but `main`'s `publish-version.sh` now requires it.

This makes the three `install.ps1` objects optional: they are verified and promoted only when the release staged them. A release with `install.ps1` still needs all three. Without it, the script logs that the public PowerShell installer is unchanged and carries on.

After this merges, re-run the publish-version workflow for v2026.10.14 (workflow_dispatch, `version=v2026.10.14`).

Tests: two new cases in `scripts/test-install-release-age.py` (release with and without `install.ps1`); all 27 pass.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes release publication paths for public installers on S3; mistakes could skip promoting ps1 or leave stale public installers, but shell installer requirements are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`publish-version.sh` no longer hard-requires `install.ps1`**, so recovery publishes for tags staged before the PowerShell installer existed (e.g. v2026.10.14).
> 
> The script always requires **`install.sh` and its signatures**, then lists S3 under `$TAG/install.ps1`. If that object exists, it also **head-checks and promotes** `install.ps1`, `.sig`, and `.minisig` to the public URLs; otherwise it logs that the public PowerShell installer is unchanged and skips those steps.
> 
> **Tests** in `scripts/test-install-release-age.py` add a `publish_with_staged_keys` helper and cover publish-without-ps1, full ps1 promotion, and failure when staged ps1 is missing a signature (no `s3 cp`).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7b1d975e7aa277368cc0b9578d793b3abb2a77b2. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

* **Tests**
  * Added regression coverage for both publication scenarios and for missing signatures, verifying that incomplete installer assets are not copied.

title: feat(dotnet): add lts and sts version aliases
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/884
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

`dotnet@lts` and `dotnet@sts` were not recognised, so you had to look up which .NET channel is current and write `dotnet@10` yourself, then bump it by hand when the next LTS ships ([discussion 10273](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/10273)). Node hardcodes its `lts` aliases, but a hardcoded .NET table would go stale with every release.

## Change

```toml
[tools]
dotnet = "lts"   # the newest SDK in the current LTS channel (10.0.x today)
```

`lts` and `sts` now follow Microsoft's release index. They pick the newest channel of that type that is in `active` or `maintenance` support, so previews, `go-live` releases and end-of-life channels are skipped, then resolve to an SDK in that channel. `mise latest dotnet@lts` gives `10.0.402` and `dotnet@sts` gives `9.0.319` against today's index.

To make that possible, `Backend` gets an async `resolve_dynamic_alias` hook (default: `None`) that `Config::resolve_alias` asks after config-defined and built-in aliases. A `[tool_alias.dotnet.versions]` entry named `lts` still wins. The channel list is cached under the remote-versions cache duration, so repeat resolutions don't hit the network. Runtime-only installs still need an exact version.

Channel versions are compared numerically as `major.minor` inside the dotnet plugin only; no version ordering is added elsewhere.

## Testing

Unit tests cover channel selection, and the new `e2e/core/test_dotnet_channel_aliases` checks both aliases, that `ls-remote dotnet lts` stays inside the resolved channel, and that a user alias takes precedence. clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

> **Overview**
> Adds **`dotnet@lts`** and **`dotnet@sts`** so SDK version requests track Microsoft’s current LTS/STS channels without hand-updating major versions. Resolution uses the releases index: newest channel of that type in **active** or **maintenance** support (skipping preview, go-live, and EOL), then picks an SDK in that channel; **`[tool_alias.dotnet.versions]`** still overrides built-in names. Runtime-only installs are unchanged and still need exact versions.
>

The dotnet plugin implements it with a cached channel list (including offline use of stale cache), plus **`select_channel`** unit tests and an e2e script for alias shape, **`ls-remote`** scoping, offline behavior, and user alias precedence. title: feat(dotfiles): add dotfiles.windows_symlinks to link files instead of copying on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/883
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On Windows, `symlink-each` copies every file, and `symlink` quietly falls back to a copy when Windows refuses to create the link. Someone who wants their dotfile targets to follow edits to the source had no way to ask for real links, and no way to find out that a link silently became a copy.

`dotfiles.windows_symlinks` (default `false`, env `MISE_DOTFILES_WINDOWS_SYMLINKS`) turns that on:

```toml
[settings.dotfiles]
windows_symlinks = true

[dotfiles]
"~/.config/nvim" = { mode = "symlink-each" }
```

With it on, both `symlink-each` and `symlink` create real file symbolic links, and the apply fails when Windows won't create one (Developer Mode off and not elevated) instead of leaving a copy:

```
cannot link ~/.gitconfig to ~/.dotfiles/.gitconfig; turn on Developer Mode or run elevated, or set dotfiles.windows_symlinks = false
```

With it off, nothing changes: `symlink-each` copies, `symlink` tries a link and falls back to a copy. Directory links are junctions either way, and the setting is ignored on other platforms.

`symlink-each` was kept on the copy path because its state tracking and unapply planner were Unix-only; a link there made unapply demand `--force`. Those now run on Windows when the setting is on. Turning it back off and then running `mise dot unapply` on entries still holding links needs `--force`, which the docs say.

Follow-up to #14654, which made the `symlink-each` messages report copies. Refs #14646.

## Validation

- `mise run lint`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and the `files::` unit tests pass on Linux.
- The Windows branch of `link_path` type-checks against `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` in a scratch crate. It has **not been run on Windows**: the new `link_path_link_never_leaves_a_copy` test and the unapply path with links need a Windows runner.

title: feat(bootstrap): add --prune-dotfiles to remove orphaned dotfiles
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/882
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap --upgrade` applies and upgrades a machine in one command, but removing copied dotfiles whose sources were deleted still needed a separate `mise dot apply --prune`. `mise bootstrap` now takes `--prune-dotfiles` to do both in one run:

```sh
mise bootstrap --upgrade --prune-dotfiles
```

The flag runs the same pruning as `mise dot apply --prune` at the end of the dotfiles phase, before the `post-dotfiles` hook. It removes files that a group deployed but no active entry deploys now: files of a deselected or deleted group, and files a group stopped deploying after a new `exclude` or a deleted source.

- Opt-in; without the flag, bootstrap behaves as before.
- Keeps the existing protections: copies you changed since mise wrote them, unrelated files and source directories stay in place, and the output lists what was removed or skipped.
- Honors `--dry-run` (prints `rm ...`, removes nothing) and phase selection (`--skip dotfiles` skips the prune too).
- Asks before removing on a terminal unless `--yes` is given, like `dot apply --prune`; without a terminal it prunes.
- Runs even when no entries remain, so deleting the last entry still cleans up.
- Fails up front in safe mode when ignored project configs declare dotfiles, as `dot apply --prune` does.

I did not add a per-group `prune = true` setting: pruning is driven by recorded state, so it covers groups that were deselected or removed, and a setting on the group would disappear exactly then.

Not covered: `mise bootstrap remote`/`mise ssh` do not forward the flag.

Tested with a new e2e (`test_bootstrap_dotfiles_prune`) plus the existing dotfiles group and bootstrap e2e tests; clippy is clean.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14677

title: fix(task): keep task commands working when one task's dir template is broken
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/881
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A template error in one task's `dir` made every task command fail, including `mise tasks validate`, which could not report it.

```toml
[tasks.ok]
run = "echo ok"

[tasks.bad]
run = "echo bad"
dir = "{{ nonexistent_var }}"
```

Before, `mise tasks ls`, `mise tasks info ok`, `mise run ok` and `mise tasks validate --json` all failed with a bare `__tera_one_off` error. Now:

- `mise tasks validate --json` reports `invalid-directory-template` for `bad`.
- `ls`, `info ok` and `run ok` keep working. `ls --json` warns and reports a null `dir` for `bad`.
- Using `bad` itself (`run bad`, `info bad`) fails with `failed to render \`dir\` of task bad in <config file>`.

Fixes #14676

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/880
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

Someone running the \`dotnet\` backend against a password-protected Nexus feed could not tell where to put credentials ([discussion 12241](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/12241)). The private-feeds section covered \`NuGet.Config\` for installs but said nothing about the version-listing step, which authenticates separately.

## Change

The private-feeds section of the dotnet backend page now says:

- version listing reads the NuGet service index through mise's HTTP client, which sends [\`netrc\`](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/settings.html#netrc) credentials to matching hosts by default, with an example \`~/.netrc\` entry
- \`dotnet tool install\` does not read netrc, so the feed's credentials also go in \`NuGet.Config\` (or \`dotnet nuget add source\`)

Docs only. I confirmed from the code that \`nuget_search_url\` fetches through \`HTTP_FETCH\`, which applies netrc. I did not test against a real authenticated feed.

+[`netrc`](/configuration/settings.html#netrc) credentials to a matching host
+with HTTP Basic authentication, so a password-protected Nexus or Artifactory
+feed needs a `~/.netrc` entry for it:

+```text
+machine nexus.example.com
+  login myuser
+  password mytoken
+```

+NuGet in `NuGet.Config`, either as a `packageSourceCredentials` entry or
