title: docs(secrets): add setup, CI and migration guidance to the fnox page
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/878
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The [fnox secrets page](https://mise.jdx.dev/environments/secrets/fnox.html) explained every rule but left readers to work out why they would want task grants, how to use a real secret store, and how to run it in CI. This adds that guidance:

- **Why not `[env]`?** A table comparing an `[env]` value (SOPS, age or plain) with an fnox grant: who receives the value, when it is fetched, and redaction.
- **Real provider in the quick start.** A 1Password reference in `fnox.toml`, plus a pointer to fnox's age provider for committed ciphertext.
- **A profile per environment.** `mise.toml` with `profile = "dev"` and `mise.prod.toml` with `profile = "prod"`, so `MISE_ENV=prod mise run deploy` reads production values.
- **Run in CI.** A GitHub Actions workflow that runs `mise run deploy` with `OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN` on the step. It also says that `experimental` must be in the committed `mise.toml` or `MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`, to install the provider CLI with mise, that a task's `raw`/`interactive` setting does not turn off redaction without a terminal, and that mise-action does not mask `mise x --secrets` output.
- **Troubleshooting checklist.** `mise secrets ls`, `mise tasks validate`, `fnox check --all` and `MISE_DEBUG=1`, each checking a different layer.
- **Migration before/after.** A `mise.toml` using `_.fnox-env` next to its `[secrets.fnox]` replacement, plus a note for tasks that wrap `fnox exec`.

The quick start now puts `experimental = true` under `[settings]` in the example `mise.toml`. The old `mise settings experimental=true` wrote only to the global config, so teammates and CI did not get the setting. The sign-in/CI/daemon section now comes before the security reference. All existing anchors are kept.

Validation: `hk check` (oxfmt, markdownlint, llms render), `mise run docs:build` with its link check, and the `schema_matches_parser` test, which checks every new `mise.toml` example against the schema and parser.

title: docs(config): add an interactive mise.toml editor and playground
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/877
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The docs gain a [mise.toml playground](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/playground.html): an editor that knows mise's config schema. Paste or write a `mise.toml`, and it explains each key and catches mistakes as you type. The same editor can replace any TOML example in the docs.

## What it does

- **Hover a key or value** to see its full path, type, description, allowed values, default, and whether it is deprecated or experimental, with a link to that key on the [mise.toml reference](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/reference.html) or, under `[settings]`, the settings page. Hovering a value highlights which of the allowed choices it is.
- **Completion:** on a new line, or with <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Space</kbd>, it offers the keys a table can take, with their types and descriptions, leaving out keys already set. It offers section names after `[`, `true`/`false` and the allowed choices for a value, and backend prefixes such as `"github:` under `[tools]`.
- **Problems as you type:** TOML syntax errors; keys mise does not read, with the key that was likely meant (`jobz` → "did you mean jobs?"); values of the wrong kind (`hide = "yes"` → "expected boolean"); and deprecated keys, struck through.
- **Copy link** puts the config in the page's address, so a config can be shared. Nothing is sent anywhere.

The editor uses the same rules as `mise config explain` to decide which shape a table is in. For example, `port` beside a daemon's `project` is reported as unread, while it is fine on a daemon that runs a command. Its messages match what mise prints.

## In docs pages

Any `toml` block can become an editor by adding `editor` to the fence. Add `readonly` to keep the hover help without editing, and `share` to put the config in the page's URL:

````md
```toml editor
[tools]
node = "24"
```
````

The block is still a `toml` block, so `schema_matches_parser` checks it like every other example. The playground is the only page that uses it for now. Existing examples are unchanged, since most are short excerpts in tabbed code groups. The reference page now links to the playground.

## How it works

- `docs/.vitepress/mise-toml/scan.ts` reads a mise.toml well enough to say where each key and value is and what key path it has, even while it is half written. `smol-toml` checks the syntax.
- `docs/.vitepress/mise-toml/schema.ts` reads `schema/mise.json`. It ports the shape-matching rules of `src/cli/config/explain.rs` (`fits`, shapes chosen by the table's own keys, known keys, the "did you mean" distance). title: refactor(schema): generate the multi-shape task field schemas from declaration types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/876
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The tasks part of `schema/mise.json` is now generated from declaration types in `mise-config`. Seventeen task fields that accept several shapes (a string or a list, a name or a table) took their schema from hand-written JSON functions; each is now a type with doc comments, and `task/schema.rs` goes from 516 to 96 lines. Nothing changes for users: I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json` structurally and they are identical.

For example, `depends`, `depends_post` and `wait_for` take the same shapes and differ only in what they say they do, so they come from one macro:

```rust
task_dependencies!(TaskDepends, "task with args to run before this task");
task_dependencies!(TaskDependsPost, "task with args to run after this task");
task_dependencies!(TaskWaitFor, "task with args to wait for completion first");
```

## What changes for maintainers

- `crates/mise-config/src/task/shapes.rs` holds the types: `alias`, `confirm`, the three dependency fields, `daemons`, `outputs`, `sources`, the task and `[task_config]` caches, `rust_cache`, `output`, `silent`, `run` and `run_windows`, `secrets`, `watch` and the shared `$defs` for dependency items and run entries.
- `TaskDecl` and `TaskConfig` attach them with `schemars(with = ..)`, so the runtime types of the fields (`Vec<TaskDep>`, `Option<TaskConfirm>`, ...) are untouched and nothing parses into the new ones.
- A task's `tools` repeated the key patterns of `[tools]`; they now come from the backend table added in #14669, so a new backend is one row in one place.
- Where a parser has a typed struct, two tests compare its fields with the declared keys: `TaskWatchOptions`, `TaskCacheConfig` (for the task and `[task_config]` caches) and `TaskRustCacheOptions`, and the keys a dependency table reads through `TaskDep`. I checked that both fail when a key is declared that the parser does not read.
- `AGENTS.md` says where each of these lives.

## Validation

- Structural comparison of the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json`: no differences. `schema/miserc.json` is unchanged.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p mise-config` (`schema_files_are_up_to_date` and the two new tests), `cargo test -p mise --lib schema_matches_parser` and `cargo test -p mise --lib task::` (555 tests)
- `mise run test:e2e config/test_schema_ajv config/test_schema_tombi` and a sample of the `tasks/test_task_*` tests covering depends, includes, aliases and `task_config`

Stacked on #14671.

title: refactor(schema): generate the [env] and [vars] schema from declaration types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/875
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[env]` and `[vars]` parts of `schema/mise.json` are now generated from declaration types in `mise-config`, instead of 490 lines of hand-written JSON beside the parser. Nothing changes for users: I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json` structurally and they are identical.

`[env]` accepts a plain value or a table that says what the value is (`value`, `default`, `required`, or an `age`-encrypted value), plus an `_` table of modules (`file`, `path`, `python`, `source`). The parser reads these with visitors, which a derive can't describe, so the schema comes from types next to it. For example, a variable with an encrypted value:

```rust
/// [experimental] age-encrypted environment variable
Age(EnvAgeTable),
```

where the doc comment is the description editors show on hover.

## What changes for maintainers

- `crates/mise-config/src/env/decl.rs` holds the types: one per table shape for `[env]` and `[vars]` (they differ: `[vars]` values are strings, integers or `true`, and a variable may carry a `prompt`), the `_` modules, and the small shared definitions such as `env_value` and `env_required`.
- Nothing parses into them. The parser still reads the options of a variable into `EnvDirectiveOptions`, so a new test checks that the option keys the types declare (`tools`, `redact`, `required`, `expand`, `find_up`, `prompt`) are exactly that struct's fields. I checked that it fails when a key is declared that the parser does not read.
- The schema generator closes every typed object with `additionalProperties: false`, but several `[env]` shapes deliberately leave their other keys open. A new `x-mise-open` marker tells it to skip such an object, and it is removed from the output.
- `AGENTS.md` says where to change these.

## Validation

- Structural comparison of the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json`: no differences. `schema/miserc.json` is unchanged.

title: fix(fmt): keep multiline inline tables intact
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/874
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise fmt` mangled multiline inline tables (TOML 1.1). Comments inside them were hoisted out of the table, and entries after the first lost their indentation. Reported in discussion 14667.

Before, for this config:

```toml
[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents]
# Use the 1Password SSH agent with any SSH client
SSH_AUTH_SOCK = {
  program = "/bin/sh",
  args = ["-c", "true"],
  run_at_load = true,
}
```

`mise fmt` produced:

```toml
# Use the 1Password SSH agent with any SSH client
[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents]
SSH_AUTH_SOCK = {
  program = "/bin/sh",
args = ["-c", "true"],
run_at_load = true,
}
```

(the comment also moved to after the closing brace in the reporter's larger example). Now the table is left exactly as written, and the rest of the file is still formatted and sorted as before.

The cause is in taplo, which rebuilds inline tables without their newlines. `mise fmt` now replaces each multiline inline table with a placeholder string before running taplo and restores the original text afterwards. Single-line inline tables are formatted as before. Multiline tables are preserved verbatim rather than reformatted.

Tested with a new unit test using the reporter's config (output must equal input); `cargo test --bin mise cli::fmt` and `cargo clippy --bin mise --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

Thanks to @ponko2 for the report.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-299_agent.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes only affect `mise fmt` output, not config loading or runtime behavior; placeholder collision is guarded by a unique prefix.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise fmt` no longer destroys multiline inline tables (TOML 1.1).** taplo was collapsing them to a single line, which broke indentation and pulled comments out of the table.
> 
> The formatter now **stashes** each multiline inline table (and arrays that contain one) as a unique placeholder string, runs the existing taplo pass via a new `format_with_taplo` helper, then **restores** the original table text. Single-line inline tables are still normalized by taplo as before.
> 
> Unit tests assert round-trip equality for reporter-style configs, single-line tables with decor-only newlines, and multiline tables inside arrays.

title: refactor(schema): generate the [tools] option schemas from declaration types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/873
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[tools]` part of `schema/mise.json` is now generated from Rust declaration types in `mise-config`. It was the largest hand-written block left: about 1,600 lines of JSON for 22 sets of tool options, a wrapper per backend, six platform tables and the key patterns that pick a backend. Nothing changes for users: I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json` structurally and they are identical.

## What changes for maintainers

A backend's options are now a struct with doc comments, which are the descriptions editors show. For example, adding an option to the `github:` backend is a field:

```rust
pub struct ToolGithubOptions {
    /// api base url, for github enterprise or self-hosted instances
    pub api_url: Option<String>,
    // ...
}
```

`crates/mise-config/src/tools/schema.rs` goes from 1,612 to about 430 lines. It composes the types instead of repeating JSON:

- `BACKENDS` has one row per backend: its key pattern, the option sets that apply and its platform table. The wrappers and the `patternProperties` of `[tools]` come from it.
- `PLATFORM_TABLES` has one row per table of per-platform overrides: which of a backend's options a platform may set.

mise also reads these definitions by name at runtime (`OptionSpec`) to reject unknown tool options, so the types now feed that check too. Their names and contents are unchanged, so it behaves as before.

Repeated shapes got shared types: a name or a table of `glob = new name` for `rename_exe`, a string or a list of strings, an integer or a string for `size` and `strip_components`, and a boolean, a string or a list for the npm `allow_*` options. One option, `version_order`, keeps a small hand-written schema function, because its schema is an enum with no `type`.

A new test, `every_reference_in_the_schema_resolves`, checks that every `$ref` in the generated schemas points at something. The platform tables refer to single options of other definitions by JSON pointer (`#/$defs/tool_http_options/properties/url`), so renaming or removing an option would otherwise leave a dangling reference. I checked that the test fails when a platform table names an option that does not exist.

## Validation

- Structural comparison of the old and new `schema/mise.json` and `schema/mise-task.json`: no differences.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`

pub struct MacosTrackpad {
    /// enable tap to click for built-in and Bluetooth trackpads

  - the declared hook phases must equal mise-system's `BootstrapHookPhase`;

- The schema generator now drops the `format: "double"` that schemars writes for floating-point fields, as it already drops the integer formats, since neither says anything to an editor.
- mise-system gets `schemars` as a dev-dependency, for the macOS test.
- `AGENTS.md` says where these live.

- Structural comparison of the old and new `schema/mise.json`: no differences.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: refactor(schema): generate the [hooks] schema from declaration types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/871
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[hooks]` part of `schema/mise.json` is now generated from declaration types in `mise-config`, instead of 16 hand-written JSON definitions. Nothing changes for users: I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` structurally and they are identical.

A hook can be a command string, `{ run = ... }`, `{ script = ..., shell = ... }`, `{ scripts = [...], shell = ... }` or `{ task = ... }`, and which of those an event accepts differs: `enter`, `leave` and `cd` evaluate a `script` in the active shell when `shell` is set, while `preinstall` and `postinstall` ignore the `shell`. The types now say that directly. For example:

```rust
// The same keys without a `shell` run in a subprocess, which is deprecated in favor of `run`.
pub struct HookSpawnedScriptTable {
    /// deprecated alias for run when an enter/leave/cd hook has no shell
    pub script: HookScripts,
}
```

where the doc comment is the description editors show and the deprecation is carried into the schema.

## What changes for maintainers

- `crates/mise-config/src/hooks/decl.rs` holds the types: one per table shape (`HookRunTableDecl`, `HookCurrentShellScriptTable`, `HookInstallScriptTable`, ...), the unions of them an event accepts (`HookDefinitionItem` for `enter`/`leave`/`cd`, `HookInstallDefinitionItem` for the install events), and `HooksDecl`, which names the five events.
- The parser still reads one table, `HookTable`, for every event, and nothing parses into the new types. Two tests keep them from drifting: one checks that the declaration types name exactly the keys `HookTable` reads, and one checks that `HooksDecl` has an entry for each hook event. The events test uses an exhaustive `match`, so adding a `Hooks` variant fails to compile there until the schema has it.
- `HookScripts` now derives its own schema, replacing the `hook_script_value` definition.
- `AGENTS.md` says where to change hook shapes.

## Validation

title: refactor(schema): generate the [daemons] and [daemon_providers] schema from types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/869
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[daemons]` and `[daemon_providers]` parts of `schema/mise.json` are now generated from declaration types in `mise-config`. Before, they were about 260 lines of hand-written JSON that had to be kept in step with mise-daemons by hand. Nothing changes for users: I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` structurally and they are identical.

For example, adding a key to a preset daemon is now a field with a doc comment:

```rust
pub struct DaemonPresetDecl {
    /// Persistent preset data directory, relative to the declaring project root or absolute. Defaults to mise state storage.
    #[schemars(length(min = 1))]
    pub data_dir: Option<String>,
    // ...
}
```

and the comment is the description editors show on hover.

## What changes for maintainers

- A `[daemons]` entry is one of six shapes. `DaemonDecl` lists them: a bare version string, a command (`run`), a task (`task`), a preset (`preset` and `version`), another project's daemon (`project`) and a shared provider (`provider`). The keys that tell the shapes apart are named in `not` on each type, so a table with both `run` and `task` matches none of them.
- The shared pieces (`daemon_port`, `daemon_proxy`, `daemon_proxy_tls`, `daemon_proxy_idle_timeout`, `daemon_init`) are derived and referenced through `$defs`, as before.
- A definition stays a raw table that mise-daemons reads key by key, and keys it does not know are forwarded to pitchfork. So these types describe a table; nothing parses into them, and there is no parity test as there is for `[dotfiles]` and `[secrets]`. A key added in mise-daemons has to be added to the types too. `AGENTS.md` says so.

## Validation

- Structural comparison of the old and new `schema/mise.json`: no differences.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p mise-config` (`schema_files_are_up_to_date`) and `cargo test -p mise --lib schema_matches_parser`
- `mise run test:e2e config/test_schema_ajv config/test_schema_tombi`

title: fix(rust): list channels when GitHub is unreachable behind a mirror
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/868
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing Rust through a `RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER` / `RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT` mirror (e.g. panamax) on a network that cannot reach GitHub failed with a DNS error, because listing remote versions always queried GitHub's rust-lang/rust releases first.

With a mirror configured, a failed release listing now logs a warning and falls back to the `stable`, `beta` and `nightly` channels, so `mise install rust@stable` can proceed through the mirror. Numbered versions such as `1.80.0` still need the GitHub listing. Without a mirror the error is unchanged.

```toml
[env]
RUSTUP_DIST_SERVER = "https://panamax.internal"
RUSTUP_UPDATE_ROOT = "https://panamax.internal/rustup"

[tools]
rust = "stable"
```

Fixes #14652

title: fix(npm): run allow_builds scripts despite ignore-scripts in .npmrc
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/867
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14647

## Problem

If `~/.npmrc` sets `ignore-scripts=true` (a common hardening setting), the npm backend silently skips lifecycle scripts that `allow_builds` approved. The install reports success, but tools that rely on a build step are broken. For example, `npm:pnpm` with `allow_builds = ["pnpm"]` leaves its `pnpm` bin as the placeholder that `install.js` should have replaced, and running it fails with `SyntaxError: Invalid or unexpected token`.

```toml
[tools]
"npm:pnpm" = { version = "12.10.1", allow_builds = ["pnpm"] }
```

mise already tells the embedded install `ignore_scripts = false` when `allow_builds` is set, but the user's npmrc setting still won.

## Fix

When `allow_builds` is set, mise now also writes `ignoreScripts = false` to the throwaway project's `.config/aube/config.toml`, which takes precedence over the user's `.npmrc`. Tools without `allow_builds` still skip scripts.

## Testing

Extended `test_write_aube_embed_project_emits_aube_config_and_manifest` to assert `ignoreScripts = false` is written. I did not run the full pnpm repro from the issue.

title: feat(install): add a PowerShell installer at mise.run/powershell
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/866
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Windows had no equivalent of `curl https://mise.run | sh`, so installing the official binaries meant a package manager (which can lag a release) or a manual zip download. This adds a PowerShell installer that needs no POSIX shell and works from PowerShell 5.1+ (and from MSYS2/Git Bash via `powershell.exe`):

```powershell
irm https://mise.run/powershell | iex
```

It:

- picks the latest release at least 24h old (same `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE` rule as `install.sh`), or `MISE_VERSION`
- downloads the zip from `mise.jdx.dev`, falling back to GitHub Releases
- verifies it against `SHASUMS256.txt` from GitHub Releases (never the download host) and refuses to install unverified
- installs `mise.exe` and `mise-shim.exe` side by side in `~\.local\bin` (required for `windows_shim_mode = "exe"`)
- adds that directory to the user `Path` without expanding existing `%VARS%`; no admin needed
- is safe to re-run: keeps an equal or newer install, upgrades otherwise, and renames a running `mise.exe` out of the way

Options: `MISE_VERSION`, `MISE_INSTALL_PATH`, `MISE_INSTALL_MODIFY_PATH=0`, `MISE_INSTALL_SHIMS_PATH=1` (also adds the shims dir for cmd.exe), `MISE_INSTALL_FROM_GITHUB=1`. Documented in `docs/installing-mise.md`.

The script is published with each release alongside `install.sh` (with `.sig`/`.minisig`), and the mise.run worker serves it at `/powershell` and `/pwsh`. The worker route only works once a release publishes `install.ps1`.

Closes the request in discussion 14651.

## Testing

Ran the script under PowerShell 7 on Linux (platform guard bypassed, Path editing disabled) against the real 2026.10.12 release, for x64 via the mirror and arm64 via GitHub: checksum verified and both exes installed. Not tested on Windows: the registry Path edit, the running-exe rename, and re-run on an existing install.

Fixes #14648.

`mise lock` (and any other path that resolves a new npm lock) failed when the user's own aube config chose a different lockfile name:

```

mise ERROR No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

With `defaultLockfileFormat = "pnpm"` or `defaultLockfile = "pnpm-lock.yaml"` in `~/.config/aube/config.toml`, the embedded aube wrote `pnpm-lock.yaml` into mise's temporary project, but mise reads `aube-lock.yaml`. Those settings are reasonable for a user's own projects and should not change mise's lock.

The throwaway project's `.config/aube/config.toml` now sets `defaultLockfile = "aube-lock.yaml"`. Project config takes precedence over the user's, and pinning `defaultLockfile` covers both user settings (pinning only `defaultLockfileFormat` would not cover a user's `defaultLockfile`). The same project is used when installing from `mise.lock`, so both paths agree.

title: refactor(schema): generate the [deps] and [secrets] schema from their types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/864
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[deps]` and `[secrets]` parts of `schema/mise.json` are now generated from Rust types, as most of the rest of the schema already is. Before, each was a hand-written JSON block that had to be kept in step with the parser by hand. This is the first step in typing the sections that are still hand-written.

Nothing changes for users: the published schema is the same. I compared the old and new `schema/mise.json` structurally; the only difference is an explicit `additionalProperties: true` on `[secrets]`, which means the same as leaving it out.

## What changes for maintainers

- **`[deps]`:** `DepsDecl` and `DepsProviderDecl` derive `JsonSchema`, and their doc comments are the descriptions editors show. The list of built-in providers (`npm`, `uv`, `git-submodule` and the rest) moves from mise into `mise-config` as `BUILTIN_PROVIDERS`, so the schema and mise's provider code read one list. A new provider has to be added in one place.
- **`[secrets]`:** it still stays raw TOML so a malformed `[secrets]` cannot fail a whole file. Its schema now comes from `SecretsDecl` and `FnoxDecl`. A new test in mise, `the_fnox_keys_match_the_declaration`, checks that the hand-written parser reads exactly the keys the declaration lists, so a key added to one without the other fails a test.
- `AGENTS.md` now says which sections are generated and which are still hand-written.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p mise-config`, which includes `schema_files_are_up_to_date`
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: `schema_matches_parser`, which checks every `toml` block in `docs/` and every e2e config against the schema and the parser, the `deps::` tests, and the new secrets parity test
- `mise run test:e2e config/test_schema_ajv config/test_schema_tombi`

title: fix(install): extract 7z archives when the data dir contains `..`
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/863
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14649

Installing a `.7z` tool failed whenever mise's data dir contained a `..` segment, which is what a localized mise at `tools/mise` gets (`MISE_DATA_DIR=<root>/tools/../.mise`):

```
mise ERROR Failed to install aqua:ip7z/7zip@latest: failed to extract 7z archive: ...
Other("unsafe entry path contains a parent-directory component: E:\\...\\tools\\..\\.mise\\installs\\7zip\\26.04\\7-zip.chm")
```

`sevenz-rust2` rejects any `..` in an entry's destination path, including one inherited from the extraction directory. mise already validates entry names itself, so `un7z` now lexically cleans the destination before joining entries onto it. Such installs now extract normally.

Added a regression test that extracts into `<tmp>/tools/../out_dir`; `cargo test -p mise-util 7z` passes.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to 7z extraction path handling with a regression test; entry-path sanitization is unchanged and canonicalization only runs when `dest` already contains `..`.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **7z tool installs failing** when the extraction directory path includes `..` (for example a localized mise data dir like `tools/../.mise/installs/...`), because `sevenz-rust2` treats any `..` in the final entry path as unsafe even when it only comes from the caller’s `dest`.
> 
> **`un7z`** now detects a `ParentDir` component in `dest`, creates the target directory, **canonicalizes** it, and passes that resolved path into decompression so joined entry paths no longer contain `..`. Archive entry names are still sanitized separately.

title: fix(shim): keep the version tag in the Windows release mise-shim.exe
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/862
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise doctor` and `mise reshim --force` reported the `mise-shim.exe` shipped in the Windows release as older than mise ("it has no version tag"), and no amount of `mise self-update` or reshimming cleared it.

The shim embeds a `mise-shim-version:<release>` tag (and the native-shim marker) as `#[used]` statics, but nothing referenced them. `#[used]` only survives compilation; the MSVC linker's dead-code removal in the LTO `serious` build still dropped them, so the released binary carried no tag. `main` now takes the address of both statics through `black_box`, giving the linker a reference it cannot discard.

After this, `mise-shim.exe` from the next Windows release should carry the tag, so the stale-template warning disappears once mise is updated and `mise reshim --force` is run.

Fixes #14650

Validation: `cargo test -p mise-shim` (new test asserts the built shim contains the tag prefix and marker) and clippy pass on Linux. I could not build the MSVC `serious` profile here, so the Windows release binary itself is unverified.

## Problem

A project with `"packageManager": "pnpm@10.15.0+sha224.…"` in `package.json` can no longer install pnpm:

```
mise ✗ pnpm@10.15.0 · failed: pnpm: option `checksum` is not used by the npm backend

The `packageManager` checksum is passed to the npm backend as a `checksum` option, which it reads, but the unknown-option check added in #14629 did not list it.

Add `checksum` to the npm backend's known options. `core/test_package_manager_checksum_slow` passes again. That test only runs with `TEST_ALL=1`, so it first failed on the release PR (#14601).

title: chore(schema): generate the [dotfiles] schema from typed entries
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/859
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `[dotfiles]` and `[dotfile_groups]` parts of `schema/mise.json` are now generated from declaration types in mise-config, as the rest of the schema already is. Before, they were the last large blocks of hand-written JSON, kept in step with mise-system's parsers by hand.

## What changes for users

Editors that use the mise schema now flag a typo in a dotfile entry. Before, the schema left the entry table open, so this passed without a complaint:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.gitconfig" = { source = "gitconfig", mod = "copy" }   # flagged now: unknown key `mod`
```

The schema also documents two keys it left out before, so editors now complete them:

- `autosave`: in track mode, `false` saves the path only on `mise dotfiles save <path>`.
- `enabled`: `false` turns off an entry inherited from another config file.

mise itself still reads dotfile entries exactly as before. Each entry stays raw TOML until mise expands the dotfiles, and an unknown key in one is still ignored at that point.

## Implementation

- **Declaration types.** `crates/mise-config/src/dotfiles.rs` gains `DotfileEntryDecl` (a source string or a table) and `DotfileTableDecl` (every key a whole-file entry or an edit may hold). It also gains `DotfileVariantDecl`, `DotfileGroupDecl` and `DotfileGroupEntryDecl`, and `MergeSetting` moves here from mise-system. Each key's doc comment is its schema description.
- **Cross-key rules.** Which keys an entry may combine depends on its mode, and on whether it is a whole-file entry or an edit; for example, `relative` applies only to symlink modes. A derive can't express that, so these rules stay hand-written in `crates/mise-config/src/dotfiles/schema.rs` and are added to the derived schema. They moved over unchanged.
- **Parity tests.** mise-system still decides whether a table is a whole-file entry or an edit, and parses it with its own types. New tests, `dotfile_keys_match_the_declaration` and `group_keys_match_the_declaration`, check that those parsers together read exactly the keys the declarations list, so a key added to one without the other fails a test. `FileTomlEntry::Table` becomes the struct `FileTomlTable` so its keys can be listed.

Apart from the closed entry table and the two added keys, the generated `[dotfiles]` and `[dotfile_groups]` schemas are semantically identical to the hand-written ones (compared with `jq -S`).

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --exclude mise`. The new parity tests fail when a key is removed from the declaration.
- `cargo test --all-features -p mise --lib`, including `schema_matches_parser`, which validates every `toml` block in `docs/` and every e2e heredoc against the closed schema.
- `mise run test:e2e`: `config/test_schema_ajv`, `config/test_schema_tombi`, all `config/test_schema_dotfiles_*`, and 14

title: feat(config): add mise config explain
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/858
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

New command, `mise config explain [KEY]`. It describes each key a mise TOML file sets, using the descriptions from the mise.toml schema, and flags keys mise doesn't read.

```toml
[tools]
node = "22"

[settings]
experimantal = true

[tasks.build]
run = "cargo build"
```

```
$ mise config explain
~/src/app/mise.toml
   1  tools                  dev tools to use
   2  tools.node             a version of the tool, or a table with its version and options
   4  settings               mise settings
   5  settings.experimantal  not a key mise reads; did you mean experimental?
   7  tasks                  task runner tasks
   7  tasks.build            a task: a script, a list of scripts and task references, or a table
   8  tasks.build.run        script to run
```

- **Unknown and deprecated keys:** an unknown key is marked, with the known key it most likely meant. A deprecated key is marked "deprecated".
- **Narrowing:** `mise config explain tasks` shows only the keys under `[tasks]`.
- **JSON:** `--json` prints each key's path, line, description, deprecation and suggestion.
- **Choosing a file:** like `mise config get`, it reads the highest-precedence loaded TOML file, or the one picked with `--file`, `--global`, `--system` or `--override`.
- **Broken files:** it reads the file as plain TOML, so it also works on a config mise refuses to load.

The `[tasks]` and `[tools]` entry definitions gain a description in `schema/mise.json`, so a task or tool entry is described as a whole rather than by one of its shapes. Editors show the same text on hover.

Not covered yet: explaining which config file's value wins when several layers set the same key.

## Validation

- New e2e test `cli/test_config_explain`.
- `command_effects` classifies the command as read-only.
- `mise.usage.kdl`, `docs/cli`, the man page and `cli_commands.ts` are regenerated. The diff is only the new command.
- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- The schema freshness and conformance tests.

Stacked on #14641.

title: docs(config): add an interactive mise.toml reference generated from the schema
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/857
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The docs gain a [mise.toml reference](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/reference.html): every key mise reads from a `mise.toml`, from the top-level sections down through their tables, with each key's type, choices, default and description. Before, the only complete list of keys was `schema/mise.json` itself, and the descriptions an editor shows on hover appeared nowhere in the docs.

## The page

The page opens with each section and the keys directly in it. Click a key to open the keys inside it, or type in the filter box to search every key's name and description. With a filter, only the matching keys show, with the keys above them, and the filter is kept in the URL (`/configuration/reference.html?filter=rename_exe`). A link to any key, such as `#tasks.<name>.depends`, opens the keys above it and scrolls to it, and **Expand all** shows the whole tree.

A key that has the same keys as another links to it instead of repeating them. For example, `tasks.<name>.tools.<github:…>` says "Same keys as `tools.<github:…>`", and `task_templates.<name>.run` points at `tasks.<name>.run`. This brings the reference from 2,663 keys to 1,074; the tool options repeated under tasks, task templates and monorepo task defaults were most of the difference.

Names in angle brackets stand for keys the user chooses. `[settings]` links to the existing [settings reference](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/settings.html) rather than repeating it.

## Markdown for agents

The page needs its script to show most keys, so the docs build also writes the reference as plain Markdown: an index at [`/configuration/reference.md`](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/reference.md) and one file per section under `/configuration/reference/`, such as `tasks.md`. Every key is written out with its full path. The largest file, `bootstrap.md`, is 39 KB. `llms.txt` lists the index next to the page.

## Size

Measured on the built site, compared with rendering every key into the page:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `reference.html` | 972 KB | 313 KB (about 290 KB of it is the site's sidebar and theme, as on every page) |
| `<li>` in the HTML | 2,724 | 226 |
| page JavaScript | 582 KB | 41 KB |
| rest of the reference, loaded after the page shows | — | 232 KB (26 KB gzipped) |

## Implementation

- `docs/config-reference.data.ts` is a VitePress data loader, like `settings.data.ts`. It follows `$ref` and the combinators to collect each key's types and children. Only `$ref` and `allOf` count for deprecation, so one deprecated alternative form doesn't mark the whole key deprecated. Keys a shape forbids with `false`, as task templates do for `hide` and five others, are left out. Repeated trees are found by comparing what each key has below it; the key kept is the one that is not deprecated, outside a derived section (`task_templates`, `monorepo`), nearest the top, and then first in the

title: fix(config): say which shapes a hook, run entry or env value takes
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/856
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A config value with several accepted forms now says which forms it takes, or names the wrong key. Before, it said only that the value matched none of them.

| Config | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `[hooks] enter = 1` | data did not match any variant of untagged enum HookDef | expected a command string, a table with `run`, `script`, `scripts` or `task`, or a list of those |
| `enter = { runn = "x" }` | data did not match any variant of untagged enum HookDef | unknown field `runn`, expected one of `run`, `run_windows`, `shell`, `script`, `scripts`, `task` |
| `enter = { task = "a", shell = "bash" }` | data did not match any variant of untagged enum HookDef | a hook with `task` cannot set any other key |
| `run = [{ tsk = "lint" }]` | data did not match any variant of untagged enum StringOrValue | a run entry table needs `task` (one task) or `tasks` (tasks run in parallel) |
| `depends = [{ tsk = "lint" }]` | data did not match any variant of untagged enum StringOrValue | unknown field `tsk`, expected one of `task`, `args`, `env`, `optional` |
| `[env] FOO = [1]` | failed to parse environment variable 'FOO': data did not match any variant of untagged enum Val | Environment variable 'FOO' cannot be an array. Set it to a string, integer or boolean, or to a table with `value`, `default`, `required` or `age`. |

Every value that parsed before still parses the same way. One side effect: an unknown key inside a `run` or `depends` table item now gets mise's usual unknown-field warning; before, it was silently ignored.

## Implementation

- `HookDef` and `HookDefItem` read a hook table into one struct that rejects unknown keys, then choose the variant from the keys that are set. The rules match the old untagged order.
- `RunEntry` reads a table with `task` or `tasks`. When both are set, `task` still wins.
- `deserialize_arr`'s list items hand a table straight to the item type, so the item type's own error is the one shown. This covers `depends`, `run`, `sources` and the other list fields.
- An env value that is an array, a float or a date is rejected by name before the `Val` parse. For a table no variant accepts, the untagged message is replaced with what each key takes.

## Validation

- `cargo test --all-features -p mise`: everything passes except the one sandbox-only failure, which is unrelated. That includes the hook and task parser tests, which list accepted and rejected inputs.
- `mise run test:e2e` passes for the new `config/test_config_shape_errors`, all `config/test_hooks*` tests, and the task dependency tests.

title: feat(config): say where an unknown mise.toml key is and what it meant
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/855
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The warning for an unknown `mise.toml` key now says where the key is and, when a known key is close, suggests it. Before, it gave only the file and the key path. The path also included serde's internal `?` segments, as in `monorepo.?.config_root`.

```toml
[tool]
node = "22"

[settings]
experimantal = true
```

Before:

```
mise WARN  unknown field in ~/app/mise.toml: tool
mise WARN  unknown field in ~/app/mise.toml: settings.experimantal
```

After:

```
mise WARN  unknown field in ~/app/mise.toml:1:2: tool (did you mean tools?)
mise WARN  unknown field in ~/app/mise.toml:5:1: settings.experimantal (did you mean experimental?)
```

A key gets a suggestion when a known key at the same level is at most two edits away; a swap of two neighboring letters counts as one. The warning stays on one line, because it prints on every mise command, including the shell hook.

## Implementation

- **Location:** `src/config/config_file/unknown_key.rs` rebuilds the key path from `serde_ignored::Path` segment by segment, so a key containing a dot stays one segment. It then finds the key's position with `toml_edit`'s spans.
- **Suggestions:** the known keys come from `schema/mise.json`. It is now embedded once in the library as `crate::config::schema`, with the `$ref`, combinator, `patternProperties` and `items` walk that `mise config get`/`set` completion already used. `config get`/`set` completion, the backend option check from #14629 and this warning share that one copy, in place of three separate `include_str!`s.
- The edit-distance match moves from `secrets::grant` into `crate::fuzzy::nearest`, which secrets suggestions still use.

## Validation

- New unit tests in `unknown_key.rs` cover top-level keys, nested tables, inline tables, dotted keys, and a key with no near match.

title: refactor(config): parse mise.toml through MiseTomlDecl
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/854
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise.toml` is now parsed through mise-config's `MiseTomlDecl`, the same declaration that generates `schema/mise.json`. Before, `MiseToml` had its own serde derive with the same fields, and a test kept the two key lists equal. Now there is one definition of what a `mise.toml` may contain. There's no change for users: the same files parse the same way, with the same warnings and errors.

## What changed

- `MiseTomlDecl<T = ToolSpec, S = toml::Table>` derives `Deserialize` with the serde attributes `MiseToml` had. Two fields need types from crates above mise-config, so they are type parameters:
  - `[tools]` entries: mise checks tool options while parsing.
  - `[settings]`: `SettingsPartial` lives in mise-settings.
  With the default parameters, mise-config can parse a `mise.toml` on its own.
- `MiseToml` implements `Deserialize` by parsing `MiseTomlDecl<MiseTomlTool, SettingsPartial>`. `MiseToml::from_decl` then moves each field over and builds the `BackendArg` keys and `Task`s. Every caller, including `serde_ignored` and `toml::from_str::<MiseToml>`, keeps working unchanged.
- The `[tasks]` visitor (including the string and list shorthands) and the `[task_templates]` visitor move to mise-config as `TaskDecls` and `TaskTemplateDecls`, with the same error text.
- The `schema_keys_match_parser` test from #14632 is gone: `MiseToml` can no longer read a key `MiseTomlDecl` lacks.

## Validation

- `cargo test --all-features -p mise`: 3,077 of 3,078 pass. The one failure, `has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, fails because this sandbox can't write `/usr/local/share/mise`; this change doesn't touch it.
- The schema freshness test passes, so `schema/mise.json` is unchanged.
- `mise run test:e2e` passes for all 102 non-slow tests in `e2e/config/`.

Stacked on #14637.

title: feat(task): read #MISE headers through TaskDecl
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/853
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A file task's `#MISE` header now accepts the same properties and values as a `[tasks.<name>]` table. Before, headers had their own hand-written parser, and it had drifted from TOML tasks.

## What changes for users

**Keys that only worked in `mise.toml` now work in a header:** `timeout`, `vars`, `global`, `args`, and the sandbox keys `deny_all`, `deny_read`, `deny_write`, `deny_net`, `deny_env`, `allow_read`, `allow_write`, `allow_net` and `allow_env`. Before, they were ignored with an "unknown field(s)" warning.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#MISE description="Integration tests"
#MISE timeout="10m"
#MISE deny_net=true
cargo test --test integration
```

**A bad value warns and is skipped, and the rest of the header still applies.** Every task in a project is loaded in one loop, so one broken script must not stop the others from loading. Before, a bad value was handled one of three ways, depending on the key:

| Header | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| `#MISE hide="true"` (a string), or a bad `quiet`, `raw`, `silent` or `output` | silently ignored, no message | warns `invalid hide in task file header, ignoring` |
| `#MISE outputs=[1]` | panic | warns and skips `outputs` |
| a bad `tools`, `depends`, `env`, `sources`, `cache`, `watch`, `daemons` or `secrets` | error; every task in the project failed to load | warns and skips that key |
| `#MISE run="..."`, `run_windows`, `file`, `usage` | "unknown field(s)" warning | warns that the key has no effect in a file task, since the script is the `run` and `#USAGE` lines are the usage |

**A bad `confirm` or `deny_*` value is still an error.** Skipping either would let a typo remove a confirmation prompt or a sandbox restriction, so these keys fail closed. Skipping a bad `allow_*` value only grants less, so those keys warn and are skipped like the rest.

A small change for task templates: a header's `silent` now counts as explicitly set, the same as in a TOML task. Before, a template named with `extends` overrode a header's `silent`; now the header's own value wins.

## Implementation

- `header_decl` in `src/task/mod.rs` turns the merged header table into a `TaskDecl`, with the behavior above. `Task::from_decl` is split into `Task::apply_decl`, so a file task keeps its name, path and load state while taking the declared fields. A non-executable script is still always hidden.
- The hand-written reader (`TomlParser` and `TrackingTomlParser`) is gone, and so is `src/config/config_file/toml.rs`. `deserialize_arr`'s tests moved to `mise_config::de`.
- `mise_config::de::struct_fields::<T>()` reads a derived struct's serde field list. `header_decl` uses it to spot unknown keys, the `MiseToml` key-parity test from #14632 now uses it too, and `test_parses_all_fields` uses it to check that its header sets every `TaskDecl` key a header can.

body:

`e2e/backend/test_npm` started failing on every branch because it installs `npm:tldr@3.4.0`, and aube now refuses that package:

```
aube install failed: refusing to add tldr: only 777 weekly downloads (threshold: 1000)
```

The check was added in #2532 to make sure `mise install npm:<pkg>` works when node comes from `mise use node` and the package has npm dependencies. It doesn't need tldr in particular, so this switches it to `npm:http-server@14.1.1`. That package and each of its 13 direct dependencies have about 4M or more weekly downloads, so the test no longer depends on a package that is losing users.

I didn't use `allow_low_downloads = true`: it exempts only the tool's own package, so the test could still break if one of tldr's dependencies dropped below the threshold.

`mise run test:e2e backend/test_npm` passes locally.

title: chore(schema): generate the whole schema from a top-level MiseTomlDecl
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/850
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Contributors no longer edit `schema/mise.json` by hand. mise-config now generates all three published schemas (`schema/mise.json`, `schema/mise-task.json` and `schema/miserc.json`) from Rust types and `settings.toml`, and `mise run render:schema` writes them. For users, the schemas that editors and the JSON Schema Store load are unchanged apart from key order.

## What changes for contributors

- **The top level is a type.** `MiseTomlDecl` (`crates/mise-config/src/mise_toml.rs`) declares every top-level `mise.toml` key with its description, deprecation and schema. A new top-level key goes in `MiseTomlDecl` and in `MiseToml`. The new `schema_keys_match_parser` test fails until both read the same keys. It takes `MiseToml`'s key list from the field names serde passes to `deserialize_struct`.

- **The hand-written parts sit next to their types.** Some schemas were still hand-written JSON in `mise.json` because a derive can't describe them. Those moved into Rust `json_schema!` functions:

title: refactor(config): declare [tools] in mise-config, keyed by string
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/849
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. Parsing, errors and `schema/mise.json` stay the same. `[tools]` is now declared in `crates/mise-config`, keyed by the tool as written, and the `[tools]` part of the schema lives next to that declaration. With this, every table-shaped section of `mise.toml` has its declaration types in `mise-config`, except `[settings]` (driven by `settings.toml`), `[hooks]`, `[dotfiles]`/`[dotfile_groups]` and `[redactions]`. The plain top-level keys (`shell_alias`, `plugins`, `include`, …) remain fields on `MiseToml` until a top-level `MiseTomlDecl` replaces it.

## What `mise-config` declares

- **`ToolsDecl = IndexMap<String, ToolSpecList>`**: each key as written (`node`, `"cargo:ripgrep"`, `"node[os=linux]"`), each value a version string, a table, or a list of them.
- **`ToolSpec { request, options }`**: the request stays unrendered, so a `:` inside a template isn't read as a selector, and the table's other keys stay raw. `None` marks the string form, which mise treats differently from a table with no options.
- **`ToolSpecList<T = ToolSpec>`**: the string, table or list shape, generic over the element (see below).
- **`CoreToolOptions`** moves from mise as data. **`EnvValue`** moves with it; `mise-util` re-exports it from its old path, and the `[env]` parser now uses it in place of its private copy from #14621.

## What stays in mise

mise builds `BackendArg` and `ToolRequest`, and checks options, because `auto_update` reads settings. Two behaviors are kept on purpose:

- **Aliases still collapse.** `MiseToml` still keys tools by `BackendArg`, which compares by short name, so `node`, `nodejs`, `core:node` and `"node[opts]"` stay one entry, and `mise use`/`mise rm` edit the file as before.
- **Errors keep their spans.** mise parses `ToolSpecList<MiseTomlTool>`, and `MiseTomlTool` checks its options inside its own visitor. toml attaches a span only to errors raised while it is inside that value, so a bad option still points at the tool's own table, even inside a list:

  ```text
   2 │ node = [{ version = "20", lazy = "yes" }]
     ·         ────────────────┬───────────────
     ·                         ╰── lazy must be a boolean
  ```

  A first attempt validated after parsing the whole list, and that moved this caret to the array. I compared the error output for four configs (bad `postinstall`, bad `lazy` in a list, `version` with `path`, and `"node[os=linux]"` with `nodejs`) before and after: identical.

## Schema

`/properties/tools` and the 52 `tool*` `$defs` (`tool`, `tool_options`, `tool_platforms`, `tool_bool*`, and each `tool_<backend>` / `tool_<backend>_options` / `tool_<backend>_platforms`) moved unchanged into `crates/mise-config/src/tools/schema.rs`. They are hand-written because the schema picks a backend's options by key pattern (`patternProperties` on `^github:`, `^npm:`, …), which a derive on raw options

title: feat(backend): reject tool options a backend does not read
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/848
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A tool option that a backend does not read used to be accepted without any signal, so an install looked like it had applied a setting it ignored (the cause of #14623, where `rename_exe` was silently dropped by the cargo backend). Now the install fails and names the option:

```toml
[tools]
"cargo:eza" = { version = "latest", asset_pattern = "*.tar.gz" }
```

```text
cargo:eza: option `asset_pattern` is not used by the cargo backend
hint: Remove it, or check the spelling against the backend's documented options
```

Each backend opts in on its own, by declaring which `schema/mise.json` definitions document its options (`Backend::option_spec`). A backend with no declaration is not checked. Keys under `platforms` are checked too. Declared so far: cargo, conda, gem, github/gitlab/forgejo, go, http, npm, packslip, pipx, s3, spinel, spm and ubi.

Not declared: aqua, because its `vars` accept arbitrary keys, so there is no fixed set to check against (an e2e test caught this); and the plugin and core-language backends.

This is an error, so a config that carries a typo or a key meant for a different backend will now stop installing until it is fixed. The key lists come from the schema, which `schema_matches_parser` already keeps in line with every config in the docs and e2e tests, and a unit test checks that every option the schema documents for a backend is accepted by it.

Stacked on #14626 (the cargo `rename_exe` fix); review that first.

Tested with unit tests and the backend e2e tests that exercise options (github, forgejo, gem, conda, aqua).

title: fix(shim): render command wrappers with their config file's config_root
body:
Command wrapper templates (#14565) could not use `config_root`, which the [templates docs](https://mise.jdx.dev/templates.html#variables) list as available everywhere:

```toml
[wrappers.foo]
command = "fakeshow"
args = ["{{ config_root }}"]
```

```console
$ foo hello
Error:
   0: error: Variable `config_root` is not defined. Available variables: cwd, env, mise_bin, mise_pid, system_brew_prefix, tools, vars, xdg_cache_home, ...
```

Relative paths in template functions also resolved from the directory the shim ran in, so `args = ["{{ read_file(path='token.txt') | trim }}"]` with `token.txt` next to `mise.toml` worked from the project root and failed from a subdirectory:

```console
$ cd sub && foo hello
Error:
   0: error: Failed to read file '/w/proj/sub/token.txt': No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

A wrapper now renders like the other values in its config file: with that file's `config_root` and `config_source`, and with relative paths resolved from the file's directory. Both work from any directory under the project:

```console
$ foo hello
fakeshow args: /w/proj hello
$ cd sub && foo hello
fakeshow args: SECRET hello
```

A wrapper no file declares, such as the one mise adds for Rust, renders as before.

## Validation

- In a Debian container, with `foo` dispatched through the shim:

  | wrapper value                                | main                     | this branch          |
  | -------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ | -------------------- |
  | `args = ["{{ vars.x }}"]`                    | `vx`                     | `vx`                 |
  | `args = ["{{ config_root }}"]`               | `config_root` not defined | `/w/proj`           |
  | `command = "{{ config_root }}/..."`          | `config_root` not defined | runs the command    |
  | `read_file(path='token.txt')` from the root  | `SECRET`                 | `SECRET`             |
  | `read_file(path='token.txt')` from `sub/`    | file not found           | `SECRET`             |

- `e2e/cli/test_command_wrappers_template` gains a wrapper that uses `config_root` and `read_file`, run from the project root and from a subdirectory.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

body:

https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/846

`rename_exe` was silently ignored by the cargo backend, so a tool installed with it kept its original executable name even though the install reported success (#14623).

```toml
[tools."cargo:https://github.com/Michael-F-Bryan/wit-lsp"]
version = "rev:c90addb21d37f2bd62a9474adca1dd8f6320d437"
crate = "wit-cli"

It applies after any install route (cargo-binstall, native binary install, or `cargo install`), is recorded in the install state so changing it reinstalls, and is added to the schema and the cargo backend docs.

Tested with a new e2e test covering install, change and removal (`e2e/backend/test_cargo_rename_exe`, stub `cargo`), the schema conformance test, and the cargo backend unit tests.

title: chore(schema): generate the task schema from TaskDecl and TaskTemplate
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/845
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. The schema accepts the same configs as before. The task part of `schema/mise.json` (`$defs/task_props`, `task_template` and `task_config`), and with it all of `schema/mise-task.json`, is now generated from the task types in `crates/mise-config`. Adding or changing a task field now means editing `TaskDecl` and its doc comment. A test fails if `schema/mise.json` is not regenerated afterwards. Tasks drew 10 of this year's `fix(schema)` commits, the most of any section.

The `$defs` names are unchanged, so `$ref`s, the `mise edit` editor and `config keys` completion keep working. Both files are **semantically identical** to `main`'s (`jq -S` compares equal). The diff is key order only.

## How each part is built

- **`task_props`** is derived from `TaskDecl`, in the same field order:
  - Fields with a single shape derive their schema, with the doc comment as the description: `description`, `dir`, `hide`/`quiet`/`interactive`/`raw`/`raw_args`, `file`, `shell`, `usage`, `timeout`, `skip_if`, and the `deny_*`/`allow_*` sandbox fields.
  - Fields whose parser accepts several shapes take their schema from a function in `crates/mise-config/src/task/schema.rs`, next to the types: `alias`, `confirm`, `depends`/`depends_post`/`wait_for`, `daemons`, `tools`, `outputs`/`sources`, `cache`, `rust_cache`, `output`, `silent`, `run`/`run_windows`, `secrets`.
  - `env`, `vars` and `watch` are `$ref`s.
  - `args` and `global` stay out of the schema, as they are today: mise sets them while loading, and the docs never mention them. `extends` is in `$defs/task`, so templates don't take it.
- **`task_template`** is `task_props` with every key a template cannot set turned off. That list is not typed by hand. It comes from `TaskTemplate`'s parser: the generator offers each `task_props` key to `TaskTemplate` and keeps the ones serde reports as ignored, plus `secrets`, which templates read only to reject (G7). A field added to `TaskDecl` but not `TaskTemplate` is therefore forbidden for templates automatically.
- **`task_config`** is derived from `TaskConfig`.
- **`task`**, **`task_dependency_item`/`task_dependency_table`**, **`task_run_entry`** and **`task_watch`** are hand-written in `task/schema.rs`. They are small, and they describe shapes the custom deserializers accept.

`TaskDecl`'s and `TaskConfig`'s fields are reordered to match the schema, which serde doesn't care about. The empty-default transform now also drops `""`, so `String` fields with `#[serde(default)]` don't get `"default": ""`.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `schema_json_is_up_to_date` passes. It fails on `$defs/task_props` after a one-word doc comment change on `timeout` (reverted). `schema_matches_parser` (#14613) passes.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: `task` 647 passed, `config` 433 passed.
- e2e: all

title: refactor(task): split TaskDecl from Task
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/844
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. Behavior stays the same, and `schema/mise.json` is unchanged. A `[tasks.<name>]` table now parses into `mise_config::task::TaskDecl`, and mise builds its runtime `Task` from it with `Task::from_decl`. With this, everything a task can declare lives in `crates/mise-config` as plain data, which the task schema can be generated from next.

## Changes

- **`TaskDecl`** has every field `Task` read from TOML. `Task` no longer derives `Deserialize`, and its `#[serde(skip)]` runtime fields (config source, overlays, rendered templates, …) stay in mise.
- **Presence is in the type.** `hide`, `raw`, `raw_args`, `interactive`, `quiet` and `silent` are `Option`s on `TaskDecl`. An overlay has to tell "not set" from "set to `false`", and `Task::from_decl` records which ones the table set. That replaces `TaskBoolPresenceMapAccess`, which wrapped serde's `MapAccess` to watch for those six keys, and `TaskTomlBoolPresence::record`.
- **`config_precedence`:** `from_decl` sets `0`, which is what `#[serde(skip)]` gave a table-form task before. `Task::default()` starts at `usize::MAX`. Loading reassigns it either way. String and array shorthand tasks (`build = "cargo build"`) are still built from `Task::default()`, as before.
- **`TaskTemplate`** moves to `mise-config`, together with `G7_TEXT` (templates cannot list `secrets`). Its merge logic is `impl Task` and stays in mise.
- **`TaskConfig`** (`[task_config]`) moves to `mise-config`.
- **`[deps]`** parses into `mise_config::deps::{DepsDecl, DepsProviderDecl}`. mise's `DepsConfig` and `DepsProviderConfig` keep their shape and the tera context they render with. They are built from the declaration in the one place that context is attached, so the 19 deps provider files are unchanged.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: `task` 647, `config` 433, `deps` 52, and `schema_conformance` (from #14613) all pass. `mise-config`: 6 passed.

title: refactor(task): move the task declaration field types into mise-config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/843
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. Behavior stays the same, and `schema/mise.json` is unchanged. The types that a `[tasks.<name>]` table's fields parse into now live in `crates/mise-config`. This is the first half of splitting the task declaration from the runtime `Task`. The next PR adds `TaskDecl` and `Task::from_decl` on top of these types. `Task` itself does not move yet.

## What moved

These move as is, with their pure methods, and mise re-exports each from its old path:
- `TaskConfirm`
- `TaskDep`, including `parse_shell_style_env` (adds `shell-words` to `mise-config`)
- `RunEntry`
- `TaskOutputs`
- `Silent`
- `TaskDaemons` (`names_mut` becomes `pub`)
- `TaskSecrets`, with its G4/G5 error messages
- `TaskWatchOptions`
- `TaskCacheConfig`
- `TaskRustCacheConfig`
- `TaskToolValue` / `TaskToolValueMap`
- `ParsedToolMap`
- `TaskOutput`

Methods that render tera templates or build tool requests stay in mise as extension traits:

| Trait | Methods |
|---|---|
| `TaskDepExt` | `render` |
| `RunEntryExt` | `render`, `has_tera_template` |
| `TaskOutputsExt` | `paths`, `render`, `re_render_with_env`, `has_tera_template`, `raw_templates_without_env` |
| `TaskToolValueExt` | `to_tool_arg`, `has_template`, `render_templates` |

`TaskOutputsExt` is `pub` and re-exported from `crate::task`, because `mise tasks info` in the binary calls `paths`. `RawOutputTemplates` is re-exported with it.

## `TaskOutput` and the crate graph

`TaskOutput` (the `output = "prefix"`/`"interleave"`/… style) lived in `mise-settings`. `mise-settings` pulls in reqwest, hyper and tokio through `mise-cache-core`, so depending on it would undo the point of #14608. Instead, `TaskOutput` moves into `mise-config`, and `mise-settings` now depends on `mise-config` and re-exports it, so `mise_settings::TaskOutput` still works. `xtasks/release-plz` now publishes `mise-bootstrap` and `mise-config` before `mise-settings`, since neither depends on it.

title: refactor(env): move env directives and the [env] parser into mise-config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/842
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. Parsing, warnings and output stay the same. `[env]` and `[vars]` are now parsed in `crates/mise-config`, and their JSON schema is written by hand next to that parser instead of directly in `schema/mise.json`. Changing what `[env]` accepts now means editing one file and its neighbor: `env.rs` for the parser, `env/schema.rs` for the schema. A test fails if `schema/mise.json` is not regenerated afterwards.

This is the largest move in the stack so far. Tasks come next, and they need it, because a task's `env` and `vars` are an `EnvList`.

## What moved

- `EnvList`, `EnvDirective`, `EnvDirectiveOptions`, `RequiredValue` and `AgeFormat` move into `mise_config::env`. mise re-exports them from `config::env_directive` and `config_file::mise_toml`, so the roughly 70 call sites are unchanged. The options' fields go from `pub(crate)` to `pub`.
- The parser moves without changes: the `EnvList` visitor with its ordered `_` table and its `value`/`default`/`required`/`age` rules, plus `deserialize_vars` and `deserialize_root_env`.
- **Deprecations are values.** `env.mise`, and `value`/`values` in a `file`, `path` or `source` directive, are now `mise_config::env::Deprecation` values. The parser passes them to a handler that mise registers at startup in `register_util_hooks`. mise still warns with `deprecated_at!`, and the ids, versions and messages stay the same, so `e2e/env/test_env_file` passes unchanged. The version policy stays in mise.
- `EnvDirective`'s `Display` impl (used by `mise tasks info`) shows paths through a second registered hook, so the home directory still reads as `~`.
- The parser's string/integer/boolean value type is a private copy of `mise_util::env_value::EnvValue`, because `mise-config` does not depend on `mise-util`. `EnvValue` itself stays in `mise-util`, where `cmd` and `env` use it.

## Schema

`$defs/env`, `$defs/vars` and the 13 `env_*` definitions moved unchanged into `crates/mise-config/src/env/schema.rs` as `json_schema!` literals. A script generated them from the committed JSON. `mise run render:schema` leaves `schema/mise.json` byte for byte the same. These hand-written fragments skip the generator's transforms, so they are emitted exactly as written. `EnvList` gets a `JsonSchema` impl that points at `$defs/env`, for the upcoming task declaration types.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p mise --lib config`: 431 passed. `task`: 647 passed. `secrets`: 136 passed. `mise-config`: 6 passed.
- e2e: 63 tests pass. They are every non-slow `e2e/env` test, plus `test_vars*`, `test_schema_ajv`, `test_schema_tombi` and the `tasks info` tests.

title: feat(env): let a find_up env._.file entry search several names together
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/841
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With two `find_up` entries in `env._.file`, a `.env.local` in a parent directory overrides a `.env` in the project (#14598). The docs said "a variable in a closer file wins", which is only true within one entry: each entry searches the whole tree on its own, and entries apply in the order listed, like every other `[env]` directive. There was no way to ask for "nearest directory first, then filename order".

This PR documents that rule and adds the way to get the other order: give one entry a `path` list.

```toml [~/.config/mise/config.toml]
[env]
_.file = { path = [".env", ".env.local"], find_up = true }
```

One entry searches directory by directory. The closest directory wins, and within one directory a name later in the list wins:

```text
workspace/
├── .env.local       # EXAMPLE=parent
└── project/
    └── .env         # EXAMPLE=project
```

Inside `project`, two separate entries give `EXAMPLE=parent` (unchanged), and the grouped entry gives `EXAMPLE=project`. A `.env.local` next to that `.env` would still override it.

Details:
- A `path` list already parsed, but mise split it into one search per name. It now stays together when `find_up` is set. Without `find_up` a list is the same as separate entries, so nothing changes there.
- Only plain relative names are searched together. A name with a template or `$VAR`, an absolute path, or a `~` path stands alone in list order, as a separate entry would, so a template can still use a value from a file listed before it.
- The group is uncacheable like any `find_up` entry, since the result depends on the current directory.
- Paranoid-mode trust applies to each file the search finds, as before.
- The existing `_.file = [...]` list of entries keeps its meaning.

The `env_file` setting keeps its own behavior and is unaffected.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# Separate `_.file` find_up entries each search the whole tree, in the order listed, so a parent's
+# later-listed file beats a closer earlier-listed one. One entry with a `path` list searches the
+# names together, directory by directory: the closest directory wins, and within one directory a
+# later name wins.
+mkdir -p workspace/project

+printf 'EXAMPLE=parent\nONLY_PARENT=1\n' >workspace/.env
+printf 'EXAMPLE=project\nONLY_PROJECT=1\n' >workspace/project/.env
+printf 'EXAMPLE=abs\nONLY_ABS=1\n' >workspace/abs.env
+cd workspace/project || exit 1
+
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[env]
+_.file = [
+  { path = ".env", find_up = true },
+  { path = ".env.local", find_up = true },
+]
+TOML

+

+[env]
+_.file = { path = [".env", ".env.local"], find_up = true }
+TOML

+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "ONLY_PARENT_LOCAL=1"
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "ONLY_PROJECT=1"
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "ONLY_PARENT=1"
+
+# Within one directory a later name wins.
+printf 'EXAMPLE=project-local\n' >.env.local
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=project-local"
+rm .env.local
+
+# The group works as one item of a longer list, and a later entry still overrides it.
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<TOML
+[env]
+_.file = [
+  { path = [".env", ".env.local"], find_up = true },
+  "$PWD/../abs.env",
+]
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=abs"
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "ONLY_PROJECT=1"
+
+# An absolute path ends a group: the names before and after it are searched as separate groups,
+# in list order, so a later name beats the absolute file and an earlier one loses to it.
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<TOML
+[env]
+_.file = { path = ["$PWD/../abs.env", ".env"], find_up = true }
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=project"
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<TOML
+[env]
+_.file = { path = [".env", "$PWD/../abs.env"], find_up = true }
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=abs"
+# ...even when the later name is only found in a parent directory.
+mv .env .env.hidden
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<TOML
+[env]
+_.file = { path = ["$PWD/../abs.env", ".env"], find_up = true }
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=parent"
+mv .env.hidden .env
+
+# A name listed twice loads at its last position, so it still wins over names listed between.
+printf 'EXAMPLE=local\n' >.env.local
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[env]
+_.file = { path = [".env", ".env.local", ".env"], find_up = true }
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise env --dotenv" "EXAMPLE=project"
+rm .env.local
+
+# Every occurrence still loads in order, so a file between two loads of the same file can expand
+# values from the earlier one.
+mkdir -p repeated
+# shellcheck disable=SC2016
+printf 'BASE=/opt/app\nAFTER=$OUTPUT\n' >repeated/base.env
+# shellcheck disable=SC2016
+printf '{"OUTPUT": "$BASE/out"}\n' >repeated/derived.json
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'

+_.file = { path = ["base.env", "derived.json", "base.env"], find_up = true, expand = true }

+assert_contains "cd repeated && mise env --dotenv" "AFTER=/opt/app/out"
+
+# A templated name resolves after the files listed before it, so it can use their values.
+mkdir -p staged
+printf 'STAGE=dev\n' >staged/.env
+printf 'FROM_DEV=1\n' >staged/dev.env
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'

+_.file = { path = [".env", "{{ env.STAGE }}.env"], find_up = true }
+TOML

https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/840

`trusted / unit-macos` has been failing on `main` and on every open PR since #14582. One test, `mise-oci registry::tests::large_blob_uses_one_content_range_free_patch`, is killed at 1 second on both nextest attempts, while the other 3,015 tests in that job pass.

`.config/nextest.toml` already gives this test a larger budget (`1s` period, `terminate-after = 5`) because it streams a sparse body just over 64 MiB through a local registry. The override's filter was `test(oci::registry::tests::...)`. #14582 moved the code into the `mise-oci` crate, so the test's name became `registry::tests::...` and the filter stopped matching: `cargo nextest list -E` on the old filter lists 0 tests. The default 1-second ceiling then applied again.

The filter is now `package(mise-oci) & test(registry::tests::large_blob_uses_one_content_range_free_patch)`, which lists exactly that one test. I also checked the other overrides in the file, and they still match. I could only run this on Linux, where the test takes about 0.9s; I haven't reproduced the macOS timing, so `unit-macos` on this PR is the confirmation.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/838
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors. The schema accepts the same configs as before. `[doctor]`, `[tool_config]`, `[[watch_files]]` and `[wrappers]` now live in `crates/mise-config`, and their part of `schema/mise.json` is generated from those types. Changing one of these sections now means editing the Rust type and its doc comments. A test fails if `schema/mise.json` is not regenerated afterwards.

## What moved

- `DoctorConfig`/`DoctorCheck`, `ToolConfig`, `WatchFile` and `CommandWrapper`/`CommandWrapperOptions` moved without behavior changes. mise re-exports them from their old paths, so call sites are unchanged.
- `DoctorCheck::applies` uses the host's OS matcher, so it is now the free function `config::doctor::applies` in mise.
- `deserialize_arr` moved to `mise_config::de`, because doctor's `os` field uses it. `config_file::toml` re-exports it.

## Schema

- `doctor` and `wrappers` derive a schema identical to the hand-written one. `doctor` keeps `additionalProperties: true` on purpose, and `test_schema_ajv` checks that unknown container keys stay valid.
- `tool_config` derives its schema with `additionalProperties: false` in place of the equivalent `unevaluatedProperties: false`.
- `WatchFile` is one flat struct for both its run and task forms. Its `JsonSchema` impl is therefore written by hand next to the struct, as the same two closed variants. A derived version with a `not` was rejected by `test_schema_tombi`, because tombi ignores `not` and would have let a task with a `shell` through.

`[hooks]` stays hand-written. Its schema allows a current-shell `shell` only on `enter`/`leave`/`cd` and marks the install-hook script forms deprecated. The parser uses one `HookDefItem` for every hook, so there is no type to derive those rules from.

## Validation
