title: fix(schema): generate [bootstrap] from its parser types
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/837
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap]` in `schema/mise.json` is now generated from the Rust types that parse it, as `[history]` is since #14611. Editors now get the keys and checks mise actually uses. Generating it found one gap right away: launchd agents accept `keep_alive_on_failure` and `nice`, but the hand-written schema didn't list them, so editors flagged both as unknown.

## Schema changes for users

- **Unknown keys are rejected throughout `[bootstrap]`.** `[bootstrap]` itself and its `macos`, `linux`, `user`, `brew`, `apt`, `dnf`, `macos.launchd`, `linux.systemd`, launchd agent and systemd unit tables used to accept any key in the schema, while mise warned about the unknown ones. They now reject unknown keys, like the rest of the schema, so an editor flags typos like this one:

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.user]
  login_shel = "/bin/zsh"   # now flagged; mise already warned "unknown field"
  ```

- **New keys:** launchd agents gain `keep_alive_on_failure` and `nice`, with the rules mise enforces when it builds the agent: `nice` from -20 to 20, and `keep_alive_on_failure` not combined with `keep_alive = true`.
- **Defaults:** boolean options and `phase` now show their defaults (`template = false`, `start = true`, …). `[history]` loses the empty `[]` and `{}` defaults #14611 added.

I validated all 104 `[bootstrap]` TOML examples in `docs/` against the old and new schema. None that passed before fails now. (`macos-defaults` example 4 fails both, an existing gap in the hand-written `macos.defaults` schema.)

## How it is built

- Each typed subsection derives `JsonSchema`. That covers files, directories, packages, repos, remote, services, compose, secrets, groups, users, brew, login items, launchd agents, systemd units and the firewall. Field doc comments are the descriptions, with the existing text kept. Cross-field rules (`if`/`then`, `oneOf`, `dependentRequired`, `propertyNames`) are `#[schemars(extend(...))]` attributes on the type they constrain.
- Fields that stay raw TOML have no type to derive from: `hooks`, `mise_shell_activate`, apt `sources`, dnf `repos`, and the macOS `dock`/`finder`/`keyboard`/`trackpad`/`defaults` tables. They keep raw TOML so newer shapes warn instead of failing. Their hand-written schema moved unchanged into `$defs` (`bootstrap_hooks`, `bootstrap_macos_dock`, …), and the generated tree points at it with `$ref`. `config keys` completion and the `mise edit` editor already follow `$ref`s.
- `bootstrap_remote_install_mise` and `launchd_calendar_interval` stay in `$defs` and are now generated too.
- `schemars` is a plain dependency of `mise-config`, and the `schema` feature from #14611 is gone. mise already links schemars through `rmcp`, and putting `cfg_attr` on every one of these annotations made them hard to read.
- New generator transforms: strip `null` from `Option` enums and `anyOf` (TOML has no null), drop empty `[]`/`{}` defaults,

title: fix(bootstrap): parse [bootstrap.linux.firewall] on every OS
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/836
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.linux.firewall]` is now parsed the same way on every platform.

- **Firewall:** before this change, only Linux type-checked `[bootstrap.linux.firewall]`. macOS and Windows kept it as an unchecked map, so a mistake showed up only on the Linux machines that load a shared config. All platforms now parse the typed form. macOS and Windows still skip the section at bootstrap time with the same warning (`ignoring [bootstrap.linux.firewall] on non-Linux host`), but an invalid value is now an error there too:

  ```toml
  [bootstrap.linux.firewall]
  backend = "iptables"
  ```

  ```text
    × Invalid TOML in config file
   2 │ backend = "iptables"
     ·           ─────┬────
     ·                ╰── unknown variant `iptables`, expected one of `auto`, `ufw`, `firewalld`, `nftables`
  ```

- **brew adopt:** #14613 already landed the same change on `main` (Windows no longer warns about `[bootstrap.brew] adopt`), so this PR now only carries the firewall part.

This also prepares for generating `schema/mise.json` from the `mise-config` types (#14611), because the declaration types no longer depend on the build host.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo check -p mise-config` for `aarch64-apple-darwin` and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. `mise-system` can't be cross-compiled here because of its C build scripts, so the macOS and Windows CI jobs cover the one-line `firewall_non_linux.rs` change.
- `mise-config` and `mise-system` nextest: 750 passed. `test_bootstrap_linux_firewall` is no longer Linux-only. After merging `main`, the conformance test from #14613 passes too.
- The error above is from a debug build.

title: test(schema): check schema/mise.json against the config parser
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/835
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`schema/mise.json` is written by hand, and nothing checked it against the parser that actually reads `mise.toml`, so the two kept drifting apart. Editors flagged valid configs as errors, or accepted keys that mise ignores, until someone filed a `fix(schema)` PR. This PR adds a unit test that turns that drift into a CI failure, and fixes the drift it found.

## Schema fixes (what editors now accept)

Each of these configs is valid for mise, but the schema used to reject it:

```toml
[bootstrap.macos.defaults."com.apple.dock"]
# arrays and tables become property list arrays and dictionaries, as documented
"persistent-apps" = [{ "tile-type" = "file-tile", "tile-data" = { "file-label" = "Terminal" } }]

[bootstrap.user]
login_shell = "{{ vars.shell_dir }}/zsh" # a template, rendered before the absolute-path check

[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents.sync]
program = "/usr/local/bin/sync"
queue_directories = ["{{ vars.svc_root }}/queue"] # also templated

[bootstrap.linux.systemd.units.sync]
exec_start = "/usr/local/bin/sync"
umask = "{{ vars.umask }}" # also templated

[vars]
mode = { value = "tool", tools = true } # [vars] entries take `tools`, like [env]

[tasks.build]
run = "cargo build"
rust_cache = { verify = true } # still accepted as a deprecated no-op
```

`login_shell` also accepts surrounding whitespace now, which mise already trims. `schema/mise-task.json` is regenerated from these changes.

On Windows, `[bootstrap.brew].adopt` no longer triggers an "unknown field" warning. Windows used to compile the field out, so a config shared with a Mac warned there. The per-package `adopt` already parsed on every platform; brew itself still runs only on macOS and Linux.

## The conformance test

`schema_matches_parser` (`src/config/config_file/mise_toml/schema_conformance.rs`) runs in `cargo test`. It checks documents on all cores (about 0.25s on 32 cores), and nextest's CI profile gives it the same 4s budget as the other corpus-sized tests. Outside a repository checkout, such as the published crate, it skips itself. Its corpus is:

- every fenced `toml` block in `docs/` (about 650), except blocks titled with a file that is not a mise config, such as `[mise.lock]`,
- every mise config an e2e test writes with a heredoc (about 2,500); unquoted heredocs count only when the shell has nothing to expand,
- a few seeded invalid configs, which both the parser and the schema must reject.

Each document goes through `MiseToml`'s real parse path (a new `parse_body_reporting`, without the trust check), recording errors and the fields `serde_ignored` reports as unknown. The test also validates the document against the schema with the `jsonschema` crate (draft 2020-12, a new dev-dependency). It fails when the parser reads a config cleanly and the schema rejects it, or when the schema accepts a config that the parser rejects or reads with unknown-field warnings.

So

title: chore(schema): generate the [history] schema from mise-config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/834
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change for contributors; `schema/mise.json` validates the same configs as before. `[history]` in `schema/mise.json` is now generated from the Rust types that parse it, instead of written by hand. This is the first section moved over. The others follow one PR at a time.

Today a contributor changes a parser and has to remember to edit the matching JSON by hand. 2026 so far has 42 `fix(schema)` commits from that drift. For a section that lives in `crates/mise-config`, the doc comments on its types are now the schema descriptions. A test fails while the committed file is stale:

```text
schema/mise.json/properties/history differs from the mise-config types; run `mise run render:schema`
```

## How it works

- `mise-config` has a default `schema` feature that derives `schemars::JsonSchema`. `mise` and `mise-system` depend on it with `default-features = false`, so the CLI does not build the derives.
- `mise_config::schema::fragments()` returns each generated section with the JSON pointer it replaces (`/properties/history` for now). Three transforms keep the output in the file's existing style:
  - drop `null` types and `null` defaults, since TOML has no null
  - add `additionalProperties: false` to objects that don't say otherwise (mise warns about unknown keys, and the schema rejects them so editors flag typos)
  - put `type` and `description` first
- `mise run render:schema` runs `cargo run -p mise-config --example render-schema` and writes each fragment at its pointer, the same way it already fills in `$defs.settings` from `settings.toml`. The pointer has to exist already, so a mistyped one fails.
- `mise-config`'s `schema_json_is_up_to_date` test compares the committed file with the generated fragments. It runs in CI's `cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude mise` step, where the default feature is on.

## Schema diff

The `[history]` descriptions keep their existing text. The diff to `schema/mise.json` is key order plus `"default"` values for `exclude` (`[]`), `reload` (`{}`) and `encryption.recipients` (`[]`). No config validates differently.

## Validation

- `cargo +1.95 clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus `-p mise-config` with default features
- `schema_json_is_up_to_date` passes. It fails, with the message above, after a one-word doc comment change in `history.rs` (reverted).
- `mise run render:schema` on a clean tree produces no further diff
- `mise run test:e2e test_schema_tombi test_schema_ajv`

Stacked on #14608.

title: feat(config): add config.override.toml so global config can override project config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/833
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A project's `mise.toml` or `mise.local.toml` always beats your global config, so a repo can replace the `node` version, an env var like `AWS_PROFILE`, or a setting you chose for yourself. The only escape hatch today is the special-case `settings.env_file`. This adds a global-only override file that outranks all project config for any section.

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.override.toml
[env]
AWS_PROFILE = "personal"

[tools]
node = "24"

[settings]
jobs = 8

[tasks.lint]
run = "my-lint --strict"
```

In any project, `AWS_PROFILE`, the `node` request, `jobs` and the `lint` task now come from this file, even when the project's `mise.toml` or `mise.local.toml` sets them. Anything the override file does not mention still comes from the project and your other global config.

## Behavior

- **Files:** `config.override.toml` and `config.<env>.override.toml` in the global config dir (`MISE_ENV` variants follow the usual order, later envs win). The env-specific file beats the base override file, and the whole tier ranks above every project file, including `mise.<env>.toml` and `mise.local.toml`. It is not `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES`, which only renames the files mise reads.
- **All sections:** `[env]`, `[tools]`, `[tasks]`, `[settings]` (applied during settings load, not afterwards), hooks, etc. fall out of the same ordered merge.
- **Global config:** the files are trusted by path and get global-config safe-mode treatment, so the paranoid-mode `_.file`/`_.source` operator-owned check also covers them.
- **Never a default write target.** `mise use`, `mise set`, `mise settings set`, `mise trust`/`untrust`, `mise unuse` (first declaring config), `mise config get|set` default and the `--global` existing-declaration lookups skip it. Writing needs an explicit long-only `--override` flag (with `--env` selecting `config.<env>.override.toml`) on `use`, `unuse`, `set`, `unset`, `settings set|add|unset` and `config get|set`. It conflicts with `--global` and `--path` (`--local` for `settings`).
- **Lockfiles:** a tool declared in the override file shadows the project's pin. It resolves from the global `mise.lock`, never from the project's `mise.lock`, and `--locked` does not require the project lock to pin it. Other tools are still enforced.
- **`MISE_GLOBAL_CONFIG_FILE`** means "this is the only global config", so no override files load and `--override` errors.
- **Visibility:** `mise config ls` adds a `Tier` column (`override`) when an override file is loaded, `mise config ls --json` gains `"override": true|false`, and `mise doctor` labels the files.

```console
$ mise config ls
~/proj/mise.toml                     (none)
~/proj/mise.local.toml               (none)
~/.config/mise/config.override.toml  (none)  override
```

`settings.env_file` is unchanged.

title: feat(config): let paranoid take a list of categories
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/832
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`paranoid` was all or nothing, so approving the dotenv files that a global `find_up` entry loads meant also turning on content-hashed project config trust, no CI trust, and provenance re-verification. It now also takes a list of categories, so you can pick only what you want:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings]
paranoid = ["env_files"]

[env]
_.file = [{ path = ".env", find_up = true }]
```

With this, mise refuses to load a `.env` it finds in a repository until you run `mise trust .env`, and asks again after every edit. Project config trust, CI, plugins and provenance behave as in normal mode.

## Categories

- `config`: content-bound trust for project config, no automatic or CI/`--yes` trust, no worktree or monorepo-marker sharing.
- `env_files`: content-bound trust for `_.file`, `_.source` and the `env_file` setting (from #14604, now merged).
- `plugins`: refuse unregistered community plugins by short name.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/831
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no change for mise users. This renames the `mise-system-config` crate to `mise-config`. It is the first step toward generating `schema/mise.json` from the Rust types that parse `mise.toml`, instead of maintaining it by hand (2026 so far has 42 `fix(schema)` commits).

`mise-config` will hold every `mise.toml` declaration type: plain data parsed from the file, with no templating, settings or filesystem access. For now it holds the existing `[bootstrap]`, `[dotfiles]`, `[dotfile_groups]` and `[history]` types.

## Changes

- `crates/mise-system-config` → `crates/mise-config`, with import paths updated in `mise-system` and the root crate.
- The crate no longer depends on `mise-system-packages` or `mise-util`. Only three `PackageTomlConfig` methods (`snap_options`, `desired`, `is_os_supported`) used them. Those methods now live in a `PackageTomlConfigExt` trait in `mise-system`, their only caller, with the same bodies. With that, `mise-config` no longer pulls in reqwest, tokio or sigstore.
- `xtasks/release-plz` publishes `mise-config` in the slot `mise-system-config` had. `mise-config` 0.0.0 is reserved on crates.io with trusted publishing from `release-plz.yml` (trusted publishing only), matching the other subcrates. It has no tag yet, so the next release publishes it.

`mise-system-config` stays on crates.io at its last version and gets no new releases.

title: perf(dotfiles): build snapshot trees without a git process per tracked file
body:
`mise dot status` and `mise dot sync` got slower with every tracked file, because building a snapshot tree started two `git` processes (`ls-files` and `update-index`) per tracked file. On a home directory tracking about 860 files, `mise dot status --json` took about 10 seconds, nearly all of it spent starting git. The background watcher pays the same cost on every sync.

`compose` now applies the overlays to an in-memory listing of the base tree and writes the result with a single `update-index --index-info` and `write-tree`, instead of two git calls per overlay. Nothing changes for users except speed: the resulting trees are identical, and so are the failures. A path added beneath an existing file is still refused, as `update-index` refuses it, and a subtree still replaces a file in its way, as `read-tree --prefix` does.

## Results

Measured on macOS (Apple Silicon) with debug builds of `main` and of this branch, each run against its own copy of the same state directory and the same 860 tracked files, `mise dot status --json`, three runs each:

| Build | Time | git processes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` | 10.3s, 9.9s, 9.9s | 2,599 |
| this PR | 4.1s, 3.9s, 4.0s | 879 |

The status output of the two builds was identical. Most of the remaining processes are the one `hash-object -w` per tracked file that writes each blob, which this PR does not change.

## Testing

- The previous per-overlay implementation stays as a test-only reference (`compose_by_git`). A new unit test, `compose_matches_git`, runs both over 15 overlay sequences and requires the same tree, or the same refusal where git refuses. The sequences cover replacing and removing files and directories, siblings that sort next to a directory (`dir-b`, `dir.txt`, `dir0`), subtrees over and beneath files, an empty subtree, a later overlay undoing an earlier one, duplicate paths, gitlinks and symlinks.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --lib history::` passes (295 tests), and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: feat(config): let env_file take several filenames
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/830
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `env_file` setting loads a dotenv file by one name, found in the current directory and every parent. A global config could load `.env` or `.env.local`, but not both, which people ask for since `.env.local` is the conventional machine-local override (raised in #14600).

`env_file` now takes a list:

```toml [~/.config/mise/config.toml]
[settings]
env_file = [".env", ".env.local"]
```

or `MISE_ENV_FILE=.env:.env.local`, with names separated by the OS path separator. The file nearest the current directory still wins, and within one directory a name later in the list wins. It still applies after every config file's `[env]`, so these values override project `[env]`.

Existing configs keep working: a single string (`env_file = ".env"`) is read as a one-name list, `mise settings set env_file .env` still writes one name, and `MISE_ENV_FILE=.env` is unchanged. The JSON schema accepts a string or an array.

Under paranoid mode each file found this way needs its own trust (#14604), same as before.

> **Overview**

> Loading walks the same directory tree for each name. **Nearest directory still wins** over parents; **within one directory, a later name in the list wins**. Absolute paths are deduped on walk-up so list order controls precedence vs nearby relative files. Docs/schema accept string or array; env-cache hashing includes every configured name.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>aubepkg/aube (aube)</summary>

### [`v2.8.1`](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/releases/tag/v2.8.1): : pnpm 11 lockfile parity, Yarn Berry and npm lockfile fixes

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/v2.8.0...v2.8.1)

v2.8.1 brings aube-written `pnpm-lock.yaml` files closer to pnpm 11's output and fixes lockfile round-trips for npm and Yarn Berry. It also fixes `minimumReleaseAge` in `update`/`dedupe`, `install --force`, workspace detection for nested projects, and handling of an empty `CI` variable.

##### Fixed

##### Lockfiles

- **pnpm 11 parity** ([#​1792](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1792), [#​1793](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1793), [#​1788](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1788)): when a tool such as Dependabot regenerates the lockfile with pnpm, it should rewrite fewer lines that did not change.
  - Peer suffixes are now sorted by the full `name@version` string, e.g. `(react-dom@18.2.0(react@18.2.0))(react@18.2.0)`.
  - With `dedupePeerDependents` on (the default), aube resolves an optional peer from any matching version in the graph and lists it under `optionalDependencies:`. Compatible variants of a package are merged across importers.
  - `catalogs:` no longer lists entries that an override replaces.
- **npm `package-lock.json`**:
  - `aube add` now keeps `"optional": true` (for example on `@esbuild/*` platform packages) and `"hasInstallScript": true`. Previously, dropping these made npm fail with `Unsupported platform` ([#​1775](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1775)).
  - Root `file:` directory dependencies now keep their link and target entries, so `npm ci` no longer reports `Missing: … from lock file` ([#​1799](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1799)).
- **`file:` peers on re-resolve** ([#​1775](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1775)): `aube add` no longer fails with `ERR_AUBE_BLOCKED_EXOTIC_SUBDEP` when a direct `file:` dependency satisfies another package's peer.
- **Yarn Berry `yarn.lock`** ([#​1798](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1798)):
  - Changes to `package.json` are now detected even when some dependencies are unchanged. Previously aube could print "Lockfile is up to date" and leave `yarn.lock` stale. This also applies to Yarn Classic.
  - Rewritten lockfiles now keep the `__metadata` version and `cacheKey`, the root workspace entry, `bin:` maps and `builtin<compat/…>` patch blocks, and use Yarn's formattin

title: fix(config): require content-bound trust for env files in paranoid mode
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/828
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

In paranoid mode, trusting `mise.toml` also approved whatever dotenv, JSON, YAML or TOML file its `env._.file` pointed at. mise hashed the config but never the file, so a `git pull` that edited `.env` changed the environment of every later command with no new approval. A global `env._.file = [{ path = ".env", find_up = true }]` made it worse, since it loads files from parent directories that no config hash covers. The `env_file` setting had the same gap.

Now, with paranoid mode on, each existing file loaded through `_.file`, found by the `env_file` setting, or run by `_.source` needs its own trust, bound to its content:

```console
$ mise env
Error:
   0: The environment file ~/src/app/.env is not trusted, and paranoid mode ties trust to a file's contents.
      Review it, then trust it with `mise trust ~/src/app/.env`.
$ mise trust .env
$ mise env   # works until .env changes again
```

The error names the file and prints none of its values.

`mise trust` with no path now approves everything the project reads: the nearest untrusted config, then the env files and scripts it loads. It resolves the env the way `hook-env` does, records the files it would have refused, and trusts them. It repeats until nothing new turns up, since a trusted script can name the next file. `mise trust <path>` still trusts only that file, and `mise trust --all` also covers env files. `mise trust --show` still lists configs only.

- Opt-out: put the file under `trusted_config_paths`. It is global-only, so a project cannot exempt its own files, and it matches how global and system config already stay trusted by path.
- Not checked: a global `_.file` entry without `find_up`, because it names a file the operator chose, and files that do not exist.
- Nothing changes outside paranoid mode.
- `_.source` scripts get the same check before they run, since they execute code. A script that sources other files is only hashed at the top level.

Raised in discussion #14599, which asked for an opt-in `require_trust`; this makes the check the paranoid-mode default instead. See also #14600 for how `env_file` and `_.file` differ.

title: docs(env): explain env_file and _.file find_up are different features
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/827
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`env_file` (the setting) and `env._.file` with `find_up = true` both find a `.env` in the current directory and its parents, and the docs described them as doing "the same" thing. They don't behave the same: `env_file` is applied after every config file's `[env]`, so its values win, while an `_.file` entry is an ordinary `[env]` entry that a project's own `[env]` values override. Someone moving a global `env_file = ".env"` to `_.file = [{ path = ".env", find_up = true }]` can silently change which value a command receives (see discussion #14600).

These are separate features, so this clarifies the docs instead of changing behavior:

- the `env._.file` page now says `env_file` is a different feature and states the precedence difference
- the `env_file` setting description says its values override `[env]` and that `_.file` entries do not

No code changes.

> 
> **Overview**
> **Documentation only** — clarifies that `env_file` / `MISE_ENV_FILE` and `[env] _.file` with `find_up` are separate mechanisms, not interchangeable ways to walk parent directories for `.env`.
> 
> The environments guide now states that `_.file` participates in normal `[env]` precedence (project config can override a global `find_up` entry), while `env_file` is applied **after** all config `[env]` blocks and therefore usually wins, except it **skips** any dotenv file already loaded via `_.file`. title: fix(rust): don't put an external rustup's directory ahead of mise's tools
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/825
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With an external rustup whose proxies live in a shared directory (pacman's `rustup` puts them in `/usr/bin`), `mise exec`, tasks and shims ran the system Node from `/usr/bin` instead of the Node version mise manages, because mise prepended `/usr/bin` to PATH as the `rust` tool's bin path.

Now the rust tool exposes only the external rustup's proxies (cargo, rustc, rustup, ...) through a mise-owned directory of symlinks, so Rust lookup and shims keep working while other tools in that directory no longer take precedence.

```toml
[tools]
rust = "1.98.1"
node = "24"
```

`mise exec -- node -v` now reports Node 24 instead of the system Node.

Fixes #14587

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how Rust contributes to PATH for external rustup users; failures during proxy isolation omit Rust from PATH rather than re-shadowing shared directories.
> 
> **Overview**
> **External rustup** no longer prepends its real bin directory (e.g. pacman’s `/usr/bin`) to PATH. For that provider, `list_bin_paths` now returns a mise-owned directory under `rust-proxies/` containing symlinks or copies of only known Rust proxies (`cargo`, `rustc`, `rustup`, etc.), so unrelated binaries in the shared folder no longer win over other mise tools.
> 
> Isolation is maintained incrementally (stale links removed, Windows uses size/mtime checks for copies), and proxy linking errors propagate instead of falling back to the shared dir. Managed rust still exposes `~/.cargo/bin` unchanged.
> 
> **Toolset PATH caching** skips `LIST_PATHS_CACHE` when any tool’s `list_bin_paths` fails, so a transient error is not cached as an empty path set.
>

title: fix(bootstrap): find nix installed by a pre-packages hook
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/824
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap` can now install `[bootstrap.packages]` with the `nix:` manager when Nix itself was installed earlier in the same run, for example by a `pre-packages` hook.

Before, with Nix installed via the hook and `--no-modify-profile`:

```toml
[bootstrap.hooks]
pre-packages = "[ -d /nix ] || curl -fsSL https://artifacts.nixos.org/nix-installer | sh -s -- install --no-confirm --no-modify-profile"

[bootstrap.packages]
"nix:nixd" = "latest"
```

the hook succeeded but the package phase reported `nix: 1 package(s) skipped (nix not found on PATH)`. Hooks run in a child process, so nothing they do reaches mise's own `PATH`.

Now, when `nix` is not on `PATH`, mise falls back to `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix`, where the Nix installers put the CLI for all users, and runs that binary directly. The unavailable message now names both locations. A `nix` already on `PATH` is still preferred.


Validation: not compiled or tested locally, because `mise-sigstore` fails to build on this base before reaching the changed crate (unresolved `sigstore_verify` imports). CI is the first real build.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: Anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Overview**
> **Nix bootstrap detection** now resolves the `nix` CLI via `PATH` first, then falls back to `/nix/var/nix/profiles/default/bin/nix` when that file exists and is executable. `query`, `action`, and `is_available` all use this resolver so `[bootstrap.packages]` with `nix:` can run in the same `mise bootstrap` run after a `pre-packages` hook installs Nix with `--no-modify-profile` (hooks run in a child process, so they do not update mise’s `PATH`). The skip message when Nix is missing now mentions both locations.

title: fix(npm): report an unusable TLS root store instead of aborting
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/823
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise upgrade` (and anything else that touches the npm backend) aborted with a core dump when the system TLS root store could not be loaded:

```console
$ mise upgrade
The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  failed to build HTTP client: reqwest::Error { kind: Builder, source: InvalidCertificate(BadEncoding) }
Location: aube-registry-2.7.0/src/client/http.rs:335
Aborted (core dumped)
```

The panic is an `.expect()` inside the embedded `aube-registry` crate, and release builds use `panic = "abort"`, so mise cannot catch it. aubepkg/aube#1758 adds `RegistryClient::try_from_config`, which returns the error. mise now uses it and reports the failure, with the underlying causes:

```console
$ mise upgrade
mise ✗ npm:playwright · failed: Could not initialize the npm registry HTTP client: builder error: ...
```

The `aube` crates are bumped to 2.7.2, which includes `RegistryClient::try_from_config` (aubepkg/aube#1758). Unlike a TLS-root probe, this also covers a malformed certificate from `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or an `.npmrc` `ca`/`cafile`.

I did not reproduce the original crash on a system with a bad system certificate; the aube PR has unit tests for the error paths.

Fixes #14591

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-299_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how npm registry HTTP/TLS setup fails (panic vs reported error), which affects any command using the npm backend but narrows blast radius by failing only those operations.
> 
> **Overview**
> **npm registry client initialization no longer panics** when building the HTTP client fails (e.g. bad system TLS roots, malformed `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, or `.npmrc` `ca`/`cafile`).
> 
> The lazy `RegistryClient` is built with **`try_from_config`** from **aube 2.7.2** instead of the old path that could `.expect` inside `aube-registry` and abort the process under `panic = "abort"`. Failures are stored once in a process-wide lazy `Result`, surfaced through a small **`client()`** helper, and returned as normal mise errors with the **full error cause chain** on packument fetch, search, and tarball download.
>

title: fix(activate): stop fish not-found recursion after mise implode
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/822
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With fish, `mise implode` could end with `The call stack limit has been exceeded. Do you have an accidental infinite loop?` because the shell integration was still active after the `mise` binary was removed.

fish passes the failing command to `fish_command_not_found` as written, and after implode that is the full path (`/home/user/.local/bin/mise`). The handler's guard only skipped a bare `mise` or `mise-*`, so it ran `mise hook-not-found` on the missing binary, which failed, re-entered the handler, and recursed until fish gave up.

The guard now also skips a path ending in `mise` or `mise-*`:

```fish
string match -qrv -- '^(?:.*/)?(?:mise$|mise-)' $argv[1]
```

bash and zsh are unaffected: they don't call their not-found handler for a command containing a slash (checked with a nonexistent `/nonexistent/bin/mise` in both).

Validated with `cargo test --lib shell::fish` (activate snapshot updated) and by running the new pattern in fish against a mise path and `node`. I did not reproduce the full `mise implode` flow.

Fixes #14590

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow fish shell-integration change with regression test; no auth or data-path impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a fish shell infinite loop after `mise implode` when not-found auto-install is enabled.
> 
> The generated `fish_command_not_found` guard now treats **path-shaped** invocations like `/home/user/.local/bin/mise` or `.../mise-foo` the same as bare `mise` / `mise-*`, so it does **not** run `mise hook-not-found` for those names. That stops re-entering the handler when the binary is gone and fish passes the full path.
> 
> Other missing commands still go through `hook-not-found`. Adds an e2e fish test and updates the fish activate snapshot.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 18345cd326741a9effd5bf6bdab9f661ba1ecf5a. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

--- e2e/cli/test_fish_hook_not_found_mise_path (+31/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# Test that fish's fish_command_not_found handler ignores a full path to mise.
+# After `mise implode`, fish passes the removed binary's absolute path to the handler;
+# calling `mise hook-not-found` on it re-entered the handler until fish hit its call stack limit.
+# https://github.com/jdx/mise/issues/14590
+
+if ! command -v fish >/dev/null; then
+  echo "fish not installed, skipping"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+mkdir -p stub
+cat >stub/mise <<EOF
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "\$@" >>"$PWD/calls.log"
+exit 1
+EOF
+chmod +x stub/mise
+
+MISE_NOT_FOUND_AUTO_INSTALL=1 mise activate fish --no-hook-env | sed "s#'\\?$(command -v mise)'\\?#$PWD/stub/mise#g" >activate.fish
+assert_contains "cat activate.fish" "$PWD/stub/mise hook-not-found"
+
+# a path to mise must return without calling hook-not-found, and without recursing
+fish -c "source activate.fish; fish_command_not_found /nonexistent/bin/mise; fish_command_not_found /nonexistent/bin/mise-foo; true" 2>&1
+assert_not_contains "cat calls.log 2>/dev/null || true" "hook-not-found"
+
+# any other command still reaches hook-not-found

title: fix(pipx): bind the real python for locked uv installs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/821
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

With a `python` tool configured and a `pypi:` tool installed from its locked uv graph, mise ran `uv sync --frozen … --python` with an **empty** interpreter path. uv then discovered its own interpreter (e.g. Homebrew `python@3.15`) instead of the configured mise python, which broke `--no-build` installs such as `yamllint` (no cp315 wheel for pyyaml).

`restore_uv_python` records the configured python's identity with an empty path placeholder, and `prepare_install_version` only bound the real interpreter when `uv_python` was unset. It now also binds when the restored path is empty, so `--python` receives the configured interpreter.

Fixes #14592

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Single conditional change in pipx install prep; only affects uv-lock installs with configured python and no behavior change when a real path is already bound.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes locked PyPI (`pipx`) installs passing an empty `--python` to `uv sync` when a mise `python` tool is configured.**
> 
> `restore_uv_python` can leave `uv_python` set with an **empty path** (identity only). `prepare_install_version` previously called `bind_uv_python` only when `uv_python` was missing, so frozen uv-lock installs could run with `--python ""` and uv would pick its own interpreter (e.g. Homebrew 3.15), breaking `--no-build` tools like `yamllint` on the intended CPython.
> 
> The bind step now runs when `uv_lock` is present and `uv_python` is unset **or** the stored interpreter path is empty, so `uv sync --python` always gets the real mise-managed executable.
>

title: feat(doctor): flag a mise-shim.exe template older than mise
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/820
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

On Windows, "exe" shims are byte copies of the `mise-shim.exe` that ships beside `mise.exe`. An update that replaces `mise.exe` but leaves an older `mise-shim.exe` behind keeps producing shims with the old launcher: `mise reshim --force` copies whatever template it finds, and nothing said so. In discussion #14494 a winget install had mise 2026.10.11 next to a `mise-shim.exe` from 2026.7.0, which predates the shim's recursion guard, so a cargo command wrapper looped forever through `mise x` no matter how often shims were rebuilt. The `.version` marker in the shims directory did not help: it records the mise that ran reshim, not the template the shims came from.

## What changes

`mise-shim.exe` now carries the mise release it shipped with, as a `mise-shim-version:<release>` tag mise can read back from the file. The release comes from the workspace `Cargo.toml`, not the `mise-shim` crate's own version, which does not move with releases.

When the template beside mise is older than mise, or has no tag at all (every `mise-shim.exe` before this change):

- `mise doctor` lists it as a problem.
- `mise reshim` (including `mise reshim --force` and the reshims that follow a tool install) warns once per run, and still rebuilds the shims.

Both say the same thing:

```text
mise-shim.exe at C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Microsoft\WinGet\Links\mise-shim.exe is older than mise 2026.10.13: it is from mise 2026.7.0
shims copied from it keep the old launcher, however often `mise reshim --force` runs
update mise with the package manager that installed it (or `mise self-update`) so mise-shim.exe is replaced too, then run `mise reshim --force`
```

For an untagged template the first line ends with `it has no version tag, so it predates this check`. Nothing is reported outside `windows_shim_mode = "exe"`, when no template exists (that case already warns), or when the template is the same release as mise or newer. `mise self-update` already refreshes `mise-shim.exe` next to mise; it copies the whole file, so the tag comes with it.

## Validation

Unit tests cover the tag scan (a current tag, an older tag, the prefix without a version, an unterminated tag, and bytes without a tag) and the staleness comparison. The tag's presence and its terminating newline were checked in `mise-shim` binaries built for Linux, `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, and the release profile. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes. The `mise doctor` and `mise reshim` paths themselves are `#[cfg(windows)]` and were not run here: the Windows CI builds `mise.exe` and `mise-shim.exe` from the same tree, so they exercise the "template is current" case.

Fixes the diagnosis gap from #14494. Requires a mise release built after this change on both sides: an older `mise-shim.exe` is reported as untagged, which is the intended outcome.

title: fix(hooks): don't report git rewrites when HEAD stayed on the same commit
body:
A `watch_files` command that skips git rewrites with `MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN`, as the docs suggest for format-on-edit hooks, also skipped files you had just edited when the next git command moved HEAD without changing commits:

```toml
[[watch_files]]
patterns = ["**/*.go"]
run = '[ -n "$MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN" ] || { IFS=:; hk fix $MISE_WATCH_FILES_MODIFIED; }'
```

Edit `main.go`, then run `git checkout -b feat` (or `git switch -c`, `git reset` to unstage, `git branch -m`) before the next prompt: the variable was `1` and `hk fix` never ran on the edit.

mise treated any HEAD reflog entry written after the file as git rewriting it, unless the entry was a commit. Those commands log an entry that leaves HEAD on the same commit, or, for a branch rename, logs no old commit, so they cannot have rewritten anything. mise now skips such entries and compares the files with the last entry that moved HEAD from one commit to another, so `git checkout other && git checkout -b feature` is still reported as a rewrite.

`git reset --hard` without a commit also leaves HEAD in place, so it is no longer reported as a rewrite. The docs now say so, next to the existing `git stash` limitation.

## Validation

- In a Debian container, edit a watched file, then run each command and read the variable from `mise hook-env`:

  | command after the edit       | 2026.10.12 | this branch |
  | ---------------------------- | ---------- | ----------- |
  | none                         | unset      | unset       |
  | `git checkout -b feat`       | `1`        | unset       |
  | `git add` + `git reset`      | `1`        | unset       |
  | `git branch -m feat feat2`   | `1`        | unset       |
  | `git switch -c feat3`        | `1`        | unset       |
  | `git checkout other` (no edit) | `1`      | `1`         |
  | `git checkout other && git checkout -b feature` (no edit) | `1` | `1` |

- `e2e/config/test_watch_files_git_rewritten` gains the `git checkout -b`, `git reset`, and checkout-then-`git checkout -b` cases; its existing `git checkout -` case still reports `1`.
- New unit tests for the reflog entry check in `src/watch_files.rs`.

title: refactor(daemons): move the daemon declarations, ports, presets, and runtime into mise-daemons
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/819
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change: the daemon declaration loader, ports, urls, presets, prune, providers, and the supervisor runtime (about 10k lines) become the `mise-daemons` crate. Behavior is unchanged.

Daemons are tied to mise's toolsets more tightly than the other splits, so this PR separates what only describes and runs daemons from what drives mise's config and toolsets, and moves the first group:

- **In `mise-daemons`:** the `[daemons]`, `[daemons_settings]`, and `[daemon_groups]` loader (`load`) and `DaemonSet`, ports, hostnames and urls, the preset engine, the preset registry itself (`registry/daemon-presets/*.toml` moved to `crates/mise-daemons/presets/`, with its build-time validation moved into the crate's `build.rs`), prune, providers, and the supervisor runtime.
- **Staying in `src/daemons/`:** `glue` (resolving and installing a project's tools for its daemons, plus `DaemonSetExt` for the toolset requests, exported env entries, and task validation that need mise's types), the `mise daemons providers` and `resource` commands, task daemons, and the hook-env integration. `mise::daemons` re-exports the crate, so existing `crate::daemons::…` paths still resolve.

The crate reaches mise only through `daemons::host`: a view of the loaded config files, config discovery and trust checks, and three function-level entries (`global_runtime`, `install_provider_tools`, `provider_tool_paths`) for the tool resolution a provider needs. mise registers it at startup from `daemons::glue`. Callers outside the crate convert a real `ConfigMap` with `glue::view_map`, or call `glue::load`.

Tests: the 165 tests that do not need mise's config run in the crate, against a stand-in host that parses the daemon tables from a config body and keeps its own trust list. The 13 that do (tool requests, exported env entries, and `paranoid` trust) moved to `src/daemons/glue_tests.rs` and still run in mise.

Stacked on #14582. `release-plz` publishes `mise-daemons` after `mise-oci`; it depends only on `mise-settings` and `mise-util`.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`.
- `cargo test -p mise -p mise-daemons --lib`: 3057 pass in mise and 165 in mise-daemons, one failure in mise (`has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, which fails on `main` in this sandbox). Together they account for the same tests as before the split.
- I did not run the daemon e2e tests, which need pitchfork.

title: refactor(system): move the bootstrap, dotfiles, and history modules into mise-system
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/817
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change: `src/system` (about 80k lines: bootstrap resources, dotfiles, history, services, files, edits, repositories, and the rest) becomes the `mise-system` crate. Behavior is unchanged.

This is the payoff of the previous PRs. System was the second most-edited area of the codebase; an edit to mise's core no longer recompiles it, and an edit to it no longer recompiles the core. `mise::system` re-exports the crate, so existing `crate::system::…` paths still resolve.

## What moved, and what stayed

- Everything under `src/system` moved with `git mv` except three files that need mise's config, toolset, and plugins: `bootstrap_host` (registers the host from #14575), `package_plugin`, and `packages_host`. They stay in `src/system/`.
- `mise-system` reaches mise only through `system::host`. Two more host entries were needed: `verify_release_signature` (so `remote` can check a mise release without owning mise's release key) and the history `describe_command` setting.
- `windows_job` moves to `mise-util` (it depends only on `windows-sys`; both system and the daemons use it), and `ui::table` moves to `mise-ui`.
- The macOS notification helper is now built by `mise-system`'s own `build.rs` instead of mise's, with its two icon assets copied into the crate (`assets/`) so the published package is self-contained.
- The crate logs through plain `log` and `calm_io` wrappers, as `mise-system-packages` does.
- The 749 system unit tests moved with the code. They run against a small stand-in host (`test_host.rs`) that parses the `[bootstrap]`, `[dotfiles]`, `[dotfile_groups]`, and `[history]` tables straight from a config body; the signed-release test verifies against a fixture key.
- Cleanup: root dependencies that only the system modules used are removed, and `release-plz` now publishes `mise-system` last, with `mise-system-config` moved after the crates it depends on. This also fixes `mise-system-config` being published before them.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, with no new warnings. macOS-only code in the moved files could not be compiled here.
- `cargo test -p mise -p mise-system --lib`: 3317 pass in mise and 749 in mise-system. One test fails in mise (`has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`), as it does on `main` in this sandbox. The two counts add up to the 4066 that passed before the split.

title: chore(deps): update zipsign-api and the release zipsign CLI to 0.2.2
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/816
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

zipsign 0.2.2 (released 2026-10-16) moves its `zip` dependency to 9, which has the fix for the `extract()` symlink and permission advisories (RUSTSEC-2026-0367, -0368, -0369). mise uses zipsign in two places, and both move to 0.2.2:

- **`mise self-update`:** `zipsign-api` 0.2.1 to 0.2.2 in the lockfile, which drops the `zip` 7.4.0 copy. The `Cargo.toml` requirement (`0.2`) already allows it.
- **Release signing:** `scripts/setup-zipsign.sh` installs the `zipsign` CLI that `scripts/release.sh` uses to sign and verify the release `.tar.gz` and `.zip` archives. It now installs 0.2.2 instead of 0.2.1. The old comment said `--locked` was needed because every `zip` release 0.2.1 resolved against had been yanked; 0.2.2 no longer has that problem, so the comment now just says it builds against zipsign's published lockfile. I ran `cargo install zipsign --version 0.2.2 --locked` locally and it builds and reports 0.2.2.

The remaining `zip` 8.6.0 in the lockfile comes from aube and ubi, so the `deny.toml` ignores stay, but their reasons no longer mention zipsign-api.

Validated with `cargo deny check` (clean), clippy with `-D warnings`, the `self_update` tests, and `shfmt -d` on the script. The signing flow itself only runs in the release workflow, so I haven't exercised it end to end.

title: ci: pin perf-runner image by tag and stop automerging it
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/815
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Renovate's runs on this repo report `Package lookup failures` for the perf-runner image (`Could not determine new digest for update`). The perf workflows pin the image by digest only, so Renovate looks for the `latest` tag, which `jdx/perf-runner` never publishes (it only pushes `jdx-perf-v1`), and gets a 404.

The pin now names the published tag as well:

```yaml
image: ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner:jdx-perf-v1@sha256:5263c143…
```

The digest is unchanged, so the image the perf jobs run does not change. Renovate can now follow the `jdx-perf-v1` tag and open a PR when the image is rebuilt.

The shared preset automerges digest updates, so this also adds a package rule that turns automerge off for `ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner`. A rebuilt image changes the toolchain every perf baseline is measured on, and that should go through the perf check, not merge on its own.

The `image:` strings that the workflows echo into the report are left as they were.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: Anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI workflow and Renovate config only; the container digest is unchanged so measured environments are unaffected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Renovate **package lookup failures** for the perf CI container by pinning `ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner` with the published **`jdx-perf-v1` tag** alongside the existing digest in `perf.yml` and `perf-pr.yml`. The digest is unchanged, so perf jobs still run the same image; Renovate can now track tag updates instead of resolving a non-existent `latest` tag.
> 
> Adds a **Renovate package rule** that disables automerge for `ghcr.io/jdx/perf-runner`, so image rebuilds (and toolchain changes) get reviewed rather than merging via the shared digest-automerge preset.
>

title: chore(deps): cargo update and bump zip to 9 for the symlink advisory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/813
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`zip` before 9.0.0 applies Unix permissions through extracted symlinks without checking the target stays inside the destination (GHSA-4684-h2q9-2vcp). mise extracts downloaded `.zip` tool archives with `ZipArchive::extract` (`mise_util::file::unzip`), so this moves mise's own `zip` dependency to 9.x. `cargo deny check` was failing on the advisory in CI for every open PR.

Per the maintainer's call this PR also runs a full `cargo update` rather than keeping the lockfile focused. It is run with `CARGO_RESOLVER_INCOMPATIBLE_RUST_VERSIONS=allow` so the resolver does not fall back to older Rust-1.88-compatible crates (a plain `cargo update` downgraded `aws-sdk-s3` and pulled in an `lru` version with RUSTSEC-2026-0253). Changes beyond the lockfile:

- `zip` 8 → 9 in the three manifests that declare it. `ZipFile::name()` now returns a `Result`, so the two SLSA content-check errors that print an entry name fall back to `<unreadable name>`.
- `rattler` 0.53 → 0.54 and `rattler_conda_types` 0.56 → 0.57, which the updated `rattler_solve` requires. The conda backend's test helper builds a `PackageRecord` with the new `BuildString` type.

`xx` is now 2.6.3, which uses zip 9 (jdx/xx#308, #310). `zip` 8.6.0 (via aube and ubi) and 7.x (via `zipsign-api`) remain in the lockfile where those crates still pin them; mise does not call their zip extraction. aube's own bump is jdx/aube#1756 and needs a release before mise can pick it up.

Validated with clippy (`-D warnings`, `--locked`), the conda and `mise-util` tests, and a clean `cargo deny check` (advisories, bans, licenses, sources) with a fresh advisory db.

title: fix(vfox): report an HTTP client that cannot be built instead of panicking
body:
On a system where the HTTP client cannot be built, for example a minimal container with no CA certificates, any vfox plugin that made an HTTP request aborted mise instead of failing with an error:

```console
$ mise install
The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  Failed to create reqwest client: reqwest::Error { kind: Builder, source: General("No CA certificates were loaded from the system") }
```

The vfox crate built its two HTTP clients with `.expect("Failed to create reqwest client")`. The failure now stays with the client and is returned by the request that needs it, as mise's own HTTP client already does:

```console
$ mise install
mise ✗ vfox:file:///plug@latest · failed: runtime error: Could not initialize the HTTP client: builder error: unexpected error: No CA certificates were loaded from the system
```

The message now includes the error's causes, since reqwest's `builder error` alone does not say what went wrong.

Plugin calls to `http.get`, `http.head` and `http.download_file` raise this as a Lua error. `http.try_get`, `http.try_head` and `http.try_download_file` return it as `nil, err`, like their other failures. Downloads during `mise install` return it as an install error.

This came up while checking #12237, whose crash in `mise use chromedriver` did not reproduce on 2026.10.11 or on the reporter's 2026.8.10 with the network unreachable.

## Validation

- In a Linux `rust:1` container with `ca-certificates` removed, a local vfox plugin whose `Available` hook calls `http.get`, run through `mise install`:
  - Released 2026.10.11: aborts with exit code 134 and the panic above.
  - This branch, built with the release features (`--no-default-features --features rustls-native-roots,vfox/vendored-lua,self_update`): exits 1 with the error above. With the default `native-tls` features the client builds without CA certificates, so that build never reaches this path.
- New unit test `http::tests::a_client_that_failed_to_build_is_an_error`; the `vfox` crate's `http` tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: refactor(system): reach the config layer through a registered host
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/812
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change, the last step before the system modules (bootstrap, dotfiles, history, about 80k lines) can move into their own crate. Behavior is unchanged.

The system modules read mise's loaded `Config` and its config files directly, which pins them to the same crate as the config layer. They now reach it only through `system::host`:

- `BootstrapConfig` and `ConfigFileView` describe the slice of `Config` and `ConfigFile` the system modules read: the config files per bootstrap root, the template context for a file, the dry-run variables, redaction, the tracked config files, and a few more. Inside `system`, the name `Config` is an alias for `dyn BootstrapConfig`, so most signatures are unchanged.
- `Host` carries the config-layer functions they call back into: the global config paths, trust checks, parsing a config file or a static config body, and reloading the config.
- mise registers all of it at startup from `system::bootstrap_host`, next to the existing hooks. Outside `system`, callers that hold a real `ConfigMap` convert it with `bootstrap_host::view_map`.

`ConfigFile` gains `history_config`, next to the other declaration accessors (`bootstrap_config`, `dotfiles_config`, `dotfile_groups_config`); `MiseToml` implements it with the same value as before. `defaults_from_config_files` is split out of `defaults_from_config` so a test no longer needs `Config::with_config_files`.

Stacked on #14573.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: 4066 pass, 1 fails (`has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, which fails on `main` in this sandbox).
- Seven e2e tests pass against a debug build of this branch: `test_bootstrap_config_roots`, `test_bootstrap_system_files`, `test_bootstrap_repos`, `test_bootstrap_secrets`, `test_bootstrap_dotfiles_reload`, `test_dotfiles_capture`, and `test_dotfiles_apply_config_first`.

title: refactor(config): move the [bootstrap] declaration types into mise-system-config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/810
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change, second step toward splitting `system/history` and the dotfiles modules out of mise's core. Behavior is unchanged.

After the previous PR moved `[dotfiles]`, `[dotfile_groups]`, and `[history]`, this moves the rest of what mise's config layer stores: the whole `[bootstrap]` tree. `mise-system-config` now holds `BootstrapTomlConfig` and every typed section it embeds:

- secrets, users and groups, repos, login items, launchd agents, remote hosts, managed files and directories, services, compose projects, systemd units, the Linux firewall (with its non-Linux raw-value form), and the package declarations;
- `Templated<T>` split in two: the data type and its `Deserialize` stay in the crate, and `render` / `render_with` become an extension trait (`TemplatedExt`) in mise, because rendering needs the config's template context.

The old paths re-export the types, so system-module call sites are unchanged. Two things stay in mise on purpose: `merge_below` for `[bootstrap]` (now the `BootstrapMerge` extension trait, since it applies mise's macOS-defaults normalization), and anything that interprets a declaration rather than describing it.

The point is the last commit. `config` no longer refers to `crate::system::…` for any type, and its one call into the dotfiles module (clearing cached invalid declarations on a config reload) now goes through `config::register_reset_hook`, registered at startup next to the other hooks. The dotfiles and history modules can therefore move into their own crate without a cycle through `config`; that is the next step.

Types moved verbatim; `pub(crate)` became `pub` where a method crossed the crate boundary. Stacked on #14569.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. I could not check macOS-only code here.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: 4060 pass, 1 fails (`has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, which fails on `main`-based branches in this sandbox).

+    accounts, compose, firewall, login_items, managed_files, packages::PackageTomlConfig, remote,
+    repos, secrets, services_common as services, templating::Templated,
+};
+
+/// `[bootstrap]` as parsed from a single mise.toml
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapTomlConfig {
+    /// Independent configuration roots whose declarative files and dotfiles
+    /// participate in bootstrap composition.
+    pub config_roots: Option<Vec<String>>,
+    /// The `[dotfile_groups]` (and `group = "..."` entries) to apply; every
+    /// group applies when unset. A later layer's list replaces earlier ones.
+    pub dotfile_groups: Option<Vec<String>>,
+    /// Logical secret name -> environment input declaration.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub secrets: IndexMap<String, secrets::SecretTomlConfig>,
+    /// Linux group name -> declarative local group.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub groups: IndexMap<String, accounts::GroupTomlConfig>,
+    /// Linux user name -> declarative local user.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub users: IndexMap<String, accounts::UserTomlConfig>,
+    /// Linux systemd unit name -> declarative system service lifecycle.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub services: IndexMap<String, services::ServiceTomlConfig>,
+    /// Docker Compose project name -> declarative project lifecycle.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub compose: IndexMap<String, Templated<compose::ComposeTomlConfig>>,
+    /// OpenSSH targets used by `mise bootstrap remote`.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub remote: remote::RemoteTomlConfig,
+    /// Package manager plugins that must be installed, keyed by manager name.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub plugins: IndexMap<String, String>,
+    /// `"manager:package"` -> version/options (`"latest"` or a manager-native pin).
+    /// String-keyed so configs using managers from newer mise versions (dnf,
+    /// pacman, winget, ...) parse fine on older ones.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub packages: IndexMap<String, PackageTomlConfig>,
+    /// Absolute target path -> declarative managed file.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub files: IndexMap<String, managed_files::ManagedFileTomlConfig>,
+    /// Absolute target path -> declarative managed directory.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub directories: IndexMap<String, managed_files::ManagedDirectoryTomlConfig>,
+    /// `"~/path"` -> git repo checkout.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub repos: IndexMap<String, repos::RepoTomlConfig>,
+    /// macOS-specific bootstrap config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub macos: BootstrapMacosTomlConfig,
+    /// Linux-specific bootstrap config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub linux: BootstrapLinuxTomlConfig,
+    /// User-specific bootstrap config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub user: BootstrapUserTomlConfig,
+    /// Homebrew-specific bootstrap package config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub brew: SystemBrewTomlConfig,
+    /// apt-specific bootstrap package config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub apt: SystemAptTomlConfig,
+    /// dnf-specific bootstrap package config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub dnf: SystemDnfTomlConfig,
+    /// Shell activation setup. Values stay raw TOML so future options can warn
+    /// and be skipped without rejecting the whole config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub mise_shell_activate: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// Bootstrap phase hooks. Values stay raw TOML so newer hook shapes can
+    /// warn and be skipped without rejecting the whole config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub hooks: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+}
+
+/// The commands of a `[bootstrap.hooks]` value, in the shapes the hook parser accepts.
+pub fn hook_commands(value: toml::Value) -> Option<Vec<toml::Value>> {
+    match value {
+        toml::Value::String(_) => Some(vec![value]),
+        toml::Value::Array(values) => Some(values),
+        toml::Value::Table(mut table) => match table.remove("run")? {
+            run @ toml::Value::String(_) => Some(vec![run]),
+            toml::Value::Array(values) => Some(values),
+            _ => None,
+        },
+        _ => None,
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapUserTomlConfig {
+    /// desired login shell for the current user, applied with `chsh -s`
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub login_shell: Option<String>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapMacosTomlConfig {
+    /// Friendly Dock settings that compile into `[bootstrap.macos.defaults]`.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub dock: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// Friendly Finder settings that compile into `[bootstrap.macos.defaults]`.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub finder: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// Friendly keyboard settings that compile into `[bootstrap.macos.defaults]`.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub keyboard: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// Friendly trackpad settings that compile into `[bootstrap.macos.defaults]`.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub trackpad: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// `[bootstrap.macos.defaults.<domain>]` -> key -> value. Values stay raw TOML so
+    /// shapes from newer mise versions (arrays, dicts) parse fine on older
+    /// ones; the domain level is also raw so a malformed section warns
+    /// instead of failing the whole config.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub defaults: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,
+    /// Explicit preferences with a selectable host scope.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub defaults_entries: Vec<BootstrapMacosDefaultsEntry>,
+    /// `[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents.<name>]`: declarative macOS user
+    /// LaunchAgents rendered to ~/Library/LaunchAgents.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub launchd: BootstrapMacosLaunchdTomlConfig,
+    /// `[bootstrap.macos.login_items]`: applications to open at login.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub login_items: Option<login_items::LoginItemsTomlConfig>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
+#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
+pub struct BootstrapMacosDefaultsEntry {
+    pub domain: String,
+    pub key: String,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub host: HostScope,
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub path: Option<Vec<String>>,
+    pub value: toml::Value,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapMacosLaunchdTomlConfig {
+    /// User LaunchAgents, keyed by a short stable name. mise gives these a
+    /// `dev.mise.<name>` label when rendering the plist.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub agents: IndexMap<String, Templated<LaunchdTomlConfig>>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapLinuxTomlConfig {
+    /// Declarative Linux host firewall policy and rules.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub firewall: Option<firewall::FirewallTomlConfig>,
+    /// `[bootstrap.linux.systemd.units.<name>]`: declarative systemd user
+    /// services and timers rendered to ~/.config/systemd/user.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub systemd: BootstrapLinuxSystemdTomlConfig,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct BootstrapLinuxSystemdTomlConfig {
+    /// User services and timers, keyed by a short stable name. mise gives
+    /// these a `dev.mise.<name>.<service|timer>` unit name when rendering.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub units: IndexMap<String, Templated<SystemdTomlConfig>>,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone, Deserialize)]
+pub struct SystemBrewTomlConfig {
+    /// Adopt identical existing app bundles for brew-cask entries by default.
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub adopt: Option<bool>,
+    /// `[bootstrap.brew.taps]`: `owner/tap` -> GitHub git URL. Like
+    /// `[plugins]`, this lets shared config name tap remotes while package
+    /// entries stay focused on formulae/casks.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub taps: IndexMap<String, String>,
+}

+pub struct SystemAptTomlConfig {

+    /// before apt packages are installed.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub sources: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,

+    /// `[bootstrap.dnf.repos]`: repository name -> COPR project, enabled
+    /// before dnf packages are installed.
+    #[serde(default)]
+    pub repos: IndexMap<String, toml::Value>,

title: feat(bootstrap): expose system_brew_prefix to templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/809
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Config that refers to the built-in Homebrew prefix had to hard-code it per platform (`/opt/homebrew` on macOS, `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew` on Linux), usually with a platform-specific config file just to set a var. Templates can now use `{{ system_brew_prefix }}`, available everywhere templates are, like `xdg_config_home`:

```toml
[env]
PKG_CONFIG_PATH = "{{ system_brew_prefix }}/opt/mysql-client/lib/pkgconfig"
```

On Linux `mise env` exports `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/opt/mysql-client/lib/pkgconfig`; on Apple Silicon it exports the `/opt/homebrew` path. The value is exactly the prefix `mise bootstrap` installs brew packages into, including the undocumented `MISE_SYSTEM_BREW_PREFIX` override: the resolution now lives in one `mise_util::env::system_brew_prefix()` shared by the brew code and the template context.

Combined with #14570 (templated `bootstrap.user.login_shell`), `login_shell = "{{ system_brew_prefix }}/bin/zsh"` works. This is the second half of jdx/mise#14568. It does not detect an existing Homebrew install elsewhere (e.g. Intel `/usr/local`); it reports mise's own prefix.

Validated with the new `e2e/cli/test_system_brew_prefix_template` and clippy. Local `hk` `cargo-check` fails on an unrelated `Cargo.toml` manifest lint, so the commit skipped the hook.

> **Overview**
> Adds **`{{ system_brew_prefix }}`** so config can reference mise’s built-in Homebrew install prefix without hard-coding `/opt/homebrew` vs `/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew`.
>

title: fix(bootstrap): render templates in bootstrap.user.login_shell
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/808
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.user].login_shell` was the one `[bootstrap]` string that mise never rendered, so `{{ vars.* }}` stayed literal and the path was rejected as not absolute. It is now a template, rendered without `exec()` like other `[bootstrap]` values.

```toml
[bootstrap.user]
login_shell = "{{ vars.brew_prefix }}/bin/zsh"

[vars]
brew_prefix = "/opt/homebrew"
```

`mise bootstrap user status` now reports `/opt/homebrew/bin/zsh`. A template that fails to render warns and skips that entry, like other invalid `login_shell` values. Reported in jdx/mise#14568 (first half).

Validated with `e2e/cli/test_system_login_shell` (new `vars` case) and clippy. Local `hk` `cargo-check` fails on an unrelated `Cargo.toml` manifest lint, so the commit skipped the hook.

title: refactor(config): move [dotfiles], [dotfile_groups], and [history] types into mise-system-config
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/807
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change, first step of a series that lets mise's config layer and its system modules (`system/history`, dotfiles, bootstrap) become separate crates. Behavior is unchanged.

Today `config` stores the parsed `[bootstrap]`, `[dotfiles]`, `[dotfile_groups]`, and `[history]` sections, while the system modules interpret them and call back into `Config`. That cycle is what keeps `system/history` (about 35k lines) and its neighbors from being extracted. The way out is to put the plain declaration types in a crate below both.

This PR creates `mise-system-config` and moves the three smallest self-contained sets into it:

- `DotfilesTomlConfig` (`[dotfiles]`) and `DotfileGroupsTomlConfig` (`[dotfile_groups]`);
- `HistoryTomlConfig` (`[history]`) with `OriginTomlConfig` (`[history.origin]`) and `FileEncryptionConfig` (`[history.encryption]`).

The old paths re-export them, so no call sites change. Parsing, defaults, and `deny_unknown_fields` are untouched; the types moved verbatim, with `pub(crate)` widened to `pub`.

Next in the series: the `[bootstrap]` tree (`BootstrapTomlConfig` and the typed sections it embeds), then a host seam for the few `Config` calls the system modules make, then the extraction itself.

Stacked on #14567. `release-plz` publishes the new crate first, since it has no internal dependencies.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`.
- I did not re-run the unit-test suite: no code besides these type definitions changed.

title: refactor(system): move system package managers into mise-system-packages
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/806
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal change: `src/system/packages` (about 38k lines: apt, dnf, brew, brew-cask, pacman, and the other system package managers) becomes the `mise-system-packages` crate. Behavior is unchanged.

The point is build time. An edit to mise's core no longer recompiles these managers, and an edit to a manager no longer recompiles mise's core. `mise::system::packages` re-exports the crate, so existing `crate::system::packages::…` paths still resolve.

## What changed

- The code moves with `git mv`; the only edits are visibility (`pub(crate)` becomes `pub` where mise or `oci` calls across the boundary) and the crate-path rewrite.
- The crate depends on `mise-util`, `mise-settings`, and `mise-ui`, and reaches mise only through `packages::host`, set up in the previous PR.
- `debug!`, `info!`, `warn!`, and `miseprintln!` are thin wrappers over `log` and `calm_io` inside the crate. mise's versions only capture output in mise's own tests, and nothing here read that capture.
- `mise-brew-metadata` and `mise-brew-relocation` are now dependencies of this crate rather than mise; Windows-only builds no longer pull in the unix-only ones.
- The crate's tests use a `test/` home under the crate (gitignored), because the cask tests need ancestors that are not world-writable, so `/tmp` does not work. They use the settings defaults and a PATH-based host: ruby comes from `PATH` instead of being provisioned.
- `release-plz` publishes the new crate after `mise-brew-metadata`.

Stacked on #14564.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-targets` passes on Linux and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`, without new warnings.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib`: 4060 pass, 1 fails (`has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, which fails on the earlier PRs too).
- The new crate's own tests: 566 pass, 6 fail (`brew::tap::tests::*`). They execute a real Ruby, and the only one in this sandbox lives under `~/.local/share/mise`, which the metadata sandbox refuses to execute. Hosts with a system Ruby should not hit this, but I could not confirm that here, so CI is the real check.
- For scale, a one-line edit then `cargo check --workspace` takes 7s in `src/toolset/mod.rs` and 8s in a package manager. I did not measure the same edits before the split.

title: fix(mcp): include the cause when a resource read fails
body:
An MCP client that reads a resource in a project whose config needs trust gets only the outer error:

```text
Failed to load config: error parsing config file: ~/src/app/mise.toml
```

The reason and the `mise trust` hint are dropped: the resource handlers format the eyre report with `{e}`, which prints only its top message. They now use `{e:#}`, as `mise doctor` does, so the client gets the whole chain:

```text
Failed to load config: error parsing config file: ~/src/app/mise.toml: Config files in ~/src/app/mise.toml are not trusted.
Trust them with `mise trust`. See https://mise.jdx.dev/cli/trust.html for more information.
```

I checked it with agents in an untrusted project with valid TOML: Claude Code (Opus 5.5, Haiku 5.5) and opencode (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.3, GPT-5.6 Luna, Qwen 3.8 Flash, Kimi K3). With the old message, all seven took it for a TOML syntax error and suggested editing the file. With this change, all seven said the file isn't trusted and gave `mise trust`.

The other errors in `read_resource` (tool request set, toolset, tool versions, tasks, env) wrap reports the same way and get the same change. `docs/mcp.md` shows the new message, and `e2e/cli/test_mcp_config_error_cause` reads each resource in an untrusted project.

Not changed here: `docs/errors.md` and `docs/faq.md` say `mise doctor` reports an untrusted file only as `failed to load config: error parsing config file: <path>`, but doctor already prints the cause after it.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.301.*

title: feat(shim): render command wrapper values as templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/805
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[wrappers]` values were passed through literally, so a wrapper could not build a path the way a task can. Now `command`, `args` and `env` render as templates when the shim runs:

```toml
[vars]
mode = "fast"

[wrappers.foo]
command = "foo-real"
args = ["--mode={{ vars.mode }}"]
env = { FOO_HOME = "{{ [xdg_data_home, 'foo'] | join_path }}" }
```

- Templates see `vars`, `env` and the usual functions; values without template syntax are untouched.
- A command that renders blank is an error.
- Not available: `tools` and `config_root`, since wrappers resolve before tools are necessarily installed.

Closes discussion #14563.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Shim dispatch now depends on template rendering and different Tera contexts for command vs args/env; misconfigured templates or unintended `{{` in values could change wrapper behavior at runtime.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Command wrapper `command`, `args`, and `env` values are now rendered as [Tera templates](/templates.html) when a shim runs**, instead of being passed through literally.
> 
> `command` is evaluated with `vars` and the process environment only (via `config.tera_ctx`), so auto-install and self-delegation checks use the rendered target; a blank rendered command fails. `args` and `env` use the full toolset context (including resolved `[env]`) when any value contains template syntax; otherwise the fast path keeps static args/env. A shared `render_template` helper skips rendering when there is no template syntax.
> 
> Docs explain the context split, `join_path` / `vars` examples, and `{% raw %}` for literals like Docker's `{{.Names}}`. An e2e test exercises templated args and env through a fake wrapper command.
