title: fix(vfox): pass each version only its own tool options
body:
When a `vfox:` tool lists several versions, each one is meant to get its own tool options. An option that only the first entry sets reached the other versions' plugin hooks too:

```toml
[tools]
"vfox:file:///path/to/plugin" = [
  { version = "1.0.0", extensions = "a" },
  { version = "2.0.0" },
]
```

While `2.0.0` was installing, its hooks saw `MISE_TOOL_OPTS__EXTENSIONS=a`. With the second entry on its own, the variable is unset.

The vfox backend built the options for a version's hooks from the config's options for the tool, then layered the version's own request options over them. The config lookup always took the first entry, so any option a later entry left out came from the first one. The config layer is now the entry for that version, picked the way mise already matches a version named on the command line to its config entry (`configured_options_for_runtime_request`). When no entry matches, the first one is still used, as before.

The config layer stays because some paths have no options of their own. `mise uninstall vfox:…@1.0.0` builds its request from the argument alone, and the plugin's uninstall hook still needs the options configured for `1.0.0`. Dropping the config layer broke that case in `test_vfox_tool_options`.

#14537 fixes the same problem for `github:`. `http:` and `s3:` already install from each version's own options.

## Validation

- New `e2e/backend/test_vfox_multi_entry_options`: a local plugin records `MISE_TOOL_OPTS__EXTENSIONS` per version, with `extensions` set on `1.0.0` only.
- In a Linux `rust:1` container, the new test fails with the released 2026.10.11 (`2.0.0` sees `opentelemetry`) and passes with this branch. `test_vfox_tool_options`, `test_vfox_install_env` and `test_vfox_pre_uninstall` pass too.
- `backend::vfox`, `toolset::tool_request_set` and `config` unit tests pass, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `test_vfox_backend_npm` fails in that container with both the released binary and this branch, because the container has no `npm`.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/802
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-visible change: `mise lock` output, ordering, locking and rollback behavior are unchanged.

`run_with_installed` in `src/cli/lock.rs` was a ~700-line function mixing option setup, input snapshotting, per-target resolution, lockfile writing/pruning and the atomic publish/rollback transaction. It is now a short driver over named phases, which makes each step reviewable and testable on its own:

- `snapshot_inputs`: reads config/lockfile inputs and takes the generation locks
- `prepare_targets`: resolves the tools for every lockfile target before anything is written
- `lock_target`, dispatching to `prune_empty_target`, `dry_run_empty_target`, `dry_run_target` and `generate_target` / `bind_and_write_target`
- `plan_config_bumps`, `report_no_lock_targets`
- `publish_staged_writes` and `report_published_write`: the atomic commit with rollback

State that used to be local variables now lives in small context structs (`LockSetup`, `LockInputs`, `LockRun`, `PreparedTarget`, `ResolvedTarget`, `LockOutcome`) instead of long parameter lists. No logic, message or ordering changes, and no clippy exclusions.

It is the first step toward splitting `system/packages` out of the core crate, which needs these pieces below it (`system::sudo` and the brew installers both use them).

`crates/mise-ui` holds `progress_report`, `multi_progress_report`, `install_progress`, `text_install_progress`, `tty_install_progress`, `prompt`, `ctrlc`, and `theme`. `mise::ui` re-exports the crate, so every existing `crate::ui::…` path still resolves.

title: perf(config): parse each settings file once per load
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/796
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Startup no longer reads the global settings file twice. #14538 made settings loading a two-step process: a global-only pass that the trust check depends on, then a trusted pass that adds the project files. Both passes parsed the global config, so every mise invocation read and parsed `~/.config/mise/config.toml` (and any system config) twice.

Each settings file is now parsed once per load. The two passes share a cache that exists only while `load()` runs, so reloads still see edits made between loads. A failed parse is cached too, so its warning is not repeated.

This landed in the same branch as #14538 but after it was squash-merged, so it is not on `main` yet. There is no behavior change beyond the avoided work. I did not time startup; the guarantee is covered by a unit test (`test_load_parses_each_settings_file_once`) that edits a file between two parses in one load and checks that the second parse still sees the first result, while a parse outside a load sees the edit.

Also run: the settings unit tests, the trust and settings e2e tests (including `test_untrusted_project_settings` and `test_config_env`), and clippy with `-D warnings`.

title: fix(ci): install zipsign with --locked
body:
## Problem

The `release` job of the `release` workflow fails in `./scripts/setup-zipsign.sh`:

```
error: failed to compile `zipsign v0.2.1`, intermediate artifacts can be found at `/tmp/cargo-install4nnkeK`.
  failed to select a version for the requirement `zip = ">=2.0.0, <7.0.0"`
```

This is what failed the [v2026.10.12 release run](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/38903293961) (job `release`, all tarball builds green): the tag exists but has no GitHub Release, so v2026.10.12 never shipped and every later release hits the same step.

## Root cause

`cargo install zipsign` resolves dependencies against the live index. Every `zip` release in the range zipsign 0.2.1 accepts — 2.0.0 through 8.6.0 — has been yanked from crates.io (only 9.0.3+ is live, above zipsign-api's `<8` bound). Fresh resolution has no candidate, so the install fails deterministically; re-running the workflow cannot fix it.

This also blocks users from the aqua registry fix vendored in v2026.10.12 (#14496, aquaproj/aqua-registry@c6a1898576): on 2026.10.11, `mise install oxlint@latest` still fails with `This version is unavailable` because oxc renamed its release tags back to `oxlint_v` in 1.85.0 and the older baked registry marks that prefix as unavailable for >= 1.17.0.

## Change

`cargo install zipsign --locked` builds from zipsign 0.2.1's published `Cargo.lock`, whose pinned `zip` version still resolves — yanking removes a version from fresh resolution, not from existing lockfiles.

## Validation

- `cargo install zipsign --root …` (unpinned, current behavior): fails with the same resolver error as CI (`required by package zipsign-api v0.2.0 … version 6.0.0 is yanked`).
- `cargo install zipsign --locked --root …`: installs; `zipsign --version` → `zipsign 0.2.1`.

After this merges, re-dispatching the release workflow for v2026.10.12 should publish it.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Setup now installs zipsign using locked dependency versions, making its installation more consistent across environments. No user-facing features or behavior changed.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
author: fang2hou
diff:
--- scripts/setup-zipsign.sh (+3/-1)
@@ -7,7 +7,9 @@ if [ -z "$ZIPSIGN" ]; then
 fi
 
 if ! command -v zipsign >/dev/null 2>&1; then
-	cargo install zipsign
+	# --locked: every zip release zipsign 0.2.1 can resolve against has been
+	# yanked, so a fresh resolution fails; the published Cargo.lock still resolves.
+	cargo install zipsign --locked
 fi
 
 mkdir -p ~/.zipsign

title: feat(bootstrap): template repo url and ref, add clone options
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/794
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap.repos]` could not vary a checkout by branch, and every clone was a full one. Now `url` and `ref` render as templates, like the checkout path already does, and `filter`, `depth` and `submodules` shape the first clone.

```toml
[vars]
branch = "main"

[bootstrap.repos]
"~/src/large" = { url = "git@github.com:example/large.git", ref = "{{ vars.branch }}", filter = "blob:none", depth = 1 }
```

`mise bootstrap repos apply` then runs `git clone --branch main --filter=blob:none --depth 1 …`. Previously the literal `{{ vars.branch }}` went to git, and `filter`/`depth` were ignored with an "unknown field" warning.

- `url` and `ref` render from `[vars]` or the process environment (`env.NAME`); values set in a config's `[env]` table are not available, as with the checkout path. `exec()` is still unavailable, and reading a var never prompts.
- `filter` is passed as `--filter=<spec>`, `depth` as `--depth <n>`, and `submodules = true` as `--recurse-submodules`.
- These options affect only the first clone; an existing checkout keeps the shape it was cloned with.
- `depth` must be at least 1 and cannot be combined with a commit SHA or `refs/…` `ref`, which a shallow clone can't check out. An empty or `-`-prefixed `filter` is rejected.
- `lfs` from the discussion is not included; it needs git-lfs and separate handling.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- New unit tests cover the clone command and option validation, and `e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_repos` passes with a real shallow, blobless clone from a templated `url` and `ref`.
- `cargo test --lib system::` has 6 `brew::cask::tests::cask_shim_*` failures in code this PR doesn't touch; I did not diff them against `main`.
- The pre-commit hook's `cargo-check` step fails on an unrelated `Cargo.toml` manifest warning in this environment, so the commit skipped hk after the other steps passed.

title: feat(ls-remote): list every version range of a registry tool
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/792
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When a registry tool's backends serve different version ranges, `mise ls-remote <tool>` showed only the first backend's range. hk publishes packslip manifests from 1.58.1 and uses aqua before that, so `mise ls-remote hk` started at 1.58.1.

`ls-remote` now lists each range from the backend that serves it:

```console
$ mise ls-remote hk 1.58
1.58.0
1.58.1
```

Before this change, the same command printed only `1.58.1` (from packslip). `mise ls-remote hk` now lists 0.1.4 through 2.7.0.

## Behavior

- **Which version comes from where.** Each version is taken from the first eligible backend whose range contains it, and only if that backend lists it. A version that a fallback backend lists inside another backend's range is dropped, because installing it would select the other backend.
- **Which backends get listed.** mise lists backends in order until their ranges cover every version. A fallback the earlier ranges make unreachable is never queried; for example, an asdf plugin behind a v1/v2 split isn't installed just to list it.
- **Prefixes.** A prefix inside one range, such as `mise ls-remote hk 1.2` or `mise ls-remote hk 2`, lists only that range's backend. A prefix that crosses a boundary lists both sides.
- **Inline options** such as `mise ls-remote 'hk[prerelease=true]'` apply to each range's backend.
- **Unchanged:**
  - An explicit backend such as `mise ls-remote aqua:jdx/hk`.
  - A `MISE_BACKENDS_*` override, a config backend alias, a custom plugin, or a lockfile entry that pins another backend. Each still lists only the backend it installs from.
  - Tools with a single backend.
  - `mise ls-remote --all`.
  - `mise ls-remote --strict-metadata`, which mise-versions uses to build the list it hosts for each tool. Clients read that list as the preferred backend's own; packslip, for example, treats it as the releases that carry a packslip. So it keeps listing the preferred backend alone, and hk's hosted list still starts at 1.58.1.
  - Version resolution for `install`/`use`. `latest` already resolves on the newest range's backend, and a concrete version already routes to the backend that serves it.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover range owners, including a gap between ranges, and choosing the backend for a version.
- `test_ls_remote*` and `test_registry*` e2e tests pass.
- Checked against the live sources:
  - `mise ls-remote hk` lists 150 versions; it used to start at 1.58.1.
  - `mise ls-remote hk 1.58` prints `1.58.0` and `1.58.1`.

title: feat(registry): let one backend carry different options per version range
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/791
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A registry entry can now list one backend more than once, with each entry covering its own `min_version`/`max_version` range and carrying its own `options`. A tool whose release assets or workflow changed at some version can stay on one backend instead of needing a second backend just to change an option. This is similar to aqua's `version_overrides`.

```toml
backends = [
  { full = "github:example/tool", min_version = "2.0.0", options = { asset_pattern = "tool-v2-*" } },
  { full = "github:example/tool", max_version = "2.0.0", options = { asset_pattern = "tool-*" } },
]
version_order = "semver"
```

`tool@1.4.0` installs with `tool-*` and `tool@2.1.0` with `tool-v2-*`. Requests that aren't routed by version, such as `latest`, use the first entry's options, as they did before.

## Rules

- **A backend listed twice still counts once.** In `mise registry` and in backend selection, it sits at the first entry that applies.
- **Options must be unambiguous.** Two entries for the same backend may not give the same version different options. The bundled and floating registries both reject that. Entries whose `platforms` don't overlap are exempt; glab already lists `gitlab:gitlab-org/cli` once per platform. Identical repeated entries also stay valid, so a floating registry that still has kubeone's accidental duplicate keeps loading. This PR removes that duplicate.
- **Option lookup now checks the platform too.** When a backend has entries for several platforms, mise picks the options from the entry for the current platform.
- **Windows on arm64 matches x64 entries too, since it can run x64 builds.** The overlap check counts `windows-x64`/`x64` entries as overlapping `windows-arm64`/`arm64` ones, so arm64 can't end up with the x64 entry's options.
- **Table syntax uses the routed entry's defaults.** `tool = { version = "1.4.0" }` now takes its registry defaults from the entry that version selects. Before, mise copied the first entry's options into the request. That also affected `min_version` tools: `hk = { version = "1.57.0" }` installs from aqua but carried packslip's `workflow` option.
- **Older mise releases read only the first entry's options.** They apply them to every version, so entries that use this need a client with this change. The contributor docs say so.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover option selection by version, de-duplication, the overlap rule, and platform disjointness.
- A unit test parses `hk = { version = "1.57.0" }` and checks the request has no `workflow` option. It fails without the fix.
- `test_registry*` and `test_ls_remote*` e2e tests pass. `test_registry_floating` downloads the live floating registry.

title: fix(watch): exit quietly when watchexec is interrupted with Ctrl+C
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/790
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Pressing Ctrl+C twice in `mise watch` no longer ends with an error banner. With watchexec 2.8.0 the second Ctrl+C makes watchexec exit with status 130 (128 + SIGINT), and mise reported that as a failure:

```
^Cmise ERROR command ["watchexec", "--clear", "--restart", "--", ".../mise", "run", "..."] exited with code 130
mise ERROR Version: 2026.10.11 linux-x64 (2026-10-15)
mise ERROR Run with --verbose or MISE_VERBOSE=1 for more information
```

Now `mise watch` treats watchexec ending with exit status 130, or being killed by SIGINT, as the user interrupting it: it prints nothing and exits with 130. Any other non-zero status from watchexec is still an error, and a SIGTERM is not mistaken for Ctrl+C.

Reported in [discussion #8269](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/8269#discussioncomment-18967361).

## Validation

- Added a unit test for the exit-status classification (130, SIGINT, success, generic failure, SIGTERM).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- No e2e test: reproducing it needs a pty and a watchexec that exits 130.

Prefer xcsift's signed Packslip archives starting with its first signed release, **1.7.0**, and allow Linux x64 installation alongside macOS ARM64:

```sh

- Installed and ran `xcsift --version` on Linux x64: 1.7.0 through Packslip and 1.6.0 through the GitHub fallback.

Discovery lists 1.7.0 with a test-only zero-age override; normal discovery currently hides this fresh release under the unchanged 24-hour minimum-release-age policy. `mise link` for any version made `mise install --locked` fail for the same tool's other versions, even though `mise.lock` was untouched. Fixes #14521.

title: security(config): ignore [settings] from untrusted project configs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/787
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise now ignores the `[settings]` table of a project config until that config is trusted, the same as `[tools]` options, `[env]` and `[hooks]`. Before, a repository's `mise.toml` could change settings the moment mise discovered it, with no trust prompt.

That mattered because many settings steer what an install downloads or runs. For example, `node.mirror_url`, `node.make_opts`, `python.pyenv_repo` and `ruby.precompiled_url` all redirect a download or feed a build command. An untrusted checkout could set them and affect an install triggered from a shim or `mise ls-remote`, even though its `[tools]` were never loaded.

```toml
# mise.toml in a freshly cloned repo
[settings.python]
pyenv_repo = "https://example.invalid/pyenv.git"
```

```console
$ mise settings get python.pyenv_repo   # before: https://example.invalid/pyenv.git
https://github.com/pyenv/pyenv.git      # after, until `mise trust`
$ mise trust && mise settings get python.pyenv_repo
https://example.invalid/pyenv.git
```

- Trusted projects behave as before, so a repo can still pin a mirror or `compile = true` once you trust it.
- Global and system config, environment variables and CLI flags are unaffected.
- Commands that implicitly trust the active config (`mise run`, `mise exec`, `mise install`, ...) reload settings after trusting it, so the project's settings still apply to that same invocation.
- This replaces the per-key `global_only` list as the safeguard for project settings: new settings are covered without having to be flagged. The list stays for settings that must never come from a project even when it is trusted.
- Settings files are parsed once per load: the global-only pass that bootstraps the trust check and the trusted pass share a per-load parse cache, so startup does not read global config twice.

The docs already said `[settings]` needs trust; this makes the code match.

Tested with the new `e2e/config/test_untrusted_project_settings` (untrusted, trusted, untrusted again, and `mise run` on a never-trusted repo), the existing trust, settings, safe-mode and paranoid e2e tests (54 files), the settings unit tests, and clippy with `-D warnings`. I could not run `mise run lint` to completion locally because of an unrelated `Cargo.toml` manifest warning; the other lint steps passed.

title: fix(github): install each version with its own request options
body:
When a `github:` tool lists several versions, each one is meant to install with its own options. An option that only the first entry sets was applied to the others too:

```toml
[tools]
"github:jqlang/jq" = [
  { version = "1.7.1", version_prefix = "jq-", rename_exe = "jqa" },
  { version = "1.8.1", version_prefix = "jq-" },
]
```

Both versions were installed as `jqa`. With the second entry on its own, `1.8.1` is installed as `jq`.

The GitHub backend (also used for `gitlab:` and `forgejo:`) read its install options from the config, which takes the first entry's options for the whole tool. It now reads them from the version's own request when it installs, when it checks that an install is complete, and when it counts install steps. The backend's other install paths already did so.

That request carries the same layers the config lookup added, registry defaults and backend-alias options included, and for a version named on the command line, the options of the config entry for that version. It moved to the config lookup in #8084 and #8492, when the request lacked aliased tools' config options and registry options. It has carried both since #9306, so their tests are part of the validation below.

This is the install-time half of the problem #14476 fixes for version resolution. Other backends that read install options from the config, such as `http:` and `s3:`, are left out.

## Validation

- New `e2e/backend/test_github_multi_entry_install_options`: `github:jdx/tiny` with `rename_exe = "my-tiny"` on `2.0.0` only; `1.1.0` must keep `tiny`.
- In a Linux `rust:1` container, the new test fails with the released 2026.10.11 (`1.1.0/bin` holds `my-tiny`) and passes with this branch. With this branch, `test_github_rename_exe*` and the tests for the earlier fixes, `test_github_tool_alias_asset_pattern` and `test_github_tool_alias_matching`, pass too.
- `backend::github` unit tests pass, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- With mise 2026.10.9 on Windows, the `jq` config above installed `1.8.1` as `jqa.exe`, and as `jq.exe` on its own.

title: fix(task): avoid deadlock when parallel tasks install the same tool
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/786
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14526.

`mise run` could hang forever when parallel tasks needed the same tool that wasn't installed yet. In the issue, tasks `a` and `b` both use `jq`: the install finished (`✓ installed 1 tool`), but `a` and `b` never started and `mise run` never exited. `--jobs 1` avoided it.

## Cause

Two blocking file locks were taken on async worker threads while the lock holder was another install in the same process:

- `reshim_for` held the shims-dir file lock across `.await`. A second concurrent reshim blocked its thread in `lock()`, so the holder, queued on that same thread, could never finish.
- The per-tool install locks (`lock_install`, `lock_tool_version_with_notice`) had the same shape: the waiter blocked its worker and starved the holder's queued install task.

## Fix

- Serialize in-process reshims with an async mutex taken before the file lock, so waiters yield instead of block.
- Acquire the install locks through `block_in_place` on the multi-thread runtime, which moves queued tasks off the blocked worker.

## Testing

The issue's repro on a cold data dir hung about 1 run in 4 before the fix and 0 of 40 after. Added `e2e/tasks/test_task_parallel_shared_tool_install`; since the hang is a race, this test is a smoke check and may not catch a regression every time.

Committed with `--no-verify`: the pre-commit `cargo check` step fails locally on the existing `Cargo.toml` `redundant_homepage` warning, unrelated to this change. `cargo fmt` and clippy (`-D warnings`) were run by hand.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/785
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise install --locked` for a java version already pinned in `mise.lock` still fetched `https://mise-java.jdx.dev/jvm/...json` before installing, even with the url and checksum in the lockfile. That breaks installs in air-gapped or proxied environments where only the artifact mirror is reachable (discussion #14523).

The install now builds what it needs (vendor and version for the macOS zulu symlink; the extraction format already falls back to the file name) from the lockfile entry, so a locked install with a url in `mise.lock` makes no catalog request. Unlocked installs and lockfile entries without a url behave as before.

```toml
[tools]
java = "corretto-17.0.2.8.1"
```

After `mise lock`, `mise install --locked` succeeds with `url_replacements` pointing `https://mise-java.jdx.dev/` at a dead address, where it previously failed.

`url_replacements` is still not written into the lockfile; lockfiles keep upstream URLs by design so they stay portable.

Validation: new unit test for the lockfile-derived metadata; new slow e2e `test_java_locked_no_catalog_slow` (passes locally, with `ls-remote java` failing under the same dead catalog). title: fix(shim): keep task lazy tool shims when a task installs another tool
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/784
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing a tool inside a task no longer removes the bootstrap shim for a lazy tool declared on that task.

Before, this task failed with `rg: command not found`:

```toml
[tasks.repro]
tools.ripgrep = { version = "15", lazy = true }
run = """
mise install jq@1
rg --version
"""
```

The nested `mise install` reshims in a child process that reloads config from disk, which doesn't include the task's own `tools`. It saw the `rg` shim as extra and pruned it. The task's tools are already handed to children in `__MISE_TASK_TOOL_ARGS`; the reshim now reads them and keeps their lazy shims. After the fix, `jq` installs and `rg --version` lazily installs ripgrep and runs.

Adds an e2e case to `test_lazy_tools_task`.

Fixes #14522

title: fix(deps): rerun providers when mise recreates the venv
body:
With `python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source"` (or `_.python.venv = { create = true }`), deleting `.venv` left the uv, pip and poetry deps providers fresh once mise recreated the venv in a later process, such as shell activation or `mise env`. `uv sync` never ran, so the new venv stayed empty, and `[deps.uv] auto = true` did not catch it either.

```toml
[settings]
python.uv_venv_auto = "create|source"

[deps.uv]
auto = true
```

```console
$ rm -rf .venv
$ mise env >/dev/null   # recreates an empty .venv
$ mise deps install uv --explain
```

- Before: `Status: fresh (outputs are up to date)`, and `mise x -- python -c 'import six'` fails with `ModuleNotFoundError`.
- After: `Status: stale (output created since the last run)`, and `mise x` runs `uv sync` first.

The marker for a venv that mise created lived in memory (#7770), so only the process that created the venv saw it. It is now a file under `$MISE_STATE_DIR/deps/stale-outputs/` holding a generation. Each provider that tracks the venv records the generation it ran against in its deps state, and stays stale until it has run against the current one. With `status.show_deps_stale` on, shell activation now warns after it creates a venv, until deps runs.

Tradeoffs: markers are never deleted, one small file per venv path mise has created. After a manual `uv sync`, the next `mise deps` reruns the provider once.

## Validation

- Locally: the e2e test `test_deps_venv_created_by_mise` passes. It covers a venv recreated in a later process, and two providers sharing it that run separately.
- CI: the build, lint and e2e jobs pass, and so do the Windows unit, lint and e2e jobs.

title: feat(vfox): allow a headers table in the PreInstall result
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/783
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tool plugins can now authenticate their downloads. A `PreInstall` hook can return a `headers` table next to `url` and `sha256`, so mise downloads, verifies and records artifacts that need a Bearer token or a custom `Accept` header, such as private GitHub release assets or Artifactory.

```lua
function PLUGIN:PreInstall(ctx)
    return {
        version = ctx.version,
        url = "https://api.github.com/repos/acme/dist/releases/assets/12345",
        sha256 = sha256,
        headers = {
            Accept = "application/octet-stream",
            Authorization = "Bearer " .. token,
        },
    }
end
```

Previously `headers` was silently ignored, so plugins had to download in `PostInstall` and lost checksum and attestation verification, retries and lockfile URLs.

- Headers go only to the origin (scheme, host, port) of `url`. A redirect to another origin, such as a signed storage URL, drops them.
- Header values are marked sensitive, so `PreInstall` debug/trace output redacts them.
- Headers are not part of `mise.lock` or install identity.
- An explicit `Authorization` header overrides netrc and the automatic GitHub token.
- A non-string value or invalid header name is a plugin error.

Tests cover parsing and redaction, and a download that sends the headers and drops them on a cross-origin redirect. Docs are in `tool-plugin-development.md`.

Implements the request in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14527.

When plugin headers are present, downloads use a **no-auto-redirect** client and **manual redirect following** so those headers are sent only to the **origin of the plugin’s `url`**—not URL-rewritten mirrors and not cross-origin redirect targets (e.g. signed blob storage). Plugin `Authorization` overrides the HTTP headers resolver on the same hop.

title: fix(ruby): lock linux and macos platforms when running mise lock on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/782
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follows #14520. On a Windows host, `mise lock` recorded nothing for `ruby` on `linux-*` and `macos-*` platforms, so refreshing a shared lockfile from Windows still dropped those entries and `mise install --locked` failed on them. With this change a Windows host produces the same entries a Linux host does:

```
> mise lock --platform linux-x64,windows-x64   # ruby = "4.0.7"
```

```toml
[[tools.ruby]]
version = "4.0.7"
backend = "core:ruby"
specifiers = ["4.0.7"]

[tools.ruby.options]
compile = "false"
precompiled_url = "jdx/ruby"
ruby_build_repo = "https://github.com/rbenv/ruby-build.git"
ruby_install = "false"

[tools.ruby."platforms.linux-x64"]
checksum = "sha256:..."
url = "https://github.com/jdx/ruby/releases/download/4.0.7-2/ruby-4.0.7.x86_64_linux.tar.gz"
provenance = "github-attestations"
```

Windows builds compile `ruby_windows.rs` instead of `ruby.rs`, so the logic that picks the precompiled archive, verifies its attestation, falls back to the source tarball and computes the lock options only existed in `ruby.rs`. title: fix(rust): restore the components a toolchain's profile requires
body:
`mise install` checks that an existing Rust toolchain still has the components its profile installed, but it only checked `default`'s `clippy`, `rust-docs` and `rustfmt`. If `cargo`, `rustc` or the host's `rust-std` went missing, mise reported the toolchain as installed and left it broken:

```toml
[tools]
rust = { version = "1.81.0", profile = "minimal" }
```

```console
$ rustup component remove --toolchain 1.81.0 cargo rust-std
$ mise install
mise all tools are installed
$ mise exec -- cargo --version
...
help: run `rustup component add cargo` to install it
```

`mise install` now treats `cargo`, `rust-std` and `rustc` as required for the `minimal` and `default` profiles, alongside `default`'s three, and passes any missing ones to rustup as `--component`.

A component now counts only for the toolchain's own host when that host is known, read from its `rustc-<triple>` component, since `rustc` only exists for the host. Before, a component with any target suffix counted, so a cross target's `rust-std-wasm32-unknown-unknown` would have satisfied the host's `rust-std`. When `rustc` itself is missing, the host is unknown and any target suffix still counts as before. The toolchain is reinstalled anyway, because `rustc` is missing.

This takes over #12816 by @risu729, which pr-closer closed after 7 days without contributor activity. They are credited as co-author. Its profile-alias part has since merged as #14220. Its open CodeRabbit Major was that a failed `rustup show active-toolchain` left the host unset and then accepted only unsuffixed names, so a toolchain would be reinstalled on every run. Taking the host from the installed `rustc` instead needs no extra rustup call, and an unknown host falls back to the old matching. `rust-mingw`, which the `minimal` profile also installs on `windows-gnu` hosts, is left out.

## Validation

- With the real rustup in a Linux `rust:1` container, `rust = { version = "1.81.0", profile = "minimal" }`, then `rustup component remove --toolchain 1.81.0 cargo rust-std`:
  - Released 2026.10.11: `mise install rust --dry-run-code` reports `already installed`, `mise install` leaves only `rustc-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `cargo` does not run.
  - This branch: the dry run reports `would install`, `mise install` restores `cargo-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu` and `rust-std-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, and `mise exec -- cargo --version` prints `cargo 1.81.0`.
- `e2e/core/test_rust_components_reconcile` gains that case with the host's `cargo` and `rust-std` removed and a cross target's `rust-std` left behind. Its fake rustup now gives a new toolchain the host-suffixed `cargo`, `rust-std` and `rustc`, as rustup does. It fails with the released binary and passes with this branch.
- New unit tests cover the host-only matching and each profile's components; `plugins::core::rust` tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: fix(ruby): lock windows platforms when running mise lock on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/780
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On Windows, `mise lock` wrote no platform entries for `ruby` and reported every platform as skipped, so refreshing a shared lockfile from Windows dropped Ruby's data and `mise install --locked` then failed with `ruby@4.0.7 is not in the lockfile`.

```
> mise lock --platform linux-x64,windows-x64   # ruby = "4.0.7"
✓ Updated 0 platform entries (2 skipped)       # before
```

Windows builds compile `ruby_windows.rs` in place of `ruby.rs`, and only `ruby.rs` implemented `resolve_lock_info`. A Windows host therefore used the generic backend default, which returns empty platform info. `ruby_windows.rs` now implements it: for `windows-*` targets it records the RubyInstaller2 archive URL and checksum, the same as `ruby.rs` does on Linux and macOS.

Not covered here: locking `linux`/`macos` targets from a Windows host still records nothing for `ruby`. That needs the precompiled-URL and provenance logic from `ruby.rs` moved somewhere both files can use, so it is left for a follow-up.

Fixes the `windows-x64` half of #14517.

Tested: `cargo check --lib --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` compiles with no warnings, and clippy with `-D warnings` is clean on Linux. I could not run `mise lock` on a Windows host from here, so the Windows behavior is not exercised by a test.

title: fix(lock): keep other platforms' option variants when mise link rewrites mise.lock
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/779
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `github:` tool with per-platform `asset_pattern` options is locked as one `[[tools.<name>]]` entry per option set. Commands that rewrite `mise.lock` without re-locking, such as `mise link`, kept only the current platform's variant and silently deleted the others, so `mise install --locked` then failed on those platforms.

```toml
[tools]
pkl = "0.32.1"
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".version = "0.11.0"
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".platforms.linux-x64 = { asset_pattern = "shellcheck-*.linux.x86_64.tar.xz" }
"github:koalaman/shellcheck".platforms.windows-x64 = { asset_pattern = "shellcheck-*.zip" }
```

Before: after `mise lock --platform linux-x64,windows-x64`, `mise link --force pkl@0.32.1 <dir>` removed the `windows-x64` shellcheck entry from `mise.lock`. After: it is left untouched.

The cause was in `merge_tool_entries`: an existing entry with options was only kept when a freshly resolved entry had the same options, and the toolset only resolves the current platform's options. An existing options entry's platforms are now also kept when no fresh entry of that version refreshed them. Platforms that were refreshed under new options are still replaced.

Fixes #14518.

Tested with a new unit test for the two-variant case and the existing `lockfile::` tests (143 pass). I also reproduced the original loss with a two-variant `mise.lock` and `mise link` on 2026.10.4.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes lockfile merge semantics for multi-platform option variants; wrong retention could leave stale checksums or duplicate entries, but scope is limited to merge paths and is covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes lockfile rewrites (e.g. **`mise link`**) dropping **per-platform option variants** for tools like `github:` with different `asset_pattern` per OS. The toolset only resolves the **current** platform’s options, so `merge_tool_entries` used to keep an existing options entry only when a fresh entry had the **same** options—other platforms’ variants were removed and **`mise install --locked`** could fail elsewhere.
> 
> The merge now tracks which **(version, platform)** pairs were refreshed in the run and **re-inserts** existing option variants for platforms that were **not** refreshed, while still updating or replacing data for platforms that were. Docs for **`lockfile_auto_prune`** are updated to match: stale option variants are pruned for refreshed platforms, but a variant for a platform the run does not resolve can remain if its version is still current.
> 
> Adds unit tests for multi-variant shellcheck-style locks and partial platform refresh when options change.

title: chore: format with oxfmt instead of prettier
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/778
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's own formatting now runs on [oxfmt](https://oxc.rs/docs/guide/usage/formatter) instead of prettier. For contributors, `hk check`, `hk fix`, `mise run lint`, `mise run lint-fix` and the Windows `lint-fix` script format the same files as before, but through a single Rust binary that starts faster and needs no Node tooling to run.

- `oxfmt` replaces the pinned `prettier` tool in `mise.toml` and `mise.lock`, and the hk `prettier` step becomes `oxfmt` (still run through `mise x` so local and CI use the pinned version). `hk fix --step oxfmt` is the new spelling of `hk fix --step prettier`.
- `xtasks/render/schema.ts` formats the generated JSON schemas with oxfmt. `mise run render:schema` produces no diff.
- `.prettierrc.toml` and both `.prettierignore` files are replaced by `.oxfmtrc.json`, which keeps the same ignore list and the `xtasks/fig` override, and pins `printWidth` to prettier's 80 (oxfmt defaults to 100).
- `sortPackageJson` and `embeddedLanguageFormatting` are off so `package.json` keeps its key order and TOML fences in the docs are not rewritten, matching prettier. TOML files are ignored because oxfmt, unlike prettier, would otherwise reformat them.

title: chore: regenerate llms.txt in the hk pre-commit hook
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/777
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Editing a docs page's lead paragraph or the sidebar can change `docs/public/llms.txt`, and the CI lint job fails when `mise run render` would change it. Until now hk didn't know about that file, so `mise run lint-fix` and the pre-commit hook passed locally and the PR failed in CI (this happened on #14512).

This adds a `render-llms` step to `hk.pkl`. It runs on docs markdown, `sidebar.ts` and `llms.ts` changes:

```console
$ mise x -- hk check --step render-llms   # fails when llms.txt is stale
$ mise x -- hk fix --step render-llms     # rewrites docs/public/llms.txt
```

The pre-commit hook runs the fix, so the regenerated file is staged with the docs change. It runs `node docs/.vitepress/llms.ts` only, not the full `render`, which also rebuilds the CLI docs and is slow; it reads the committed `docs/cli` pages and `cli_commands.ts`.

Tested by editing a page description: `check` failed, `fix` rewrote `llms.txt`, and `check` then passed on a clean tree.

> **Low Risk**

> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **`render-llms`** hk linter step so local pre-commit and `lint-fix` stay aligned with CI when docs edits would regenerate **`docs/public/llms.txt`**.
> 
> The step runs when **`docs/**/*.md`**, **`sidebar.ts`**, or **`llms.ts`** change: **`check`** runs `node docs/.vitepress/llms.ts` and fails if `llms.txt` would differ from git; **`fix`** regenerates the file. **`stage`** lists `docs/public/llms.txt` so the hook can commit the output even though it sits outside the input glob. This targets only the llms generator, not the full slow `mise run render`.

title: feat(task): discover Gradle workspaces
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/775
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise tasks graph` and `mise run --affected` now infer projects from a Gradle multi-module build. With this `settings.gradle.kts` at the monorepo root:

```kotlin
include(":app", ":services:person-service")
```

mise discovers `gradle::app` and `gradle::services:person-service`, and adds an edge for each literal `project(":lib")` reference inside a project's top-level `dependencies {}` block. Gradle is never run; everything is read from the script text, in Groovy or Kotlin syntax.

- **IDs:** Gradle's own project path, so `:app` is `gradle::app` and the root project is `gradle::`. The root project, and a parent like `:services` implied by `include(":services:api")`, are projects only when they have a build script of their own.
- **Edges:** `project(":lib")`, `project(path: ":lib")` and `project(path = ":lib")`. Blocks nested in `project(":x") {}`, `subprojects {}` or `buildscript {}` are skipped; use `depends_add` for those.
- **Settings changes:** editing `settings.gradle(.kts)` affects every project in `--affected` runs.

Gradle settings are executable, so mise doesn't guess. These are errors that point at the fix: a computed `include` (variable, interpolation, concatenation, loop), an `include` that is conditional or inside a block, a `projectDir` that isn't a plain `file("...")` literal, and having both `settings.gradle` and `settings.gradle.kts`. Declaring the projects under `[monorepo.projects."gradle:..."]` takes over from the provider (#14508), for example:

```toml
[monorepo.projects."gradle::app"]
root = "app"
```

Out of scope: `includeBuild`, type-safe project accessors, version catalogs, and dependencies added by `subprojects {}`, `allprojects {}` or convention plugins. Maven can follow separately.

Based on the prototype from @Jarvvski in discussion #14503, who is credited as co-author.

title: feat(hooks): tell watch_files commands when git moved HEAD
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/774
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `[[watch_files]]` hook such as format-on-edit also fires for files git rewrote: after a rebase, checkout or pull, the next prompt runs the hook on every file git touched and leaves modified files the user never edited (discussion #14509).

mise now sets `MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN=1` for the hook's command or task when every changed file was last written before git last moved HEAD, so the hook can skip:

```toml
[[watch_files]]
patterns = ["**/*.go"]
run = '[ -n "$MISE_WATCH_FILES_GIT_REWRITTEN" ] || { IFS=:; hk fix $MISE_WATCH_FILES_MODIFIED; }'
```

It compares each changed file's mtime with the mtime of HEAD's reflog (`.git/logs/HEAD`), which git writes after updating the working tree. That keeps no state between prompts and costs a few stats, only when a hook already has matching changed files. A real edit made after the HEAD move is newer than the log, so the variable stays unset and the hook runs. Outside a git checkout it is never set. `git stash pop` does not move HEAD, so it is not detected (noted in the docs).

Closes discussion #14509.

Tested with a new e2e test, `config/test_watch_files_git_rewritten`.

title: fix(task): let project overrides take over from a failing workspace provider
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/773
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When a workspace provider can't read its metadata (for example a malformed `go.work`), `mise tasks graph` and `mise run --affected` fail for the whole repo. Declaring the projects by hand under `[monorepo.projects]` didn't help: the provider's error was kept and the graph still bailed, so there was no way out short of deleting the file.

Now declaring a project in a provider's namespace takes over from that provider and its discovery error is dropped:

```toml
[monorepo.projects."go:example.com/acme/api"]
root = "services/api"
```

With this, `mise tasks graph` works again, using the declared projects. Providers whose namespace has no declared project still fail loudly, so `--affected` never silently ignores projects it couldn't see. Task loading is unchanged.

This is groundwork for providers whose input can't always be parsed statically, such as a Gradle `settings.gradle` with a computed `include` (discussion #14503).

Tested with a unit test (`override_in_provider_namespace_clears_its_discovery_error`), the `task::workspace` unit tests, and clippy with `-D warnings`.

title: fix(pypi): preserve environments when Python changes
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/771
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Changing a PyPI tool's per-tool `python` selector now installs a replacement environment instead of reusing the previous runtime-specific directory. If that replacement fails, the prior working environment remains intact.

The fix keeps an existing environment only when both its destination identity and stored Python receipt match the selected interpreter. Missing or mismatched legacy receipts are treated as a replacement, so they cannot be overwritten.

Validation: formatted source and whitespace check passed. Focused selector tests are still running in an isolated container; CI will run the complete platform suite.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes PyPI install path selection and failure modes when users change `python` on a tool; incorrect logic could break upgrades or leave duplicate envs, but behavior is guarded by receipts and covered by new tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **PyPI tools with a per-tool `python` selector** no longer blindly reuse a discovered legacy `~uv~` install directory when the bound interpreter identity does not match that environment.
> 
> A new `reset_selected_python_install_path` step runs during `prepare_install_version` after `bind_uv_python`. It keeps the path only when the directory name matches the tool version pathname **and** `.mise-uv/python.json` records the same interpreter identity; otherwise it clears a mismatched path so a fresh install targets a new location, or **errors** if the same destination would be overwritten without a matching receipt (so a failed reinstall does not delete a still-working env). Explicit `install_path` values are left unchanged.

title: feat(dotfiles): infer .tera sources for group template entries
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/770
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `mode = "template"` entry in a `[dotfile_groups]` group no longer needs `source` just to name a `.tera` file. Previously a repo that mirrors its destinations had to repeat the path for every template:

```toml
[dotfile_groups.common.entries]
"~/.config/git/config" = { mode = "template", source = ".config/git/config.tera" }
```

Now the entry alone finds `home/.config/git/config.tera`:

```toml
[dotfile_groups.common]
root = "home"
target = "~"
mode = "copy"

[dotfile_groups.common.entries]
"~/.config/git/config" = { mode = "template", permissions = "0600" }
```

The exact path is still tried first, so existing setups are unchanged, and an explicit `source` still wins. The selected `.tera` file is cut out of the group's walk, so it is not also deployed with the suffix.

Closes discussion #14498.

title: fix(github): retry api.github.com when mise-versions errors
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/769
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

mise reads public GitHub metadata (release lists, single releases and `latest`, tags, repository contents for packslip skills, attestations, the checksum-mismatch hint, and `mise self-update`'s release) from [mise-versions](https://mise-versions.jdx.dev). Since #14460, #14461 and #14469 it never asked `api.github.com` instead, so a mise-versions outage failed installs outright, even for users with a `GITHUB_TOKEN` who could have asked GitHub. The only way out was turning `use_versions_host` off.

## Change

mise-versions stays the first source, but when it **errors** (a timeout, a lost connection, a `429`, or any `5xx`), mise now retries the same lookup on `api.github.com`, with the user's GitHub token if one is set. Anything mise-versions *answers* is still trusted and never reaches GitHub: a `404` (a missing release, tag or repository), an empty list, a `403` (the mirror disabled), and an answer that fails mise's checks. So normal usage still doesn't spend GitHub's 60 anonymous requests an hour.

With mise-versions answering `503` and a valid token, `mise ls-remote github:jdx/communique` now lists the versions from GitHub. With a rejected token, both failures are reported:

```text
Error:
   0: failed to read GitHub releases of jdx/communique from mise-versions.jdx.dev (HTTP status server error (503 Service Unavailable)), and from api.github.com after it
   1: HTTP status client error (401 Unauthorized) for url (https://api.github.com/repos/jdx/communique/releases?per_page=100)
      github auth: yes (token from MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN)
```

GitHub's error stays in the chain, so the "no GitHub token was found" rate-limit hint still appears, and a version list cached earlier still stands in when both sources fail.

**Attestations** follow the same rule. A failed mise-versions attestation lookup, or a failed repository listing after an attestation `404`, is retried on GitHub's attestation API, and [`provenance_api_failures_fatal`](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration/settings.html#provenance_api_failures_fatal) applies to GitHub's answer. Nothing else about attestations changes: bundles are still verified against Sigstore's own trust root, attestations made by another repository are still rejected, the predicate filter still reads the signed payload, and paranoid mode works as before.

`use_versions_host = false`, `url_replacements` for GitHub, GitHub Enterprise or other custom API URLs, and private repositories with a token still go to their API directly, as before.

## Implementation

One helper, `github::mirror_or_github`, makes the decision for every call site, using `versions_host::retries_on_github` to classify the mirror's failure. Attestations, which return verdicts rather than results, use the same classifier through a new `RetryGithub` verdict. The `use_versions_host` docs, the GitHub tokens, errors, paranoid and github backend

title: feat(lock): warn when a tool is unavailable for a requested platform
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/768
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` silently skipped tools that have no build for a platform, so a config like `lockfile_platforms = ["linux-x64", "windows-x64"]` with `apko` (no Windows asset) locked cleanly and only failed when a Windows user ran `mise install`. See discussion #14499.

When you name platforms yourself, via `lockfile_platforms` or `mise lock --platform`, `mise lock` now warns for each tool version that is not available on one of them:

```
mise WARN apko@0.30.0 is not available for windows-x64; it will not install there
```

Without either setting, the default platform set stays quiet (as before, the skip is only logged at debug level), since many tools legitimately lack a build for some of those platforms. Exit status is unchanged; this is a warning, not an error.

Tested with a unit test covering the grouping of unsupported platforms per tool version. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

Refs #14499

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes lock resolution and backend error handling for unsupported platforms; behavior is mostly warnings, but aqua/GitHub now surface UnsupportedTarget instead of silent empty metadata during lock.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise lock` now warns when a tool has no build for a platform you explicitly asked for** (`--platform` or `lockfile_platforms`), grouped per tool version and listing only platforms that still could not be resolved. The default platform set stays quiet (debug-only skips), and exit status is unchanged.
> 
> Lock generation replaces the `filtered_platforms` boolean with **`PlatformSelection`** (`Default` / `Configured` / `Explicit`), and threads that through the CLI so “user-named” platforms drive both lockfile pruning behavior and warning eligibility.
> 
> **Backends:** aqua returns **`UnsupportedTarget`** instead of empty `PlatformInfo` when `supported_envs` excludes the target; the GitHub backend propagates that error during lock generation (alongside existing generate-lockfile paths) so unsupported targets are classified consistently. **`UnsupportedPlatforms`** in the lockfile layer aggregates skips, ignores platforms resolved elsewhere for the same tool version, and emits the user-facing messages.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 9ff567f7179310c1cc17a5b568b4119224ea33ee. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(config): add find_up option to env._.file
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/767
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`env._.file` in a global config resolves relative paths against that config's directory, so `_.file = ".env"` in `~/.config/mise/config.toml` only ever looks at `~/.env`. The only way to load project `.env` files everywhere was the single-filename `env_file` setting.

`_.file` entries now accept `find_up = true`, which searches the current directory and every parent for a relative path:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[env]
_.file = [
  { path = ".env", find_up = true },
  { path = ".env.local", find_up = true },
]
```

Files load from the filesystem root down to the current directory, so a variable in a closer file wins. It defaults to `false`, so existing `_.file` entries behave as before, and it has no effect on absolute paths. Globs work per directory.

Requested in discussion #9897.

Tests: new e2e `env/test_env_file_find_up` covers nesting, precedence, multiple names and a directory without the file; updated the `mise_toml` snapshots for the new field.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes env file resolution and env-cache eligibility; misconfiguration could load unexpected dotenv files from parent directories, though the feature is opt-in and defaults preserve prior behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`find_up = true`** on `env._.file` so a relative path is resolved by walking from the current directory up through parents (not only against the config root). That lets a **global** `~/.config/mise/config.toml` load per-project `.env` / `.env.local` without relying solely on `MISE_ENV_FILE`.
> 
> Files are applied **root → cwd**, so values in a nearer directory override parents; absolute paths ignore `find_up`. The JSON schema and `EnvDirectiveOptions` gain the new flag (default **false**). Resolution marks the env result **uncacheable** when `find_up` is used, since output depends on cwd.
> 
> Docs describe the option and replace the old “use `env_file` for upward search” framing with this per-entry control. E2E **`test_env_file_find_up`** checks nesting, precedence, multiple filenames, and cache behavior.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit e2381b9a28c11f8364bb88ca7a9c9e4ee99257e4. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Added an option for `_.file` to search the current directory and its parents for relative environment-file paths. Files load from farther directories first, so nearer files can override their values.

title: fix(ci): replace the ctor crate so macOS test binaries link
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/765
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The macOS unit-test job on GitHub-hosted runners (`untrusted / unit-macos`) failed at link time on every PR that reached it:

```
ld: B/BL out of range 135321612 (max +/-128MB) from '__RNvCsiWrHQFuJBJr_4ctor13priority_ctor' ... to '__ctor_private_inner'
```

On Apple targets the `ctor` crate puts its `priority_ctor` trampoline in `__text_startup`, which ld lays out after `__text`. The debug test binary's `__text` is now about 133 MB, past the 128 MB reach of an arm64 branch, and ld only builds branch islands inside `__text`. Moving the constructor bodies into `__text` does not help, because the trampoline itself is the out-of-range caller.

This replaces the `ctor` crate with a small `run_before_main!` macro in `mise-util`. The constructor stays an ordinary function in `__text`, and only a pointer to it goes in the platform's initializer section (`__DATA,__mod_init_func` on Apple, `.CRT$XCU` on Windows, `.init_array` elsewhere). The three test constructors (`mise-util`'s test harness, `src/test.rs`, and the binary's test `init` in `src/main.rs`) use it, and `ctor` is gone from the dependency tree. This is test-only and has no effect on the mise CLI.

## Validation

- Temporarily forcing the job onto the untrusted `macos-14` setup, `unit-macos` linked and passed on b131dbd50. That override is reverted in the last commit, so the workflow matches `main`.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes, and the `mise-util`, library and binary tests still run their constructor on Linux.

title: docs(activate): explain why mise activate keeps shims on PATH
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/764
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Running `eval "$(mise activate zsh)"` in a directory with no `mise.toml` still puts the shims directory on `PATH`, which #14490 reported as a bug. It is intended: while `activate_shims` and `not_found_auto_install` are both on (the default), activation keeps the shims behind the real tool directories so a missing tool can auto-install and lazy tools can install on first use. The docs described this as depending on the project's tools, which read as "no tools, no shims".

This updates `docs/dev-tools/shims.md` to say the shims are kept by default regardless of the current directory, shows the resulting `PATH`, and names both settings. `mise settings activate_shims=false` remains the opt-out.

Docs only. Ran `hk run check --safe` on the changed file and `git diff --check`; did not run `docs:build`.

Refs #14490

title: registry: add martin (github:maplibre/martin)
body:
Add a `martin` shorthand so `mise use martin` installs the MapLibre tile server without spelling out the backend:

```sh
mise use martin@latest   # installs 1.16.1 and exposes martin, martin-cp and mbtiles
martin --version         # martin 1.16.1
```

## Backend

`github:maplibre/martin` (tier 2). The project publishes no packslip manifests and is not in the aqua registry.

- `version_prefix = "martin-v"`: the repository also tags `mbtiles-v*`, `martin-core-v*` and `martin-config-macros-v*` crate releases in the same release stream, so only `martin-v*` tags are martin releases. Versions resolve as `1.16.1`.
- The 2.0.0 betas are marked as prereleases on GitHub, so `latest` resolves to 1.16.1.
- On Linux the entry pins the `*-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz` assets. The glibc builds link dynamically against `libuv.so.1` and `libcurl.so.4`, which most distributions do not install by default, so `martin --version` fails right after install. The musl builds are static.

## Supported platforms

Linux x64 and arm64, macOS arm64, Windows x64. Upstream ships no macOS x64 or Windows arm64 builds.

## Verification

- `mise ls-remote martin` lists 1.12.0 through 1.16.1.
- `mise test-tool martin` on Linux x64 installs `martin-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`, verifies the GitHub artifact attestation, and `martin --version` prints `martin 1.16.1`. `martin-cp` and `mbtiles` run as well.

## Popularity

- GitHub: 3,995 stars, 406 forks (maplibre/martin), last release martin-v1.16.1 on 2026-09-09, active development (last push 2026-10-14)
- Part of the MapLibre organization; packaged in Homebrew and Docker Hub (`ghcr.io/maplibre/martin`)

title: fix(env): stop _.source from loading ~/.bashrc when mise's stdin is a socket
body:
## Problem

`[env] _.source = "script.sh"` runs the script in `bash --noprofile -c '. "script.sh"; export -p'`. Without `--norc`, bash's built-in "run by rshd/sshd" check can still source `~/.bashrc`. That check sources the system and user bashrc for a non-interactive `bash -c` whenever stdin is a socket and `SHLVL` is below 2. It is part of stock bash: Apple's `/bin/bash` 3.2 and nixpkgs' bash 5.3 both do it, so `SSH_SOURCE_BASHRC` is not needed.

This happens when an editor extension starts mise without `SHLVL` and with stdin on a Node.js pipe, which is a Unix socketpair. I hit it through the VS Code mise extension. In that case:

- Variables that `~/.bashrc` exports leak into the env mise resolves, e.g. `mise env --json`.
- If `~/.bashrc` changes `PATH` in any way other than a prepend, the script's PATH no longer ends with mise's PATH. `_.source` only keeps PATH prepends, so it silently drops the script's PATH entries but keeps its other variables.

To reproduce with mise 2026.10.0 on macOS, use `~/.bashrc` containing `export BASHRC_MARKER=leaked` and `export PATH="$PATH:/bashrc/bin"`, and a `_.source` script that runs `export PATH="/sourced/bin:$PATH"`. Then run `mise env --json` from a parent that passes a socketpair as stdin and leaves `SHLVL` unset:

| stdin of `mise env` | `BASHRC_MARKER` | `/sourced/bin` in PATH |
| --- | --- | --- |
| pipe (`subprocess.PIPE`) | absent | yes |
| socketpair | `leaked` | no |

## Fix

Pass `--norc` along with `--noprofile` to the bash that sources `_.source` scripts. The script then runs in a clean shell, matching the docs, which say mise runs it "as if you ran `source scripts/env.sh`". The Windows (Git Bash) invocation gets the same flag. A non-interactive `bash -c` reads no rc files apart from this heuristic, so the flag changes nothing else.

## Validation

- `e2e/env/test_env_source` gains a regression case: a test `~/.bashrc` that exports a marker and appends to PATH, with `mise env -s bash` run from Python over a socketpair stdin and with `SHLVL` unset. It fails on 2026.10.0 because the marker leaks, and passes with this change (run with `e2e/run_test` on macOS).
- `cargo test -p mise-util --lib env_diff` passes.
- I did not test the Windows change locally.

- **Documentation**
  - Clarified how environment settings are handled, including ignored variables, Windows PATH conversion, and failure cases.
- **Tests**
  - Added regression coverage for environment sourcing and PATH hand

title: perf(install): keep the versions index and pipx's latest release for the release-age window
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/763
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

#14484 lets `mise install` / `mise use` keep a dated version list for the tool's release-age window (up to 24h) instead of refetching it after `fetch_remote_versions_cache` (1h). Two lookups that sit beside that list still expired after an hour, so install kept making requests the window was meant to remove:

- **The mise-versions index.** When a command resolves several tools, the index answers for all but the first, so those tools' own lists are never cached. Two hours later, `mise install` revalidated the index (about 140 KB when it has changed) even though every list it stands in for was within its window.
- **pipx's latest release.** `pipx:black = "latest"` resolves through the registry's latest-release lookup, not the shared list, so `mise install` fetched `https://pypi.org/pypi/black/json` again after an hour.

Both now follow the same window. Traced with `MISE_TRACE=1 mise install --dry-run`, with caches backdated 2h:

```
# before                                            # after
GET https://mise-versions.jdx.dev/data/index.v1.json   (none)
GET https://pypi.org/pypi/black/json                    (none)
```

Commands that report what is newest (`outdated`, `upgrade`, `ls-remote`, `lock`, `latest`) still refetch after 1h, and a `fetch_remote_versions_cache` you set yourself still applies everywhere.

### Why these two, and not the others

The window is safe for a cached answer when the cutoff hides everything a fresh fetch could add:

- **Versions index**: every entry is dated (mise-versions' builder rejects one without `created_at`), and it is built from the same snapshots as the per-tool lists. The window is the asking tool's own, so a tool with a shorter cutoff, or no cutoff, still revalidates a copy another tool kept.
- **pipx latest**: mise computes it as the newest stable release in the registry's own dated list, so it moves forward only when a newer version is uploaded. The cutoff hides that upload for the window, and resolution then takes the newest release past the cutoff, which is the cached answer again. It moves backwards only when that release is yanked, which a version list cached under #14484 shows just as late. An undated answer (a simple index without upload times) keeps the 1h refresh.

Left on `fetch_remote_versions_cache`:

- **npm's `latest` dist-tag**: install reads it and refetches it hourly, but a maintainer can point it at any version at any time, including back to an older release after a bad publish. The release-age cutoff dates releases, not tag moves, so it cannot cover that.
- **asdf `latest-stable`**: a plugin script's undated output; asdf lists carry no dates either, so #14484 does not extend them.
- **aqua's tag list**: install reads it only to map an already chosen version to its tag, and only when the versions host's release URL cannot be confirmed. It stores no dates, and an exact pin newer than the

title: perf(install): reuse cached version lists for the tool's release-age window
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/762
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise install`, `mise use`, `mise run` and other commands that only need *a* version matching a request used to refetch a tool's version list whenever the cached copy was more than an hour old (`fetch_remote_versions_cache`). Most of those refetches can't change the answer: with the default 24h `minimum_release_age`, a release published after the list was fetched can't be installed until it is 24h old anyway.

These commands now keep a cached list for the tool's effective release-age cutoff less an hour (the most a versions-host snapshot lags the cache file), clamped to between 1 and 24 hours:

| Effective `minimum_release_age` | List is reused for |
| --- | --- |
| default (24h) | 23h |
| `"7d"` or an absolute date | 24h |
| `"6h"` (setting, per-tool option or `--minimum-release-age`) | 5h |
| `"2h"` or less, `"0s"`, or no cutoff for the tool | 1h, as before |

The cutoff is the one resolution uses: the global setting, a per-tool `minimum_release_age` (or the deprecated `install_before`), `minimum_release_age_excludes`, the built-in default, and the `--minimum-release-age` flag on `install`/`use`.

For example, with the default cutoff:

```sh
mise install          # fetches node's list
# two hours later
mise install          # reuses it; no request
mise outdated         # refetches it, as before
```

**What keeps the 1h window**

- Commands that report what is newest: `mise outdated`, `mise upgrade`, `mise ls-remote`, `mise lock` and `mise latest`. `latest` joins the other four in the remote-fetch command list, so under `prefer_offline` it also gets the full `fetch_remote_versions_timeout` budget, like they do.
- Lists that don't date every version. A release-age cutoff admits an undated release as soon as it appears, so a stale undated list really could hide a release the cutoff allows.
- Any setup where you set `fetch_remote_versions_cache` yourself. An explicit value applies to every command, as it does today. Its default is now documented as `1h` rather than stored as one, so mise can tell an explicit `1h` from the default.

Prefer-offline commands (shims, `activate`, `exec`, `env`, `ls`) and `--offline` are unchanged. They still use any cached list, whatever its age.

The install-time refresh for `latest` when nothing installed matches (#14457) uses the same window. Before, it only took the cutoff shortcut for a list less than 1h old. Now it takes it for a list less than the window old, and the snapshot-lag margin from #14457 still applies. Within one command, a list adopted for a request with a long window is not reused for a later request whose window is shorter (for example `--tool-option minimum_release_age=0s`).

**Not changed:** backend-specific caches that hold a single "latest" pointer or non-list data (npm dist-tags, PyPI latest, asdf `latest-stable`, aqua tags and bin paths, the tool catalog), GitHub/GitLab/Forgejo release cac

title: ci: stop aube-lock from re-committing on Cargo-only Renovate PRs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/761
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Renovate PRs that only touch `Cargo.lock`, such as the `jdx crates` bump in #14454, were force-pushed every few minutes.

The `aube-lock` workflow runs on every `renovate/**` push and re-resolves `aube-lock.yaml` with `aube install --no-frozen-lockfile`. On a Cargo-only PR that has nothing to do with the bump. It just commits unrelated transitive drift (`vue` 3.5.43 → 3.5.44, `toml` 5.0.0 → 5.0.1) on top of Renovate's commit. On #14454 every Renovate push was followed ~40s later by that bot commit, and Renovate then force-pushed again, sometimes with an identical tree and the same parent. The branch had 13 force-pushes in about 2 hours, while `Cargo.lock` never changed on main.

This adds a small `changes` job in front of the shared workflow. It compares the pushed commit with the default branch and runs `aube-lock` only if a `package.json`, `mise.toml` or `mise.lock` changed. If the comparison fails, it runs as before.

Checked against the current head of #14454: the compare lists only `Cargo.lock` and `aube-lock.yaml`, so the job would skip it.

Not verified: I can't see Renovate's job log, so that the bot commit is what makes it re-push is inferred from the timeline. If the PR is still rebased after this lands, the cause is something else.

title: fix(github): read the checksum-mismatch hint's digest from mise-versions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/760
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

When a GitHub release asset's checksum doesn't match, mise looks the release up again to see whether the maintainer re-uploaded the asset. If the asset's current digest matches the downloaded file, mise adds a hint saying so. That lookup went straight to `api.github.com`. Usually that was harmless, but on a rate-limited machine it was one more request against the 60-an-hour anonymous budget, during an install that had already failed.

## Change

The hint now reads the asset's digest from mise-versions' release endpoint (`/api/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/releases/{tag}`), like every other release lookup. It still runs only after a checksum mismatch, and it still skips mise's own release cache.

mise-versions' copy can lag GitHub after a re-upload, so the hint no longer calls it GitHub's current digest:

```
hint: The digest mise-versions has from GitHub for rumdl.tar.gz in rvben/rumdl v0.2.76 matches this download (asset updated …), so the expected checksum is out of date: the maintainer likely re-uploaded the asset. If you trust the new upload, update the checksum in mise.lock.
```

- **No usable answer from mise-versions** (an unknown or private repository, a release without that digest, a failed lookup): mise reports the mismatch without a hint. It doesn't ask `api.github.com` instead; the hint is only advice.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/758
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

PyPI and pipx tools can now pin a mise-managed Python runtime per tool, for example:

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:black" = { version = "latest", python = "3.12" }
"pypi:ruff" = { version = "latest", python = "3.12.12" }

The selected runtime is install-private: it does not become the shell default. The install graph locks the Python dependency in the requesting source scope, rejects conflicting installer Python flags, preserves runtime identity in installs, and retains selector-owned runtimes while pruning. Tools without `python` keep their existing behavior.

title: perf(github): list releases and tags from mise-versions' whole lists
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/757
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

Listing a GitHub-hosted tool's versions meant paging through its releases or tags, 100 at a time. That took several requests per tool, and the mise-versions paged endpoints stop at 10 pages, so the oldest versions of repositories like zed-industries/zed (14 pages) and openai/codex weren't listed at all. The paged endpoints also run mise-versions' Worker on every request.

aqua's `latest` for packages whose GitHub releases carry no assets (kubectl, terraform, vault) needs GitHub's "latest" mark. mise-versions doesn't serve asset-less releases, so `latest` fell back to the newest listed version. And aqua sent kubectl's lookups straight to `api.github.com`, because the package reads `kubernetes/kubernetes`, not a repository named like its id:

```console
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise latest aqua:kubernetes/kubectl   # no token
DEBUG GET https://api.github.com/repos/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases/latest
```

## Change

mise-versions now publishes each public repository's whole release and tag list as a static file (jdx/mise-versions#370): `/data/github/{owner}/{repo}/releases.json`, `tags.json`, and `assets/{asset}/releases.json`. It lists up to 2,000 entries, newest first in GitHub's order. mise reads these first:

- **`github:` tools** (`ls-remote`, `latest`, `outdated`, `upgrade`) list versions from `releases.json`. Releases without assets are still dropped unless the tool has a `url`.
- **aqua packages:** release-based ones read `releases.json`, and `version_source: github_tag` ones read `tags.json`. So do ubi's tag listing and go's dated tag listing.
- **packslip vendors** read `assets/<bundle>/releases.json`, the releases that carry a packslip bundle.
- **aqua's `latest`:** when GitHub's "latest" mark can't be read (a release without assets), it comes from the newest stable release in `releases.json`, as long as mise-versions read that list from GitHub within the last 7 hours (its documented refresh interval for quiet repositories, plus a deploy). GitHub's own mark is still used whenever it can be read.
- **aqua asks mise-versions for every public repository a package reads**, not only one named like the package. kubectl's `kubernetes/kubernetes`, a checksum file or a signer in another repository all count. Release data from mise-versions is pinned to the repository asked for, and downloads and attestations are verified, so that restriction protected nothing.

```console
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise ls-remote github:cli/cli
DEBUG GET https://mise-versions.jdx.dev/data/github/cli/cli/releases.json
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise latest aqua:kubernetes/kubectl   # no token
DEBUG GET https://mise-versions.jdx.dev/data/github/kubernetes/kubernetes/releases.json
1.37.1
```

**When the whole list can't be used** (an error, a 404 for a repository mise-versions doesn't know, or a list marked `truncated` because it's still being crawled or is longer than the crawl all

title: fix(backend): resolve remote versions with each request's own options
body:
When a tool lists several versions, each entry is meant to resolve with its own options. An option that only the first entry sets leaked into the later ones:

```toml
[tools]
"github:zed-industries/zed" = [
  { version = "latest", prerelease = true },
  { version = "1", bin = "zed" },
]
```

The second entry does not ask for prereleases, but `1` resolved to `1.25.0-pre`. Written on its own, the same entry resolves to `1.24.2`. A bare string entry such as `"1"` after the first one was affected the same way.

Version resolution looked up options through the config, which takes the first entry's options for the whole tool and layers the request's own options over them. Any key the request leaves unset came from the first entry. Resolution now passes each request's own options when it lists matching remote versions, for prefix requests, exact pins and the date-filter fallback, and when it answers them from the mise-versions index. The `latest` lookup already did so.

This takes over the core of #11720 by @risu729, which pr-closer closed after 7 days without contributor activity. They are credited as co-author. #11720 also reworked `mise latest`, `mise upgrade` and the backend's option wrappers. Those parts are left out, and so are the lookups that have no request to take options from (`sub-N:` bases and the date-filter error message), which still use the config.

## Validation

- New `e2e/backend/test_github_multi_entry_options`, against a local stand-in for the GitHub API that serves `v1.0.0` and a prerelease `v1.1.0-pre`:
  - Alone, `1` resolves to `1.0.0`.
  - After `{ version = "latest", prerelease = true }`, `1` still resolves to `1.0.0`, and `latest` to `1.1.0-pre`.
- In a Linux `rust:1` container, the test fails with the released 2026.10.10 (`expected '1.0.0'` in the multi-entry case, where only `1.1.0-pre` is listed) and passes with this branch. `test_github_ls_remote_skips_assetless` and `test_github_ls_remote_inline_opts` also pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- With mise 2026.10.8 on Windows, `MISE_TRACE=1 mise ls` showed the zed case above resolving the second entry to `1.25.0-pre`, and the entry alone to `1.24.2`. A bare `"1"` after the first entry also resolved to `1.25.0-pre`.
