body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/576
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

fish uses a single `config.fish` for interactive shells and scripts alike, so `[bootstrap.mise_shell_activate]` could not express "full activation at the prompt, shims everywhere else". Users who wanted that had to leave bootstrap's block off and hand-write it with a `[dotfiles]` edit.

`fish = "auto"` now writes that conditional block:

[bootstrap.mise_shell_activate]
fish = "auto"
```

if status is-interactive

end

title: feat(dotfiles): refuse to publish saved versions that look like secrets
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/575
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise dot sync` now refuses to publish saved versions that look like they contain a secret.

The history credential filter only looks at file names (`*token*`, `*.pem`, …). A tracked `~/.bashrc` passes it however many tokens are exported in it, and removing a token from the file leaves it in every earlier saved version, so a push publishes it permanently. This came up on omacom/omarchy#14452, which tracks `~/.bashrc` by default.

Before publishing, mise reads the versions the origin does not have yet and stops on a line that looks like:

- a provider token: `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `glpat-`, `sk-`, `AKIA…`, `xox…`
- a private key block
- an assignment to a name ending in `_KEY`, `_TOKEN`, `_SECRET`, or `_PASSWORD` (`keybind = …` and `export TOKEN=$(gh auth token)` do not match)

```console
$ mise dot sync
Error: cannot publish: line 2 of home/.shellrc in saved version 3f2a9c1d0e4b looks like a secret. Removing it from the file does not remove it from saved versions. Encrypt the file with `encrypt = true`, remove that history (see https://mise.jdx.dev/dotfiles/encryption.html#remove-plaintext-from-history), or run `mise dot sync --allow-plaintext-history` to publish it anyway
```

The message names the file, line, and version, never the value.

## Behavior

- Only versions the origin does not have are read. A secret that was already published does not block every later sync, and a clean sync costs nothing.
- Background syncs (`history.sync = "sync"`) refuse the same way. The failure shows in `mise dot status`; this PR adds no new notification.
- The existing `--allow-plaintext-history` flag and `history.allow_plaintext_history` setting skip this check along with the encryption check. Their docs and help text say so. There is no per-file opt-out yet.
- Files over 1 MiB and binary files are not read. This is a safety net for obvious cases, not proof a version is clean, and it only applies when publishing, not when pulling.

## Testing

New unit tests cover the patterns (including the non-matches above), a removed secret still blocking until published, and binary files. `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_secret_scan` runs the flow: block, still blocked after removal, publish with the flag, later syncs pass. Nine existing dotfiles sync e2e tests pass, and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: ci: stop installing direnv for the e2e tests
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/574
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

CI installs direnv from apt on every e2e job, and apt mirror failures have been failing those jobs (for example the 30 minute hang in the `release` workflow's e2e tranche). The only e2e test that needs a real direnv binary tests a combination mise does not support, so there is no reason to keep installing it.

## Why this is safe

- `docs/direnv.md` says running direnv and mise together is unsupported and that compatibility PRs are not accepted.
- `mise direnv` is deprecated (`cli.direnv`, warns since 2026.10.4, removal at 2027.10.4).
- `e2e/direnv/test_direnv` was the only test calling `require_cmd direnv`. It is deleted.
- `e2e/direnv/test_direnv_command_deprecated` stays. It covers the deprecated `mise direnv` command, and its `mise direnv exec` call already ignores the exit status because it needs direnv itself.
- `mise exec direnv -- direnv --version` in `e2e/test_top_runtimes` and the `direnv` plugin check in `test-plugins.yml` install direnv through mise, so they are unaffected.

## Changes

direnv is removed from the apt package lists in `release.yml` and `test-plugins.yml`, `packaging/e2e/Dockerfile`, `.cursor/install.sh`, and the host package lists in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/contributing.md`. `packaging/alpine/Dockerfile` also installs direnv, but it builds apk packages rather than running e2e, so I left it alone.

title: registry: rename mprocs to dekit and keep mprocs as an alias
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/573
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

mprocs v0.10.0 was renamed to dekit upstream, and its release tarball now contains only a `dekit` binary. The aqua-registry entry was updated to match ([aquaproj/aqua-registry#62053](https://github.com/aquaproj/aqua-registry/pull/62053)), but `registry/mprocs.toml` still tested `mprocs --version`, so the registry check for the 2026.10.5 release PR ([#14060](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14060)) failed with:

```
sh: 1: mprocs: not found
mise available bins in /tmp/mise-data/installs/mprocs/latest
dekit
```

## Change

`registry/mprocs.toml` becomes `registry/dekit.toml`, tested with `dekit --version`, with `mprocs` kept as an alias:

```toml
aliases = ["mprocs"]
backends = ["aqua:pvolok/dekit"]
test = { cmd = "dekit --version", expected = "dekit {{version}}" }
```

`mise use mprocs` and existing `mise.toml` entries keep resolving to `aqua:pvolok/dekit`, and `mise use dekit` works too. For v0.10.0 and later the installed command is `dekit`, not `mprocs`; versions up to 0.9.6 still provide `mprocs`. `bins` is inferred from the aqua package, so it covers both names once the vendored registry includes the dekit entry.

## Validation

- `mise registry` lists both `dekit` and `mprocs` as `aqua:pvolok/dekit`.
- With the vendored aqua-registry from the `release` branch temporarily overlaid, `mise test-tool dekit` and `mise test-tool mprocs` both install 0.10.0 and print `dekit 0.10.0`, and `bins` is `["dekit", "mprocs"]`.
- **Ordering:** `main` still vendors an aqua-registry commit from before the dekit fix, so `test-tool` for this entry fails on `main` until the vendored registry is updated (the release PR does this). I did not include the vendor bump here.

title: fix(vfox): resolve embedded plugin files from the manifest dir
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/572
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

The release PR for 2026.10.5 ([#14060](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14060)) failed `windows-lint`, `windows-unit` and `build-windows` while compiling the `vfox` crate:

```
error: couldn't read `W:/actions-runner-2/_work/mise/mise/crates/vfox/embedded-plugins/vfox-emsdk/hooks/parse_legacy_file.lua`: The system cannot find the file specified. (os error 2)
  --> ${out_dir}\embedded_plugins.rs:211:31
```

The job ran on `jdx-win-ci-3` (`W:\actions-runner-3`), but the failing path is under `actions-runner-2`. `parse_legacy_file.lua` exists in git at that commit; this release is the first to add it.

`crates/vfox/build.rs` generates `embedded_plugins.rs` with `include_str!("<absolute path>")`, built from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` at build-script time. The Windows runners reuse build script output from a shared cache, so a job in one checkout can compile generated code that points at another checkout. Any release that adds or renames an embedded plugin file can then fail this way.

## Fix

The generated code now uses `include_str!(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/embedded-plugins/..."))`. rustc resolves the path in the checkout it is compiling, so the generated file no longer depends on where the build script ran.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p vfox --lib`: 149 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p vfox --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo +1.95 check -p vfox` are clean.
- The generated `embedded_plugins.rs` has no occurrence of the checkout path.
- New test `generated_code_has_no_checkout_path` passes with this change and fails against the old `build.rs`.

I did not reproduce the shared-cache scenario on the Windows runners, so the root cause comes from the failing logs rather than a reproduction. This removes the checkout path from the cached output, which is the only way the logs show the wrong checkout being used. The release PR needs this change merged into `release` and the Windows jobs re-run to confirm.

title: fix(brew): infer formula version from the GitHub release tag path
body:
mise reads a tap formula without Homebrew. When the formula declares no `version`, mise has to guess it from the stable URL, and it only looked at the file name. GitHub release assets are often named for their platform, not their version, so two things went wrong:

- **No version in the file name, so the formula failed.** `goku`'s URL is `…/GokuRakuJoudo/releases/download/v0.8.0/goku-arm.zip`, and mise stopped with `could not infer formula version; add an explicit version declaration`.
- **A platform suffix was read as part of the version.** `…/releases/download/v1.10.0/apfel-1.10.0-arm64-macos.tar.gz` installed as version `1.10.0-arm64-macos`.

mise now reads the tag in a `/releases/download/<tag>/` URL first, as Homebrew does. Homebrew's GitHub release parser (`Library/Homebrew/version.rb`, `VERSION_PARSERS`) runs ahead of its file-name parsers. This ports that parser, `v`/`V`/`r` tag prefixes included. Other URLs still use the file name, and an explicit `version` still wins.

This takes over #13327 by @waynehoover, which pr-closer closed for 7 days without contributor activity. Its CI had passed and its review threads were resolved. They are credited as co-author, and the change is theirs, unchanged. In their run over the 253 tap formulae they had installed, it fixed `goku` and 8 mis-versioned formulae (`apfel`, `apfel-gui`, `apfel-run`, `apfel-tag`, `auge`, `bgbgone`, `ohr`, `translate`) and broke none. Greptile asked on #13327 whether a release suffix such as `tool-1.2.3-1.tar.gz` under tag `v1.2.3` should keep the `-1`. It should not, to match Homebrew, which the test records and which the check below confirms.

## Validation

- Ran the formula metadata shim from `main` and from this PR in a `ruby:3.4` container. I also ran Homebrew 7.0.9's own `Version.detect` on the same URLs:

  | URL | before | after | Homebrew 7.0.9 |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `…/releases/download/v0.8.0/goku-arm.zip` | error | `0.8.0` | `0.8.0` |
  | `…/releases/download/v1.10.0/widget-1.10.0-arm64-macos.tar.gz` | `1.10.0-arm64-macos` | `1.10.0` | `1.10.0` |
  | `…/releases/download/v1.2.3/widget-1.2.3-1.tar.gz` | `1.2.3-1` | `1.2.3` | `1.2.3` |
  | `…/releases/download/1.4.0/widget.zip` | error | `1.4.0` | `1.4.0` |
  | `…/releases/download/V2.0.1/widget.zip` | error | `2.0.1` | `2.0.1` |
  | `…/releases/download/r3.1/widget.zip` | error | `3.1` | `3.1` |
  | `…/archive/refs/tags/v1.5.0.tar.gz` | `1.5.0` | `1.5.0` | `1.5.0` |
  | `https://ftp.gnu.org/gnu/wget/wget-1.21.4.tar.gz` | `1.21.4` | `1.21.4` | `1.21.4` |
  | `https://example.com/noversion.tar.gz` | error | error | none |

  An explicit `version "9.9.9"` stays `9.9.9` both before and after. The GitHub release parser moved ahead of the file-name parsers in Homebrew/brew@bae7b0408a. An older Homebrew, 4.6.20, still returns `1.2.3-1` for the third URL.
- New unit test `infers_version_from_github_release_tag_path` in `src/system/packages/brew/tap.rs` covers these cases. Like the existing shim tests, it runs on Linu

+        // URL, not "1.2.3-1".
+        let f = formula_metadata(

+        )

+        // Tag prefixes brew accepts: bare, and r/v/V optionally followed by "_".

+
+# e.g. https://github.com/foo/bar/releases/download/v1.2/foo-1.2.0.tar.gz
+GITHUB_RELEASE_URL = %r{github\.com/.+/releases/download/(?:[rvV]_?)?(#{NUMERIC_WITH_DOTS})/}
+
+# The tag path segment of a GitHub release URL. Homebrew tries this before any
+# filename pattern (Library/Homebrew/version.rb, VERSION_PARSERS), and the order
+# matters: release assets are routinely named for their platform rather than
+# their version, so the path is both the only source when the filename carries
+# no version at all (goku-arm.zip) and the more accurate one when it carries a
+# partial version followed by a platform suffix (foo-1.2-darwin-arm64.tar.gz,
+# where the filename pattern below over-captures "1.2-darwin-arm64").
+def version_from_url_path(url)
+  match = url.to_s.match(GITHUB_RELEASE_URL)
+  match && match[1]
+end
+
+# The version carried by the archive's own filename, e.g. wget-1.21.4.tar.gz.
+def version_from_basename(url)
   basename = File.basename(url.to_s).sub(/\.(tar\.(gz|xz|bz2|zst)|tgz|txz|zip|gz)\z/i, "")
   match = basename.match(/(?:^|[-_v])([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9A-Za-z]+)+(?:[-_.][0-9A-Za-z]+)*)/)
   match && match[1]
 end
 
+# Homebrew tries its URL parsers in a fixed order and takes the first that
+# matches; these are the two that cover the formulae mise builds from taps.
+def inferred_version(url)
+  version_from_url_path(url) || version_from_basename(url)
+end
+

title: fix(exec): install exact versions when the version list times out
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/571
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise x <tool>@<exact-version> -- cmd` could fail with a confusing error when the tool's remote version list was slow or unreachable. `x`/`exec` are prefer-offline commands, so that lookup gets a single 3s attempt. When it timed out, mise only warned and left the version unresolved, so nothing was installed and the command itself failed:

```
mise WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for ubi:goreleaser/goreleaser: ... HTTP timed out after 3.00s for https://api.github.com/repos/goreleaser/goreleaser/releases?per_page=100 ...
Error: 0: "goreleaser" couldn't exec process: No such file or directory
```

This was seen in CI in `e2e/backend/test_ubi`.

Now, when a prefer-offline command can't reach the server for the version list (a timeout or connection failure) and the requested version is fully qualified, mise installs that version as written:

```
mise WARN  failed to fetch versions for ubi:goreleaser/goreleaser, installing v1.25.0 as written: HTTP timed out after 3.00s ...
mise ✓ ubi:goreleaser/goreleaser@v1.25.0
```

If that release doesn't exist, or the network is still down, the command now fails with the installer's error instead of "couldn't exec process".

A version counts as fully qualified if it has at least two dots (`1.2.3`, `v1.0.0`) or the backend's `is_exact_version` accepts it. Configured versions in prefer-offline mode already skip the lookup by this rule. The version string is used as written and never compared or ordered. Prefixes such as `node@20` and `latest` still need the list, so a failed lookup behaves as before. Other lookup errors, such as an invalid `pipx.registry_url`, are still reported as before. The 3s cap for shims and activation is unchanged (see discussion 11185). One tradeoff: if a request like `1.2.3` would normally resolve to a longer release such as `1.2.3.4`, a failed lookup now tries to install `1.2.3` and reports what the backend says about that release. A configured `1.2.3` already behaves this way.

### Tests

`e2e/cli/test_exec_version_list_timeout` serves a tarball locally behind an http-backend `version_list_url` that never responds. On main, this test fails with `"hello-timeout" couldn't exec process`. With this change it installs and runs `1.0.0`. `test_ubi`, `test_exec_*`, and `test_http_*` also pass locally.

While testing, I also found that the http backend fetches `version_list_url` with the plain `http_timeout` rather than the 3s prefer-offline cap. That is out of scope here.

The docs rewrite (#14096, #14097, #14098) merged after a batch of behavior fixes, so several rewritten pages still described the old behavior. For example, the paranoid mode page said a monorepo root trusted before paranoid mode was turned on still trusts every config below it, and the `mise run ./script` section told you to run from the project root or pass an absolute path. This PR updates the pages so they describe what mise does now. It only changes documentation and one schema description.

## Trust, safe mode and hooks

- `paranoid.md`, `tasks/monorepo.md`: paranoid mode never lets a monorepo root stand in for a descendant's own trust, even for a root trusted in normal mode. The `MISE_PARANOID=0 mise trust --untrust` workaround is gone ([#14105](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14105)).
- `hooks.md`, `security.md`: `--no-hooks`, `MISE_NO_HOOKS`, `no_hooks` and safe mode also skip `[[watch_files]]` commands and tasks ([#14108](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14108)).
- `environments/secrets/index.md`: `mise env --redacted` leaves out variables that set `redact = false`, so CI masking does not mask them ([#14109](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14109)).
- `mcp.md`: the `install_tool` result also includes the install log as `output` ([#14111](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14111)).
- `schema/mise.json` (and the generated `mise-task.json`): the `allow_net` description says per-host filtering is not supported, so Linux and macOS reject it ([#14106](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14106)). `sandboxing.md` already described the #14106 and #14107 behavior.

## Tasks

- `tasks/file-tasks.md`: `mise run ./build.sh` resolves the path from the current directory, and the script still runs in the config root ([#14120](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14120)). Only a script extension such as `.sh` or `.py` is dropped from a file task's name, so `mise-tasks/gen.proto` is `gen.proto` ([#14159](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14159)).
- `tasks/running-tasks.md`: `MISE_TASK_NAME` is the name `mise tasks ls` shows, without a script extension ([#14159](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14159)). `mise watch` passes its watchexec flags on, and watchexec's `--env` and `--quiet` are spelled `--watchexec-env` and `--watchexec-quiet` ([#14115](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14115)):

  ```sh
  mise watch -E dev --watchexec-env LOG_LEVEL=debug build

- `tasks/task-discovery.md`, `mise-cookbook/presets.md`: file tasks in `$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/tasks` are global without a global config file. The cookbook no longer creates an empty `config.toml` ([#14122](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/14122)).

title: test(backend): give test_ubi a longer version-fetch timeout
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/569
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`e2e/backend/test_ubi` lists releases live from api.github.com and gitlab.com. On 2026-10-08 it failed on #14117, #14139 and #14146 (both harness attempts on two of them) and passed on rerun:

```
$ mise x ubi:goreleaser/goreleaser@v1.25.0 -- goreleaser -v | grep -o 1.25.0
mise WARN  Failed to resolve tool version list for ubi:goreleaser/goreleaser: ... HTTP timed out after 3.00s for https://api.github.com/repos/goreleaser/goreleaser/releases?per_page=100 ...
Error:
   0: "goreleaser" couldn't exec process: No such file or directory
```

The 3s budget belongs to `mise x`, not to the setting (default 20s). `x` and `exec` are prefer-offline commands, so `fetch_remote_versions_timeout()` returns `min(configured, 3s)`. Raising `MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_TIMEOUT` alone does nothing for the failing lines. A local check against an unroutable `api_url` with it set to `30s` still timed out after 3.00s.

The test now:

- exports `MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_TIMEOUT=30s`, which covers the `ls-remote`, `use` and `install` calls;
- runs `mise ls-remote` for the two tools whose first use is a cold `mise x` (goreleaser, and glab with `provider=gitlab`). `ls-remote` honors the full timeout. Prefer-offline commands never treat the cached list as stale, so `mise x` then reads it from the cache. With `MISE_LOG_HTTP=1`, a cold `mise x` sends `GET .../releases?per_page=100` and a warmed one sends none.

No retries were added. `ls-remote` runs under `set -e`, so a release listing that is broken rather than slow still fails the test, and `mise x` still does the install and the exec.

`http_timeout` (30s, reset on every read) covers the artifact downloads. None of the failures involved it, so it is unchanged. No other e2e test sets either timeout.

A related product bug is not part of this PR. When `mise x` cannot resolve the version list it warns and skips the install, so the user sees `couldn't exec process` instead of the timeout.

`mise run test:e2e test_ubi` passes locally (19s).

title: fix(task): strip script extensions only from file task names
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/568
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise dropped whatever followed the last `.` in every task name, including TOML tasks. Two tasks such as

```toml
[tasks."test.unit"]
run = "cargo test --lib"

[tasks."test.e2e"]
run = "./e2e/run.sh"
```

were both listed as `test` by `mise tasks ls`, their output was prefixed `[test]`, and `mise run test` ran both. The `MISE_TASK_NAME` a task saw disagreed with the listed name in the other direction: `mise-tasks/build.sh` was listed as `build` but saw `MISE_TASK_NAME=build.sh`.

Now only file tasks lose an extension, and only a known script extension. With `mise-tasks/build.sh` (which echoes `$MISE_TASK_NAME`), `mise-tasks/gen.proto`, and the two TOML tasks above:

```console
$ mise tasks ls --no-header
build
gen.proto
test.e2e
test.unit
$ mise run build
build-ran name=build
$ mise run test
Error:
   0: no task test found
```

- TOML task names are shown, prefixed, and matched as written. The exception is a block that takes a discovered script over under the script's own name (`[tasks."hello.sh"] run = "..."`): it stands in for that file task and is still listed as `hello`.
- A file task drops one of `sh bash zsh fish ksh nu py rb pl php lua js mjs cjs ts mts ps1 bat cmd com exe vbs`, plus anything in `windows_executable_extensions` (case-insensitive). Any other extension is part of the name.
- `MISE_TASK_NAME` is the name `mise tasks ls` shows, so `build.sh` sees `build`.

## Behaviour changes and migration

- **`mise run <stem>` no longer reaches dotted TOML tasks.** `mise run test` used to run every `test.*` task. Run them by full name, or add a `test` task that depends on them.
- **A file task with an unknown extension keeps it.** `mise-tasks/gen.proto` was `gen` and is now `gen.proto`, so `mise run gen` and a `[tasks.gen]` block no longer reach it. Rename the file without the extension (or to a script extension), or use the full name `gen.proto`. No file task in mise's own e2e suite relied on this.
- **`MISE_TASK_NAME` no longer includes a file task's script extension.** A script that needs the file name can read `MISE_TASK_FILE`.
- **A TOML task named like a script keeps its extension when no script backs it.** `[tasks."lint.sh"] run = "..."` with no `mise-tasks/lint.sh` was listed as `lint` and run by `mise run lint`; it is now listed as `lint.sh` and runs only as `mise run lint.sh`.

## Validation

- New e2e `tasks/test_task_name_script_extensions` covers both TOML tasks listed and runnable by their full names, `build.sh` running as `build`, an unknown extension kept, a `[tasks."deploy.sh"]` takeover still listed as `deploy`, a TOML `lint.sh` with no script reachable only by its full name, and `MISE_TASK_NAME` in each case. It fails on `main`.
- New unit tests for `display_name` (file vs TOML tasks, monorepo paths with dots, `file = ...` TOML tasks) and for `is_match` / `get_matching` (only a file task matches without its script exten

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# Only a file task drops its extension, and only a known script extension:
+# `mise-tasks/build.sh` is `build`, but a TOML task's name is kept as written,
+# so `test.unit` and `test.e2e` are two tasks rather than both showing as
+# `test`. MISE_TASK_NAME carries the same name `mise tasks ls` shows.
+
+mkdir -p mise-tasks
+
+cat <<'EOF' >mise-tasks/build.sh
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "build-ran name=$MISE_TASK_NAME"
+EOF

+# `.proto` is not a script extension, so it stays part of the name.
+cat <<'EOF' >mise-tasks/gen.proto
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "gen-ran name=$MISE_TASK_NAME"
+EOF

+chmod +x mise-tasks/build.sh mise-tasks/gen.proto

title: fix(migrate): keep an unwritable stderr from aborting mise during a migration
body:
mise aborted with SIGABRT and dumped core when it had a migration to announce and could not write to stderr. Migrations run at the start of every command. In the original report, two `mise activate` processes aborted when a terminal closed while they were starting: a pty returns `EIO` once its master is gone. #10773 made mise's other stderr writes ignore such failures with `safe_eprintln!`, but the two prints in `src/migrate.rs` still used `eprintln!`, which panics on a failed write.

With mise 2026.10.3 on Linux, a pending migration plus an unwritable stderr:

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p "$tmp"/{d,s,c,cfg,work}
mkdir -p "$tmp/d/tracked-config-files"   # a legacy directory to migrate
cd "$tmp/work" && env HOME="$tmp" MISE_DATA_DIR="$tmp/d" MISE_STATE_DIR="$tmp/s" \
  MISE_CACHE_DIR="$tmp/c" MISE_CONFIG_DIR="$tmp/cfg" mise version >/dev/null 2>/dev/full
echo $?   # 134 (Aborted, core dumped); 0 without the legacy directory
```

Now both prints use `safe_eprintln!`, so the message is dropped and the command goes on.

This takes over #12301 by @GustavoDRL, who found and diagnosed the abort. pr-closer closed it after 7 days of a failing check. That check was the `nightly` toolchain job, which failed on compiler warnings unrelated to the change. They are credited as co-author. Since then, main went from four `eprintln!` calls in `migrate.rs` to two, and this changes those two. CodeRabbit and Greptile had no findings on #12301.

## Validation

- `e2e/cli/test_broken_stderr` now leaves a legacy `tracked-config-files` directory and runs `mise version` with stderr on `/dev/full`. It checks that the command succeeds and that the directory was moved, so the print was actually reached. The existing check runs with nothing to migrate, so it never reached these prints. The new step also removes the destination first, because an existing destination skips the move.
- With mise 2026.10.3 in a Debian container, the same sequence aborted with exit code 134. With stderr writable, it printed `migrating ~/.local/share/mise/tracked-config-files to ~/.local/state/mise/tracked-configs` and moved the directory, which is what the new assertions expect once the print cannot abort.
- CI: `cli/test_broken_stderr` passed in the Linux `e2e` job with this change.

title: security(http): redact URL credentials in debug logs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/567
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Debug logging printed credentials embedded in URLs. mise's logger only hides values that were registered as secrets, and a token in a URL's userinfo never is. With an spm `api_url` like `https://user:TOKEN@git.example.com/api/v1`, `MISE_DEBUG=1` printed the token in the HTTP request lines and, when the URL was passed on the command line, in the `DEBUG ARGS:` line.

Before:

```
DEBUG ARGS: mise x http:demo[url=https://user:SECRETTOKEN@127.0.0.1:9/x.tar.gz]@1.0.0 -- true
DEBUG GET https://user:SECRETTOKEN@127.0.0.1:9/x.tar.gz
```

After:

```
DEBUG ARGS: mise x http:demo[url=https://[redacted]@127.0.0.1:9/x.tar.gz]@1.0.0 -- true
DEBUG GET Downloading https://[redacted]@127.0.0.1:9/x.tar.gz to …/downloads/http-demo/1.0.0/x.tar.gz
DEBUG GET https://[redacted]@127.0.0.1:9/x.tar.gz
```

## How

- New `mise_util::redactions::redact_url_userinfo` replaces the `user:password@` part of every `scheme://` URL in a string with `[redacted]@`. The userinfo is everything before the last `@` in the authority, so an unencoded `@` in a password stays hidden; an `@` in the path or query is left alone. In log text whitespace ends a URL, so `https://host:8080 me@example.com` is left intact.
- The logger applies it to every record after the registered-secret redaction, on the terminal and in `MISE_LOG_FILE`.
- `DEBUG ARGS:` redacts each argument before joining them. Inside one argument only `/`, `?` or `#` ends the authority, so a password with a raw space (`https://user:my secret@host`, which URL parsers accept) is hidden too.
- The HTTP client's log sites, the `MISE_LOG_HTTP` line (an `eprintln!` that bypasses the logger), the retry warning, the `url_replacements` trace lines, and the HTML, request-timeout and download-timeout error messages also redact the URL directly. Errors are printed outside the logger, so they need their own redaction.

Only the userinfo is redacted. Query-string tokens (`?token=…`) are still logged as before.

## Validation

- Unit tests for `redact_url_userinfo` (password and username-only forms, `@` in path/query/password, several URLs in one line, URL inside parentheses, a port URL followed by an email address, spaces in an argument's userinfo) and for the HTTP client's URL formatting, plus a test that a request timing out against a `user:TOKEN@` URL returns an error without the token.
- Ran the debug binary with the command above and confirmed the token does not appear anywhere in the output.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: fix(plugins): install and compare git:: subdirectory sources from [plugins]
body:
Fixes the first two points of #14149.

A `[plugins]` entry in the `git::<url>//<subdir>?ref=<ref>` form installs, but:

- **On a data dir that never held a plugin**, the install clones into `plugin-repos/` and fails linking `plugins/<name>` because nothing created `plugins/` (`failed to ln -sf … No such file or directory`). `install_git_plugin_source` now creates the parent before `make_symlink`.
- **`configured_plugin_url` expanded the entry as a registry shorthand** (`https://github.com/:ssh://….git`). The drift check then warned on every `mise install`, and `mise plugins install --force <name>` reinstalled from the mangled URL, failed and left no plugin. `plugin_entry_to_url` now keeps a source that `RemoteSource::parse_git` recognises as is.

Tests:

- `test_plugin_entry_to_url_keeps_ref_outside_shorthand_expansion` gets `git::` ssh/https cases (with and without `?ref=`).
- `test_install_git_plugin_source_subdir_creates_the_plugins_dir` installs a local subdirectory plugin into a `plugins/` that does not exist yet.

Both fail on `main` without the change (`left: "https://github.com/:ssh://…"`; `failed to ln -sf … No such file or directory`) and pass with it. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --lib --tests -- -D warnings` are clean.

The third point of the issue (auto-install of `mise run` / `mise exec` resolving tools before `[plugins]` is installed) is not addressed here.

title: fix(config): apply config environment files in directory order
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/566
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When `MISE_ENV` is set, `mise.local.toml` now overrides `mise.<env>.toml` in the same directory, as the environments docs have said since 2024. Before this fix, a directory found by walking up from the cwd loaded its files in a different order from the global config directory. So your untracked local overrides lost to the committed environment file:

```toml
# mise.ci.toml (committed)
[env]
API_URL = "https://ci.example.com"

# mise.local.toml (untracked, your machine)
[env]
API_URL = "http://localhost:8080"
```

```console
$ MISE_ENV=ci mise env | grep API_URL
export API_URL='https://ci.example.com'   # before
export API_URL='http://localhost:8080'    # after
```

Every directory now ranks its files the same way, highest first:

1. `mise.<env>.local.toml`
2. `mise.local.toml`
3. `mise.<env>.toml`
4. `mise.toml`

The same rule covers the `.mise.*`, `mise/config.*`, `.config/mise/config.*` and `conf.d` variants. Across directories nothing changes: a project's files beat its parent directories and the global config.

This also fixes the global config directory (`~/.config/mise`). With a cwd under `$HOME`, mise found that directory again during the walk up from the cwd and used the walk's order. So `config.<env>.toml` beat `config.local.toml`, unless `MISE_CEILING_PATHS` stopped the walk. It now uses one order in both cases. The lockfile helper that lists `mise.*.lock` files already used this order.

### Migration

This only matters when one directory has both `mise.local.toml` (or another `.local` file) and `mise.<env>.toml`, and both set the same key. If you relied on the environment file winning, move those keys into `mise.<env>.local.toml`. `MISE_OVERRIDE_CONFIG_FILENAMES` behaves as before.

When `mise use` runs without `--env` in a directory that has only `mise.local.toml` and `mise.<env>.toml`, it now writes to `mise.<env>.toml`. mise writes to the lowest-precedence file, and that is now the environment file.

### Validation

- New e2e test `e2e/config/test_config_env_precedence` covers both `[tools]` and `[env]` for project vs parent vs global, env vs non-env, and local vs non-local, with and without `MISE_CEILING_PATHS`. On `main` it fails at the first walked-global check: `config.test.toml` beats `config.local.toml`.
- New unit test for the filename order. `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_request_precedence` asserted the old order as a side effect. It now expects the `mise.local.toml` pin to beat `mise.ci.toml`.
- The config, lockfile and env e2e areas, related cli tests, `cargo test --lib config::` and clippy (`-D warnings`) all pass.

title: fix(task): send mbx-cache headers to the remote task cache
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/565
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's remote task cache could not talk to the current cache server. mise sent `mise-cache-protocol` and `mise-cache-namespace` request headers, but [mbx-cache](https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington-cache) requires `mbx-cache-protocol` and `mbx-cache-namespace` and rejects any request without them with `426 Upgrade Required`. Every remote lookup and upload failed, so a configured `task.cache.remote_url` behaved like a local-only cache.

mise now sends the `mbx-cache-*` names, and remote task-cache hits work against mbx-cache. The [remote cache protocol guide](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/remote-cache-protocol.html) and the `scripts/task-cache-remote-compat.sh` conformance script use the new names too, and the [remote task cache guide](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/remote-cache.html) now names mbx-cache as the reference server. mbx-cache has no release yet, so the guide installs it with `cargo install --git https://github.com/jdx/mr-boxington-cache`.

## Before and after

With `task.cache.remote_url` pointing at an mbx-cache server, a run on a protected-branch push uploads its result, and a second checkout with an empty local cache should then restore from the remote cache.

Before:

```
mise WARN  remote task cache lookup failed for eee8f7c0…; using local cache only: HTTP status client error (426 Upgrade Required) for url (http://127.0.0.1:18471/v1/action-results/blake3/eee8f7c0…/332)
[build] cache miss: no matching cache entry
mise WARN  failed to mirror task cache entry eee8f7c0… remotely: HTTP status client error (426 Upgrade Required) …
```

After, in the second checkout:

```
[build] restored outputs from cache 9d2341fa…
```

## Compatibility

Servers that still read the old `mise-cache-*` headers (for example `mise-cache` 0.1.x) no longer accept mise's requests. Upgrade the server to mbx-cache. The remote task cache is experimental.

## Header names on the server

I checked the names in mbx-cache's source (jdx/mr-boxington-cache at `64eccb1`, `src/auth.rs` and `src/server.rs`) and in the protocol crate it uses (jdx/mr-boxington, `crates/mbx-cache-protocol/src/lib.rs`):

| Header | mise before | mbx-cache |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Protocol version | `mise-cache-protocol` | `mbx-cache-protocol` |
| Namespace | `mise-cache-namespace` | `mbx-cache-namespace` |
| Blob-pack count | `mise-cache-pack-blobs` | `mbx-cache-pack-blobs` |
| Blob-pack bytes | `mise-cache-pack-bytes` | `mbx-cache-pack-bytes` |

The routes, action-result and directory JSON shapes, and digest algorithms already match.

The blob-pack extension still differs in two ways: mbx-cache uses `application/vnd.mbx.cache-blob-pack.v1` and the magic `MBXPACK1`, while mise expects `application/vnd.mise.cache-blob-pack.v1` and `MISEPK01`. The task cache does not call the blob-pack client today, so this PR does not change it.

## Validation

- Against a local mbx-cache built from `64eccb1` (`-

title: feat(java)!: default java versions to Temurin builds
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/564
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Java versions without a vendor prefix (`java@21`, `java@lts`, `java@latest`) now install Eclipse Temurin builds. They used to install OpenJDK builds from jdk.java.net, which stop at the next feature release, so `java@21` was stuck on 21.0.2 (January 2024) with no security updates.

```console
$ mise latest java@21     # before
21.0.2
$ mise latest java@21     # after
21.0.12+101.0.LTS
$ mise latest java@lts    # before: 25.0.2, after:
25.0.4+101.0.LTS
```

The change is the default of `java.shorthand_vendor`, from `openjdk` to `temurin`. Vendor-prefixed requests such as `openjdk-21`, `temurin-21`, or `corretto-21` are unaffected.

## Migration

To keep the old builds, set the vendor back or ask for OpenJDK explicitly:

```toml
[settings]
java.shorthand_vendor = "openjdk"

[tools]
java = "openjdk-21" # or this, per project
```

What happens to existing setups after upgrading:

- **Installed versions keep working.** mise prefers an installed match, so `java = "21"` with OpenJDK 21.0.2 installed keeps using it in `mise x`, shims, and `mise ls`. `mise upgrade` / `mise outdated` now offer the Temurin build. A shorthand version that the current vendor does not publish, such as that installed `21.0.2` (Temurin's is `21.0.2+13`), still maps to the OpenJDK build when it is installed from OpenJDK or locked to the OpenJDK download, so locking and reinstalling it keep working. A fresh request never falls back: `java@12.0.2` finds nothing, as `mise latest` does.
- **Lockfiles record the vendor.** Since #9989, a shorthand lock entry stores `shorthand_vendor = "openjdk"` as part of its identity, and the version string is used as-is. That entry still matches when `java.shorthand_vendor = "openjdk"` is set. Without that setting:
  - `mise install --locked` (or `locked = true`) fails with `java@21 is not in the lockfile` and the hint to run `mise install` without `--locked`.
  - If no OpenJDK build is installed, an unlocked `mise install` or `mise lock` resolves the request again and replaces the entry with the Temurin build.
  - If the OpenJDK build is still installed, both reuse it. `mise lock` adds a `21.0.2` entry under the Temurin vendor with the OpenJDK download URLs, next to the old entry, so `mise install --locked` works again, including on machines without the OpenJDK build, which then install it from those URLs. `mise install` records `21.0.2` under the Temurin vendor with no download URLs.
  
  To keep the pinned OpenJDK build, set `java.shorthand_vendor = "openjdk"`. To move to Temurin, run `mise lock --bump java` and commit the result.
- **Versions Temurin doesn't publish.** Temurin has no builds of Java 9, 10, or 12 through 15. Shorthand requests for those versions now find nothing; use `openjdk-12` and similar.
- Shorthand versions now include Temurin's build suffix (`21.0.12+101.0.LTS`, `17.0.2+8`). A pinned `java = "17.0.2"` still resolves, to

title: fix(generate): update the GitHub Actions and devcontainer templates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/563
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise generate github-action` and `mise generate devcontainer` produced setups that were out of date or incomplete.

**GitHub Actions workflow.** The generated workflow used `actions/checkout@v6` and `jdx/mise-action@v3`, which are behind the current major releases (checkout v7.0.1 and mise-action v5.1.1). It also set `MISE_EXPERIMENTAL: true` for the whole workflow, which turned on experimental features that the generated `mise run <task>` step does not need. The workflow now uses the current majors and has no `env:` block:

```yaml
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: jdx/mise-action@v5
      - run: mise run ci
```

If your project relies on an experimental feature in CI, add `MISE_EXPERIMENTAL: 1` to the workflow yourself.

**Devcontainer.** The devcontainer feature installs mise but not the project's tools, so a fresh container started without them. The generated `devcontainer.json` now always sets `"postCreateCommand": "mise install"`. With `--mount-mise-data`, the command runs after the existing ownership fix: `"sudo chown -R vscode:vscode /mnt/mise-data && mise install"`. Like other `mise install` runs, this trusts the workspace's mise config, except in CI or when the `paranoid` setting is on.

Files that were already generated are not changed. To pick up these updates, run the generator again or edit the files by hand.

## Validation

- Added `e2e/generate/test_generate_github_action`. It fails on `main` because of the `checkout@v7` assertion, and it passes with this change.
- Updated `e2e/generate/test_generate_devcontainer` so it checks `image` and `postCreateCommand`. Its field lists named a `description` key that the generator never outputs, so `image` was never compared before.
- The `generate` e2e tests pass. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: chore: run e2e tests from mise run test and fix the registry test example
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/562
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise run test` (and so `mise run ci`) is meant to run the unit and e2e suites. It ran the unit tests, then called `test:e2e` with no arguments. That name resolves to the `xtasks/test/e2e` file task, which overrides the `test:e2e` entry in `tasks.toml`. With no arguments it runs no tests and exits 0, so the run reported success without running any e2e tests.

```console
$ mise tasks info test:e2e | grep Source
Source: ~/src/mise/xtasks/test/e2e
$ mise run test        # before: unit tests, then test:e2e with no tests run
$ mise run test        # after:  unit tests, then `test:e2e --all`
E2E: ran N tests, skipped M tests
```

This PR:

- makes `mise run test` call `mise tasks run test:e2e --all`
- removes the `test:e2e` entry from `tasks.toml`, which the file task always overrode
- fixes the example in the registry workflow's "New tools missing required 'test' field" error. It showed `test = ["mytool --version", "v{{version}}"]`, which the registry schema and `build.rs` reject. It now shows `test = { cmd = "mytool --version", expected = "{{version}}" }`, the form every registry entry uses.
- removes `[package.metadata.release]` from `Cargo.toml`. It configured cargo-release, whose task was removed in #11342, and nothing reads it now.

CI does not call `mise run test` or `mise run ci`, so CI is unaffected. Locally, `mise run test` now takes as long as a full e2e run. Slow tests still run only with `TEST_ALL=1`.

Validation: with the change, `TEST_TRANCHE_COUNT=600 TEST_TRANCHE=0 mise tasks run test:e2e --all` ran 3 tests; before, `mise tasks run test:e2e` ran none. Clippy, taplo and prettier pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Local developer workflow and docs-only CI messaging; no production runtime or security paths changed.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise run test`** (and **`mise run ci`**) now runs the full e2e suite by invoking **`test:e2e --all`**. Previously it called **`test:e2e`** with no args; that resolves to the **`xtasks/test/e2e`** file task, which ran zero tests and still exited successfully.
> 
> The redundant **`test:e2e`** block was removed from **`tasks.toml`** because the file task always took precedence.
> 
> The registry workflow’s error message for new tools missing a **`test`** field now shows the correct table form **`test = { cmd = ..., expected = ... }`** instead of an invalid array example.
> 
> Dead **`[package.metadata.release]`** config was removed from **`Cargo.toml`** after the cargo-release task was dropped elsewhere.

title: fix: point error hints at current commands
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/561
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Several error and warning messages suggested an outdated command, used an old feature name, or gave advice that cannot work. This PR updates them. Only the message text changes; mise behaves the same otherwise.

**Remote installs gave advice that cannot work.** When `mise bootstrap remote` installs mise (`install_mise`) to a directory that is not on the host's login PATH, the warning used to say:

```
WARN  /home/me/bin/mise is not on host's login PATH; add its directory to PATH or declare [bootstrap.mise_shell_activate] in the bootstrap project
```

Declaring `[bootstrap.mise_shell_activate]` does not help. The activation blocks it writes run `mise activate …` by name, so they also need mise on PATH. The warning now names the directory to add:

```
WARN  /home/me/bin/mise is not on host's login PATH; add /home/me/bin to PATH
```

**Other messages**

- When watchexec is missing, `mise watch` now suggests `mise use -g watchexec`, the same command its help shows. It used to suggest `watchexec@latest`.
- `mise cache task` now says "No artifact cache entries for …", the feature's current name. It used to say "output cache".

No migration is needed. Scripts that match on the old wording of these messages will need updating.

**Validation:** e2e tests now check each new message, and each of those tests fails without this change. One is new, `e2e/cli/test_watch_missing_watchexec`, which runs `mise watch` with only mise on PATH and a 30 second limit; the others are updated assertions in `test_bootstrap_remote` and `test_task_artifact_cache_inspect`. Clippy (`-D warnings`) and hk checks pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

> **Low Risk**
> String-only changes to warnings and error hints; scripts that assert on old message text may need updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> **User-facing message fixes** so hints match current behavior and workable fixes—no functional behavior changes beyond wording.
> 
> **Remote bootstrap:** When an installed `mise` binary isn’t on the host’s login PATH, the warning now tells users to add the **parent directory** to PATH and drops the misleading `[bootstrap.mise_shell_activate]` suggestion (activation still needs `mise` on PATH).
> 
> **`mise watch`:** Missing `watchexec` now suggests `mise use -g watchexec` instead of `watchexec@latest`, aligned with help text. New e2e covers this with a PATH that only contains `mise`.

> 
> **Tests:** Remote bootstrap e2e captures install output and asserts the new PATH warning (and that `mise_shell_activate` isn’t mentioned).

title: fix(plugins): install packslip entries in [plugins] as vfox plugins
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/560
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `[plugins]` entry with no type prefix that points at a signed packslip plugin archive was treated as an asdf plugin until it was installed:

```toml
[plugins]
external-bfs = "packslip:mise-plugins/vfox-bfs#0.1.0-dev.2"
```

Before this change, `mise tool external-bfs` resolved to asdf, and `mise install` tried to clone `packslip:...` with Git, which failed. `mise plugins install external-bfs` already used the vfox type for packslip sources. Config loading and the `[plugins]` auto-install now do the same: the tool resolves to `vfox:external-bfs`, and `mise install` installs the plugin from the signed archive.

A plugin that is already installed keeps the type found on disk. If you change an existing entry from a Git URL to a packslip archive, an installed asdf plugin is still treated as asdf, not driven as a vfox plugin.

An entry with an explicit non-vfox prefix and a packslip source, such as `"asdf:foo" = "packslip:..."`, now fails in `mise install` with the same message `mise plugins install` gives ("packslip plugin sources require the vfox plugin type"). Before, it failed with a confusing Git error.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core plugin-type resolution during config load and install; wrong inference could mis-route installs, but behavior is narrowed with tests and preserves on-disk types for existing plugins.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Unprefixed `[plugins]` entries that use a `packslip:` source now resolve and install as vfox plugins** instead of defaulting to asdf and attempting a Git clone.
> 
> Plugin type detection gains `PluginType::from_plugin_entry(key, url)`: explicit key prefixes still win; if the plugin is not yet on disk, a `packslip:` URL selects vfox and other URLs stay asdf. **Config load** (install-state registration) and **`mise install`’s `[plugins]` auto-install** both use this logic so `mise tool` and install agree with `mise plugins install`. Already-installed plugins keep the type inferred from disk even if the config URL changes to packslip.
> 
> **`asdf:…` (or other non-vfox prefixes) with a packslip URL** now fails during `mise install` with *packslip plugin sources require the vfox plugin type* instead of a Git error. An e2e script and unit tests cover unprefixed packslip install and the explicit-prefix rejection.

title: fix(plugins): install git:: plugins from a subdirectory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/559
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing a plugin from a `git::` source that points at a subdirectory of a repository failed when it was the first plugin installed:

```console
$ mise plugins install tiny "git::https://git.example.com/org/monorepo.git//plugins/tiny"
mise plugin:tiny     clone https://git.example.com/org/monorepo.git
mise plugin:tiny     link ~/.local/share/mise/plugins/tiny
Error:
   0: failed to ln -sf ~/.local/share/mise/plugin-repos/tiny/plugins/tiny ~/.local/share/mise/plugins/tiny
   1: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

mise clones the repository into `plugin-repos/` and links `plugins/<name>` to the subdirectory, but nothing had created the `plugins/` directory yet. When the install did succeed, it also printed a spurious `WARN failed to open git repository at ".../plugins/tiny"`, because mise read the commit from the linked subdirectory instead of from the clone.

Now the install creates `plugins/` before linking, and reports the installed commit from the clone without a warning:

```console
$ mise plugins install tiny "git::https://git.example.com/org/monorepo.git//plugins/tiny"
mise plugin:tiny   ✓ https://git.example.com/org/monorepo.git#d066db6
```

Nothing to migrate. Whole-repository git, zip and local plugin installs are unchanged.

Validation: the new e2e test `e2e/plugins/test_plugin_install_git_subdir` installs a subdirectory plugin from a local git repository into an empty data directory. It fails on `main` and passes with this change. The existing plugin install, link, update and drift e2e tests still pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Low Risk**
> Narrow fix in git subdirectory plugin install path creation and return value; other install modes untouched.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`git::…//subdir`** plugin installs when **`plugins/`** does not exist yet (e.g. first plugin on a fresh data dir). The clone still goes under **`plugin-repos/`**, but mise now **creates the parent of the plugin symlink** before linking, so **`ln -sf`** no longer fails with “No such file or directory”.
> 
> After linking, install reporting now uses the **`Git` handle from the clone** instead of opening git at the symlinked subdirectory, which removes the spurious **WARN** about failing to open the repository at **`plugins/<name>`**.
> 
> Adds e2e **`test_plugin_install_git_subdir`**: local monorepo fixture, empty **`MISE_DATA_DIR`**, asserts symlink target, no WARN, and **`mise ls-remote`** works. Whole-repo git, zip, and local plugin installs are unchanged.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# A git:: source with a //subdir clones the whole repository into

+
+repo="$PWD/sources/monorepo"
+mkdir -p "$repo/plugins/tiny/bin"
+cat >"$repo/plugins/tiny/bin/list-all" <<'EOF'

title: fix(bootstrap): support absent and unapply for systemd units
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/558
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Before this change, `[bootstrap.linux.systemd.units]` had no way to remove a unit. `state = "absent"` was reported as an unknown field, and an entry without `exec_start` was rejected. `mise bootstrap unapply` also left a module's systemd units in place. Timer units in particular were never removed by any command.

Now an entry can be declared absent:

```toml
[bootstrap.linux.systemd.units.backup]
state = "absent"

[bootstrap.linux.systemd.units.backup-timer]
state = "absent"
```

`mise bootstrap` or `mise bootstrap linux systemd-units apply` then stops, disables and deletes `dev.mise.<name>.timer` and `dev.mise.<name>.service` for each name. It removes timers first, then runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload`. You don't need to say whether the name was a service or a timer, and the other keys can stay in the entry. `status` shows such entries as `present` until they are removed and `absent` afterwards, and `--missing` passes once nothing is installed.

`mise bootstrap unapply <env>` now also removes the systemd user units an environment contributes, timers included. As with other resources:
- units the base configuration still declares are kept;
- a unit whose file or enablement changed since it was written is kept unless you pass `--force`;
- `--dry-run` lists units as `systemd-unit:dev.mise.<name>.<service|timer>`.

The JSON schema accepts `state = "present" | "absent"` on systemd units. No migration is needed: existing entries default to `present`.

Validation: a new e2e test uses a fake `systemctl --user` to cover absent apply, the converged second run, and unapply with and without `--force`. On main it fails at the first `state = "absent"` check. Unit tests and the tombi schema test were also extended.

title: fix(bootstrap): keep applying other package managers after one fails
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/557
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Until now, `mise bootstrap packages apply` (and `mise bootstrap`) stopped at the first package manager that hit an error. That manager's pending installs and every manager declared after it were silently skipped. A single `state = "absent"` entry was enough to cause this:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"apt:nano" = { state = "absent" }   # apt cannot remove packages declaratively
"apt:curl" = "latest"
"brew:ripgrep" = "latest"
```

Before: if nano was installed, the apply failed with `apt does not support declarative package removal`, and neither curl nor ripgrep was installed. A removal that fails on a manager that does support removal had the same effect. Examples are Scoop with an app installed in the global scope, or pacman/zypper refusing to remove a package that another one depends on.

After:

- Each package manager runs on its own. If a removal fails, that manager still installs its other packages. If any step fails, the next manager still runs.
- The run still fails at the end when anything failed. A single failure keeps its usual message. Several are listed together, one line per manager:
  ```
  2 package manager operations failed:
    scoop: scoop: 'git' installed globally; ...
    zypper: ...
  ```
- An absent entry that a manager cannot remove (apk, apt, dnf, brew, ...) is skipped with a warning during a whole-config apply, the same way an unsatisfiable version pin is. `mise bootstrap packages status` still reports it. When the run is scoped with `--manager <name>` or explicit packages, the entry still fails the run, as an unavailable manager does in those scopes. The other packages are installed first.

Unit tests use a fake manager to cover these cases: an unsupported removal in a whole-config run and in a scoped run, a failed removal, a failed install, and several failures combined. The zypper and status e2e tests still pass.

title: fix(bootstrap): skip the firewall section where it is unsupported
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/556
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A shared `mise.toml` with a `[bootstrap.linux.firewall]` section broke `mise bootstrap` on macOS and Windows. On Linux, several read-only firewall commands failed when they should have reported. This PR fixes five such problems.

### macOS and Windows skip the Linux firewall

Before, `mise bootstrap` and `mise bootstrap plan` failed with `bootstrap firewall management is only supported on Linux` whenever a config declared a Linux firewall. Now they skip the section with a warning, the same way they handle users and groups:

```
mise WARN ignoring [bootstrap.linux.firewall] on non-Linux host
```

The explicit `mise bootstrap firewall apply` still refuses to run on those hosts.

### Read-only commands report an SSH lockout risk instead of failing

mise refuses a firewall config that could lock out the SSH session it runs in. That check used to run while the config loaded, so `mise bootstrap firewall status`, `firewall apply --dry-run`, `bootstrap status`, `bootstrap plan` and `bootstrap --dry-run` all failed. They now show the firewall as `unknown`, give the reason, and do not need sudo to inspect it. A real `mise bootstrap firewall apply` still refuses, and so does `mise bootstrap`, before it changes anything.

**Behaviour change:** a dry run of a lockout-prone config now exits 0 and warns:

```
would not change firewall:linux: current unavailable: refusing firewall ... (manual action required)
```

If CI gates on `mise bootstrap --dry-run`, that check will now pass while the real run still refuses.

### Dry runs work after the firewall has been applied

Applying the firewall saves state in a root-only file. Later, a non-root `mise bootstrap firewall apply --dry-run` or `mise bootstrap --dry-run` failed with `Permission denied` whenever changes were pending. The preview is now computed by the elevated inspection, so the dry run never reads that file itself.

### The UFW preview lists every command apply runs

With `backend = "ufw"`, the dry run now shows the `ufw --force reset` that `exclusive = true` runs, and the default policy commands:

```
would run ufw --force reset
would run ufw allow ...
would run ufw default deny incoming
would run ufw default allow outgoing
would run ufw --force enable
```

### `--dry-run --skip firewall` leaves the firewall alone

`mise bootstrap --dry-run --skip firewall` no longer inspects the firewall, which needed sudo, while it predicts Compose projects.

title: fix(bootstrap): show hooks that use exec() in dry runs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/555
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap --dry-run` (and `mise bootstrap dotfiles apply --dry-run`) stopped as soon as a `[bootstrap.hooks]` command needed `exec()`:

```toml
[bootstrap.hooks.post-packages]
run = "echo {{ exec(command='git rev-parse HEAD') }}"
```

```
Error: [bootstrap.hooks.post-packages] in mise.toml: failed to render template: exec() is disabled during dry run
```

The same thing happened, with a "variable not found" error, when a hook read a var that is computed with `exec()` in config the dotfiles introduce:

```toml
# dotfiles/mise/config.toml, linked to ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[vars]
sha = "{{ exec(command='git rev-parse HEAD') }}"

[bootstrap.hooks.post-dotfiles]
run = "echo {{ vars.sha }}"
```

Such a hook is now printed as written, with a note that carries the render error, and the preview continues:

```
mise [bootstrap.hooks.post-dotfiles] in ~/.config/mise/config.toml: showing the command unrendered because a dry run does not run exec() or compute the vars that need it; render error: error: Field `sha` is not defined.
sh -o errexit -c 'echo {{ vars.sha }}'
```

The rule:

> A dry run never calls exec() and never substitutes made-up values. Hooks and dry-run vars are rendered with the values the dry run could compute; vars that need exec() (directly or through another var) are left undefined. If that render succeeds, the preview shows it. If it fails and the dry run left any var unresolved or the template called exec(), the hook is shown unrendered with a note that includes the render error, and the dry run continues. If it fails with nothing unresolved and no exec() call, it is an error, as in a real run. While any var is unresolved, a template that uses the `vars` map as a whole rather than one entry at a time (`vars | json_encode`, `{% for k, v in vars %}`, `{% set v = vars %}`) is also shown unrendered, since it would render without the vars the dry run could not compute. The check for this does not parse the template: any `vars` not written as `vars.NAME` or `vars[...]` counts, even in a `{% raw %}` block or plain text, so it can only err toward an unrendered preview.

Known limitation: a template that tolerates an undefined var (`default`, `is defined`) renders its fallback in the preview.

Real runs are unchanged. Under `tera_v1`, render errors now keep their cause, so the note says what failed instead of only "Failed to render '__tera_one_off'".

Tests: unit test `test_render_for_dry_run` in mise-util, on both Tera engines. e2e coverage in `e2e/cli/test_bootstrap`: a hook that calls `exec()`; hooks that read an exec()-computed var from dotfiles config directly, through an alias (`{% set v = vars %}`), through `read_file(path=...)`, `| hash_file`, and `| extname`, or through the whole map (`vars | json_encode`, a `for` loop over `vars`), are shown unrendered and do not run; a broken hook next to an unresolved var is shown unren

title: fix(bootstrap): keep shell activation when a dotfile is tracked
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/554
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tracking a shell startup file made `mise bootstrap` stop writing mise's activation block into it. Tracking only records a file's history and writes nothing, so it should not change what bootstrap writes.

With this global config:

```toml
[bootstrap.mise_shell_activate]
zsh = true

[dotfiles]
"~/.zshrc" = { mode = "track" }
```

**Before:** `mise bootstrap --dry-run` planned only `edit ~/.zprofile (block:activate)`. `~/.zshrc` never got `eval "$(mise activate zsh)"`, and `mise bootstrap mise-shell-activate status` did not list the zshrc target.

**After:** bootstrap plans and applies the activation block in both `~/.zprofile` and `~/.zshrc`. The rest of the tracked file is left as it was.

Rules that already applied are unchanged. A `[dotfiles]` entry that deploys the whole startup file, or an explicit edit with the same block id (for example `"~/.zshrc/activate"`), still replaces the generated activation block. The same fix covers `mode = "track-local"`. No migration is needed.

Validation: the new e2e test `cli/test_bootstrap_shell_activate_tracked` fails without the fix and passes with it. The existing `test_bootstrap_shell_activate` and `test_dotfiles_files` tests still pass.

title: fix: keep temporary files out of the cache directory
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/553
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

On Windows, mise's default cache directory is `%TEMP%\mise`. That is also the default temporary directory (`MISE_TMP_DIR`). Running `mise cache clear`, or the automatic cache prune, deletes the whole cache directory, so it also deleted temporary files mise was still using: the envrc files `mise direnv envrc` writes and node's build and patch directories.

The same thing happened on any platform when `MISE_CACHE_DIR` pointed at `$TMPDIR/mise`, including when it was written differently from the system temp path, for example macOS `/private/var/folders/...` instead of `/var/folders/...`.

## Fix

When `MISE_TMP_DIR` is not set and the default `<temp>/mise` is inside the cache directory, temporary files now go to `<temp>/mise-tmp`. The check compares resolved paths, so symlinks, `..`, and differences in letter case on Windows are handled.

- An explicit `MISE_TMP_DIR` is used as before.
- `MISE_CACHE_DIR` and the cache location are unchanged.
- On Linux and macOS with default settings nothing changes: the cache is under `~/.cache` / `~/Library/Caches`, so temporary files stay in `<temp>/mise`.

Before (Windows defaults):

```
%TEMP%\mise\direnv\...   <- deleted by `mise cache clear`
```

After:

```
%TEMP%\mise\             <- cache
%TEMP%\mise-tmp\direnv\  <- temporary files, kept by `mise cache clear`
```

If `MISE_CACHE_DIR` is the temp directory itself or one of its parents (for example `MISE_CACHE_DIR=/tmp`), no default outside the cache exists. mise logs a debug message suggesting a `MISE_TMP_DIR` outside the cache.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Startup path selection for unset MISE_TMP_DIR only; explicit overrides and normal Unix/macOS defaults are unchanged, with tests covering edge cases.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`mise cache clear`** (and cache prune) wiping live temporary files when the default cache and temp locations overlap—especially on Windows where both default to **`%TEMP%\mise`**.
> 
> When **`MISE_TMP_DIR`** is unset, the default temp root is still **`<temp>/mise`**, but if that path is inside **`MISE_CACHE_DIR`** (checked via resolved **`is_within`**, so symlinks, `..`, and Windows case differences count), mise uses **`<temp>/mise-tmp`** instead. Explicit **`MISE_TMP_DIR`** and typical Linux/macOS layouts (cache under home, temp under **`$TMPDIR`**) are unchanged. If no sibling outside the cache exists, a debug log suggests setting **`MISE_TMP_DIR`**.
> 
> Adds unit coverage for **`default_tmp_dir`** and an e2e check that **`mise direnv envrc`** temp dirs survive **`mise cache clear`** when **`MISE_CACHE_DIR=$TMPDIR/mise`**.

title: fix(ruby): expand {os} and {arch} in precompiled URLs correctly
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/552
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When `ruby.precompiled_url` is a custom URL template, the `{arch}` and `{os}` placeholders were split wrong. mise split the platform id on its first underscore, so on x86_64 Linux it downloaded from a URL that did not exist:

```toml
[settings.ruby]
precompiled_url = "https://mirror.example.com/ruby-{version}-{arch}-{os}.tar.gz"
```

| Platform | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| x86_64 Linux | `ruby-3.3.0-x86-64_linux.tar.gz` | `ruby-3.3.0-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| arm64 macOS | `ruby-3.3.0-macos-.tar.gz` | `ruby-3.3.0-arm64-macos.tar.gz` |
| arm64 Linux | `ruby-3.3.0-arm64-linux.tar.gz` | unchanged |

mise now splits the platform id on its last underscore. The arm64-only macOS build, whose platform id is just `macos`, now expands to `{arch}`=`arm64` and `{os}`=`macos`. When `ruby.precompiled_arch` and `ruby.precompiled_os` are both set, `{arch}` and `{os}` take those values as given, so an override such as `precompiled_os = "linux_musl"` is not split. Templates that use only `{platform}` and `{version}`, and the default `jdx/ruby` GitHub source, are unaffected. No migration is needed.

New unit tests cover x86_64 Linux, arm64 Linux, macOS, and an explicit `arm64` / `linux_musl` override. They fail without the fix. The existing Ruby plugin tests pass.

title: fix(node): verify GPG signatures for every node version
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/551
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise is supposed to check node's signed `SHASUMS256.txt` before it trusts a download's checksum, but it only did this when the version string started with `2`. So installing node 18, 19, 16 or any older release skipped signature verification without saying so, even though nodejs.org publishes `SHASUMS256.txt.sig` for those releases. The same check would also have stopped working once node reached 30.x.

Before:

```console
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise install node@18.20.8 2>&1 | grep SHASUMS
GET https://nodejs.org/dist/v18.20.8/SHASUMS256.txt 200 OK
```

After:

```console
$ MISE_DEBUG=1 mise install node@18.20.8 2>&1 | grep SHASUMS
GET https://nodejs.org/dist/v18.20.8/SHASUMS256.txt 200 OK
GET https://nodejs.org/dist/v18.20.8/SHASUMS256.txt.sig 200 OK
```

Now every node version is checked, unless `node.gpg_verify` (or the global `gpg_verify`) is `false`. The bundled node release keyring verifies real signatures from v0.10.48 through v25.0.0. A few early releases (for example 0.12.0, 4.0.0 and 5.12.0) never published a signature; those still install, with the existing `gpg signature not found, skipping verification` warning.

Migration: you do not need to change anything. If you use a mirror that has no signatures, or that answers the `.sig` request with something other than 404, older versions now behave the way 20+ already did. Set `node.gpg_verify = false` to turn the check off.

Validation: a new e2e test (`e2e/core/test_node_gpg_verify`) serves an 18.x mirror whose signature does not match. The install fails on main's behaviour and is now rejected at the signature check. I also did real installs of 18.20.8 and 5.12.0 from nodejs.org.

The mistaken prefix check meant 18.x/19.x and future 30.x would skip signature validation even though nodejs.org publishes `.sig` files; releases without a signature still skip via the existing 404 path in `verify_with_gpg`.

title: fix(java): key the version cache by vendor and keep release_type
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/550
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Two Java version-listing bugs:

**Changing `java.shorthand_vendor` had no effect until the cache expired.** Shorthand versions like `21.0.2` were saved in the Java metadata cache for whichever vendor was set when the cache was filled. After switching vendors, mise kept resolving to the old vendor's builds:

```console
$ mise latest java@21
21.0.2
$ MISE_JAVA_SHORTHAND_VENDOR=temurin mise latest java@21
21.0.2                 # before: still the openjdk build
21.0.12+101.0.LTS      # after: temurin
```

The cache now stores only full `<vendor>-<version>` entries. Shorthand versions are worked out from the current vendor each time versions are listed, so a vendor change takes effect immediately and `mise cache clear` is no longer needed.

**Inline `release_type` was ignored.** `release_type = "ea"` worked in `mise.toml`, but the inline form was dropped when listing or resolving a prefix:

```console
$ mise latest 'java[release_type=ea]@openjdk-28'
                       # before: nothing found
openjdk-28.0.0-ea+18   # after
```

`mise ls-remote 'java[release_type=ea]'` now lists early-access builds too. Installing an exact EA version already worked and is unchanged.

There is no migration. Install paths, lockfile entries and the default vendor are unchanged. With the default vendor, `mise ls-remote java` output is identical to before.

### Validation

- New unit tests cover the cache contents across vendors and an inline `release_type` reaching the Java backend. Both fail with the old behaviour.
- New e2e test `e2e/core/test_java_listing_options`.
- Existing Java e2e tests pass, including `test_java_shorthand_vendor_slow` and `test_java_slow` (EA install).

title: fix(spm): use a custom api_url for cloning and skip lockfile URLs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/548
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Two fixes for Swift Package Manager (`spm:`) tools.

## Packages given as a slug clone from the `api_url` host

Before, a package given as `owner/repo` was always cloned from github.com or gitlab.com, even when `api_url` pointed at GitHub Enterprise or a self-managed GitLab. Releases were listed from your server, but the clone went to the public host and failed (or fetched a different repository with the same name).

```toml
[tools."spm:acme/SwiftTool"]
version = "1.2.0"
api_url = "https://github.acme.com/api/v3"
```

Before, this cloned `https://github.com/acme/SwiftTool.git`. It now clones `https://github.acme.com/acme/SwiftTool.git`.

The clone host is derived from `api_url` only when the URL has a recognized shape:

| `api_url` | clones from |
| --- | --- |
| `https://github.acme.com/api/v3` | `https://github.acme.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` |
| `https://api.acme.ghe.com` | `https://acme.ghe.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` |
| `https://gitlab.acme.com/api/v4` | `https://gitlab.acme.com/<owner>/<repo>.git` |
| `https://acme.com/gitlab/api/v4` | `https://acme.com/gitlab/<owner>/<repo>.git` |
| anything else, e.g. a proxy at `https://ghproxy.acme.com/api/github` | github.com / gitlab.com, as before |

Credentials embedded in `api_url` are not copied into the clone URL. A cached checkout whose remote differs from the package URL is cloned again. To clone from any other host, give the full repository URL as the tool name (`spm:https://git.acme.com/acme/SwiftTool.git`).

## `mise install --locked` works for spm tools

spm packages are usually built from source, so `mise lock` records no download URL for them. `mise install --locked` then always failed:

```
No lockfile URL found for spm:acme/SwiftTool@1.2.0 on platform linux-x64 (--locked mode)
```

spm is now exempt from the lockfile-URL check, like cargo, go and pipx. Checksum verification is unchanged.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/547
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On the `github`, `gitlab` and `forgejo` backends, mise ignored a `size` tool option unless `checksum` was also set. A config like this downloaded and installed the asset without checking its size:

```toml
[tools."github:owner/repo"]

size = "4096"

**Stricter `size` parsing:** on these backends, a `size` value that is not a number (for example `size = "4k"`) used to be ignored when no checksum was set. It now fails the install. On every backend that reads the option (`http`, `s3`, `github`, `gitlab`, `forgejo`), the error now names the option, `invalid size option: 4k`, instead of a bare `invalid digit found in string`.

title: fix(generate): skip hidden and global tasks in task-stubs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/546
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise generate task-stubs` wrote a stub for every task mise could see, including hidden tasks and tasks from your global config (`~/.config/mise/config.toml`). Those stubs get committed to the project. A stub for a global task runs a task that other contributors don't have, and a hidden task, which is meant to be internal, got a public `bin/` entrypoint.

Given this setup:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[tasks.myglobal]
run = "echo myglobal"

# mise.toml
[tasks.visible]
run = "echo visible"

[tasks.secret]
run = "echo secret"
hide = true
```

Before:

```console
$ mise generate task-stubs
Wrote to bin/myglobal
Wrote to bin/myglobal.cmd
Wrote to bin/secret
Wrote to bin/secret.cmd
Wrote to bin/visible
Wrote to bin/visible.cmd
```

After:

```console
$ mise generate task-stubs
Wrote to bin/visible
Wrote to bin/visible.cmd
```

The command's help text now mentions that hidden and global tasks are skipped.

**Migration:** stubs generated earlier for hidden or global tasks are not deleted. Remove them from `bin/` by hand if you don't want them. If you need a stub for a hidden task, write it by hand, or remove `hide = true` from the task.

title: fix(settings): reject settings set in places mise ignores them
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/545
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise settings set` used to accept settings in files where mise never reads them. The command reported success and nothing changed:

- **Early-init settings** (`env`, `auto_env`, `env_conf_d`, `ceiling_paths`, `ignored_config_paths`, `override_config_filenames`, `override_tool_versions_filenames`) decide which config files load. mise reads them only from `miserc.toml` files and environment variables. `mise settings set` still wrote them into `config.toml` or `mise.toml`.
- **Global-only settings** (`yes`, `trusted_config_paths`, `paranoid`, …) are removed from project configs for security reasons. `mise settings set --local` still wrote them into the project's `mise.toml`. After that, every command printed an "is ignored for security reasons" warning, and `mise settings get` showed the old value.

Now both are refused, and the error says where the setting has to go:

```console
$ mise settings set ceiling_paths /tmp
Error: ceiling_paths cannot be set in a config file: mise reads it before config files load. Set it in ~/.config/mise/miserc.toml or the MISE_CEILING_PATHS environment variable instead.

$ mise settings set --local env_conf_d true
Error: env_conf_d cannot be set in a config file: mise reads it before config files load. Set it in .miserc.toml or the MISE_ENV_CONF_D environment variable instead.

$ mise settings set --local yes true
Error: yes cannot be set in ~/project/mise.toml: mise ignores it outside the global config for security reasons. Drop --local to set it in the global config, or use the MISE_YES environment variable.
```

`mise settings add` gets the same checks. Setting a global-only setting without `--local` works as before. `mise settings unset` is not affected, so you can still use it to remove an entry that an earlier version wrote.

**Migration:** scripts that ran these commands were already getting no effect, so nothing that worked before breaks. They now fail instead. Move the setting to `miserc.toml`, the global config, or its `MISE_*` environment variable, as the error says.

Validation: the new e2e test `e2e/cli/test_settings_set_placement` fails on `main` and passes with this change. The existing `settings` e2e tests and the settings unit tests pass.
