title: fix(shim): stop system fallback cycles through wrappers
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/512
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When an unconfigured Unix shim falls back to a system wrapper that execs the bare command name again, the wrapper can re-enter the shim indefinitely. Mise now rejects a repeated `(command name, canonical fallback path)` handoff in the same PID with an error telling the user to set a version or remove the shim.

Addresses [discussion #14086](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14086), as a follow-up to #14084's separate npm backend fix. Based on @alleneubank's proposed PID-owned fallback chain, with co-author credit.

A child process starts a fresh chain, so legitimate nested calls such as `bun run` invoking `bun` remain valid. Distinct wrappers can form a finite chain, with a 32-handoff safety limit. Configured tools and command wrappers clear the chain. Recording happens only after the final lookup, including any `auto_update` lookup, and the serialized paths retain their exact bytes.

This guard covers Unix symlink-shim fallback through same-process `exec` chains. It does not bound cycles that spawn new child processes or change Windows shim dispatch.

Validation on macOS:
- Six focused unit tests pass.
- The new e2e regression fails against released 2026.10.4 and passes with the patch. It covers normal and relocated shims, a 12-wrapper finite chain, legitimate child-process nesting, and clearing state on configured-wrapper resolution, including templated early settings.
- Four existing shim/exec regression tests pass.
- `cargo check --all-features`, strict workspace Clippy, formatting, ShellCheck, and shfmt pass. hk's Cargo step denies existing manifest warnings (redundant homepage and unused optional OpenSSL dependency), so that step was skipped in the scoped hk run and Cargo was checked directly.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core Unix shim dispatch and system-fallback behavior; mistakes could block legitimate wrapper chains or fail to stop infinite loops.
> 
> **Overview**
> On Unix, when an unconfigured shim uses **system fallback** and the resolved binary is a wrapper that `exec`s the same command name again, mise could loop indefinitely. This PR adds a **PID-scoped fallback chain** (`__MISE_SHIM_FALLBACK_CHAIN`) that records each `(command name, canonical fallback path)` handoff and **bails** if the same pair repeats, with a **32-handoff** cap and guidance to set a version or remove the shim.
> 
> Shim resolution is refactored to return a **`ShimCommand`** (`Tool`, `Wrapper`, or `SystemFallback`); only **system fallback** paths extend the chain after the final lookup (including post-`auto_update` re-resolve). Entering a configured tool or command wrapper **clears** inherited chain state so wrappers do not leak across resolutions. Child processes get a fresh chain, so patterns like a wrapper spawning the same name r

title: ci: install mold from its GitHub release instead of apt
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/511
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `lint` job fails whenever the Ubuntu mirrors behind `apt-get install mold` time out. Recent runs failed at "Install mold" with `Connection failed [IP: 91.189.91.81 80]`, so unrelated PRs go red on a network error.

This installs mold from its GitHub release through the mise binary the job already downloads, so it no longer depends on the Ubuntu mirrors:

```yaml
- name: Install mold
  working-directory: ${{ runner.temp }}
  run: mise x mold@2 -- sh -c 'dirname "$(command -v mold)"' >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
```

It runs from `runner.temp` so the repo's own tools are not installed at that point, and it puts the directory holding `mold` and `ld.mold` on `PATH`, as the apt package did. I ran the same command locally and it installs mold 2.42.1 and prints that directory.

Nothing else in the repo references mold, so if the lint job does not need it at all, this step can be deleted instead. I kept it to avoid changing what lint runs against.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI-only change to how the linker is installed; no application or build logic changes.

> **Overview**
> **Replaces apt-based mold installation in the lint job** with a post-artifact step that installs **mold 2** via the downloaded `mise` binary (`mise x mold@2`), appending its directory to `PATH` the same way the apt package did.

title: fix(npm): stop npm view from re-entering mise through a foreign shim
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/510
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14068. Recreates #14072 by @tfournet, who found and fixed the bug.

With `npm.shell_out`, `mise latest npm:<pkg>` could run a mise shim from another data dir as `npm`. That happens when an outer mise's shims are on `PATH` while `HOME` or `MISE_DATA_DIR` point elsewhere, as in test runners and CI. The shim re-entered mise, which ran `npm view` again for every `latest` npm tool. The process count grew at every level until the machine ran out of memory.

`npm view` now resolves `npm` from the child `PATH` itself and skips any candidate that is the running mise binary. If a mise shim was the only npm, mise stops with an error instead of spawning it:

```
npm.shell_out needs npm, but the only npm on PATH is a mise shim (/outer/shims/npm); running it would re-enter mise. Install node first (`mise install node`) or disable npm.shell_out.
```

If a real npm exists later on `PATH`, it is used. If there is no npm at all, the behavior and error are unchanged. Windows is unchanged.

Changes from #14072:
- A hard link to the mise binary is now detected by device and inode. `file::same_file` compares paths, so it missed hard links.
- An empty `PATH` entry resolves to an absolute path. A bare `npm` made the child search `PATH` again and find the shim that was just skipped.
- A directory named `npm` is no longer picked over a real npm later on `PATH`.
- The e2e test's process cap counts threads, since `RLIMIT_NPROC` counts them. It is also no longer executable, as the repo requires.

Unit tests cover the foreign shim, shim-only, no-npm, hard-link, directory and empty-entry cases. `e2e/backend/test_npm_shell_out_foreign_shim` fails with a fork storm without the fix and passes with it.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-289_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how npm is resolved for shell-out metadata lookups on Unix; wrong detection could block valid npm or still recurse, but scope is limited to npm.shell_out and includes regression tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes a **fork storm** when `npm.shell_out` is on and a **foreign mise shim** (e.g. another install’s shims on `PATH` while `HOME`/`MISE_DATA_DIR` differ) is the first `npm` on the child `PATH`. `mise latest npm:*` could re-enter mise and repeat `npm view` for every tool (#14068).
> 
> On Unix, **`npm view` now picks the executable explicitly** from the dependency `PATH`: skip known mise shim directories, treat symlink/hard-link copies of the running `mise` binary as shims, resolve empty/relative `PATH` entries to absolute paths, and ignore a directory named `npm`. If only a mise shim remains, mise **errors with a clear message** instead of spawning it; a real `npm` later on `PATH` is used; missing `npm` behavior is unchanged. Windows

title: feat(dotfiles): add track-local for history that never leaves the machine
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/509
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Some files are worth a history but should never leave the machine: application state, a work-only config, a credential you want to be able to roll back. Until now, every tracked file went into the one history that a setup repository shares, so the only choices were to share the file or not track it at all.

`mode = "track-local"` keeps a file's history on this machine only:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/app/state.json" = { mode = "track-local" }
```

Or run `mise dot track --local ~/.config/app/state.json`.

### What you can do with it

Local-only files are saved, browsed and restored like any tracked file:

```sh
mise dot save                                     # saves both histories
mise dot history --path ~/.config/app/state.json  # goes to the local history
mise dot rollback ~/.config/app/state.json
mise dot --local history                          # list local-only checkpoints
mise dot --local undo
```

- **Routing:** a command that names a path goes to the history that keeps it, and one command can't mix paths from both. `mise dot --local` selects the local history for commands without a path. `sync`, `pull`, `origin` and `conflicts` are refused there.
- **`mise dot watch`:** also watches local-only files, through a child watcher it stops when it exits.
- **`mise dot capture`:** saves a labeled local checkpoint before and after the command.
- **`mise dot status`:** says how many local-only entries there are.

### What never leaves the machine

The local history is a separate history store under `$MISE_STATE_DIR/history-local`, with no origin. The shared history never enrolls a local entry, so neither the file's contents nor its declaration reach the shared manifest, a commit, or a push.

A local path can sit inside a shared tracked directory. For example, `state.json` can be local inside a shared `~/.config/app`:
- **Saving and syncing:** the shared history leaves that file out, never applies incoming versions to it, and carries forward whatever it already held for that path, so it never publishes a deletion that would remove the file on another machine. Versions saved there before the path became local stay, as with `untrack`.
- **Rolling back the directory:** the local file stays untouched, including after the history index is rebuilt from Git.

`track-local` takes no `encrypt` or `variants`. Credential-named files still need `allow_plaintext = true`. A mise that predates this skips `track-local` as an unknown mode, so it fails closed instead of tracking the file as shared. For the same reason it is a mode, not a boolean key.

Malformed local declarations remain excluded from shared capture, including commit metadata. A shared save refuses affected paths while still allowing an unrelated selected shared file to be saved. Filenames with Git pattern characters are treated literally when carrying forward previously shared versions.

title: feat(dotfiles): add merge = "missing" to fill in defaults the app may change
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/508
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to [discussion #13986](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13986). Stacked on #14076, so the base is that branch until it lands.

## What changes

Apps like Codex and Claude Code write the model you pick with `/model` into the same config file a `merge` entry manages. A regular merge reverts that choice on the next apply, and leaving the key out of the source means a fresh machine gets no default. `merge = "missing"` sets only the keys the target has no value for:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.codex/config.toml/shared" = { merge = true }
"~/.codex/config.toml/defaults" = { source = "codex/defaults.toml", merge = "missing" }
```

- A key the target already has keeps its value, even a different one. A key the app removes is filled in again on the next apply.
- Tables are compared key by key, so a default inside a table is added without touching its siblings.
- `mise dot status` and `mise dot diff` report only missing keys, never a differing value.
- A `missing` entry never conflicts with another entry for the same key. The other entry's value wins whichever applies first, and the result is stable across applies.
- TOML and YAML are still edited in place, and JSON keeps key order and indent.

## Tests

Unit tests for the fill logic in all three formats and for the entry parsing, plus an e2e case with an enforced and a defaults entry on one file. The schema and `docs/dotfiles.md` are updated.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes dotfile merge apply/status/diff semantics and ordering on shared config files; mistakes could overwrite or mis-report state, but fill-only mode is additive and defers to enforced merges.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`merge = "missing"`** for dotfile edit entries so JSON/TOML/YAML targets get default keys only where the file has no value yet—app-chosen values (e.g. `/model`) are left alone, and keys the app deletes are re-filled on the next apply.
> 
> **`mise-util` structured merge** gains `missing` / `fill_missing` (recursive key-by-key for nested tables). Dotfile apply uses `fill_missing` instead of full merge when `missing_only` is set; enforced `merge = true` runs first, then missing fills, with deferred re-checks when an enforced merge changes the same file. **`mise dot status` / `diff`** evaluate missing merges against that projected post-merge text via `check_selected` and `projected_text`; drift is reported only for absent keys, not value mismatches. Missing merges skip merge-key conflict detection.
> 
> Docs (`dotfiles.md`), JSON schema, unit tests, and e2e coverage for mixed enforced + defaults entries, ordering, filtered apply, and competing defaults.
>

title: fix(daemons): run argv and Windows readiness probes in the tool environment
body:
mise runs a daemon's `ready_cmd` and `health_cmd` through `mise x`, so the probe sees the project's tools and `[env]`, not whatever environment the shared pitchfork supervisor happened to start with. Two kinds of probe skipped that:

- **An argument array.** pitchfork 2.30.0 accepts `ready_cmd` and `health_cmd` as an argument array, which it runs without a shell (jdx/pitchfork#1012, #1015). mise wrapped only a string, so an array ran outside `mise x`.
- **Any custom probe on Windows.** For a `run` or `task` daemon, mise wrapped probes on Unix only. Preset probes were already wrapped on Windows too (#13929).

```toml
[env]
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://127.0.0.1:5432/app"

[daemons.api]
run = "node server.js"
ready_cmd = ["node", "scripts/ready.js"]
```

Here the probe found neither the project's `node` nor `DATABASE_URL` when the supervisor had been started from another project. It failed until pitchfork's timeout, and `mise daemons start` reported the daemon as failed.

mise now wraps both kinds:

- An array stays an array: `["<mise>", "x", "--", "node", "scripts/ready.js"]`, still run without a shell.
- A string on Windows becomes `"<mise>" x -- cmd /c <command>`, the form presets use, with the command escaped for cmd.

`mise = false` still leaves probes unwrapped. The docs now describe this and the array form.

## Validation

- New unit test `argv_probes_stay_argv_inside_the_tool_environment` checks both `ready_cmd` and a structured `health_cmd`. The existing `task_probe_environment_respects_explicit_opt_out` now runs on Windows too.
- New `e2e-win/daemons_probe_env.Tests.ps1` starts the pitchfork 2.30.0 supervisor from a directory without the project's `[env]`, then starts a daemon whose readiness probe passes only when it sees a value from `[env]`. It covers an array probe and a string probe. With mise 2026.10.2 on Windows 11, both daemons failed when the 30-second ready timeout ran out (exit code 124), and the probe ran unwrapped. With this change, built by CI, both pass, and so do the existing `daemons_task` and `daemons_task_init` e2e tests.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Readiness and health checks now use the project’s tools and environment settings across platforms, unless a daemon opts out with `mise = false`.
  * Probe commands can be configured as argument arrays. Pitchfork 2.30.0 and later runs these without a shell.
* **Documentation**
  * Updated daemon guidance to explain probe environment behavior and argument-array command support.

title: feat(installs): move installs that cannot be reinstalled into the identity layout during migrate
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/507
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise installs migrate` no longer fails when some legacy installs can't be reinstalled. It moves them into the new layout as they are.

Migrate reinstalls each legacy version from its backend. Old versions hit withdrawn releases, releases signed by a different identity than mise accepted before (stricter signer checks landed in 2026.10.0), or no network. Those installs work fine on disk, but migrate printed an ERROR for each one and exited 1. On one machine, `mise installs migrate -y` migrated ~170 installs and then failed on every old `aube`:

```
mise ERROR could not migrate aube@2.2.4: Failed to install packslip:github.com/aubepkg/aube@2.2.4: github.com/aubepkg/aube has no release 2.2.4 carrying packslip.sigstore.json ...
```

Now, when the reinstall can't happen, the existing directory is renamed into its own `<label>-<hash>` directory, gets the same `.mise-install.toml` receipt an install writes, and the old `installs/<tool>/<version>` path becomes a link to it. Paths the tool recorded about itself (venv shebangs, `node_modules/.bin` links) keep resolving through that link.

```
relocated aube@2.2.4 to ~/.local/share/mise/installs/aube-4h2kfq7a
  aube@2.2.4 could not be reinstalled (github.com/aubepkg/aube has no release 2.2.4 ...); moved as it is
170 migrated, 12 relocated, 0 kept legacy, 0 failed
```

- Reinstall is still tried first. Relocation is the fallback.
- If the directory can't be moved either (another file system, say), it stays in the legacy layout untouched and is reported as `skipped ... (kept legacy layout)`. That is not an error.
- Exit is non-zero only for a real failure: the old directory could not be put back, the version link could not be made, or the runtime links could not be rebuilt after a restore.
- The move is journaled like a reinstall. An interrupted run puts the directory back on the next `mise installs migrate`.
- A relocated install's identity holds only what the old directory can say: backend, version, platform and request options. Lockfile-derived digests (artifact checksum, aube/uv graph) are not reconstructed.

I also fixed a separate bug. Directories made with a lockfile can be named `<version>~aube~<digest>` (or `~uv~`). Migrate reinstalled that whole string as the version, which is where `npm:openclaw@2026.9.3~aube~f375ab1a2e9919a1` ("did not install into the identity layout") came from. It now uses the real version, computed before the directory moves. The installer's extra unsuffixed version link is removed, so exactly one link remains. The `-aube-` suffix is read from the lockfile inside the directory before it moves aside.

Not changed: for a version pinned by the project's `mise.lock`, migrate still reinstalls with `use_locked_version=false`, so the migrated install can have a different identity than the lockfile-resolved request. In my repro `mise doctor` then said the tool was not installed u

title: fix(dotfiles): stop prompting for recoverable operations
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/506
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stacked on #14071.

## Problem

`mise dot pull` prints the plan and then asks `apply these incoming changes?`. `mise dot undo`, `rollback`, `connect`, `bootstrap --adopt` and `dot track` do the same. Each of these is journaled with a protective checkpoint, so you can undo it, and you had already named what to do on the command line. The prompt was a second confirmation of the thing you just typed.

## Change

These operations now print their plan and proceed, with or without a terminal. Uncovered ownership targets still need explicit approval.

For example, `mise dot pull` now applies the incoming changes right after printing the plan, and `mise dot undo` reverses them.

Removed prompts:
- `history: apply this plan?` (undo, rollback, history apply)
- `history: apply these incoming changes?` (pull)
- `Connect this setup repository?`
- `Set this machine up from the repository?` (unless `--replace-history`)

title: feat(dotfiles): infer merge sources and keep app state when switching from symlink
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/505
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Two follow-ups to merge entries from [discussion #13986](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13986).

## Omitted `source` is inferred

A merge entry can leave out `source`, like a `symlink` entry. It reads the target's path under `dotfiles.root`:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.codex/config.toml/shared" = { merge = true }
# source: <dotfiles.root>/.codex/config.toml
```

This also helps when `mise.toml` is itself symlinked into `conf.d/`, where a relative `source` resolves from the wrong directory.

## Switching from `symlink` to `merge` is safe

If the target is a symlink to the merge entry's own source, `mise dot apply` now replaces the link with a regular copy and then merges. The application's keys survive when the source is later trimmed to the owned keys. Previously apply stopped with "target is a symlink; edit the real file instead", and replacing the link by hand in the wrong order lost the app's state.

A symlink to anywhere else is still refused, and the message now says to copy the real file first.

## Tests

Added e2e cases for the inferred source, the symlink switch (including trimming the source afterwards), and the refused foreign symlink.

> **Merge dotfile edits** can omit `source`, mirroring symlink entries: mise reads from the target’s path under `dotfiles.root` (e.g. `{ merge = true }` on `~/.codex/config.toml/shared` uses `<dotfiles.root>/.codex/config.toml`). Targets outside `$HOME` (including `~/../…` tricks) still require an explicit `source`.
> 
> **Switching from symlink to merge** is automated when the target symlink points at the merge source: `mise dot apply` atomically replaces the link with a writable copy (including clearing read-only bits), then merges so application-owned keys survive if you later trim the source. Status shows a “symlink to the merge source” diff instead of a hard block; symlinks to any other path stay refused with guidance to copy the real file first.
>

title: feat(packslip): add a workflow option to pin the signing workflow
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/504
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `packslip:github.com/owner/repo` tool is accepted today when *any* workflow of that repository signed the release, including one running on a branch. Pinning a single release workflow on tags currently means spelling out the full certificate identity prefix and the GitHub OIDC issuer by hand.

This adds a `workflow` option that takes the workflow file name:

```toml
[tools]
"packslip:github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk" = { version = "latest", workflow = "release.yaml" }
```

That expands to the identity prefix `https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/` with GitHub's issuer (both derived from the project name), so a branch workflow can no longer sign a release.

- GitHub projects only; a monorepo tool path (`github.com/o/r/tool`) pins its repository's workflow.
- Rejected when combined with `pubkey`, `identity`, `identity_prefix`, or `issuer`, which remain the way to pin another ref or forge.
- The workflow must be a bare file name (no `/` or `@`).

This is a prerequisite for narrowing the `worktrunk` registry entry in #14073 to one option. Covered by a unit test; `cargo clippy` and the packslip unit tests pass locally. The e2e suite was not run.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes packslip trust policy for tools that set `workflow`, tightening which sigstore identities are accepted during install and version listing; misconfiguration could block installs until options are corrected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **`workflow`** packslip tool option so GitHub projects can require releases (and, by default, the signed release list) to be signed by a **named Actions workflow on tag refs**, instead of accepting any workflow in the repo—including branch runs.
> 
> Setting e.g. `workflow = "release.yaml"` builds an identity policy equivalent to pinning `https://github.com/{repo}/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/` with GitHub’s OIDC issuer; **`list_identity_prefix`** remains the escape hatch when the list is signed elsewhere. The option is **GitHub-only**, must be a bare filename (no `/` or `@`), and **cannot be combined** with `pubkey`, `identity`, `identity_prefix`, or `issuer`.
> 
> Docs and JSON schemas document the option; **`pin()`** routes `workflow` through new **`workflow_policy()`** as an identity pin (not forge-wide verification), and unit tests cover prefix expansion, monorepo paths, conflicts, and validation errors.

title: security(worktrunk): pin the registry default to the release workflow on tags
body:
Pin the Worktrunk registry default to `release.yaml` signatures from a tag, using the Packslip `workflow` option added in #14075.

Worktrunk restricts creation and updates of all tags to repository administrators, but the registry default only checked the repository, so a signature from a branch workflow was also accepted. The shorthand `mise use worktrunk` now rejects those:

```toml
{ full = "packslip:github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk", min_version = "0.80.0", options = { workflow = "release.yaml" } }
```

`workflow` expands to the identity prefix `https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/.github/workflows/release.yaml@refs/tags/` with the GitHub Actions OIDC issuer. Explicitly selected backends and user overrides keep their own policy.

Verified earlier with Packslip 1.5.1 against the untouched v0.80.0 bundle: the release workflow/tag policy passes signature and transparency-log validation, while a wrong workflow, a branch ref, and a wrong issuer are rejected.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex and Claude Code; model: OpenAI/GPT-6 and Anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable (Codex) and 2.1.289 (Claude Code).*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

@@ -1,5 +1,5 @@

-  { full = "packslip:github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk", min_version = "0.80.0" },
+  { full = "packslip:github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk", min_version = "0.80.0", options = { workflow = "release.yaml" } },
   "aqua:max-sixty/worktrunk",

title: fix(dotfiles): don't require --yes without a TTY for recoverable confirmations
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/502
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

`ssh host 'mise dot pull'` printed the plan and ended with `mise history: skipped`; nothing was applied unless `-y` was passed. `sync::origin::confirmed` (used by pull, connect, onboard) and `history::replay` (undo, rollback) treated "no terminal" as "no", so a missing TTY silently declined.

## Semantics

Without a terminal a confirmation must never skip silently or hang:

- **Recoverable** (journaled, protective checkpoint, undoable): proceed. New `prompt::confirm_recoverable`.
- **Irreversible**: fail with an error naming `--yes`. New `prompt::confirm_destructive` (same convention as prune, bootstrap unapply, tasks).
- A prompt that was shown but whose stdin hit EOF is an error, not a skip.

## Fixed

- `dot pull`, `dot undo`, `dot rollback`, `dot origin` connect, `bootstrap --adopt`: proceed without a TTY.
- `bootstrap --adopt --replace-history`: requires `--yes` (loud error).
- Replay "plan changed since shown" prompt: loud error naming `--yes`.
- `dot recover --keep-current` (discards recovery copies): requires `--yes`, loud error (previously silent skip).
- `mise implode`: previously silently did nothing without a TTY; now errors naming `--yes`.
- `upgrade --interactive` without a terminal: errors instead of hanging in the picker.
- Replay paths now also honour global `--yes`/`MISE_YES`.

## Audited, left alone

- Sites guarded by `user_attended_stderr()` (dot apply/unapply/track/add/edit, system install/prune/driver/services/compose/accounts/firewall/managed files, edits/files): already proceed without a TTY.
- trust, tasks `confirm`, prune, daemons prune, bootstrap unapply, self-update, install-into, remote adoption, plugin install (community plugins), non-executable task fix, track credential plaintext: already fail loudly naming `--yes` or an equivalent flag.
- `set --prompt`, `use`/`search` selectors, secret prompts: explicit interactive features, not confirmations.

## Tests

- e2e `test_non_tty_confirm_slow` (pull/rollback/undo proceed, implode errors); `test_dotfiles_onboard_review` updated.
- unit test for the new prompt helpers.

Note: `mise run lint-fix` fails locally on an unrelated pre-existing `openssl` unused-dependency warning; fmt and clippy are clean for changed code.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes default non-TTY behavior for sync, replay, and implode across history/dotfiles flows; mistakes could apply plans or block scripts, though recoverable paths remain journaled and destructive paths fail closed without `--yes`.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Non-interactive confirmation behavior** is split into recoverable vs destructive paths. **Recoverable** (journaled, undoable) operations such as dot pull/sync, rollback, undo, and initial history replay now **proceed without a TTY** via `confirm_recoverable`, instead of s

@@ -0,0 +1,52 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Without a terminal a confirmation must neither skip silently nor hang:
+# recoverable operations (journaled, with a protective checkpoint) proceed,
+# irreversible ones fail with an error that names --yes. e2e runs with stderr
+# and stdin detached from any tty.
+require_cmd git
+export MISE_HISTORY_NOTIFY=false
+export MISE_YES=0
+
+origin="$PWD/origin.git"
+git init -q --bare -b main "$origin"
+echo base >~/.native
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles track ~/.native --yes'
+assert_succeed "mise bootstrap dotfiles origin set file://$origin --sync manual --yes"
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles sync'
+
+second="$(dirname "$HOME")/nontty-b"
+mkdir -p "$second"
+b() {
+  (
+    cd "$second" || exit
+    env HOME="$second" XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$second/.config" MISE_CONFIG_DIR="$second/.config/mise" \
+      MISE_STATE_DIR="$second/.local/state/mise" MISE_DATA_DIR="$second/.local/share/mise" \
+      MISE_CACHE_DIR="$second/.cache/mise" MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS="$second" mise "$@"
+  )
+}
+export second
+export -f b
+assert_succeed "b bootstrap --adopt file://$origin --yes </dev/null"
+
+# pull applies without --yes (and without a terminal)
+echo incoming >~/.native
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles sync'
+assert_succeed 'b bootstrap dotfiles sync --fetch-only'
+assert_not_contains 'b bootstrap dotfiles pull </dev/null 2>&1' 'skipped'
+assert "cat $second/.native" incoming
+
+# rollback and undo (journaled, undoable) apply without --yes too
+mkdir -p ~/.config/hypr
+echo kitty >~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles track ~/.config/hypr --yes'
+echo alacritty >~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles save'
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles rollback ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua </dev/null'
+assert 'cat ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua' kitty
+assert_succeed 'mise bootstrap dotfiles undo </dev/null'
+assert 'cat ~/.config/hypr/bindings.lua' alacritty
+
+# irreversible: refuse loudly and name --yes, never skip silently
+mkdir -p "$HOME/implode-me"
+assert_fail 'mise implode </dev/null' '--yes'
+assert_succeed "test -d '$MISE_DATA_DIR' -o -d '$MISE_CONFIG_DIR'"

title: fix(cargo): do not resolve dependencies to mise shims
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/501
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem
`mise installs migrate tokei` (identity install layout) failed with `~/.local/share/mise/shims/cargo-binstall exited with non-zero status` and the install stayed legacy.

## Root cause
Not migrate-specific. `Backend::dependency_which` (used by the cargo backend to locate `cargo-binstall`) searched the process PATH first, shims directory included. When `cargo-binstall` is installed but active in no config, its shim is found there and returned, and the shim errors with "No version is set for shim: cargo-binstall". The dependency toolset, which could never contain it anyway, was never consulted. A fresh `mise install cargo:foo` fails the same way whenever the shims dir is on PATH; migrate just hit it.

## Fix
Skip mise shim/wrapper dirs in `dependency_which`. With no real `cargo-binstall` found, the cargo backend falls back to native binstall / `cargo install`.

## Test
`e2e/backend/test_cargo_binstall_shim_slow` puts a failing `cargo-binstall` shim on PATH and checks the install falls back to `cargo install`. Verified it fails without the fix and passes with it.

title: fix(doctor): recognize a `mise` entry in the dedicated shims dir
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/500
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise doctor` reported `Missing shims: mise` right after `mise reshim`, even though `shims/mise` existed as a symlink to the mise binary.

Root cause: `is_mise_shim` unconditionally treated the name `mise` as the dispatcher (meant for shared bin dirs where a package manager installs mise itself), so a `shims/mise` created for a tool that provides a `mise` binary was never counted as owned/current. Doctor (and every reshim diff) saw it as missing forever. The exemption now applies only outside mise's dedicated shims dir.

Test: extended the unit test in `src/shims.rs` covering dispatcher vs. dedicated-dir behavior.

title: fix(dotfiles): let MISE_YES confirm rollback, undo, and recover
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/499
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`MISE_YES=1` (the `yes` setting) answers the confirmation prompts of `mise dot sync`, `pull`, `origin set`, and `track`, but `mise dot rollback`, `mise dot undo`, and `mise dot recover --keep-current` asked anyway. Without a terminal, they then skipped:

```console
$ MISE_YES=1 mise dot rollback ~/.zshrc </dev/null
~/.zshrc  write  ...
mise history: skipped
```

They now take `MISE_YES` as the answer, like the rest of `mise dot`, so a script or a wrapper (Omarchy's `omarchy dots restore`, for one) can restore files without `--yes`. `--yes` still works, and the credential-store prompt in `mise dot track` still defaults to no.

A new e2e test, `test_dotfiles_rollback_mise_yes`, checks that rollback still skips with `MISE_YES=0` and no terminal, and that rollback and undo proceed with `MISE_YES=1`. The e2e harness exports `MISE_YES=1`. I checked that no existing test relied on these commands skipping, and the rollback, nested-repository, and review-safety e2e tests pass.

title: fix(dotfiles): say when incoming history changes no files on this machine
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/498
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When another machine changes only its own version of a tracked file (a `profile` or `os` variant this machine doesn't use, or a per-machine file), nothing on this machine needs to change. Sync still has to record that history before this machine can publish again, but the messages described it as a pending file change:

```console
$ mise dot sync
mise history: nothing new to publish
mise history: 1 incoming change(s) pending; `mise dot pull` applies them
$ mise dot pull
mise history: applied 0 incoming change(s)
```

Now:

```console
$ mise dot sync
mise history: nothing new to publish
mise history: incoming history changes no files here; `mise dot pull` records it before this machine publishes again
$ mise dot pull
mise history: recorded incoming history; no files here changed
```

When files are also waiting, the count covers just those files, plus any directories whose permissions the pull would change. `mise dot status` already listed this case as "repository enrollment or inactive files". The watcher's JSON `pending` count is unchanged.

A new e2e test, `test_dotfiles_sync_repository_only`, uses a `profile` variant on the second machine to produce a change that writes nothing on the first. It checks both messages and that the first machine publishes after pulling. The existing sync e2e tests pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> User-facing log and pending-reporting changes only; sync behavior is clarified rather than reworked, with new e2e coverage.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Dotfile sync messaging** now separates *repository-only* incoming history (another machine’s variant, enrollment, etc.) from changes that would actually modify files or directory permissions on this machine.
> 
> After `mise dot sync`, when the only pending work is recording remote history with no local writes, users see **incoming history changes no files here** instead of a misleading pending file-change count. After `mise dot pull` with zero writes, the log says **recorded incoming history; no files here changed** instead of **applied 0 incoming change(s)**.
> 
> The pending count shown when real work remains now **excludes** repository-metadata-only pending state but **includes** tracked directories whose incoming permissions differ (pull still updates modes even when no file content changes). `SyncStatus` / `SyncOutcome` gain `pending_directories` and surface `pending_repository` for reporting; overall `pending` semantics for watchers are unchanged per the PR description.

title: fix(dotfiles): save files replaced when adopting a setup, and add --take-remote-all
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/497
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Setting up a second machine from a shared dotfiles repository could lose that machine's own files, and the documented way to adopt over existing local history didn't work.

### Fixed: replaced files were not saved on a fresh machine

The setup guide's flow for a machine that already has, say, a `~/.bashrc` is:

```sh
mise bootstrap --adopt you/setup     # pauses on files that differ
mise dot pull --take-remote-all      # take the repository's versions
```

The guide promises that the replaced versions are saved first and that `mise dot undo` reverses the pull. On a machine with no history yet, neither was true: the pull overwrote the files without saving them, and `mise dot undo` reported "nothing to undo". A fresh pull skips its protective checkpoint so it doesn't create a history unrelated to the repository's. When such a pull is about to replace existing files, it now adopts the repository's history first, then saves those files on top of it before writing. `mise dot undo` restores them.

That checkpoint holds every path the pull writes, so `undo` also removes files the adoption created, including manual-save ones. A file history can't save, such as one larger than it captures, stops the adoption with nothing written, instead of being replaced without a copy.

### New: `mise bootstrap --adopt <url> --take-remote-all`

This makes the same choice during adoption, in one command:

```sh
mise bootstrap --adopt you/setup --take-remote-all
```

It also completes `--replace-history`, for a machine that already saved history of its own (for example, one that tracked the same files before they were shared). Previously, `--replace-history` refused whenever any existing file differed ("move the conflicting files aside and retry"), which on a new machine with default configs is almost always. Now:

```sh
mise bootstrap --adopt you/setup --replace-history --take-remote-all
```

discards this machine's history and adopts the repository's. Each file that differs is saved first, and `mise dot undo` restores this machine's versions. Without `--take-remote-all`, `--replace-history` still refuses and keeps the local history untouched. The error now names the flag, or, when the flag was given and something else holds a path (such as staged Git changes), says that instead.

### Fixed: `--replace-history` failed on its first attempt

Its preview fetched the repository shallowly, and the confirmed run seeded the real store from that preview. Git refuses to copy a branch out of a shallow repository but still exits successfully, so the run failed with "setup repository has no fetched branch". The preview now fetches the complete branch, and the seed checks that the branch actually arrived.

### Validation

- A new e2e test, `test_dotfiles_adopt_take_remote`, covers each path, plus `undo` removing a created manual-save file and a 17 MB local file stopping the adopt

+# a machine with its own home, configuration, and history store

title: security(npm): redact normalized SSH diagnostics
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/496
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When resolving an unpinned npm Git source written as a colon-form SSH URL, mise converts it to Git's scp-style remote form. Diagnostics now remove the SSH user and replace a query value with a digest in both the command trace and Git-derived errors, while Git still receives the unchanged operational remote.

For example, a source like `npm:git+ssh://git@host:owner/repo.git?token=…` no longer exposes its query value in diagnostics.

Validation: synthetic npm Git-source regression coverage, adjacent npm Git tests, formatting, and strict full-workspace Clippy in a disposable Docker container.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Diagnostic-only redaction for npm Git `git_head` paths; Git command arguments are unchanged. Low risk aside from possible over-redaction in rare error messages.
> 
> **Overview**
> **npm Git SSH diagnostics** no longer leak credentials when sources are normalized from `git+ssh://…` URLs into Git’s scp-style `host:path` form.
> 
> New helpers build a **display-only** remote (SSH user stripped, query values digested) while **`git ls-remote` still uses the full operational remote**. Command traces, `git_head` errors, and stderr from Git are rewritten through `display_git_remote` / `redact_git_stderr` so tokens in query strings and `git@` userinfo do not appear in output.
> 
> Regression tests cover scp-style remotes with query parameters and assert `git_ls_remote_args` is unchanged.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 4ceadb646e08eb0143dd337fb97d310a97a52db3. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved error diagnostics for Git operations using scp-style SSH remotes. Displayed errors now redact sensitive remote details, including credentials and query tokens, and replace the remote and path in command error output.
  * Git commands continue to use the original remote, so this change affects diagnostic output without changing command behavior.

title: fix(shim): skip version lookups for lazy tools that are not installed
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/495
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Shims, `mise x`, and `mise env` resolved the version of every lazy tool in the config, not just the command being run. For a lazy tool that isn't installed, `latest` meant a remote version lookup, so one shim call queried every missing lazy tool:

- **Offline with a cold version cache**, each lookup waited for its timeout. With Omarchy's 20 lazy defaults, running an already-installed `gh` took about 42 seconds, and the failed lookups weren't cached, so every call stalled again until the machine was back online.
- **Online with a cold cache**, the same `gh --version` sent 26 requests to `api.github.com`, because the offline-preferring commands skip mise's versions host.

A lazy tool that has no installed version now keeps its requested version (such as `latest`, a `prefix:` or `sub-N:` selector, or a rolling channel) in those commands. Running its shim, `mise install --include-lazy`, or `mise install <tool>` resolves and installs it as before. Installed lazy tools still resolve to their installed versions, and `mise ls` still shows resolved versions. Commands that manage versions, such as `mise lock`, resolve lazy tools as before even with `prefer_offline` set.

Measured with Omarchy's lazy tool config (omacom/omarchy#9596), an installed `gh`, and an empty cache:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `gh --version`, network unreachable | 42.06 s | 0.09 s |
| `gh --version`, online | 0.77 s, 30 HTTP requests | 0.09 s, 0 requests |

## Validation

- New e2e test `test_lazy_tools_deferred_resolution`: with missing lazy tools requesting `latest`, `prefix:0`, and `sub-1:latest` and a cold cache, running another tool's shim, `mise x`, or `mise env` never calls the GitHub credential command, and `mise install --include-lazy --dry-run` still resolves `gh` to a concrete version. It fails without this change.
- Existing lazy tool, shim, `exec`, `hook-env`, `which`, `where`, and `current` e2e tests pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes version resolution on hot paths (shims, exec, env) but only when prefer_offline, lazy, and nothing is installed; install/upgrade behavior is explicitly unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Shims**, **`mise x`**, and **`mise env`** no longer resolve every lazy tool in config when building the toolset. Under **`prefer_offline`**, uninstalled lazy entries keep their configured version string (e.g. `latest`, `prefix:0`) instead of listing remote versions, so one shim call does not time out or hit GitHub for tools nobody invoked.
> 
> A new **`ResolveOptions.defer_missing_lazy_tools`** flag and **`ToolsetBuilder::with_deferred_lazy_resolution()`** turn this on for those run paths. **`mise install`**, **`upgrade`**, and **`use`** leave the flag off

title: feat(dotfiles): give each machine its own tracked version with a machine variant
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/494
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Some tracked files describe the machine rather than the person: a monitor layout, a trackpad setting, a hardware quirk. Until now, tracking one meant either sharing it, so sync applied the laptop's monitor layout on the desktop, or leaving it out of history entirely.

A `machine` variant gives every machine its own version of the file:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua" = { mode = "track", variants = [{ machine = true }] }
```

or `mise dot track ~/.config/hypr/monitors.lua --machine`.

Each machine saves, rolls back, and restores its own version. Sync shares the other tracked files as usual but never applies one machine's version on another. Each machine's version is still pushed to the origin with the rest of the history, so it is kept off the machine and can be restored on it later.

### Machine names

The stream is named `machine-<name>`, for example `machine-omarchy-3f2a9c1b`: the hostname plus a random suffix, generated the first time and kept in `$MISE_STATE_DIR/history/machine`. A hostname alone is not enough, because installers often leave every machine with the same default hostname (Omarchy's is `omarchy`), and renaming a host should not move its history. To choose the name, or to continue a machine's history after reinstalling it, set it in that machine's global configuration:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.local.toml
[history]
machine = "desk"
```

If the machine name can't be read or kept, history stops with an error for per-machine entries rather than falling back to a name another machine might share. Rolling back a per-machine file on a machine that joined later never deletes it: another machine's checkpoint holds no version from this one, and that counts as "not saved here", not as a deletion. A deletion this machine saved itself is still restored as a deletion.

### Limits

- A `machine` variant must be the entry's only variant (no `os`, `profile`, or `default` beside it).
- It cannot be combined with `encrypt = true`. The plaintext-history audit lists every encrypted stream from the shared manifest, and other machines' stream names are not known there.
- Track mode only; destination variants reject it.
- Upgrade every machine sharing a setup before using it. Older versions refuse the setup rather than read the entry as shared and apply one machine's version on the others.

### Validation

- A new e2e test (`test_dotfiles_machine_variant`) runs two machines with the same hostname through sync in both directions. Each keeps its own `monitors` file while a shared file syncs, both streams end up in the origin, and `[history] machine` renames a stream.
- The same e2e test checks that rollback on the second machine, whose only version is its latest checkpoint, deletes nothing, and that a deletion it saved is restored even after rebuilding its index from Git.
- Unit tests cover selection, validation, stream owner

title: feat(bootstrap): add an os filter to files and directories
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/491
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Fixes discussion #14056 (feature request).

Before: `[bootstrap.packages]` could be limited to an OS with `os = ...`, but `[bootstrap.files]` and `[bootstrap.directories]` applied everywhere, so writing `/etc/docker/daemon.json` on Linux and a colima file on macOS meant splitting config with `MISE_ENV`.

After: files and directories accept the same `os` selector as packages (one value or a list, including `unix` and `linux/x64` style pairs):

```toml
[bootstrap.files."/etc/docker/daemon.json"]
os = "linux"
source = "./files/docker-daemon.json"

[bootstrap.files."~/.colima/default/colima.yaml"]
os = "macos"
source = "./files/colima.yaml"
```

An entry that doesn't match the host is skipped as if undeclared by apply, status, and dry-run; mise never touches its target.

How: `os` is parsed with the package deserializer and entries are filtered with `os_selector_matches` while each config layer is merged, so a non-matching entry can't conflict with or shadow others. Schema, docs, and an e2e test are included.

## Summary

Git-based npm tool sources can include URL userinfo or query tokens. Some mise-originated diagnostics formatted the source directly, so values were conditionally exposed unless already registered for redaction.

This follow-up to #14044 uses the existing identity-safe URL renderer only at diagnostic boundaries: Git default-branch lookup failures, checksum rejection, lock validation, warnings, lifecycle/aube errors. Install requirements, Git remotes, and dependency identity retain the original URL values.

## Tests

- Added synthetic percent-encoded userinfo and query-token checks without registered redactions for checksum and lock errors.
- Added safe HTTPS and SSH display coverage, plus an assertion that the raw Git install requirement is preserved.

- cargo test --lib credentials --ignore-rust-version -- --nocapture

title: fix(daemons): quote deferred daemon commands for cmd.exe on Windows
body:
A daemon's `run` can use mise's `[vars]`, `[env]` and template filters. Since pitchfork 2.30.0, pitchfork leaves those for `mise x` to render when the daemon starts (jdx/pitchfork#966; mise side #13894). The `quote` filter always produced POSIX quoting, so on Windows, where pitchfork runs the command with `cmd /C`, a quoted value did not reach the program intact:

```toml
[vars]
title = "my title"

[daemons.api]
run = "node server.js --title {{ vars.title | quote }}"
```

cmd does not treat `'` as a quote, so `'my title'` reached `node` as the two arguments `'my` and `title'`. A value with `&`, such as `50% & more`, was worse: cmd ran the part after `&` as a separate command.

When `mise x` renders a command pitchfork deferred and the program is cmd, `quote` now quotes the value for cmd. `my title` becomes `"my title"`, so the value can also be the program cmd starts, such as `C:\Program Files\node\node.exe`. Each `%` stays outside the quotes, escaped with `^`, so cmd does not expand `%VAR%`: `50% & more` becomes `"50"^%" & more"`. A backslash right before such a quote is doubled, so `C:\data\%cache folder` still reaches the program as one path. A value that itself contains `"` is escaped with `^` throughout, so the quote cannot end cmd's quoting and expose what follows. Other shells, and every other use of `quote`, keep POSIX quoting.

The docs now say this needs pitchfork 2.30.0 or later, not "a release newer than 2.29.0". They also note that on Windows such a command is read by cmd, which has no `exec`.

The cmd escaping already used for daemon presets (#13929) moves to `mise_util::path::escape_arg_for_cmd_line`, so presets, task daemons and `mise x` share it.

## Validation

- New `e2e-win/daemons_deferred_template.Tests.ps1` starts a daemon with pitchfork 2.30.0 whose `run` passes `{{ vars.title | quote }}` and `{{ vars.symbols | quote }}` (`my title`, `50% & more`) to a script that records its arguments. With mise 2026.10.2 on Windows 11 the script received `'my`, `title'` and `'50%`, and the rest ran as a separate command. With this change, built by CI, it receives exactly `my title` and `50% & more`. The same build also passes `e2e-win/daemons_presets.Tests.ps1` on a machine without administrative rights, including postgres, since presets use the same escaping.
- New unit test `test_quote_for_cmd` checks the cmd form of `quote` on both Tera engines: a value with a space, a program path, a value with `'`, ones with `%`, and one with an inner `"` and `&`.
- On Windows 11, 18 values were passed through `cmd /S /C` as pitchfork does, among them `50% & more`, `%APPDATA%`, `C:\data\%cache folder`, `a" & echo INJECTED & "b`, `!bang!`, a trailing backslash and an empty string. All arrived unchanged, and a program path quoted this way started; with every quote escaped by `^`, cmd could not find the program.

title: fix(task): list monorepo subproject tasks in the mise://tasks MCP resource
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/488
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `mise://tasks` resource served by `mise mcp` only listed tasks from the current directory's config, so AI agents working in a monorepo could not see subproject tasks such as `//app:build`.

The resource now loads tasks with `TaskLoadContext::all()`, the same context `mise tasks ls --all` uses, so every subproject task is included. `docs/mcp.md` notes this.

Fixes #14052

I have not added an e2e test or run this against a real monorepo.

title: fix(install): keep incomplete-install markers out of the cache
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/487
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When an install doesn't finish, mise marks that version incomplete so nothing selects it until a later install repairs it. That covers an install that fails partway and, since jdx/mise#14037, a failed tool-level `postinstall` hook. The marker was stored in the cache directory, so `mise cache clear` or cache pruning deleted it. After that, the half-installed version counted as installed: `mise ls --installed` listed it and fuzzy requests resolved to it.

Here is how to reproduce it with `halfdone = { version = "1", postinstall = "exit 1" }` configured and 1.0.0 already installed:

```console
$ mise install halfdone@1.2.0          # postinstall fails; 1.2.0 stays incomplete
$ mise ls --installed halfdone
halfdone  1.0.0
$ mise cache clear
$ mise ls --installed halfdone         # before this PR
halfdone  1.0.0
halfdone  1.2.0  ~/workdir/mise.toml  1
$ mise x -- halfdone                   # before: runs the half-done 1.2.0
```

With this PR, `1.2.0` stays hidden after `mise cache clear`, and `halfdone = "1"` keeps resolving to 1.0.0.

## Changes

- The marker moves to `$MISE_STATE_DIR/incomplete-installs/<tool>/<version>/incomplete`, outside anything `mise cache clear` or `mise cache prune` removes.
- **Existing markers are migrated.** On startup, a one-time migration in `migrate.rs` moves any marker an older mise left in the cache to the state dir, then writes `incomplete-installs/.migrated` so later runs skip the scan. It runs before auto-prune and before the command, so `mise cache clear` cannot delete those markers first. A version whose lock is held by an install in progress keeps its old marker, and the migration retries on a later run.
- **The old location is honored until migration finishes.** Until the `.migrated` file exists, a marker at `$MISE_CACHE_DIR/<tool>/<version>/incomplete` still counts. This covers the first run after upgrading, which scans installed versions before the migration runs.
- **The legacy code has an expiry date.** The migration and the fallback are guarded by `remove_by!("2027.1.0", "legacy-incomplete-markers")`. `remove_by!` is a new compile-time assertion that fails the build once mise's version reaches 2027.1.0, so the code can't ship past that date unnoticed. Unlike `deprecated_at!`, it doesn't depend on any code path running. AGENTS.md now documents it next to the deprecation policy.
- **The lock identity stays the same.** The tool-version lock, including #14037's postinstall-token check, is still keyed by the old cache path, so an older and a newer mise running at the same time still serialize on one version.
- `mise uninstall` and `mise plugins uninstall --purge` now remove the marker explicitly, because it no longer sits in `cache/<tool>/<version>`.

## Validation

- `e2e/cli/test_install_incomplete_survives_cache_clear` covers three cases: a failed install kept with `MISE_ALWAYS_KEEP_INSTALL`, a failed `p

title: docs(http): show a package proxy recipe for url_replacements
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/486
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Routing mise through an internal package proxy does not need regex rules. A plain `url_replacements` key is a prefix match that keeps the rest of the URL, so these two rules are enough for a proxy that mirrors GitHub under a path prefix:

```toml
[settings.url_replacements]
"https://github.com/" = "http://pkgproxy.internal:8080/generic/github/"
"https://api.github.com/" = "http://pkgproxy.internal:8080/generic/github-api/"
```

This is the same mapping as the regex rules in the discussion below, without capture groups. This PR adds that recipe to the URL Replacements docs, along with a note that rerouting `api.github.com` stops mise from using mise-versions for GitHub metadata. No behavior changes.

Context: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14048

Docs only; I did not build the docs site.

> The new text walks through the resulting URL mapping, notes that the two keys do not overlap, and warns that rerouting the API is only appropriate when the proxy serves it—otherwise mise stops using **mise-versions** for release/attestation metadata—and points readers to regex only when the proxy path layout is not a simple prefix.

title: fix(http): retry downloads when an HTTP/2 stream reset fails the body read
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/485
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #14045

A download whose HTTP/2 stream is reset mid-body (`error decoding response body: ... stream error received`) failed on the first attempt regardless of `http_retries`. reqwest reports that as a `Decode` error wrapping an `h2::Error`, which `is_transient` did not recognize.

`is_transient` now treats `Decode` errors as transient unless a `serde_json::Error` is in the source chain, so JSON deserialization failures stay non-retryable. A unit test covers the deserialization case; a reset-stream positive test would need a TLS+h2 test server, which the harness lacks.

title: fix(release): skip the vfox-tiny test fixture when vendoring embedded plugins
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/484
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The release PR (#13964) fails e2e because the release step vendors a `vfox-tiny` plugin into `crates/vfox/embedded-plugins/`. `tiny` is a fake plugin the e2e suite relies on as a non-embedded fixture. Once it is embedded, `mise use tiny@1` writes `backend = "vfox:jdx/vfox-tiny"` to `mise.lock` instead of `vfox:tiny`, and `mise where tiny` returns `installs/vfox-tiny-…` instead of `installs/tiny-…`. That breaks `cli/test_use_latest` and `cli/test_install_layout_migrate`.

`xtasks/release-plz` now skips `vfox-tiny` when re-cloning embedded plugins, so release PRs keep passing without changing those tests.

I did not confirm why embedding changes the resolved name; the cause is inferred from the release diff and the failing assertions.

title: feat(npm): install packages from git repositories
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/483
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

The npm backend can now install a package straight from a git repository, the way the pipx backend already can. Previously this failed with `invalid package name` because mise looked the URL up in the npm registry.

```sh
mise use 'npm:git+https://github.com/presmihaylov/claude-security'
mise use 'npm:github:owner/repo@v1.2.0'
```

The version is the git ref (tag, branch or commit); `latest` is the repository's default branch. `git+`, `git://`, `github:`, `gitlab:` and `bitbucket:` specs are recognized. Registry lookups are skipped for them, and the embedded aube root dependency is written under an alias taken from the repo name.

Not in this PR: pinning `latest` to a commit SHA in `mise.lock`.

Fixes discussion #14043.

## Testing

- New e2e `backend/test_npm_git` installs from a local `git+file://` repo at `latest` and at a tag.
- Installed the repo from the discussion with the embedded aube.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> New install and version-resolution paths depend on git remotes and URL parsing; mistakes could affect installs or rolling `latest`, but registry packages are unchanged.
> 
> **Overview**
> The **npm backend** can install CLI tools from **git sources** (`git+https://…`, `github:`, `gitlab:`, `bitbucket:`) instead of only the registry, using the ref as the version and treating **`latest`** as the remote default branch.
> 
> Git specs bypass registry version listing; for rolling **`latest`** on an unpinned URL, mise resolves HEAD via **`git ls-remote`**. Installs use npm-style URL/`#ref` specifiers, alias the dependency to the **repo name** in embedded aube `package.json`, and reject **checksum** for git sources. Lockfile validation and related paths use **`package_key`** / **`package_requirement`** instead of the raw tool name.
> 
> Docs describe git install usage; e2e **`test_npm_git`** covers `git+file://` at `latest` and a tag. Unit tests cover URL parsing and requirement building.
>

title: fix(cargo): serialize rustup state across cargo install fallbacks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/482
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Parallel \`cargo:\` installs that fall back to a plain \`cargo install\` could corrupt the shared rustup toolchain (\`could not rename 'component' file ... Directory not empty\`, \`detected conflict: 'bin/rust-gdb'\`), because each \`cargo\` child can invoke rustup on its own. The lock added in #11794 only covered the core rust plugin.

The cargo backend now takes the same rust state lock (keyed on the resolved \`RUSTUP_HOME\`/\`CARGO_HOME\`) before running \`cargo install\`. Source builds with the same homes now run one at a time; binstall paths are unaffected.

Fixes #14041

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches install-time locking for shared rustup state; wrong home resolution could over- or under-serialize, but scope is limited to cargo install fallback paths.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Extends rustup state locking to the cargo backend** so parallel `cargo:` installs that fall back to `cargo install` no longer race the core rust plugin on shared `RUSTUP_HOME` / `CARGO_HOME` (fixing rustup “component rename” / bin conflicts).
> 
> Before spawning `cargo install`, the cargo backend now holds the same filesystem locks the rust plugin uses. A new `lock_rust_state_for_config` helper resolves those homes from the effective child environment (process env, toolset env, and per-install env overrides). The rust module is re-exported as `pub(crate)` so the cargo backend can call it.
> 
> **cargo-binstall** paths that return early are unchanged; only source / `cargo install` fallbacks are serialized per resolved rust home pair.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit ee119aecbfd1bba01397fd6c982cb3b86b871d34. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(bootstrap): add a tool-update service that keeps auto_update tools current
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/481
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Tools with [`auto_update`](https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html#automatic-tool-updates) (jdx/mise#14026) normally update when a shim or `mise x` launches them, so that launch waits for the download. Tools run straight from PATH under shell activation never update at all. This adds a built-in user service that updates them in the background instead. Declare it in your global config the same way as the dotfile history watcher:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[tools]
claude = { version = "latest", auto_update = true }

[bootstrap.services.mise-tool-update]
builtin = "tool-update"
```

```sh
mise bootstrap services apply   # or a full `mise bootstrap`
```

- **What's installed:** a systemd user unit (Linux), LaunchAgent (macOS), or scheduled task (Windows) that runs `mise __tool-update --watch`.
  - It runs at low priority and restarts on failure.
  - It has the same crash-loop cap as `history-watch`: at most 3 starts per 5 minutes, or `ThrottleInterval=300` on macOS.
  - It's removed with `mise bootstrap services remove mise-tool-update`.
- **What it does:** once an hour it checks every tool with `auto_update` in global config and updates the ones whose interval (`auto_update = true` → `tool_update.check_duration`, or a per-tool duration) is due. Each update is the same `mise __tool-update <tool>` the launch path runs: global config only, from `$HOME`, so a project's config and lockfile are never touched. Its output goes to the service log (journal, or the LaunchAgent's log).
- **While it runs, launches don't update.** The service holds a lock for its active environments (`MISE_ENV`) for as long as it runs. Shims and `mise x` with the same environments skip their own update; with other environments, or with the service stopped or not installed, launches update in the foreground as before.
- **Each hourly pass** runs as a child (`mise __tool-update --due`) started the same way as a launch's update. It resolves each opted-in tool on its own, so one failed version lookup doesn't stop the others. It runs in its own process group (a job object on Windows): after 30 minutes, or when the service is stopped, the pass and everything it started are killed. If a pass can't be started at all, the service exits so it doesn't hold the lock.
- Failures show in `mise doctor`, like foreground failures.

### Tests

- New e2e `test_tool_update_service`: runs the watch loop and checks that it installs the update. While it runs, a launch with a due check runs the installed version without updating; after the service stops, the launch updates again. The middle assertion fails if launches ignore the service lock (checked by disabling that check).
- New unit test: `builtin = "tool-update"` expands to `<mise> __tool-update --watch` with the restart cap on systemd and launchd.
- Clippy (also for `x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`), the 1.95 MSRV check, and `test_tool_updat

title: feat(config): move mise's auto-update settings under self_update.*
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/480
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's own auto-update settings move under the existing `self_update.*` section:

| Before (deprecated) | After |
|---|---|
| `auto_update` / `MISE_AUTO_UPDATE` | `self_update.auto` / `MISE_SELF_UPDATE_AUTO` |
| `auto_update_check_duration` / `MISE_AUTO_UPDATE_CHECK_DURATION` | `self_update.check_duration` / `MISE_SELF_UPDATE_CHECK_DURATION` |

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/config.toml
[settings]
self_update.auto = true
self_update.check_duration = "7d"
```

The top-level `auto_update` name was easy to confuse with the per-tool `auto_update` option for background tool updates (jdx/mise#14026), and the other self-update settings (`api_url`, `repository`, `minimum_release_age`) already live under `self_update`.

**Migration:** nothing breaks. The old keys and env vars keep working. When both spellings are set in the same place, the new key wins, and the priority between sources (env over global config, and so on) is unchanged. The deprecation warning starts in 2027.4.0, and the old keys are removed in 2028.4.0. The warning is delayed because older mise rejects an unknown key inside `[settings.self_update]` and then ignores that settings file. So a config that has to work with both old and new mise should keep the old spelling for now.

One visible difference: `mise settings get auto_update` reports "not set" when only the config sets it, because the value is moved to the new key. The renamed `install_before` setting behaves the same way.

**Tests:** new e2e `test_settings_self_update_aliases` covers old and new keys in config and env, which one wins, and writing them with `mise settings`. New unit tests cover the alias mapping. Clippy, the 1.95 MSRV check, and the self-update e2e tests pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes global self-update behavior and settings precedence/migration paths; mistakes could affect when mise replaces its own binary, though aliases aim to preserve existing configs.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Moves mise’s automatic self-update configuration under `self_update.*`** so it sits with the other self-update settings and avoids clashing with per-tool `auto_update`.
> 
> - **`auto_update` → `self_update.auto`** (`MISE_SELF_UPDATE_AUTO`) and **`auto_update_check_duration` → `self_update.check_duration`** (`MISE_SELF_UPDATE_CHECK_DURATION`).
> - **Backward-compatible migration:** deprecated keys and env vars still apply when the new ones are unset; within the same layer the new keys win; env precedence is unchanged via a dedicated alias layer in settings loading. Deprecation warnings target **2027.4.0**, removal **2028.4.0**.
> - **Runtime and UX:** `maybe_auto_update`, version hints, and `mise settings` writes use the new names; docs and JSON schema

title: fix(install): keep a version incomplete until its postinstall hook succeeds
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/479
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A tool-level `postinstall` hook that fails no longer leaves its version looking installed.

```toml
[tools]
dummy = { version = "1.0.0", postinstall = "exit 1" }
```

Before: `mise install` failed, but `mise ls --installed` listed `dummy 1.0.0`. Later commands selected the half-installed version, and nothing repaired it short of `mise uninstall`. After: the version stays incomplete until the hook succeeds, so it isn't selected, and the next `mise install` (or `mise x`) installs it again.

A hook that runs mise against the version it is installing (`postinstall = "mise x -- dummy"`) still sees that version as installed and doesn't wait on its own install lock. This uses the same exact-install check packslip already used for its skills hook, now shared by every backend. The check now needs a token the install gives only to the hook it's running (`MISE_TOOL_INSTALL_TOKEN`), and the install must still hold its lock. A process left over from a failed or killed hook, or from an earlier attempt, can't use the half-installed version.

Verification failures are unchanged. For example, packslip still keeps a working binary when only its skills fail to download.

This is a prerequisite for jdx/mise#14026, where background tool updates install without anyone watching the output.

**Tests:** new e2e `test_install_postinstall_failure`, which fails on `main` at the `mise ls --installed` assertion. Backend unit tests (packslip included) and clippy pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core install completion, locking, and “installed” detection across all backends; behavior is security-sensitive around half-done installs but is covered by new e2e and token tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> Failed tool-level **postinstall** hooks no longer leave a version selectable or listed as installed. The **incomplete marker** stays until the hook finishes successfully (cleared only after `finish_install_changes` / postinstall, then verification). A failed hook still triggers **unpublish** of a half-done layout so the next `mise install` can repair it.
> 
> Hooks that invoke mise for the version being installed (e.g. `mise x -- tool`) are allowed to treat that install as complete while the marker is still present. A shared **`is_active_postinstall_install`** check (HTTP, default backend, packslip) now requires matching install-path env vars plus a fresh **`MISE_TOOL_INSTALL_TOKEN`** tied to the running hook; **`PostinstallToken`** writes/removes the token file, and acquiring the version lock drops stale tokens from killed or retried installs.
> 
> Adds e2e **`test_install_postinstall_failure`** and a unit test for token matching semantics.
>

title: fix(github): warn when attestations are skipped because the Sigstore trust root is unreachable
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/478
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When mise verifies a GitHub release's attestations, it passes as soon as any one of them verifies. If the others were skipped because the Sigstore trust root couldn't be fetched, nothing said so, and the debug line added in #14035 labelled the cause "attestation signature verification failed".

Reported in [#14033](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/14033): in a sandbox that blocks `tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev`, installing `github:DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp@0.11.0` printed

```
INFO  github:DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp@0.11.0 [3/4] ✓ GitHub artifact attestations verified
```

The two GitHub-internal attestations verified against the embedded root. The two public-good Sigstore ones (SLSA provenance and SBOM) need the TUF fetch, failed, and were never mentioned.

## What changes

- A failure to load the Sigstore or GitHub TUF trust root is now its own error (`AttestationError::TrustRoot`) instead of being folded into a signature failure, including when GitHub's root is loaded as a retry after the embedded root rejects a bundle. Debug output for those attestations reads "could not load the TUF trust root needed to verify the signature".
- When verification passes while some attestations were left unchecked for that reason, mise logs one warning:

  ```
  WARN  2 GitHub attestation(s) were not checked because a TUF trust root could not be loaded; verification passed on the remaining attestations. This usually means the Sigstore or GitHub TUF repository (tuf-repo-cdn.sigstore.dev and tuf-repo.github.com by default) is unreachable, or a configured mirror served invalid metadata; run with -v for details
  ```

- The direct GitHub API path now logs each failed attestation at debug level too, and warns about trust-root failures. It still stops at the first attestation that verifies, so it only reports failures from bundles tried before that one. Previously it dropped them silently.

Whether an install succeeds is unchanged: one verified attestation still passes. Only attestations that failed for a trust-root fetch reach `warn`. A tampered or mismatched bundle stays at debug, since a bad bundle next to a good one is not something the user can act on. The log text never includes the underlying error string, which can contain mirror URLs or credentials.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p mise-sigstore --lib` passes. New tests check that an unreachable TUF repository produces a `TrustRoot` error with the new summary, that the GitHub retry keeps that category (and keeps other failures as verification errors), and that the warning fires once and only when something was skipped. Invalid-metadata failures share the `TrustRoot` category but are not exercised by a test.
- `cargo clippy -p mise-sigstore -p mise-util --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- I did not reproduce the full install from the discussion, because no public-good Sigstore bundle fixtur

title: docs: keep code blocks and alert markers out of llms.txt summaries
body:
The `llms.txt` generator skipped fence delimiter lines but still read the code inside them as page prose. A guide opening with a fenced TOML example could therefore get `[tools] node = "24"` as its summary instead of the explanatory paragraph after the example. Skip complete backtick and tilde fences, respecting the closing fence's character and length, and stop a prose paragraph when a fence begins.

Also omit GitHub alert markers while retaining their warning text. Regenerating the index removes the literal `[!WARNING]` from the Remote Cache Protocol summary; the other 405 page entries are unchanged.

Validation on Node 24: seven new regression tests and all three existing CLI-reference tests pass. The new cases failed against the previous parser. Regenerated all 406 page entries, checked TypeScript formatting with the repository-pinned Prettier, and checked the updated task with Taplo. The regression suite now runs before `render:llms` generates the index. The full documentation site build was not run.
