+| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `[daemon] enabled = true` in the project's fnox config, a daemon is running, and every key is cached | One socket round trip instead of a resolving fnox call. Debug output (`MISE_DEBUG=1`) shows `secrets: fnox daemon hit`.                                                                                             |
+| A key is not cached, or needs a lease                                                                | Runs `fnox env --json` on your terminal. fnox resolves, prompts if it must, and stores the values in the daemon, so the next run hits.                                                                              |

+| No daemon is running                                                                                 | Runs the fnox CLI. If your fnox config enables the daemon, fnox may start it; mise never runs `fnox daemon start`.                                                                                                  |
+| The daemon speaks another protocol, or its socket is not owned by you                                | Runs the fnox CLI.                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

+| CI, no TTY, or stdin is not a terminal                                                               | Runs `fnox env --json --non-interactive --no-daemon`. CI never resolves through the daemon. Only the `mise secrets ls` table asks a running daemon for its protocol, and only when fnox reports the daemon enabled. |
+

+daemon protocol 6; with an older fnox mise keeps using the CLI.

--- e2e/secrets/test_mise_secrets_fnox_daemon_slow (+78/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,78 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# With fnox's daemon enabled, the first interactive `mise run` resolves on the terminal through
+# the fnox CLI (which stores into the daemon) and the second reads the daemon's cache with no
+# fnox resolve at all. mise never starts the daemon itself.
+FNOX_VERSION=1.39.0 # the first fnox with `fnox env --json` and daemon protocol 6
+
+if ! script -qec true /dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+  echo "Skipping: util-linux script is not available"
+  exit 0
+fi
+if ! mise ls-remote fnox | grep -qx "$FNOX_VERSION"; then
+  echo "Skipping: fnox $FNOX_VERSION (the first fnox with daemon protocol 6) is not listed by mise ls-remote"
+  exit 0
+fi
+
+# Installed without declaring it in the project: the project's own tools win over PATH, which
+# would bypass the logging wrapper.
+mise install "fnox@$FNOX_VERSION"
+FNOX_REAL="$(mise which fnox --tool "fnox@$FNOX_VERSION")"

title: feat(task): allow {{ secrets.X }} in task env values
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/439
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

[experimental] A task can now compose an environment value from a secret without a wrapper script:

```toml
[secrets.fnox]

[tasks.migrate]
env.PGURL = "postgres://app:{{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}@db.internal/app"   # the reference is the grant
run = 'psql "$PGURL" -f schema.sql'
```

**Before:** `{{ secrets.DB_PASSWORD }}` in a task env value failed with Tera's "Variable `secrets.DB_PASSWORD` not found".

**After:** `PGURL` is composed just before the task starts and is redacted in its output. `DB_PASSWORD` itself is not exported (unless the task also lists it, which is an error because both would claim the name). The reference is the grant, so `mise secrets ls` shows `migrate (env.PGURL)` and `mise tasks info --json` shows the template, never a value.

## Where `{{ secrets.X }}` is allowed

Only in a task's own `env` values (`env.K = "..."` or `env.K = { value = "..." }`, a file task's `#MISE env=` header, or the env of a `[tasks.<name>]` overlay). Everywhere else is rejected when config loads:

- `run` and `run_windows`: error pointing to `$NAME`, because `run` becomes `sh -c` argv, which other local users can read through `ps` and `/proc`. `{% raw %}...{% endraw %}` still prints a literal `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}`.
- `[env]` and `[vars]`: error, since they are computed at config load and reach your shell, `mise env` and the env cache.
- Any other field (`depends`, their `env`, run-entry env, `[task_templates]`, `task_defaults`, hooks, `[tools]`): error.
- A value that uses a reference may hold only literal text and `{{ secrets.NAME }}`. Filters, other variables, `{{-` and `secrets["X"]` are an error; there is no Tera involved, so no `exec()` and no value in any Tera error.

A composed value follows normal env precedence (last writer wins): it overrides a parent task's env (through a run entry), a template's or a lower config block's value, and defaults; a dependency's or run entry's env replaces a value from the task's own definition, but a value from a `[tasks.<name>]` block layered over the task still wins, as plain values do; a higher block's value or `env.PGURL = false` replaces it, and then no secret is fetched. `[env]`, tools and settings that set the same name still fail with "PGURL is both a secret and a mise env var", and so does listing the key in `secrets` while an env value takes its name. Env that reaches a task through a dependency or a run entry is never recorded as a grant. Composed values never reach the task env map, the Tera context, the env cache or subtask inheritance, and they are redacted.

Also refused: composing a secret that fnox delivers as a file (`as_file = true`), `$VAR` syntax in the literal text of a composed value when `env_shell_expand` is on (a value built at spawn is not shell-expanded), and a `$` right before a referenc

title: test(e2e): stabilize task timing assertions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/438
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The no-timings e2e test treated merged stdout/stderr output from parallel tasks as a contiguous line. The streams can interleave after `2>&1`, making the assertion flaky.\n\nCapture one run, assert both task prefixes are present, and verify it emits the expected two task timings plus one run timing.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> E2e test-only change with no production or runtime behavior impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stabilizes the **no-timings** e2e coverage for parallel `mise run` by stopping reliance on full `"[a] Finished in"` / `"[b] Finished in"` substrings in separate shell runs.
> 
> The test now **captures a single** `mise run a ::: b 2>&1` output, checks that both `[a]` and `[b]` prefixes appear, and asserts there are **exactly three** `"Finished in"` lines (two per-task timings plus one run total). Comments clarify that merged stdout/stderr from concurrent tasks may interleave after `2>&1`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 85753bc3c46ee1c0ec2aadddaee06bd2dcc71a4d. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Updated the parallel-task timing test to verify both task prefixes and exactly three completion-time messages in a single run.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
author: jdx
diff:
--- e2e/tasks/test_task_no_timings (+8/-3)
@@ -12,9 +12,14 @@ run = 'echo b-out'
 run = 'mise run a ::: b'
 EOF
 
-# parallel tasks default to prefix output, which times each task and the run
-assert_contains "mise run a ::: b 2>&1" "[a] Finished in"
-assert_contains "mise run a ::: b 2>&1" "[b] Finished in"
+# Parallel tasks default to prefix output, which emits two task timings and a
+# run timing. Capture one run: its stdout and stderr are concurrent streams,
+# so their individual writes may legally interleave after `2>&1` joins them.
+timed_output="$(mise run a ::: b 2>&1)"
+assert_contains_text "$timed_output" "[a]"
+assert_contains_text "$timed_output" "[b]"
+timing_count="$(grep -oF "Finished in" <<<"$timed_output" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
+[[ $timing_count == 3 ]] || fail "expected two task timings and one run timing, got $timing_count: $timed_output"
 
 assert_not_contains "mise run --no-timings a ::: b 2>&1" "Finished in"

title: feat(secrets): add --secrets and --secrets-all to mise run and mise x
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/437
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Experimental. Stacked on #13974 (tasks get the secrets they list). This adds one-off grants from the command line, with the same least-privilege rule: only the process you name receives a value.

## Before / After

**Before.** `mise x` cannot get a secret without `fnox exec`, and giving one task a secret once means editing `mise.toml`.

**After.**

```sh
mise run --secrets STRIPE_KEY deploy        # deploy gets it; its dependencies do not
mise run --secrets-all deploy ::: smoke     # every injectable key, to those two tasks only
mise x --secrets GH_TOKEN -- gh release list
mise x -- gh release list                   # nothing; fnox never runs
mise run deploy --secrets X                 # NOT a grant: after the task name, flags go to the task (mise warns)
```

## Only the tasks named on the command line

`--secrets KEY[,KEY]` goes to the tasks you name (explicit names, globs, `default`, `--all`), never to their dependencies, post-dependencies or tasks started by a `run` entry. `mise run --secrets A build ::: deploy` names both. A task's own `secrets` list still applies, and a command-line grant is not held to the "project config only" rule for where the task is defined (you are the one granting). It is still refused when a hook, daemon or `mise bootstrap` started the run. `mise tasks run` takes the same flags.

## `--secrets-all`

Every key fnox can inject (`env = true` or `"exec"`, never `env = false`). For tasks it asks fnox once without `--keys`, so keys from dynamic (`command`) leases come back too, and file secrets are delivered as files. The document is filtered against fnox's own description: a key it marks not injectable, or one it never described (unless a dynamic lease ran), is dropped. A key that mise sets itself for the task, or that the task's sandbox would drop, is skipped with a warning instead of failing the run.

## `mise x`

- Nothing by default; fnox never runs. There is no environment variable or setting that turns the flags on, and shims, `mise en` and pitchfork probes never pass them.
- File secrets (`as_file = true`) are not given, because `exec` replaces mise and nothing can delete the file: `--secrets GCP_SA_JSON` fails, and `--secrets-all` names every other injectable key explicitly and skips the files with a warning.
- Output is not redacted (same as `fnox exec`).
- If `exec` fails, mise removes the values from its own environment before building the error hint, since it keeps running.
- `mise x --secrets` is refused in safe mode.

Also: `mise secrets ls` SCOPES now reads `run, exec` / `run` / `-`, `--secrets <TAB>` completes key names, and the docs have a "Grant for one command" section.

## Validation

Unit tests pass (the 7 known local failures, 6 brew cask and `has_linked_version_ignores_mise_managed_absolute_targets`, are unchange

title: feat(task): give tasks only the fnox secrets they list
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/436
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Tasks can now list the fnox secrets they need and receive exactly those, only while they run. Stacked on #13967 (project `[secrets.fnox]` config and `mise secrets ls`), which sits on #13966.

## Before

Users wrap the run in `fnox exec -- mise run deploy`, which has four problems:

- every task in the graph gets every fnox secret (build, lint, dependencies, hooks and every shim);
- `{{ env.DEPLOY_KEY }}` in `run` puts the value into `sh -c` argv;
- fnox adds the values after mise's sandbox filter;
- a `secrets` field on a task is a hard error, because `Task` rejects unknown fields.

## After

```toml
min_version = "2026.10.4"   # older mise rejects `secrets` on a task

[secrets.fnox]
profile = "prod"

[tasks.build]
run = "cargo build"                         # receives nothing; fnox never runs for it

[tasks.deploy]
depends = ["build"]
secrets = ["DEPLOY_KEY", "DATABASE_URL"]    # only these keys, only this task
run = './deploy.sh'                          # reads $DEPLOY_KEY
```

`mise run deploy` validates every grant up front with one `fnox env --json --describe` call, runs `build` with nothing, makes one fnox call for the two keys, starts `deploy` with them, and prints `[redacted]` wherever a value appears in output. No fnox call happens for a task without a grant, a task skipped because its sources are fresh, a declined confirmation, `-n`, `mise env`, hook-env or a shim.

`secrets` also works in file task headers (`#MISE secrets=["DEPLOY_KEY"]`). `mise secrets ls` gains SCOPES and TASKS columns (and `scopes`, `tasks`, `problems` in JSON), and `mise tasks info/ls`, MCP and `mise tasks validate` show or check the grants.

## Who gets what

| Process | Receives the secret |
| --- | --- |
| A task that lists the key | Yes |
| Its dependencies, post-dependencies and `run = [{ task }]` subtasks | No, only their own lists |
| A nested `mise run` | Only tasks that list it |
| Shims, `mise x`, tools the task calls | Yes, they inherit the variable |
| Hooks, `mise env`, hook-env, daemons | No |

Values go only into the child's environment map, after every template is rendered and after `__MISE_DIFF` is computed. They never enter `__MISE_DIFF`/`__MISE_SESSION`, the env cache, Tera contexts, hook-env, shims or `mise env`; mise keeps them in memory for the process and registers them with the output redactor.

## Behavior to know

- **Redaction wins over raw.** A task that receives secrets ignores `--raw` and the `raw` setting and does not get stdin; `raw = true` or `interactive = true` on the task hands it the terminal (output is then not redacted). mise says so once.
- **Interactive sign-in.** In a terminal, fnox may prompt; mise takes the terminal as an `interactive = true` task does and waits for running siblings. In CI or without a TTY it runs fnox with `--non-inte

title: fix(dotfiles): explain missing sources in conflicting declaration errors
body:
When a whole-resource `[dotfiles]` entry has a source that does not exist, mise reserves its entire target, so any entry declared under that target fails with `conflicting dotfile declarations`. The config itself shows no conflict, which makes the error hard to diagnose. A common trigger is a relative `source` that resolves somewhere unexpected, for example a global `config.toml` deployed as a symlink into `~/.config/mise/`, where `../claude` resolves against the symlink's directory rather than the real file's.

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.claude" = { source = "../claude", mode = "copy" }               # ../claude does not exist
"~/.claude/skills" = { source = "../skills", mode = "symlink-each" }
```

Before:

```
mise ERROR conflicting dotfile declarations for /home/me/.claude

  first:
    config: /home/me/.config/mise/config.toml
    source: /home/me/.config/mise/../claude

  second:
    config: /home/me/.config/mise/config.toml
    source: /home/me/.config/mise/../skills
```

After, the declaration whose missing source caused the reservation is annotated:

```
conflicting dotfile declarations for /home/me/.claude

  first:
    config: /home/me/.config/mise/config.toml
    source: /home/me/.config/mise/../claude
    note: the source does not exist, so the whole target is reserved and nothing can be declared under it

  second:
    config: /home/me/.config/mise/config.toml
    source: /home/me/.config/mise/../skills
```

The note appears only when a declaration reserves its target as a single leaf because its source is unavailable. Missing `symlink-each` sources and grouped copy trees keep their directory shape and are not annotated. The conflict rules themselves are unchanged.

Tested with the existing `composed_file_footprints_*` unit tests (extended to assert the note is present for a missing source and absent for a real nested-leaf conflict) and by reproducing the configuration above with the built binary.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.283.*

* **Bug Fixes**

title: fix(dotnet): disable lockfile url enforcement for dotnet tool backend
body:
## Problem

`mise install --locked` (and `mise install` with `MISE_LOCKED=1`) fails for any tool from the `dotnet:` backend with:

```
No lockfile URL found for dotnet:<tool> on platform <platform> (--locked mode) hint: Run `mise lock` to generate lockfile URLs, or disable locked mode
```

Running `mise lock` does not help: the `dotnet:` backend installs tools via `dotnet tool install` from NuGet, so it never has a downloadable artifact URL torecord in the lockfile. Locked mode therefore demands a URL the backend can never produce, making `dotnet:` tools uninstallable in `--locked` mode.

## Cause

In locked mode, `Backend::install_version()` requires a lockfile URL for every backend whose `supports_lockfile_url()` returns `true`. That method defaults to `true`, and backends that install through external installers (no lockable download URL) override it to return `false` — `go`, `gem`, `cargo`, `npm`, `pipx`, `ubi`, the core `rust`/`swift`/`dotnet` SDKs, etc.

`DotnetBackend` was missing that override, so it inherited the default `true` and hit the URL requirement it can never satisfy. This is the same gap that was fixed for the Go backend in #8790.

## Fix

Override `supports_lockfile_url()` to return `false` on `DotnetBackend`, matching the other installer-driven backends:

```rust
fn supports_lockfile_url(&self) -> bool {
    false
}
```

## Result

**Before:** `mise install --locked` fails for every `dotnet:` tool.

**After:** `dotnet:` tools install normally in locked mode; the version is still pinned via the lockfile, and the backend is skipped for URL-lock enforcement just like `go`, `gem`, and the core dotnet SDK.

*AI-assisted — Tool: GitHub Copilot; model: copilot/claude-opus-4.8; version: vscode 1.140.0*

* **Bug Fixes**
  * The .NET backend now clearly identifies lockfile URLs as unsupported, preventing locked installs from reporting a missing lockfile URL. Locked execution continues to use the version pinned in the lockfile.

title: feat(secrets): add [secrets.fnox] project config and mise secrets ls
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/432
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

**Merge gate satisfied:** this needed an fnox release with `fnox env --json` (jdx/fnox#936). fnox 1.39.0 is released (and on crates.io) and is the first release that has it (1.38.0 and 1.38.1 do not have `env`), so `FNOX_ENV_MIN_VERSION` (`src/secrets/fnox/mod.rs`) is `1.39.0`.

## Before
`[secrets.fnox]` printed `WARN unknown field in mise.toml: secrets` and was ignored. mise could not show which keys a project's fnox config has.

## After
A project names fnox as its secrets source in its own `mise.toml`:

```toml
[tools]
fnox = "latest"

[secrets.fnox]          # this project's secrets come from fnox, discovered from this directory
profile = "dev"         # optional; passed as fnox -P
```

```
$ mise secrets ls
fnox · profile dev · ~/src/app (mise.toml) · fnox 1.39.0        <- stderr
KEY                ENV    FILE  DESCRIPTION                     <- stdout
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID  -      no    (lease aws)
DATABASE_URL       true   no    app database
DEPLOY_KEY         exec   no
GCP_SA_JSON        exec   yes
SIGNING_KEY        false  no    release signing key
```

Values are never shown. `-J/--json` prints the same data as JSON. mise runs `fnox [-P <profile>] --non-interactive --no-daemon env --json --describe` once, in the directory of the nearest file declaring `[secrets.fnox]`, with the environment of an activated shell there (no mise bookkeeping variables, no shims).

## Scope
- Experimental (`mise settings experimental=true`).
- Project config only: global config, system config and files in or above `$HOME` are ignored (reported by `mise secrets ls` and `mise doctor`). The nearest project file wins per field, so `mise.local.toml` can override `profile`.
- Trust-gated, and refused in safe mode.
- Requires fnox 1.39.0 or newer (the first release with `fnox env --json`). Older fnox gives a clear "cannot run `fnox env --json`" error.
- Nothing receives secrets yet; this adds the config, the `SecretSource` boundary in `src/secrets/`, `mise secrets ls`, a `mise doctor` check (including a deprecation warning for the `mise-env-fnox` plugin), the schema entry, and docs.

## Note
A user task named `secrets` was previously reachable as `mise secrets`; it now needs `mise run secrets`.

## Validation
Build, clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo +1.95 check`, new unit tests, and `e2e/secrets/test_mise_secrets_ls` plus `e2e/config/test_trust_safe_config` pass; generated docs/usage/man/schema regenerated. The e2e tests use a stand-in `fnox` (`e2e/helpers/scripts/fnox_stub.py`).

@@ -0,0 +1,107 @@
+---
+description: "Use fnox as a project's secrets source and list its keys with mise secrets ls."
+---
+
+# mise secrets with fnox
+
+<Badge type="warning" text="experimental" />
+
+[fnox](https://fnox.jdx.dev) can be the secrets source for a project. mise reads the list of
+keys fnox knows about and shows it with `mise secrets ls`. Values are never shown, and nothing
+receives secrets yet.
+
+mise secrets is experimental. Enable it with:
+
+```sh
+mise settings experimental=true
+```
+
+## Quick start
+
+Add fnox to the project and name it as the secrets source:
+
+```toml [mise.toml]
+[tools]
+fnox = "latest"
+
+[secrets.fnox]          # this project's secrets come from fnox, discovered from this directory
+profile = "dev"         # optional; passed as fnox -P
+```
+
+```sh
+mise use fnox
+mise secrets ls
+```
+
+```
+fnox · profile dev · ~/src/app (mise.toml) · fnox 1.39.0
+KEY                ENV    FILE  DESCRIPTION
+AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID  -      no    (lease aws)
+DATABASE_URL       true   no    app database
+DEPLOY_KEY         exec   no
+GCP_SA_JSON        exec   yes
+SIGNING_KEY        false  no    release signing key
+```
+
+The header goes to stderr and the table to stdout. mise needs fnox 1.39.0 or newer.
+
+## Where the source is declared
+
+`[secrets.fnox]` is read from project `mise.toml` files only.
+
+- The nearest file wins per field. `mise.local.toml` and `mise.<env>.toml` can override
+  `profile`. fnox runs in the directory of the nearest file that declares `[secrets.fnox]`, and
+  finds its `fnox.toml` from there.
+- Global config, system config, and files in or above your home directory are ignored, because
+  they apply to every project. `mise secrets ls` and `mise doctor` name any ignored file.
+- The file must be [trusted](/cli/trust.html), as with the rest of project config.
+- Safe mode (`MISE_SAFE=1`) refuses to use secrets sources.
+
+## `mise secrets ls`
+
+| Column      | Meaning                                                              |
+| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| KEY         | The name of the secret or lease key                                  |
+| ENV         | fnox's `env` setting: `true`, `exec`, `false`, or `-` for lease keys |
+| FILE        | `yes` if fnox provides the value as a file                           |
+| DESCRIPTION | fnox's description, or `(lease <name>)`                              |
+
+`-J`/`--json` prints the same information as JSON:
+
+```json
+{
+  "source": {
+    "kind": "fnox",
+    "root": "/home/me/src/app",
+    "declared_in": ["/home/me/src/app/mise.toml"],
+    "profile": "dev",
+    "tool": {
+      "path": "/home/me/.local/share/mise/installs/fnox/1.39.0/fnox",
+      "version": "1.39.0"
+    }
+  },
+  "keys": [
+    {
+      "key": "DEPLOY_KEY",
+      "kind": "secret",
+      "env": "exec",
+      "as_file": false,
+      "lease": null,
+      "description": null
+    }
+  ],
+  "dynamic_leases": [],
+  "ignored": []
+}
+```
+
+`env` is `true`, `"exec"`, `false`, or `null` for lease keys. `profile` is the profile fnox used,
+including `FNOX_PROFILE` or `default` when `mise.toml` sets none.
+
+mise looks for the fnox CLI in the project's tools first, then on `PATH`.
+
+## Migrating from mise-env-fnox {#migrating}
+
+mise secrets does not pass values to tasks or commands yet, so keep `_.fnox-env` and the
+`mise-env-fnox` plugin in `mise.toml` until it does. `[secrets.fnox]` can sit beside them now to
+list keys with `mise secrets ls`. `mise doctor` flags the plugin as deprecated.

title: security(env): keep secrets inherited from a parent mise out of templates, caches and other tasks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/431
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

A mise started inside a process that holds secrets (experimental mise secrets) should not spread them. This makes a nested mise treat variables named in a names-only `__MISE_SECRET_KEYS` marker as secrets it must not copy anywhere. This is preparatory hardening: nothing sets the marker until the mise secrets task grants land (M3), so this changes nothing today. It pairs with overlap-safe redaction (M0b, #13962).

## Before

A mise started inside a process that holds secrets:

- lets templates read them: `{{ env.DEPLOY_KEY }}` or `{{ get_env(name="DEPLOY_KEY") }}` renders the value into a task's `sh -c` argv, or into `[env]` and so into `mise env` and hook-env output. `{{ exec(...) }}` commands see it too.
- can write it into its env cache.
- records it in plaintext in `__MISE_DIFF.old` when its config overrides the same key (#13950 hashes only `new`).
- logs it unredacted before `Config` loads (`ARGS: ...` is logged before the redactor knows about it).
- hands it to every task of a nested `mise run`, including tasks that never listed it.
- hands it to `pitchfork`, and so possibly to a long-lived per-user supervisor.

## After

With `__MISE_SECRET_KEYS=DEPLOY_KEY` and `DEPLOY_KEY=...` in its environment, a nested mise:

1. registers the value (and its lines and JSON-escaped form) for redaction before anything is logged;
2. hides `DEPLOY_KEY` from every template, from `get_env()` and from `exec()` children;
3. writes no env cache;
4. never stores `DEPLOY_KEY` in `__MISE_DIFF.old` (leaving a directory unsets it rather than restoring it);
5. removes `DEPLOY_KEY` and the marker from the environment of every task it runs, including tasks whose sandbox `allow_env`, `pass_through_env` or `cache.env` would otherwise read them back from the process environment;
6. removes them from `pitchfork` invocations;
7. never passes them to the secret sources it runs.

```console
$ export __MISE_SECRET_KEYS=FOO FOO=s3cr3t
$ mise run t     # run = 'echo "foo=${FOO-unset}"'
foo=unset
$ mise x -- sh -c 'printf %s "$FOO"'
s3cr3t
```

`mise x`, shims, and tools a granted script calls still inherit the value through the OS environment, so a deploy script's `aws` call keeps working. A forged marker can only add redaction, turn caches off, or hide those keys from templates and nested tasks; it never grants anything. Reserved names (`PATH`, `HOME`, `USER`, `SHELL`, `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, `LANG`, `__MISE_*`) and invalid names are ignored, so `__MISE_SECRET_KEYS=PATH` does nothing.

## Validation

Unit tests cover marker parsing, stripping, `__MISE_DIFF` exclusion, redaction patterns, the pitchfork command, and the env-cache gate. New e2e `e2e/secrets/test_mise_secrets_inherited_marker` passes alongside `test_env_cache`, `test_task_redactions` and `test_exec_pitchfork_template_context`. `cargo

title: fix(env): fully redact secrets when redaction values overlap
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/428
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

When two redacted values overlap, mise redacted only one of them and printed the rest of the other in clear. The Aho-Corasick redactor reported a single match per position (the one that ends first), so a shorter value hid part of a longer secret and the remainder leaked.

```toml
redactions = ["SHORT", "LONG"]
[env]
SHORT = "abc"
LONG = "xxabcSECRETPART"
[tasks.a]
run = 'echo "long:$LONG"'
```

**Before:** `mise run a` printed `long:xx[redacted]SECRETPART`.

**After:** it prints `long:[redacted]`.

Picking the longest match alone is not enough when values cross rather than nest. With `abcdefgh`, `cd` and `efghSECRET` registered, redacting `abcdefghSECRET` with longest-match printed `[redacted]SECRET`, because the second secret starts inside text already consumed. Now:

**After:** `[redacted]`.

The redactor finds every occurrence of every pattern, including overlapping ones, and merges overlapping matches into one `[redacted]`, in the naive fallback (used if the automaton fails to build) too. Matches that merely touch stay separate (`abcdef` with `abc`, `def` gives `[redacted][redacted]`). This matches what the `redactions` docs already promise, and it matters for any value registered alongside its own substrings (lines of a multi-line secret, JSON-escaped forms).

Tests: unit tests in `redactions.rs` run each case through both the automaton and the fallback (crossing values in every insertion order, nested and prefix pairs, self-overlap, adjacency, non-ASCII, value plus line fragments plus JSON-escaped form, `with_additional`), an e2e case in `test_task_redactions`; clippy clean.

title: fix(mcp): reject run_task task names that start with a dash
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/427
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

The MCP `run_task` tool passed the caller's `task` straight to `mise run`, so a task name beginning with `-` was parsed as a flag. MCP callers are AI agents; the tool should only ever run the task it names.

**Before:** `run_task` with `task: "--raw"` ran `mise run --raw` (the `default` task with raw I/O); `task: "--cd=/path"` ran `default` in another directory.

**After:** the call fails with an `INVALID_PARAMS` error:

```
invalid task name '--raw': task names cannot start with '-'
```

An empty name is rejected too (`invalid task name '': a task name is required`). Normal names such as `build`, `//sub:build`, `lint:fix` and `a-b` are unchanged, and `args` were already passed after `--`.

Tests: unit tests for rejected and accepted names; clippy clean.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.289.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Input validation on the MCP tool path only; valid task names behave as before and the change reduces mistaken or abusive flag injection from MCP clients.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Hardens the MCP `run_task` tool** so caller-supplied task names cannot be interpreted as `mise run` CLI flags.
> 
> `run_task` now runs `validate_task_name` before spawning `mise run`. Empty names and any name starting with `-` (e.g. `--raw`, `--cd=/tmp`) return `INVALID_PARAMS` with explicit messages instead of running unintended behavior such as the default task with raw I/O or a different working directory. Legitimate task names (`build`, `//sub:build`, `lint:fix`, etc.) are unchanged; task arguments still go after `--`.
> 
> Unit tests cover rejected flag-like/empty names and accepted normal names.

title: registry: add jactionlint (github:jdx/jactionlint) and deprecate actionlint
body:

## What
- Adds `jactionlint`, a fork of `actionlint` (`github:jdx/jactionlint`).
- Deprecates `actionlint` in the registry with a message pointing at `jactionlint`, same style as `localstack` -> `lstk`.

## Why
jactionlint is an actively maintained fork of [rhysd/actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) with upstream pull requests and fixes merged, plus new checks (parallel steps, `$/` self-repository `uses:`, opt-in rules, inline ignore comments, ...). The binary is `jactionlint`, so it is a separate registry entry rather than a new backend for `actionlint`. The existing `actionlint` entry keeps working and only gains the deprecation notice.

## Popularity
`jdx/jactionlint` currently has 6 stars, 0 forks. It is a new maintained fork of [rhysd/actionlint](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint), which is the project users of the `actionlint` registry entry are being pointed away from. The entry is added by the registry's maintainer, so this is recorded for reference rather than as the basis for acceptance.

## Verification
Released as [v1.8.2](https://github.com/jdx/jactionlint/releases/tag/v1.8.2) with prebuilt binaries for linux/darwin/windows/freebsd.

$ mise x github:jdx/jactionlint@1.8.2 -- jactionlint --version
1.8.2
installed by downloading from release page

title: fix(install): switch backends into a new installation, and resolve CLI-named versions without guessing
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/423
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Stacked on `mise installs migrate`. Closes the two behaviour gaps the identity install layout (jdx/mise#13678) left: backend switches, and versions named on the command line.

**`mise backends switch`.** Before: under the identity layout, the new backend's installation is a different installation from the old backend's, so after switching `hk` from aqua to packslip the version counted as "not installed" and the switch did not reinstall anything. After: the switch installs the new backend's installation of every switched version whose version path exists (the old install or its version link), points the version link at it, and leaves the old backend's installation for prune.

```sh
$ mise backends switch hk
$ mise where hk
~/.local/share/mise/installs/hk-r5n2w6cp      # packslip's installation; aqua's is still there until prune
```

**A version named on the command line.** Before: `mise where tool@1.0` ignored the install options a configuration sets for the tool, while `mise x tool@1.0` and the rest applied them. Outside a project, `where` alone fell back to an installation made with options, and with several it picked whichever the version link named. `which`, `bin-paths`, `x` and `install` treated the version as not installed, a regression from #8888 for `filter_bins`. After:
- In a project, every command, `where` included, applies the configuration's options to a version named on the command line.
- Outside one, a version named without options that has no installation of its own uses the one installation of that version made with other options, in every command, as before the layout. Such a stand-in never becomes the bare request's selection, and `mise install --force tool@1.0` makes the plain variant.
- With several variants, `mise where` lists them and asks for options (`tool[matching=server]@1.0`) instead of guessing.

```sh
$ mise where dummy@2.0.0
mise ERROR dummy@2.0.0 is installed with several sets of options:
  ~/.local/share/mise/installs/dummy-jzljafcj
  ~/.local/share/mise/installs/dummy-pj47cthv
Run this where the configuration that sets them applies, or name them, for example `dummy[option=value]@2.0.0`
```

Not changed, on purpose: the runtime aliases of shared and system installs directories. They are maintained by whoever runs mise for that directory, as before the layout. Nothing here writes into them.

Validation: new `e2e/cli/test_install_layout_switch` (hk aqua → packslip, the new installation and version link, the old one kept) and `e2e/cli/test_install_layout_cli_variants` (a lone variant found by `where`/`bin-paths`/`which`/`x`/`install`, several listed, options naming one, configuration options applied in a project, a forced plain install). The other layout tests and `cli/test_where` pass.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# A version named on the command line carries no install options, so under the
+# identity install layout it can mean an installation a configuration made with
+# options. `mise where` uses one such installation when it is the only one, and
+# lists them instead of guessing when there are several.
+export MISE_EXPERIMENTAL=1
+export MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=identity
+work="$PWD"
+
+mkdir env opt
+cat >env/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+dummy = { version = "2.0.0", install_env = { DUMMY_VARIANT = "musl" } }
+EOF2
+cat >opt/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+dummy = { version = "2.0.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+
+echo "=== the only installation of the version is found ==="
+assert "mise -C $work/env install"
+env_dir="$(mise -C "$work/env" where dummy)"
+assert "mise where dummy@2.0.0" "$env_dir"
+
+echo "=== several are listed, not guessed between ==="
+assert "mise -C $work/opt install"
+opt_dir="$(mise -C "$work/opt" where dummy)"
+assert_fail "mise where dummy@2.0.0" "installed with several sets of options"
+assert_fail "mise where dummy@2.0.0" "$(basename "$opt_dir")"
+assert_fail "mise where dummy@2.0.0" "$(basename "$env_dir")"
+
+echo "=== naming the options finds the variant ==="
+assert "mise where 'dummy[flavor=full]@2.0.0'" "$opt_dir"
+assert "mise -C $work/opt where dummy@2.0.0" "$opt_dir"
+
+echo "=== a lone variant stands for the bare version in every command ==="
+mkdir solo
+cat >solo/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+dummy = { version = "1.0.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/solo install"
+solo_dir="$(mise -C "$work/solo" where dummy)"
+assert "mise where dummy@1.0.0" "$solo_dir"
+assert "mise bin-paths dummy@1.0.0 | xargs realpath" "$(realpath "$solo_dir/bin")"
+assert "mise which dummy --tool dummy@1.0.0 | xargs realpath" "$(realpath "$solo_dir/bin/dummy")"
+assert_contains "mise x dummy@1.0.0 -- dummy" "This is Dummy 1.0.0!"
+assert_contains "mise install dummy@1.0.0 2>&1" "already installed"
+assert "test \"\$(mise installs ls dummy --json | jq '[.[] | select(.version == \"1.0.0\")] | length')\" -eq 1"
+# a forced install of the bare version makes its own installation, which it then uses
+assert "mise install --force dummy@1.0.0"
+assert "test \"\$(mise installs ls dummy --json | jq '[.[] | select(.version == \"1.0.0\")] | length')\" -eq 2"
+plain_dir="$(mise where dummy@1.0.0)"
+[[ $plain_dir != "$solo_dir" ]] || fail "the bare version still resolves to the variant"
+assert "mise -C $work/solo where dummy" "$solo_dir"
+
+echo "=== a lone variant that has to be installed again is not installed over for the bare version ==="
+mkdir solo2
+cat >solo2/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "3.1.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/solo2 install"
+solo2_dir="$(mise -C "$work/solo2" where tiny)"
+assert "mise where tiny@3.1.0" "$solo2_dir"
+# as if a refresh of the variant had been interrupted
+mkdir -p "$MISE_CACHE_DIR/tiny/$(basename "$solo2_dir")"
+touch "$MISE_CACHE_DIR/tiny/$(basename "$solo2_dir")/incomplete"
+assert "mise install tiny@3.1.0"
+bare_dir="$(mise where tiny@3.1.0)"
+[[ $bare_dir != "$solo2_dir" ]] || fail "the bare version was installed into the variant"
+# the variant is still the project's, once its own refresh is done
+rm "$MISE_CACHE_DIR/tiny/$(basename "$solo2_dir")/incomplete"
+assert "mise -C $work/solo2 where tiny" "$solo2_dir"
+assert "mise installs ls tiny --json | jq -r '.[] | select(.selected and .version == \"3.1.0\") | .dir' | sort | tr '\n' ' '" "$(printf '%s\n' "$bare_dir" "$solo2_dir" | sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
+
+echo "=== a postinstall hook that always runs never runs in a variant standing in ==="
+mkdir variant hooked
+cat >variant/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "3.0.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/variant install"
+variant_dir="$(mise -C "$work/variant" where tiny)"
+cat >hooked/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "3.0.0", postinstall = { run = "touch \"$MISE_TOOL_INSTALL_PATH/hooked\"", when = "always" } }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/hooked install tiny@3.0.0"
+assert "test ! -e '$variant_dir/hooked'"
+assert "test -e \"\$(mise -C '$work/hooked' where tiny@3.0.0)/hooked\""
+
+echo "=== another tool aliasing the same backend never stands in ==="
+mkdir aliased
+cat >aliased/mise.toml <<EOF2
+[tool_alias]
+tinier = "$(mise tool tiny --backend)"
+
+[tools]
+tinier = { version = "2.1.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/aliased install"
+tinier_dir="$(mise -C "$work/aliased" where tinier)"
+[[ $tinier_dir == "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/"tiny-* ]] || fail "$tinier_dir is not an identity installation"
+assert_fail "mise where tiny@2.1.0"
+
+echo "=== a version a configuration gives options never takes an installation with more ==="
+mkdir env2 more
+cat >env2/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "1.0.0", install_env = { TINY_BUILD = "1" } }
+EOF2
+cat >more/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "1.0.0", install_env = { TINY_BUILD = "1" }, flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/more install"
+assert_fail "mise -C $work/env2 where tiny@1.0.0"
+# while the version named alone does find it
+assert "mise where tiny@1.0.0" "$(mise -C "$work/more" where tiny)"
+# options written on the command line are the version's own too
+assert_fail "mise where 'tiny[flavor=full]@1.0.0'"
+
+echo "=== a lone variant in a shared root whose catalog is gone still stands in ==="
+mkdir sharedvar
+cat >sharedvar/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+tiny = { version = "1.0.1", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert "MISE_INSTALLS_DIR='$HOME/shared-variants' mise -C $work/sharedvar install"
+mv "$HOME/shared-variants/.mise" "$HOME/shared-variants/.mise.lost"
+assert_matches "MISE_SHARED_INSTALL_DIRS='$HOME/shared-variants' mise where tiny@1.0.1" "^$HOME/shared-variants/tiny-"
+# a second copy made with the same options is the same variant: its selection says which
+export MISE_SHARED_INSTALL_DIRS="$HOME/shared-variants"
+assert "mise -C $work/sharedvar install --force"
+own_copy="$(mise -C "$work/sharedvar" where tiny)"
+[[ $own_copy == "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/"tiny-* ]] || fail "$own_copy is not in the user's root"
+assert "mise where tiny@1.0.1" "$own_copy"
+# with the selected copy gone, the other copy is not taken in its place
+rm -rf "$own_copy"
+assert_fail "mise where tiny@1.0.1"
+unset MISE_SHARED_INSTALL_DIRS
+
+echo "=== a version named with options a configuration sets never stands in for another variant ==="
+mkdir minimal
+cat >minimal/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+dummy = { version = "1.1.0", flavor = "minimal" }
+EOF2
+assert "mise -C $work/minimal install"
+mkdir full
+cat >full/mise.toml <<'EOF2'
+[tools]
+dummy = { version = "1.1.0", flavor = "full" }
+EOF2
+assert_fail "mise -C $work/full where dummy@1.1.0"
+assert_fail "mise -C $work/full where dummy 1.1.0"

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# `mise backends switch` under the identity install layout: the new backend's
+# installation is a different one from the old backend's, so the switch installs
+# it (instead of finding the version "already installed"), and the version link
+# moves to it. hk moved from Aqua to Packslip at 1.58.1.

+export MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=identity

title: fix(dotenv): leave a value ending in escaped whitespace unquoted
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/422
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Before: `render_value` quoted any dotenv value whose last character is whitespace. The parser only trims trailing whitespace that a backslash does not escape, so a value such as `a\` followed by a vertical tab was quoted even though it parses back unchanged without quotes. The `values_are_quoted_exactly_when_raw_input_would_not_round_trip` proptest catches exactly this, and it fails whenever proptest generates such a value. That has been happening on every recent macOS unit run (minimal input `"a\\\u{b}"`), for example on #13951.

After: trailing whitespace makes a value need quotes only when it is not escaped, which is the parser's own rule (`trim_unquoted_trailing_whitespace`). A backslash before a space or tab is still rejected further down, because the parser decodes those.

Validation: a unit test covers the escaped vertical tab (unquoted, round-trips), an unescaped one (quoted), and a backslash before a space (quoted). The `render::` proptests pass with `PROPTEST_CASES=20000`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to dotenv value quoting logic with parser-aligned rules and new unit coverage; no auth, data, or runtime path impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **`render_value`** so trailing horizontal whitespace forces quoting only when the parser would trim it—i.e. when there is an **even** run of backslashes immediately before that whitespace. Values like `a\` + vertical tab stay **unquoted** because they already round-trip unquoted, which restores the **`values_are_quoted_exactly_when_raw_input_would_not_round_trip`** proptest (previously flaky on macOS).
> 
> Adds a unit test for escaped vs unescaped trailing whitespace and backslash-before-space cases; behavior for decoded `\ ` / `\t` escapes is unchanged (still quoted).
>

title: feat(installs): move legacy installations into the identity layout
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/421
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stacked on `mise installs ls`/`select` (and #13951). Adds the explicit operation the identity install layout (jdx/mise#13678) promised for legacy installations: mise never moves them on its own, and now there is a command that does.

Before: with `install_layout = "identity"`, installations made before the layout was turned on stayed in `installs/<tool>/<version>` forever. The only way to move one was to uninstall and reinstall it by hand, which breaks anything that recorded the old path in between.

After:

```sh
$ mise installs migrate --dry-run
would migrate node@20.11.1 from ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/20.11.1 to ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node-k7m3q2vd
$ mise installs migrate node
migrated node@20.11.1 to ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node-k7m3q2vd
$ readlink ~/.local/share/mise/installs/node/20.11.1
../node-k7m3q2vd
```

- Each legacy version is **reinstalled** from its backend into its own `<label>-<hash>` directory, not copied, so files that record their own path (shebangs, venvs) are written for the new location. Then the old directory is removed and the version link takes its place, so a path that pointed into it (a venv's interpreter, an IDE SDK entry) still resolves. Runtime aliases (`20 -> ./20.11.1`) keep working through the link.
- The old directory is moved aside while the replacement installs and put back if the install fails. Each migration first writes a journal to `installs/.mise/migrations/`, records there every installation directory its install is about to write into (once the install holds that directory's lock and has found it must write), and marks itself finished only after the replacement is installed (postinstall included), checked and linked. The old directory is deleted only after that. If a run is killed or fails, the next `mise installs migrate` puts the old directory back and withdraws exactly what the interrupted run was making, then migrates the version again; an installation it only reused is left alone.
- One version is migrated at a time, under a run-wide lock and the version's lock, so an install with the legacy layout cannot put a directory back where the old one has to return.
- `TOOL` or `TOOL@VERSION` arguments narrow it (`node@20` names the installed versions that start with 20, as for `mise uninstall`, and `node@latest` the newest installed one); with none, every legacy installation moves. `--dry-run` lists the plan and what an interrupted run left.
- Skipped, with a warning when named: versions whose recorded backend is not what their tool resolves to now (mise isn't using them; uninstall them if unneeded), and tools that keep the legacy layout (`http:`, `rust`, `dotnet`).
- Experimental, and needs the layout on, like the rest of `mise installs`.

Validation: `e2e/cli/test_install_layout_migrate` covers the

title: feat(installs): list installations and choose the one requests without a lockfile use
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/420
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Stacked on the Windows store PR (and #13951). Adds the explicit selection interface the identity install layout needs (jdx/mise#13678), and stops mise from guessing when several installations answer one request.

Before: with `install_layout = "identity"`, several installations of one version can exist (a forced refresh that could not replace a lockfile's copy, or copies different lockfiles pinned), but there was no way to see them side by side or to say which one requests without a lockfile should use. If the remembered selection was lost, mise silently fell back to the request's first allocation.

After:

```sh
$ mise installs ls jq
Installation  Tool  Version  Platform   Status
jq-hm3qa4vb   jq    1.7.1    linux-x64  selected
jq-ezjqmxa4   jq    1.7.1    linux-x64  pinned
$ mise installs select jq-ezjqmxa4
selected ~/.local/share/mise/installs/jq-ezjqmxa4 for jq@1.7.1 (linux-x64); every project that asks for it without a lockfile now uses it
```

- `mise installs ls [TOOL]... [--json]` lists every installation with its tool, version, platform, options and status: `selected` (requests without a lockfile use it), `pinned` (a lockfile adopted it), `shared` (in a read-only shared installs directory). `--json` adds the backend, mode, options and artifact checksum.
- `mise installs select <dir|path>` records the selection for that installation's request (tool, version, platform, options) for every project on the machine, and points the version link at it. Locked requests are unaffected. Passing a path selects an installation in a shared root; the selection is stored in the user's own catalog and nothing is written to the shared root.
- With no selection (it was lost, or only lockfiles ever installed the request), mise reuses and selects the one installation that answers the request; when several do it stops and lists them instead of guessing:

  ```text
  mise ERROR jq@1.7.1 matches several installations and none is selected:
    jq-hm3qa4vb
    jq-ezjqmxa4 (a lockfile pins it)
  Choose one with `mise installs select <dir>`, or install a fresh one with `mise install --force jq@1.7.1`
  ```
- A selected installation whose payload was pruned is restored in its own directory instead of falling back to another one, and a selected shared installation that disappeared is reported rather than silently replaced.

title: feat(install): add an opt-in identity-based install layout
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/418
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Implements #13678 behind a new opt-in setting, `install_layout = "identity"` (it also needs `experimental = true`, but experimental users do not get it unless they ask; a later release will fold it into `experimental`): installs are named by what they are, so shorthands share installs and incompatible variants of one version coexist.

Before: every non-core tool lives in `installs/<short>/<version>`, and the backend that made it is recorded once per tool. `age` and `aqua:FiloSottile/age` are two downloads, a registry move (or a version-split tool like `hk`) reads one backend's files with another's layout, two builds of one version overwrite each other, and on Windows `installs/maven/3` is a text file that an IDE's SDK picker cannot follow.

After, with `experimental = true` and `install_layout = "identity"` (or `MISE_INSTALL_LAYOUT=identity`):

```text
installs/
  age/                        tool directory, as before
    1.2.1 -> ../age-hlencrst  version link (a junction on Windows)
    latest -> ./1.2.1         runtime aliases keep their ./<version> form
  age-hlencrst/               the installation: <label>-<hash of its identity>
    .mise-install.toml        receipt, written last (a directory without one is incomplete)
  .mise/                      catalog: assigned names, unlocked selections
```

```sh
$ mise install age@1.2.1 && mise where age
~/.local/share/mise/installs/age-hlencrst
$ mise install aqua:FiloSottile/age@1.2.1   # same canonical backend: already installed
```

- **Identity.** A hash of the canonical backend, concrete version, platform, install-affecting options and any pinned artifact checksum or dependency graph (`install_env` is hashed, never recorded; URL credentials are stripped). Shorthand and explicit spellings share one directory; variants that differ in an install-affecting option (`restate-server` vs `restatectl`, `symlink_bins`, a different `matching`) get their own. Names collide-extend by two hash characters and are never renamed.
- **PATH.** Unlocked requests keep putting `installs/<tool>/<alias>/bin` on PATH (`mise which node` still shows `installs/node/20/bin/node`) when that link is the selected installation; locked requests use the installation directory. `mise where` prints the real directory.
- **Lockfiles and selections.** A lockfile checksum is part of the identity and adopts an unlocked install of the same artifact without reinstalling it; an adopted install is never replaced in place, a later forced refresh moves the shared unlocked selection to a new generation. Restoring a pruned install from a different artifact than the one recorded is an error.
- **Lifecycle.** `ls`, `uninstall`, `prune` and upgrade retention work per installation (`mise ls` marks variants with their directory, `uninstall` asks for `--all` when

title: security(env): stop copying secret values into shell state and the env cache
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/417
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN?thread=cmsg_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN7sQVGQ8CTByEhrjb3YpLaz)_

mise no longer leaves a second plaintext copy of your secrets in shell state, and no longer writes decrypted secrets to the env cache.

## What changes for users

- **`__MISE_DIFF` and `__MISE_SESSION` hold digests, not values.** Both variables are inherited by every child of an activated shell, every task, and every `mise x` child. They used to carry the full text of every env value mise set (including secrets). They now carry a `blake3:<hex>` digest per value; they only ever compared values, so behavior is unchanged. `old` values in `__MISE_DIFF` are untouched because restoring the previous environment needs them.
- **Secrets are never env-cached.** A config with an `age` value (even with `redact = false`, or one in `[vars]` that `[env]` renders), a sops-encrypted `_.file`, or any directive with `redact = true` (including an env plugin that returns `redact = true`) is not written to the env cache; mise just recomputes the environment.
- **A non-cacheable env module is honored.** The env cache save only looked at tools-phase results, so a non-tool module returning `cacheable = false` was still cached. It now keeps the combined env uncached.
- **`redact` on an env module works.** `_.my-plugin = { redact = false }` was silently ignored, so the plugin's preference always won, contradicting `docs/env-plugin-development.md`. The user's setting now wins and is no longer passed through to the plugin; a non-boolean `redact` is a config error.

```toml
[env]
API_TOKEN = { value = "...", redact = true }   # no longer in the env cache or any copy in __MISE_DIFF/__MISE_SESSION
_.my-plugin = { redact = false }               # now overrides the plugin's redact preference
```

## Compatibility

`__MISE_DIFF` and `__MISE_SESSION` now carry a schema version (a missing field means 1; mise writes 2). A shell that keeps running across an upgrade holds version 1 plaintext, which still matches and reverses cleanly, and is rewritten as version 2 on the next prompt. Version 2 compares digests only. A version 1 mise reading a version 2 blob sees the values as changed.

## Caveat

The digests are a plain blake3 of the value, not a keyed hash. The value is still in each child's environment, so this is not a secret store: the win is that no extra plaintext copy exists, removed or unset values do not linger in shell state, and the copy is not exposed to anything that scans `__MISE_*` variables. A low-entropy value could be brute-forced from its digest.

## Also fixed

- `mise x -- fish` used to put every env value in fish's argv (`-C "set -gx K V"`), readable through `ps`/`/proc`. That re-apply exists because fish's config files run before `-C` and ca

title: fix(env): resolve dotenv ${VAR} against the file's own values before ambient env
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/416
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN?thread=cmsg_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN9wxJ1v4tSGsdF2HqeQ8cWu)_

Before: `${VAR}` in a dotenv file resolved from the process environment first. With `mise activate` exporting `.env` into the shell, `.env.test` containing `VAR_A="test"` and `VAR_B="test_${VAR_A}"` produced `VAR_B=test_base`, and the result changed after editing `.env`. See discussion #13941.

After: a dotenv file's own earlier assignments win, then values loaded so far (`expand = true`) or the process environment. The example now gives `VAR_B=test_test` and `VAR_C=test_test_test` whether or not the variables are already exported.

The cause was dotenvy checking `env::var` before same-file values. This vendors `dotenv-ng-core` 1.0.0 (MIT, a dotenvy fork) as `crates/mise-dotenv`, trimmed of process-environment mutation and with no clippy exemptions. A new `mise_dotenv::parse` never reads the process environment. `dotenvy` is removed. Both `_.file` dotenv loading and `env_file` setting go through it.

Notes:
- Dotenv files still always expand same-file references, as documented; docs updated to say own values take precedence.
- To match the old parser, braced text that is not a substitution (such as `${VAR:=x}`) stays literal, and the `env_file` setting keeps the assignments read before a syntax error and warns with the file name. `_.file` still fails on a syntax error, as before.
- `${VAR:?message}` and the other `:-`/`:+` forms now work in dotenv files.
- Added `e2e/env/test_env_file_ambient`; `mise-dotenv` unit tests pass; clippy `--workspace --all-features --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

+    /// An IO error may be encountered when reading from a file or reader.
+    Io(io::Error, Option<PathBuf>),
+    /// The variable was not found in the environment. The `String` is the name of the variable.
+    NotPresent(String),
+    /// The variable was not valid unicode. The `String` is the name of the variable.
+    NotUnicode(OsString, String),
+    /// An environment variable name was not valid Unicode.
+    NotUnicodeName(OsString),
+    /// When a load function is called with no path or reader.
+    ///
+    /// This can occur when `EnvLoader::with_paths` or `EnvLoader::with_readers` receives an empty
+    /// iterator.
+    NoInput,
+}
+
+impl Error {
+    #[must_use]
+    pub fn not_found(&self) -> bool {
+        if let Self::Io(e, _) = self {
+            e.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound
+        } else {
+            false
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl error::Error for Error {
+    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn error::Error + 'static)> {
+        match self {
+            Self::Io(e, _) => Some(e),
+            Self::Parse(error, _) => Some(error),
+            Self::NotPresent(_)
+            | Self::NotUnicode(_, _)
+            | Self::NotUnicodeName(_)
+            | Self::NoInput => None,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl fmt::Display for Error {
+    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter) -> fmt::Result {
+        match self {
+            Self::Io(e, path) => {
+                if let Some(path) = path {
+                    write!(f, "error reading '{}': {e}", path.to_string_lossy())
+                } else {
+                    e.fmt(f)
+                }
+            }
+            Self::Parse(error, Some(path)) => {
+                write!(f, "error parsing '{}':\n{error}", path.to_string_lossy())
+            }
+            Self::Parse(error, None) => error.fmt(f),
+            Self::NotPresent(s) => write!(f, "{s} is not set"),
+            Self::NotUnicode(os_str, s) => {
+                write!(f, "{s} is not valid Unicode: {os_str:?}")
+            }
+            Self::NotUnicodeName(os_str) => {
+                write!(
+                    f,
+                    "environment variable name is not valid Unicode: {os_str:?}"
+                )
+            }
+            Self::NoInput => write!(f, "no input provided"),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+impl From<(io::Error, PathBuf)> for Error {
+    fn from((e, path): (io::Error, PathBuf)) -> Self {
+        Self::Io(e, Some(path))
+    }
+}
+
+impl From<io::Error> for Error {
+    fn from(error: io::Error) -> Self {
+        Self::Io(error, None)
+    }
+}
+
+impl From<(ParseBufError, Option<PathBuf>)> for Error {
+    fn from((e, path): (ParseBufError, Option<PathBuf>)) -> Self {
+        match e {
+            ParseBufError::Parse(error) => Self::Parse(Box::new(error), path),
+            ParseBufError::Io(e) => Self::Io(e, path),
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::Error;
+    use crate::{EnvLoader, EnvSequence, iter::ParseBufError};
+    use std::{
+        error::Error as StdError,
+        ffi::OsString,
+        io::{self, Cursor},
+        path::PathBuf,
+    };
+
+    fn parse_error() -> Box<crate::ParseError> {
+        let error = EnvLoader::with_reader(Cursor::new("BROKEN value"))
+            .sequence(EnvSequence::InputOnly)
+            .load()
+            .unwrap_err();
+        let Error::Parse(error, _) = error else {
+            panic!("expected a parse error");
+        };
+        error
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn reports_underlying_error_sources() {
+        let io_error = Error::from(io::Error::other("reader failed"));
+        assert_eq!(io_error.source().unwrap().to_string(), "reader failed");
+
+        let parse_error = Error::Parse(parse_error(), None);
+        assert!(parse_error.source().is_some());
+
+        assert!(Error::NotPresent("MISSING".to_owned()).source().is_none());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn displays_every_context_free_error_variant() {
+        assert_eq!(
+            Error::from(io::Error::other("reader failed")).to_string(),
+            "reader failed"
+        );
+        assert!(
+            Error::Parse(parse_error(), None)
+                .to_string()
+                .starts_with("dotenv syntax error at line 1, column 8")
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            Error::NotPresent("MISSING".to_owned()).to_string(),
+            "MISSING is not set"
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            Error::NotUnicode(OsString::from("raw-value"), "VALUE".to_owned()).to_string(),
+            "VALUE is not valid Unicode: \"raw-value\""
+        );
+        assert_eq!(
+            Error::NotUnicodeName(OsString::from("raw-name")).to_string(),
+            "environment variable name is not valid Unicode: \"raw-name\""
+        );
+        assert_eq!(Error::NoInput.to_string(), "no input provided");
+        assert!(!Error::NoInput.not_found());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn converts_reader_errors_with_optional_path_context() {
+        let error = Error::from((
+            ParseBufError::Io(io::Error::other("reader failed")),
+            Some(PathBuf::from("config/.env")),
+        ));
+        assert_eq!(
+            error.to_string(),
+            "error reading 'config/.env': reader failed"
+        );

title: feat(dotfiles): add dotfile groups
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/415
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff**_

Many dotfiles repositories are laid out like GNU Stow packages: one directory per application or machine role, each deployed into `~`. Until now, every tree needed its own `[dotfiles]` entry, and a machine could not choose which trees to apply. Dotfile groups add both (from discussion #13934).

```toml
[dotfile_groups.zsh]
root = "zsh"                     # ~/.dotfiles/zsh, walked into ~

[dotfile_groups.home]
root = "home"
dot_prefix = true                # dot-config/ deploys as .config/
exclude = ["README.md"]

[dotfile_groups.home.entries]    # ordinary whole-file entries, cut out of the walk
"~/.config/kitty" = { mode = "symlink" }                            # link this directory whole
"~/.gitconfig" = { source = "git/config.tmpl", mode = "template" }  # relative to the root
"~/.kitty-old.conf" = { mode = "absent" }

[bootstrap]
dotfile_groups = ["home", "zsh"]   # unset: every group applies
```

## What groups do

- **Group trees.** `[dotfile_groups.<name>]` requires a `root`. A relative root resolves against `dotfiles.root`, not the declaring file's directory. Other keys: `target` (default `~`), `mode` (`symlink-each` by default, or `copy` or `symlink`), `exclude`, `dot_prefix`, `manifest`, `relative`. mise walks the root and deploys each file at the same path under the target, so you don't list files. A more local config's table replaces the whole group.
- **Group entries.** `[dotfile_groups.<name>.entries]` uses the same syntax as `[dotfiles]`, keyed by target, and each entry is cut out of the walk. This is how a directory is linked whole, a file rendered as a template, copied with `permissions`, removed with `absent`, and so on.
  - An entry without `source` finds it under the root at its path inside the group target; a relative `source` starts at the root, and a source inside the root is not also deployed by the walk.
  - An entry without `mode` deploys like the group: a file as one link, or as one copy in a `copy` group.
  - Walking entries inherit the group's `dot_prefix`, `manifest`, and its `exclude` patterns without `/`.
  - Entries must lie inside the group target. An entry beneath a directory linked whole would change a file in the root itself, so it fails as a conflict before anything is written.
- **`[dotfiles]` entries take no `group`.** They always apply, and entries belong to a group only by being declared under it.
- **Selection.** `[bootstrap] dotfile_groups` chooses the groups a machine applies; the most local list wins. If the list names a group that nothing declares, mise warns.
- **Conflicts.** If two selected groups write the same file, or one links a directory another writes into, apply and status fail before anything is written. The error names both groups. Two groups with the same tree conflict too.
- **Orphans and removal.** Ea

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->

<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN?thread=cmsg_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iNTJaRPgGigv9vxThHpVsm3s)_

Task `confirm` prompts always showed "Yes" / "No", which doesn't fit confirmations whose outcome isn't a plain yes or no (see discussion #13940). The object form of `confirm` now accepts `yes` and `no` labels:

```toml
[tasks.deploy]
confirm = { message = "Deploy to production?", yes = "Deploy", no = "Cancel", default = "no" }
run = "deploy.sh"
```

The interactive prompt shows `Deploy` / `Cancel` instead of `Yes` / `No`.

- `default` is now optional in the object form (it still defaults to `yes`), so `{ message, yes, no }` is valid on its own.
- The labels support the same Tera templates as the message, including `usage.*` values.
- Non-interactive use is unchanged: piped answers (`echo y | mise run deploy`) still accept `y`/`n`, and `--yes` still skips the prompt. When labels are set, the stdin hint adds `(y = Deploy, n = Cancel)`.
- Plain-string `confirm` and existing `{ message, default }` configs behave as before.

Docs and both JSON schemas are updated. Added unit tests for parsing (header and `mise.toml`); `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. The interactive widget rendering itself wasn't exercised in a TTY.

title: fix(exec): limit @latest resolution to the tools named on the command line
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/413
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"jdx"} -->
_Requested by **Jeff** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iN?thread=cmsg_01Xr4EsA36tZ7bQySmQU67iNPHQxXGrNMsBhhEgKyrC2Jv)_

Before: `mise x claude@latest -- ls` in a project with `latest` tools in `mise.toml` warned `missing: tak@0.0.14 cargo-binstall@1.25.1 …`, even though the next `mise i` said "all tools are installed". Passing any `tool@latest` made `mise x` resolve every configured tool against the newest remote release and ignore the lockfile, so tools that were installed and locked at an older version were reported as missing.

After: only the tool named as `@latest` is resolved to the newest release. Configured tools keep resolving from installed versions and the lockfile, so `mise x claude@latest -- ls` no longer warns about tools `mise install` considers satisfied.

The new `ResolveOptions::latest_versions_for_arguments_only` flag makes `ToolVersionList::resolve` drop `latest_versions` and re-enable `use_locked_version` for any list whose source is not a command-line argument. `mise x` sets it when an argument is `@latest`.

How: added `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_exec_latest_arg`, which fails without the change and passes with it. `test_exec_latest`, `test_exec_lockfile` and `test_lockfile_exec` still pass, and clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(ruby): expose depends tools to ruby-build
body:
`depends` tools must reach the build itself, not just install ordering:
ruby-build's JRuby definitions check the `java` on PATH, so a system JDK would otherwise shadow a `java` declared as a dependency. 

Only applied when dependencies are declared, so a plain source build keeps its current PATH.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# A tool listed in ruby's `depends` must be usable by ruby-build itself, not only
+# installed first. JRuby definitions run `require_java`, which checks $JAVA_HOME
+# before the `java` on PATH; without the dependency env a system JDK wins.
+
+RUBY_BUILD_REPO="$PWD/ruby-build"
+DEPENDENCY_SEEN_FILE="$PWD/dependency-seen"
+
+mkdir -p "$RUBY_BUILD_REPO/bin"
+
+cat >"$RUBY_BUILD_REPO/install.sh" <<'SH'
+#!/bin/sh
+set -eu
+mkdir -p "$PREFIX/bin"

title: feat(bootstrap): render templates in Compose projects
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/412
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Compose projects declared in shared bootstrap configuration can now use Tera values such as `{{ config_root }}` and `{{ env.HOME }}` for `project_dir`, instead of hardcoding a machine-specific absolute path.

```toml
[bootstrap.compose.mempalace]
project_dir = "{{ config_root }}/mempalace"
files = ["compose.yaml"]
env_files = [".env"]
```

Every Compose string value now renders in the context of the config that declared it before path validation and command construction. Template values retain the existing no-`exec()` safety rule, and declarations are compared after rendering so independently composed roots do not silently select a project with a different resolved path. Unknown Compose keys continue to warn.

## Validation

- Focused Rust regression: rendered project, file, environment-file, command, profile, and dependency values pass the normal request validation.
- Added e2e coverage that verifies a templated `project_dir`, file, environment file, and Compose command reach the Compose frontend.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13937

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes bootstrap Compose loading and path resolution for all projects; mis-rendered templates or shadowing edge cases could break existing compose apply flows.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`[bootstrap.compose]`** now treats every string (and string-array) field as a [Tera template](/templates.html), aligned with systemd units and LaunchAgents. Values such as `project_dir`, `files`, `env_files`, `command`, and `depends_on` are rendered in the declaring config’s context **before** path validation and Compose CLI construction, so shared configs can use `{{ config_root }}`, `{{ vars.* }}`, and `{{ env.* }}` instead of machine-specific paths.
> 
> Bootstrap stores compose entries as `Templated<ComposeTomlConfig>`, renders during config merge, and still forbids `{{ exec(...) }}` so status/plan/dry-run/apply stay consistent. Unknown compose keys are warned explicitly, and ignored fields are stripped before rendering so typos cannot break template evaluation. Docs and JSON schema document template behavior; Rust unit tests and e2e coverage verify resolved paths reach the Compose frontend and that a local declaration shadows a global one without evaluating the shadowed template.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 62647ca3d441f8fc7f8020019aeef8b95622999c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

title: docs: show pinned packslip bootstraps for mise and Docker
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/410
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Explain how to keep a reviewed packslip bootstrapper fixed while allowing mise to follow upstream releases. The installation guide separates the verifier version, mise version, and signer pin, and explains when this is useful for CI, base images, and distribution packages.

```sh
packslip install github.com/jdx/mise --pin ps1_nlhmwtfeufglxv5myvwvronk7a
```

This authenticates the current mise release without fixing its version. The Docker cookbook adds a complete Debian example with packslip 1.5.1 pinned by its verified multi-platform image digest, an optional `MISE_VERSION` build argument, and instructions to rebuild without caching the `latest` installation. It also explains why a later build stage must retain the complete installation tree. The installation page distinguishes this bootstrap from mise's built-in packslip tool backend.

Validation: the full documentation build, changed-file Prettier/Markdown checks, and CI pass. Built and ran the exact Docker example on Linux amd64. Checked a user-scoped installation of mise 2026.9.18, Bash activation and `mise exec`, self-update through its exported command to 2026.10.1, and a subsequent packslip reinstall without `--force`. Other platforms were not exercised.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-6; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Documentation-only changes with no runtime or security-sensitive code paths affected.
> 
> **Overview**
> Documentation now treats **packslip** as the recommended alternative for CI/Docker (alongside official images) and substantially expands how to install mise through it.
> 
> The installing guide clarifies verification steps, supported platforms, signer pins vs release versions, PATH/shell follow-up, and a new **“Pin the bootstrapper and let mise float”** workflow for fixing a reviewed packslip binary or image digest while installing current mise releases. It also separates the standalone packslip installer from mise’s built-in packslip tool backend.
> 
> The Docker cookbook adds a **Bootstrap with packslip** section: a multi-stage Debian example with a digest-pinned packslip image, optional `MISE_VERSION`, cache/rebuild notes, and guidance on copying the full install tree between stages. `llms.txt` mirrors the updated Docker blurb.
