+packslip prints the installed command paths. A Unix user gets `~/.local/bin/mise`;
+root gets `/usr/local/bin/mise`. It does not change PATH or your shell files.
+Continue with [shell setup](#shells) for automatic project activation.
+
+The signer pin is the fingerprint of mise's GitHub repository. It stays the same
 across renames, transfers, and new releases, and a different repository that
 takes the name does not match it. Without `--pin`, packslip trusts the
 repository GitHub reports for the name on first use and holds later installs
 on that machine to it.
 
-`mise self-update` works in this installation. Running
-`packslip install github.com/jdx/mise` again replaces it with the newest
-release. Use `--version` to choose a release.
+Omitting `--version`, or passing `--version latest`, requests the current stable
+release. To fix mise too:
+
+```sh
+packslip install github.com/jdx/mise --version 2026.10.1 \
+  --pin ps1_nlhmwtfeufglxv5myvwvronk7a
+```
+
+`mise self-update` works through this installation. You can also rerun
+`packslip install` to replace mise with the release you request. See
+[packslip's install guide](https://packslip.dev/docs/bootstrap/) for system
+scope, destination overrides, and trust settings.
+
+#### Pin the bootstrapper and let mise float
+
+The packslip version, mise version, and signer pin control different things.
+You can keep a reviewed packslip binary or container digest fixed while
+omitting `--version` to install current mise releases. The signer pin continues
+to authenticate mise as new versions are published; it does not freeze a
+release. This is useful for a base image, CI bootstrap, or distribution package
+that should not need a new installer for each mise release.
+
+Pin packslip with its
+[versioned install script or container digest](https://packslip.dev/docs/getting-started/#install-packslip).
+The [Docker cookbook example](/mise-cookbook/docker.html#bootstrap-with-packslip)
+shows a complete pinned-verifier, floating-mise setup and how to rebuild it
+without reusing a cached installation. packslip does not update itself or
+automatically update mise; rerun installation, use `mise self-update`, or enable
+mise's [automatic updates](#installation-methods).
+
+The stable packslip version 1 format allows the bootstrapper and mise to evolve
+independently. Security fixes or new signing formats can still require a verifier
+update; an unchanged bootstrapper is not guaranteed to work forever. See
+[packslip's compatibility policy](https://packslip.dev/docs/compatibility/#maintaining-packaged-verifiers).
+
+Once mise is installed, its [packslip backend](/dev-tools/backends/packslip.html)
+can install other tools with commands such as `mise use -g packslip:github.com/jdx/hk`.
+That backend is built into mise and does not need a separate packslip executable.

title: registry: prefer signed packslips for helmfile and dagu
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/409
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

helmfile and dagu now publish a signed [packslip](https://packslip.dev) with each release: helmfile starting with v1.8.1 (helmfile/helmfile#2809), and dagu starting with v2.18.0 (dagucloud/dagu#2891). From those versions on, `mise use helmfile` and `mise use dagu` install from the release manifest. mise checks that the manifest was signed by the project's own release workflow, checks the archive's digest and size against it, and installs the agent skills each project ships with the release.

```console
$ mise use helmfile@1.8.1
mise ✓ packslip:github.com/helmfile/helmfile@1.8.1  skills/helmfile/metadata.json
$ helmfile --version
helmfile version 1.8.1
```

Earlier releases have no packslip, so they still install through `aqua:` (helmfile also keeps asdf). `mise ls-remote` lists versions from the preferred backend; use `mise ls-remote aqua:helmfile/helmfile` or `mise ls-remote aqua:dagucloud/dagu` to see older releases. Both entries now declare their executable (`helmfile`, `dagu`), so lazy-install shims can find them.

## Verification

- `mise ls-remote packslip:github.com/helmfile/helmfile` lists 1.8.1, and `mise ls-remote packslip:github.com/dagucloud/dagu` lists 2.18.0 and 2.18.1.
- `mise exec packslip:…@<version>` printed `helmfile version 1.8.1`, `2.18.0` and `2.18.1`. Each output matches its registry test.
- Both release workflows sign with packslip 1.4.0 or later, which fixes the libc label on static Linux builds and goreleaser's `386` naming. dagu pins v1.4.0 by SHA. helmfile uses `jdx/packslip@v1`, which pointed at 1.4.x or later when 1.8.1 was released.

Tracks #13712. Same shape as #13780 (timoni, worktrunk).

title: fix(dotfiles): read saved history after directory-to-symlink changes
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/408
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Replacing a previously tracked directory with a symlink can make subsequent `mise dot save` and history synchronization fail while rebuilding the history index. For example, moving personal skills into `~/.agents/skills` and linking the old Claude skill directories breaks reads of earlier checkpoints that enrolled `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.

Read historical enrollment from its saved manifest without checking the current filesystem. Live enrollment and replay retain their destination safeguards. A regression test verifies that old checkpoint coverage remains identical after the directory becomes a symlink and that enrolling through that live symlink remains rejected.

Validated with the regression test, the explicit-tracking and manifest-enrollment end-to-end tests, full workspace/all-features Clippy with warnings denied, and `mise run lint-fix` on stable Rust. Also used the patched binary to rebuild and save the affected live history; ordinary saves and sync work again. Beta Cargo's new manifest warnings block the unmodified repository's lint task, so lint was checked on stable.

title: fix(task): report a timed-out task as failed even when it exits cleanly
body:
On Unix, a task whose `timeout` expired was reported as successful if it handled SIGTERM and exited 0. mise stopped the task, but `mise run` printed no error and exited 0, so a timeout could go unnoticed in CI or in a task chain.

```toml
[tasks.clean_exit]
run = "trap 'exit 0' TERM; while true; do sleep 1; done"
timeout = "2s"
```

Before (macOS, debug build of `main`):

```
$ mise run clean_exit
[clean_exit] $ trap 'exit 0' TERM; while true; do sleep 1; done
Terminated: 15
$ echo $?
0
```

After:

```
$ mise run clean_exit
[clean_exit] $ trap 'exit 0' TERM; while true; do sleep 1; done
Terminated: 15
[clean_exit] ERROR timed out after 2s
[clean_exit] ERROR task failed
$ echo $?
1
```

A command is now reported as timed out whenever its timeout stopped it, whatever its exit status. Windows already worked this way, since a task stopped there with Ctrl+C can also exit 0. The task `timeout` docs now say that a timed-out task fails even if it exits successfully once stopped.

### Validation

- New case in `e2e/tasks/test_task_timeout`: a task that traps SIGTERM and exits 0 must fail with `timed out`. On macOS, `mise run test:e2e test_task_timeout` passes (`All timeout tests passed!`).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on macOS.
- Linux and Windows have not been run locally; CI covers them.

title: feat(daemons): support daemon presets on Windows
body:
Service presets now work on Windows. Until now, `mise daemons start` refused any preset daemon on Windows. For example, this config now starts PostgreSQL there, creates the `app` database on first start, and exports the connection variables:

```toml
[tools]
postgres = "18"

[daemons.db]
preset = "postgres"
version = "18"
options = { database = "app" }
```

Every preset except `redis` works, since redis has no Windows build. Presets run under pitchfork's default `cmd /C` shell on Windows; another `windows_shell` is not supported.

## What changed

- Preset values (paths, URLs, hosts) and the `__init` step are quoted for cmd on Windows and for `sh` on Unix. On Windows each value is quoted, and then cmd's metacharacters are escaped with `^`, so a `"` or `%VAR%` in a value reaches the server unchanged. A `%` in the mise path stays outside the quotes and is escaped. On Windows the run has no `exec` prefix, and readiness probes run whole as `"<mise>" x -- cmd /c <command>`, as `sh -c` does on Unix, so each part of `a && b` runs in the tool environment.
- Programs that an init step calls are looked up on the PATH that `mise x` built, including `.cmd` files. Conda's PostgreSQL provides `initdb` and similar tools as `.mise-bins\*.cmd` shims.
- A database's temporary init server runs in its own process group and is stopped with Ctrl+Break. Killing it at once left a temporary-directory record that later crashed CockroachDB's real server.
- Two preset commands are rewritten to quote the same way in `sh` and cmd: postgres's `-k ''` becomes `-k ""`, and cockroachdb's `-e 'SELECT 1'` becomes `-e "SELECT 1"`.
- The Windows refusals in preset initialization and tool validation are removed. The docs now describe Windows support.

PostgreSQL stops cleanly only with pitchfork 2.29.0 or later, which sends it Ctrl+C on Windows. Older versions terminate it, and it recovers on the next start. PostgreSQL also refuses to run with administrative rights, so it does not start from an elevated prompt. Windows also reserves some port ranges for Hyper-V and WSL. On the test machine, SpiceDB's default HTTP port 8443 fell in one, and moving it with `ports` fixed it. The docs say this.

## Validation

- On Windows 11 with pitchfork 2.29.0, postgres, nats, spicedb and cockroachdb started, passed their readiness checks and stopped. postgres stopped cleanly (`pg_controldata` reports `shut down`), and cockroachdb started both on existing data and on a fresh data directory. These runs predate the `^` escaping and the `cmd /c` probe wrapper added during review. After that change, only the e2e test below covers nats and postgres; spicedb and cockroachdb have not been re-run.
- New `e2e-win/daemons_presets.Tests.ps1` checks two presets with pitchfork 2.29.0. For nats, it checks the health endpoint and `NATS_URL`, and that no server process is left after stop. For postgres, it checks that the requested database is served and that the cluster shuts down cleanly. The test fails on mise 2026

title: fix(daemons): start a task daemon with init under cmd.exe on Windows
body:
On Windows, a task daemon that has `init` steps failed to start. For example:

```toml
[tasks.dev]
run = "npm run dev"

[daemons.dev]
task = "dev"
args = ["--port", "3000"]
init = ["npm ci", "npm run migrate"]
```

mise chains the `init` steps and the task into one shell command for pitchfork, and wrote the task part for a POSIX shell: `exec '<mise>' run 'dev' -- '--port' '3000'`. pitchfork runs that command with `cmd /C` on Windows by default. cmd has no `exec` and does not treat `'` as a quote, so `mise daemons start` reported `'exec' is not recognized` and the daemon stopped with an error.

On Windows, mise now writes the task part as cmd reads it: `"<mise.exe>" run dev -- --port 3000`. It double-quotes the mise path and keeps any `%` in it outside the quotes, escaped. It quotes any argument that needs quotes, then escapes cmd's own metacharacters in it with `^`. Without that escape, a `"` inside an argument would end cmd's quoting, so a following `&` would start another command, and cmd would expand `%VAR%` even inside quotes. The `init` steps then run, and the task starts with its arguments unchanged. Unix keeps the `exec` form. A task daemon without `init` was already started without a shell (#13714) and is unchanged.

The docs no longer say this case is unsupported, and tell Windows users to write `init` steps as cmd commands.

The quoted command reaches cmd intact only with #13887, which is merged. If pitchfork's `windows_shell` is set to PowerShell, a command that starts with a quoted path still does not run there.

## Validation

- Unit test `a_task_after_init_is_a_command_line_cmd_can_read` checks the cmd form: a mise path with spaces, and arguments containing `'`, `&`, an inner `"` and `%APPDATA%`, and a mise path containing `%TEMP%`.
- On Windows 11, a program in a directory literally named `%USERNAME% x` failed to start (`The system cannot find the path specified.`) with the path only quoted, and started with this form.
- On Windows 11, 12 arguments were passed through `cmd /s /c "<init> && <command>"`, which is how a `mise = true` daemon reaches cmd. They included `a" & echo INJECTED & "b`, `%APPDATA%`, `!bang!`, `^caret` and an empty string. All 12 reached the program unchanged. With quoting alone, the first ran `echo INJECTED` and the second arrived expanded.
- New `e2e-win/daemons_task_init.Tests.ps1` starts a task daemon with `init` under the default `cmd /C`, using pitchfork 2.28.0. The test checks that `init` ran and that the task received `["a b", "x&y"]`. It failed with `'exec' is not recognized` on mise 2026.9.15 and passed with this change on Windows 11.

title: fix(config): skip miserc discovery with --no-config
body:
## Problem

A malformed `.miserc.toml` anywhere in the discovery chain fails even config-free invocations: `run_inner` calls `miserc::init()?` unconditionally (`src/cli/mod.rs`) before no-config is honored anywhere, and TOML errors propagate via `?`. So `mise --no-config version` run from a directory with a broken repo-level (or global/system) miserc exits non-zero instead of ignoring config.

## Fix

Guard the four miserc entry points on the pre-existing `Settings::no_config()` (`MISE_NO_CONFIG` env or pre-`--` argv `--no-config`):

- `load_miserc_settings()` → `Ok(default)`
- `load_global_miserc_settings()` → default
- `get()` → default (folded into the existing `is_package_query()` early return, mirroring that precedent)
- `get_global_ignored_config_paths()` → `None`

No new API; `no_config()` already exists. No-config now means no early-config.

## Semantic edge (call-out for reviewers)

- `get_global_ignored_config_paths() → None` disables ignored-paths filtering (consumed via `env.rs`) under no-config. Consistent with "no config", but changes `prune`-family verdicts for no-config invocations.
- `no_config()` argv detection requires `ARGS` populated — true at the `run_inner` call site (`ARGS` is written just above the `miserc::init()?` call), so both `MISE_NO_CONFIG=1` and `--no-config` forms work.

## Test plan

- New `e2e/config/test_no_config_skips_miserc`: malformed project + global + system miserc; `MISE_NO_CONFIG=1` and `--no-config` both succeed on `version`/`exec` from root and nested cwd; control without the flag still fails with `Invalid TOML in config file`. Passes.
- Existing `e2e/config/test_miserc`, `test_miserc_local`, `test_no_config` all still pass.

title: fix(config): report a failed settings reload instead of aborting
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/406
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Several commands rebuild settings partway through a run: `mise install`, `mise upgrade`, `mise use`, `mise uninstall`, `mise prune` and friends after they change what is installed, and `mise ls-remote --prerelease` / `--no-versions-host` to apply the flag. That rebuild was lazy. The cached settings were dropped and the next `Settings::get()` loaded them again, and if that load failed there was nothing to return the error to, so `Settings::get()` panicked. Release builds are compiled with `panic = "abort"`, so a settings problem ended the command with SIGABRT and a core dump instead of an error message.

This is the crash in #13923: `mise install github:can1357/oh-my-pi@latest` for a tool that was already installed aborted on the main thread, and the only clue left in the core was a panic location inside the settings loader. The one-off trigger there is still unknown, but the abort is what turned it from an error into a crash.

A reload can only fail when one of its inputs changed since startup, so a deliberate trigger is contrived. A `preinstall` hook that removes the directory `--cd` pointed at does it: re-applying `--cd` during the reload fails.

`sub/mise.toml`:

```toml
[hooks]
preinstall = "rm -rf $PWD"
```

Before (2026.9.17 release build; paths shortened):

```
$ mise --cd sub install age@1.3.2
mise ⇢ age@1.3.2  7ms · already installed
mise ████████████████ 1/1 · installed 0 tools · 1 already installed in 25ms

The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value:
   0: failed to set current directory to /tmp/demo/sub
   1: No such file or directory (os error 2)
$ echo $?
134
```

After:

```
$ mise --cd sub install age@1.3.2
mise ⇢ age@1.3.2  15ms · already installed
mise ████████████████ 1/1 · installed 0 tools · 1 already installed in 52ms
Error:
   0: failed to reload settings
   1: failed to set current directory to /tmp/demo/sub
   2: No such file or directory (os error 2)
$ echo $?
1
```

`Settings::reload()` and `Settings::override_with()` now build the new settings first and only then swap them in, returning the error otherwise; `Config::reset()` and the `ls-remote` and `test-tool` flags propagate it. The previous settings stay cached until the new ones are ready, so readers on other threads never find the cache empty mid-reload either. A failed `override_with()` also puts the CLI layer back as it was, so the override it could not apply is not picked up by a later reload, and `ls-remote` folds `--prerelease` and `--no-versions-host` into one override so they rebuild settings once.

Validation: a new unit test makes a reload fail (`MISE_YES=maybe` set after the first load) and checks that `reload()` and `override_with()` return the error while `Settings::get()` keeps returning the previous settings, and that the failed override is not applied once the environment is corrected. title: feat(schema): type tool options per backend and core tool
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/405
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Editors validate and autocomplete `mise.toml` from `schema/mise.json`, but a `[tools]` entry only ever got the generic options, so `asset_pattern`, `features`, `release_type` and friends were untyped and invisible. This makes the schema offer each backend's own options, and the core tools' options, only for tools of that kind.

```toml
[tools]
"github:cli/cli" = { version = "2", asset_pattern = 5 }        # flagged: must be a string
"aqua:o/r"       = { version = "1", libc = "uclibc" }          # flagged: glibc, gnu or musl
java             = { version = "21", release_type = "stable" } # flagged: ga or ea
"cargo:ripgrep"  = { version = "latest", features = ["pcre2"] } # completes and validates
```

## What changes

- **Typed options per backend.** A `patternProperties` entry on `tools` matches the backend prefix (`^github:`, `^(pypi|pipx):`, ...) and points at a definition that extends the generic tool. Covered: github, gitlab, forgejo, ubi, http, s3, aqua, cargo, npm, pypi/pipx, gem, go, conda, spm, packslip, and spinel from #13922. Every other key still gets the generic definition, so an unrelated `cargo:foo = { entrypoint = 5 }` is unaffected.
- **Core tools.** `python` (`patch_sysconfig`), `java` (`release_type`), `rust` (`profile`, `components`, `targets`, `mr_boxington`) and core `dotnet` (`runtime`), including `core:` and bracketed spellings.
- **Task tool tables.** `[tasks.*.tools]` uses the same typed definitions.
- **Per-platform overrides.** `platforms.<os>-<arch>` (and the `platform` alias) is modelled for every tool, and typed for the options each backend actually reads per platform (for example `github` `asset_pattern` and `url`, `http` `url` and `checksum`).
- **`prerelease`** is added as a generic option, because every backend reads it. `lazy_bins` now accepts a string as well as an array, matching the parser.
- **Booleans** accept `true`/`false`, the strings `"true"`/`"false"`, and `1`/`0`, because mise coerces them. This avoids flagging configs that work today.
- **`experimental_monorepo_root`** is accepted as a deprecated key. mise still honors it with a warning, but the root schema rejected it.

Option definitions live once in `tool_<backend>_options`, and platform entries `$ref` into them, which keeps the diff to one definition per option. `schema/mise-task.json` is regenerated by `render:schema`.

The option lists come from the backend source (what each backend actually reads), not only the docs. Options the docs miss, such as the `format` option on `github`, `http` and `s3`, are included.

## Out of scope

Left for follow-ups: per-preset daemon `options` and `ports`, the undocumented `[bootstrap]` `secrets`, `groups`, `users` and `compose` sections, and typed options in `mise-registry-tool.json`.

## Testing

- `ajv compile --strict-types --strict-tuples` passes on both schemas, the same flags `hk` runs.

title: feat(backend): add experimental spinel backend
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/404
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Adds an experimental `spinel:` backend that compiles a Ruby command-line tool from a GitHub repository into a native executable with [Spinel](https://github.com/matz/spinel), Matz's Ruby AOT compiler (requested in discussion 13301).

```toml
[tools."spinel:tobi/try"]
version = "1.10.1"
entrypoint = "try.rb"
bin = "try"
tag_prefix = "v"
```

```
$ mise install && mise x -- try --help
try v1.10.1 - ephemeral workspace manager
```

`mise ls-remote spinel:tobi/try` lists git tags through `git ls-remote`, so it never touches the GitHub API. Options are `entrypoint`, `bin`, `tag_prefix`, `source_ref` and `spinel`. The backend needs the `spinel` compiler on `PATH`, or its path in the `spinel` option. Spinel ships as source, so mise does not install it yet. macOS and Linux only.

## Status

We're doing this, but only because it's for Matz. It is gated behind `experimental`, and it may not survive. If it turns into a large maintenance burden, or Spinel doesn't take off, it will be removed. The docs page says the same.

Based on [nateberkopec/mise-backend-spinel](https://github.com/nateberkopec/mise-backend-spinel); Nate is credited as co-author.

## Testing

I built Spinel at the commit Nate's README pins, then ran `mise install` and `mise x -- try --help` against `tobi/try`. Unit tests cover tag parsing and option validation. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean. `mise run lint-fix` fails locally on the repo's existing `package.homepage` manifest warnings, so lint did not run; CI will.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.286.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Install runs git and an external compiler on user-supplied repos; inputs are validated and the feature is experimental-only, but failed or malicious source could still affect the build environment.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **experimental** `spinel:` installation backend that builds a Ruby CLI from a GitHub repo (`owner/repo`) into a standalone native binary via the external Spinel AOT compiler, without bundling Ruby or Spinel in the output.
> 
> Install flow shallow-fetches a tag or `source_ref` with `git`, runs the configured `spinel` binary on `entrypoint`, and writes the result to `bin/`. Remote versions come from `git ls-remote` tags (optional `tag_prefix`), not the GitHub API. Tool options include `entrypoint`, `bin`, `tag_prefix`, `source_ref`, and `spinel` (install-time only).
> 
> Wiring updates register `BackendType::Spinel`, hook it into backend dispatch and `mise edit`, extend the registry JSON schema, and add docs/sidebar/`llms.txt` entries. Use requires `mise settings experimental=true`; Windows is rejected at install time.
>

+---
+description: "Compile Ruby command-line tools from GitHub source with the experimental Spinel backend."
+---
+
+# Spinel Backend <Badge type="warning" text="experimental" />
+
+The `spinel:` backend compiles a Ruby command-line tool from a GitHub repository into a native
+executable with [Spinel](https://github.com/matz/spinel), Matz's Ruby AOT compiler. The result needs
+neither Ruby nor Spinel to run.
+
+::: warning
+This backend is experimental, and it may not stay. Spinel is young, and the backend is only worth
+keeping while Spinel takes off and the backend stays cheap to maintain. If either stops being true,
+it will be removed. Enable it with `mise settings experimental=true`.
+:::
+
+## Requirements
+
+- macOS or Linux (Windows is not supported).
+- `git`.
+- The `spinel` compiler on `PATH`, or its path in the `spinel` tool option. Spinel ships as source:
+  see its [Quick Start](https://github.com/matz/spinel#quick-start) to build it.
+- A C compiler, which Spinel invokes to produce the executable.
+
+Spinel supports only part of the Ruby language, so many Ruby tools will not compile. The backend
+compiles a single entrypoint file. It does not install gems, copy data files, or fetch submodules.
+
+## Usage
+
+```sh
+mise settings experimental=true
+```
+
+Most tools need options, such as the entrypoint, so declare them in `mise.toml` and then install:
+
+```toml
+[tools."spinel:tobi/try"]
+version = "1.10.1"
+entrypoint = "try.rb"
+bin = "try"
+tag_prefix = "v"
+```
+
+```sh
+mise install
+```
+
+`mise ls-remote spinel:tobi/try` lists the repository's git tags (via `git ls-remote`, not the GitHub
+API). With `tag_prefix = "v"`, the tag `v1.10.1` is the version `1.10.1`.
+
+## Tool Options
+
+The following [tool-options](/dev-tools/#tool-options) are available for the `spinel` backend—these
+go in `[tools]` in `mise.toml`.
+
+### `entrypoint`
+
+The Ruby file to compile, relative to the repository root. Defaults to `main.rb`.
+
+### `bin`
+
+The name of the executable written to `bin/`. Defaults to the repository name.
+
+### `tag_prefix`
+
+Text before the version in each git tag, such as `v`. Only tags with the prefix are listed.
+
+### `source_ref`
+

+# Task timeout and Ctrl-C fixes, Windows daemon and shim fixes
+
+This release is mostly bug fixes. `mise run` now stops tasks properly when `--timeout` expires or you press Ctrl-C. Task daemons and native shims work better on Windows. `core:rust` now follows `mise.lock` and picks up new stable and beta toolchains. Lockfile, GitHub asset selection, Homebrew cask and plugin update problems are also fixed.
+
+## Fixed
+
+### Tasks
+
+- **`mise run --timeout` now stops the tasks it was running.** Before, mise printed the timeout error and exited, but the task processes could keep running in the background. Now the whole-run timeout (`--timeout` or the `task.timeout` setting) stops tasks the same way a per-task `timeout` does. On Unix, mise sends SIGTERM and then SIGKILL after 5 seconds. On Windows, it runs `taskkill /F /T`. Tasks with `raw = true` are not stopped by the whole-run timeout. [#13876](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13876) by @Marukome0743
+- **A single Ctrl-C lets tasks shut down cleanly.** Before, one Ctrl-C could make mise exit right away while tasks were still cleaning up. This happened in three cases: a task that runs `mise run` itself got SIGINT twice; a tool like `docker compose up` treated the duplicate SIGINT as a force-quit; and a task that exits non-zero on SIGINT caused mise to send SIGTERM to its sibling tasks. Now mise waits for tasks to finish and then exits with status 130. A second Ctrl-C still force-quits. [#13904](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13904)
+- **Tab completion for the `:task` shorthand.** In a monorepo, `mise run :<TAB>` now suggests tasks from the current config root, and task flags complete after the shorthand. [#13882](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13882) by @pikeas
+
+### Daemons
+
+- **Task daemons start on Windows.** A daemon declared with `task =` failed under `cmd /C` with `'exec' is not recognized`. mise now registers it as an argv command that pitchfork starts without a shell, so `args` reach the task exactly as written on every platform. **This needs pitchfork 2.28.0 or later.** With an older pitchfork, mise shows an error that tells you to upgrade, for example with `mise use pitchfork@latest`. Task daemons that use `init` still run through a shell, so they still don't work under `cmd /C`. [#13714](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13714) by @JamBalaya56562
+- **Daemon `run` commands can use `[env]` and `[vars]`.** Before, a template such as `{{ vars.test_var }}` failed with `Variable 'vars' is not defined`. `mise x` now renders the command when the daemon starts, using the project's `[env]`, `[vars]` and mise template filters. Pitchfork's own variables, such as `{{ name }}`, still work. This applies only to `run` and requires a pitchfork release newer than 2.29.0. [#13894](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13894)
+
+  ```toml
+  [vars]
+  greeting = "it's"
+
+  [daemons.hello]
+  run = "exec echo {{ vars.greeting | quote }} from {{ name }}"
+  ```
+
+### Windows shims
+
+- **No more endless process chains from duplicate shim copies.** If two copies of `mise-shim.exe` were on PATH (for example, one from winget's `Links` directory), they could keep calling each other through `mise x`. Running `mise-shim` by its own name now exits with an error. If `mise x` resolves a tool to another shim copy, mise stops after one step and names the PATH directory to remove. [#13681](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13681) by @JamBalaya56562
+- **Node IPC works through the `node.exe` shim.** A Node parent that spawned the shim with an `'ipc'` stdio entry used to wait forever. JSON IPC messages and disconnects now pass through the shim. Passing socket or server handles over the channel is still not supported. [#13903](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13903)
+
+### Rust
+
+- **`mise upgrade rust` updates `stable` and `beta`.** mise didn't recognize rustup 1.29's new `update available:` text. Even when it detected an update, the upgrade skipped the toolchain as already installed. mise now reads both spellings, counts only updates for the toolchain it manages, and updates the toolchain in place. If the update fails, the old toolchain stays usable. [#13898](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13898)
+- **`core:rust` follows `mise.lock`.** mise mistook rustup's symlinks for `mise link`ed versions, so it ignored the lockfile and installed the newest version even with `locked = true`. [#13915](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13915)
+
+### Backends, lockfiles and bootstrap
+
+- **GitHub auto-detection no longer installs metadata files.** SBOMs, signatures, checksums and other sidecar files with platform names, such as `*.tar.gz.sbom.json`, could be chosen as the tool and saved to `mise.lock`. Automatic selection now skips them. Explicit `url` and `asset_pattern` options are unchanged. [#13908](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13908)
+- **`mise lock` removes outdated duplicate entries.** After you changed a tool option, for example by adding `uvx = false` to a `pipx:` tool, `mise lock --upgrade` could leave the old unbound entry next to the new bound one. Unfiltered `mise lock` runs now remove the old entry, unless it has platform data (checksum or URL) that the new entry doesn't have. [#13909](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13909)
+- **Aqua registry cache errors after upgrading.** Compiled registry caches from earlier versions could load but then fail when a package was resolved. mise now ignores those caches and rebuilds them. [#13884](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13884)
+- **Packslip installs retry missing skills.** If the binary installed but a declared skill couldn't be fetched, mise still marked the install as complete. Now the install fails with an error. The next `mise install` fetches only the missing skills and doesn't reinstall the tool. [#13885](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13885)
+- **Pkg-based `brew-cask` packages are no longer reinstalled on every run.** Casks such as `google-drive` list package IDs for several architectures, and mise expected every one of them to be installed. Receipts now store only the patterns that match on your machine. Casks recorded by earlier versions are reinstalled once to write a corrected receipt. [#13893](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13893)
+- **`mise plugins update` works when the remote isn't named `origin`.** This happens, for example, when git's `clone.defaultRemoteName` is set to something else. mise uses `origin` if it exists and otherwise uses the first remote. [#13914](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13914)
+
+## Changed
+
+- `mise skills sync`, the table output of `mise skills ls`, and other human-facing messages now show paths under your home directory with `~`. This includes output from `mise deps install`, task source lines, `mise completion --install` and daemon messages. `--json` output and script-oriented commands still print full paths. [#13910](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13910)
+
+**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/jdx/mise/compare/vfox-v2026.10.0...v2026.10.1

title: chore: add hk pre-commit hook and drop redundant crate homepages
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/402
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`hk.pkl` defined only `fix` and `check` hooks, so `hk install` set up no git hooks and lint ran only when invoked by hand. Contributors could commit code that CI then rejected.

This adds a `pre-commit` hook (`fix = true`, `stash = "git"`) that runs the same linters as `fix`.

It also removes `package.homepage` from the ten workspace crates where it duplicated `package.repository`. Recent cargo warns about the redundancy, and with `build.warnings = "deny"` that made `cargo-check` (and so `mise run lint`) fail locally. `aqua-registry` and `mise-brew-relocation` keep their distinct `homepage`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Developer workflow and crate metadata only; no runtime CLI or install behavior changes for end users.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **git `pre-commit` hook** in `hk.pkl` that runs the same hk linter steps as `fix`, with auto-fix enabled and `stash = "git"` so unstaged work is preserved. **`hk install --mise`** now installs that hook (including in cloud agent bootstrap docs), replacing guidance that said nothing was installed.
> 
> **Contributor docs** (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/contributing.md`) now describe the hook and note that on **Windows**, `mise run lint-fix` still only runs Clippy, Prettier, and `cargo fmt`, not the full hk set.
> 
> Removes redundant **`package.homepage`** from ten workspace crates where it duplicated `repository`, so Cargo’s homepage warning no longer fails `cargo-check` under `build.warnings = "deny"`. Crates with a distinct homepage (e.g. `aqua-registry`, `mise-brew-relocation`) are unchanged.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 97cb5385e43796eeebfc118a1d4dab5ec4259453. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: fix(activate): keep loading trusted configs when a project config is untrusted
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/401
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

Opening a shell in a project whose \`mise.toml\` is not yet trusted made \`mise hook-env\` fail entirely, so tools and env from the trusted global config were not applied (e.g. \`fish: Unknown command: foo\`):

\`\`\`
mise WARN ~/project/mise.toml is not trusted, run \`mise trust\` to enable it
\`\`\`

## Fix

\`hook-env\` now skips untrusted configs and keeps loading the rest, still printing the same one-time warning. Explicit commands (\`mise run\`, \`mise x\`, ...) behave as before. The warning marker is no longer cleared while a config is skipped, so the warning still shows once per directory.

Fixes #13918

## Tests

- New \`e2e/cli/test_hook_env_untrusted_keeps_global\`: global env is emitted, local env is not, warning is shown.
- Existing trust-warning e2e tests still pass.

title: docs: retime the mise run captions to the vocal
body:
The captions on the [mise run music video](https://mise.jdx.dev/mise-en-place.html) were often out of step with the singing. They came from a forced alignment of the lyric sheet that lost its place in several sections:

- In the breakdown, cues appeared while the previous line was still being held: "I'll be standing at ease" showed 1.6 s before it is sung, and "Every blade laid out" and "And my heart on the beat" about 0.5 s early.
- In the drops, the chants had placeholder cues: one "MISE RUN!" stayed on screen for 12 s over several different chants, and a "MISE! (RUN!)" cue started 1.2 s before the chant.
- Suno sang more repeats than the lyric sheet lists ("One command!" and "MISE! (RUN!)" in the first build-up, ten "Ship!"s instead of four, the drop chants), and those had no captions at all.

This retimes `docs/public/mise-run.en.vtt` against the vocal itself. Every cue now starts on its line's first sung word (0.03 s early). It ends when the line's last note ends, or when the next line starts. Every sung repeat gets its own cue, so there are 75 cues instead of 64. The caption text still matches the lyrics on the page.

| | Shipped captions | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cue start vs. first sung word, median | 0.08 s | 0.03 s early |
| Worst cue | 1.64 s early | 0.03 s early |
| Cues off by more than 0.3 s | 12 of 64 | 0 |
| Sung repeats without a cue | 11 | 0 |

**Music video:** the lyrics burned into the video frames came from the same timing, with 36 of 252 words off by more than 0.25 s. The worst were "MISE IS NIX FOR PEOPLE WITH WORK TO DO!" (up to 0.95 s early) and "I'll be standing at ease" (1.6 s early). The video has been re-rendered from its renderer with the same alignment. The new 1080p and 4K MP4s are already live in R2 at the same URLs, with the same formats and the same audio track, so this PR changes only the caption file.

**How it was measured:** onsets were measured on an isolated vocal stem (Demucs). Each section and each line was force-aligned separately with a CTC aligner, with onsets snapped to the vocal and cross-checked against Whisper transcripts. Every section was then reviewed on spectrogram plots, and the remaining disagreements were set by hand. The drop chants, where the vocal stem is mostly synth bleed, were placed from the spectrograms.

title: fix(rust): honor mise.lock for core:rust installs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/398
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13912

`mise install rust` ignored the `mise.lock` entry. With `rust = "latest"` and a lock pinning `1.98.0`, mise installed `1.99.0` even with `locked = true`.

core:rust installs are symlinks to rustup's `$CARGO_HOME/bin`, which is outside mise's directories. `has_linked_version()` took that for a `mise link`ed version, and linked tools skip lockfile resolution. `has_linked_version()` now ignores a core:rust symlink whose target contains the `rustup` binary. A rust version the user linked by hand still counts as linked.

Reproduced with an isolated data dir: a `1.99.0` install symlinked to a dir containing `rustup`, plus a lock pinning `1.98.0`.

```
before: mise install --dry-run rust  ->  rust@1.99.0 ⇢ would install
after:  mise install --dry-run rust  ->  rust@1.98.0 ⇢ would install
```

Added a unit test covering both the rustup bin dir and a real user link.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.286.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes linked-version detection used to gate lockfile resolution; scope is narrow (core:rust + absolute external symlinks) but incorrect classification could still affect install/lock behavior for Rust setups.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Fixes `mise.lock` being ignored for `core:rust`** when normal rustup installs symlink into `$CARGO_HOME/bin` outside mise’s data dirs. Those symlinks were misclassified as user `mise link` installs, which disables lockfile resolution during `ToolVersion::resolve`.
> 
> `has_linked_version()` now treats **`core:rust` install entries** that point at a directory containing `rustup` and use a **rustup toolchain name** (`stable`, `beta`, `nightly*`, or numeric versions like `1.99.0`) as mise-managed, not user-linked. A symlink to the same rustup bin dir under a **non-toolchain name** (e.g. `custom`) still counts as linked.
> 
> Adds **`is_rustup_install`** / **`is_rustup_toolchain_spec`** helpers and unit tests for toolchain naming and the linked-vs-rustup distinction.
>

title: fix(plugins): update plugin repos whose remote is not named origin
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/397
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise plugins update` failed for plugins whose clone has no remote named `origin`, for example when git's `clone.defaultRemoteName` is set to `upstream`:

```
$ mise plugins update
mise ERROR [android-sdk] plugin update
mise ERROR git failed: ... fetch --prune --update-head-ok origin main:main ...
fatal: 'origin' does not appear to be a git repository
```

mise now looks up the repo's remotes and uses `origin` when it exists. Otherwise it uses the first remote listed, so the update works without renaming the remote. This applies to the fetch, `ls-remote` and remote-URL lookups in `crates/mise-util/src/git.rs`. Repos with an `origin` behave as before.

Tested with a unit test for the remote selection. I did not run it against a real clone with a renamed remote. `src/cli/bootstrap.rs` still assumes `origin`, but it manages mise's own checkout, so I left it alone.

Fixes #13913

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.286.*

title: test(zig): follow indexed master version
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/396
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fix the release-blocking Zig E2E expectation. Zig’s official download index currently maps `master` to stable `0.17.0`, while the test required a `-dev.` suffix. The test now reads `.master.version` from the official index, verifies `zig@master` installs/reports that concrete version, and keeps the regression checks that it does not reuse `0.13.0` or create a frozen `master` install directory.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> E2E test-only change; no production resolver or install logic modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the slow Zig E2E test for **`zig@master`** so it no longer assumes master always resolves to a **`-dev.`** nightly.
> 
> The test now loads **`.master.version`** from Zig’s official `index.json`, asserts **`mise x zig@master`** reports that same concrete version (with a one-time index re-fetch if master moved mid-run), and still fails if mise reuses the unrelated **0.13.0** install or creates a frozen **`installs/zig/master`** directory. The old glob check for any **`*-dev.*`** install dir is replaced by verifying **`installs/zig/$master_version`** exists.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit da404079b4e5b26115df9240cd9cd57e4bb66b6c. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Behavior Changes**
  * Startup no longer runs the one-time runtime symlink migration or removes directories as part of that migration.
  * Listing a plugin with a stale, non-symlink `latest` directory leaves it unchanged. Installing a version sets the `latest` selector to that version.
<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

diff:
--- e2e/core/test_zig_slow (+13/-12)
@@ -2,16 +2,17 @@
 
 assert "mise x zig@0.13.0 -- zig version" "0.13.0"
 
-# #10251: zig@master is a rolling channel. Even with only a STABLE zig installed
-# (0.13.0 above), zig@master must resolve to the concrete nightly (e.g.
-# 0.17.0-dev.NNN) -- it must NOT short-circuit to the unrelated installed stable --
-# and install under a versioned dir rather than a frozen "master" dir, so
-# `mise upgrade`/`outdated` can track new nightlies.
-assert_contains "mise x zig@master -- zig version" "-dev."
+# #10251: zig@master is a rolling channel. Resolve its current concrete version
+# from Zig's official index; master may temporarily point at a stable release.
+# It must not short-circuit to the unrelated installed 0.13.0 or create a frozen
+# "master" install directory.
+master_version=$(curl -fsSL https://ziglang.org/download/index.json | jq -r '.master.version')
+resolved_version=$(mise x zig@master -- zig version)
+if [ "$resolved_version" != "$master_version" ]; then
+  # master can move between mise's index fetch and ours; accept only a fresh
+  # official index value, so a resolver regression still fails.
+  master_version=$(curl -fsSL https://ziglang.org/download/index.json | jq -r '.master.version')
+fi
+assert "printf '%s' \"$resolved_version\"" "$master_version"
 [ ! -d "$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/zig/master" ] || fail "zig@master must not create a frozen installs/zig/master dir"
-# A concrete nightly dir (e.g. 0.17.0-dev.NNN) must exist under installs/zig.
-# Use a glob rather than `ls | grep` (SC2010) to tolerate odd filenames.
-shopt -s nullglob
-dev_dirs=("$MISE_DATA_DIR"/installs/zig/*-dev.*)
-shopt -u nullglob
-[ ${#dev_dirs[@]} -gt 0 ] || fail "zig@master should install a concrete -dev nightly"

title: fix(skills): show $HOME as ~ in skills sync output
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/395
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise skills sync` printed every path in full, so a project under your home directory produced rows like this:

```
linked /home/you/work/api/.claude/skills/hk-debug -> /home/you/.local/share/mise/installs/hk/2.2.0/skills/hk-debug
```

It now abbreviates `$HOME` to `~`, as the rest of mise's human-facing output does:

```
linked ~/work/api/.claude/skills/hk-debug -> ~/.local/share/mise/installs/hk/2.2.0/skills/hk-debug
```

The same applies to the `removed` and "already linked in" rows, the path column of `mise skills ls`, and the `skills.auto_sync` messages after an install. `mise skills ls --json` still prints full paths.

## Other places fixed

An audit of paths printed to people turned up a few more that used `Path::display()` instead of `file::display_path`:

- `mise deps install` source and output lists
- `mise tasks` source provenance lines
- `mise completion --install` ("installing to ...")

title: fix(lock): prune unbound entries superseded by a bound entry
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/394
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

`mise lock --upgrade` could leave two entries for the same tool version after a tool option changed. With a format-0 `mise.lock` containing `pipx:cowsay` 6.1 and a `mise.toml` that adds `uvx = false`, the lockfile ended up with the old unbound entry beside the new bound one, and later `mise lock` runs never removed it.

```toml
# mise.toml
"pipx:cowsay" = { version = "6.1", uvx = false }
```

After this change, `mise lock --upgrade` (or any unfiltered `mise lock`) leaves a single bound entry.

## Details

An unfiltered lock run now drops an unbound entry (no specifiers) when a bound entry of the same version and backend exists for a tool resolved in that run. An unbound entry is kept when there is no such bound sibling, when its backend differs, or when its platform data (checksum, URL) is missing from or differs in the bound entry, so no pin or artifact data is lost. Lockfile versions are compared as opaque strings.

Fixes #13906

## Test plan

- Unit test `test_retain_unsuperseded_unbound_entries`
- E2E `cli/test_lock_prune_superseded_unbound`

title: fix(github): never auto-select metadata assets as the tool
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/393
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's automatic GitHub asset selection could pick a metadata file, such as an SBOM, signature or checksum, as the tool. Releases that publish platform-tagged metadata (for example `editorconfig-checker-darwin-all.tar.gz.sbom.json` next to the real archives) have assets whose names carry the same OS and architecture tokens as the real binary. Metadata files were only penalized by 100 points, so one could still score above zero and be chosen, installed as the tool, and recorded in `mise.lock`.

Now automatic selection never picks a metadata asset, so a lock entry mise writes always points at a real archive or binary. For `editorconfig-checker@4.0.2`, `mise use github:editorconfig-checker/editorconfig-checker@4.0.2` installs the platform archive and never an `.sbom.json`.

Metadata is recognized by a shared `is_metadata_asset` helper (`.json`, `.jsonl`, `.intoto.jsonl`, `.sbom`, `.sig`, `.sha256`, `.pem`, and similar suffixes) that the existing scoring penalty now also uses. Explicit `url` and `asset_pattern` options do not go through automatic selection, so they are unaffected and can still name any file.

Fixes #13907

## Test plan

- Unit tests cover `is_metadata_asset` and selection with platform-tagged SBOM and checksum files next to the real archive, and with metadata-only candidates (nothing selected).
- New e2e test `e2e/backend/test_github_auto_detect_skips_sbom` installs `editorconfig-checker@4.0.2` through auto-detection. `test_github_auto_detect`, `test_github_matching_lock` and `test_github_additional_assets` still pass.
- `cargo clippy -p mise --all-targets` shows no warnings in the changed files. `-D warnings` fails on an existing `unreachable expression` in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs` that this PR does not touch.

title: ci(release): arm release PR after daily cutoff
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/392
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Updates the existing `auto-merge-release` workflow instead of adding another release policy. Its scheduled run now arms the release PR after the 15:00 America/Chicago cutoff, using 15:15 with 15:30/15:45 fallback runs. It confirms the existing `release-window` is pending before arming; auto-merge remains blocked until the existing 03:00 Central window and every other required check pass. The documented `release-now` label still overrides that scheduled-window hold.

This restores the daily behavior previously provided by dot: the old seven-day age gate is removed because it would skip daily release PRs. The existing substantive `fix`/`feat` and release-description guards remain. A draft release PR is an explicit hold: the scheduled run never arms it, and converting an armed release PR to draft disables auto-merge. It rechecks the draft state, labels, head SHA, and release-window state immediately before enabling auto-merge.

Validation: `actionlint .github/workflows/auto-merge-release.yml`; `shellcheck` on the workflow shell step. GitHub CI is running for this revision.

Scheduled arming still requires the commit **`release-window`** status to be **pending** (unless **`release-now`**); actual merge waits for the existing **03:00 Central** window and other checks.

Tightens discovery to **`jdx:release` → `main`**, checks out **`default_branch`**, and **re-validates** draft state, head SHA, labels, and release-window before enabling auto-merge. **Removes** the **7-day-since-last-tag** gate; **keeps** fix/feat-since-tag and non-empty PR body guards.

title: fix(task): let tasks shut down after a single Ctrl-C
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/391
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A single Ctrl-C during `mise run` could make mise exit right away and kill tasks that were still cleaning up. The shell prompt came back while child processes were still stopping, so their output landed on top of it.

This happened in three situations:

- **A task runs `mise run` itself.** The inner mise got the SIGINT twice, once from the terminal and once from the outer mise, and took the second as a repeated Ctrl-C.
- **A task needs a single SIGINT to shut down cleanly.** `docker compose up` stops gracefully on the first SIGINT and force-quits on the second.
- **A task exits non-zero on SIGINT** instead of dying by it, as `aws-vault` and many CLIs do. mise counted that as an ordinary failure and sent SIGTERM to the other tasks mid-shutdown.

Repro:

```toml
[tasks.slow]
run = "trap '' INT; sleep 6; date > done.txt"

[tasks.outer]
run = "mise run slow"
```

Run `mise run outer` in a terminal and press Ctrl-C once.

- **Before:** mise exits immediately with status 130, `slow` is killed, and `done.txt` is never written.
- **After:** mise waits for `slow` to finish, writes `done.txt`, then exits with status 130.

A second Ctrl-C still force-quits, as before.

### Changes

- `CmdLineRunner::kill_all` no longer re-sends SIGINT to children that share mise's process group when that SIGINT has already reached them: from the terminal, or from an outer mise that owns the group and signals all of it with `killpg`. Children in their own process group or session are still signalled.
- On Linux, mise records where each SIGINT came from, so a `kill -INT <mise pid>` that reaches mise alone is still passed on to every task. The record is only ever set by a SIGINT and cleared by `kill_all`, so a second SIGINT arriving first cannot hide it.
- The per-command signal forwarder no longer forwards SIGINT; `kill_all` from the Ctrl-C handler already does.
- A Ctrl-C no longer triggers the "task failed, killing siblings" SIGTERM. The SIGINT handler marks the run as cancelled itself, so the check doesn't lag behind a task that took the same SIGINT and exited non-zero first.

### Behavior notes

- **macOS:** macOS reports a terminal Ctrl-C and `kill -INT` identically, so a `kill -INT <mise pid>` sent while mise is in the terminal's foreground is no longer passed to children in mise's process group. Ctrl-C is unaffected.
- **Nested mise:** a `kill -INT` sent to a nested `mise run` alone is not passed on to its tasks, because a nested mise assumes its outer mise's group-wide signal already reached them.
- **Linux:** `kill -INT -<pgid>` and `kill -INT <pid>` look the same to mise, so a SIGINT sent to the whole group can reach children twice. A duplicate beats a lost signal that leaves mise waiting on a task.

### Testing

New e2e tests, all driving real signals: a pty Ctrl-C through a nested `mise run`, the same nesting with no terminal (the task must see exactly one SIG

title: fix(shim): forward Node IPC through Windows shims
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/390
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Native exe-mode shims on Windows now preserve libuv's inherited CRT stdio table across the shim → mise → node process chain. Node processes launched through `node.exe` with `stdio: [..., 'ipc']` can exchange JSON IPC messages and fully disconnect the channel before the Node child exits.

Before this change, a Node parent could start `%LOCALAPPDATA%\mise\shims\node.exe`, but its child never received an IPC message and the parent waited indefinitely. The shim forwards the startup data libuv uses for the extra descriptor, and mise preserves it when launching the selected `node.exe`.

The specialized Windows launcher activates only for a validated Node IPC descriptor and a native `node.exe`; other Node spawns and `.cmd`/`.bat` tools keep their normal process path. It also preserves standard executable resolution for bare and extensionless-path `mise` commands.

The Windows e2e regression test forces exe shim mode, starts the copied `node.exe` shim from a Node parent with an IPC stdio entry, and asserts a JSON ping/pong plus that the parent observes IPC disconnect before it releases the still-running target.

Scope: this fixes JSON IPC messages. Windows socket/server-handle transfer through the channel still targets the original shim PID and remains a separate limitation.

Validation: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`; `git diff --check`; and the full exact-head CI suite, including Windows build, lint, unit, and e2e plus the aggregate `test-ci` gate. No build or test ran on the credential-bearing development host.

Fixes #13901.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Windows process creation and inherited handle/CRT cleanup on a narrow Node IPC path; mistakes could affect shim dispatch or handle lifetime, but activation is gated on `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` and pipe validation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **Node `stdio: 'ipc'` hanging or failing** when a Windows parent spawns the **`node.exe` exe shim** (shim → `mise x` → real `node.exe`). Ordinary `std::process::Command` rebuilds `STARTUPINFO` and drops libuv’s inherited CRT descriptor table keyed by `NODE_CHANNEL_FD`.
> 
> On Windows, **`mise-shim`** and **`mise exec`** now detect a validated Node IPC pipe in the parent startup data and launch the next hop with **`CreateProcessW` while preserving that startup info**. The shim path also injects **`__MISE_SHIM_PATH`** via a child-only Unicode environment block (no `set_var`). Non-IPC spawns and non-`node.exe` tools keep the existing launch path.
> 
> Adds **`mise-util::windows_process`** for the main binary and a **self-contained duplicate in `mise-shim`** (no extra crate dependency), plus a **Windows e2e** that pings IPC through the exe shim and checks disconnect before exit.
>

title: docs: stop the showreel's dark gradients from banding into rings
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/389
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The landing-page showreel showed faint, slightly rainbow-tinted rings in its dark backgrounds. They were sharpest around the chef's glow on the end card, where they swept outward as the glow swelled ("blooming"), and in the stage lamp at the open and during the chef morph. This change removes them, so those areas now look smooth and grainy as drawn.

**Cause.** The lamp, the vignette and the glows are huge, soft gradients on a near-black stage. Each one climbs only 5 to 12 levels of 8-bit colour across hundreds of pixels, so every level is a 40–100 px band. The overlay film grain hides those steps in the drawn frames, but it was re-seeded 24 times a second. New noise on every frame is something x264 cannot predict from the previous frame, so at the reel's bitrate it rounded the grain away and the bare steps came back as rings.

The tint comes from red, green and blue rounding to the next level at slightly different radii. Video then stores those small colour differences more coarsely than brightness. The rings move because the glows' radius and strength are animated.

Ruled out by experiment on lossless frames: the JPEG frame capture, the colour-range conversion, and x264's deblocking.

**Fix.** The grain is now still: the same pattern on every frame. `fx.grain` reads the `STAGE_FX.grain.fps` setting, which existed but was unused, and that setting is now 0. The encoder carries a still pattern from frame to frame almost for free, so it survives the encode and keeps dithering the steps. The encoder settings are unchanged.

Measured on 60 fps drafts of the three worst sections (dark 8×8 luma blocks, sampled every half second):

| Section | Perfectly flat dark blocks | Mean run of identical luma | Video bitrate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| End card | 83.8% → 26.4% | 19.1 → 3.4 px | 256 → 365 kb/s |
| Open | 83.2% → 32.7% | 25.1 → 3.9 px | 621 → 687 kb/s |
| Morph | 78.8% → 43.8% | 21.3 → 7.1 px | 718 → 758 kb/s |

The lossless frames measure about 1.6 px. A full-reel 60 fps measurement of the same change put the shipped `showreel.mp4` at 35.1 → 38.5 MB (+14% video bitrate). The 30 fps reel grew 4%.

**Look.** The grain no longer flickers. Over the end card's final hold, only the rising motes move now. `ART.md`, `STORYBOARD.md` and the end card's comments are updated to match.

Not done here: drawing the glows as native canvas gradients, which Chromium dithers and the current scaled sprite does not, would further reduce the faint colour fringing. It makes no difference after the encode on its own.

`aube run typecheck:showreel` passes; `aube run test:showreel`: 166 pass, 1 skipped (needs a capture run not on this machine).

title: docs: replace the landing-page showreel's synthesized music with a Suno track
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/388
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The seven-minute showreel on the landing page (mise.jdx.dev/#showreel) gets new music. Its soundtrack used to be a band synthesized in Web Audio, with an act-by-act operetta, organ, reggae and rock arrangement and the old theme song's chorus line sung over the end card. It is now a calm instrumental deep-house track made in Suno, "mise screenreel". The track plays from the first frame to the last, under the same synthesized sound effects as before.

What a viewer hears:

- **New music, same sound effects.** Every on-screen accent still has its own synthesized sound, timed to the recorded terminal sessions: printer ticks, tears, stamps, slams, clicks and stingers. The music dips under the accents that ask for it.
- **An arrangement that follows the acts.** Each act opens on a drop or a change. Environments sits on the track's drumless breakdown. The music rests for the screen wipe at 5:50–5:54. The quiet stretch and the near-silent breath come before the clone. The loudest groove lands on the climax at 6:38. The track's own outro plays under the end card.
- **No sung line on the end card.** "mise-en-place" writes on, and the tagline, the install command, mise.jdx.dev and the glint arrive on an eighth-beat grid. They take the same times, rounded, that the vocal used to set. A few light effects mark the name, the URL and the glint.
- **Pitched effects follow the new track's chords** (F minor, C minor, B♭, and F with no third where the track leans major). The old key change on `cd ../dashboard` is gone.

Measured on a full local audio render with ffmpeg `ebur128`: the whole reel is -17.0 LUFS integrated with a true peak of -2.8 dBTP before the AAC encode. That is the target the old mix had. By act:

| Act | Loudness |
| --- | --- |
| Acts I–VI | -17.6 to -15.8 LUFS |
| Environments | -20 LUFS |
| Quiet stretch before the clone | -23 LUFS |
| Breath | -35 LUFS |
| Climax | -13.9 LUFS |

## How it's built

- **The bed.** `score/bed.opus` is the track, already arranged on reel time: 436.000 s of 48 kHz stereo Ogg Opus, 11.5 MB, pinned by sha256 in `score/bed.ts`. Suno rendered it at an exact 120 BPM, so it is trimmed to its first downbeat and not stretched: every 2 s bar of the bed lines up with two of the reel's 60 BPM beats. `score/BED.md` records where it came from, how it was arranged, the measurements, and who owns it.
- **Playback.** The renderer reads the bed, checks its hash and format, and passes it to the headless page in chunks of 20 MiB or less. The page decodes it with `decodeAudioData`. `audio.ts` plays it on the music bus, starting on an exact frame, so a draft rendered from the middle of the reel plays the same samples as a full render. The bus keeps the ducking, the section fader and the master limiter. A cross-correlation of the full render against the decoded bed finds it at lag 0.
- **Removed.**
  - The synthesized band: every se

--- .gitignore (+2/-1)
@@ -40,6 +40,7 @@ comment.md
 
 .claude/settings.local.json
 
-# showreel capture runs (mise run docs:showreel-capture)
+# showreel capture runs (mise run docs:showreel-capture) and the bed fit tool (docs:showreel-bed)
 /docs/.vitepress/showreel-capture/out/
 /docs/.vitepress/showreel-capture/__pycache__/
+/docs/.vitepress/showreel-bed/__pycache__/
--- docs/.vitepress/showreel-bed/README.md (+167/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,167 @@
+# The showreel's bed
+
+The showreel's music is one instrumental track, the bed, which plays under the
+sound effects from the first frame to the last. The page plays
+`docs/.vitepress/theme/showreel/score/bed.opus` on its music bus, which ducks
+under the sound effects that ask for it and follows each section's level, so the file has to be
+arranged on reel time already:
+
+- Ogg Opus, 48 kHz, stereo
+- decoded sample 0 is reel time 0
+- exactly 436.000 s (20,928,000 frames): the whole reel, end card included,
+  with the bed's own ending
+- 120 BPM 4/4, every bar line on the reel's grid: a bar is 2.000 s (96,000
+  frames), two of the reel's 60 BPM beats
+
+`score/bed.ts` pins the file by its sha256, so the bed changes only in a commit
+that changes both.
+
+`mise run docs:showreel-bed` (`xtasks/docs/showreel-bed`, which runs `bed.py`
+here) turns a downloaded track into that file. It is not part of the render;
+the render cache key covers `bed.opus` itself. The committed bed is "mise
+screenreel", jdx's Suno track, arranged by `bed.toml`; `score/BED.md` records
+how it was built.
+
+## Needs
+
+- ffmpeg with libopus
+- the Rubber Band CLI: `brew install rubberband` on macOS, or
+  `apt install rubberband-cli` on Debian and Ubuntu. `build` checks for it
+  even when the track is already on the grid and it is not run
+- uv, which runs `bed.py` with its dependencies (librosa, numpy, scipy,
+  soundfile, soxr) from its inline metadata. If no uv is on PATH, the task
+  runs one through `mise exec`
+
+## Workflow
+
+1. **Generate and download.** Ask Suno for an instrumental at 120 BPM in 4/4,
+   F minor if you can get it (the sound effects' chord-aware stingers are in F
+   minor), six or seven minutes long (the arrangement repeats or cuts bars to
+   fill 7:16), calm, with an ending that rings out. Download the WAV, not the
+   MP3, and record its sha256 before moving it (`score/BED.md`'s provenance
+   table).
+
+2. **Look at the reel and the track.**
+
+   ```sh
+   mise run docs:showreel-bed -- sections
+   mise run docs:showreel-bed -- analyse ~/Downloads/bed.wav
+   ```
+
+   `sections` lists every section's start and length in bed bars. `analyse`
+   prints the track's tempo (tracked, then fitted to one constant tempo, with
+   the residuals and the drift every 30 s), where bar 0's downbeat is, the key
+   and the semitone shift to F minor, and a chord guess for every source bar.
+   If the downbeat is wrong (the phase scores are a close call, or bar 1 sounds
+   off), pass `--first-downbeat SECONDS`. If the tempo read is wrong, pass
+   `--bpm`. If the track drifts (the p95 residual is over 20 ms), try
+   `--map detected`, which pins each bar to its own detected downbeat instead of
+   the constant-tempo fit.
+
+   Suno appears to render on an exact tempo clock: the beats of "mise
+   screenreel" sit within a few milliseconds of an exact 120 BPM grid (median 1
+   ms, p95 3 ms). The unpinned fit misreads such a clock: a plain `analyse` of
+   "mise screenreel" read 119.72 BPM, a p95 residual of 202 ms and a first
+   downbeat at 1.434 s, and warned to try `--map detected`. For a Suno track,
+   run `analyse --bpm 120` instead (it read the first downbeat at 0.105 s, p95
+   3 ms), and the fix for that warning is `--bpm 120`, not `--map detected`.
+   Then pass `--bpm 120` and the first downbeat it found
+   (`--first-downbeat 0.105` there) to `build`: every bar line is
+   then on its frame already, and the build trims the track to its first
+   downbeat instead of stretching it. A fitted tempo a ten-thousandth of a BPM
+   off would put the last bar lines more than a frame out, and the whole track
+   would be stretched for nothing.
+
+3. **Arrange.** A spec maps source bars to reel bars. `bed.toml`, the default
+   `--spec`, is the arrangement of one particular track, the one its comments
+   name ("mise screenreel"): its bar numbers mean nothing for another. For a
+   new track, write a spec of its own, starting from the generic block at the
+   end of `bed.toml` (the track as it comes, from its first downbeat, ringing
+   out at its end), and loop or cut bars, using `sections` and the chord list
+   to put the changes and the ending where they belong (the end card is reel
+   bars 211 to 218). The file's comments describe every field.
+
+4. **Build.**
+
+   ```sh
+   mise run docs:showreel-bed -- build ~/Downloads/bed.wav --spec my-bed.toml --semitones auto
+   ```
+
+   This stretches the track onto the grid (Rubber Band R3, with a time map from
+   source downbeat k to frame k × 96000, plus a pitch shift if asked for),
+   unless every bar line is already within a frame of its place and no pitch
+   shift is asked for: then it only trims the track to its first downbeat
+   (R3 at ratio 1 would still resynthesise every sample). For a track on the
+   grid:
+
+   ```sh
+   mise run docs:showreel-bed -- build ~/Downloads/bed.wav --bpm 120 --first-downbeat 0.105
+   ```
+
+   Then it arranges the track, sets one gain to `--lufs` with the sample peak at
+   or below `--peak` (default -3 dBFS), and encodes Opus at 192 kb/s. The
+   default, -32 LUFS integrated, is staged against the master chain in
+   `audio.ts`, whose makeup lifts the bed about 11 dB: "mise screenreel" at -32
+   LUFS and `BED.gainDb` 0.7 put the whole reel at -17.0 LUFS, the target, where
+   a bed at -20 LUFS put it at -11.6 with the limiter clamped throughout. So
+   `bed.wav` is quiet to listen to on its own; trim the level in the render with
+   `BED.gainDb`, not here. Then it verifies the file it wrote. It decodes it,
+   checks the length frame for frame, and tracks the beats again. It measures
+   each bar line by its own onset: the strongest attack within 40 ms of the grid
+   line, counted only if it is a clear one, a rise of at least 20 dB over 4 ms
+   (a kick or a click; a pad's or an arpeggio's swell falls anywhere). A fill or
+   a pickup still lands near some bar lines, so it fails on the median and the
+   90th percentile of the deviations, not the worst bar: over 5 ms median or 15
+   ms at the 90th percentile (`--max-median-ms`, `--max-p90-ms`), or fewer than
+   8 bar lines with a clear onset. It checks that the bed is silent by 436.0 s,
+   and prints a chord chart per section as `harmony.ts` changes. Every
+   intermediate file stays in the work directory it prints: `stretched.wav`
+   (only when it stretched), `arranged.wav`, `bed.wav`, `analysis.json`,
+   `chords.json`.
+
+5. **Listen.** Listen to `bed.wav` in the work directory, especially the joins
+   and the ending. Then hear it under the sound effects in a draft render. The
+   renderer checks the file against `BED.sha256`, so paste the hash the build
+   printed into `score/bed.ts` first:
+
+   ```sh
+   cp <work>/bed.opus docs/.vitepress/theme/showreel/score/bed.opus
+   aube run showreel:video --audio-only /tmp/reel.wav --from 400 --until 436
+   ```
+
+   Change the spec or the overrides and build again until it sits right.
+
+6. **Commit once.** Commit `score/bed.opus` and `score/bed.ts`, with its
+   `sha256` line, together. Do not commit the WAV. With the same tool versions,
+   the same WAV, spec and options give the same bytes, so a rebuild reproduces
+   the pinned hash; record the versions in `score/BED.md`'s provenance table.
+   The Python packages are pinned by date (`exclude-newer` in `bed.py`'s
+   inline metadata), but ffmpeg with libopus and Rubber Band come from PATH,
+   and a different version of either can change the bytes (Rubber Band's
+   only when the track was stretched). To check a
+   committed file again, run:
+
+   ```sh
+   mise run docs:showreel-bed -- verify docs/.vitepress/theme/showreel/score/bed.opus
+   ```
+
+## Notes
+
+- **Resampling.** Homebrew's ffmpeg has no soxr resampler, so ffmpeg only
+  decodes. Resampling to 48 kHz uses soxr's Python binding at its very high
+  quality setting.
+- **The time map leaves out `0 0`.** With that line in the map, Rubber Band
+  4.0.0's R3 engine plays the whole first bar at ratio 1. On a 118.7 BPM click
+  track, every later bar line came out about 21 ms late. Without the line, every
+  bar line came out within a millisecond.
+- **Joins.** Where one segment ends on the bar line where the next starts, they
+  crossfade with equal power over `crossfade_ms`, ending on the bar line. The
+  incoming segment fades in over the source audio just before its first bar, so
+  its downbeat lands at full level.
+- **Tested on a synthetic track.** The input was a 300 s, 44.1 kHz click track
+  at 118.7 BPM: first downbeat at 0.37 s, an accented click on each bar, a
+  plain click on each beat, and a quiet Fm–D♭–E♭–C pad. Its 148 bars were
+  looped to fill 218. The fit
+  found 118.7000 BPM and a downbeat at 0.371 s. The verify pass measured every
+  bar line within 3 ms of the grid (median 1 ms). Measured directly from the
+  waveform, the clicks were within 2.3 ms.

title: ci: build real Windows releases on a dedicated release runner
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/387
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Real Windows x64 releases can now be built on a dedicated release runner and account instead of the shared CI runner, so the binary that gets signed is not built on a machine where pull-request code has run. Nothing changes until a new repository variable is set.

## Why

`build-tarball-windows` is the job that produces the shipped `mise.exe`. It uses no secrets itself (signing happens afterwards in the `release` job on a hosted runner), so the risk this closes is build integrity: on the shared runner, a pull-request job from a trusted author shares an account, a Rust toolchain, compiler proxies and a build cache with whatever builds the release.

## What changes

- **Routing.** The release PR's dry run keeps using the shared trusted runner (`WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED=true`). A real release uses `[self-hosted, jdx-win-release-v1]` when the new repository variable `WINDOWS_RELEASE_SELF_HOSTED` is `true` and the run starts from a `v*` tag (push or dispatch) or from `main`, `release` or `mise`, the refs that runner accepts. A dispatch from any other branch builds on the hosted runner instead of failing on the runner's own refusal. Either variable unset falls back to `windows-latest`, so a release never queues for a machine that is off, and the new variable ships off.
- **No release build uses the mbx cache.** This removes the `MBX_DISABLE` plumbing and the `mbx` switch from the release workflow and `scripts/build-tarball.ps1` that came in with the runner PR. The dry run rehearses the real build, so both use plain cargo from a clean build, as the Linux and macOS release jobs do. The fat-LTO link of `mise`, which is most of the time, was never cacheable.
- **Real releases never use the shared runner.** With only `WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED` set, a tag push builds on the hosted runner, not the shared one.

## The runner side (not in this diff)

- A separate local account that cannot log in interactively, over RDP or over the network, with its own Rust toolchain, temp directory and runner directory. The shared runner's account has no access to any of them, and the release account cannot write the shared runner's.
- The runner's binaries and configuration are read-only to its account (only its work and log folders are writable), and runner self-update is off, so a build step cannot rewrite the runner or its hook.
- A host-side job-started hook, set as a per-service environment value the account cannot change, accepts only `release.yml` for `jdx/mise`, started by `jdx` or `mise-en-dev`, on a `v*` tag push or a dispatch from a `v*` tag, `main`, `release` or `mise`. It refuses pull requests, schedules and everything else.
- The shared runners now also refuse real releases, so a routing mistake cannot ship a release from the shared account.

## Verification

- The routing expression, checked against these trigger scenarios (dry run, fork and untrusted PRs, tag push,

+    # gets signed is not built where pull-request code has run (repository variable

     strategy:
       fail-fast: false

--- scripts/build-tarball.ps1 (+2/-8)
@@ -38,17 +38,11 @@ if (-not $Env:CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO -and $MemoryGB -lt 48) {
 }
 Write-Host ("LTO: {0} ({1:N0} GB RAM)" -f $(if ($Env:CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO) { $Env:CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO } else { "fat (profile default)" }), $MemoryGB)
 
-# Only the release PR's dry run may use the shared mbx build cache (release.yml
-# leaves MBX_DISABLE=0 there). A real release sets MBX_DISABLE=1 and always
-# compiles from scratch with plain cargo. Hosted runners have no mbx.
-$Cargo = "cargo"

-
