title: ci: limit each contributor to one open draft PR
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/357
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stops an outside contributor from leaving several draft pull requests open at once. GitHub has no setting that caps a contributor's open PRs, so this adds a small workflow that enforces it.

When a draft PR is opened, reopened, or converted back to a draft, the workflow counts the author's other open drafts. If they already have one, it closes the new draft with a comment:

> Thanks for the contribution! To keep review manageable, this repository allows each contributor 1 open draft pull request(s) at a time, and you already have #123.
>
> Please finish it (mark it ready for review) or close it, then reopen this pull request.

- Owners, members, and collaborators are exempt, and so are bots (Renovate, etc.), so this only affects outside contributors.
- When two drafts are opened at the same moment, only the newer one is closed.
- Ready-for-review PRs are never counted or closed.
- The limit is `max_drafts` (default 1) in the caller.

The logic lives in the shared [jdx/workflows](https://github.com/jdx/workflows) repo and is pinned to v1.0.0, so Renovate will keep it current. The trigger is `pull_request_target` because fork PRs only get a write token there; the workflow never checks out or runs the PR's code, and the `zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]` in the file records that.

Validation: actionlint and zizmor (including the online audits) pass, and the decision logic was exercised against a stubbed `gh` for the open/reopen/convert/exempt/race cases. It has not yet run against a real outside contributor's PR.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.284.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> New CI policy workflow with minimal permissions and a pinned reusable action; `pull_request_target` is documented and scoped to closing excess drafts without running PR code.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a **draft-limit** GitHub Actions workflow so outside contributors can only keep **one open draft PR** at a time. On `opened`, `reopened`, or `converted_to_draft`, it calls the pinned reusable workflow in `jdx/workflows` (v1.0.0) with `max_drafts: 1`; if the author already has another draft, the workflow comments and closes the extra one.
> 
> It runs on **`pull_request_target`** so fork PRs get token scope to comment and close, with job-level **`pull-requests: write`** only and no checkout of the PR branch. Maintainers, collaborators, and bots are handled in the shared workflow (not in this diff).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 2b050cf4fdea89aaf96acb1a400b33f4ae7a29e7. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

author: jdx
diff:
--- .github/workflows/draft-limit.yml (+22/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+name: draft-limit
+
+# Closes a draft pull request when its author already has another open draft,
+# so an outside contributor can't leave a pile of drafts to triage. Maintainers
+# and bots are exempt. See jdx/workflows for the workflow implementation.
+
+on:
+  # Fork pull requests only get a write token under pull_request_target, which
+  # the shared workflow needs to comment and close. It never checks out or runs
+  # the pull request's code.
+  pull_request_target: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers]
+    types: [opened, reopened, converted_to_draft]
+
+permissions: {}
+
+jobs:
+  draft-limit:
+    permissions:
+      pull-requests: write # comment on and close the extra draft
+    uses: jdx/workflows/.github/workflows/draft-limit.yml@5583759b56aa6c1bee8a35b2597c1b8ccf3626a4 # v1.0.0
+    with:
+      max_drafts: 1

title: fix(dotfiles): restart the history watcher after mise is upgraded
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/355
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13844.

After upgrading mise, the `history-watch` service kept running the old binary. When the new CLI wrote a manifest field the old watcher didn't know (`allow_plaintext`), every capture failed with `unknown field ...` until the service was restarted by hand, and edits in the meantime weren't saved.

The watcher now checks once a minute whether the mise executable it started from was replaced. Once the replacement has held still for two checks, it saves what is pending and exits with a failure status. The service manager (systemd `Restart=on-failure`, launchd `KeepAlive`) then starts it on the new version. A watcher started by hand with `mise dot watch` stops and has to be started again.

Reporting: `mise dot status` no longer says `automatic capture: running (edits are saved automatically)` while captures are failing, and `mise dot track` warns instead of printing "watcher running" when the last capture failed:

```
automatic capture: running but failing (edits are not being saved until a capture succeeds).
```

This only helps watchers that already run this version. The watcher in the issue predates it, so the next upgrade is the first one it protects.

Not addressed: the transient checkpoints seen on restart (31 files removed, then re-added), which the issue has no repro for.

Tests: unit tests for replacement detection; `test_dotfiles_watch` and `test_dotfiles_retrack` e2e pass. `mise run lint` and workspace clippy fail on this branch's base from an existing `unreachable_code` warning in `crates/mise-util/src/http.rs`; nothing in the changed files warns.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.284.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes long-running watcher lifecycle and exit codes on upgrade, which affects automatic dotfile capture until the service restarts; mis-detection could stop the watcher or hide real failures, though two-check settling and unit tests mitigate that.
> 
> **Overview**
> After a mise upgrade, the **history watcher** could keep running the old binary and fail every capture (e.g. unknown manifest fields) until someone restarted the service manually. The watcher now **polls every minute** whether the executable it started from was replaced; once the change is stable across two checks, it **flushes pending work and exits with status 1** so systemd/launchd restarts it on the new binary. Manual `mise dot watch` exits the same way and must be started again.
> 
> If the binary path disappears without a replacement, the process **stays up** but sets **`executable_gone`** in `health.json`; **`mise dot status`**, **`mise doctor`**, and enrollment **`report()`** surface that and point at **`mise bootstrap services apply`**.
> 
> **Health reporting** no longer treats a predecessor’s

title: feat(config): include a shared config file from a remote git or OCI source
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/354
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Teams that want every repo on the same tool versions, env or hooks today have to copy that config around. `include` in `mise.toml` now pulls it from a shared, remote file:

```toml
include = [
  "git::https://github.com/myorg/platform.git//mise.toml?ref=main",
  "oci::ghcr.io/myorg/platform-config@sha256:0f1e2d3c...",
]

[tools]
node = "22"   # the file's own entries override the included ones
```

A `git::` include points at a `.toml` file; an `oci::` include points at an artifact with a `mise.toml` at its root. Requested in discussion #13838, which asked for the `task_config.includes` behavior for whole config files.

## Behavior

- **A fragment is merged into the file that includes it**, so it never appears as a config file of its own and trust, config root, relative paths (such as `_.file`), `{{ config_root }}`, safe-mode scoping and the lockfile are all the including file's. It may contain `[tools]`, `[tool_alias]`, `[env]`, `[vars]`, `[hooks]`, `[alias]`, `[shell_alias]`, `[plugins]`, `[wrappers]` and `min_version` (enforced). Its entries rank below the including file's own; a later `include` entry overrides an earlier one. Hooks of the same type from both files all run (the shared ones first), version aliases merge per name, and the including file's PATH entries come before the shared ones.
- **Trust is the including file's.** `include` is not a trust-exempt key, so an untrusted repo cannot make mise fetch a URL when you `cd` into it, and safe mode never fetches for project config. Outside paranoid mode trust is by path, so a trusted config already runs whatever its repository holds after the next `git pull`; a fragment that moves is no different.
- **Paranoid mode needs a pin.** Paranoid mode binds trust to content, so there an include must be a full commit sha or an OCI digest, which the including file's hash then covers. A branch or tag is an error.
- **Cached.** A fragment is fetched once into `MISE_CACHE_DIR/config-includes`. A sha or digest is never fetched again. A branch, tag or OCI tag is refreshed once it is older than `fetch_remote_versions_cache` (1h), and only by commands that look at remote versions (`install`, `up`, `use`, `config`, ...); hook-env, `mise ls`, `mise exec`, shims and offline mode use the cache without checking. If a refresh fails or returns something that cannot load with this mise (an unsupported section, or a `min_version` it does not meet), the cached copy keeps working with a warning, and the next attempt waits a full TTL. A cold cache with no network is an error. hook-env watches the cache files, so a refresh reloads an open shell once and then settles.
- **Anything else is an error, not a silent no-op:** `include` (no nesting); `[settings]` and the monorepo keys, which are read before an include can be resolved; `[tasks]`, `task_config` and `task_templates`, which are discovered from files (share tas

diff:
--- docs/configuration.md (+21/-0)
@@ -284,6 +284,27 @@ Examples:
 node = { version = "22", postinstall = "corepack enable" }
 ```
 
+### `include` - Share config from a remote file {#include}
+
+`include` pulls a remote config file into this one, so an organization can publish a baseline and have every repo use it:
+
+```toml
+include = [
+  "git::https://github.com/myorg/platform.git//mise.toml?ref=main",
+  "oci::ghcr.io/myorg/platform-config@sha256:0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f00f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0",
+]
+
+[tools]
+node = "22" # this file's own entries override the included ones
+```
+
+A `git::` include points at a `.toml` file; an `oci::` include points at an artifact with a `mise.toml` at its root. The fragment ranks just below the file that includes it and above lower-precedence configs. It is merged into the including file, and may contain `[tools]`, `[tool_alias]`, `[env]`, `[vars]`, `[hooks]`, `[alias]`, `[shell_alias]`, `[plugins]`, `[wrappers]` and `min_version`. Relative paths (such as `_.file`) and `{{ config_root }}` resolve against the including file, its tools are locked in the including file's lockfile, and its `min_version` is enforced. A later entry in `include` overrides an earlier one, and the including file overrides them all.
+
+- **Trust is the including file's.** `include` is not trust-exempt, so an untrusted repo cannot make mise fetch a URL when you `cd` into it, and [safe mode](/configuration/settings#safe) never fetches for project config. Once trusted, the fragment runs with that trust, like a `mise.toml` that changes on `git pull`.
+- **Paranoid mode needs a pin.** [Paranoid mode](/configuration/settings#paranoid) binds trust to file content, so there an include must be a full commit sha (`?ref=<40 hex digits>`) or an OCI digest (`@sha256:…`). The including file's hash then covers it.
+- **Cached.** A fragment is read on every config load, so it is fetched once and kept under `MISE_CACHE_DIR`. A commit sha or OCI digest is never fetched again. A branch, tag or OCI tag is refreshed once the cache is older than [`fetch_remote_versions_cache`](/configuration/settings#fetch_remote_versions_cache) (one hour by default). Only commands that look at remote versions, such as `mise install`, `mise up` and `mise use`, refresh; hook-env, `mise ls`, `mise exec` and shims, and offline mode, use the cached copy without checking. If a refresh fails, or returns something that cannot load with this mise (an unsupported section, or a `min_version` it does not meet), mise keeps the cached copy and warns; on a cold cache that is an error. `mise cache clear` forces a refetch.
+- **Anything else is an error, not a silent no-op.** That includes `include` (no nesting); `[settings]` and the monorepo keys, which are read before an include can be resolved; `[tasks]`, `task_config` and `task_templates`, which are discovered from files (share tasks with [`task_config.includes`](/tasks/task-configuration#task_config.includes)); and the system sections such as `[dotfiles]` and `[daemons]`.
+
 ### `[tool_config]` - Config-root-scoped tool policy
 
 `[tool_config]` applies policy to tools declared by configs sharing the same
--- e2e/config/test_config_include_remote (+248/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,248 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# `include` merges the [tools] of a pinned remote fragment into a config file.
+#
+# Uses `crane registry serve` (an in-memory OCI registry) on a loopback port and
+# `crane append` to publish the fragment as a tar layer.
+
+mise install crane@latest >/dev/null 2>&1
+
+find_available_port() {
+  python3 -c "import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(('127.0.0.1',0)); print(s.getsockname()[1]); s.close()"
+}
+
+REGISTRY_PID=""
+cleanup() {
+  if [[ -n ${REGISTRY_PID:-} ]]; then
+    kill "$REGISTRY_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+    wait "$REGISTRY_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+  fi
+}
+trap cleanup EXIT
+
+PORT="$(find_available_port)"
+REGISTRY="127.0.0.1:$PORT"
+mise x crane@latest -- crane registry serve --address "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
+REGISTRY_PID=$!
+for _ in $(seq 1 50); do
+  if curl -fsS "http://$REGISTRY/v2/" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+    break
+  fi
+  sleep 0.2
+done
+assert_succeed "curl -fsS http://$REGISTRY/v2/"
+
+# publish <dir> <name> prints the digest of the artifact it pushed
+publish() {
+  local dir="$1" ref="$REGISTRY/e2e/$2:v1"
+  tar -czf "$dir.tar.gz" -C "$dir" .
+  mise x crane@latest -- crane append --oci-empty-base -f "$dir.tar.gz" -t "$ref" >/dev/null
+  mise x crane@latest -- crane digest "$ref"
+}
+
+mkdir -p base env-fragment bad-fragment task-fragment min-fragment
+cat >base/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+tiny = "1"
+shellcheck = "0.9"
+TOML
+cat >env-fragment/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[env]
+FROM_FRAGMENT = "1"
+OVERRIDDEN = "fragment"
+ROOT = "{{ config_root }}"
+_.file = ".fragment.env"
+_.path = ["frag-bin"]
+TOML
+echo "FROM_DOTENV=yes" >.fragment.env
+cat >bad-fragment/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[settings]
+experimental = true
+TOML
+cat >min-fragment/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+min_version = "2099.1.1"
+TOML
+cat >task-fragment/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tasks.a]
+run = "echo a"
+TOML
+BASE="$(publish base base)"
+ENV_FRAGMENT="$(publish env-fragment envfrag)"
+BAD_FRAGMENT="$(publish bad-fragment badfrag)"
+TASK_FRAGMENT="$(publish task-fragment taskfrag)"
+MIN_FRAGMENT="$(publish min-fragment minfrag)"
+
+version_of() {
+  mise ls --json | jq -r --arg t "$1" '.[$t][0].requested_version // empty'
+}
+source_of() {
+  mise ls --json | jq -r --arg t "$1" '.[$t][0].source.path // empty'
+}
+# assert runs its command in a new bash
+export -f version_of source_of
+
+# The fragment's tools apply, and the including file's own entries win.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/base@$BASE"]
+
+[tools]
+shellcheck = "0.10"
+TOML
+assert "version_of tiny" "1"
+assert "version_of shellcheck" "0.10"
+# fragment tools are sourced from the including file, not from the cache
+assert "source_of tiny" "$PWD/mise.toml"
+
+# A git include is cloned and read like an OCI one. Only https and ssh URLs are
+# accepted, so rewrite a fake https host onto a local repository.
+git init -q gitsrc
+mkdir gitsrc/base
+cat >gitsrc/base/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+tiny = "3"
+TOML
+git -C gitsrc add base/mise.toml
+git -C gitsrc -c user.email=e2e@example.com -c user.name=e2e commit -q -m base
+GIT_SHA="$(git -C gitsrc rev-parse HEAD)"
+git -C gitsrc branch -M main
+git config --global url."file://$PWD/gitsrc".insteadOf "https://example.test/org/platform.git"
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["git::https://example.test/org/platform.git//base/mise.toml?ref=$GIT_SHA"]
+TOML
+assert "version_of tiny" "3"
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["git::https://example.test/org/platform.git//base/mise.toml?ref=main"]
+TOML
+assert "version_of tiny" "3"
+
+# A git include must point at a .toml file (checked before any fetch).
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["git::https://github.com/jdx/mise.git//tasks?ref=main"]
+TOML
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "must point at a .toml file"
+
+# A fragment is a whole config file: its env applies and the including file's
+# own entries win.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/envfrag@$ENV_FRAGMENT"]
+
+[env]
+OVERRIDDEN = "local"
+_.path = ["own-bin"]
+TOML
+assert "mise env --json | jq -r .FROM_FRAGMENT" "1"
+assert "mise env --json | jq -r .OVERRIDDEN" "local"
+# relative paths and config_root resolve against the including file, not the cache
+assert "mise env --json | jq -r .ROOT" "$PWD"
+assert "mise env --json | jq -r .FROM_DOTENV" "yes"
+# the including file's PATH entries come before the shared ones
+assert "mise env --json | jq -r '.PATH | split(\":\") | map(select(test(\"-bin$\"))) | map(sub(\".*/\"; \"\")) | join(\",\")'" "own-bin,frag-bin"
+
+# [settings] is read before an include can be resolved, so it is refused rather
+# than silently ignored.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/badfrag@$BAD_FRAGMENT"]
+TOML
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "is not supported in a config include"
+
+# A fragment's min_version is enforced like any config's.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/minfrag@$MIN_FRAGMENT"]
+TOML
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "2099.1.1"
+
+# Tasks are discovered from files, not loaded configs; point at task_config.includes.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/taskfrag@$TASK_FRAGMENT"]
+TOML
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "task_config.includes"
+
+# Paranoid mode binds trust to content, so an include must be pinned there.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/base@$BASE"]
+TOML
+export MISE_PARANOID=1
+assert_succeed "mise trust"
+assert "version_of tiny" "1"
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/base:v1"]
+TOML
+assert_succeed "mise trust"
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "must be pinned to a commit sha or an OCI digest"
+unset MISE_PARANOID
+
+# Once cached, a digest-pinned fragment loads without the registry, whatever
+# the ttl, and MISE_TASK_REMOTE_NO_CACHE does not force a refetch.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/base@$BASE"]
+TOML
+assert "version_of tiny" "1"
+
+# A tag is mutable: it is served from the cache until the ttl passes, then
+# refetched.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/base:v1"]
+TOML
+assert "version_of tiny" "1"
+cat >base/mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+tiny = "2"
+TOML
+publish base base >/dev/null
+assert "version_of tiny" "1"
+# `mise ls` (like hook-env, exec and shims) never refreshes; a command that
+# looks at remote versions does, once the cache is older than the ttl.
+assert "MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s version_of tiny" "1"
+assert_succeed "MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s mise config ls"
+assert "version_of tiny" "2"
+
+# hook-env notices a refreshed fragment once, then settles on the fast path.
+export MISE_ENV_CACHE=0
+eval "$(mise activate bash 2>/dev/null)"
+sleep 1
+assert_succeed "MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s mise config ls"
+output=$(mise hook-env -s bash 2>/dev/null)
+if [[ $output == *"__MISE_SESSION"* ]]; then
+  ok "a refreshed include bypasses the hook-env fast path once"
+else
+  fail "a refreshed include should bypass the fast path but got: '$output'"
+fi
+eval "$output"
+output=$(mise hook-env -s bash 2>&1)
+if [[ -z $output ]]; then
+  ok "hook-env takes the fast path after the refresh"
+else
+  fail "expected the fast path after the refresh but got: '$output'"
+fi
+
+# A refresh that is not usable never replaces the copy that works, whether it
+# is an unsupported section or a min_version this mise does not meet.
+cp min-fragment/mise.toml base/mise.toml
+publish base base >/dev/null
+assert_succeed "MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s mise config ls"
+assert "version_of tiny" "2"
+cp bad-fragment/mise.toml base/mise.toml
+publish base base >/dev/null
+assert_succeed "MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s mise config ls"
+assert "version_of tiny" "2"
+
+# When the refresh fails, the stale copy keeps working.
+kill "$REGISTRY_PID"
+wait "$REGISTRY_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
+REGISTRY_PID=""
+export MISE_FETCH_REMOTE_VERSIONS_CACHE=0s
+assert_succeed "mise config ls"
+assert "version_of tiny" "2"
+export MISE_TASK_REMOTE_NO_CACHE=1
+assert "version_of tiny" "2"
+# but a fragment that was never cached is an error
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+include = ["oci::$REGISTRY/e2e/other:v1"]
+TOML
+assert_fail_contains "mise ls" "failed to load config include"
+# safe mode never lets a project config fetch anything
+assert_succeed "MISE_SAFE=1 mise ls"
+# ...and never renders a templated include either
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+include = ["{{ exec(command='id') }}"]
+TOML
+assert_succeed "MISE_SAFE=1 mise ls"

title: ci(deps): remove the aube crates lock workflow
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/353
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Removes `.github/workflows/aube-crates-lock.yml` from #13824. It ran on Renovate's aube branch to refresh the other `aube-*` crates in `Cargo.lock` and the aube entry in `mise.lock`, but its first real run (on #13798) broke `lint` by rewriting the `mise.lock` specifier from `latest` to a pinned version. Patching around it from mise is the wrong layer.

The underlying problem is that published `aube` requires its sibling crates only as `^2`, so a Renovate bump of just `aube` and `aube-registry` leaves the siblings on the old release and the build fails. That is being fixed in aube itself, by publishing matching sibling version requirements, so no workflow is needed here.

The `renovate.json` rule description no longer refers to the workflow. No behavior change for mise users.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: 2.1.284.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI-only cleanup with a docs tweak in Renovate config; no application runtime or mise user behavior change described.
> 
> **Overview**
> Removes the **`aube-crates-lock`** GitHub Actions workflow that reacted to Renovate pushes on the grouped **`aube`** branch to run `cargo update` across all **`aube-*`** crates and bump **`mise.lock`**, then commit back with an app token.
> 
> The **Renovate** package rule for **`aube`** / **`aube-registry`** is unchanged in behavior (still grouped); only its description is shortened so it no longer documents that workflow or hosted-Renovate **`postUpgradeTasks`** limitations.
> 
> This drops CI automation that was meant to keep sibling crates aligned when Renovate only touched direct lock entries; upstream **`aube`** releases are expected to pin matching sibling versions instead.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 19e64d232f56d3d8d06251fc04c36463afc05e02. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Chores**
  * Removed the automated workflow that refreshed Cargo workspace lockfiles and the `mise.lock` entry when updating Aube.
  * Updated the Aube release-group description to clarify that `aube` and `aube-registry` are released and updated together.

-# aube entry in mise.lock must also match the embedded version.

-env:

-jobs:
-  aube-crates-lock:
-    # Only react to Renovate's own pushes (checked by the sender's immutable
-    # numeric id, not a spoofable login); our fix-up push has a different
-    # sender, so this also prevents self-retriggering.
-    if: github.event.sender.id == 29139614 # renovate[bot]
-    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
-    # Job-level, so a push whose job the `if` skips (e.g. aube-lock.yml's
-    # lockfile commit) never cancels a Renovate-triggered refresh in flight.
-    concurrency:
-      group: aube-crates-lock-${{ github.ref }}
-      cancel-in-progress: true
-    steps:
-      # No GITHUB_TOKEN fallback: it is read-only here and would not retrigger
-      # CI, so a missing App secret should fail this step loudly.
-      - name: Generate app token
-        id: app-token
-        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
-        with:
-          app-id: ${{ secrets.AUBE_LOCK_APP_ID }}
-          private-key: ${{ secrets.AUBE_LOCK_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
-          permission-contents: write
-      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
-        with:
-          persist-credentials: false
-      - uses: jdx/mise-action@c2a87611a18de5b3828c5652fe268e992400cb5c # v4.3.0
-        with:
-          install: false
-      - name: Refresh aube lockfiles
-        run: |
-          # the version Renovate selected is the one it wrote for the direct

-          version="$(awk '/^name = "aube"$/ { getline; gsub(/[^0-9.]/, "", $0); print; exit }' Cargo.lock)"
-          if [ -z "$version" ]; then
-            echo "::error::could not find the aube version in Cargo.lock"
-            exit 1
-          fi
-          echo "refreshing aube crates to ${version}"
-          cargo update \
-            -p aube -p aube-registry -p aube-codes -p aube-lockfile -p aube-settings \
-            -p aube-linker -p aube-manifest -p aube-resolver -p aube-runtime \
-            -p aube-scripts -p aube-store -p aube-util -p aube-workspace \
-            --precise "$version"
-          mise lock --bump --minimum-release-age 0s "aube@${version}"
-      - name: Commit and push if changed
-        env:
-          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
-          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
-          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
-        run: |
-          git add -- Cargo.lock mise.lock
-          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
-            echo "aube lockfiles already up to date"
-            exit 0
-          fi
-          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
-          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
-          base="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
-          git commit -m 'chore(deps): refresh aube crates and mise.lock'
-          remote="https://x-access-token:${PUSH_TOKEN}@github.com/${REPO}.git"
-          # aube-lock.yml starts from the same Renovate push and commits
-          # aube-lock.yaml to this branch, so it can land first and make the
-          # lease fail. Its push is not Renovate's, so nothing reruns this job:
-          # rebase onto it and retry. A tip that no longer contains the commit
-          # we built on means Renovate force-pushed; that push starts a fresh
-          # run of this workflow, so drop this one.
-          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
-            # The lease pins the push to the tip we built on, so a Renovate
-            # force-push that landed meanwhile is never clobbered.
-            if git push --force-with-lease="refs/heads/${BRANCH}:${base}" \
-              "$remote" "HEAD:${BRANCH}"; then
-              exit 0
-            fi
-            git fetch --quiet "$remote" "$BRANCH"
-            tip="$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)"
-            if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$tip"; then
-              echo "::notice::${BRANCH} was force-pushed; the new push reruns this workflow"
-              exit 0
-            fi
-            git rebase "$tip"
-            base="$tip"
-          done
-          echo "::error::could not push the aube lockfile refresh to ${BRANCH}"
-          exit 1

title: fix(daemons): tell the user how to pin a different port when a daemon's port is taken
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/350
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A daemon declared with `port = { auto = true, base = 3000 }` gets a port derived from the checkout's path. When something else already holds it, `mise daemons start` used to end like this:

```
pitchfork ERROR Daemon shop-…/api failed to start
✗ [shop-…/api] failed (exit code 1): Failed to start daemon shop-…/api: port 3000 is already in use by process 'python3' (PID: 1573063)
mise ERROR pitchfork exited with non-zero status: exit code 1
mise ERROR Version: 2026.9.17 linux-x64
mise ERROR Run with --verbose or MISE_VERBOSE=1 for more information
```

Nothing there says the number came from the checkout and can be changed, and the trailer repeats what pitchfork just explained. Now it ends like this:

```
pitchfork ERROR Daemon shop-…/api failed to start
✗ [shop-…/api] failed (exit code 1): Failed to start daemon shop-…/api: port 3000 is already in use by process 'python3' (PID: 1573063)
mise WARN  [daemons] api did not start and its port 3000, derived from this checkout's path, is in use by another process. To move it, declare the daemon again in a gitignored mise.local.toml with a fixed `port = <n>`, or with `port = { auto = true, base = <n> }` to move its range. That declaration replaces the whole daemon, so repeat its other keys.
```

The command still exits 1.

## What changes

- **Hint.** After a failed `mise daemons start` (or the daemon start a task's `daemons` requirement triggers), mise looks at the automatically allocated ports of the daemons it launched. For each one that is not running and whose loopback port cannot be bound, it prints the warning above. Fixed ports and ports that are free are left alone, and the check runs only after a failure. mise does not parse pitchfork's message; it checks the port itself, so it holds for any pitchfork.
- **Redeclare, not just set `port`.** A `[daemons.<name>]` in a higher-precedence file replaces the whole daemon, so a `mise.local.toml` containing only `port = 4001` fails to load. The hint and `docs/daemons.md` say to repeat the other keys. The existing conflict error for a port another mise project is running on now gives the same advice instead of the older "set an explicit port on one of them".
- **No redundant trailer.** When a pitchfork command run for `mise daemons ...` exits non-zero, mise now exits with pitchfork's status and prints nothing more, because pitchfork already wrote its explanation to the terminal. A pitchfork killed by a signal is still reported as an error.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the bind probe, which claims are reported (auto and free, auto and taken, fixed and taken) and the quiet exit status. New `e2e/cli/test_daemons_port_taken` holds a port with a Python server, starts an auto-port daemon on it with released pitchfork 2.25.0, and checks the hint is present, the trailer is absent and the exit status is non-zero. It then frees the port and starts the daemon. Th

title: fix(daemons): install preset tools on the first daemons start
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/349
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The first `mise daemons start` (or `restart`) on a machine that doesn't have a preset's tool installed failed, and only worked when run a second time:

```toml
[daemons.postgres]
preset = "postgres"
version = "18"
```

```
$ mise daemons start postgres
Error: daemon postgres requires postgres@18 (18), but [tools] selects 18.6
```

Now the first run installs the tool and starts the daemon, as `docs/daemons.md` already promises ("Start and restart install missing tools").

## Cause

`mise daemons start` installed with the default install options, which only install tools named on the command line — here, pitchfork. A preset's tool comes from the daemon declaration, so postgres was never installed. Validation then compared the version resolved from the network (`18.6`) with the offline resolution of the request (`18`) and reported a mismatch. The second run passed because the first had warmed the version cache. `mise run` on a task with `daemons = [...]` was not affected in the same way.

## Change

`mise daemons start` and `restart` now install pitchfork and the tools of the daemons they validate and start — the requested daemons plus their dependencies. A tool that belongs to another daemon, or to no daemon, is left alone, so an unrelated daemon's tool that is missing (or can't be installed) does not keep the one you asked for from starting. `mise run` on a task that requires daemons installs on the same rule.

A `[tools]` version that a preset can't use still fails with the same "requires ... but [tools] selects ..." error.

Note that a daemon's own command runs through `mise x`, which installs the project's other missing tools when that daemon launches, as it did before.

## Validation

- Reproduced the error with the config above on a fresh `MISE_DATA_DIR`; with the fix, the first `mise daemons start api` starts postgres and api.
- New e2e `e2e/cli/test_daemons_preset_install`: starts a `nats` preset with `nats-server` not yet installed, and checks that a conflicting `[tools]` version still errors. The existing `test_daemons` (offline, with an unrelated `postgres` preset declared next to the daemon it starts) covers leaving other daemons' tools alone. Both pass via `mise run test:e2e`.
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. I did not confirm the new e2e fails without the fix; the manual repro above covers that.

title: docs(daemons): document proxy_idle_timeout and type it in the schema
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/348
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Opening a daemon's proxy URL starts it and its dependencies, but nothing stops them again unless pitchfork's idle shutdown is on, and it is off by default. `proxy_idle_timeout` is how a project turns it on for one daemon, but mise never documented it: the schema let it through as an untyped extra property, so editors did not complete it and nothing explained the semantics.

```toml
[daemons.web]
run = "npm run dev"
port = 5173
depends = ["db"]
proxy_idle_timeout = "30m"   # or false to opt out
```

Visiting `https://web.shop.localhost` starts `db` and `web`. After 30 minutes without proxy traffic `web` stops, then `db` if nothing else needs it.

## What changes

- `docs/daemons.md` has a new "Stopping idle daemons" section covering: off by default; pitchfork's global `proxy.idle_timeout` as the default the per-daemon key overrides; an explicit start (`mise daemons start`, the shell hook, `boot_start`) exempts a daemon and its dependencies; a dependency inherits the requested daemon's timeout; open requests, WebSockets, streaming responses and TLS passthrough connections keep a daemon alive; and how `false` differs from leaving the key out when a global timeout or a dependent's timeout applies. It needs pitchfork 2.27.0. The semantics come from pitchfork's own documentation for the feature.
- `schema/mise.json` types `proxy_idle_timeout` (a string starting with a digit, or `false`) on custom, task and preset daemons, regenerated with `mise run render:schema`.
- mise now rejects `true`, a bare number such as `30`, and a string that is not duration-shaped with `[daemons.<name>].proxy_idle_timeout ...`, the way it already validates `proxy` and `proxy_tls`. It checks only the shape; pitchfork owns the duration grammar and still parses the value, so a valid pitchfork duration is never refused here. Before, a bad value surfaced as an error from pitchfork with no daemon named.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the accepted and rejected shapes and that the value is passed through as written. `e2e/cli/test_daemons` checks it lands in the generated pitchfork config, and `e2e/cli/test_daemons_presets` checks the errors for custom and preset daemons.

-started keeps running until you stop it. Open streaming responses and WebSockets
-count as activity. The next request starts the daemon again, and preset data stays
-on disk. See pitchfork's
+With this, visiting `https://web.shop.localhost` starts `db` and `web`. Thirty minutes
+after the last request, `web` stops, then `db` if nothing else still needs it, and the
+next visit starts them again.
+
+The value is a duration string such as `"30m"`, `"1h"` or `"90s"`, or `false`. Mise
+checks its shape and pitchfork parses it, so it needs pitchfork 2.27.0 or later.
+
+- **Default off.** A daemon without `proxy_idle_timeout` is stopped for inactivity
+  only when pitchfork's own `proxy.idle_timeout` setting is on, for example
+  `PITCHFORK_PROXY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=15m` or `idle_timeout = "15m"` under `[settings.proxy]`
+  in pitchfork's user configuration. `proxy_idle_timeout` overrides that default for one
+  daemon.
+- **Only proxy-started daemons.** `mise daemons start`, the shell hook and
+  `boot_start` are explicit starts, and a daemon started that way is exempt along with
+  its dependencies, however long it sits idle.
+- **Dependencies inherit.** A dependency without its own `proxy_idle_timeout` takes the
+  timeout of the daemon the proxy was asked to start, so `db` above also uses `"30m"`,
+  not the global default. One that is already running keeps the timeout it started with.
+- **Open connections count.** A request counts until its response has been sent, and a
+  WebSocket, a streaming response or a TLS passthrough connection keeps the daemon
+  active for as long as it stays open, so a browser tab holding a hot-reload socket
+  keeps a dev server up. Traffic sent straight to the daemon's port does not count, so
+  a client that bypasses the proxy should use `false`.
+- **`false` opts out.** It exempts the daemon even when the proxy started it as a
+  dependency of one that has a timeout, and even when a global `proxy.idle_timeout` is
+  set. Leaving the key out is different in exactly those two cases: the daemon then
+  follows the global default, or the timeout it inherited. With no global setting and no
+  dependent that has a timeout, `false` and leaving it out behave the same. `"0"` is
+  the same as `false`.
+
+Shutdown is checked every pitchfork `general.interval` (10 seconds by default), and a
+daemon stops only when no running daemon depends on it and no tracked shell session
+needs it, so it can outlive the timeout by a little.
+See pitchfork's
 [idle shutdown](https://pitchfork.jdx.dev/guides/port-management#idle-shutdown)
 for the full activity rules.

title: feat(daemons): export a preset's named ports as environment variables
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/347
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Presets with more than one listener (cockroachdb's console, nats' monitoring port, spicedb's HTTP and metrics ports) had no way to tell the project where a named port ended up. With `port = "auto"` each worktree's named ports move by the same slot as the primary port, so a project that needed the console port had to compute it itself, for example `8080 + (cockroach_port - 26258)`, which ties it to mise's slot rule.

mise now exports every named port as `<NAME>_<PORT_NAME>`, with the daemon's name folded the way `<NAME>_PORT` is:

```toml
[daemons.crdb]
preset = "cockroachdb"
version = "26"
port = "auto"

[env]
COCKROACH_CONSOLE = "http://127.0.0.1:{{ env.CRDB_HTTP_PORT }}"
```

`CRDB_HTTP_PORT` is the value in the `--http-addr` of the command mise generates: the preset default, the worktree offset from `port = "auto"`, or a `ports.http_port` you set. A `spicedb` daemon named `authz` exports `AUTHZ_HTTP_PORT` and `AUTHZ_METRICS_PORT`. These are available through `mise env`, `mise x` and the daemon's environment, like the existing exports.

## Collisions

- Two names that fold onto one variable (`db-a` and `db_a`) warn and export neither port; both daemons still run.
- A preset's own exports win. A custom daemon whose `<NAME>_PORT` matches a named-port variable (`crdb-http` beside `crdb`) gives way, with the existing warning.
- A daemon imported with `project =` exports into the project that declares it, not here.
- A name starting with a digit gets no variables, as today.

Only named ports are added. A preset daemon still does not export `<NAME>_PORT` for its primary port; its usual connection variables (`COCKROACH_URL`, `NATS_URL`, `SPICEDB_ENDPOINT`, ...) carry that.

## Testing

Unit tests cover the default, a worktree slot (export equals the port in the run command), an override, imported daemons, and each collision above. `e2e/cli/test_daemons_presets` asserts the variables for cockroachdb, nats and spicedb. `docs/daemons.md` documents them.

title: fix(daemons): register the hostname label with pitchfork so printed URLs route
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/346
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A project with `[daemons]` and no explicit `[daemons_settings] namespace` printed a URL that pitchfork's proxy did not serve. `mise daemons urls` and `<NAME>_URL` said `http://web.shop.localhost`, but once the checkout was registered pitchfork served `web.shop-528f92b13a6784f0.localhost`, so the printed URL returned 404. This affected the primary checkout and every linked worktree. Setting an explicit namespace hid it.

mise registers each project under a namespace containing a hash of its path, so two checkouts never share daemon IDs. Pitchfork treats a registered namespace as the project's hostname label, so the hash became part of the hostname.

mise now passes the project label it advertises to `pitchfork config add --label <label>`:

```
pitchfork config add .../pitchfork.toml --dir /work/shop --namespace shop-528f92b13a6784f0 --label shop
```

The registry then holds `label = "shop"` beside the hashed namespace, and `web.shop.localhost` and `web.feature.shop.localhost` (for a linked worktree `feature`) both route.

## Compatibility

`config add --label` is not in a released pitchfork yet (it is in jdx/pitchfork's `fix/registry-project-label`). mise detects the flag from `pitchfork usage` rather than by version, so a pitchfork without it is driven exactly as before, and the printed URL only routes with an explicit `namespace`, as today. mise remembers whether the label was registered, and retries once the pitchfork executable changes, so upgrading pitchfork picks it up without editing anything. A changed label (for example a renamed project) re-runs `config add`, which replaces the recorded label.

## Testing

- Unit tests for the `usage` probe (a `--label` on `daemons add` or `config remove` does not count) and for when registration is re-run.
- New `e2e/cli/test_daemons_project_label_slow`: a primary checkout with no explicit namespace and a linked worktree, an isolated supervisor with an unprivileged HTTP proxy, and a check that the URL from `mise daemons urls` returns 200 through the proxy for both. It skips with a message unless `MISE_TEST_PITCHFORK` names a pitchfork with `config add --label`. Run against a pitchfork built from that branch it passes; with mise's label registration disabled it fails with a 404, as before.
- The other proxy e2e tests still pass with that pitchfork build. `test_daemons_pitchfork` (released pitchfork 2.25.0, no `--label`) passes up to its fish activation step, which needs fish, absent on this machine.

Note for whoever runs the e2e: pitchfork's proxy can return 404 for about a second after a checkout is first registered, so the test polls for the 200.

title: feat(gem): use the GitHub token for GitHub Packages sources
body:
Follow-up to #13391. A `rubygems.pkg.github.com` gem source no longer needs a token templated into its URL: with no credentials, it uses the GitHub token mise already resolves (see `mise token github`).

```toml
[tools]
"gem:internal-cli" = { version = "1.4.2", source = "https://rubygems.pkg.github.com/acme" }
```

- Only https GitHub Packages sources get the token; explicit credentials and other hosts are unchanged.
- The version lookup sends source credentials as an `Authorization` header, so HTTP logs and errors can't print them.
- `gem install` gets a credentialed source through an environment variable instead of `--source`, so the token never shows in `ps`.
- GitHub Packages has no JSON versions API, so `latest` and prefixes there now fail with a "pin an exact version" message instead of a 404.
- The token needs `read:packages`, which a default `gh auth login` lacks.

title: fix(lock): warn with the cause when a tool is skipped
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/345
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` reported unresolved tools as `N skipped` but logged the cause at debug level only, so a rate-limited or otherwise failing run needed a second pass with `MISE_VERBOSE=1` to find out why.

Now, when a tool can't be resolved for a platform, `mise lock` prints a WARN with the cause once the run finishes:

```
WARN failed to resolve github:jdx/fnox for linux-x64: GitHub attestation API query failed for jdx/fnox: API error: GitHub API returned 403 Forbidden: {"message":"API rate limit exceeded ...
✓ Updated 0 platform entries (1 skipped)
```

If several platforms fail for the same tool, there is one warning per tool with the first error and `(and N more platform(s))`, so a rate limit hitting every platform doesn't print dozens of lines.

Targets a tool doesn't support (e.g. no Windows build) are an expected skip and stay at debug level, so they don't add warnings. Fatal conda solve errors are unchanged: they already fail the command.

Fixes #13829

Tested with the `cli::lock` unit tests. I did not reproduce the GitHub rate-limit case end to end.

title: docs(daemons): document stopping idle daemons with proxy_idle_timeout
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/344
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Daemons started through their proxy hostname never stop on their own unless an idle timeout is configured, and the daemon docs only mentioned the machine-wide setting. This documents the per-daemon option so a project can decide for itself which servers stop when idle.

Add `proxy_idle_timeout` to a custom daemon:

```toml
[daemons.api]
run = "exec npm run dev -- --port $API_PORT"
port = { auto = true, base = 3000 }
proxy_idle_timeout = "15m"
```

After 15 minutes without proxy traffic, pitchfork stops the API. Idle shutdown needs Pitchfork 2.27.0 or newer. The next request to its hostname starts it again, and preset data stays on disk. `proxy_idle_timeout = false` exempts a daemon from a global `[settings.proxy] idle_timeout`.

The new "Stop idle daemons" section in `docs/daemons.md` also states what the timeout does not cover: a daemon started with `mise daemons start`, or by a task, keeps running until stopped. The development-stack guide links to it.

This is docs only. Mise already forwards unknown keys on custom daemons to pitchfork (`additionalProperties: true` in `schema/mise.json`), so no code or schema changed. I did not document it for presets, which opt out of the proxy already.

## Testing

Prettier passes on both pages. I ran the documented behavior end to end with a debug build of this branch and Pitchfork 2.27.0, in an isolated environment with no global idle timeout and the proxy enabled:

- A per-daemon `proxy_idle_timeout = "5s"` reaches the generated pitchfork config. Opening the daemon's hostname starts it and its dependency, both stop after the timeout, and the next request starts them again.
- `proxy_idle_timeout = false` keeps a proxy-started daemon running past the timeout.
- A daemon started with `mise daemons start` is not stopped by the timeout.

The inheritance rule for running dependencies comes from Pitchfork's port-management guide and was not exercised separately.

title: fix(daemons): make `mise daemons stop --all` cover the project's daemons
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/342
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Problem

`mise daemons stop --all` failed instead of stopping anything:

```
error: the argument '[ID]…' cannot be used with '--all'
Error:
   0: pitchfork exited with non-zero status: exit code 2
```

mise forwards the project's daemon IDs to pitchfork, and pitchfork refuses `--all` combined with IDs. `mise daemons start --all` and `restart --all` hit the same conflict.

## What changes

For `start`, `stop` and `restart`, `--all` (or `-a`) now means **every daemon in the current project**:

```sh
mise daemons start --all    # every project daemon, not only the `default` group
mise daemons stop --all     # same set a bare `mise daemons stop` stops
mise daemons restart --all
```

mise selects the project's daemons itself and drops the flag, so it never reaches daemons belonging to other projects the way pitchfork's own `--all` would. `start --all` and `restart --all` also skip the `default`-group narrowing that a bare `start`/`restart` applies.

`--all` combined with daemon names or `--group` is rejected before anything is installed or started:

```
Error: --all selects every daemon in this project; drop it or drop the daemon names and --group
```

`logs` and `status` are unchanged (`-a` means something else there). `docs/daemons.md` describes the flag.

## Verification

- New unit tests cover flag handling per action, the name/`--group` conflict, and `--all` skipping the `default` group. The daemons CLI tests pass.
- Checked with a real pitchfork 2.27.0 on Linux against a project with two daemons: `start --all` started both, `stop --all` stopped both with no leaked processes, and `stop --all web` was rejected with the message above.
- `cargo clippy -p mise --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean. `daemons::prune::tests::state_that_cannot_be_examined_is_reported_and_skipped` fails when run as root because it relies on an unreadable directory; it is unrelated to this change.

title: ci(deps): refresh aube crates via a workflow instead of postUpgradeTasks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/340
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Renovate's aube update PRs (e.g. #13798) fail to build because \`Cargo.lock\` is only half-updated: Renovate bumps just \`aube\` and \`aube-registry\`, leaving \`aube-lockfile\`, \`aube-codes\` and the other \`aube-*\` crates on the old release, which lack APIs the new \`aube\` calls. \`mise.lock\` is not refreshed either.

#13801 and #13802 tried to fix this with \`postUpgradeTasks\`, but those only run on self-hosted Renovate. The Mend-hosted app rejects them ("has not been added to the allowed list in allowedCommands"), so the commands never ran.

This replaces them with \`.github/workflows/aube-crates-lock.yml\`, modelled on the existing \`aube-lock\` workflow. On a push from renovate[bot] to \`renovate/aube\` it reads the selected version from \`Cargo.lock\`, runs the same \`cargo update … --precise\` and \`mise lock --bump --minimum-release-age 0s aube@<version>\`, and pushes the result with the existing \`AUBE_LOCK_APP_*\` App token so CI reruns. The dead \`postUpgradeTasks\` block is removed from \`renovate.json\`.

Not verified end to end: it needs a real Renovate push. \`zizmor\` reports no findings, and the version-extraction \`awk\` returns \`2.5.1\` against the current \`Cargo.lock\`. The committer (\`github-actions[bot]\`) is already in the shared \`gitIgnoredAuthors\`, so Renovate keeps rebasing the branch.

Once this merges, retrigger #13798 (rename it to start with \`rebase!\`) to get the lockfile fixed.

> **Low Risk**
> Scoped to Renovate dependency branches and reuses existing lockfile automation secrets; no runtime or auth behavior changes for users.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Renovate’s hosted app cannot run the `postUpgradeTasks` that were supposed to keep all `aube-*` crates and `mise.lock` aligned when `aube` / `aube-registry` bump**, so those tasks are removed from `.github/renovate.json` and the config comment now points at a new workflow.
> 
> **Adds `.github/workflows/aube-crates-lock.yml`**, which runs on `renovate[bot]` pushes to `renovate/aube`: it reads the version Renovate wrote into `Cargo.lock`, runs the same `cargo update … --precise` across the full `aube-*` set, bumps `aube@` in `mise.lock`, and commits with the existing `AUBE_LOCK_APP_*` token (same pattern as `aube-lock.yml`) so CI reruns. Push logic uses force-with-lease and rebases to avoid racing `aube-lock.yml` on the same branch.

--- .github/workflows/aube-crates-lock.yml (+106/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,106 @@
+name: aube-crates-lock
+
+# Renovate only bumps the direct `aube` and `aube-registry` entries in
+# Cargo.lock; the other aube-* workspace crates stay behind (aube requires
+# them only as "2") and break the build against the new API. The standalone
+# aube entry in mise.lock must also match the embedded version.
+# `postUpgradeTasks` would do this, but they only run on self-hosted Renovate,
+# not the Mend hosted app, so this workflow refreshes both lockfiles on the
+# Renovate branch instead. Like aube-lock.yml, it commits with an App token so
+# CI reruns on the pushed commit.
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches: ["renovate/aube"]
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  # mise.toml wraps cargo through mbx, which install: false never provides
+  MBX_DISABLE: "1"
+
+jobs:
+  aube-crates-lock:
+    # Only react to Renovate's own pushes (checked by the sender's immutable
+    # numeric id, not a spoofable login); our fix-up push has a different
+    # sender, so this also prevents self-retriggering.
+    if: github.event.sender.id == 29139614 # renovate[bot]
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    # Job-level, so a push whose job the `if` skips (e.g. aube-lock.yml's
+    # lockfile commit) never cancels a Renovate-triggered refresh in flight.
+    concurrency:
+      group: aube-crates-lock-${{ github.ref }}
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      # No GITHUB_TOKEN fallback: it is read-only here and would not retrigger
+      # CI, so a missing App secret should fail this step loudly.
+      - name: Generate app token
+        id: app-token
+        uses: actions/create-github-app-token@bcd2ba49218906704ab6c1aa796996da409d3eb1 # v3.2.0
+        with:
+          app-id: ${{ secrets.AUBE_LOCK_APP_ID }}
+          private-key: ${{ secrets.AUBE_LOCK_APP_PRIVATE_KEY }}
+          permission-contents: write
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - uses: jdx/mise-action@c2a87611a18de5b3828c5652fe268e992400cb5c # v4.3.0
+        with:
+          install: false
+      - name: Refresh aube lockfiles
+        run: |
+          # the version Renovate selected is the one it wrote for the direct
+          # `aube` package in Cargo.lock
+          version="$(awk '/^name = "aube"$/ { getline; gsub(/[^0-9.]/, "", $0); print; exit }' Cargo.lock)"
+          if [ -z "$version" ]; then
+            echo "::error::could not find the aube version in Cargo.lock"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "refreshing aube crates to ${version}"
+          cargo update \
+            -p aube -p aube-registry -p aube-codes -p aube-lockfile -p aube-settings \
+            -p aube-linker -p aube-manifest -p aube-resolver -p aube-runtime \
+            -p aube-scripts -p aube-store -p aube-util -p aube-workspace \
+            --precise "$version"
+          mise lock --bump --minimum-release-age 0s "aube@${version}"
+      - name: Commit and push if changed
+        env:
+          PUSH_TOKEN: ${{ steps.app-token.outputs.token }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          BRANCH: ${{ github.ref_name }}
+        run: |
+          git add -- Cargo.lock mise.lock
+          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
+            echo "aube lockfiles already up to date"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+          git config user.name 'github-actions[bot]'
+          git config user.email '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'
+          base="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+          git commit -m 'chore(deps): refresh aube crates and mise.lock'
+          remote="https://x-access-token:${PUSH_TOKEN}@github.com/${REPO}.git"
+          # aube-lock.yml starts from the same Renovate push and commits
+          # aube-lock.yaml to this branch, so it can land first and make the
+          # lease fail. Its push is not Renovate's, so nothing reruns this job:
+          # rebase onto it and retry. A tip that no longer contains the commit
+          # we built on means Renovate force-pushed; that push starts a fresh
+          # run of this workflow, so drop this one.
+          for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do
+            # The lease pins the push to the tip we built on, so a Renovate
+            # force-push that landed meanwhile is never clobbered.
+            if git push --force-with-lease="refs/heads/${BRANCH}:${base}" \
+              "$remote" "HEAD:${BRANCH}"; then
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            git fetch --quiet "$remote" "$BRANCH"
+            tip="$(git rev-parse FETCH_HEAD)"
+            if ! git merge-base --is-ancestor "$base" "$tip"; then
+              echo "::notice::${BRANCH} was force-pushed; the new push reruns this workflow"
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            git rebase "$tip"
+            base="$tip"
+          done
+          echo "::error::could not push the aube lockfile refresh to ${BRANCH}"
+          exit 1

title: feat(bootstrap): support ?ref= in bootstrap --from
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/339
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise bootstrap --from` always cloned the default branch, unlike task includes and plugin sources, which accept a go-getter style `?ref=`. It now accepts the same spelling, with an optional `git::` prefix:

```sh
mise bootstrap --from 'git::https://github.com/example/dotfiles.git?ref=v1'
mise bootstrap --from 'https://github.com/example/dotfiles.git?ref=feature/x'
```

`ref` can be a branch, tag, or commit. Other query parameters stay on the URL, and URLs without `ref` behave as before.

- **Resolution:** the ref is looked up on origin. A branch wins over a tag of the same name and is switched to (created as a tracking branch if needed); a tag is checked out at its current commit; anything else is treated as a commit. If the checkout fails (for example an unknown ref), the fresh clone is removed so a later run doesn't reuse a checkout on the wrong ref.
- **`--update`:** with `?ref=`, it fetches (forcing tags, without pruning other local tags), resolves the ref on origin again, and fast-forwards branches. A branch or tag that was deleted upstream is an error rather than being used from the stale local copy.
- **Existing checkouts:** the origin check compares against the URL without `?ref=`. A reused checkout without `--update` is left as is, same as before.
- **`--dry-run`:** prints the extra `checkout` step.

Refs that are empty or start with `-` are rejected.

Tested with a unit test for the URL parsing (in `mise-util`, as `RemoteSource::parse_git_repo`) and an extended `e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_from` (branch, tag, `git::` prefix, `--update` on a branch, a tag and a moved tag, deleted tag and branch, branch/tag name collisions, dry run, unknown ref). Clippy is clean on stable.

Discussion: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13818

> **Medium Risk**
> Bootstrap runs arbitrary git operations against user-supplied remotes and can delete a failed clone directory; ref resolution changes which config is applied on update.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise bootstrap --from`** now accepts go-getter-style **`?ref=<branch|tag|commit>`** (optional **`git::`** prefix), aligned with task includes and plugin sources. URLs without `ref` behave as before; origin validation still uses the URL without the query string.
> 
> **`RemoteSource::parse_git_repo`** in `mise-util` splits the clone URL from `ref`, keeps other query params on the URL, and rejects empty, `HEAD`, or `-`-prefixed refs. Bootstrap wires that into clone/checkout: after clone it checks out the requested ref; failed checkout deletes the new directory so a retry does not reuse the wrong default branch.
> 
> With **`--update`** and a ref, mise fetches (force tags, prune remote branches), resolves the name

title: fix(oci): let [oci.env] satisfy required env vars during mise oci
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/338
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise oci build` no longer fails on a `required` env var when `[oci.env]` gives the image a value for it, so secrets that only exist at runtime can be stubbed with placeholders instead of being exported in CI.

Given:

```toml
[env]
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = { required = "AWS access key ID for S3", redact = true }

[oci.env]
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "placeholder"
```

**Before:** `mise oci build` aborted with `Required environment variable 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID' is not defined` unless the variable was set in the build environment. `required` is validated while the config loads, before `[oci.env]` is ever read.

**After:** the build succeeds and the image config contains `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=placeholder`.

## Behavior

- Applies to `mise oci build`, `push` and `run`.
- Only keys from project configs' `[oci.env]` count, matching which `[oci]` sections are baked into the image by default. Global and system configs don't satisfy `required`.
- A required var missing from both the environment and `[oci.env]` still fails the build.
- Other commands (`mise env`, `mise x`, …) still enforce `required`.
- `[vars]` requirements are unaffected.
- The non-tool env cache is skipped for `mise oci` commands, so env resolved with this relaxation can't be reused by a command that enforces `required`.

## Testing

New e2e test `oci/test_oci_required_env` covers success with `[oci.env]`, no warning output, the placeholder in the image config, `mise env` still failing, and a build failing when `[oci.env]` doesn't define the var. `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13809

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes required-env validation and caching for OCI commands only; mis-scoping could weaken secret checks on non-OCI paths, but the flag is set narrowly and cache is bypassed when active.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise oci` no longer fails config load when a `[env]` variable is `required` but only defined in project `[oci.env]`**, so image-only secrets can use placeholders (e.g. `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "placeholder"`) without exporting them on the build host.
> 
> Before the first config load, OCI subcommands set a process flag that treats keys from **project** `[oci.env]` as satisfying `required` during validation. Global/system `[oci.env]` does not count. **`mise env` and other commands still require the variable on the host**, and builds still fail if neither the environment nor `[oci.env]` defines it. Non-tool env caching is disabled while that flag is set so relaxed resolution is not reused elsewhere.
> 
> Docs describe the pattern; e2e `test_oci_required_env` covers success, image `Env`, non-OCI

title: feat(task): include task catalogs from OCI artifacts with oci:: prefix
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/337
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Teams that distribute signed, immutable artifacts through an OCI registry can now share task catalogs the same way. `task_config.includes` accepts an `oci::` reference, mirroring the existing `git::` includes:

```toml
[task_config]
includes = [
    "oci::ghcr.io/myorg/shared-tasks:1.0.0",
    "oci::registry.example.com/platform/tasks@sha256:0f1e2d3c...",
]
```

The artifact is pulled, unpacked into a cache directory and loaded like a local task directory, so executable file tasks and `.toml` task files both work. It can be published with the tools people already use:

```sh
oras push ghcr.io/myorg/shared-tasks:1.0.0 build.toml scripts/deploy
```

Requested in [discussion #13811](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13811).

## Behavior

- **Reference syntax** is the `docker pull` one: `<registry>/<repo>` plus `:<tag>` or `@sha256:<digest>`. Pin a version tag or digest; a mutable tag like `latest` is cached like any other reference.
- **Layers** are read as follows:
  - A layer with an `org.opencontainers.image.title` annotation becomes that file (`oras push`, `podman artifact add`).
  - A titled tar layer with `io.deis.oras.content.unpack=true` (an `oras push` of a directory) is extracted into that directory.
  - An untitled tar, tar+gzip or tar+zstd layer is extracted at the root with whiteouts applied, so an artifact made of tar layers (e.g. via `crane append`) works too. This is not a general container-image reader: layers containing symlinks or device files are rejected.
- **Executable bit**: artifacts don't carry file modes, so non-`.toml` files starting with `#!` are made executable.
- **Auth** reuses the `mise oci push` machinery: `docker login` / `podman login` credentials, otherwise anonymous. Loopback registries use plain HTTP; others need `oci.insecure_registries`.
- **Caching** goes to `MISE_CACHE_DIR/remote-oci-tasks-cache`, populated atomically. `MISE_TASK_REMOTE_NO_CACHE=true` pulls on every run into a temporary directory that is cleaned up afterwards.

## Safety

Every blob is checked against the manifest digest, and a manifest fetched by `@sha256:` reference (including an index child) is checked against that digest, so a digest pin binds the catalog contents. Each tar layer is extracted to a scratch directory and vetted for links before it is merged, so nothing can be written through a link planted by an earlier layer. Layer titles must be plain relative paths (no `..`, no absolute paths), and any symlink or special file in an unpacked artifact is rejected, since task includes follow symlinks.

## Not included

Signature verification (e.g. cosign/sigstore) is not part of this PR; integrity currently rests on the digest, so pin `@sha256:` if you need immutability. Single-file `oci::` includes and a `//subpath` selector are also not supported — the artifact is always a directory.

## Testing

- Unit tests for layer classifi

title: feat(lock): add --sidecars to list native dependency sidecars
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/336
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise lock` keeps native dependency graphs for npm and Python tools in [sidecar directories](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/mise-lock.html#native-dependency-sidecars) that must be committed with `mise.lock`. Until now, the only way to learn where they live was to re-implement mise's layout rules. Renovate did that for its mise manager (renovatebot/renovate#46514), and the copy can't follow a symlinked lockfile, whose sidecars live beside its target.

`mise lock --sidecars` now reports them. It is read-only: it resolves no tools, installs nothing, and writes no files.

```console
$ mise lock --sidecars
mise.lock (sidecars in .mise/locks)
  npm:prettier@3.9.9 aube .mise/locks/npm-prettier/3.9.9
```

Add `--json` for scripts and automation:

```json
[
  {
    "lockfile": "mise.lock",
    "root": ".mise/locks",
    "sidecars": [
      {
        "tool": "npm:prettier",
        "version": "3.9.9",
        "graph": "aube",
        "path": ".mise/locks/npm-prettier/3.9.9",
        "digest": "sha256:…",
        "exists": true
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

- `root` is the directory mise uses for that lockfile, following its layout rules, including `mise.local.lock` and `.config/mise` layouts.
- `graph` is `aube` (npm) or `uv` (Python).
- `exists` is false when the native lockfile is missing from disk, for example a sidecar that was never committed. The text output marks these `(missing)`.
- Paths are relative to the current directory when inside it. Sidecars of a symlinked lockfile live beside its target, so they can be absolute paths outside the current directory.
- Lockfiles that don't exist yet are not listed. `--local` and `--global` choose lockfiles as in a normal `mise lock` run.
- `--sidecars` cannot be combined with tool arguments, `--dry-run`, `--bump`, `--upgrade`, `--platform`, or `--minimum-release-age`.

## Testing

New e2e tests cover text and JSON output, a missing sidecar, a missing lockfile, leaving `mise.lock` untouched, the rejected flag combinations, a symlinked lockfile whose target is outside the working directory (`e2e/cli/test_lock_sidecars`), and a monorepo whose shared `mise.local.lock` comes only from a sibling package's config (`e2e/lockfile/test_lock_sidecars_monorepo`). Clippy (`-D warnings`) and `cargo fmt --check` pass. `mise run lint` reports an `unreachable_code` warning in `crates/mise-util`, a crate this PR doesn't touch. On Windows, `\\?\` prefixes from resolving a symlink are stripped from printed paths; that path is not exercised by CI.

title: registry: add lstk and warn when installing deprecated localstack
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/335
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

LocalStack replaced its Python-based `localstack` CLI with [`lstk`](https://github.com/localstack/lstk), and the old CLI repo now says it is deprecated. mise's registry still only offered `localstack`, so `mise use localstack` installed the deprecated tool and `mise use lstk` didn't exist. See discussion #13810.

This adds an `lstk` shorthand and lets registry entries be marked as deprecated:

```
$ mise use lstk            # new: installs github:localstack/lstk

$ mise install localstack
mise WARN  localstack is deprecated: the LocalStack CLI has been superseded by lstk. Run `mise use lstk` instead.
```

- New optional `deprecated = "<reason>"` field in `registry/<tool>.toml`. The entry keeps working; mise prints the message once per run when the tool is installed. It is documented in the registry format section of `docs/contributing.md` and added to `schema/mise-registry-tool.json`.
- `registry/localstack.toml` uses it to point users at `lstk`.
- `registry/lstk.toml` uses the `github:` backend (`lstk` is not in the aqua registry). `mise ls-remote github:localstack/lstk` lists versions and `lstk 1.2.0` installs and runs.
- The warning appears on install only, so users who already have `localstack` installed won't see it until they reinstall.

## Popularity
- `localstack/localstack`: ~65k GitHub stars. `lstk` is its official replacement CLI (37 stars, still new) and succeeds an entry already in the registry.
- Releases are active (v1.2.0 with darwin/linux/windows amd64+arm64 archives and checksums).

## Validation
- `cargo test --lib registry` passes; the dynamic-registry test covers parsing `deprecated`.
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Ran `mise install localstack --dry-run` with the built binary to confirm the warning.

> Adds optional metadata and install-time warnings without changing install semantics; the only behavioral change is informational output when deprecated tools are installed.

> Registry tools can now declare an optional **`deprecated`** string (build-time codegen, dynamic registry parsing, JSON schema, and contributing docs). Installing through a backend that belongs to that registry entry triggers a **one-time warning** via `warn_once!` with the message; aliases resolve correctly, and plugin overrides that replace the shorthand do not get a spurious warning.
> 
> **LocalStack migration:** `registry/localstack.toml` is marked deprecated in favor of **`lstk`**, and a new **`registry/lstk.toml`** entry installs `github:localstack/lstk` with an explicit `bins` and version test.

title: fix(install-script): pin the version instead of scraping the installer
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/334
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes discussion #13813.

## Problem

Since 2026.9.15 the published installer no longer has a default version, but `mise generate install-script` still scraped it from the installer and unwrapped the match. The command panicked with or without `--version`:

```
$ mise generate install-script --version 2026.9.17
The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
```

Fixing the panic alone would leave a second bug. The wrapper names its binary after its pin (`mise-2026.9.17`), but never passed that pin to the embedded installer. The installer therefore picked the newest release older than the minimum release age and installed it under the pinned name. `test -f "$MISE_INSTALL_PATH"` then skipped reinstalling on every later run, so a `2026.9.17` wrapper could permanently run `2026.9.16`.

## Fix

- The pin comes from `--version` when given. Otherwise it is the release `mise self-update` would pick, using the same release index and minimum release age. The command no longer parses the installer.
- The generated wrapper runs `MISE_VERSION="v$mise_version" install`, so the installer installs exactly the version in the binary's name. The prefix assignment does not leak into the exec'd mise.

```
mise generate install-script --version 2026.9.17 -w ./bin/mise
./bin/mise --version   # 2026.9.17
```

The e2e test now also checks the wrapper's pin and that it is passed to the installer.

Thanks to @Guria for the report and the analysis.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes bootstrap/install-script generation and first-run install behavior for project wrappers; logic is localized but affects every contributor using generated **`./bin/mise`** scripts.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise generate install-script`** no longer parses the downloaded **`install.sh`** for a default version (which started panicking once the published installer dropped that default). The pinned release is now **`--version`** when set, otherwise the same eligible release **`mise self-update`** would choose, and the fetch always uses the versioned installer URL **`/v{version}/install.sh`**.
> 
> The generated bash wrapper **forwards that pin into the embedded install** with **`MISE_VERSION="v$mise_version" install`**, so the binary installed under the versioned path matches the wrapper’s name instead of whatever release the installer would pick on its own.
> 
> E2e coverage asserts the default pin in the script, that install line, and that running a **`--version 2026.9.15`** wrapper reports that version.
>

title: fix(dotfiles): keep internal Git commands working with Git for Windows 2.56
body:
On Windows with Git for Windows 2.56.0, commands that go through mise's internal Git plumbing, such as `mise dot ls`, fail immediately:

```
mise ERROR git -c core.hooksPath=... --git-dir=...\mise\history\repo.git ... rev-parse --is-bare-repository failed (exit code: 128): fatal: unable to access 'NUL': Invalid argument
```

mise isolates these commands from the user's Git configuration by setting `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to the null device, and on Windows it passed `NUL`. Git for Windows 2.56.0 moved to a UCRT-based build, and its null-device special case only matches lowercase `nul` and the literal `/dev/null`. Any other spelling now reaches UCRT's `_waccess()`, which rejects it. That is a Git for Windows regression (reported as git-for-windows/git#6449), but mise can avoid it without waiting for an upstream release.

mise now sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` on every platform. Git for Windows maps the literal `/dev/null` to its null device in both the MSVCRT build (2.55) and the UCRT build (2.56), so this also keeps working on older Git versions. Behavior on Linux and macOS does not change.

With plain Git on the same machine:

| `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` | Git for Windows 2.55.0.windows.5 | Git for Windows 2.56.0.windows.1                  |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `NUL`               | works                            | `fatal: unable to access 'NUL': Invalid argument` |
| `/dev/null`         | works                            | works                                             |

## Validation

- The plumbing test now asserts the exact `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` value instead of only checking that the variable is set.
- `cargo test -p mise-util --lib git::` on Windows with Git for Windows 2.56.0.windows.1 first on `PATH`: 11 passed with this change. Without it, the three plumbing tests that run Git fail with `unable to access 'NUL': Invalid argument`. The tests also pass with 2.55.0.windows.5.
- `cargo clippy -p mise-util --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Desktop; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.9939.4 (a166d8).*

  * Improved Git configuration handling on Windows to avoid errors with certain Git builds.

`SemverError` is now a lightweight error without detailed diagnostics ([8b0b01c](https://redirect.github.com/cijiugechu/nodejs-semver/commit/8b0b01c96809f77f936b276d5af835c6181a2bb9)).

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>jdx/renovate-config (jdx/renovate-config)</summary>

### [`v1.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/renovate-config/releases/tag/v1.0.1): : Stop Renovate's npm and pep621 managers from relocking mise sidecars

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/renovate-config/compare/v1.0.0...v1.0.1)

The shared preset now keeps Renovate's npm and pep621 managers out of `mise lock` dependency sidecars. Before this, Renovate and the `mise-lock` workflow kept overwriting each other's changes.

##### Fixed

- **mise lock sidecars are no longer relocked by other managers.** `mise lock` pins npm and Python tool dependencies in sidecars under `.mise/locks/` or `.config/mise/locks/` and stores a digest of each one in `mise.lock`. Renovate's npm and pep621 managers were treating these sidecars' `package.json` and `pyproject.toml` as regular package files. Lock file maintenance then rewrote the sidecar lockfiles (for example with `uv lock --upgrade`) without updating the digests in `mise.lock`. The `mise-lock` workflow fixed the digests, and Renovate overwrote the fix on its next run. The preset now adds `**/.mise/locks/**` and `**/.config/mise/locks/**` to `ignorePaths`, so only the mise manager updates sidecars. Repos that extend the preset get this fix right away because the preset is read from `main`. ([#​30](https://redirect.github.com/jdx/renovate-config/issues/30), [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx))

  `ignorePaths` doesn't merge, so the preset now lists the defaults from `config:recommended`'s `:ignoreModulesAndTests` (`node_modules`, `bower_components`, `vendor`, `examples`, `__tests__`, `test`, `tests`, `__fixtures__`) alongside the two mise paths. If your repo sets its own `ignorePaths`, that list replaces the preset's. To keep the fix, add the two mise sidecar globs to your list.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/jdx/renovate-config/compare/v1.0.0...v1.0.1>

</details>
