title: ci(deps): pin the aube mise.lock refresh to the version Renovate selected
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/326
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Follow-up to #13801. That PR pins the `cargo update` step of the Renovate `aube` rule to the version Renovate selected, but the `mise.lock` step (`mise lock --bump --minimum-release-age 0s aube`) still resolves the newest aube. If a newer release lands inside Renovate's release-age window, `Cargo.lock` and `mise.lock` could end up on different versions.

`mise lock` already accepts `tool@version`, so the step now runs `mise lock --bump --minimum-release-age 0s aube@{{{newVersion}}}`, keeping both lockfiles on the release Renovate chose. No mise code change is needed.

Checked locally with a clean state: `mise lock --dry-run --json --bump --minimum-release-age 0s aube@2.6.0` resolves aube to 2.6.0, and `renovate-config-validator` accepts the config. Not verified through a real Renovate run.

title: ci(deps): refresh all aube workspace crates in Renovate aube updates
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/325
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Renovate's aube update PRs (e.g. #13798, aube 2.5.1 → 2.6.0) fail to build. Renovate only bumps the direct `aube` and `aube-registry` entries in `Cargo.lock`. The other 11 aube workspace crates (`aube-lockfile`, `aube-codes`, `aube-settings`, …) stay at the old version because `aube` requires them only as `"2"`, so the new `aube` compiles against stale APIs:

```
error[E0425]: cannot find function `parse_lockfile_selecting` in crate `aube_lockfile`
error[E0425]: cannot find value `WARN_AUBE_OVERRIDE_TOO_DEEP` in module `aube_codes::warnings`
```

This adds a `cargo update -p …` post-upgrade step for all 13 aube crates to the existing `aube` Renovate rule, so the lockfile moves them together (this matches the `update-aube` skill's "refresh all aube workspace crates" step). `Cargo.lock` is added to the rule's `fileFilters` and `rust` to `installTools` so the step can run and its result is committed.

## Validation

- `renovate-config-validator` accepts `.github/renovate.json`.
- `cargo update --dry-run` with the new command moves all 13 aube crates from 2.5.1 to 2.6.0.
- Not verified: that the Renovate runner's `allowedCommands` permits `cargo update`. If it doesn't, the step is rejected and the allowlist needs an entry.

Existing aube PRs need a Renovate rebase to pick this up.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI-only Renovate configuration; no runtime or application behavior changes, though the runner must allow the new `cargo update` command.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes broken Renovate **aube** bump PRs by extending the existing grouped rule’s **post-upgrade** workflow so all 13 related crates move to the same version, not only `aube` and `aube-registry`.
>

title: ci: allow publishing docs via workflow_dispatch
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/324
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The docs site only deploys when a stable \`v*\` release is published, so docs-only changes merged to \`main\` (like the new [mise run](https://mise.jdx.dev/mise-en-place) theme song page) wait for the next release. Running the \`docs\` workflow by hand doesn't help today: it always builds as a dry run.

This adds a \`deploy\` checkbox to the \`docs\` workflow's manual run. Checking it on a run from \`main\` publishes the site to production; leaving it unchecked (the default) keeps the current dry-run behavior.

```bash
gh workflow run docs.yml --ref main -f deploy=true
```

- The caller (\`docs.yml\`) now decides whether a run deploys and passes that to \`docs-impl.yml\` as a \`deploy\` input. A run deploys for a stable \`v*\` release (unchanged) or a manual run on \`main\` with \`deploy\` checked.
- A manual run on any other branch, or by anyone other than the existing trusted actors, stays a dry run.
- Deploys now queue instead of cancelling each other. Previously a newer deploy cancelled one already uploading to R2; with a manual trigger that could leave the bucket half-updated.

Validated with actionlint and zizmor; the only findings are pre-existing (the \`$/\` reusable-workflow path and \`persist-credentials\`), not from this change. I haven't triggered a real deploy.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Manual production deploys to Cloudflare R2 are now possible for trusted actors on main, so mis-triggered runs could publish docs; concurrency changes reduce risk of partial uploads during overlapping deploys.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds a manual path to publish the docs site without waiting for a stable release, and tightens how deploy vs validation runs behave in CI.
> 
> The **`docs`** workflow now exposes a **`deploy`** checkbox on **`workflow_dispatch`** (default off). The trusted job forwards **`deploy: true`** only for stable **`v*`** releases (same as before) or a manual run from **`main`** with the box checked; **`DRY_RUN`** in **`docs-impl`** is now **`!trusted || !deploy`** instead of inferring deploy from release event metadata alone.
> 
> **`docs-impl`** gains a **`deploy`** callable input. Deploy jobs share one concurrency group and **no longer cancel in-progress uploads**; validation runs still cancel superseded runs per branch/ref.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/323
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The mise-en-place song page now features **mise run**, a new theme song with a 5-minute music video, replacing the old MP3-only ballad. The landing page also gets a small announcement chip so people can find it.

**Song page** (`/mise-en-place`, same URL and `#lyrics` anchor)

- Plays the music video in a 1080p, 120 fps H.264 player with a poster frame and optional English captions (`mise-run.en.vtt`, one cue per lyric line).
- Offers downloads of the video in 1080p or 4K (3840×2160 HEVC), both at 120 fps, plus an MP3 of the song.
- Shows the new lyrics as text. The page, sidebar entry, and `llms.txt` are retitled "mise run: The Song".

The video is a kinetic lyric video rendered in code in the site's palette, fonts, and chef mascot. Every lyric is timed to the vocal.

**Landing page**

A "New: **mise run**, the theme song and music video →" chip sits above the hero title and links to the song page. On narrow screens it shortens to "the theme song" so it stays on one line. It uses the existing brand tokens in both light and dark themes.

**Hosting**

The two MP4s (285 MB and 839 MB) are too large for the repo, so the page loads them from `https://mise.jdx.dev/mise-run.mp4` and `https://mise.jdx.dev/mise-run-4k.mp4`. They are uploaded to the `mise` R2 bucket separately. `mise run docs:release` now checks that both objects exist before publishing, so a release can't ship the page with a broken player (dry runs, including PR validation, skip the check). The release only prunes `assets/` and `*.html`, so root-level files persist. The poster, captions, and MP3 ship in `docs/public`. The old `mise-en-place.mp3` is removed.

**Validation**

- `mise run docs:build` passes, including the social-image checks for all 414 pages.
- prettier and markdownlint pass on the changed files.
- In a built-site preview, the landing chip was checked in light and dark themes at desktop and 375 px widths. Clicking it opens the song page, where the poster and captions load.

title: docs: add a seven-minute showreel of mise to the landing page
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/321
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The mise.jdx.dev homepage now has a video tour of mise, right under the hero. It runs 7:16 and has nine chapters: mise, Dev tools, Versions, Environments, Tasks, Dotfiles, Everywhere, A new machine, and Install mise. It is built the same way as the hk and Mr Boxington showreels. The picture is drawn in code, the score is composed in code, and the whole thing is rendered to MP4 in the docs build.

It walks through one project's `mise.toml` as it grows:

- **Dev tools:**
  - `mise use jq` when `jq` is missing;
  - 1,000+ tools by short name;
  - the npm backend installing `npm:prettier` in a project with no `package.json`;
  - `github:cli/cli`, plus the other backends.
- **Versions:** `cd` switches Node between two projects. Upgrading hk changes its Tab completions, and `mise skills sync` links that version's agent skills, both through hk's signed packslip.
- **Environments:** env vars load and unload on `cd`, `.env` files load, and `redact = true` masks secrets in task output.
- **Tasks:**
  - dependencies run in parallel, with labelled output;
  - `sources`/`outputs` skip up-to-date work;
  - `#USAGE` adds arguments and `--help`;
  - a task declares the Postgres daemon it needs.
- **Dotfiles:** `mise dot track`, autosave, history and `mise dot rollback`.
- **Everywhere:** `mise.toml` asks for a Node major and `mise.lock` records the exact version. CI installs from the same lock.
- **A new machine:** `mise bootstrap --adopt` restores the dotfiles and config. Then `git clone … && cd api && mise run ci` installs what the lock pins and runs the tasks.

## Every terminal line is real

The reel draws recorded output only. `mise run docs:showreel-capture` records every scene in Docker, on two simulated machines, using a released mise binary. Tests fail if a drawn terminal line doesn't match a recording, or if a scene hard-codes a version number.

- Install progress replays sped up, under a "time-lapse" badge, and cuts before any totals.
- Placeholder repositories (`you/api`, `you/setup`) carry an "illustration" badge.
- There are no benchmarks or speed claims.

The music is a new score that quotes the chorus of [mise-en-place](https://mise.jdx.dev/mise-en-place.html) without vocals. The end card plays the song's own "It's mise-en-place for dev machines" line and its ending.

## It follows mise's Node LTS on its own

The two Node versions on screen come from the capture run, never from the code:
- one project uses the major that mise's `lts` alias resolves to (24 today);
- the other uses the newest major above it (26 today), or the previous LTS when there is none.

Captures are recorded with the newest mise release; a release's own docs build uses the version it publishes. So when a release moves the `lts` alias in `src/plugins/core/node.rs`, that release's docs build sees the new versions, re-records the scenes and re-renders the reel. Nobody edits

title: fix(config): keep edited configs untrusted with --yes in paranoid mode
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/320
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Paranoid mode currently honors global yes when a command asks to trust a config. For example, `MISE_PARANOID=1 MISE_YES=1 mise env` approves a new or edited file without a separate trust decision. This PR changes that behavior so content-bound trust still requires an explicit approval.

`MISE_YES=1`, `-y`, and CI auto-confirmation no longer approve config trust in paranoid mode. An unattended command fails on the untrusted file until it is reviewed and approved with `mise trust`; an interactive confirmation can still approve it. The paranoid-mode documentation explains this behavior.

Validation: the new e2e test covers new and edited configs with `MISE_YES=1`, `-y`, and CI; adjacent trust tests, the build, ShellCheck, workspace Clippy, and `mise run lint-fix` pass. The PR also applies Prettier's formatting to six tracked Entire runner JSON files that caused the repository-wide lint check to fail; their values are unchanged.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable/unavailable; version: 0.157.0.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes config trust boundaries in paranoid mode; scope is narrow and covered by a targeted e2e test, but mistaken gating could break unattended CI that relied on auto-trust.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Problem:** In paranoid mode, unattended “yes” paths (`--yes`, `MISE_YES=1`, CI auto-confirmation) could approve config trust during `trust_check`, including after a config edit invalidated the content hash.
> 
> **Solution:** `trust_check` only treats automatic yes as consent when **not** in paranoid mode; paranoid loads must fail until `mise trust` (or an interactive prompt) explicitly approves. `docs/paranoid.md` documents this, and `e2e/config/test_paranoid_yes_trust` asserts the behavior for new/edited configs across `MISE_YES`, `-y`, and `CI=1`.
> 
> Six `.entire/runners/*.json` files only reformat `trigger_types` arrays (Prettier).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 3a0c48285518a3a3d204b2e0bc32d78910362269. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * In paranoid mode, `--yes`, `MISE_YES=1`, and CI auto-confirmation no longer trust configuration files automatically. Untrusted files must be explicitly trusted before they can be loaded.
  * Editing a trusted configuration file revokes its trust. Review and explicitly trust the updated file before loading it again.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified how configuration trust works in paranoid mode, including the need to explicitly trust reviewed configuration for unattended runs.

title: fix(backend): preserve Go install errors for resolved versions
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/319
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When `go:golang.org/x/tools/gopls@latest` resolves to a semantic version such as `0.23.0`, a failed `go install ...@v0.23.0` used to trigger a second attempt at `...@0.23.0`. That invalid retry hid the original Go error. Mise now reports the original failure without retrying a version resolved from `latest`.

An explicitly requested unprefixed version such as `go:example.com/tool@1.2.3` still gets the unprefixed retry for repositories with tags that lack `v`. If both attempts fail, the error includes the original failure first and the retry failure afterward.

This also applies Prettier's existing formatting rule to six Entire runner JSON files. Their values are unchanged; the formatting clears a repository lint failure that appeared in this PR's CI run.

Validated with focused Go backend unit tests, a stubbed Go end-to-end test covering failed install attempts, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `mise run lint`.

Fixes #13793.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-6; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes Go tool install retry and error reporting on a common installation path; behavior is narrowed and covered by new unit and e2e tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Problem:** When a `go:` install resolved `@latest` to an unprefixed semver (e.g. `0.23.0`), a failed `go install …@v0.23.0` could trigger a second attempt at the same version without `v`, masking the real Go error.
> 
> **Solution:** Install now picks primary and optional fallback versions via `go_install_versions`, comparing the resolved version to what the user actually requested. Unprefixed semver retries without `v` only when the request explicitly used that exact unprefixed version (for repos whose tags omit `v`); resolved versions from `latest`/`v`-prefixed requests no longer get that retry. If both attempts run and fail, the error leads with the first failure and notes the retry. Semver detection uses `versions::SemVer` instead of a regex helper.
> 
> Adds unit tests for version selection and combined errors, plus an e2e script with a stub `go` binary to assert invocation counts and message text. Six `.entire/runners/*.json` files only reformat `trigger_types` arrays (behavior unchanged).
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit d3f50879a151015a7ec5b5c22d687639dd868111. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(dotfiles): identify history commits by machine
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/318
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Shared dotfiles history currently gives every mise commit the same `mise@localhost` email, making it hard to tell which machine saved a checkpoint in Git. This adds an opt-in email setting for history commits:

```toml
[history]
git_email = "mise@{hostname}"
```

On `work-mbp.local`, new commits use `mise <mise@work-mbp.local>` for both author and committer. The hostname is resolved when each commit is created, so one global configuration can be shared across machines. Manual saves, watcher saves, and mise-created merge commits use the setting. A fixed email also works. Without the setting, `mise@localhost` remains the default; existing commits are unchanged.

The setting is documented in the dotfiles history guide and configuration schema.

Validation: focused unit test, dotfiles history Git identity end-to-end test, `mise run lint-fix`, and workspace Clippy with all features and targets.

Related: https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13787

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Opt-in config with validation; only affects author/committer metadata on new local history commits, not auth or sync semantics.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds optional **`[history].git_email`** so new dotfiles history commits can show which machine created them instead of always using **`mise@localhost`**. Set a fixed address or **`mise@{hostname}`** in shared config; **`{hostname}`** is expanded at commit time from the machine name (Unix now prefers **`gethostname()`** via the **`nix`** **`hostname`** feature).
> 
> History **`commit-tree`** plumbing passes per-call **`GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL`** / **`GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL`** through new **`PlumbingCall::env`** overrides (blocked on network git calls). Manual saves, **`history-watch`**, and merge commits pick up the setting; existing commits are unchanged. Docs, schema, unit tests, and an e2e test cover default vs configured identity.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit a58467aff0cf14f0101db66210bd521657f52707. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(install): allow tool postinstall on every install
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/316
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A tool-level `postinstall` command normally runs only when mise installs or repairs that tool. If another config already installed the selected version, a project cannot use that command to set up the tool for its own workflow.

Add an opt-in mode that runs the command on every `mise install` selecting the tool, including when its version is already installed:

```toml
[tools]
node = { version = "26", postinstall = { run = "npm install -g corepack", when = "always" } }
```

The command runs once per selected tool request on each invocation. It does not record completion per config file. The existing string form and a table without `when` remain install-only. Dry runs do not execute the command, and an already-installed tool is not counted as a new installation. Safe mode continues to reject tool-level postinstall commands. The JSON schemas now accept the table form for editor validation.

Closes #13788.

Validation: `mise run render:schema`, schema validation for accepted and rejected `when` values, focused parser tests; end-to-end tests for an existing installation, repeated and explicit installs, `mise use` config writes, dry runs, failure propagation, existing string behavior, and safe mode; `mise run lint-fix`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-6; version: unavailable.*


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

* **New Features**
  * Post-install commands can now be configured to run on every explicit `mise install` for a selected tool, including when the tool is already installed.

* **Documentation**
  * Clarified how the new option differs from the existing command-string form, which runs after a fresh install or repair.

title: ci: report release checks for stacked pull requests
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/315
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stacked PRs targeting a feature branch can leave `release` and `release-window` unreported because both workflows only accept PRs targeting `main`. Remove the base-branch filters so those checks also report for stacked PRs, including #13785.

Ordinary feature PRs still skip release builds and receive `release-window: success`. The release-build gate now explicitly requires a same-repository `release` PR targeting `main`, preserving the restriction previously supplied by the trigger filter. The auto-merge build gate, quiet-hours policy, and shared-release-commit protection remain unchanged. Existing PRs need a fresh synchronize or reopen event after the updated workflows are available to populate missing statuses.

Validated with `mise run lint-fix`, the CI-equivalent high-severity zizmor scan, and local shell checks covering ordinary PRs, armed/unarmed release builds, an armed `release` PR targeting a feature branch, quiet hours, fork branches named `release`, and shared release commits.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI trigger and gate-expression changes only; release build eligibility is still explicitly limited to same-repo `release` → `main` PRs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Stacked PRs that target a feature branch instead of `main` no longer miss the **`release`** and **`release-window`** required checks, because both workflows drop the `pull_request` / `pull_request_target` **`branches: ["main"]`** filter and run for PRs against any base branch.
> 
> **Release tarball builds stay gated the same way in practice:** the `release` workflow’s gate job now requires **`github.base_ref == 'main'`** in addition to a same-repo **`release`** head branch, replacing the old “only PRs to `main`” behavior that lived entirely in the trigger. Non-release PRs still get a passing **`release-window`** status and do not arm expensive PGO builds unless auto-merge is enabled on a real release PR to **`main`**.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit faee444465332069a3d84579af9a9da1ce2f8cd9. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

title: feat(self-update): verify packslips against the mise repository ID
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/314
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise self-update` now verifies the release's signed packslip before replacing the executable. Releases from v2026.9.3 onward must provide a valid manifest: verification checks the archive digest and size, the selected version, the release workflow, and transparency-log evidence. The existing embedded archive signature remains required too.

The trust anchor is mise's immutable GitHub repository ID, `586920414`, checked against the signing certificate. The same repository can move between organizations or change its name; a different repository taking over its former name is rejected. Custom mirrors must preserve the original signed manifest and archives rather than supplying their own signer.

The minimum release age also applies to the verified log timestamp, including automatic updates. Explicit version pins bypass the delay. Older releases without a packslip remain installable with the existing signature verification. Missing or invalid manifests for modern releases fail without replacing mise; download progress is retained.

Adds real replacement coverage on Linux, macOS, and Windows: a shared integration test starts each case from a disposable copy of the CI build, installs current, first-packslip, and legacy releases, checks the binary changed, and executes the result. The CI binary itself remains untouched. Offline tests verify a published mise manifest and cover tampering, version/age mismatches, repository renames/transfers, wrong or missing repository IDs, and the legacy boundary.

Stacked on #13783 (native updater), which is stacked on #13782 (release-age policy).

Validation: 26 focused self-update tests, strict workspace/all-feature/all-target Clippy, lint, build, and macOS end-to-end tests for real replacement and release-age selection passed. Linux and Windows replacement runs are wired into CI. The test workflow also runs for stacked PRs targeting `codex/**` branches.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes the self-update trust path and binary replacement gate for all users on modern releases; misconfiguration or mirror issues could block updates, though failures are designed not to replace the running binary.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise self-update`** now requires a valid **packslip** (`packslip.sigstore.json`) for releases **v2026.9.3+**, in addition to the existing zipsign archive check. Before replacing the running binary, it verifies the manifest against the downloaded archive, the selected version, the **release workflow** signer, and the **Sigstore transparency-log** timestamp. Trust is pinned to GitHub repository ID **`586920414`**, so renames/transfers of the real repo still work while a name-squatter cannot substitute releases. Missing or invalid manifests for modern releases abort without touching the install;

title: refactor(self-update): use native downloads and signature verification
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/313
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise self-update` now downloads releases through mise's async HTTP client and displays download progress through mise's native progress renderer. This removes the `self_update` crate and ten packages from `Cargo.lock`, while retaining embedded release-signature verification and `self-replace` for replacing the running executable.

The update verifies the signed archive and extracts only its expected executable before replacement. HTTPS-only requests, redirect downgrade protection, macOS code-signing checks, Windows shim refresh, explicit versions, and the minimum-release-age policy remain supported. The existing `self_update` Cargo feature remains available.

Stacked on #13782; this PR's diff is only the updater refactor. Packslip verification is a separate possible follow-up.

Validated with 21 focused self-update tests (including signed tar/ZIP fixtures, tampering, filename binding, and unsafe archive entries), three self-update end-to-end tests, a build with self-update disabled, lint, and strict workspace/all-feature/all-target Clippy. Windows execution will be covered by CI.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Self-update replaces the running binary after signature verification; regressions in download, verification, or replacement could brick installs or accept bad artifacts.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise self-update` no longer uses the `self_update` crate.** Updates are implemented in `src/cli/self_update.rs` with mise’s async `reqwest` client, GitHub release/tag lookup, and the existing download progress UI.
> 
> After a **strict platform archive name** match, the flow downloads the asset, **verifies the zipsign signature** (filename-bound for tar/zip), **extracts only** `mise/bin/mise` (or `mise.exe`) as a regular file, optionally checks macOS code signing on the staged binary, then calls **`self-replace`**. HTTPS-only transport, redirect downgrade blocking, install-dir/TEMP preflight checks, confirmation/`--yes`, minimum release age, and Windows shim refresh are preserved.
> 
> **Dependencies:** `Cargo.toml` drops `self_update` and wires the `self_update` feature to optional `self-replace`, `tar`, and `zipsign-api` (fewer lockfile packages). **Tests:** new signed-archive/tampering/symlink/HTTPS unit tests; Windows e2e now asserts no release API call on long `TEMP` and uses the installed version for an offline “already up to date” path.
>

title: feat(self-update): apply minimum release age to mise updates and installs
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/312
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Unpinned `mise self-update` and mise.run installs now select the newest stable mise release published at least 24 hours ago. Automatic updates and update notifications use the same policy.

Reuse the existing `minimum_release_age` setting, with a mise-specific override in this PR:

```toml
[settings]
minimum_release_age = "7d"
self_update.minimum_release_age = "24h"
```

Precedence is `mise self-update --minimum-release-age` → `self_update.minimum_release_age` → `minimum_release_age` → `24h`. Environment overrides are `MISE_SELF_UPDATE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE` and `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE`. Use `0s` for immediate releases; explicit versions bypass the delay. An unpinned update never downgrades an already newer installation, including with `--force`.

```sh
mise self-update --minimum-release-age 0s
curl -fsSL https://mise.run | MISE_SELF_UPDATE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=7d sh
```

The bootstrap installer reads environment variables, not TOML files, and supports integer `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, and `w` durations. The native CLI also accepts the existing calendar durations and cutoff dates. Saving the installer no longer pins its default version; set `MISE_VERSION` for reproducible installs.

The publication workflow publishes a stable-release index with GitHub publication timestamps after checking release artifacts. The public installer is promoted only after that index is uploaded. Both default-source clients evaluate publication timestamps at runtime, including from the version-check cache, so releases age into eligibility without another deployment. Custom self-update mirrors use paginated GitHub API results. Failed lookups or malformed/missing publication metadata do not bypass the delay.

Validation: 32 focused Rust tests, 15 offline installer/publication tests, three CLI e2e tests (including mirror pagination and settings/cache precedence), strict workspace Clippy, lint checks, and regenerated CLI docs/schema. The production release index and public installer are deployed in that order by the updated publication workflow; neither has been deployed from this PR.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

title: feat(config): auto-install unconfigured registry bins on command not found
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/311
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

## Summary

The command-not-found handler can now install a tool even when no config has declared it. Set `not_found_auto_install_registry = true` to opt in; the default remains `false`.

```toml
[settings]
not_found_auto_install_registry = true
```

With this setting, running an unknown command such as `rtx-tiny` installs the uniquely matching registry tool (`tiny`) and records it in the global config. Registry aliases count as the same tool. The handler skips commands with multiple providers, disabled or OS-incompatible tools, and bins without a registry match. Configured tools continue to use the existing not-found installation path.

## Validation

- End-to-end tests for the new registry path and the existing configured-tool path; focused unit coverage for aliases, disabled tools, and OS compatibility
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Opt-in by default, but when enabled the handler can mutate global config and trigger installs from a mistyped command; ambiguity is guarded, yet wrong unique registry matches could still install unexpected tools.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **opt-in** shell command-not-found path: when `not_found_auto_install_registry` is `true` (default `false`, env `MISE_NOT_FOUND_AUTO_INSTALL_REGISTRY`), mise can install a tool that was never declared in config if **exactly one** enabled registry entry provides the missing binary.
> 
> After the existing configured-tool `install_missing_bin` flow fails, `hook-not-found` resolves the bin via new `registry_bin_provider` logic (respects `enable_tools` / `disable_tools`, `auto_install_disable_tools`, OS support, non-empty backends; registry aliases count as one tool; ambiguous bins are skipped). It then runs `Use::use_global_registry_tool`, equivalent to `mise use --global TOOL@latest`, and writes the tool into global config.
> 
> Supporting changes: public `RegistryTool::provides_bin`, `Use` gains `Default` and the internal global-use helper, plus schema/settings/docs/troubleshooting updates and e2e coverage for success, ambiguity, disabled tools, and opt-out when the setting is off.
>

Timoni and Worktrunk now publish signed packslips with their releases. `mise use timoni@0.35.0` and `mise use worktrunk@0.80.0` can install from the release manifests, verifying the workflow signature and artifact digest while also receiving the completions and version-matched skills declared by each project.

title: feat(lock): warn when old lockfile formats are overdue for upgrade
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/309
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When mise uses an active lockfile whose format was superseded more than six calendar months ago, it now warns during commands such as `mise install`, `mise exec`, and task runs. Even an install with no tools to resolve checks its active lockfiles. Lockfiles read through project tool stubs are covered, including projects outside the current config search. The warning names the file and gives the upgrade command for its scope: `mise lock --upgrade` for a project, or `mise lock --global --upgrade` for a global config. Legacy monorepo lockfiles point to the monorepo root. Each file is warned about once per process.

For example, format version 1 entered mise on August 23, 2026, so a version 0 lockfile starts warning on February 24, 2027. The format bump dates are recorded alongside the current lockfile version. If an active environment or platform lockfile has no matching config file, the warning explains that the config must be added before upgrading, or the lockfile removed if it is no longer needed.

Validation: `mise run lint-fix`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and the lockfile age boundary unit test passed.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/GPT-6; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> User-facing warnings only; no change to lock resolution or install semantics beyond deduplicated notice logic and a small refactor of which paths are read.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **outdated lockfile format warnings** when mise touches active lockfiles whose `lockfile_version` is more than six calendar months behind a newer on-disk format. Version bump dates live in `LOCKFILE_VERSION_DATES` next to `CURRENT_LOCKFILE_VERSION`; `warn_outdated_lockfiles` scans env/platform lock paths (via shared `active_lockfile_paths_in_dir`), legacy monorepo locks, and tool-stub sources, emits **once per config** through `LockfileDiscovery` atomics, and suggests scope-specific `mise lock --upgrade` (or config cleanup when a lock has no matching `mise.toml`).
> 
> Warnings run from lockfile read paths (`read_all_lockfiles`, per-config reads) and are **explicitly invoked on `mise install`** so bare installs still check even with nothing to resolve. **`mise lock`** calls `suppress_outdated_lockfile_warning` so upgrade runs do not double-notify. Lockfile loading reuses the new path helper instead of duplicating precedence-order enumeration.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/308

A machine can now select its mise environment in `~/.config/mise/miserc.local.toml` without changing a shared global `miserc.toml` or adding a file to every project:

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/miserc.local.toml

Project miserc files, `MISE_ENV`, and `-E` retain their existing precedence. title: test(upgrade): cover --bump keeping short versions short
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/305
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Adds an e2e test that `mise upgrade --bump` keeps a short version short when that version still covers the latest release. It installs the newer release but leaves the config line as it is.

With releases `19.0.0 20.0.0 20.5.0 20.5.3`:

| config | installed | after `mise upgrade --bump` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `prefixtest = "20"` | `20.0.0` | installs `20.5.3`, config stays `"20"` |
| `prefixtest = "20.5"` | `20.5.0` | installs `20.5.3`, config stays `"20.5"` |

mise already behaves this way, but no test covered it. jdx/mise#13759 would have changed it without CI noticing: its fallback in `outdated_info.rs` turns the "no config change needed" result into the full latest version for any plain version request, so `"20"` would be rewritten to `"20.5.3"`.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e test_upgrade_bump_keeps_prefix` passes on main.
- With #13759's `src/toolset/outdated_info.rs` change applied, the test fails with `Would bump prefixtest@20.5.3 in ~/workdir/mise.toml`.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# `--bump` keeps the specificity of a version request. When the request still
+# covers the latest release, upgrading installs that release but leaves the
+# config alone rather than pinning it (e.g. "20" must not become "20.5.3").

title: test(dotfiles): fix flaky timeout in retrack prompt test
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/304
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`cli/test_dotfiles_retrack` could fail with `track prompt timed out` a few seconds into the test, well before its 10-second deadline. It failed that way twice in a row on jdx/mise#13759, whose changes don't touch dotfiles.

The prompt check drives `mise dot track` through a pty. When mise exits and closes its end, the next pty read fails and the loop breaks. The script then checked once with `process.poll()`. On a busy runner, mise can close the pty just before it can be reaped, so that check still saw it running, and the script killed it and reported a timeout.

The script now calls `process.wait()` for whatever remains of the original deadline, and reports a timeout only if that wait expires.

This only changes the test; mise's behavior is unchanged.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e test_dotfiles_retrack` passes locally on macOS. The race wasn't reproduced locally, so the evidence for the fix is the diagnosis above.

title: chore(deps): update gix to 0.88
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/303
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Updates gix from 0.87.1 to 0.88.0, along with the rest of the gix family and gix's new `sha1dc` dependency. mise uses gix to read its history repository (`src/system/history`). Users should see no change in behavior.

This unblocks the weekly lock maintenance PR (#13767). mise declares `gix = "<1"`, so that refresh already picked up 0.88. mise then stopped compiling on every platform, because gix 0.88 returns `gix::Exn` from several APIs: topo traversal, `CommitRef::message_raw`, and `ObjectId::from_hex`. `Exn` does not implement `std::error::Error`, so `?` can no longer convert it to an eyre error:

```
error[E0277]: `?` couldn't convert the error: `Exn: StdError` is not satisfied
   --> src/system/history/shadow.rs:733:21
```

The six call sites (five in `shadow.rs` and one in a `manifest.rs` test) now convert with `Exn::into_error()`. That returns `gix::Error`, which implements `std::error::Error`, and keeps gix's error chain intact.

Validation: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo +1.95 check` (the MSRV) pass, all 252 `system::history` unit tests pass, and `cargo deny check` is clean.

title: chore(deps): refresh markdownlint-cli's locked dependencies
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/301
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Refreshes the npm packages that markdownlint-cli 0.49.1 pulls in, which the repo uses for linting. Three of them had new releases: `ansi-regex` 6.4.0, `ignore` 7.0.10, and `micromark-factory-space` 2.1.0. markdownlint-cli itself is still 0.49.1, the latest release.

This also unblocks the weekly lock maintenance PR (#13767). Renovate ran the same `mise lock --bump`, which rewrote `.mise/locks/npm-markdownlint-cli/0.49.1/aube-lock.yaml` and put its new digest in `mise.lock`. Renovate's mise manager only commits `mise.lock`, though, so that branch has the new digest next to the old file. Every `mise install --locked` there fails with:

```
dependency sidecar .mise/locks/npm-markdownlint-cli/0.49.1: digest mismatch; run `mise lock` to accept the edited graph
```

This PR commits the regenerated file and its digest together. `mise lock --bump npm:markdownlint-cli` on main reproduces Renovate's digest exactly (`sha256:6fcd571b…`). `mise install --locked npm:markdownlint-cli` succeeds on this branch.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.281.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> Refreshes the **mise** sidecar lock for `npm:markdownlint-cli` **0.49.1** (the tool version is unchanged) by regenerating `.mise/locks/npm-markdownlint-cli/0.49.1/aube-lock.yaml` and updating the matching **aube digest** in `mise.lock`.

title: fix(npm): pass minimum release age in kebab-case for pnpm 12
body:
When `npm.package_manager = "pnpm"`, mise passes `minimum_release_age` to pnpm so the cutoff also applies to transitive dependencies. It sent the value as `--config.minimumReleaseAge=<minutes>`. pnpm 12 ignores that spelling without a warning, so it resolved transitive dependencies with its built-in default (1440 minutes) instead of the configured value. A `7d` cutoff was not enforced, and `0` did not turn the filter off.

mise now sends `--config.minimum-release-age=<minutes>`, which works on pnpm 10.16+, 11, and 12.

```toml
[settings.npm]
package_manager = "pnpm"

[tools]
"npm:some-package" = { version = "latest", minimum_release_age = "7d" }
```

The top-level package version was not affected: mise applies the cutoff itself before calling pnpm.

## Cause

pnpm 11 and earlier converted every `--config.<key>` to camelCase, so both spellings worked. pnpm 12's Rust CLI matches `--config.` keys exactly against a kebab-case table and drops unknown keys silently. pnpm's [CLI docs](https://pnpm.io/pnpm-cli) only show kebab-case keys with the `--config.` 

## Repro

`autoprefixer@10.6.1` (published 13 days ago) depends on `caniuse-lite@^1.0.30001810`. At test time, `caniuse-lite` 1.0.30001812 was 4 days old and 1.0.30001810 was 35 days old.

```toml
[settings]
npm.package_manager = "pnpm"

[tools]
pnpm = "12.7.0"
"npm:autoprefixer" = { version = "latest", minimum_release_age = "7d" }
```
	
`MISE_DEBUG=1 mise install` runs, show:
	
```
DEBUG $ pnpm add --global autoprefixer@10.6.1 --config.minimumReleaseAge=10080
```

| pnpm | Installed `caniuse-lite` |
| --- | --- |
| 10.34.5 | 1.0.30001810 (35 days old) |
| 12.7.0, before this fix | **1.0.30001812 (4 days old)** |
| 12.7.0, with `--config.minimum-release-age=10080` | 1.0.30001810 (35 days old) |

On pnpm 12 the 7-day cutoff is ignored with no warning, and a 4-day-old transitive dependency is installed.

Until this fix is released, pnpm 12 users can pass the setting themselves:

```toml
"npm:autoprefixer" = { version = "latest", minimum_release_age = "7d", pnpm_args = "--config.minimum-release-age=10080" }
```

body:
`e2e-win/task_ctrl_c.Tests.ps1` could quietly skip, or fail for a reason unrelated to mise, depending on how the test host was started:

- **Silent skip in a windowless console.** The test checked for a console with `GetConsoleWindow`, which returns null for a console created with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (for example, when an IDE or agent runs `pwsh` in the background). `AllocConsole` then fails because a console is already attached, so the test was skipped even though it could raise the control event. It now checks `GetConsoleCP() != 0`, which is non-zero whenever a console is attached, windowed or not.
- **`sleeper.cmd` not found.** The task ran `sleeper.cmd` by bare name. `cmd.exe` does not search the current directory when `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath` is set, so the task never started and the test failed at "the task should start". The task now runs `.\sleeper.cmd`.

What the test checks is unchanged.

## Validation

On Windows 11, in a windowless console with `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1`, running the test file with Pester:

| Version of the test | Result |
|---|---|
| before | Skipped: "the test host has no console to raise a control event on" |
| console check fixed only | Failed: "Expected $true, because the task should start" |
| both fixes | Passed |

title: fix(brew): prepend the shim's `Pathname#write` override
body:
The source-build shim reopened `Pathname` and defined `write` to create missing parent directories before calling `super`. Reopening the class replaces the core `Pathname#write` rather than wrapping it, so `super` has nothing to reach and every call raised:

    super: no superclass method 'write' for an instance of Pathname

Any formula that writes through `Pathname#write` failed after its build finished, most visibly via `generate_completions_from_executable` (e.g. starship after `cargo install`) and `inreplace`. This is independent of the Ruby version; it reproduces on 3.4 and 4.0.

Move the override into a module prepended onto `Pathname`, matching Homebrew's `WriteMkpathExtension`, and forward arguments with `(...)` so keyword options such as `mode:` reach the core method.

title: chore(ci): run clippy on Windows and fix the lints only it finds
body:
CI runs Clippy on Linux only. `#[cfg]` decides whether code exists, so Windows-only code was never linted: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` on a Windows checkout failed with four errors that CI could not see.

This adds a `windows-lint` job that runs that command on `windows-latest`, and fixes the four errors so it starts green.

## CI

`windows-lint` runs alongside `windows-unit` instead of inside it, so it does not add to the Windows test job's time (13–21 minutes on recent `main` runs, with a 40-minute limit). It runs when full CI runs, like the other Windows jobs, and `test-ci` requires it.

It uses default features. `--all-features` does not build on Windows without NASM, which `aws-lc-sys` needs, and feature combinations are already linted on Linux.

## Fixes

| Location | Lint | Change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/packslip/completions.rs` | `chunks_exact` with a constant size | `as_chunks::<2>()` |
| `src/shims.rs` | `needless_return` | Return value as the block's tail |
| `src/system/remote.rs` | `permissions_set_readonly_false` | Clear only the read-only attribute with `SetFileAttributesW`, which is what `set_readonly(false)` does on Windows, on the `\\?\`-prefixed canonical path so paths past MAX_PATH work as they do with std. New Windows tests for making a read-only directory writable and restoring it, including one nested past 260 characters. |
| `src/system/service_exec.rs` | `disallowed_methods` (`std::process::exit`) | New `exit::exit_with_windows_status`, see below |

The service launcher relays a service's whole 32-bit status to Task Scheduler. `exit::status` narrows to a byte, and a stable `ExitCode` cannot hold more: `ExitCodeExt::from_raw` is still unstable (rust-lang/rust#111688, rejected by rustc 1.98.1). `exit_with_windows_status` flushes stdout and calls `ExitProcess`, which is what `std::process::exit` does on Windows (`rt::cleanup` flushes stdout, then `sys::exit` calls `ExitProcess(code as u32)`), so the behavior is unchanged. It is kept to processes that only relay another's status and have nothing left to unwind.

## Validation

On Windows 11:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --ignore-rust-version -- -D warnings`, the command the new job runs, passes after rebasing onto current `main`. Before the fixes it reported the four errors above.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib -- system::remote::tests packslip::completions shims::` passes (67 tests), including the new Windows test.
- The workflow change itself has not run yet; this PR's CI is its first run.

title: feat(task): add aliases for monorepo task paths
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/298
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Deeply nested monorepo projects can now have short task paths. Define an alias for a configured root, then use it with any task in that root:

```toml
monorepo_root = true

[monorepo]
config_roots = ["foo/bar/baz/abc/123"]

[monorepo.path_aliases]
"123" = "foo/bar/baz/abc/123"
```

`mise run //123:build` runs the existing `//foo/bar/baz/abc/123:build` task. Aliases also work for task dependencies, patterns such as `//123:*`, and child paths. Tasks retain their full path as their canonical identity. Aliases must name a configured root and cannot overlap an existing root path.

This addresses [discussion #13753](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13753).

Validation: `mise run test:e2e test_task_monorepo_path_aliases`; existing monorepo config-root, dependency, and alias-precedence e2e tests; `mise run lint-fix`; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes monorepo task discovery, caching, and alias resolution, but behavior is opt-in and guarded by strict config validation.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`[monorepo.path_aliases]`** so configured monorepo roots can be referenced with a single-segment shortcut (e.g. `//123:build` → `//foo/bar/baz/abc/123:build`). Full paths stay canonical; aliases are also registered on tasks for listing, dependencies, patterns like `//123:*`, and nested paths such as `//123/sub:build`.
> 
> Config loading validates aliases (require `config_roots`, single segment, in-repo target, no overlap with real roots including globs/symlinks) and merges layered `mise.toml` values. Task loading expands aliases in **path hints** and the tasks cache key, then synthesizes alias task names after workspace resolution. The alias lookup map treats explicit `//…` alias names as first-class keys.
> 
> Documentation and JSON schema describe the new table; a dedicated e2e script covers run, info, conflicts, and inferred workspace tasks.
>

title: fix(brew): unpack source archives whose URL names no extension
body:
Formula sources were staged by file name alone. A URL such as GitHub's `https://codeload.github.com/<owner>/<repo>/tar.gz/refs/tags/v0.0.23` has no extension, so `ExtractionFormat::from_file_name` returned `Raw` and the tarball was copied into the build directory unextracted. The formula's `install` then ran against a lone gzip file, e.g. `go build` failing with "go.mod file not found". `brew` handles these by falling back to the file's content when the name is inconclusive.

This surfaced building `cf-vault` from my custom tap, whose `url` is a codeload URL: https://github.com/jacobbednarz/homebrew-tap/blob/b03141211969573bb4b4fcc9c3016ba04e5898ec/Formula/cf-vault.rb

Add `ExtractionFormat::detect`, which keeps the name's verdict when it has one and otherwise sniffs the leading bytes via `ExtractionFormat::from_magic`: zip, or a gzip/xz/bzip2/zstd/plain stream whose payload opens with a ustar header. Requiring the tar header keeps bare compressed files and binaries staged as-is. Formula source staging uses it, and it replaces the cask fetcher's zip-only `detect_extraction_format`, so suffixless tarballs in casks are unpacked too rather than copied as a raw binary.

The shim's `MiseDownload.unpack`, which stages formula resources, had the same name-only check; it now falls back to the zip magic or a `tar tf` probe.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Archives can now be recognized by their contents when they don’t have a known file extension, including tar archives compressed with gzip, xz, bzip2, or zstd.
  * Package and source downloads can extract extensionless ZIP and tar archives; unrecognized files are preserved as-is.
* **Bug Fixes**
  * Empty files and non-archive files are no longer mistaken for tar archives.

title: fix(dotfiles): allow explicit plaintext tracking of credential-like files
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/296
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A file such as `commit-mossy-token.md` matches mise's credential-name guard. Previously, `mise dot track` could report that it was tracking the file while every history save omitted it.

`mise dot track ~/commit-mossy-token.md` now asks whether to save that directly tracked file in plaintext, with **No** as the default. Declining leaves the file undeclared. For scripts and other noninteractive use, the explicit choice is:

```sh
mise dot track --allow-plaintext ~/commit-mossy-token.md
```

The choice is recorded as `allow_plaintext = true` on that file's `[dotfiles]` entry and in shared enrollment metadata. It can also approve a file before it exists. Later saves capture it and warn that the credential-like file may be shared with an origin. `--yes` does not approve plaintext tracking. For actual credentials, use `mise dot track --encrypt` with encryption recipients configured. The existing filter for files found inside a tracked directory remains in place.

Older mise versions cannot read enrollment metadata carrying this new field, so upgrade machines sharing the history before using the option.

## Validation

title: fix(lock): record forge IDs in lockfile revision 3
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/288
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Packslip lockfile entries can record forge repository identity in an inline table under lockfile revision 3:

```toml
lockfile_version = 3

[tools.hk."platforms.linux-x64"]
repository_ids = { repository = "922514152", owner = "216188" }
```

`owner` is omitted when the signing certificate does not provide it. The repository ID keeps the signature commitment tied to the same GitHub or GitLab repository across renames; the owner ID also detects transfers when available.

New and empty lockfiles use revision 3. Existing lockfiles keep their revision during ordinary writes. If a revision 2 write encounters verified forge IDs, mise warns and omits those revision 3 fields. Run `mise lock --upgrade` when ready to adopt revision 3 and store them. The repository's own `mise.lock` stays at revision 2 until a revision 3 capable mise is released, so CI can install tools with the released binary. The unreleased flat `repository_id` and `repository_owner_id` lockfile fields are rejected rather than silently ignored; the five such entries in this repository's revision 2 lockfile have been removed pending its explicit upgrade after release.

Packslip plugin state is stored separately from `mise.lock`. Its reader accepts previously installed plugins with flat forge IDs, while new plugin state writes the grouped ID shape. This preserves plugin listing, reinstall, and update through the lockfile format change.

Validated with 105 focused lockfile unit tests, the plugin state regression test, strict workspace Clippy, generated-docs checks, and focused lockfile, Packslip, npm, and Python end-to-end tests. The five e2e selectors affected by this change passed locally. An additional npm test matched by a broad selector failed on macOS because it uses unsupported `find -printf`; the intended npm lockfile test passed.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

* **New Features**

title: security(sigstore): require expected SLSA signer identity
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/277
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

SLSA provenance verification now requires the expected Fulcio certificate URI identity and OIDC issuer. A valid Sigstore signature from an unrelated workflow can no longer satisfy SLSA verification for a tool.

For a GitHub release whose workflow is tied to the release tag:

```toml
[tools]
"github:myorg/mytool" = { version = "latest", slsa_signer_identity = "https://github.com/myorg/mytool/.github/workflows/release.yml@refs/tags/v{{version}}", slsa_signer_issuer = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" }
```

Aqua registry entries can provide `signer_identity` and `signer_issuer` in `slsa_provenance`. vfox plugins can return `slsa_signer_identity` and `slsa_signer_issuer` alongside `slsa_provenance_path` in their `PreInstall` attestation.

During migration, mise skips SLSA when those fields are absent and can use other available verification. The bundled Aqua registry currently has 62 packages with SLSA metadata but no signer fields; their SLSA check is skipped until metadata is added. An existing lockfile requiring SLSA fails clearly when the expected signer is absent. SLSA lock entries are always reverified against the current signer, even when a checksum is present. This repo's sops lock entries have been refreshed to omit unconfigured SLSA while retaining their checksums.

Validated with the mise-sigstore test suite, focused Aqua/GitHub/vfox tests, lockfile provenance e2e tests, `mise run lint-fix`, and strict workspace Clippy. This PR builds on #13717, which only reorganizes the sigstore crate.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes core artifact verification and lockfile semantics for installs; misconfigured or legacy SLSA locks can fail until signer metadata is added, but the behavior closes accepting unrelated valid Sigstore signatures.
> 
> **Overview**
> **SLSA provenance verification now binds to an expected publishing workflow**, not only Sigstore trust and artifact digests. Callers must supply a Fulcio certificate URI identity and OIDC issuer (`SlsaSignerIdentity`); after chain validation, `verify_slsa_signer_certificate` rejects mismatched signers for both Sigstore bundles and DSSE envelopes.
> 
> **Configuration surfaces:** Aqua `slsa_provenance` gains `signer_identity` / `signer_issuer`; the GitHub backend adds `slsa_signer_identity` / `slsa_signer_issuer` (with version templating); vfox `PreInstall` attestation accepts the same pair with paired-field validation. **Without both fields, SLSA is skipped** at install/lock time rather than accepting any valid Fulcio cert.
> 
> **Lockfile and install behavior:** SLSA is no longer skipped when a checksum+provenance lock exists—signer policy is always re-checked. Locks omit SLSA when signer metadata is missing; locks that still require SLSA fail with actionable errors if

- **Faster repeated fresh installs** ([#​1631](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1631) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): When the OSV Bloom filter flags a package that turns out to have no malicious advisory, aube used to confirm it with a live OSV query on every install. That added about 220–250 ms each time. aube now caches a clean result for 30 seconds. A cached result is reused only when both the exact package/version pairs and the validated Bloom filter match. On a warmed Svelte fixture, installing with `node_modules` and `aube-lock.yaml` removed went from a 346 ms median to 107 ms.
  - Failed OSV queries, failed Bloom filter refreshes and confirmed malicious hits are never cached.
  - Explicit `add`/`update`/`dlx` checks, `advisoryCheck = required` and `advisoryCheckEveryInstall = true` still query OSV live every time.
  - **Tradeoff:** if a malicious-package advisory is published for a version that was just cleared, a repeated ordinary install may take up to 30 seconds to catch it.
- **About 0.6 ms faster startup on Linux** ([#​1625](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1625) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): The Linux GNU release binaries (x86\_64 and aarch64) for `aube`, `aubr` and `aubx` are now linked as non-PIE. The loader no longer has to patch about 56k pointers at each launch, so `aube --version` drops from about 2.2 ms to 1.6 ms.
  - **Tradeoff:** ASLR no longer randomizes aube's own code and data. The heap, stack and shared libraries are still randomized.
  - musl, macOS and Windows builds are unchanged, as are `cargo install`, source builds and the PPA/COPR packages.

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/98be8d1ba7d861d6fceecf6cc3857f43592e4b76...v2.5.1>

title: fix(task): make `mise run --no-timings` hide each task's elapsed time again
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/270
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise run --no-timings` is documented to "hide the elapsed time printed after each task completes", but since v2025.11.2 it has only hidden the run's total. Each task still printed its own timing line (mise 2026.9.12):

```console
$ mise run --no-timings a ::: b
[a] $ echo a-out
[b] $ echo b-out
[b] b-out
[a] a-out
[b] Finished in 1.6ms
[a] Finished in 1.8ms
```

With this fix, `--no-timings` hides both kinds of timing line again:

```console
$ mise run --no-timings a ::: b
[b] $ echo b-out
[a] $ echo a-out
[a] a-out
[b] b-out
```

`--no-timings` also overrides `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=1` and the hidden `--timings` flag, as it did before the regression, and nested `mise run` calls inside a task get `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=0` even when both flags are passed. `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=0` is unchanged: it hides the per-task lines and keeps the run's total, which #5175 made deliberate.

## Cause

When the executor was split out of `run.rs` (#6852), the per-task gate went from `self.timings() && …` to `self.timings || …`. `timings()` is the method that checks `--no-timings` and `--quiet`; `timings` is the field that holds the `--timings` flag. `--quiet` was wired back in by #10885, but `--no-timings` never reached the executor. This PR passes it through and checks it first.

## Testing

`e2e/tasks/test_task_no_timings` covers the parallel run with and without `--no-timings`, `--no-timings` against `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=1` and `--timings` (directly and through a nested `mise run`), and `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=0` keeping the total. Each `--no-timings` assertion fails without the matching executor change. The existing output-style, raw-output and keep-order task e2e tests pass. A manual comparison across `-j 8` and `-j 1`, `a ::: b` and a `depends` task, and each `MISE_TASK_TIMINGS` value changed only the `--no-timings` cases.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.281.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow CLI-to-executor wiring and output gating for task timing lines; covered by new e2e tests with no security or data-handling impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise run --no-timings`** again suppresses each task’s **“Finished in …”** line (not only the run total), matching documented behavior after the task executor split stopped honoring the flag.
> 
> The CLI **`no_timings`** value is passed into **`TaskExecutorConfig`** / **`TaskExecutor`**. **`task_timings()`** returns false when **`no_timings`** is set, so it overrides **`--timings`**, **`MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=1`**, and per-task timing defaults—including for nested **`mise run`** via **`MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=0`** in the child env. **`MISE_TASK_TIMINGS=0`** behavior (hide per-task lines, keep run total) is unchanged.
>

https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/268
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Two pages of the task docs described defaults that `settings.toml` and the code no longer use.

**Default job count.** [Running tasks](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/running-tasks.html) and [Task architecture](https://mise.jdx.dev/tasks/architecture.html) both said tasks run with at most 4 parallel jobs by default. The `jobs` setting has defaulted to `8` since #3409. Both pages now say 8. The architecture page's examples (`--jobs 8`, `jobs = 8`) repeated the new default, so they now show `--jobs 16` and `jobs = 4`.

**Default task output mode.** The redaction warning in [Environments](https://mise.jdx.dev/environments/) said `mise run` defaults to the `replacing` output mode and suggested switching to `prefix` or `interleave` in CI. The actual default is `prefix` when tasks run in parallel (`jobs` > 1) and `interleave` when `jobs` is 1 or all tasks run sequentially (`OutputHandler::output`). Both print full output with redactions applied. The warning now says that, and keeps the CI advice only for `replacing` and `timed`, which don't print every line. The note that redactions need a non-`raw` output mode is unchanged. The `task.output = "prefix"` config example is gone, because it only restated the default.

Docs-only; `hk run check` (markdownlint, prettier) passes on the changed files.

Blob-pack downloads now retry transient stream failures when the HTTP error is wrapped as an I/O error. Previously those failures bypassed the remote cache retry policy, even though ordinary blob downloads retried the same class of failure.

The shared remote cache crate is also divided into protocol data, client requests, blob-pack decoding, credentials, and retry modules. This keeps each part reviewable as the cache grows while preserving its public API and wire behavior.

title: fix(daemons): start task daemons without a shell so they work on Windows
body:
On Windows, a daemon declared with `task =` never started. `mise daemons start` reported `failed with exit code 1`, and pitchfork's log showed cmd.exe's `'exec' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. Daemons declared with `run` were not affected.

```toml
[settings]
experimental = true

[tasks.hello]
run = "ping -n 60 127.0.0.1"

[daemons.hello]
task = "hello"
```

mise registered a task daemon as the POSIX command line `exec '<mise>' run 'hello'`. Since pitchfork 2.26.0, `run` strings go through `cmd /C` on Windows by default, and neither `exec` nor the single quotes work there.

mise now registers a task daemon with an argv `run`, which pitchfork 2.28.0 starts without any shell:

```toml
[daemons.hello]
run = ['C:\Users\me\AppData\Local\Programs\mise\bin\mise.exe', "run", "hello"]
```

The task starts the same way whether pitchfork's shell is `cmd /C`, `sh -c` or `pwsh -Command`, on every platform, and `args` reach the task exactly as written, with no quoting. On Unix this replaces the `exec` command line with the same process, so the tracked PID is still mise's.

## Requirements

Task daemons now need pitchfork 2.28.0 or later. When mise registers a project that has a task daemon, it checks this by reading `pitchfork schema` rather than comparing version numbers, and an older pitchfork fails with:

```text
daemon hello runs a task, which needs pitchfork 2.28.0 or later; upgrade pitchfork, for example with `mise use pitchfork@latest`
```

The check also runs again when the pitchfork changes, whether a project pins an older one or a package manager replaces the executable in place, even if the generated configuration has not changed. Projects without task daemons are not affected. mise uses the latest pitchfork unless a project pins one.

## Not covered

A task daemon with `init` still runs as a shell command line (`<init steps> && exec mise run ...` under `mise x`), because the setup steps and the task share one shell. That form still does not work under Windows' `cmd /C`.

## Validation

On Windows 11 with a debug build and pitchfork 2.28.0:

- The configuration above reaches `running` under the default `cmd /C`, with `PITCHFORK_WINDOWS_SHELL='sh -c'`, and with `PITCHFORK_WINDOWS_SHELL='pwsh -Command'`.
- With `pitchfork = "2.27.0"` in `[tools]`, `mise daemons start hello` fails with the message above. Registering with 2.28.0 and then pinning 2.27.0 also gives this message on the next `mise run`, instead of pitchfork's `config::parse_error`.
- New `e2e-win/daemons_task.Tests.ps1`: a task daemon with `args = ["a b", "x&y"]` receives both arguments unchanged. It fails with mise 2026.9.15 (`'exec' is not recognized`) and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p mise --lib daemons::` passes (146 tests), including the new schema check against the shapes pitchfork 2.27.0 and 2.28.0 print.
- `e2e/cli/test_daemons` now also checks the generated argv and the old-pitchfork error. It was not run locally; CI covers it, along with the work

title: chore: use aube and Node instead of Bun for the repo's own tooling
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/266
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise's own repository tooling now uses aube and Node instead of Bun. Contributors no longer need Bun to build the docs or run `mise run render`. Nothing changes for mise users: the `bun` core plugin and `npm.package_manager = "bun"` are unaffected.

- **Docs dependencies:** `mise run docs:setup` and CI run `aube install` in place of `bun i`. `aube-lock.yaml` replaces `bun.lock`, and `bun` is removed from `mise.toml`.
- **TypeScript scripts:** `docs/.vitepress/llms.ts`, `docs/.vitepress/cli-reference.ts`, and `xtasks/render/schema.ts` now run on Node 24, which strips types natively. The CLI reference test runs with `node --test`. Node requires explicit `.ts` extensions and `import type` for type-only imports, so three imports changed to match.
- **Renovate:** added the shared `aube-lock` workflow (the same one hk and usage use). Renovate's npm manager doesn't update `aube-lock.yaml`, so this workflow regenerates it on Renovate branches.
- **mr-boxington:** bumped to 1.19.0 in `mise.lock`.

## Lockfile migration

`aube import` can't read `bun.lock` (it rejects lockfile version 2, which Bun 1.4 writes). Setting the version to 1 lets the import finish, and it pins the same 331 package versions, but the result can't satisfy peer dependencies: `bun.lock` doesn't record which copy fills each peer, so `vitepress-plugin-mermaid` never gets its `mermaid` peer and `vitepress build` fails. This lockfile is a fresh `aube install` resolve instead. It stays within the existing `package.json` ranges, but about 70 packages move by a patch or minor version (for example vue 3.5.42 → 3.5.43, rollup 4.63.1 → 4.63.5). `aube-workspace.yaml` marks `core-js-pure`'s build script as not allowed. That script only prints a funding banner, and Bun didn't run it either.

- `mise run docs:build` passes: 414 pages, social image checks included.
- `node docs/.vitepress/llms.ts` writes a `docs/public/llms.txt` identical to the one Bun wrote.
- `node docs/.vitepress/cli-reference.ts` gives the same output as `bun` on the same input.
- `node xtasks/render/schema.ts` leaves `schema/` unchanged.
- The CLI reference tests pass (3 of 3) under `node --test`.
- `mise run lint` passes, including `cargo check` with mbx 1.19.0.

The `aube-lock` workflow depends on the `AUBE_LOCK_APP_ID` and `AUBE_LOCK_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` secrets being available to this repo. Without them it falls back to `GITHUB_TOKEN`: that still fixes the lockfile, but the fix-up commit won't re-trigger CI.

body:

The `mise-bootstrap` planner now owns the rules that order managed files around packages, link resources to declared users and groups, and order files and directories against managed parent directories. Mise still gathers host state and supplies resource declarations to the planner. The Linux and non-Linux account adapters share the crate's account state type, and managed files use its managed state type.

title: fix(packslip): follow transferred repositories, and document installing mise with packslip
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/264
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise refused a `packslip:` tool whose GitHub or GitLab repository had been transferred to another owner, even though it was the same repository (same repository ID) signed by the same workflow. packslip 1.5.0 follows a transfer by the forge's repository ID, the same way it follows a rename, and refuses only a re-created name: a different repository that took a deleted one's name. This moves mise onto packslip 1.5.0 from crates.io and adopts that rule.

## What users see

**A transferred repository keeps installing.** If `jdx/hk` moves to `acme/hk`, a config that names either one installs releases signed as `acme/hk`, with the usual one-time "was renamed to …" warning. A transfer needs no acceptance: only the repository's current owner can transfer it, and that owner already signs its releases. `mise self-update` drops its own transfer exception for the same reason; it still pins mise's repository ID and release workflow.

**A refusal says which record to clear.** mise holds a release to this machine's pin (`packslip/pins.toml`) and to `mise.lock`. When the release comes from a different repository ID, the advice now covers every record that disagrees, not only the first one checked:

```
packslip:github.com/jdx/hk: this release was signed by github.com/jdx/hk as GitHub repository ID 922514152, but mise pinned GitHub repository ID 1 for it. The name now belongs to a different repository, as it would if the original was deleted and someone else created one under its name, so mise refuses it.

If the vendor re-created the repository itself, run `mise packslip forget github.com/jdx/hk` and install again.
```

A disagreeing `mise.lock` gives "remove the tool's entries from mise.lock" instead, and when both disagree the advice gives both steps.

**`mise lock` accepts a transferred repository's signer** when the repository ID and workflow path are unchanged, using packslip's `forge::same_workflow` rather than mise's own copy of that comparison.

## Installing mise with packslip

The installation guide gains a [packslip](https://packslip.dev) method that installs mise's signed release without running an install script:

```sh
packslip install github.com/jdx/mise --pin ps1_nlhmwtfeufglxv5myvwvronk7a
```

packslip checks the release's Sigstore signature and transparency-log entry against mise's GitHub repository, checks the archive's digest, and links `mise` into `~/.local/bin` (`/usr/local/bin` as root). packslip itself comes from its signed APT or RPM repository. The pin is the fingerprint of mise's repository (from `packslip pin` on the v2026.10.1 bundle). It stays the same across renames, transfers, and releases, and a recreated repository under the name does not match it. `mise self-update` works in this installation.

## Compatibility

- `mise.lock` revision 3 keeps the same shape. `repository_ids.owner` is still read but is no longer part of the

title: fix(rust): keep `cargo +nightly` working when rust@nightly installs a dated toolchain
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/262
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Since 2026.8.6, `rust = "nightly"` installs a dated toolchain such as `nightly-2026-09-26` so installs are reproducible. As a side effect, rustup no longer had a toolchain named `nightly`, so `cargo +nightly` broke ([reported in #4737](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/4737#discussioncomment-18622261)):

```
$ mise use -q rust@nightly
$ RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 cargo +nightly check
error: toolchain 'nightly-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu' is not installed
```

With rustup's auto-install left on, the same command quietly downloaded a second, unpinned nightly instead.

Now, after installing the dated nightly for a rolling `nightly` request, mise also gives rustup a `nightly-<host>` toolchain made from it, so `cargo +nightly` runs the same pinned nightly with no extra download:

```
$ mise use -q rust@nightly
$ RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0 cargo +nightly -V
cargo 1.101.0-nightly (3d7cf6e93 2026-09-25)
```

## Behavior

- mise only writes `nightly-<host>` when it is missing, older than the nightly just installed, or the same nightly without all of its components and targets (for example after adding `components = "rust-src"`). A rustup `nightly` that is already newer, for example after `rustup update nightly`, is left alone, and so is one with components or targets that the dated toolchain lacks (for example `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown --toolchain nightly`), since replacing it would remove them. mise records in a `.mise-seeded` file inside the copy when rustup's `components` file was written; while rustup hasn't changed any component since, everything in the copy came from mise and may be dropped, so a switch to a smaller `profile` still refreshes it. If rustup is mid-change when mise goes to swap, mise re-checks and backs off.
- Replacing an older copy swaps the directories atomically on Linux (`renameat2(RENAME_EXCHANGE)`) and macOS (`renamex_np(RENAME_SWAP)`), so a concurrent `cargo +nightly` never sees it missing. Elsewhere it falls back to two renames and restores the old copy if the second fails; if even that restore fails, the old copy is kept on disk and its path is included in the warning instead of being deleted.
- Explicitly dated requests such as `rust = "nightly-2026-08-13"` never touch rustup's `nightly`.
- Once written, the toolchain belongs to rustup. `rustup update nightly`, `rustup component add --toolchain nightly`, and `rustup toolchain uninstall nightly` work normally and never change the dated toolchain mise installed. mise does not remove it when uninstalling the dated nightly.
- mise deletes rustup's `update-hashes/nightly-<host>` when it replaces the toolchain, so a later `rustup update nightly` can't wrongly report it as unchanged.
- If this step fails, install still succeeds and prints a warning.
- Existing installs pick this up on their next nightly install or upgrade, or right away with `mise install -f rust`.
