<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/228
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Sandboxed apps such as Safari and many Mac App Store apps keep their preferences in `~/Library/Containers/<domain>/Data/Library/Preferences/<domain>.plist`, not `~/Library/Preferences`. `mise bootstrap macos defaults` addressed every domain by its bare name, so for these apps `status` showed values that were already set as `unset`, and `apply` wrote a new `~/Library/Preferences/<domain>.plist`, reported success, and had no effect on the app.

```toml
[bootstrap.macos.defaults."com.apple.Safari"]
ShowFavoritesBar = false
```

Before this change, `apply` reported success for this entry but Safari never saw the value. Now, when `~/Library/Containers/<domain>` exists, mise reads and writes the container's plist, which is the file `defaults read com.apple.Safari` uses. Domains without a container behave as before.

- **Current-host entries** (`host = "current"`) go to the container's `ByHost/<domain>.<hardware UUID>.plist`.
- **Containers without a plist yet** (an app that has been launched but has never saved a preference) are still detected, because mise checks for the container, not the plist.
- **Protected containers:** macOS may require Full Disk Access for your terminal to write another app's container. If the write fails, the error says so. mise no longer falls back to a plist the app never reads.
- **Dry runs** print the container plist path, for example `defaults write /Users/you/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Preferences/com.apple.Safari ShowFavoritesBar -bool false`, so the printed command writes the same file `apply` does.
- **Apps that have never been launched** have no container yet, so their defaults still go to `~/Library/Preferences`. The docs say to launch the app once before applying.

Proposed in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13654, and based on @hugoh's branch, who is credited as a co-author.

### Validation

The macOS-only tests run in the `unit-macos` CI job. I couldn't run them locally.

- **Round trip:** writes both any-host and current-host values into a fake container that has no `Preferences` folder, then checks `status`, the plist on disk, and that nothing appeared under `~/Library/Preferences`.
- **Host UUID:** the round trip expects a specific ByHost filename, so a separate test checks that the UUID it uses matches the one Core Foundation puts in its own ByHost file names.

Container path resolution is covered by a unit test that also runs on Linux. The macOS module passes `cargo clippy -D warnings` for `aarch64-apple-darwin`.

title: fix(bootstrap): refresh apt lists when a package has no install candidate
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/227
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

On a machine installed from an ISO, `mise bootstrap` could fail at the packages step with errors like:

```
E: Package 'python3-venv' has no installation candidate
E: Unable to locate package nala
mise ERROR sudo exited with non-zero status: exit code 100
```

mise only ran `apt-get update` before installing in two cases: when you passed `--update`, or when `/var/lib/apt/lists` held no package lists at all. That second check covers a fresh container. An ISO install already has lists, but they may cover only the install media, so mise skipped the refresh. Every package goes into a single `apt-get install`, so one package missing from the lists failed the whole bootstrap before repos, dotfiles and tools ran. Until now, the fix was a manual `sudo apt-get update` or `--update`, which also updates configured repos.

With this change, when the lists exist, mise first simulates the exact install (`apt-get --simulate install …`, which needs no root). It runs `apt-get update` once if the simulation fails. `--dry-run` shows the refresh too:

```
$ mise bootstrap packages apply apt:nala apt:mise-nonexistent-pkg-xyz --dry-run
sudo env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update
sudo env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -- nala mise-nonexistent-pkg-xyz
```

The simulation resolves packages the same way the real install does, so:
- A pinned version missing from the lists (`"apt:foo" = "1.2.3"`) also triggers the refresh.
- A virtual package that apt resolves to a single provider, such as `libc-dev`, installs without a refresh.
- If the install would succeed, mise installs without refreshing, as before.
- If the simulation can't run, mise skips the refresh and installs as before.

A package that doesn't exist at all, such as a typo, now costs one `apt-get update` before it fails.

Fixes #13653

## Validation

- Unit test against the real `apt-get`: `bash` alone doesn't trigger a refresh, but adding a nonexistent package or pinning `bash` to a version that doesn't exist does.
- `e2e/cli/test_system_install_apt` checks that `apply --dry-run` prints `apt-get update` only when needed. It then deletes the `main` component's package lists while leaving the others in place, and runs a real `mise bootstrap packages apply --yes`. That install refreshes the lists and installs `bc`.
- Ran that e2e test as root in an `ubuntu:24.04` container; it passes. With the check disabled, it fails at the dry-run assertion. With that assertion removed as well, it fails at the real install.

title: fix(exec): warn instead of failing when a missing tool's command falls back to PATH
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/226
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

jdx/mise#13650 made `mise exec` fail when auto-install is off and the command belongs to a missing tool. This keeps the old fallback, so the command runs from `PATH` again, but prints a warning that the pinned tool isn't installed.

The warning matters because the fallback used to be silent. The generic `missing:` notice is hidden by default when no other version of the tool is installed (`status.missing_tools = "if_other_versions_installed"`). So in a git hook or CI job, a different, unpinned binary ran with no indication (jdx/mise#13649).

```toml
# mise.toml; jq 1.7.1 is not installed, /usr/bin/jq is 1.7
[tools]
jq = "1.7.1"
```

```
$ MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 mise x -- jq --version
mise WARN  jq@1.7.1 is not installed and auto-install is disabled, so mise looks for jq on PATH instead. Install it with: mise install jq@1.7.1
jq-1.7
$ echo $?
0
```

Before jdx/mise#13650, the same command printed only `jq-1.7`. With jdx/mise#13650, it exited 1 with an error.

## Behavior

- "Auto-install off" covers `exec_auto_install = false`, `auto_install = false`, and a tool listed in `auto_install_disable_tools`.
- The detection from jdx/mise#13650 is unchanged. mise treats a missing tool as the command's provider when its name matches the command, the registry's `bins` lists the command, or another installed version of the tool ships it.
- There's no warning when another configured version of the same tool is installed and provides the command, when a command wrapper is configured for it, or when an `env._.path` entry that isn't already on the inherited `PATH` provides it.
- Tools named in the warning are left out of the generic `missing:` notice, so they aren't listed twice.
- The warning doesn't depend on `status.missing_tools`.
- With default settings nothing changes.

## Tests

`e2e/cli/test_exec_missing_tool_no_path_fallback` is renamed to `test_exec_missing_tool_path_fallback_warning`. It covers the same cases, now checking that the command runs from `PATH` with the warning, or runs without it where an exemption applies. The test fails when the warning is downgraded to `debug!`. `test_auto_install_false` and `test_config_auto_install_disable_tools` go back to their pre-#13650 assertions (`couldn't exec process`, since nothing named `dummy` is on `PATH` there). The exec, command-wrapper, lazy-tool, and auto-install e2e tests pass, and so does `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

title: registry: list cog as cocogitto's bin
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/225
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

cocogitto installs one executable, `cog`, and that name doesn't match the tool's. With no `bins` entry, mise can't tell that `cog` belongs to cocogitto until some version of cocogitto has been installed. This adds `bins = ["cog"]`.

With the entry, mise can map `cog` to cocogitto before it's ever installed:

- When `cog` isn't found, `not_found_auto_install` can install the configured cocogitto.
- A `cocogitto = { version = "…", lazy = true }` entry gets `cog` as its lazy bin without setting `lazy_bins` by hand.
- `mise x -- cog` recognizes cocogitto as the missing provider when auto-install is off. This is the check from jdx/mise#13650, which previously only recognized cocogitto when another version was already installed (jdx/mise#13649).

I checked this by installing cocogitto 5.1.0 and 6.1.0 with the aqua backend: each ships only `cog`. `mise registry --json` lists the new bin. In a fresh data dir, `MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 mise x -- cog` now names `cocogitto@5.1.0` as the missing tool.

title: fix(exec): don't fall back to PATH for a missing tool when auto-install is off
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/224
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

With auto-install turned off for `mise exec`, a missing tool no longer gets silently swapped for some other binary with the same name, whether it comes from `PATH` or from another tool.

## Problem

Auto-install can be off because of `exec_auto_install = false`, `auto_install = false`, or because the tool is listed in `auto_install_disable_tools`. In that state, `mise exec` skipped installing a missing tool and then ran the next matching binary on the inherited `PATH`. That binary could be a different, unpinned version, and exec still exited 0. By default this printed no warning either, unless some other version of the tool was installed. That's easy to miss in git hooks and CI. The same fallback happened for tools passed on the command line (`mise x dummy@1.0.0 -- dummy`). The existing e2e test only failed because nothing named `dummy` was on `PATH`.

```toml
# mise.toml; jq 1.7.1 is not installed, /usr/bin/jq is 1.7
[tools]
jq = "1.7.1"
```

Before:

```
$ MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 mise x -- jq --version
jq-1.7
$ echo $?
0
```

After:

```
$ MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 mise x -- jq --version
mise ERROR Tool not installed for command: jq
Missing tool version: jq@1.7.1
Auto-install is disabled, and mise will not run a different jq in its place.
Install it with: mise install jq@1.7.1
$ echo $?
1
```

## Behavior

- mise treats a missing tool as the command's provider when any of these hold: its name matches the command, the registry's `bins` metadata lists the command, or another installed version of the tool ships it. These are the same signals `not_found_auto_install` uses.
- The command still runs in three cases:
  - Another configured version of the same tool is installed (`node = ["22", "20"]` with only 20 installed).
  - A [command wrapper](https://mise.jdx.dev/dev-tools/shims.html#command-wrappers) is configured for the command.
  - An `env._.path` entry that isn't already on the inherited `PATH` provides it, such as `{{config_root}}/bin`. exec searches those entries ahead of tool paths, so they'd run even with the tool installed. An entry that *is* already on `PATH` is searched after tool paths, so it doesn't count.
- A different tool that ships the same command doesn't count. For example, Node's bundled `npm` won't stand in for a pinned `npm` tool that's missing. This matches how shims let a pinned tool override an executable bundled with another tool.
- Missing tools the command doesn't use still only warn, so `mise x -- make` keeps working when an unrelated tool isn't installed. This matches `mise run`.
- With default settings nothing changes.

## Limitations

- Before a tool is installed, the only way mise can know which commands it provides is from those signals. A tool whose command name differs from its own name, with no registry `bins` and no installed version, still falls back. `cocogitto` (`cog`) in a fresh data dir is one exampl

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# Regression test for #13649: with auto-install off, `mise exec` ran a same-named
+# binary from the inherited PATH when the tool providing the command was missing,
+# exiting 0 with at most a warning.
+
+mkdir -p "$HOME/fallback-bin"
+cat >"$HOME/fallback-bin/dummy" <<'SCRIPT'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "dummy from PATH"
+SCRIPT
+chmod +x "$HOME/fallback-bin/dummy"
+export PATH="$HOME/fallback-bin:$PATH"
+
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = "1.0.0"
+TOML
+
+# A tool from config, with exec_auto_install and with auto_install disabled.
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@1.0.0"
+MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@1.0.0"
+# A tool listed in auto_install_disable_tools.
+MISE_AUTO_INSTALL_DISABLE_TOOLS=dummy assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@1.0.0"
+# A tool passed on the command line.
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x dummy@1.1.0 -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@1.1.0"
+assert_fail "test -d '$MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/dummy'"
+
+# A missing tool that does not provide the command still only warns.
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert "mise x -- echo ran" "ran"
+
+# Another configured version of the tool supplies the command from mise's paths.
+mise install dummy@1.0.0
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = ["2.0.0", "1.0.0"]
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_contains "mise x -- dummy" "1.0.0"
+
+# The tool's name does not match the command, so an installed version of it is
+# what identifies it as the provider.
+mise plugin link -f mytool "$MISE_DATA_DIR/plugins/dummy"
+mise install mytool@1.0.0
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+mytool = "2.0.0"
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: mytool@2.0.0"
+
+# A different configured tool that ships the same command does not stand in for it.
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+mytool = "1.0.0"
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@2.0.0"
+
+# A project `_.path` entry is searched ahead of tool paths, so its copy runs.
+mkdir -p project-bin
+cat >project-bin/dummy <<'SCRIPT'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo "project dummy"
+SCRIPT
+chmod +x project-bin/dummy
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+
+[env]
+_.path = ["{{config_root}}/project-bin"]
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_contains "mise x -- dummy" "project dummy"
+
+# An entry the inherited PATH already has is searched after tool paths, so it does not.
+cat >mise.toml <<TOML
+[tools]
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+
+[env]
+_.path = ["$HOME/fallback-bin"]
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- dummy" "Missing tool version: dummy@2.0.0"
+
+# A command wrapper configured for the command runs, even before its shim exists.
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+
+[wrappers]
+dummy = "echo"
+TOML
+assert_fail "test -e '$MISE_DATA_DIR/command-wrappers/bin/dummy'"
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert "mise x -- dummy wrapped" "wrapped"
+
+# A wrapper's own command gets the same check when the wrapper dispatches it.
+# That lookup skips the wrapper directories, so the dummy wrapper does not apply.
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+
+[wrappers]
+cargo = "dummy"
+dummy = "echo"
+TOML
+MISE_EXEC_AUTO_INSTALL=0 MISE_NOT_FOUND_AUTO_INSTALL=0 assert_fail "mise x -- cargo --version" "Missing tool version: dummy@2.0.0"
+
+# With auto-install on, the pinned version is installed and run as before.
+cat >mise.toml <<'TOML'
+[tools]
+dummy = "2.0.0"
+TOML
+assert_contains "mise x -- dummy" "2.0.0"

title: fix(dotfiles): report already-tracked paths instead of re-enrolling them
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/223
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Running `mise dot track` again on a path that is already tracked went through the whole enrollment again. It asked for confirmation, rewrote the config file, recorded a fresh baseline checkpoint even when nothing had changed, and reported the path as newly tracked:

```
$ mise dot track ~/.config/nvim/lua/config/autocmds.lua
dotfiles: track ~/.config/nvim/lua/config/autocmds.lua? Yes
mise history: saved baseline checkpoint 51
mise dotfiles: tracking ~/.config/nvim/lua/config/autocmds.lua (declared in ~/.config/mise/config.toml)
mise history: watcher running; autosave-enabled files are saved automatically
```

Now, when the declaration would be written exactly as it already is, the command leaves the config file untouched, skips the prompt, and says so. This applies to both inline and `[dotfiles."path"]` table declarations:

```
$ mise dot track ~/.config/nvim/lua/config/autocmds.lua
mise dotfiles: ~/.config/nvim/lua/config/autocmds.lua is already tracked (declared in ~/.config/mise/config.toml)
```

A re-track still records a checkpoint when there is something to record. That covers file contents changed since the newest checkpoint, and a hand-edited declaration (for example, a new `include` list) that history has not picked up yet. Tracking with a flag that changes the declaration, such as `--no-autosave` or `--os`, still rewrites it and prompts as before. In a command that mixes new and already-tracked paths, the prompt lists only the new ones. Repeating a path in one command treats it as one target. Re-tracking an autosave-enabled path still reports watcher health, including a stopped-watcher warning.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13638.

### Validation

- `mise run test:e2e test_dotfiles_retrack` passes on the current head. It covers unchanged inline and long-form declarations, changed contents, declaration-changing flags, duplicate targets, watcher warnings, and a declined interactive prompt with mixed paths.
- `mise run lint-fix` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes dotfiles enrollment and history baseline/checkpoint skipping; behavior is well covered by new e2e tests but affects user config and git history state.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise dot track`** on a path whose declaration already matches what the command would write is now treated as a **re-track**, not a fresh enrollment.
> 
> Re-tracks **leave the config file unchanged** (inline and long-form `[dotfiles."path"]` tables), **skip the confirmation prompt** when every target is a re-track, and log **`is already trac

--- e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_retrack (+93/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,93 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Re-tracking a path that is already tracked changes nothing: no rewrite,
+# no new checkpoint, and it says so.
+require_cmd git
+repository="$MISE_STATE_DIR/history/repo.git"
+echo original >~/.retrackrc
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+# kept as written
+[dotfiles]
+"~/.retrackrc"={mode="track"}
+TOML
+cp "$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" "$PWD/declared.toml"
+
+assert_succeed 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc'
+first=$(git --git-dir="$repository" rev-parse HEAD)
+# the declaration already says this, so the file is not reformatted
+assert "diff -q $MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml $PWD/declared.toml >/dev/null && echo same" 'same'
+
+# A long-form table has the same meaning and must keep its formatting too.
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[dotfiles."~/.retrackrc"]
+mode = "track"
+TOML
+cp "$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" "$PWD/declared.toml"
+assert_contains 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc 2>&1' '~/.retrackrc is already tracked'
+assert_contains 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc 2>&1' 'automatic capture is inactive'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repository rev-parse HEAD" "$first"
+assert "diff -q $MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml $PWD/declared.toml >/dev/null && echo same" 'same'
+
+assert_contains 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc 2>&1' '~/.retrackrc is already tracked'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repository rev-parse HEAD" "$first"
+assert "diff -q $MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml $PWD/declared.toml >/dev/null && echo same" 'same'
+
+# a re-track still saves what changed since the newest checkpoint
+echo edited >~/.retrackrc
+assert_succeed 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repository show HEAD:home/.retrackrc" 'edited'
+
+# and one that changes the declaration still rewrites it
+assert_succeed 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc --no-autosave'
+assert_contains "cat $MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" 'autosave = false'
+
+# Repeated spellings of a target count as one changed declaration.
+mise dot track ~/.retrackrc "$HOME/.retrackrc" --os linux >duplicate-output 2>&1
+assert_contains 'cat duplicate-output' 'dotfiles: tracking ~/.retrackrc'
+assert_not_contains 'cat duplicate-output' 'is already tracked'
+
+# tracking a new path beside an already-tracked one baselines the new one
+echo other >~/.otherrc
+require_cmd python3
+python3 - <<'PY' >prompt-output
+import os
+import pty
+import select
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import time
+
+master, slave = pty.openpty()
+env = os.environ.copy()
+env.pop("MISE_YES", None)
+process = subprocess.Popen(
+    ["mise", "dot", "track", os.path.expanduser("~/.retrackrc"), os.path.expanduser("~/.otherrc")],
+    stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, env=env,
+)
+os.close(slave)
+output = b""
+sent = False
+deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
+while time.monotonic() < deadline and process.poll() is None:
+    ready, _, _ = select.select([master], [], [], 0.1)
+    if ready:
+        try:
+            output += os.read(master, 4096)
+        except OSError:
+            break
+        if b"dotfiles: track " in output and not sent:
+            os.write(master, b"n\n")
+            sent = True
+if process.poll() is None:
+    process.kill()
+    process.wait()
+    sys.exit("track prompt timed out")
+os.close(master)
+sys.stdout.buffer.write(output)
+if not sent or process.returncode:
+    sys.exit("track prompt did not complete")
+PY
+assert_contains 'cat prompt-output' 'dotfiles: track ~/.otherrc'
+assert_not_contains 'cat prompt-output' 'dotfiles: track ~/.retrackrc'
+assert_fail "git --git-dir=$repository cat-file -e HEAD:home/.otherrc"
+assert_contains 'mise dot track ~/.retrackrc ~/.otherrc 2>&1' 'dotfiles: tracking ~/.otherrc'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repository show HEAD:home/.otherrc" 'other'

title: refactor: split mise into a library and a thin CLI binary
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/222
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. It builds on #13642, which removed every core → `cli` dependency.

## Why

Most day-to-day changes land in `src/cli/`: 1,660 file changes in the last three months, more than twice any other area. Until now, every one of those edits recompiled the whole `mise` crate.

## What changes

- **The `mise` package now has two targets.**
  - **Library** (`src/lib.rs`): everything except the command line.
  - **Binary** (`src/main.rs` plus `src/cli/`): registers the frontend hooks and dispatches to `Cli`.

  No files move, so `cargo install mise` and the single published crate are unchanged.
- **Existing CLI paths remain valid.** `main.rs` glob-imports the library root (`use mise::*`) and uses `#[macro_use] extern crate mise`, so `crate::config::…`, `info!` and the other `crate::…` paths inside `cli` still resolve.
- **Visibility:** about 1,650 core items that `cli` uses change from `pub(crate)` to `pub`, and the modules they live in become `pub mod`. The library denies `unreachable_pub`, so anything `cli` doesn't reach stays `pub(crate)`. One trade-off: an item that `cli` stops using will no longer get a `dead_code` warning.
- **OCI image builds:** the library builder now takes an explicit path for the mise binary to embed; the CLI supplies its own executable. Library callers can choose the binary, and `--no-mise` still omits it.
- **Tests:** `cfg(test)` is not set on a library when a dependent crate's tests are built, so the binary's tests see the library's non-test code.
  - The fixture setup moves from `src/test.rs` to `src/testing.rs`. Both test binaries call it from their own constructors.
  - `cfg!(test)` switches that the CLI tests depend on now check `mise_util::testing::in_tests()`, as #13620 did for four statics: config trust, config discovery, settings, hints, tables, and `install_state::get_plugin_type`.
  - `windows_file_shim_body` is now compiled on every platform, because a CLI test compares it with the launcher.
  - The library's own tests register a stand-in frontend (no subcommands; the post-install lockfile update is skipped), since they have no CLI to register the real one.
  - Runnable library doctests stay enabled, including the `cmd!` example. Two illustrative snippets that cannot compile as standalone public examples are marked as text.
- **Small fixes that clippy requires on newly public items:**
  - `ToolRequestSet::into_iter` is renamed to `into_tools`, because clippy's `should_implement_trait` rejects a public method named `into_iter`.
  - Three types that are now public (`BrewManager`, `BrewCaskManager`, `RemoteTaskArtifactsGuard`) get `Default` impls.
  - The non-Linux system stubs and `ctrlc` stubs match the visibility of the modules they stand in for.
- `AGENTS.md` describes the split.

## Measured

`cargo build -p mise --bin mise` (debug) after a one-line edit, warm increme

title: fix(config): don't cache settings loaded before a concurrent reset
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/221
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Settings could lose a just-applied override when one thread was loading settings while another changed them. The load read the old CLI overrides, the other thread set a new override and cleared the cache, and then the in-flight load finished and cached its stale snapshot. The next `Settings::get()` returned settings without the override.

This mostly showed up as flaky unit tests. For example, `config::settings::tests::test_reload_preserves_cli_settings` failed with `assertion failed: Settings::get().offline()` even though it holds `SettingsGuard`. The same interleaving could happen in the CLI whenever settings are reset or overridden while another thread is loading them.

### Fix

- The settings cache in `mise-settings` now has a generation counter, and both `clear()` and `store()` bump it.
- `Settings::try_get` records the generation before it runs the loader. It caches the result only if the generation hasn't changed.
- If the generation changed during the load, the caller still gets what it loaded, but the next read reloads.
- If two loads finish in the same generation, the first result is kept, so every reader gets the same snapshot.
- Loaders now only build settings, and `try_get` does the caching. So mise's loader and `load_defaults` no longer call `store`. Explicit `store()` calls work as before.
- The safe-mode fallback now reads `safe` from the last settings that were actually cached (new `mise_settings::last_cached()`), not from the loader's `LAST_SAFE` side-channel. `safe_mode()` uses this fallback while settings are cleared, for example during the config parse after `Config::reset()`. Previously a discarded stale load could still change the fallback, which could let project settings through when safe mode should exclude them.

A second commit fixes a separate flake found while checking this. Some `backend::latest_version_tests` read the `offline` setting through `list_remote_versions` but didn't hold `SettingsGuard`, while neighboring tests set `offline=true`. Those tests now take the guard.

### Validation

- New `mise-settings` unit tests run the interleavings deterministically on a local cache instance: a clear during a load, a store during a load, and two loads in the same generation. The clear and store tests fail if the generation check is removed.
- I ran `cargo test --all-features --bin mise -- --test-threads=8 install_before::tests config::settings::tests plugins::core::ruby backend::latest_version_tests` 10 times on each setup:
  - `main`: failed in 5 of 6 runs.
  - Only the test-guard commit: failed in 8 of 10 runs (`ruby`, `install_before`).
  - Both commits: passed all 10 runs.
- The `config/test_safe_mode` and `cli/test_doctor_project` e2e tests pass.
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint` pass.

<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/220
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise run test:unit` (`cargo test --all-features` with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1`) failed 22–23 tests on `main` on macOS. Starting with `system::packages::pacman::tests::test_pacman_query_file_advisory` (`getcwd: cannot access parent directories`), every later test that touches the working directory failed: `system::remote`, `system::remote_repository`, `task::deps`, `task::tests::test_from_path` (`.mise/tasks/filetask` not found), `task::workspace`, `tera::tests::test_{exists,is_dir,is_file,canonicalize}`, and `uv::tests::test_resolve_uv_venv_path`.

## Cause

Bisecting the tests that run before pacman found one culprit, and it reproduces on its own: `system::packages::brew::tap::tests::ignores_mise_shim_when_selecting_system_ruby`. That test re-runs the test binary as a child process so it gets fresh process-wide statics. The child runs the harness ctor in `src/test.rs`, which calls `remove_all(test/cwd)` and then recreates the directory. This unlinks the directory the parent process is still in. Nextest runs each test in its own process, so it never hits this; single-threaded `cargo test` shares one process across tests and does.

## Fix

Once the ctor has written the fixture tree, it exports `__MISE_TEST_FIXTURES_READY`. A child process inherits the variable, so its ctor now chdirs into the existing tree instead of resetting it. This also covers any future test that re-execs the binary.

## Validation

- `mise run test:unit`: 4211 passed, 0 failed (previously 22 failed on this base)
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: registry: nub serves 0.9.5+ from github:nubjs/nub and lists the nubr bin
body:
Puts `github:nubjs/nub` first in the `nub` registry entry for 0.9.5 and later, keeps `npm:@nubjs/nub` for the versions before it, and lists `nubr` as a third bin.

From [nub 0.9.5](https://github.com/nubjs/nub/releases/tag/v0.9.5) the release archives carry `bin/nubx` and `bin/nubr` themselves: relative symlinks to `bin/nub` in the tarballs, a small stub executable under each name in the Windows zips ([nubjs/nub#956](https://github.com/nubjs/nub/pull/956)). A plain extraction is a complete install, so the GitHub backend can serve it. Earlier archives shipped only `bin/nub`, which is what kept the entry on the npm package and its Node launcher ([#13191](https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/13191)); `min_version` routes those versions to npm as before.

Verified on macOS arm64 with mise 2026.9.14, a clean `MISE_DATA_DIR`, and `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0` because 0.9.5 is younger than a day:

```
$ mise ls-remote github:nubjs/nub | tail -3
0.9.2
0.9.3
0.9.5
$ mise install github:nubjs/nub@0.9.5
mise ✓ github:nubjs/nub@0.9.5  5.0s  nub-darwin-arm64.tar.gz
$ ls -l $MISE_DATA_DIR/installs/github-nubjs-nub/0.9.5/bin
-rwxr-xr-x  nub
-rwxr-xr-x  nub-launcher-darwin-arm64
lrwxr-xr-x  nubr -> nub
lrwxr-xr-x  nubx -> nub
$ mise x github:nubjs/nub@0.9.5 -- nubr --version
0.9.5
$ mise x github:nubjs/nub@0.9.5 -- nubx --help | head -1
Run a tool from `node_modules/.bin`, fetching it on a local miss (`npx`/`pnpm
```

The release publishes no artifact attestations, so there is no `attestations_since`. `registry/nubr.toml` stays on `npm:@nubjs/runner`, the Node-only runner package.

`bins` is one list per tool, not per backend. `nubr` exists in the npm package from 0.9.3, so only a pin at 0.9.2 or older gets a `nubr` shim with nothing behind it, the same as any tool that gained a bin between releases.

body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/218

Internal refactor; no user-visible behavior change.

After this PR, nothing outside `src/cli/` and `src/main.rs` refers to `crate::cli`. This is the last prerequisite for splitting mise into a library crate (config, toolset, backends, tasks, …) and a thin binary crate (`main` plus `cli`). With that split, the most-edited code (`src/cli`) would no longer force the whole core to rebuild.

What moved:

- **Out of `cli`, into core:**
  - `HookReason` → `hook_env`
  - `ToolStubFile` → `src/tool_stub.rs`
  - `prunable_tools` → `toolset`
  - the system-package driver → `system/driver.rs`
  - the upgrade hints → `src/upgrade_hint.rs`

  `self_update.rs` and its no-feature stub each carried their own copy of the upgrade hints; there is now one.
- **Into `cli`:** the shim entry point (`handle_shim` / `which_shim`) moves from `shims.rs` to `cli/shim.rs`, since its job is to dispatch to `mise exec`. The helpers it uses stay in `shims.rs`.
- **Settings:** the loader now takes a `SettingsPartial`, which `Cli::settings_layer` builds from the global flags, instead of reading `&Cli`.
- **Hooks:** two calls go the other way, from core into command code: lockfile generation after an install (`mise lock`), and the subcommand list used for "did you mean" task suggestions. Both now go through `src/frontend.rs`, which `cli` registers at startup next to the existing mise-util hooks.

**LOC:** `src/` goes from 368,704 to 368,755 (+51: the new module headers and hook plumbing, minus the removed self-update stub duplicate). `src/cli/` goes from 57,752 to 57,363. mise-util is unchanged at 41,875.

**Validation:** `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean. `cargo check` also passes without the `self_update` feature. Unit tests fail the same way locally with and without this change: the same 22 tests (a test that deletes the working directory makes the rest cascade), and the base branch fails a superset of them.

title: refactor(cli): move the tool and backend argument types out of cli
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/217
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the first step toward giving the CLI its own crate.

## Why

Most day-to-day changes land in `src/cli/`: 1,594 file changes in the last three months, more than twice any other area. Every one of them recompiles the whole `mise` crate. Splitting mise into a library (config, toolset, backends, tasks, system, …) and a thin binary (`main` plus `cli/`) would let a CLI edit skip recompiling the other ~300k lines.

That needs the core to stop referring to `crate::cli`. Today 72 non-CLI files do, and almost all of them only for the argument types.

## Change

`src/cli/args/` (`ToolArg`, `BackendArg`, `BackendResolution`, `EnvVarArg`, `TruncateArg`, …) moves to `src/args/` as `crate::args`. These are core types: they depend on config, toolset, the registry and backends, not on anything CLI-specific. `cli` keeps `crate::cli::args` as an alias, so code inside `src/cli/` is unchanged. Outside it, the paths are updated.

After this, about a dozen core call sites still reach into `cli`: `HookReason`, `ToolStubFile`, `prunable_tools`, `Lock::generate_after_install`, the self-update instructions, `Cli` in the settings loader, the `shims` entry points, and the system-deps driver called from `toolset`. The next PR handles those.

## Validation

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- All 4212 mise unit tests pass. The only retry was the known 1-second timeout in `aube_node_gyp_bootstrap`, which isn't related to this change.

title: chore(release): refuse release prep when a workspace manifest is already dirty
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/214
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Release prep in `xtasks/release-plz` now runs `git add crates/*/Cargo.toml`. That staging has to be broad, because bumping one subcrate rewrites the version requirement in every workspace crate that path-depends on it. The downside is that an edit already sitting in any workspace manifest would be committed into `chore: release …` along with the bump. Before this change, the per-crate `has_uncommitted_changes` check only looked at the four subcrates it bumps, and `git status` only printed the state, so nothing stopped that.

Release prep now checks `Cargo.toml` and `crates/*/Cargo.toml` before it touches anything, and exits if either has uncommitted changes:

```
Workspace manifests have uncommitted changes before release prep:
 M crates/mise-util/Cargo.toml
```

The release workflow runs on a fresh checkout, so a normal release is unaffected. Nothing between checkout and this point edits a manifest; the publish branch exits before reaching it.

The original content of this PR (updating every workspace path dependency on a subcrate bump, and staging every subcrate manifest) already reached `main` through #13631. After merging `main`, this check is all that is left in the diff.

**Validation:** `bash -n` passes. I ran the check against a clean tree, a dirty `crates/mise-util/Cargo.toml` (blocked), and a dirty non-manifest file under `crates/` (allowed).

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> CI-only release script change that fails early on a dirty workspace; no runtime or user-facing behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Adds a fail-fast guard** at the start of the release **prep** path in `xtasks/release-plz` (after the publish-and-exit branch, before bumping `mise`).
> 
> If `Cargo.toml` or any `crates/*/Cargo.toml` already has staged, unstaged, or untracked changes, the script prints those paths to stderr and **exits 1** instead of continuing. Prep later `git add`s all workspace manifests, so unrelated manifest edits would otherwise be swept into the automated `chore: release` commit; this check avoids guessing which hunks belong to the run.

@@ -453,6 +453,16 @@ if [[ $cur_version != "$latest_version" ]]; then
 	exit 0

+# Prep stages every workspace manifest (see the `git add` below), so an edit
+# already sitting in one would ride along into the release commit. Refuse to
+# start rather than guess which hunks belong to this run.
+preexisting_manifest_changes="$(git status --porcelain -- Cargo.toml 'crates/*/Cargo.toml')"
+if [[ -n $preexisting_manifest_changes ]]; then
+	echo "Workspace manifests have uncommitted changes before release prep:" >&2
+	echo "$preexisting_manifest_changes" >&2
+	exit 1
+fi

title: refactor(http): move http, github, gitlab, forgejo and tokens into mise-util
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/213
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the seventh PR in the crate-split stack.

## What moves into `crates/mise-util`

| Module | From |
|---|---|
| `http` | `src/http.rs` |
| `github`, `github::oauth`, `github::sigstore` | `src/github.rs`, `src/github/` |
| `gitlab`, `forgejo` | `src/*.rs` |
| `github_relay`, `tokens`, `parallel` | `src/*.rs` |
| `versions_host` (the GitHub release/attestation mirror half) | `src/versions_host.rs` |
| `shells` (inline/file shell settings) | `SettingsExt::default_inline_shell` and friends |

Also moving: `env::scoped_var` / `with_install_env` with their task-local, which now sit next to `EnvValue`.

What stays in mise:
- `versions_host::list_versions` and `track_install`, which need backends, core plugins and the registry.
- The `SettingsExt` methods of the same names. They delegate to `mise_util::shells`.

mise keeps a one-line re-export per module, so call sites are unchanged.

## Startup hooks

A few things these modules need can only come from mise. `register_util_hooks()` in `main.rs` now registers all of them, both in `main` and in the test harness constructor:

- the settings loader and base cache keys (from earlier PRs)
- the HTTP User-Agent, which names mise's version and the shell (`mise_util::user_agent`)
- mise's version, for version-gated deprecation warnings (`mise_util::deprecation`, with a `deprecated_at!` that mirrors mise's)
- whether the inline shell is the implicit default, which needs every config layer (`mise_util::shells::set_implicit_inline_shell`)

Each hook panics with a message naming its setter if something reads it before registration.

## Test-only overrides

Several modules had `#[cfg(test)]` hooks in production code: token-file overrides, the OAuth cache path, the fast HTTP retry schedule and the relay test upstream. `cfg(test)` does not reach a dependency crate, so these are now always compiled. They only take effect when a test sets them, or when `mise_util::testing::in_tests()` is true, which covers `cfg(test)` in `mise-util` and mise's harness after `testing::enable`.

All of these modules' unit tests moved with them. Tests that called `Config::get()` only as a fixture drop that line. Tests that reset settings use a new `testing::reset_settings`, which layers overrides over the `MISE_*` environment and the defaults.

## Release

`mise-util` now depends on `mise-sigstore`, so the release script publishes `mise-sigstore` before `mise-util`, and a `mise-sigstore` bump updates `mise-util` instead of `mise`. The lower PRs in the stack already fix the order for `mise-cache-core` and `mise-settings`.

`axum` and `mise-sigstore` are no longer direct dependencies of `mise`. mise's TLS features reach them through `mise-util`.

| after | 372,777 | 37,826 |

title: refactor: move network flags, cache manager and exit plumbing into mise-util
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/212
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the sixth PR in the crate-split stack.

This moves the pieces `http` and `github` depend on, so the next PR can move those modules as a block.

## What moves into `crates/mise-util`

- **`args`:** `GLOBAL_FLAGS_WITH_VALUES` and `first_non_global_arg_idx_cached`. They find the subcommand in raw arguments without building the clap tree. mise's test that checks the list against clap stays in mise, as does the `usage_rs`-based `first_non_global_arg_idx`.
- **`env`:** `PREFER_OFFLINE`, `REMOTE_FETCH_COMMAND`, and the helpers that derive them from the command being run.
- **`network`:** the settings accessors `offline`, `prefer_offline`, `bound_remote_version_lookups`, `http_timeout`, `http_download_timeout`, `http_retries`, `fetch_remote_versions_timeout`, `configured_fetch_remote_versions_timeout` and `fetch_remote_versions_cache`. They are now free functions over `&Settings`, and the `SettingsExt` methods of the same names delegate to them.
- **`cancel`:** the "Ctrl-C was pressed" flag. mise's Unix and Windows Ctrl-C handlers set it; its test stub still never does.
- **`exit`:** `exit.rs`, the requested-exit-status error.
- **`cache`:** `CacheManager`, its builder, and cache-directory pruning. `auto_prune` and `cache_dirs` stay in mise because they know about the task and env caches.

## Startup hook

Cache file names include a hash of mise's build identity (version, profile, target, features), which lives in mise's build script. `mise_util::cache::set_base_cache_keys` receives it from `crate::cache::register_base_cache_keys()`. That runs in `main` and in the test harness constructor, next to the settings loader registration.

## Lines of code

| | `src/` (mise crate) | `mise-util` |
|---|---|---|
| before (#13628) | 388,048 | 21,596 |
| after | 386,956 | 22,818 |

1,092 lines move out of the `mise` crate. This layer is mostly plumbing; the next one moves `http`, `github`, `gitlab`, `forgejo`, `tokens` and `github_relay` (~13k lines).

## Validation

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Unit tests: all 4534 mise tests pass. `mise-util` and `mise-settings` pass 334 of 335; the timeout is `git::tests::update_resolves_short_branches_and_tags`, which times out on this machine throughout the stack.

+//! Locating the subcommand in mise's raw arguments without building the clap
+//! tree, for code that runs before arguments are parsed.
+
+/// Long and short forms of the top-level flags that consume a following argument.
+///
+/// Hardcoded rather than derived because `env.rs` needs it from `Lazy` statics
+/// during startup — before anything has parsed arguments — and deriving it means
+/// building the entire clap tree, which costs ~3.1M instructions. Doing that
+/// there is what made every mise command ~6.3M instructions more expensive.
+///
+/// mise's `test_global_flags_with_values_matches_clap` asserts this equals what clap
+/// reports, so adding a value-taking flag to its `Cli` without updating this list
+/// fails CI rather than silently mis-parsing arguments.
+pub const GLOBAL_FLAGS_WITH_VALUES: &[&str] = &[
+    "--cd",
+    "-C",
+    "--env",
+    "-E",
+    "--jobs",
+    "-j",
+    "--profile",
+    "-P",
+    "--shell",
+    "-s",
+    "--tool",
+    "-t",
+    "--log-level",
+    "--output",
+];
+
+/// The index of the first argument that is not a global flag or one of its
+/// values, against [`GLOBAL_FLAGS_WITH_VALUES`].
+///
+/// For callers with no `Command` to hand, which would otherwise build the whole
+/// tree just to read its top-level arguments.
+pub fn first_non_global_arg_idx_cached(args: &[String]) -> Option<usize> {
+    first_non_global_arg_idx_with(|f| GLOBAL_FLAGS_WITH_VALUES.contains(&f), args)
+}
+
+/// As [`first_non_global_arg_idx_cached`], with `takes_value` deciding which
+/// flags consume the next argument.
+pub fn first_non_global_arg_idx_with(
+    takes_value: impl Fn(&str) -> bool,
+    args: &[String],
+) -> Option<usize> {
+    let mut i = 1;
+    while i < args.len() {
+        let arg = &args[i];
+
+        if arg == "--" {
+            return None;
+        }
+
+        if !arg.starts_with('-') {
+            return Some(i);
+        }
+
+        let flag_takes_separate_value = if arg.starts_with("--") {
+            if arg.contains('=') {
+                false
+            } else {
+                let flag_name = arg.split('=').next().unwrap();
+                takes_value(flag_name)
+            }
+        } else if let Some(flag_name) = arg.get(..2) {
+            // `arg.get(..2)` (not `&arg[..2]`) avoids panicking when the arg is
+            // not valid UTF-8 in the first place: args are read lossily, so a
+            // malformed byte becomes a multi-byte U+FFFD and byte index 2 may not
+            // be a char boundary. A short flag is always ASCII, so a non-ASCII
+            // prefix simply matches no value-taking flag.
+            arg.len() == 2 && takes_value(flag_name)
+        } else {
+            false
+        };
+
+        if flag_takes_separate_value && i + 1 < args.len() {
+            i += 2;
+        } else {
+            i += 1;
+        }
+    }
+    None
+}

title: refactor: move self-contained leaf modules into mise-util
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/211
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the fifth PR in the crate-split stack.

## What moves

Self-contained modules that needed nothing from mise beyond what `crates/mise-util` already has:

| Module | From |
|---|---|
| `sysconfig` (with its `LICENSE-MIT`) | `src/sysconfig/` |
| `windows_posix`, `windows_console` | `src/*.rs` |
| `platform` | `src/platform.rs` |
| `semver`, `duration`, `jobs`, `rand` | `src/*.rs` |
| `deps_graph`, `packslip_pins` | `src/*.rs` |
| `fuzzy`, `wildcard`, `timeout` | `src/*.rs` |
| `time`, `resolve_progress` | `src/ui/time.rs`, `src/ui/resolve_progress.rs` |

mise keeps a one-line re-export for each module, so call sites are unchanged.

The `RecordingReport` test double moves from `resolve_progress`'s test module to `mise_util::testing`, because `http`'s tests use it and `cfg(test)` code in a dependency crate isn't visible to them.

Some modules stay in mise on purpose:
- `ui/table`, `ui/tree` and `ui/info` print through `miseprintln!`, which mise's tests capture.
- `ui/ctrlc` is swapped for a stub under `cfg(test)`.
- `agecrypt` has a `directive` submodule that depends on `config`.

`nucleo-matcher` is no longer a direct dependency of `mise`.

## Lines of code

| | `src/` (mise crate) | `mise-util` |
|---|---|---|
| before (#13625) | 392,379 | 17,233 |
| after | 388,048 | 21,596 |

4,331 lines move out of the `mise` crate.

## Validation

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Unit tests: all 4547 mise tests and all 322 `mise-util` + `mise-settings` tests pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> **Low Risk**
> Mechanical relocation with re-exports preserves behavior; risk is limited to import/dependency wiring mistakes rather than new user-facing logic.

> **Overview**

> 
> **What lands in `mise-util`:** dependency scheduling (`deps_graph`), packslip signer pins, platform/libc detection, semver/duration/time helpers, job concurrency normalization, timeouts, fuzzy/wildcard matching, resolver progress scoping, Windows PATH/console helpers, Python `sysconfig` (now public API there), and related tests. **`mise-util`’s `Cargo.toml`** picks up the dependencies those modules need (e.g. `petgraph`, `jiff`, `nucleo-matcher`); **`nucleo-matcher` is dropped** from the top-level `mise` crate.

title: chore: fix lints reported by the Rust 1.99 beta toolchain
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/210
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal cleanup with no user-facing change. The Rust 1.99 beta toolchain reports two new warnings on `main`, and both fail `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint` (whose `cargo check` denies warnings) for anyone whose default toolchain is beta:

- `src/cmd/bounded.rs`: `AtomicUsize::fetch_update` is deprecated on beta in favor of `try_update`, but `try_update` is still unstable on stable Rust, so neither builds on both. The budget check is now an explicit `compare_exchange_weak` loop, which is what both methods do internally.
- `crates/mise-agent-env`: `for signal in ["AI_AGENT"]` loops over a single element (the new `single_element_loop` diagnostic). It's now a plain binding with the same checks in the same order.
- `crates/mise-agent-env` declared `rust-version = "1.85"`, but that check uses a let chain, which Rust stabilized in 1.88, so the crate never built on its declared minimum. It now declares 1.88 and builds with `cargo +1.88.0`.

`cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes on both stable 1.98.1 and beta 1.99, and the `mise-agent-env` and `cmd::bounded` unit tests pass.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Refactors are driven by new compiler/clippy diagnostics; logic is intended to be equivalent for agent detection and bounded subprocess output.
> 
> **Overview**
> Internal cleanup so **`cargo clippy -D warnings`** and **`mise run lint`** pass when the default toolchain is Rust 1.99 beta, with no intended behavior change.
> 
> In **`src/cmd/bounded.rs`**, shared output-budget accounting no longer uses **`AtomicUsize::fetch_update`** (deprecated on beta in favor of unstable **`try_update`**). It now uses an explicit **`compare_exchange_weak`** loop via a new **`spend`** helper, preserving the same byte-limit enforcement for isolated command capture.
> 
> In **`crates/mise-agent-env`**, the single-element **`for signal in ["AI_AGENT"]`** loop is replaced with a direct **`AI_AGENT`** check (same detection order and **`ClaudeCowork`** override). The crate **`rust-version`** is raised from **1.85** to **1.88** so it matches code that already relies on let chains.
>

title: refactor(cmd): move process execution and git into mise-util
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/208
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the fourth PR in the crate-split stack.

## What moves

`crates/mise-util` now holds mise's process-running and git layer:

| Module | From | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `cmd` | `src/cmd.rs`, `src/cmd/bounded.rs` | `CmdLineRunner` and the rest of process execution; mise keeps its `cmd!` macro |
| `git` | `src/git.rs` | gix, libgit and the git CLI paths |
| `sandbox` | `src/sandbox/` | Landlock, seccomp and Seatbelt |
| `path_env`, `netrc`, `redactions`, `inline_command` | `src/*.rs` | |
| `env_value` | `EnvValue` from `config/env_directive` | re-exported there |
| `errors` | new | `ProcessError` (see below) |

It also takes `shared_install_dirs()`, `install_path_category()` and `find_in_shared_installs()` from `env.rs`, and adds `dirs::system_installs_dir()`, which `SettingsExt::system_installs_dir` now delegates to.

### `ProcessError`

`cmd` raised `Error::ScriptFailed` and `Error::TaskInterrupted`, but the rest of mise's `Error` enum refers to toolset and backend types. Those two variants are now `mise_util::errors::ProcessError`, with the same messages. `Error::get_exit_status`, `is_sigint`, `is_killed_by_signal` and `is_task_interrupted_before_start` keep their names and delegate, so `mise run` and telemetry are unchanged. The five places that matched the variants directly (script manager, zypper, brew cask flights) now downcast to `ProcessError`.

### Test-only behavior

`cmd` skipped registering its signal-forwarding handler under `#[cfg(test)]`, which does not reach a dependency crate. The handler code now compiles on every unix build and is skipped at runtime while `mise_util::testing::active()`, the flag mise's test harness sets. Release builds are unaffected. `sandbox`'s `cfg(not(test))` gates only hid items tests don't call, so they are gone.

### Features and dependencies

- `mise-util` gets `native-tls` / `rustls` / `rustls-native-roots` features for gix's HTTP transport. mise forwards its own TLS features to them, like `mise-cache-core`.
- `aho-corasick`, `netrc-rs`, `landlock` and `seccompiler` are no longer direct dependencies of `mise`.

Tests that need mise's `Config` fixtures or `SettingsExt` stay in mise; the rest moved with their code.

## Lines of code

| | `src/` (mise crate) | `mise-util` |
|---|---|---|
| before (#13624) | 400,334 | 9,220 |
| after | 392,379 | 17,225 |

7,955 lines move out of the `mise` crate.

## Validation

- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Unit tests: all 4638 mise tests pass. `mise-util` and `mise-settings` pass 230 of 231; the timeout is `git::tests::update_resolves_short_branches_and_tags`, which moved here with `git.rs` and times out on this machine on every branch in the stack. `mise-util`'s own tests register `mise_settings::load_defaults` as their settings loader (new in this PR), sin

title: refactor(file): move file, path, hash and process helpers into mise-util
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/207
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the third PR in the crate-split stack.

## What moves

`crates/mise-util` now holds mise's filesystem and path layer:

| Module | From | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `src/file.rs` | archive extraction, symlinks and junctions, `which`, `display_path`, … |
| `path` | `src/path.rs` | |
| `hash` | `src/hash.rs` | `file_hash_prog` is now `pub` so a mise snapshot test can still call it |
| `lock_file` | `src/lock_file.rs` | |
| `style` | `src/ui/style.rs` | |
| `env_diff` | `src/env_diff.rs` | activation diffs |
| `progress` | part of `src/ui/progress_report.rs` | only the `SingleReport` trait and `ProgressIcon`; mise's renderers stay and implement it |
| `cmd` | part of `src/cmd.rs` | only the `cmd()` function and `cmd!` macro; `CmdLineRunner` stays |

Three things also move so the moved code doesn't reach back into mise:

- `__MISE_DIFF`, `PRISTINE_ENV` and `PATH` (the pre-activation environment), from `env.rs`.
- `dirs::shims()` and `dirs::system_shims()`. `SettingsExt::system_shims_dir` now delegates to them, and the unused `SettingsExt::shims_dir` is removed.
- `EnvVarGuard` and `lock_ignoring_poison`, into `mise_util::testing`, so both crates' tests can use them.

mise keeps `src/file.rs`, `src/path.rs`, `src/hash.rs`, `src/lock_file.rs`, `src/env_diff.rs` and `src/ui/style.rs` as one-line re-exports, so call sites are unchanged. Tests that depend on mise's test fixtures (`Config::get()`, the `test/` home directory, insta snapshots) stay in those files; the rest moved with the code.

`bzip2`, `digest`, `md-5`, `sevenz-rust2`, `sha1`, `siphasher` and `xz2` are no longer direct dependencies of `mise`.

`mise-util` now depends on `mise-settings`, which depends on `mise-cache-core`, so the release script publishes `mise-cache-core`, then `mise-settings`, then `mise-util`, and points each dependent at the version it just published.

## Lines of code

| | `src/` (mise crate) | `mise-util` |
|---|---|---|
| before (#13620) | 408,277 | 1,209 |
| after | 400,334 | 9,220 |

7,943 lines move out of the `mise` crate.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Unit tests: `mise-util` and `mise-settings` pass (127 tests). mise passes 4742 of 4743; the timeout is `git::tests::update_resolves_short_branches_and_tags`, which also times out on #13616 and #13620 on this machine.
- The Windows-only code moved verbatim and the `windows-sys` features it uses are declared on `mise-util`. It isn't compiled locally, so Windows CI is the check.

+use std::ffi::OsString;

+use duct::{Expression, IntoExecutablePath};

+/// Create a command with any number of of positional arguments
+///

+/// See also the [`cmd`](fn.cmd.html) function, which takes a collection of arguments.
+///
+/// # Example
+///
+/// ```ignore
+///     use std::path::Path;
+///     use mise_util::cmd;
+///
+///     let arg1 = "foo";
+///     let arg2 = "bar".to_owned();
+///     let arg3 = Path::new("baz");
+///
+///     let output = cmd!("echo", arg1, arg2, arg3).read();
+///
+///     assert_eq!("foo bar baz", output.unwrap());
+/// ```
+#[macro_export]
+macro_rules! cmd {
+    ( $program:expr $(, $arg:expr )* $(,)? ) => {
+        {
+            use std::ffi::OsString;
+            let args: std::vec::Vec<OsString> = std::vec![$( Into::<OsString>::into($arg) ),*];
+            $crate::cmd::cmd($program, args)
+        }
+    };
+}
+
+/// Create a command with any number of of positional arguments, which may be
+/// different types (anything that implements
+/// [`Into<OsString>`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/convert/trait.From.html)).

+/// arguments.
+///
+/// # Example

+/// ```ignore
+///     use std::path::Path;
+///     use mise_util::cmd;
+///
+///     let arg1 = "foo";
+///     let arg2 = "bar".to_owned();
+///     let arg3 = Path::new("baz");
+///
+///     let output = cmd!("echo", arg1, arg2, arg3).read();
+///
+///     assert_eq!("foo bar baz", output.unwrap());
+/// ```
+pub fn cmd<T, U>(program: T, args: U) -> Expression
+where
+    T: IntoExecutablePath,
+    U: IntoIterator,
+    U::Item: Into<OsString>,
+{
+    let program = program.to_executable();
+    let args: Vec<OsString> = args.into_iter().map(Into::<OsString>::into).collect();
+
+    let display_command = std::iter::once(&program)
+        .chain(&args)
+        .map(|s| shell_escape::escape(s.to_string_lossy()))
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(" ");
+    debug!("$ {display_command}");
+
+    duct::cmd(program, args)
+}

title: feat(bootstrap): show Mac App Store app names in packages status
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/206
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Mac App Store entries in `[bootstrap.packages]` are keyed by numeric App Store IDs, so `mise bootstrap packages status` gave no hint which app each row was. mise already runs `mas list` to read installed versions, and that listing includes app names. The status table now shows the name next to each installed ID.

```toml
[bootstrap.packages]
"mas:1056643111" = "latest" # Clocker
"mas:775737590" = "latest"  # iA Writer
```

Before:

```text
Manager    Package             Installed    State
mas        1056643111          26.17        installed
mas        775737590           8.0.8        installed
```

After:

```text
Manager    Package                   Installed    State
mas        1056643111 (Clocker)      26.17        installed
mas        775737590 (iA Writer)     8.0.8        installed
```

`mise bootstrap packages status --json` adds a `name` field to these packages. Missing apps still show only their ID, because `mas list` only reports installed apps. Getting their names would require an App Store lookup, and this PR doesn't do that.

mise reads the name from `mas list --json` (`name`, falling back to `displayName`) or from the text between the ID and the version in plain `mas list` output. Package statuses now have an optional `display_name`. Every other package manager leaves it unset, so their output doesn't change.

Requested in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13619.

## Validation

- Unit tests cover name parsing for JSON-lines, JSON-array, and text `mas list` output, including padded names, names with spaces, and entries without a name.
- `cargo +stable clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Not run on macOS. The `mas` manager only runs there, and macOS CI runs only e2e files with `macos` in the name.

> **Low Risk**
> Display-only change to bootstrap package status output; mas parsing is additive and other managers are unaffected.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Mac App Store package status** now shows human-readable app names next to numeric IDs when `mas list` reports an installed app (e.g. `497799835 (Xcode)`). Missing MAS entries stay ID-only because `mas list` has no name for uninstalled apps.
> 
> `PackageStatus` gains an optional **`display_name`**. The **mas** manager fills it from `mas list --json` (`name` / `displayName`) and from plain `mas list` text parsing (name between ID and version). **`mise bootstrap packages status`** uses `package_label` for the table column and adds a **`name`** field in **`--json`** when present; other managers set `display_name` to `None` so their output is unchanged.

title: fix(dotfiles): anchor include/exclude patterns with a leading slash to the entry root
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/205
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Per-entry `include` and `exclude` lists on `[dotfiles]` entries (`mode = "track"`, and directory-walking `symlink-each` / `copy` entries) silently ignored any pattern starting with `/`. The patterns are matched against paths relative to the entry, which never start with `/`, so:

```toml
[dotfiles]
# captured ~/.codex/cache into history anyway
"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", exclude = ["/cache"] }
# selected nothing at all
"~/.claude" = { mode = "track", include = ["/rules/*.md"] }
```

A leading `/` now anchors a pattern to the entry root, as in `.gitignore`:

- `exclude = ["/cache"]` skips only the top-level `cache` directory, not `app/cache` deeper down (a bare `cache` still matches at any depth).
- `include = ["/rules/*.md"]` selects the same files as `rules/*.md`.
- `*` stops at `/` in a rooted pattern, in both lists, as it does in include lists since #13618. So `/rules/*.md` doesn't reach into `rules/sub/`. Rooted patterns never matched anything before, so unlike an unrooted exclusion, a rooted exclusion has no older `*`-crosses-`/` behaviour to deprecate.
- `/` on its own names the entry itself and still matches nothing.

For a `symlink-each` entry, a file that a fixed `/…` exclude now covers has its recorded link removed on the next apply, the same as any newly excluded file. Note that in the global `[history] exclude` list a leading `/` still means an absolute path. The docs now say so.

### Rollback compatibility

Checkpoints record the matcher version used to read these lists. A rooted `include` that now selects files an older mise never captured could make a rollback to an older checkpoint treat those files as covered but absent, and delete them. The matcher version is bumped to 2. Checkpoints written by version 1 are still read normally unless the owning entry's `include` list has a rooted pattern. In that case the affected paths are reported as unevaluable and kept. A rooted `exclude` that now matches only moves paths out of coverage, which never deletes anything.

### Implementation

`rooted_pattern` in `src/system/files.rs` is the only place that decides whether a pattern starts at the root. `is_selected` / `is_excluded` and the capture walk's pruner (`reaches_into`) all use it, so pruning and selection agree. Patterns are still stored and shared exactly as written, so none of the compile sites needed to change.

Tests: new unit tests cover the matcher, pruner/selection agreement, and replay of version 1 checkpoints. I also checked a `symlink-each` apply with `exclude = ["/cache"]` by hand. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `mise run lint-fix` are clean.

title: refactor(env): move environment and directory statics into a mise-util crate
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/204
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. Stacked on #13616, the second step in splitting mise into crates so that edits recompile less code.

## Why

Almost every module in mise starts from `env.rs` and `dirs.rs`: `HOME`, the XDG and `MISE_*_DIR` directories, `PATH_KEY`, the `var_*` helpers. `env.rs` also mixed in code that reads `.miserc.toml`, detects the shell type, parses CLI args and reverses activation diffs, so it depended on `config`, `cli` and `shell`. As a result, no low-level module (`file`, `path`, `hash`, `lock_file`, progress reporting) could move below `config`.

## What changes

- **New `crates/mise-util` crate** holding the half of `env.rs` that only reads the process environment:
  - the env-var helpers (`var_path`, `var_is_true`, `set_var`, `vars_safe`, `args_safe`, …)
  - `HOME` and the XDG / `MISE_*_DIR` statics
  - `PATH_KEY` and its helpers
  - tokens, color and terminal-width flags
  - shim and self-replace name checks
  - Windows launcher argument recovery

  It also takes the directory statics from `dirs.rs` and the `~` expander `replace_path` from `file.rs`.
- **The rest stays in mise.** Anything that needs miserc, `Settings`, `EnvDiff`, `ShellType` or CLI parsing is unchanged, e.g. `MISE_ENV`, override filenames, `PRISTINE_ENV`/`PATH`, `prefer_offline` and `shared_install_dirs`. mise's `env`, `dirs` and `file` modules re-export the moved items, so every `crate::env::…` / `crate::dirs::…` call site is untouched.
- **`#[cfg(test)]` became a runtime switch.** `cfg(test)` doesn't reach dependencies, so the four statics that behaved differently under unit tests now check `mise_util::testing::active()`: `HOME`, `IS_RUNNING_AS_SHIM`, `TERM_WIDTH` and `TERM_WIDTH_OVERRIDE`. mise's test constructor calls `mise_util::testing::enable(<repo>/test)` before anything reads the environment, the same place it already set up the test `HOME`. Release builds never call it.
- **Dependencies:** `homedir`, `terminal_size` and `mise-agent-env` move from `mise` to `mise-util`.
- **Release:** `xtasks/release-plz` publishes `mise-util` before `mise`. `mise-agent-env` bumps now update `mise-util`'s manifest.

Tests of the helpers that became private to `mise-util` moved with them: launcher argument parsing, `PATH` key casing, token precedence, and `argv[0]` basenames.

## Follow-ups

Next is moving `file.rs`, `path.rs`, `hash.rs`, `lock_file.rs` and progress reporting into `mise-util`, which needs `mise-settings` as a dependency. After that, large areas like `src/system` can start moving out of the main crate.

## Validation

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Unit tests: `mise-util` and `mise-settings` pass (26 tests). mise passes 4843 of 4844; the one timeout, `git::tests::update_resolves_short_branches_and_tags`, runs in 0.97s against nextest's 1s limit on this machine and fails the same

title: fix(dotfiles): stop `*` crossing `/` in tracked include patterns
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/203
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A tracked directory's `include` list now uses `.gitignore` rules for patterns that contain a `/`: `*` stops at a `/` and only `**` crosses directories. This fixes a rollback that could delete a live file. Per-entry `exclude` lists keep matching what they matched before, but mise now warns when an exclusion relies on `*` crossing `/`.

## The bug

Take a tracked directory with an include list:

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", include = ["rules/*.md"] }
```

Before this change, two parts of mise read `rules/*.md` differently:

- **Capture** skipped `rules/deep/` because no part of `rules/*.md` matches `deep`. So `rules/deep/two.md` was never saved.
- **Selection** (used by rollback and by the "include list leaves out" notice) let `*` cross `/`. It treated `rules/deep/two.md` as selected.

The combination was destructive. Suppose you later widened the list to `rules/**/*.md`, saved, and then ran `mise dot rollback ~/.codex --to <the earlier checkpoint>`. Rollback saw a file the old checkpoint "selected" but didn't hold, and called it absent. That is the one answer that allows removing a live file, so the rollback **deleted `~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md`**.

Now both parts read `rules/*.md` as "markdown files directly in `rules`", and the rollback leaves the nested file alone. To select nested files as well, write `rules/**/*.md`. These are the same rules the global `[history] exclude` list already uses.

## Exclude lists: deprecation, not a silent change

`exclude` lists go through the same matcher on tracked directories and on `symlink-each` and directory `copy` entries. They keep their old meaning for now, because narrowing an exclusion would quietly start saving files you asked to leave out. For example, with `exclude = ["secrets/*.json"]`, the file `secrets/prod/settings.json` would start going into history as plaintext.

Such a path is still excluded, and mise now prints a deprecation warning:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [dotfiles-exclude-star-crosses-separator]: [dotfiles] exclude pattern 'rules/*.md' matches 'rules/deep/two.md' only because `*` crosses `/`; use `**` where a pattern should match across directories, as in include lists. This will be removed in mise 2027.9.13.
```

`rules/**/*.md` keeps the same meaning and produces no warning. Patterns without a `/` and patterns without wildcards are unaffected.

| Pattern | Path | `include` before | `include` now | `exclude` (unchanged) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rules/*.md` | `rules/one.md` | matches | matches | matches |
| `rules/*.md` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | **no match** | matches, with a warning |
| `rules/**/*.md` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | matches | matches |
| `rules/*` | `rules/deep/two.md` | matches | matches (a matched directory takes its subtree) | matches |

Rollback safety for older checkpoints is unchanged. The include change only mak

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# In a tracked entry's include pattern containing `/`, `*` stops at a
+# separator and only `**` crosses one. The capture walk skips directories an
+# include list cannot reach into, and must agree with the matcher about what
+# it selects.
+require_cmd git
+repo="$MISE_STATE_DIR/history/repo.git"
+
+mkdir -p ~/.codex/rules/deep
+echo 'always test' >~/.codex/rules/one.md
+echo 'never guess' >~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md
+
+# `rules/*.md` names only the files directly in `rules`
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[dotfiles]
+"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", include = ["rules/*.md"] }
+TOML
+assert_succeed 'mise dot track ~/.codex'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repo show HEAD:home/.codex/rules/one.md" 'always test'
+assert_fail "git --git-dir=$repo cat-file -e HEAD:home/.codex/rules/deep/two.md"
+checkpoint=$(mise dot history --json | jq -r '.[0].uuid')
+
+# `**` is how a pattern reaches deeper
+echo 'still guessing' >~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[dotfiles]
+"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", include = ["rules/**/*.md"] }
+TOML
+assert_succeed 'mise dot save'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repo show HEAD:home/.codex/rules/one.md" 'always test'
+assert "git --git-dir=$repo show HEAD:home/.codex/rules/deep/two.md" 'still guessing'
+
+# A rollback reads the list the older checkpoint recorded, and must see
+# that `rules/*.md` never covered the nested file. Reading `*` as crossing
+# `/` there called it selected but absent, the one answer that deletes a
+# live file.
+echo 'always test, again' >~/.codex/rules/one.md
+assert_succeed 'mise dot save'
+assert_succeed "mise dot rollback ~/.codex --to $checkpoint --yes"
+assert 'cat ~/.codex/rules/one.md' 'always test'
+assert 'cat ~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md' 'still guessing'
+
+# An exclude list never narrows under a user: narrowing it would save
+# files they asked to leave out. `rules/*.md` still drops the nested file,
+# and says to write `**` instead.
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[dotfiles]
+"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", exclude = ["rules/*.md"] }
+TOML
+echo 'edited' >~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md
+assert_contains 'mise dot save 2>&1' "exclude pattern 'rules/*.md' matches 'rules/deep/two.md' only because"
+assert_fail "git --git-dir=$repo cat-file -e HEAD:home/.codex/rules/one.md"
+assert_fail "git --git-dir=$repo cat-file -e HEAD:home/.codex/rules/deep/two.md"
+# the pattern that means what the older reading did is quiet
+cat >"$MISE_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml" <<'TOML'
+[dotfiles]
+"~/.codex" = { mode = "track", exclude = ["rules/**/*.md"] }
+TOML
+echo 'edited again' >~/.codex/rules/deep/two.md
+assert_not_contains 'mise dot save 2>&1' 'only because'
+assert_fail "git --git-dir=$repo cat-file -e HEAD:home/.codex/rules/deep/two.md"
+

The leading-`/` fix for `[dotfiles]` `include`/`exclude` patterns landed in #13621, which superseded the implementation originally in this PR. What remains is an end-to-end test of the exact tree from https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13613. It tracks the tree for real and checks which files land in the history repository.

For a tree containing `a.ps1`, `b.ps1`, `x.txt`, `completions/c.ps1`, and `sub/completions/d.ps1`, the test asserts:

| `include = ["/*.ps1"]` | `a.ps1`, `b.ps1` |
| `include = ["/completions/*.ps1"]` | `completions/c.ps1` |
| `include = ["*.ps1"], exclude = ["/completions"]` | `a.ps1`, `b.ps1`, `sub/completions/d.ps1` |

title: refactor(config): move generated settings types into a mise-settings crate
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/201
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Internal refactor with no user-facing change. This is the first step toward splitting mise into several crates so that edits recompile less code.

## Why

The `mise` crate is about 410k lines of Rust. Measured on an M-series Mac with a unique one-string edit to `src/duration.rs`:

- With a warm incremental cache, the rebuild takes about 11s, nearly all of it in the `mise` unit.
- When that cache is cold (a fresh worktree, a switched branch, or artifacts restored from a shared build cache), the whole crate recompiles in 75–90s. Content-addressed caches can't skip any of that, because it's one unit.

Splitting helps that cold case and full builds, but only once large parts of the code live in their own crates. Low-level modules like `file`, `dirs`, `http`, `cmd` and `platform` all call `Settings::get()`, and `Settings` has been defined inside the config system at the top of the dependency graph. Nothing can move below `config` until `Settings` does.

## What changes

- **New `crates/mise-settings` crate.** It generates the `Settings` / `SettingsPartial` / `MisercSettings` types and `SETTINGS_META` from the root `settings.toml`, which moves that codegen out of mise's `build.rs`. The crate also holds the setting value enums (including `TaskOutput`), the env-var parsers, the accessors that only read fields, and the process-wide settings cache.
- **Loading stays in mise, behind a registered loader.** Loading settings needs config discovery, trust checks, templating and CLI flags. mise calls `mise_settings::set_loader(load)` at the start of `main` and in the test harness constructor. `Settings::try_get()` returns the cached value or runs that loader, so callers keep using `Settings::get()` as before.
- **Methods that need the rest of mise live on extension traits.** Rust's orphan rule stops mise from adding inherent methods to a type defined in another crate. Methods like `offline()`, `http_timeout()` and `reset()` therefore live on `SettingsExt` in `src/config/settings.rs`, and similar traits cover `SettingsNode` and `TaskOutput`. Call sites are unchanged apart from importing the trait. That import is most of the ~100-file diff.
- **The `python.uv_venv_auto = true` deprecation warning moved.** It now fires from the loader once the setting resolves to the legacy value, instead of inside the value's deserializer, which can't reach mise's `deprecated_at!`. The message and ID are unchanged. One difference: a `true` that a higher-precedence source overrides no longer warns.
- **Release.** `xtasks/release-plz` publishes `mise-settings` before `mise`. It copies `settings.toml` into the crate for packaging, the same way `mise-interactive-config` handles `mise.json`, and treats edits to `settings.toml` as changes to the crate.

`settings.toml` stays at the repository root, where the docs and schema tooling already read it.

## Follow-ups

title: chore(release): build Windows tarballs with thin LTO
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/199
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Windows release builds were timing out, which blocked the 2026.9.14 release PR. This switches the Windows tarballs from fat LTO to thin LTO so they finish reliably. Linux and macOS builds are unchanged.

## Why

On the `windows-latest` runner (4 vCPU / 16 GB), the fat-LTO compile and link of the `mise` crate is single-threaded and memory-bound:

- v2026.9.13 tag build: `Compiling mise` → `Finished` took about 65 minutes (74m56s total cargo time)
- 2026.9.14 release PR ([run 36133236032](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/36133236032)): the same stage was still running after 2h22m, and `build-tarball-windows-x64` hit the 150-minute job timeout

Larger Windows runners aren't available yet: the Namespace plan doesn't include Windows, and Buildkite's Windows hosted agents have to be enabled by their support team. Once one of those is in place, Windows can go back to fat LTO.

## Change

`scripts/build-tarball.ps1` sets `CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO=thin`, next to the existing `CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_PANIC=unwind` Windows override. This applies to both x64 and arm64. Thin LTO keeps most of the cross-crate inlining but optimizes in parallel and uses much less memory. The Windows binary may be slightly slower or larger than a fat-LTO build.

## Validation

Not run locally. The Windows jobs only run in the release workflow, so the next armed release PR is the real test.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
