> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Release-only build tuning for Windows artifacts; binaries may differ slightly in size or runtime performance but behavior and Linux/macOS builds are unaffected.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Windows release tarballs** no longer use the `serious` profile’s default fat LTO. `scripts/build-tarball.ps1` now sets `CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO=thin` (next to the existing `panic=unwind` override) so x64 and arm64 CI builds finish within the 150-minute job limit on memory-constrained `windows-latest` runners.
> 
> The release workflow comment on `build-tarball-windows` is updated to match: fat LTO link times were blowing past the timeout under memory pressure, with a note to revert to fat LTO when Windows jobs move to larger runners. **Linux and macOS tarball builds are unchanged** and still use the profile defaults.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 7bf52ff0d9f14656d0b3eb2617cd778a77373436. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

-    # Matches the Linux tarball job. 60 was sized for a non-LTO build; the fat-LTO
-    # link this job now does is the long pole and its cost varies a lot with
-    # available memory — locally the same relink took ~20 minutes with RAM to spare
-    # and ~180 minutes when it did not. If this proves too tight on a runner,
-    # thin LTO for Windows is the fallback.
+    # Matches the Linux tarball job. Fat LTO's link varied from ~65 minutes to

--- scripts/build-tarball.ps1 (+7/-0)
@@ -25,6 +25,13 @@ $Features = "rustls-native-roots,self_update,vfox/vendored-lua"

+# of the cross-crate inlining while optimizing in parallel with far less
+# memory. Go back to fat once the Windows builds move to a larger runner.
+$Env:CARGO_PROFILE_SERIOUS_LTO = "thin"

title: fix(system): follow HTTP mirror redirects for checksum-pinned brew sources
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/198
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Building a GNU formula from source with the brew system package manager failed because GNU's mirror redirector is currently sending requests to a plain-HTTP mirror:

```
$ curl -sI https://ftpmirror.gnu.org/hello/hello-2.12.3.tar.gz | grep -i location
Location: http://mirror.team-cymru.com/gnu//hello/hello-2.12.3.tar.gz
```

Since #13292, mise refuses HTTPS→HTTP redirects on downloads, so `mise bootstrap packages apply` stopped with:

```
mise brew:hello      download hello-2.12.3.tar.gz
mise brew:hello    ✗ failed
Error:
   0: error following redirect
   1: refusing to redirect a download from HTTPS to HTTP
```

Homebrew follows these redirects. Every formula source tarball is pinned by sha256, so downgrading the transport doesn't weaken the result. With this change, brew source downloads follow the redirect, the build completes, and a tarball that doesn't match the checksum is still rejected.

This failure is also what broke `cli/test_system_install_brew_source_slow` on the 2026.9.14 release PR (jdx/mise#13590).

## Implementation

- New `http::download_file_checksum_pinned(url, path, sha256, pr)`. It uses a private client whose redirect policy allows the downgrade, and it removes the file if the checksum doesn't match. That private client is the only one that allows the downgrade, and it can only be reached through this helper. Every other client keeps refusing it.
- `brew::source::fetch_source` now calls this helper instead of `HTTP.download_file` followed by `ensure_checksum`.

## Validation

- `TEST_ALL=1 mise run test:e2e cli/test_system_install_brew_source_slow` passes locally. At the time of the run, ftpmirror.gnu.org was redirecting to HTTP, so the test exercised the downgrade path.
- New unit test: a matching file is kept and a mismatched file is removed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(pipx): keep the user in git+ssh URLs out of the tool version
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/197
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13609.

`mise use 'pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/psf/black.git'` failed with a 404 from `https://api.github.com/repos/git+ssh://git/releases`. The tool argument parser split on the first `@`, so it read the `git@` part of the SSH URL as the version separator. The tool became `pypi:git+ssh://git` and the version became `github.com/psf/black.git`.

Now an `@` in a URL's user part (before the host's first `/`) stays in the tool name. Only an `@` after the host starts a version:

```text
pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/psf/black.git          -> latest
pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/psf/black.git@24.2.0   -> 24.2.0
```

`git+https://` URLs, scoped npm names, and bracketed options parse the same way as before.

**Validation:** added cases to `test_tool_arg_parse_input`. I ran the debug build of `mise use 'pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/psf/black.git'`: it resolved `26.5.1` from psf/black and ran `uv tool install git+ssh://git@github.com/psf/black.git@26.5.1`. I ran that same `uv` command directly and it installed black 26.5.1. Clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Localized change to CLI tool string parsing with expanded unit tests; no auth or install-path changes beyond fixing incorrect splits for URL userinfo.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes CLI tool spec parsing when backend URLs use **git+ssh** (or similar) with **userinfo** (`git@host`), where the first `@` was treated as the version separator and broke installs (e.g. `pypi:git+ssh://git@github.com/...`).
> 
> `parse_input` now detects a `scheme://` segment with no path slash yet and treats that first `@` as part of the URL; only a later `@` starts the version. **HTTPS** git URLs, scoped npm names, and bracketed options keep prior behavior.
> 
> Unit tests cover SSH/HTTPS URLs, trailing `@`, versions with `@` in ref strings, and `path://` versions.

This PR contains the following updates:

| [aube-registry](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube) | dependencies | minor | `2.3.0` → `2.4.0` |

---

> Some dependencies could not be looked up. Check the warning logs for more information.

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>aubepkg/aube (aube)</summary>

### [`v2.4.0`](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/releases/tag/v2.4.0): : Reuse node_modules/.aube-lock.yaml when the lockfile is missing

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/compare/v2.3.0...v2.4.0)

`aube install` can now rebuild a deleted lockfile from a hidden copy kept in `node_modules`, so it doesn't re-resolve from the registry. This release also makes cold installs on Linux faster and lighter on memory, and fixes lifecycle scripts on Windows and a workspace `aube update` that could drop members from the lockfile.

##### Added

- **Hidden lockfile in `node_modules`** ([#​1594](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1594) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)): Every install now writes a copy of the resolved graph to `node_modules/.aube-lock.yaml`. If the project has no lockfile of any supported kind, `aube install` starts from that copy, as pnpm does with its current lockfile. If the manifests haven't changed, the graph is reused with no resolve. If they have changed, only the specs that changed are resolved again, and the other packages keep their locked versions. `aube-lock.yaml` is then written again.

  ```console
  $ aube install      # writes aube-lock.yaml + node_modules/.aube-lock.yaml
  $ rm aube-lock.yaml
  $ aube install      # seeds from node_modules/.aube-lock.yaml, no registry resolve
  ```

  - `--frozen-lockfile` and `aube ci` still fail when there is no lockfile.
  - `--no-frozen-lockfile` ignores the hidden copy.
  - In auto-CI mode (`CI=true` with no explicit flags), an install that seeds from the hidden copy is treated as prefer-frozen.
  - If the hidden copy is broken, aube shows `WARN_AUBE_HIDDEN_LOCKFILE_BROKEN` and resolves normally.
  - The hidden copy is not used with `lockfile=false`, which also deletes any existing copy, or with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile=false`. It is also skipped for reuse installs from npm, yarn or bun lockfiles.

##### Changed

- **Faster, lighter cold installs on Linux** ([#​1598](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1598), [#​1603](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1603), [#​1604](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1604), [#​1605](https://redirect.github.com/aubepkg/aube/pull/1605) by [@​jdx](https://redirect.github.com/jdx)):
  - On Linux, the blocking thread pool now defaults to 8 threads instead of 12

title: feat(pypi): support #subdirectory= and .git-less URLs in git sources
body:
Python CLIs that live in a monorepo document installs like `pipx install "git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui"`. The pypi backend couldn't install that form. Now it can:

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui" = "main"
"pypi:runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=jtui" = "main"   # GitHub shorthand works too
```

Discussed in #4595.

## Before / after

| Tool name | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui` | No `.git`, so it was read as GitHub shorthand and failed with a 404 from `api.github.com/repos/git+https://…/releases` | Installs `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui@main#subdirectory=ltui` |
| `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui.git#subdirectory=ltui` | Everything after `.git` dropped; installed the repository root | Installs `git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui.git@main#subdirectory=ltui` |
| `runpantheon/ltui@main#subdirectory=ltui` (fragment in the version, the workaround from #4595) | Installs, but the version directory contains `#`. uv writes that path into launcher shebangs, and macOS then fails with `bad interpreter` | Unchanged. The docs now point to the tool-name form |

## Behavior

- `git+<scheme>://…` is recognized with or without a trailing `.git`, and the remote is used as written (so `git+file:///path/to/repo` works). GitHub shorthand still gets `.git` added, as before.
- The `#…` fragment is kept and passed to uv/pipx. `subdirectory`, `egg`, and any other keys pass through verbatim. The requested ref goes before the fragment (`git+<remote>@<ref>#subdirectory=…`), as pip and uv require. `[...]` in a tool name is still parsed as mise tool options, so extras go in the `extras` option, not `#egg=pkg[extra]`.
- The fragment is part of the tool name, so sibling packages from one repository are separate tools with separate install directories. mise's tool directory name already strips `#` (`pipx-runpantheon-ltui-subdirectory-jtui/main`), so launchers work.
- Version discovery uses only the repository. GitHub releases, `git ls-remote` tags, and default-branch HEAD work as they do without a fragment. `mise ls-remote` returns the same list for the fragment form and for `pypi:runpantheon/ltui`.
- The venv's Python link is rewritten to the minor-version path (so Python patch upgrades don't break the tool) by finding the venv under the install path. Before, it guessed the venv name from the tool name, which misses fragment tools and repos whose name differs from the distribution name (ltui's `ltui/` builds `ltui-linear`).
- Extras: on the pipx path, `egg=<pkg>[extras]` is merged into the existing fragment (one `#`). Without `package_name`, the distribution name is now guessed from `egg`, then from the last segment of `subdirectory`, and only then from the repository name.

Tool names that parsed before (all of which had `.git` or were shorthand) produce the same install requests; regression tests pin the existing

+| Source                   | Example                                               |
+| ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- |
+| PyPI, latest version     | `pypi:black`                                          |
+| PyPI, specific version   | `pypi:black@24.3.0`                                   |
+| GitHub, latest release   | `pypi:psf/black`                                      |
+| GitHub, specific release | `pypi:psf/black@24.3.0`                               |
+| Git repository           | `pypi:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git`           |
+| Git branch               | `pypi:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git@main`      |
+| Git subdirectory         | `pypi:git+https://github.com/o/repo#subdirectory=cli` |
+
+For GitHub sources, `latest` selects the newest GitHub release and installs from
+the default branch only when the repository has no releases. For other Git URLs,
+`latest` resolves default-branch HEAD to a concrete commit. Any branch, tag, or
+commit can be requested explicitly, and remote tags are also available for
+explicit version requests.
+
+### Monorepo subdirectories {#git-subdirectory}
+
+For a package that lives in a subdirectory of a Git repository, add the same
+`#subdirectory=` fragment that pip and uv accept. The `.git` suffix is optional,
+and the fragment also works with GitHub shorthand:
+
+```sh
+mise use 'pypi:git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui@main'
+mise use 'pypi:runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=jtui@main'
+```
+
+Quote the argument so the shell does not treat `#` specially. The fragment is
+part of the tool name, so each subdirectory is a separate tool, and the version
+still goes after `@`. mise places the ref before the fragment in the request it
+sends to the installer. Other fragment keys pass through unchanged, except
+that mise reads `[...]` in a tool name as [tool options](/dev-tools/#tool-options);
+use the [`extras`](#extras) option instead of `#egg=pkg[extra]`.
+
+Versions come from the repository as a whole, so `latest` selects the newest
+release even if the subdirectory did not exist at that tag. Pin a branch or
+commit when a repository's releases predate the subdirectory. When you use
+[`extras`](#extras), mise guesses the distribution name from the subdirectory;
+set `package_name` if the name differs.
 
 Direct HTTPS archive URLs are unsupported. Other source syntax may work but is
 unsupported and untested.
--- e2e/backend/test_pipx_git_subdirectory (+38/-0)

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# pip/uv VCS URL fragments (`#subdirectory=`) select a package inside a monorepo.
+require_cmd python3
+
+export MISE_PYTHON_COMPILE=0
+export MISE_PYTHON_GITHUB_ATTESTATIONS=0
+
+ref=f05b7ddaa9725baddf7e0833502795b66f9d7dd7
+ltui="pipx:git+https://github.com/runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=ltui"
+jtui="pipx:runpantheon/ltui#subdirectory=jtui"
+
+cat >mise.toml <<EOF
+[tools]
+python = "3.12.3"
+uv = "0.12.10"
+"$ltui" = "$ref"
+"$jtui" = "$ref"
+EOF
+
+mise install
+
+# The fragment is part of the tool name, so the install path has no `#`,
+# which would break the interpreter path uv writes into launcher shebangs.
+ltui_path="$(mise where "$ltui")"
+jtui_path="$(mise where "$jtui")"
+assert_not_contains "echo '$ltui_path'" "#"
+assert_not_contains "echo '$jtui_path'" "#"

+assert_contains "$MISE_DATA_DIR/shims/jtui --version" "jtui 0.3.0"
+assert_contains "mise x -- jtui --version" "jtui 0.3.0"
+
+# The venv is named after the distribution (ltui-linear), not the tool name, and
+# its Python link must use the minor-version path so patch upgrades keep working.
+assert_contains "readlink '$ltui_path/ltui-linear/bin/python' '$ltui_path/ltui-linear/bin/python3'" "/installs/python/3.12/"
+assert_not_contains "readlink '$ltui_path/ltui-linear/bin/python' '$ltui_path/ltui-linear/bin/python3'" "/installs/python/3.12.3/"

title: ci: defer release PR merges overnight with a release-now override
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/195
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Releases should be able to be kicked off in the evening and actually go out the next morning, so nothing ships while nobody is around to watch it. Two recent releases landed in the middle of the night Central time (`v2026.9.9` at 00:08 CDT, `v2026.9.3` at 01:51 CDT).

This adds a `release-window` commit status on the release PR. Once it is a required check on main:

- **Defer:** enable auto-merge on the release PR at, say, 8pm. Between 18:00 and 03:00 America/Chicago the status is `pending` ("Waiting for 03:00 Central; label release-now to release immediately"), so the PR waits instead of merging. The scheduled run shortly after 03:00 flips it to `success` and auto-merge completes on its own.
- **Override:** add the `release-now` label to the release PR. The status turns `success` immediately and the release proceeds (removing the label restores the hold).
- **Daytime:** the status is `success`, so releases behave as today.
- **Every other PR:** always `success`; normal PRs are unaffected.

Note that enabling auto-merge still starts the release dry-run build right away (the existing `auto_merge_enabled` gate in `release.yml`); only the merge, and therefore publishing, waits.

## Details

- The gate sits on the merge because merging the release PR is what makes `xtasks/release-plz` publish crates and push the tag. Gating `release.yml` instead would leave a published crate with no GitHub release.
- Six scheduled runs a day (UTC times chosen to cover both CDT and CST) flip the status at the edges: around 17:07 Central it turns `pending` (anything within an hour of 18:00 counts as quiet), and around 03:07 Central it turns `success`. Each edge has follow-up runs an hour or two later in case GitHub delays or drops one.
- Only the release PR's own events and the schedule write the status of this repository's `release` branch commit, all in one serialized concurrency group; other PRs (including forks with a `release` branch) never write it, so they cannot clear the hold or revive a removed override. A failed branch lookup fails the job without posting a status, keeping the PR blocked.
- `pull_request_target` lets the workflow post statuses on fork PRs; it reads only PR metadata and checks out no code, like `conventional-commits.yml`.

## After merging

1. Create the `release-now` label.
2. Add `release-window` to the required status checks in the main ruleset (after merge, since `pull_request_target` runs from main; PRs already open need a new push or reopen to receive the status).

## Validation

- `actionlint`, `zizmor`, and `prettier` pass; quiet-hour boundaries checked locally for every scheduled run time (16:07 success, 17:07 pending, 02:07 pending, 03:07 success).
- Not yet exercised on a live release PR.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: 2.1.236.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/cl
author: jdx
diff:
--- .github/workflows/release-window.yml (+125/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,125 @@
+name: release-window
+
+# Holds the release PR during quiet hours (18:00-03:00 America/Chicago) by
+# posting a pending `release-window` commit status, which is a required check
+# on main. Merging the release PR is what publishes crates and pushes the tag
+# (see xtasks/release-plz), so this is the only safe place to gate a release.
+# A few scheduled runs flip the status at the two edges: it goes pending when
+# quiet hours start within the hour (~17:07 Central), and back to success after
+# 03:00, when an armed auto-merge completes on its own.
+# The status is keyed by commit, so only the release PR's own events and the
+# schedule write the `release` branch commit's status; other PRs never touch
+# it, and every other commit gets success.
+#
+# To release now anyway, add the `release-now` label to the release PR.
+
+on: # zizmor: ignore[dangerous-triggers] reads only PR metadata and executes no untrusted code
+  pull_request_target:
+    branches: ["main"]
+    types: [opened, edited, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]
+  schedule:
+    # UTC times covering both CDT and CST. Evening: 17:07/18:07/19:07 CDT,
+    # 16:07/17:07/18:07 CST. Morning: 03:07/04:07/05:07 CDT, 02:07/03:07/04:07
+    # CST. Each edge gets a follow-up run in case one is delayed or dropped.
+    - cron: "7 22,23,0 * * *"
+    - cron: "7 8,9,10 * * *"
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions: {}
+
+# Every run that can write the release PR's status shares one group, so the
+# newest run (which reads the latest labels and time) always posts last. A
+# fork's `release` branch gets its own group so it cannot cancel those runs.
+concurrency:
+  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref == 'release' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository && 'release' || github.event.pull_request.number || 'release' }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+jobs:
+  status:
+    if: github.repository == 'jdx/mise'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    permissions:
+      contents: read
+      pull-requests: read
+      statuses: write
+    steps:
+      - name: Set release-window status
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
+          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
+          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
+          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
+          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+
+          set_status() {
+            gh api "repos/$REPO/statuses/$1" \
+              -f context=release-window -f state="$2" -f description="$3" >/dev/null
+            echo "$1: $2 ($3)"
+          }
+
+          # Minutes since local midnight fall in 18:00-03:00 Central.
+          is_quiet() {
+            local m=$(($1 % 1440))
+            [ "$m" -ge $((18 * 60)) ] || [ "$m" -lt $((3 * 60)) ]
+          }
+
+          release_state() {
+            read -r hour minute < <(TZ=America/Chicago date '+%-H %-M')
+            local now=$((hour * 60 + minute))
+            if is_quiet "$now" || is_quiet $((now + 60)); then
+              echo pending "Waiting for 03:00 Central; label release-now to release immediately"
+            else
+              echo success "Inside the release window"
+            fi
+          }
+
+          # Only this repository's `release` branch, never a fork's branch of the
+          # same name, identifies the release PR. Only a 404 means there is no
+          # release branch; any other failure must not fall through to success.
+          if ! release_sha=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/branches/release" --jq .commit.sha 2>lookup.err); then
+            cat lookup.err >&2
+            if ! grep -q "HTTP 404" lookup.err; then
+              echo "::error::Could not look up the release branch; leaving release-window unset"
+              exit 1
+            fi
+            release_sha=""
+          fi
+
+          if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "pull_request_target" ]; then
+            sha="$HEAD_SHA"
+            if [ "$HEAD_REF" != "release" ] || [ "$HEAD_REPO" != "$REPO" ]; then
+              # Runs for other PRs are not serialized with the release runs, so
+              # they must never write the release commit's status.
+              if [ "$sha" = "$release_sha" ]; then
+                echo "Head is the release commit; its status belongs to the release PR"
+              else
+                set_status "$sha" success "Not a release PR"
+              fi
+              exit 0
+            fi
+            if [ "$sha" != "$release_sha" ]; then
+              echo "Release branch has moved past $sha; a newer run will set its status"
+              exit 0
+            fi
+          else
+            sha="$release_sha"
+            if [ -z "$sha" ]; then
+              echo "No release branch"
+              exit 0
+            fi
+          fi
+
+          # The `owner:release` head filter only matches this repository's branch.
+          labels=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/pulls?head=${REPO%%/*}:release&base=main&state=open" \
+            --jq '.[0].labels // [] | map(.name) | join(",")')
+          if [[ ",$labels," == *",release-now,"* ]]; then
+            set_status "$sha" success "Overridden by the release-now label"
+            exit 0
+          fi
+
+          read -r state description < <(release_state)
+          set_status "$sha" "$state" "$description"

title: fix(backend): don't reuse versions-host version lists when MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/194
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Fixes #13604.

For a registry tool, mise gets the remote version list from the versions host (mise-versions.jdx.dev). The host picks up new GitHub releases after a delay, and mise then caches its list for `fetch_remote_versions_cache` (1h by default). `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0` should skip the host and fetch from the source directly. Instead it used the same cache entry, so it returned the host's older list until that entry expired.

Before, right after `jdx/tak` v0.0.11 was published:

```sh
mise ls-remote tak                           # host list cached: up to 0.0.10
MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0 mise ls-remote tak  # same cache entry: still up to 0.0.10
```

After, `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0` has its own remote-versions cache entry, so it lists versions from the backend and shows 0.0.11. Turning the host off adds a cache key, but turning it on doesn't, so caches that already exist for the default setting stay valid. The extra key is only added for backends the versions host can serve (github, aqua, core, asdf, vfox, and similar). Backends like npm and cargo always list from their own source, so they keep a single cache entry.

The hosted `latest` release cache that the issue also mentions already uses separate hosted and direct keys (`release_cache_key` in `src/github.rs`), so it needed no change. This PR doesn't change `mise cache clear <tool>`. That command still doesn't clear the tool's `github/` release cache.

### Validation

- New e2e test `e2e/cli/test_ls_remote_versions_host_cache`. A local stand-in, set up with `url_replacements`, serves both the versions host (only 0.0.10) and the GitHub API (0.0.10 and 0.0.11) for the registry tool `tak`. After the host list is cached, `MISE_USE_VERSIONS_HOST=0 mise ls-remote tak` must list 0.0.11, and the host-on cache entry must stay as it was. Without the fix, the host-off run returns only 0.0.10.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.

title: feat(config): load conf.d folders as self-contained config fragments
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/193
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

A `conf.d` fragment used to be a single `.toml` file. That makes it hard to split machine setup by purpose: a `[dotfiles]` entry in `~/.config/mise/conf.d/git.toml` can't keep its `gitconfig` next to it, so every source needs an absolute path. People used `[bootstrap].config_roots` for this, which is deprecated (#13010, discussions #12120 and #12987).

Now a **folder** inside any `conf.d` directory is also a fragment, and that folder is the config root for its files:

```text
~/.config/mise/conf.d/
├── git.toml                  # single-file fragment, unchanged
└── git-tools/                # folder fragment
    ├── mise.toml             # always loaded
    ├── mise.local.toml       # always loaded, usually gitignored
    ├── mise.linux.toml       # loaded when the linux environment is active
    └── gitconfig
```

```toml
# ~/.config/mise/conf.d/git-tools/mise.toml
[dotfiles]
"~/.gitconfig" = "gitconfig"   # resolves to conf.d/git-tools/gitconfig
```

- Works in global (`~/.config/mise/conf.d`), system (`/etc/mise/conf.d`), and project (`mise/`, `.mise/`, `.config/mise/`) `conf.d` directories.
- Relative paths resolve inside the folder, `{{ config_root }}` is the folder, and tasks defined there run there by default.
- The folder can be a symlink, so a dotfiles checkout keeps its own layout: `ln -s ~/src/dotfiles/git ~/.config/mise/conf.d/git-tools`.
- Only `mise.toml`, `mise.local.toml`, `mise.<env>.toml`, and `mise.<env>.local.toml` are read. Folders are not searched recursively, and folders starting with `.` are ignored.
- `mise.<env>.toml` files load for explicit and platform (`auto_env`) environments. Folders are new, so they are not part of the `env_conf_d` migration.
- Like single-file fragments, folder fragments are never write targets: `mise use`, `mise set`, and `mise settings set` still write to the directory's regular config.
- Precedence: folder fragments load after the single-file fragments in the same `conf.d`, in folder-name order, and before that directory's regular config (`config.toml`). Their environment and local files take the same slots as `conf.d/<name>.<env>.toml` and `conf.d/<name>.local.toml`. Project folder fragments share the project's lockfile.

Because every section loads through the normal config system, this covers what `config_roots` never did: tools, tasks, packages, hooks, and `[env]`. Migrating off `config_roots` means moving or symlinking each bundle directory into `conf.d`, with no path rewrites. `config_roots` gave each root its own `[vars]` and rejected conflicting declarations across roots. Folder fragments use normal precedence instead.

Compatibility: a directory already inside a mise `conf.d` that contains a `mise.toml` will now load. Only `conf.d` directories mise reads count (`mise/`, `.mise/`, the global and system config dirs), so a project that happens to live at `nginx/conf.d/site/mise.toml`

title: fix(prune): keep versions pinned by configs a project's .miserc.toml ignores
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/192
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise prune` could delete a tool version that another project still pins. It happened when you ran prune from a directory whose `.miserc.toml` lists that project in `ignored_config_paths`. `mise ls --prunable` and the stale-version check in `mise upgrade` had the same problem. Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13600.

Example layout:

| path | content |
|:---|:---|
| `project-a/mise.toml` | pins `jq = "1.7.1"` (trusted, installed) |
| `project-b/.miserc.toml` | `ignored_config_paths = ["../project-a"]` |

Before this change, running `mise prune --yes` in `project-b` removed jq 1.7.1, and `mise which jq` in `project-a` then failed. Running the same command from the repository root kept it. Now a project's own `.miserc.toml` no longer changes the result: `project-a/mise.toml` is still tracked, so jq 1.7.1 is kept.

### Behavior

Commands that act on every tracked config honor `ignored_config_paths` only from machine-wide sources:

- the `MISE_IGNORED_CONFIG_PATHS` environment variable
- the global `~/.config/mise/miserc.toml`
- the system `miserc.toml`

A project's `.miserc.toml` still controls which configs load for that project. It just no longer hides other projects' configs from prune or upgrade. A path ignored machine-wide is still skipped, as before. Relative paths in `MISE_IGNORED_CONFIG_PATHS` still resolve from the directory where mise was invoked. The `ignored_config_paths` setting docs now describe this.

miserc templates now render `{{ cwd }}` from the directory mise was invoked in, even after `-C` changes directory. The global ignore list is reloaded lazily, so this keeps it identical to what startup rendered.

### Implementation

Tracked-config loading now runs inside a task-local scope. In that scope, `is_ignored_via_setting` uses a matcher built from the env var and the global/system miserc files only. The scope has to cover the trust check inside config parsing too; otherwise `is_trusted` would still reject the config because of the local ignore.

### Tests

New e2e test `cli/test_prune_miserc_ignored_config_paths` reproduces the report. It fails without this change and passes with it. It also checks that a global miserc ignore still excludes the config. The existing prune, miserc, and ignored-config e2e tests pass, and clippy is clean. On macOS, `test_prune_tool_stub` fails at a BSD `touch -d` call in the test script, which this change does not touch.

title: fix(pipx): treat PEP 440 .devN releases as prereleases
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/191
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise upgrade` could install PyPI developmental releases (`.devN`) for `pypi:`/`pipx:` tools set to `latest`, even though uv and pip skip them by default. For example, with `"pypi:yt-dlp" = "latest"`, mise treated `2026.9.16.232951.dev0` as the latest stable release:

- with `minimum_release_age = "0"`, `mise upgrade` installed the dev build
- with `minimum_release_age` set, mise printed a misleading warning that the "newer release 2026.9.16.232951.dev0" was ignored by the age gate

The pipx backend's latest-stable lookup (PyPI JSON API) used a PEP 440 prerelease pattern that only recognized `aN`/`bN`/`cN`/`rcN` suffixes. It now also recognizes developmental releases (`.devN`, plus the `1.0dev` / `1.0-dev1` spellings PEP 440 normalizes to it).

Before / after, with `MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0` and `"pypi:yt-dlp" = "latest"`:

```
$ mise outdated --bump pypi:yt-dlp   # before
pypi:yt-dlp  latest  [MISSING]  [NONE]  2026.9.16.232951.dev0
$ mise outdated --bump pypi:yt-dlp   # after
pypi:yt-dlp  latest  [MISSING]  [NONE]  2026.8.19
```

Python-flavored backends (`pipx`, the `python` core plugin) now use one prerelease rule everywhere (latest-stable lookup, prerelease marking of the remote version list, and `latest`/prefix matching). That rule combines the PEP 440 suffixes with the shared channel tags such as `-rc1`, and ignores PEP 440 local labels: `1.1+gpu.dev0` from a private index is a stable release, not a prerelease. Other backends are unchanged.

Fixes #13599

Validation: unit tests for the prerelease rule, pipx latest-stable selection and stamping, and PEP 440 fuzzy matching; clippy with `-D warnings` is clean.

title: fix(bootstrap): point config_roots deprecation warning at conf.d folders
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/190
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`[bootstrap].config_roots` was deprecated in 2026.9.3 (#13010). Its warning said to "move bootstrap declarations into global or system configuration". That doesn't tell users how to keep a setup split into self-contained bundles, which is why they used `config_roots`.

#13603 added `conf.d` folders: a folder inside `conf.d` is a config fragment and the config root for its own files. That is a direct migration path, so the warning now says to use it:

```
mise WARN  deprecated [bootstrap.config_roots]: `[bootstrap].config_roots` in ~/dotfiles/mise.toml is deprecated. Move each selected root into a conf.d folder instead (or symlink it): bundles/git becomes mise/conf.d/git in the same project, or ~/.config/mise/conf.d/git when config_roots is set in global config. A conf.d folder reads only mise.toml, mise.local.toml, mise.<env>.toml, and mise.<env>.local.toml (rename other config filenames) and is their config root, so relative paths and `{{ config_root }}` still resolve inside it. See https://mise.jdx.dev/configuration.html#conf-d-folders for details. This will be removed in mise 2027.3.3.
```

For example, this setup:

```toml
# ~/dotfiles/mise.toml
[bootstrap]
config_roots = ["*/*"]   # dev/git/mise.toml, shell/zsh/mise.macos.toml, ...
```

becomes `~/dotfiles/mise/conf.d/dev-git/` and `~/dotfiles/mise/conf.d/shell-zsh/`, moved or symlinked, with the root `config_roots` removed. A project's `mise/conf.d` loads exactly when its `mise.toml` does. If `config_roots` was set in global config, the bundles go to `~/.config/mise/conf.d/` so they still apply from any directory. The warning prints the real global `conf.d` path, so it follows `MISE_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`. Relative dotfile sources keep resolving inside each folder. Unlike `config_roots`, every section in a folder participates (tools, tasks, packages, hooks, `[env]`).

The `config_roots` schema description points to the same docs. Behavior and the removal date are unchanged.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_config_roots_inventory`
- converted a `config_roots` setup with relative dotfile sources and a `mise.macos.toml` bundle to `conf.d` folders: `mise bootstrap --dry-run` (with `auto_env`) produces the same links and copies, from the new folder paths
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the **`[bootstrap].config_roots`** deprecation guidance so it tells users to migrate bundles into **`conf.d` folders** (with symlink/move examples and a link to the conf.d docs) instead of sug

title: chore: bootstrap Claude Code on the web sessions for mise development
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/189
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Contributor tooling only — no change to the mise CLI.

## Problem

Claude Code on the web sessions for this repo started with nothing usable: no `mise` on `PATH`, no `target/`, and a preinstalled rustc (1.94.1) older than the crate's `rust-version`, so an agent could not build, lint, or run tests without bootstrapping by hand first.

## What this changes

- **SessionStart hook** (`.claude/settings.json` → `.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`). It runs on session `startup`/`resume`/`fork` (not `/clear` or compaction), with a 30-minute timeout because a cold bootstrap takes about 10 minutes. It only does anything when `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, so local Claude Code sessions are untouched. It reuses the existing Cursor Cloud bootstrap `.cursor/install.sh`, so both runners share one setup path. Its output goes to stderr so build logs don't land in the model context, and it adds the mise shims and `/usr/local/bin` to the session `PATH` via `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. It runs synchronously, so the session starts once the environment is ready.
- **Latest stable Rust** in `.cursor/install.sh` instead of the `Cargo.toml` MSRV (`rustup toolchain install stable` with rustfmt and clippy, which also syncs an existing stable). This applies to Cursor Cloud Agents too.
- **Builds that match what agents run.** `mise.toml`'s `[wrappers.cargo]` (mbx) sets `HOST_CC`/`CMAKE` and leaves read-only outputs in `target/`, so a bare `cargo build` and `mise run build` invalidate each other's `-sys` crates, and a bare build can't overwrite mbx outputs at all. The bootstrap now:
  - with no `target/` yet: runs a plain `cargo build` into `target/`;
  - with an existing `target/debug/mise`: refreshes it through `mise run build`, trusting the config for that one process only, so a binary from an older checkout is never used for `mise install`;
  - if that old binary can't run this checkout's config: runs a plain `cargo build` into `target/bootstrap`.

  After `mise install` and `mise trust`, it runs `mise run build` so `target/` is warm for agents, and points `/usr/local/bin/mise` at `target/debug/mise`.
- **Tokens:** every build runs with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` unset, since builds execute checkout-controlled build scripts and task config.
- `AGENTS.md`'s cloud-agent section now covers both Cursor Cloud and Claude Code on the web.

## Validation (in a Claude Code on the web container)

- Cold hook run: exit 0 in about 9m45s, with no stdout.
- Warm reruns: about 8–10s each, 0 crates recompiled; `mise run build` afterwards is a no-op.
- Stale-binary fallback, forced with a `target/debug/mise` stub that always fails: exit 0 in 9m23s. The binary was built in `target/bootstrap`, then a real `target/debug/mise` was restored and linked.
- With the `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` gate unset, the hook exits 0 immediately.
- `hk check` (prettier and markdownlin

--- .claude/hooks/session-start.sh (+22/-0)
@@ -0,0 +1,22 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SessionStart hook for Claude Code on the web. Reuses the Cloud Agent
+# bootstrap in .cursor/install.sh so both runners share one setup path.
+# Local sessions are left alone: the bootstrap edits /etc and runs apt-get.
+set -euo pipefail

+if [ "${CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE:-}" != "true" ]; then
+	exit 0
+fi
+
+repo_root="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd -P)}"

+# The bootstrap persists shims via /etc/profile.d, which non-login agent
+# shells may not source. Export them for this session too.
+if [ -n "${CLAUDE_ENV_FILE:-}" ]; then
+	cat >>"$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE" <<'ENV'
+export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:/usr/local/bin:$PATH"
+ENV
+fi

+}

+# Builds run checkout-controlled build scripts and task config; keep every
+# GitHub token name mise reads (src/github.rs) out of their environment.
+no_tokens=(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN -u MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN -u GH_TOKEN -u GITHUB_API_TOKEN)

+# (mbx) sets HOST_CC/CMAKE and leaves read-only outputs in target/. A bare
+# `cargo build` would dirty those -sys crates and cannot overwrite them, so:

+# - old binary cannot run this checkout's config: bare build in its own dir;
+# - cold (no target/ yet): bare build in target/; `mise run build` below
+#   then brings it under the wrapper.
+boot_bin="$PWD/target/debug/mise"
+if [ -x "$boot_bin" ] &&
+	"${no_tokens[@]}" MISE_YES=1 MISE_TRUSTED_CONFIG_PATHS="$PWD" "$boot_bin" run build; then
+	:

+		cargo build --all-features --ignore-rust-version
+	boot_bin="$PWD/target/bootstrap/debug/mise"
+else
+	"${no_tokens[@]}" cargo build --all-features --ignore-rust-version
 fi

-rustup toolchain install "$msrv" --profile minimal --no-self-update -c rustfmt,clippy
-rustup default "$msrv"
-
-cargo build --all-features --ignore-rust-version
 # Always invoke this binary. `mise activate --shims` prepends shims that may
 # point at an older mise which still ran tool-level postinstall under MISE_SAFE.
 mise_bin=/usr/local/bin/mise
-"${SUDO[@]}" ln -sfn "$PWD/target/debug/mise" "$mise_bin"
+"${SUDO[@]}" ln -sfn "$boot_bin" "$mise_bin"
 hash -r
 
 export MISE_YES=1
@@ -130,6 +148,11 @@ MISE_SAFE=1 "$mise_bin" install
 # safe mode so a branch-defined hook or tool-level postinstall could not run
 # with GitHub tokens.
 "$mise_bin" trust
+# Leave target/ warm for the wrapped cargo agents use (a no-op when the warm
+# refresh above already ran) and point mise at the binary it produces.
+"${no_tokens[@]}" "$mise_bin" run build
+"${SUDO[@]}" ln -sfn "$PWD/target/debug/mise" "$mise_bin"
+hash -r
 hk install --mise
 
 # Snapshots keep disk state but reset process env, so `eval "$(mise activate …)"`
--- AGENTS.md (+5/-4)
@@ -290,18 +290,19 @@ When referencing mise documentation URLs, use the correct path structure based o
 
 Do NOT use shortened paths like `mise.jdx.dev/backends/...` - always include the full path matching the `docs/` directory structure.
 
-## Cursor Cloud specific instructions
+## Cloud agent instructions (Cursor Cloud and Claude Code on the web)
 
-Cloud Agents bootstrap from `.cursor/environment.json`, which runs `.cursor/install.sh`. Draft environment builds often run as `ubuntu` rather than `root`; the script handles both (passwordless sudo, cargo/rustup permissions, world-writable `/tmp/fslock`).
+Cursor Cloud Agents bootstrap from `.cursor/environment.json`, which runs `.cursor/install.sh`. Claude Code on the web runs the same script from the SessionStart hook in `.claude/settings.json` (`.claude/hooks/session-start.sh`), which runs on session `startup`/`resume`/`fork` (not `/clear` or compaction) with a 30-minute timeout, exits immediately unless `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE=true`, sends the bootstrap output to stderr, and adds the mise shims and `/usr/local/bin` to `PATH` through `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. The hook runs synchronously, so the session starts after the build finishes. Claude cloud containers do not provide a GitHub token by default; add `GITHUB_TOKEN` as an environment secret to avoid GitHub API rate limits during `mise install` and e2e tests. Use a fine-grained token with public-repository read-only access and no other permissions: any branch a session checks out (its hook, build scripts, tests, and tasks) can read the session environment. Draft environment builds often run as `ubuntu` rather than `root`; the script handles both (passwordless sudo, cargo/rustup permissions, world-writable `/tmp/fslock`).
 
 The install script:
 
 - cds to the repository root derived from the script path before reading `Cargo.toml` or building
 - installs host packages needed to build mise and to run most e2e tests (openssl, pkg-config, zsh, fish, direnv, python3 + venv, jq, git, build-essential, and compile-time libs). It does **not** install a JDK or GUI libraries; those live in `packaging/e2e/Dockerfile`. `apt-get` is invoked as `sudo -n env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get …` so the frontend reaches apt when elevation is required
-- selects the Rust toolchain from the root `Cargo.toml` `rust-version`, including `rustfmt` and `clippy` (do not hardcode the MSRV)
-- builds `target/debug/mise` and symlinks it to `/usr/local/bin/mise`
+- installs and defaults to the latest stable Rust toolchain (not the `Cargo.toml` `rust-version` MSRV), including `rustfmt` and `clippy`, and updates it on reruns
+- gets a bootstrap `mise` and symlinks it to `/usr/local/bin/mise`: an existing `target/debug/mise` refreshes itself with `mise run build`; if it cannot run this checkout's config, a plain `cargo build` goes to `target/bootstrap` (the `mbx` wrapper leaves read-only outputs in `target/`); with no `target/` yet, a plain `cargo build` goes to `target/`
 - keeps `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, and `GH_TOKEN` in sync via one `sync_github_tokens` helper (prefer any already-set token; fall back to `gh auth token` only when all three are empty)
 - runs `MISE_SAFE=1 /usr/local/bin/mise install` with the just-built binary so checkout-controlled hooks/templates/`[env]` and tool-level `postinstall` / `install_env` cannot run with those tokens, then `mise trust` for later agent commands
+- runs `mise run build` so `target/` is warm for the `mbx`-wrapped cargo (`[wrappers.cargo]` in `mise.toml`) that agents build with, then points `/usr/local/bin/mise` at `target/debug/mise`. Every build runs with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, and `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` unset
 - runs `hk install --mise` (`hk.pkl` has no git hook, so this may report that nothing is installed)
 - persists mise shims and token sync in one `/etc/profile.d/mise-dev-env.sh` (shims first, then `sync_github_tokens`) and rewrites the Cloud Agent block in `/etc/bash.bashrc` so non-login interactive bash picks it up after a snapshot. Fish/zsh only get this from login shells (`profile.d`), not from bashrc
 - exposes the mise-installed `node` / `npm` / `npx` / `hk` / `gh` binaries on `/usr/local/bin` (isolated e2e PATH includes that directory, not the agent's shims). Links freeze the version from install time — re-run `.cursor/install.sh` after upgrading those tools

title: fix(install): ignore interrupted installs when listing versions and runtime symlinks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/188
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

An interrupted or in-progress install leaves the version directory on disk and marks it with an `incomplete` file in the cache (`~/.cache/mise/<tool>/<version>/incomplete`). `mise install` and `mise ls` already honored that marker, but three other places still looked for it inside the install dir (`installs/<tool>/<version>/incomplete`). mise hasn't written a marker there for years, so those checks never matched.

As a result, a half-installed version:

- stayed in the install-state scan used for shims and tool listing,
- kept its runtime symlinks (`latest`, `1`, `1.2`), so `installs/node/latest` could point into a partial install. The stale-link pruning added for exactly this case never fired, and
- could still be picked as the latest installed version (for example, when resolving a `latest` request against installed versions).

These call sites now look the marker up in the cache. A shared or system install root uses the same marker as a local one.

When runtime links are rebuilt, an interrupted install's directory is still protected. For example, an unfinished `1.1` directory is never deleted and replaced with a `1.1` link to a complete `1.1.0`.

This also explains part of the confusion in #13581, where removing a hand-placed `installs/.../incomplete` file had no effect.

### Tests

- `e2e/backend/test_runtime_symlink_stale_prune` created its marker in the old location, so it tested a state mise never produces. It now writes the marker to the real path. It fails without this fix and passes with it.
- The `runtime_symlinks` unit tests create their markers in the cache under per-test tool names, so they can't interfere with each other.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5; version: unavailable.*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches install-state scans, latest-version resolution, and runtime symlink rebuild/prune—core install paths—but behavior aligns with existing install/ls semantics and is covered by updated e2e/unit tests.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Interrupted installs** are tracked only by a cache-side `incomplete` marker (`~/.cache/mise/<tool>/<version>/incomplete`), but install-state scanning, runtime symlink rebuild/prune, and “latest installed” resolution were still checking `installs/.../<version>/incomplete`, so half-finished versions could still appear in listings, keep `latest`/`1.x` links, and win version selection.
> 
> This PR **unifies those checks** on `install_state::incomplete_file_path` (and `scan_versions` keyed by the tool’s logical name when the install dir is renamed). **Runtime symlink logic** now drops links into incomplete versions while **protecting** their on-disk directories (including selector slots like `1.1` or `latest`) from being replaced by generated links. E2e and unit tests now create

title: fix(oci): apply dotfiles exclude and git manifest to directory entries
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/186
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

`mise oci build` now bakes the same files into an image's dotfiles layer that `mise dot apply` deploys. Before this fix, `[dotfiles]` entries with `mode = "symlink-each"`, or `mode = "copy"` with a directory source, ignored `exclude` and `manifest = "git"` during the build. Files you had filtered out still shipped in the image.

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~" = { source = "dotfiles", mode = "symlink-each", exclude = ["*.log", "cache"], manifest = "git" }
```

With this config, `mise dot apply` skips `dotfiles/debug.log`, everything under `dotfiles/cache/`, and any file git doesn't track. `mise oci build` used to include all of them in the layer. It now leaves them out.

Entries with `dot_prefix = true` already went through apply's filtered walk (#13585, now merged). This PR sends every directory-walking entry through that same code path. The layer still gets a directory entry for each parent of an included file. Empty or excluded directories are no longer added, which also matches apply. `mode = "symlink"` with a directory source is unchanged: apply links the whole directory, so the image still gets its full contents.

## Validation

- A new unit test, `directory_entries_use_the_filtered_walk`, builds the layer with `build_dotfiles_layer` and covers `exclude` and a real git manifest for both `symlink-each` and a directory `copy`. It fails against the old raw walk.
- The existing `oci::builder` and `system::files` unit tests pass.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes OCI dotfiles layer contents for directory entries—images may shrink or differ from prior builds—but aligns behavior with apply rather than touching auth or runtime security.
> 
> **Overview**
> **OCI dotfiles layers now honor the same filters as `mise dot apply`** for directory-walking entries (`symlink-each`, directory `copy`, and `dot_prefix`).
> 
> Previously, `mise oci build` walked directory sources with a raw tree walk, so `exclude` and `manifest = "git"` were ignored and filtered files still landed in the image. Those modes now go through **`add_source_files`**, which uses **`directory_source_files`** (renamed from `dot_prefix_files`) and the shared **`walk_source_files`** path apply uses. Inline **`symlink-each`** walk logic in the builder was removed in favor of that helper.

> Directory **`copy`** without explicit **`permissions`** on a directory source is routed through the filtered walk as well; single-file copies and **`symlink`** on a directory are unchanged. Parent directory entries in the layer follow included files only (empty/excluded dirs are not added), matching apply.

title: fix(http): warn when a download is crawling
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/184
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

If a download host throttles a transfer to a trickle, mise used to wait with no explanation. `http_timeout` resets whenever any data arrives, so a 3 kB/s stream never trips it. Only `http_download_timeout` (30 minutes by default) eventually stops it. In #13581 a throttled nodejs.org download kept a node install, and every shim queued behind its install lock, waiting for hours with no hint of the cause.

mise now prints a warning once per download when throughput stays below **16 KiB/s for a full minute**:

```
mise WARN  download from 127.0.0.1 is very slow (8.0 KiB/s over the last minute). mise keeps trying until `http_download_timeout` runs out; if the host is throttling this connection, switching to a mirror may help
```

The download itself is not aborted or retried. An automatic minimum-speed abort would turn legitimately slow links (satellite, throttled corporate proxies, very large archives) from slow into failed installs, and retrying against the same throttled host rarely helps. `http_download_timeout` is still the hard limit. There is no new setting. The threshold is fixed at the rate below which a typical tool archive can't finish within the default 30-minute budget.

The warning names only the host, because download URLs can carry credentials in their query string or path. Its advice is generic because this downloader also fetches remote task files and the registry archive, not just tools. Throughput is measured on a byte total that includes earlier retry attempts, so a retry can't hide bytes and cause a false warning.

### Validation
- Unit tests: the detector flags a ~3 kB/s window only once the full window has elapsed, ignores healthy windows, and counts bytes across retries.
- Manual: `mise install node@22.9.0` on macOS against a local mirror serving the tarball at ~8 KiB/s printed the warning after one minute (the pre-review wording, which named the full URL; the text above is the current format).

Refs #13581. Companion to #13588, which makes shims waiting on the install lock name the pid holding it.

title: fix(install): name the process holding a tool's install lock
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/183
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

When a tool install is in progress, every other mise process that needs the same tool version waits on its install lock. Usually the holder is a **shim** auto-installing the tool. A shim's command line looks like the tool itself (`node fixture-server.js`), not like mise, so when that install stalls (a slow download, for example) you can't tell what everyone is waiting on. In #13581 this looked like the lock was leaking into exec'd `node` processes, and it led to killing the wrong processes.

Waiters now name the process holding the lock:

```
  node@22.9.0  waiting for install lock held by pid 61907  3.0s
```

`mise oci` shows the same pid when it waits for a tool install.

How it works: once mise holds a tool-version install lock, it writes its pid into the lock file, and the file is truncated on unlock. Writing the pid is best effort: if it fails (for example, the disk is full), the lock is still held and used normally. A process that finds the lock taken reads that pid for its wait message. This is best effort: if the pid can't be read (for example, the holder releases the lock at that moment, or Windows refuses to read a locked file), the message stays `waiting for install lock`. Other lock files are unchanged.

### Validation
- New unit tests: a contended waiter receives the holder's pid, and unlocking clears it.
- Manual: two `node` shims on macOS against a local mirror that trickles the tarball at ~8 kB/s. The second shim printed the first shim's pid, and the lock file contained that pid.

Refs #13581

> When a tool install waits on another process’s **tool-version install lock**, progress and log messages now include the **holder’s PID** when it can be read (e.g. `waiting for install lock held by pid 61907`), instead of a generic “waiting for install lock”. The same wording is used for normal installs and **`mise oci`** waits.

title: feat(registry): let registry entries require GitHub attestations
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/182
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Stacked on #13584.

Without GitHub API calls, mise can't tell whether an artifact "has no attestations" or whether mise-versions (or a stale cache, or a lockfile written after one) just said so. Either way, a "none" answer skips attestation verification. This lets the **mise registry**, which ships inside the mise binary, declare which tools publish attestations, so that answer can't downgrade them.

```toml
# registry/aube.toml
version_order = "semver"
backends = [
  { full = "github:aubepkg/aube", attestations_since = "2.2.5" },
]
```

For `aube@2.2.5` and later installed through `github:aubepkg/aube`, whether by that name or through the `aube` shorthand:
- `mise lock` records `provenance = "github-attestations"` without probing anything, and fails if verification ends on anything else. SLSA doesn't substitute.
- Installing requires a verified GitHub attestation for every downloaded asset, including `additional_asset_patterns` assets. The registry's requirement overrides whatever the lockfile recorded (nothing, or SLSA), so such a lockfile entry can't skip verification.
- If no attestation is found, the install fails with the existing downgrade error, now worded "Lockfile or mise registry requires github-attestations provenance…", instead of silently continuing.

It costs no GitHub API calls: the requirement is baked into the registry, and verification uses the attestations mise-versions returns, which #13584 already binds to the repository.

## Scope

- **Any `version_order`.** `attestations_since` must be a complete semantic version, but mise only compares the one version being installed against it and never orders a version list. So unlike `min_version` it works for tools with `version_order = "source"`. Versions that aren't semantic versions (refs, channels, date builds) are never required. The contributor docs add the matching rule: every release whose version is semver at or past the boundary must be attested.
- **Declared backends.** The requirement is looked up from the registry entry's declared backends, so a `MISE_BACKENDS_<TOOL>` override can't drop it.
- **`github:` backends only.** aqua already declares attestations per package in the aqua registry. Making a declared-but-missing attestation a hard error for aqua is a separate follow-up.
- **Respects opt-outs.** Users who turn off `github_attestations` (globally, for the github backend, or per tool) get no requirement.
- **Seeded for 42 `github:` backends**: aube plus 41 more. Each boundary is the first release where every binary asset has a GitHub attestation (build provenance, or GitHub's release attestation for an immutable release), and no semver release at or past it lacks one. Skipped: tools whose latest release isn't fully attested, whose tags aren't semver, or with out-of-order unattested releases (cargo-dist, coursier); `terrastruct/d2`, which moved to `d2lang/d2`, sinc

title: feat(dotfiles): add dot_prefix to deploy dot-<name> sources as .<name>
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/181
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Dotfiles repositories are awkward to browse when every file is hidden. GNU Stow solves this with `--dotfiles`, where a source named `dot-bashrc` deploys as `.bashrc`. This adds the same convention to `[dotfiles]` as a per-entry option (requested in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13579).

```toml
[dotfiles]
"~" = { source = "home", mode = "symlink-each", dot_prefix = true, exclude = ["README.md"] }
```

| Source                            | Target                      |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `home/dot-bashrc`                 | `~/.bashrc`                 |
| `home/dot-config/foo/config.toml` | `~/.config/foo/config.toml` |
| `home/bin/dot-helper`             | `~/bin/.helper`             |
| `home/.editorconfig`              | `~/.editorconfig`           |

Every path component is mapped, not just the top level, and names without the prefix deploy unchanged. Today's closest workaround, a wildcard entry like `"~/.*" = "dot-*"`, only handles top-level names and, in `symlink` mode, replaces the whole of `~/.config` with a link.

## Behavior

- `dot_prefix` defaults to `false` and is valid only with `mode = "symlink-each"` or `mode = "copy"`. On other entries it is warned about and skipped during apply, and rejected by incoming-config preflight and the JSON schema.
- `exclude` and `manifest = "git"` still match source names (`dot-bashrc`, not `.bashrc`).
- If two source paths deploy to the same target (`dot-bashrc` and `.bashrc`), or a `dot-config/` directory would land where a `.config` file goes, apply fails and names both paths.
- Removing a source file removes its dotted link on the next apply, and `unapply` removes the entry's links, as with any `symlink-each` entry.
- `mise dot add` refuses to capture into an existing `dot_prefix` entry: it copies the target tree into the source verbatim, which would store `.bashrc` where the entry reads `dot-bashrc`. Edit the source directly instead.
- `mise oci` builds apply the same mapping.
- No global setting yet. A global default would also change where implied sources (`~/.zshrc` → `~/.dotfiles/.zshrc`) are looked up, which deserves its own design discussion.

## Implementation notes

The mapping lives in `walk_source_files`, which produces every source→target pair for `symlink-each` and directory `copy` and feeds status, apply, footprint validation, and unapply. The legacy target-walking paths (for installs without recorded `symlink-each` state) now identify an entry's links from each link's destination, since with `dot_prefix` a target name no longer determines its source name.

## Validation

- New unit tests cover the mapping rules (including `dot-` and `dot-.` left unchanged), the collision checks, and mode validation.
- New e2e tests: `e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_dot_prefix` (apply, stale-link removal, collision, invalid mode) and `e2e/config/te

title: feat(github): use mise-versions for any public github.com repo
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/180
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

mise-versions mirrors GitHub release metadata through a shared token pool, so installs don't spend your GitHub API rate limit. Until now mise only used it for tools in the mise registry. With this change, **any public github.com repo** goes through it, for the `github:`, `aqua:` and `packslip:` backends:

```toml
[tools]
"github:BurntSushi/xsv" = "latest"   # listing, release lookup and attestations now come from mise-versions
```

- `mise ls-remote`, `latest` resolution and installs of non-registry GitHub tools no longer need API quota in the common case.
- Private repos are unaffected. mise-versions answers 404 for them, and mise quietly uses your own token against api.github.com, as before.

**Requires jdx/mise-versions#328 to be deployed first.** It adds the list endpoint and opens the mirror to public repos. Against today's server, mise falls back to api.github.com and warns.

## What mise does and doesn't trust from the mirror

The mirror is treated as untrusted. mise enforces:

- **Downloads can't be redirected.**
  - Each asset's browser URL must be a github.com download of *that release's tag* and *that asset's name*.
  - Each API URL must be a numeric release asset.
  - The repository in both is pinned to the one you configured, so the mirror can't point a download at another repo or another file.
- **Renamed and transferred repos keep working.** GitHub reports the new name, and mise rewrites those URLs back to the name you configured, which GitHub itself redirects.
- **Attestations must come from the repo.** Anyone can attest any digest from their own repo. GitHub's attestations API scopes results to the repo, but a mirror could return anyone's. Mirrored attestations now have to name the requested repo:
  - Actions-signed provenance: the Fulcio Source Repository certificate extension.
  - GitHub's own release attestations, which every immutable release gets, including releases with no build provenance: the signed statement, trusted only when GitHub's release attester signed it.
  - A differently named repo is accepted only when the GitHub API says both names are the same repository (a rename or transfer). Anything else logs a warning and mise verifies against GitHub directly.
- **"No attestations" is taken from the mirror, except in paranoid mode.** Normal mode trusts the mirror's "none", as it already does for registry tools, so unattested tools cost no GitHub calls. With `paranoid` enabled, mise confirms that answer with GitHub before skipping verification. Otherwise a stale or dishonest "none" could be written to the lockfile as a checksum without provenance. This is documented in `docs/paranoid.md`.
- **`url_replacements` is authoritative for GitHub metadata.** If it reroutes `api.github.com`, or a repository's release and attestation API paths (a proxy, a mirror, a fixture), mise doesn't ask mise-versions for that metadata, an

title: feat(dotfiles): add opt-in relative symlinks
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/179
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Dotfile `symlink` and `symlink-each` entries always pointed at their source by an absolute path. That breaks when a home directory is mounted at different paths on different machines (for example over NFS), or when the home or dotfiles tree is moved. Links can now be created with relative targets, the way GNU Stow does it.

```toml
[settings]
dotfiles.relative_symlinks = true   # or MISE_DOTFILES_RELATIVE_SYMLINKS=1

[dotfiles]
"~/.config/foo" = { source = "~/dotfiles/foo", mode = "symlink" }            # ~/.config/foo -> ../dotfiles/foo
"~/.bashrc"     = { source = "~/dotfiles/bashrc", relative = false }         # per-entry override: stays absolute
"~/.local/bin"  = { source = "~/dotfiles/bin", mode = "symlink-each" }      # ~/.local/bin/tool -> ../../dotfiles/bin/tool
```

- **New setting:** `dotfiles.relative_symlinks`, default `false`, so nothing changes unless you opt in. An entry's new `relative` key overrides it in either direction.
- **Symlink modes only:** `relative = true` on `copy`, `template`, inline content, `absent`, `track`, or a permissions-only entry is rejected, both by preflight and by the JSON schema.
- **Switching it on converts existing links:** `mise dot status` reports an absolute link to the right source as `symlink points to … by an absolute path; relative requested`, and the next apply re-points it without `--force`.
- **Switching it off doesn't convert them back:** with relative links off, relative links that already reach the source (including ones made by hand or by Stow) still count as applied, as they did before this PR.
- **Dry-run output** shows `ln -sfr` for relative entries.
- **Windows:** the option is ignored. Directory links there are junctions, which can't be relative.

The kernel resolves `..` in a link from the directory the link physically sits in. So if a directory on the link's path is itself a symlink (say `~/.config -> /data/config`), a path worked out from the configured spelling would point at the wrong place. mise only uses that path if it actually resolves to the source. Otherwise it computes the path between the canonical locations, and if even that fails it falls back to an absolute link. Unapply and `symlink-each` pruning also recognise relative links whose source file has been deleted.

## Tests
- Unit tests cover:
  - the link text
  - a link that still works after its tree is moved
  - an absolute link counting as drift when relative is requested
  - a link directory reached through a symlink
  - preflight rejecting `relative` on non-symlink modes
- New e2e `cli/test_dotfiles_relative_symlinks` covers apply, converting existing absolute links, the per-entry override, pruning a deleted `symlink-each` source file, and unapply.
- New e2e `config/test_schema_dotfiles_relative` validates the schema with tombi.
- The existing `test_dotfiles_files`, `test_dotfiles_absent` and `test_schema_dotf

title: chore(ci): build Windows arm64 release on a native runner
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/178
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

The Windows arm64 release build timed out in the 2026.9.x release dry run ([job](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/35996250422/job/107621806048)). It compiled dependencies normally, then spent over 2h18m on the fat-LTO build of `mise` itself before the 150-minute limit cancelled it.

In the two previous releases the same job took about 60 minutes. This is the first release since #13503 switched the Windows serious profile to `panic=unwind`. Fat LTO with unwind tables is much heavier, and arm64 was being cross-compiled on the x64 `windows-latest` runner. The x64 build also slowed down, from 37–58 min to 70 min.

This PR builds arm64 on a native `windows-11-arm` runner. It keeps fat LTO, so the arm64 release binary loses no optimization, which it would have with thin LTO.

- The arm64 job now uses `windows-11-arm`. x64 stays on `windows-latest`.
- The vfox Lua-error smoke test from #13503 now runs on arm64 too. Before, the x64 runner could not execute the arm64 binary.

**Validation:** actionlint passes, apart from existing SC2129 style notes. This job only runs on an armed release PR or a tag, so the first real run will be the next release dry run.

title: fix(cli): stop debug builds from overflowing the main stack on Windows
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/177
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Debug builds of mise ran most commands within a few hundred KB of the main thread's stack limit. On Windows, where `.cargo/config.toml` links the main thread with `/STACK:8000000` (7,812 KiB), `mise bootstrap dotfiles apply` and `mise dotfiles conflicts … --force` crashed intermittently in `windows-e2e` with exit code `-1073741571` (`0xC00000FD`, `STATUS_STACK_OVERFLOW`). For example, `e2e-win/dotfiles.Tests.ps1` ("applies a symlink entry…") and `e2e-win/dotfiles_conflicts.Tests.ps1` ("applies over it with --force") failed this way, and the follow-on failures in those files and `services.Tests.ps1` came from the crashed state. A given binary crashed every time, but whether a build crashed depended on unrelated layout changes. That explains why the failure came and went across the OpenTelemetry stack (#13559, #13560) ([example job](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/35954408504/job/107492437715)).

Release builds were not affected. The fix gives the debug build used by CI roughly 5 MB of headroom on this path.

## Cause

The overflow was on the **main thread**, not on a tokio worker or `spawn_blocking` thread. The top-level `Commands::run`, `bootstrap::Commands::run` and `Dotfiles::dispatch` were `async fn`s with a `match` that `.await`ed one subcommand future per arm. At opt-level 0, LLVM doesn't reuse stack slots, so every arm's future temporary gets its own slot in the poll frame. That frame then stays on the stack for the whole command. Measured from the prologues of the Linux debug binary (`objdump`, largest `sub $N,%rsp`/probe per function):

| poll frame | bytes |
|---|---|
| `cli::Commands::run` | 1,847,296 |
| `bootstrap::Commands::run` | 1,183,744 |
| `Dotfiles::dispatch` | 622,592 |

Together with `main_`, `block_on`, `Cli::run` and `run_inner`, that added up to ~6.6 MB before any dotfiles code ran. `-Zprint-type-sizes` doesn't show this because it reports the size of the future's *state*, not the poll function's stack frame.

## Fix

These three dispatchers are now plain `fn`s that return a `LocalBoxFuture`. The per-arm temporaries live in a short frame that is popped before the command is polled, and the subcommand's future goes on the heap. Nothing else changes. `LocalBoxFuture` rather than `BoxFuture`, because several subcommand futures are not `Send`. They never needed to be, since the command runs under `block_on`.

## How it was confirmed

I did not reproduce this on Windows. I confirmed it on Linux with the same debug profile:

1. **Which thread:** a temporary build option set tokio's worker and blocking-pool stack size. `bootstrap dotfiles apply` still succeeded with 128 KiB worker stacks, so those threads have plenty of headroom. With `ulimit -s` below the default 8 MiB, the process aborted with `thread 'main' has overflowed its stack`.
2. **How much:** I bisected the smallest `ulimit -s` at which each command succee

title: fix(cli): exit quietly when help output hits a closed pipe
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/176
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Help output no longer crashes mise when the reader closes the pipe early. Before this fix, a closed stdout made mise panic. Release builds abort on panic, so the process died with SIGABRT, systemd-coredump saved a core dump and desktop crash notifiers fired, all for a closed pipe. Fixes #13571.

**Before** (2026.9.12):

```
$ mise help settings | (exec 0<&-; sleep 0.3); echo "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
The application panicked (crashed).
Message:  failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)
134
```

**After:** the same command exits 0 and prints nothing to stderr. Output to a reader that stays open is unchanged.

These commands exited 134 on 2026.9.12 and now exit 0:
- `mise --help`, `mise -h`, `mise help`, `mise help <cmd>`, `mise <cmd> --help`
- `mise run --help`, `mise watch --help`
- `mise usage`
- `mise version --json`

### Change

These paths printed with `print!`/`println!`, which panic on `EPIPE`. They now use `miseprint!`/`miseprintln!`, which return the error instead. `handle_err` already turns a `BrokenPipe` error into a quiet exit 0; #13527 used the same approach for completion.

The other raw stdout prints in command code are converted the same way: `which`, `set` completion, `config ls --tracked-configs`, `doctor` and `doctor path`, `settings ls --complete`, `registry --complete`, `search --complete`, `shell`, `ssh`, `plugins install` and the postgres daemon provider. Three of them needed more than a macro swap:
- `plugins install`: the "installing X" progress line ignores a failed write, so a closed stdout can't skip the install.
- `doctor --json`: diagnosed problems still exit 1 when the reader has gone away.
- Current-shell hooks: the hook runners can't return an error, so a failed write is recorded (with a warning unless it is `EPIPE`). `hook-env` returns it after running hooks instead of exiting 0 with truncated shell code. The `MissingArgsHelp` page and usage-error messages go to stderr and now ignore a failed write, like `safe_eprintln!`. #13527 explains why restoring the default `SIGPIPE` disposition isn't an option.

### Testing

New `e2e/cli/test_help_broken_pipe` closes the reader before mise writes. It checks for exit 0 and no panic across `--help`, `help`, `help settings`, `settings --help`, `run --help`, `watch --help` and `usage`, and checks that an open reader still gets the page. The test fails without this change (`mise --help exited 101`, the debug build's unwinding panic) and passes with it. `test_completion_broken_pipe` still passes, as do clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo +1.95 check` and the `cli::`/`hooks` unit tests.

title: feat(http): install from a local archive with a file:// url
body:
<!-- entire-trail-link-start -->
https://entire.io/gh/jdx/mise/trails/175
<!-- entire-trail-link-end -->

Closes #13568.

On a restricted network you can often download a release archive by hand (browser, internal mirror, another machine) but not let mise fetch it. There was no way to hand that file to mise: a `file://` URL failed with `URL scheme is not allowed`.

The `http:` backend now accepts a `file://` URL. mise copies the archive into its download directory instead of fetching it, then extracts, checks the checksum, and links it exactly as it would a download. No network access is needed, so it also works with `offline = true`.

```toml
[tools]
"http:my-tool" = { version = "1.0.0", url = "file:///opt/archives/my-tool-v1.0.0-linux-x64.tar.gz", checksum = "sha256:..." }
```

```
$ MISE_OFFLINE=1 mise install http:my-tool
mise ✓ http:my-tool@1.0.0
$ mise x -- my-tool
hello-from-archive
```

- To keep a machine-specific path out of a shared `mise.toml`, put the entry in `mise.local.toml`.
- `checksum` works for local files, and a mismatch still fails the install.
- A missing file fails with `local artifact not found: <path>` instead of a URL error.
- The URL goes into `mise.lock` as written, so a lockfile with a local path only works on machines that have the file there. The docs say this.

Only the `http:` backend is changed; registry tools (aqua, github) still download. The `--archive` flag, filename-based tool detection, and the offline archive directory from the issue are left out. `file://` could later be accepted in the shared HTTP client, which would let `url_replacements` point any backend at a local mirror directory, but that is a larger change and not part of this PR.

## Validation

- New e2e `backend/test_http_local_file`: offline install, the tool runs, `mise ls` lists it, a checksum mismatch fails, and a missing file gives a clear error.
- Unit test for which URLs are treated as local files.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo +1.95 check`, and `mise run lint-fix` all pass.
