title: docs: show the GitHub star count in the nav overflow menu
body:
## Problem

Between 768px and 1279px wide, VitePress collapses the nav bar's social links
into the "…" overflow menu. On mise.jdx.dev the GitHub star count disappeared
entirely at those widths — the menu showed a bare GitHub icon.

## Cause

VitePress renders the GitHub link twice: inline in the nav bar, and again inside
the overflow menu. The badge injector used `querySelector`, so it always matched
the inline link — which is `display: none` below 1280px — and appended the badge
there. The menu's copy never got one.

## Fix

Inject into every match, and disconnect the `MutationObserver` once each link has
its badge instead of re-running on every DOM mutation the page makes for the rest
of its life. This matches what hk, pitchfork, usage and mr-boxington already do.

No CSS change was needed: the badge sits 8px clear of the menu's clip box, so it
does not hit the clipping that [jdx/pitchfork#862](https://github.com/jdx/pitchfork/pull/862),
[jdx/usage#1429](https://github.com/jdx/usage/pull/1429) and
[jdx/pacvamp#91](https://github.com/jdx/pacvamp/pull/91) fix.

## Validation

Built the docs (`mise run docs:build`), served the output, and drove headless
Chromium against it:

- at 1000px the "…" menu now shows `★ 33.9k`, 8px clear of the menu's clip box
- at 1400px the inline badge's bounding box is identical to production today
  (x 1299.0, y 41, 45.9×12) and the nav bar is still 64px tall
- the hamburger nav screen below 768px is unaffected — it had no badge before
  this change either, on mise or any of the sibling sites

*AI-assisted — Tool: Claude Code; model: anthropic/claude-opus-5; version: 2.1.270.*

>

title: test(bootstrap): pin what an apply ends and runs for a scheduled task
body:
Follow-up to #13190, which fixed a bug in exactly this decision: a
`history-watch` scheduled task whose process was not watching the history
store was queued for an apply that ended and ran nothing, because Task
Scheduler keeps a running instance across an unchanged registration. The
apply reported success and automatic saves stayed off.

That decision was two inline boolean expressions with no test. It now has a
name and a table covering every combination of running / changed / wanted
running / forced restart:

```rust
fn transition(running: bool, changed: bool, start: bool, restart: bool) -> (bool, bool) {
    let replace = changed || restart;
    (running && (!start || replace), start && (!running || replace))
}
```

The row that regressed — running, unchanged, wanted running, no forced
restart — is written down as `(false, false)` next to the forced restart
that replaces it, so the reason an apply leaves a healthy task alone is
visible beside the reason it may not.

No behavior change: the extracted expression is the one that shipped in
#13190.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin mise scheduled_tasks`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `mise run lint`

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: registry: add nubr
body:
Adds `nubr`, the TypeScript runner from the Nub project, published on npm as [`@nubjs/runner`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@nubjs/runner). It runs a file, a `package.json` script, or an installed bin on plain Node, without the `nub` binary; `nub` itself is already in the registry (#10544).

**Popularity:** [nubjs/nub](https://github.com/nubjs/nub) has 4,296 stars and 60 forks. The runner ships from that repository and shares its release cadence.

**Backend:** `npm:` is the only backend that exists for this tool. `@nubjs/runner` is a Node package, a `--import` preload plus a `nubr` script that re-execs the user's Node, with a native addon in per-platform optional dependencies. There is no standalone binary, no GitHub release asset, no aqua entry, and no packslip to point a higher tier at; a Node on PATH is what the tool runs on, not an incidental dependency. This is the same situation as the existing `nub` entry, which was accepted with the npm backend.

Version listing and install verified with the npm backend (mise 2026.9.7). The first real release, 0.9.2, is under 24 hours old at the time of writing, so the default `minimum_release_age` still hides it from a plain `ls-remote`; `0.0.0` is the name reservation that preceded it.

```sh
MISE_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE=0 mise ls-remote npm:@nubjs/runner
# 0.0.0 0.9.2 
mise exec npm:@nubjs/runner@0.9.2 -- nubr --version
# 0.9.2
```

title: fix(dotfiles): restart a history watcher that is not watching this store
body:
`mise doctor` could report the dotfiles history watcher as stopped while the
service manager was running it, and the command it recommended did nothing:

```
mise doctor
  dotfiles: the history watcher is declared but not running.
     Edits are not saved automatically until it runs; explicit saves still work.
     Run: mise bootstrap services apply

mise bootstrap services apply
  user services: 1 service(s) already applied
```

## What was happening

mise 2026.9.5 (#13038) moved the history locks out of the cache directory
into `$MISE_STATE_DIR/history/`. A watcher that launchd or systemd started
before that upgrade keeps running the old binary, and keeps holding the old
cache-based lock, so nothing holds the new one — mise sees no watcher for
the store. Its unit or plist is byte-identical to what the declaration
renders, so `mise bootstrap services apply` counted it as converged and
skipped it. Nothing restarted the stale process, and no edit was saved
automatically until the next login.

A watcher started with a different `MISE_STATE_DIR` than the shell uses
presents exactly the same way.

## What changes

`mise bootstrap services apply` now restarts a `history-watch` service whose
definition matches but whose process is not the watcher for this store:

```
mise bootstrap services apply
  user service mise-history: its process is not watching the history store; restarting it
  user services: applied mise-history
```

It applies only to the built-in watcher, only when the declaration asks for
it to be running, and only while `history.enabled` is true — a watcher that
is meant to be stopped is left alone. On Windows the restart is forced
explicitly, because Task Scheduler keeps a running instance across an
unchanged registration.

`mise doctor` and `mise dot status` also tell the two states apart now,
instead of describing a running process as stopped. Both report the state
using the apply's own predicate, so they never advise an apply that would
not act:

```
mise doctor
  dotfiles: the history service is running but is not watching this store.
     Its process predates this mise version, or uses a different MISE_STATE_DIR;
     edits are not saved automatically until it is restarted.
     Run: mise bootstrap services apply

mise dot status
  automatic capture: running but not watching this store (…restart it with `mise bootstrap services apply`).
```

`mise dot status --json` reports the new state as `service-not-watching` in
`.history.watcher`; `mise doctor --json` reports it as `running but not
watching this store` in `.dotfiles.watcher`. The existing `running`,
`declared-not-running` and `not-declared` values are unchanged.

No new configuration or flags. Users already in this state are recovered by
the apply they were being told to run.

## Validation

- `cargo test --bin mise user_services scheduled_tasks doctor dotfiles` — new
  unit tests cover which services an apply restarts, which it leaves
  converged, and that the forced restart r

title: fix(packslip): install from private GitHub repositories
body:
Installing a tool from a private GitHub repository with `packslip:` failed, while the same release installed fine with `github:`:

```console
$ mise x 'packslip:github.com/my-org/internal-cli@0.1.0' -- mytool
GET https://github.com/my-org/internal-cli/releases/download/v0.1.0/packslip.sigstore.json 404 Not Found
```

GitHub serves a private repository's release assets only from its API — `github.com/.../releases/download/...` is refused there even for a caller holding a valid token. A packslip records those browser-facing URLs for the manifest, the artifact, and every resource asset it signs, and the backend fetched each one directly, so the install died at the manifest. Publishing a signed release list that named the manifest by its API endpoint got past that step and then failed the same way on the artifact.

Now these installs work with the same credentials the `github:` backend already uses (`MISE_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`, or `GITHUB_TOKEN`), with nothing new in your configuration:

```toml
[tools]
"packslip:github.com/my-org/internal-cli" = "latest"
```

Authentication is transport-only. The signature, project identity, signer continuity, artifact digest, and size checks are unchanged, and no credential is read from a signed document — the token only decides which URL the bytes come from, and the bytes are verified afterwards either way.

## How the endpoint is resolved

Only the release metadata knows an asset's API endpoint, so it comes from there in one of two ways:

- **Manifest found through a release asset.** The release listing is already fetched to locate the manifest and carries both URLs, so the existing `pick_reachable_asset_url` picks between them — the same probe `github:`, `aqua:`, and `cargo-binstall` installs use.
- **URL carried by a signed manifest, release list, or stamp.** Those name the browser URL only. mise retries at the API endpoint after the browser URL fails, so a public install still makes the one request it makes today, and a private one pays a single extra release read instead of being unusable.

GitHub refuses a private release asset in two ways — a 404, or its sign-in page with a 200 — and both now reach the fallback. A packslip names sigstore documents and binary artifacts and never an HTML document, so a page arriving from a release URL is unambiguously the refusal; when no authenticated endpoint can be resolved, mise says the token cannot read the repository instead of failing later on a digest mismatch.

The lookup deliberately skips the mise-versions cache. A repository that reaches the fallback has just refused its browser URL, so it is most likely private: the public cache cannot hold that release, and asking would only tell a public host the owner, repository, and tag.

## Also fixed along the way

- **Tags that span path segments.** GitHub leaves a tag's `/` literal in a download URL (`.../download/@biomejs/biome@2.5.2/biome-linux-x64`), including the `tool/v1.0.0` tags a packslip monorepo pr

title: fix(npm): keep global tools satisfied when lockfiles are enabled
body:
`lockfile = true` is an invocation-wide setting, but automatic lockfile maintenance deliberately excludes tools owned by global configs. Global lockfiles and their dependency data are only created explicitly with `mise lock --global`.

The new embedded-aube graph path did not preserve that distinction. When lockfiles were enabled, it generated a graph-specific installation identity for an unlocked npm request from the global config. No automatic flow could persist that graph to the owning global lockfile, so the next `mise exec` resolved the same request without a graph, treated the physically present tool as unsatisfied, performed a redundant install pass, and warned that it was missing.

Automatic graph creation now follows the existing lockfile-target policy: unlocked non-global requests can receive graphs for automatic project-lockfile maintenance, while global requests remain version-only unless they are actually resolved from an explicitly generated revision 2 global lockfile. This does not introduce project-local semantics for `[settings]`.

For example, with a global pin:

```toml
[tools]
"npm:xcodebuildmcp" = "2.7.0"
```

and `lockfile = true` enabled anywhere in the merged settings, `mise exec` now reuses the installed global tool without a redundant install pass or `missing` warning. Users who want that global tool graph-locked can opt in with `mise lock --global`.

The regression test isolates a version-only global install, verifies both `mise install --dry-run` and `mise exec` across the automatic-lockfile boundary, then confirms `mise lock --global` persists and replays the explicit global dependency graph.

Reported in https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13184.

Validation:

- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise exec -- cargo check --locked`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/backend/test_npm_aube`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

title: feat(dotfiles): add safe history replacement during adoption
body:
Fresh setup adoption could capture files declared by an existing `config.toml` before comparing them with the incoming setup. That created a new local root even when the history store had just been removed, so adoption then rejected two otherwise identical trees as unrelated.

Fresh `--adopt` now compares existing live files during the incoming application preflight without first creating local ancestry. Identical files adopt the origin's history; differences still pause the setup for an explicit decision.

For machines that genuinely retain unrelated local history and intentionally need to discard it, this also adds a one-shot replacement:

```sh
mise bootstrap --adopt <url> --replace-history --yes
```

`--dry-run` previews the local and origin commits without mutation. The replacement holds the history-operation and synchronization locks, validates the complete incoming setup, and restores the previous local branch and synchronization state if application cannot complete. Ordinary synchronization never replaces divergent history, and there is no persistent force setting.

The lockfile also updates `rustls` to 0.23.45 because the repository advisory check began rejecting 0.23.43 for RUSTSEC-2026-0285 while this PR was under review.

## Validation

- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_bootstrap_from_git`
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run render`
- `mise exec -- cargo check --locked`
- `mise x cargo-deny -- cargo-deny check advisories`

Addresses https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13171

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes bootstrap adoption and local dotfile history/git refs with locking and rollback, but only when `--replace-history` is used or during the revised fresh-adopt path.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds **`--replace-history`** to `mise bootstrap --adopt` so you can discard unrelated local dotfile history in one shot and adopt the setup repository’s branch, with dry-run messaging and rollback of branch, sync state, and status on failure.
> 
> **Fresh `--adopt`** no longer always captures local files into history before applying the remote setup. When there is no local history ref, sync skips that capture and relies on apply’s preflight so matching live files can join the origin without inventing an unrelated root; machines with only matching files and no store still adopt cleanly.
> 
> The replacement path takes history-operation and sync locks, detaches the old history head via `delete_history_head`, runs locked sync/apply without a pre-replacement checkpoint, and aborts if paths are still held. Supporting changes include `apply_locked` / `sync_locked`, `begin_replacement_apply` (`fresh_adoption`), and CLI/docs/man updates plus expanded e2e coverage.

title: feat(pypi): add semantic uv install options
body:
PyPI tools can now express common uv installation behavior as lock-aware options instead of opaque `uvx_args`:

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:azure-cli" = { version = "latest", with = ["pip"], dependency_prereleases = "allow" }
"pypi:ansible" = { version = "latest", expose = ["ansible-core"] }
```

`with` installs additional requirements, `expose` installs additional requirements and links their executable entry points, and `dependency_prereleases` controls uv's prerelease policy. These options select uv as the required installer dependency, retain Python as a dependency for graph installs, and participate in dependency graph locking and installation identity. `expose` requires uv 0.8.5 or newer.

Existing `uvx_args` and `pipx_args` remain available as escape hatches and continue to use version-only resolution. A registry semantic default can be cleared with an empty list when opting back into pipx, for example `"pypi:ansible" = { version = "latest", uvx = false, expose = [], pipx_args = "--include-deps" }`.

This migrates the Azure CLI and Ansible registry defaults to the semantic options, so those tools can benefit from uv-backed dependency graphs. Locked installs use the PyPI distribution name for executable discovery and link both package entry points and wheel-provided scripts, including when users select a tool through a registry shorthand such as `azure`.

The lockfile also updates rustls from 0.23.43 to 0.23.45 after RUSTSEC-2026-0285 began failing the repository-wide advisory check while this PR was under review.

Validation:
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run test:unit` (4,058 unit tests plus the aube bootstrap integration test)
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/backend/test_pypi_lock e2e/backend/test_pipx_uvx`
- `mise test-tool ansible azure`
- `cargo-deny check advisories`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

> **Overview**
> PyPI/pipx tools gain **lock-aware** install options **`with`**, **`expose`**, and **`dependency_prereleases`**, replacing many ad-hoc `uvx_args` uses while still allowing raw `uvx_args` / `pipx_args` for version-only installs.

Locked environments discover executables from the root distribution plus exposed packages, including **wheel data scripts** without `console_scripts`.
>

title: feat(dotfiles): add encryption flag to track
body:
`mise dot track` can now enable encrypted history while enrolling a file or directory:

```sh
mise dot track ~/.config/app/credentials --encrypt
```

The command writes `encrypt = true` into the tracked dotfile declaration and encrypts the initial baseline checkpoint. Users must configure `[history.encryption].recipients` first; enrollment fails closed and rolls back the declaration if the encrypted baseline cannot be saved. Failed baselines are rejected before history metadata is committed.

Run encrypted enrollment as a standalone command rather than from inside `mise dot capture`. This lets mise verify the encrypted baseline before retaining the declaration.

This is intended for files that should be encrypted from their first checkpoint. Enabling encryption after plaintext history already exists does not rewrite that history, and the existing plaintext-history publication safeguards still apply.

Validation:

- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_encrypted_capture`
- `mise exec -- cargo test --all-features failed_baseline_does_not_commit_metadata`
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run render`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes encrypted dotfile enrollment and when history metadata is written; safeguards limit misuse, but mistakes could still affect what gets committed to shared history.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`mise dot track`** now accepts **`--encrypt`**, which sets `encrypt = true` on the `[dotfiles]` entry and encrypts the **first** history baseline (after `[history.encryption].recipients` is configured). Docs, usage KDL, and man pages document the flag and credential-tracking examples.
> 
> Enrollment is **fail-closed**: `--encrypt` is rejected when history is disabled or when run **inside** an active `mise dot capture` (users must run track separately so the encrypted baseline can be verified). History checkpoint logic now treats baseline enrollment as **transactional**—if the baseline snapshot cannot be created (e.g. bad recipients), mise returns unavailable and **does not** commit baseline metadata or history refs.
> 
> E2E coverage switches from manual config to **`track --encrypt`** and asserts the new guardrails; **`rustls`** is bumped in **`Cargo.lock`**.

title: fix(upgrade): persist explicit selectors when bumping versions
body:
## Summary

`mise upgrade --bump` now saves explicit version selectors to the tool's existing configuration instead of leaving the configured version stale after a successful upgrade.

For example, with Flint pinned in `mise.toml`:

```bash
mise upgrade --bump aqua:grafana/flint@latest
```

upgrades Flint and writes `"latest"` to its existing entry. Like `mise use`, explicit version selectors are preserved: `node@22` writes `"22"`, and `node@latest` writes `"latest"`. With `settings.pin = true`, version requests are saved as their resolved concrete version instead.

To retain the existing version precision while bumping it, omit the selector:

```bash
mise upgrade --bump aqua:grafana/flint
```

Once an entry says `"latest"`, later bumps leave that selector unchanged; an enabled lockfile still records the concrete version. Configuration updates also work when the requested version is already installed, and dry runs show the pending configuration change. Failed requests do not overwrite working configuration.

## Validation

Focused upgrade e2e coverage and all 10 upgrade unit tests pass. Formatting, ShellCheck, shfmt, and Cargo checks pass. Local compilation required exposing the installed CMake and supplying temporary libclang/header paths; no project configuration changes were needed.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

Additional change: this PR also includes the unrelated e2e/config/test_required_env_vars_tools_filter pipefail-safe grep helper fix in commit fc676ed8f.
author: zeitlinger

   this will install 22.1.0 and set `node = "22.1.0"` in your config.
 
-  It keeps the same precision as what was there before, so if you instead had `node = "20"`, it
-  would change your config to `node = "22"`.
+  With a bare tool, it keeps the same precision as what was there before, so if you instead had

+  provided (`node@latest`, `node@3`, or `node@prefix:3`), that selector is persisted instead.
+  For version selectors, `settings.pin` persists the resolved concrete version. Requests from non-writable
+  sources are not persisted. For example, `mise upgrade node@latest --bump` writes `latest`.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+# An explicit fuzzy version must not prevent --bump from updating the config.
+cat <<'EOF' >mise.toml

+assert_contains "mise ls dummy" "dummy  2.0.0  ~/workdir/mise.toml  latest"
+assert_contains "cat mise.toml" 'dummy = "latest"'

+# An already-installed explicit selector is still persisted when another tool

+cat <<'EOF' >mise.toml

+assert_contains "cat mise.toml" 'tiny-local = "3.1.0"'

+cat <<'EOF' >mise.toml

+dummy = "1.0.0"

+EOF
+mise install tiny-local@1.0.0

+# backend succeeds, but retain installed selectors and pending explicit installs.
+mise uninstall tiny-local@3.1.0

+assert_not_contains_text "$output" "Would bump dummy@path:/does-not-exist"
+assert_not_contains_text "$output" "Would bump dummy@1.0.0"

+assert_contains "cat mise.toml" 'tiny-local = "3.1.0"'

+
+# An explicit selector must constrain the installed version instead of merely
+# changing the selector that gets persisted.
+cat <<'EOF' >mise.toml

title: fix(backend): ignore disabled backends from lockfile discovery
body:
When a parent `mise.lock` pins a shorthand to a disabled backend, `mise tool` and a fresh child lockfile can still select that backend. Backend discovery now skips disabled lockfile backends, preserves the first enabled recorded backend, and falls back to an enabled registry backend when no usable pin remains.

For example, with a parent lockfile recording `asdf:yarn`, a child project can use:

```toml
[tools]
yarn = "4.16.0"

[settings]
disable_backends = ["asdf", "vfox", "ubi"]
```

`mise tool yarn --backend` now reports `aqua:yarnpkg/berry`, and `mise lock` records that backend. If a disabled asdf entry precedes an enabled `npm:@yarnpkg/cli-dist` entry, discovery and the child lockfile retain npm. Enabled parent pins still participate in discovery, the parent lockfile is unchanged, and explicitly installing `asdf:yarn` still fails while asdf is disabled.

Follow-up to #12927: https://github.com/jdx/mise/pull/12927#issuecomment-5664003877

Validation: the new parent-lockfile regression test and `mise run lint-fix` passed, including the all-features Cargo check. title: ci: retry only failing e2e tests
body:
A flaky e2e test currently causes CI to rerun its entire tranche, including passing tests; in the main workflow this repeats both tranches in the pair. Retry each failing test in the runner instead, so passing tests run once.

Main CI allows two attempts per test and release CI allows three, with a 30-second delay between attempts. Retries retain the tranche's token and concurrency limit, and each test invocation creates a fresh isolated environment. Logs from retried tests remain visible even if they recover, and the step summary keeps only the final attempt; only tests that exhaust their attempts appear in the final failure list.

Local runs still default to one attempt. Set `E2E_MAX_ATTEMPTS` to opt in and `E2E_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS` to adjust the delay.

Validation: five stub-based runner regression tests now run in Linux e2e CI and pass locally, covering selective retries, recovery, persistent failures, local defaults, tranche selection, invalid attempt limits, and rate-limit failures before a retry starts. Scoped shell and workflow formatting checks and the required repository-wide `mise run lint-fix` pass (including Cargo checking). The full e2e suite was not run.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are limited to e2e orchestration and CI wiring; product/runtime behavior is unchanged aside from more granular flaky-test handling in CI.
> 
> **Overview**
> Moves e2e retry logic from GitHub Actions (`nick-fields/retry` rerunning whole tranches) into **`e2e/run_all_tests`**, which retries **only failing tests** via `E2E_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and `E2E_RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS` (local default remains one attempt).
> 
> CI wires those env vars directly on `./e2e/run_all_tests` (main e2e: 2 attempts; release e2e: 3; 30s wait). Retried runs keep full logs in output when a test recovers; the GitHub step summary reflects the **final** attempt only.
> 
> Adds **`scripts/test-e2e-runner.py`** and a **Test e2e runner** step in the main Linux e2e workflow to regression-test selective retries, tranche filtering, rate-limit setup failures, and invalid config.

title: ci(docs): publish documentation only for releases
body:
Documentation changes currently deploy to production whenever a trusted docs-related commit lands on `main`. This makes the production site update only after a stable `v*` GitHub release is published, so the published docs stay aligned with released behavior.

Pull requests, pushes to `main`, and manual runs still build the documentation in dry-run mode. Release deployments use their own concurrency group so validation runs cannot cancel them, while a newer release can supersede an older in-progress deployment.

Validation:
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `hk run check --safe --format json .github/workflows/docs.yml .github/workflows/docs-impl.yml`
- `zizmor --min-severity high .github/workflows/docs.yml .github/workflows/docs-impl.yml`
- `git diff --check`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: OpenAI/GPT-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes are limited to GitHub Actions docs deployment gating and concurrency; no application runtime or auth/data paths are modified.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Docs no longer go live on every trusted push to `main`.** Production publish now happens only when a **stable `v*` GitHub release** is published; PRs, pushes, and manual runs still build docs but keep **`DRY_RUN` enabled**.
> 
> The **`docs`** workflow adds a **`release` (published)** trigger and routes releases through the **trusted** job only (untrusted is skipped on release). In **`docs-impl`**, **`DRY_RUN`** switches from “push to `main`” to “non-release, prerelease, or non-`v` tag,” and **concurrency** uses separate **deploy vs validation** groups so in-flight release deployments are not cancelled by validation runs (while newer releases can still supersede older deploys).

title: feat(dotfiles): allow opting out of plaintext history checks
body:
Enabling encryption after a file has been saved leaves plaintext in older commits, which blocks sync. Users can now allow those commits to be pushed with:

```sh
mise dot sync --allow-plaintext-history
```

For ongoing use, including the history watcher, set this in the global config:

```toml
[settings.history]
allow_plaintext_history = true
```

The setting defaults to `false` and is ignored in project configs. Both options allow older plaintext to reach the origin; new saves still follow the file's encryption policy. The history guide also explains how to remove the old commits instead, with shorter repair instructions.

Addresses #13171.

Validation: focused sync unit tests and dotfiles e2e tests, documentation build, and `mise run lint-fix`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes encrypted dotfile sync/publish and pull safety checks; misconfiguration can push or adopt plaintext secrets to the origin.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds an **opt-in escape hatch** when dotfile history contains older plaintext for paths that are now encrypted—sync and pull no longer hard-fail unless you choose to allow it.
> 
> **`mise dot sync --allow-plaintext-history`** skips the plaintext ancestry check for that run. **`settings.history.allow_plaintext_history`** (global only, default `false`, `MISE_HISTORY_ALLOW_PLAINTEXT_HISTORY`) does the same for sync, publish, and **incoming** history on pull; the CLI flag can still override a `false` env. New saves stay encrypted; bypassing the audit does not relax empty encryption recipients.
> 
> Docs expand **allow vs remove** plaintext history (watcher stop, `update-ref`, `git-filter-repo`, multi-machine force-with-lease / `bootstrap --adopt`). CLI/man/schema/usage listings add the flag; sync usage lines simplify to `[FLAGS]`.

@@ -22,6 +22,7 @@ The history watcher does this on its own in `sync` and `fetch-only` mode

 - **`--fetch-only`** — Fetch without publishing
+- **`--allow-plaintext-history`** — Allow publishing older unencrypted versions of encrypted files
 - **`--best-effort`** — Warn instead of failing when the origin is unreachable
 - **`-h --help`** — Print help

@@ -523,8 +523,108 @@ Adding encryption later leaves earlier plaintext versions in Git. Before a
 push, mise checks all reachable commits, including intermediate saves and
 merge parents, for violations of encrypted-path settings. An earlier
 plaintext version blocks the push even if the newest version is encrypted.
-You must explicitly rewrite or replace that history. This checks encryption
-settings; it does not scan arbitrary unencrypted files for secrets.
+To push, remove that history or explicitly allow it as shown below. This check
+uses encryption settings; it does not scan other files for secrets.
+
+### Allow plaintext history
+
+To publish the older unencrypted versions anyway, bypass the check for one sync:
+
+```sh
+mise dot sync --allow-plaintext-history
+```
+
+To allow this for all syncs and pulls, including the watcher, add to your
+global config:
+
+```toml
+[settings.history]
+allow_plaintext_history = true
+```
+
+Both options publish the old plaintext to the origin. New saves still use the
+file's encryption policy. The setting defaults to `false` and is ignored in
+project configs.
+
+### Remove plaintext from history
+
+If you saved credentials before enabling encryption, rotate them first.
+Encryption does not protect copies in older commits, even in a private repo.
+
+Stop the supervising history watcher service and back up the repository. Keep
+the backup secure: it contains the plaintext too. If the service uses the
+documented `mise-history` name, stop and remove its installed definition with:
+
+```sh
+mise bootstrap services remove mise-history
+```
+
+This uses the configured user service manager on Linux, macOS, and Windows and
+prevents it from restarting the watcher during the repair. If you used another
+service name, replace `mise-history` with that name.
+
+If the plaintext was never pushed, you can drop the affected checkpoints and
+save the current file again with encryption enabled. This drops **all
+checkpoints after the last safe commit**, including changes to other files.
+Find that commit with `mise dot history`, or inspect the bare repository with
+the `git log` command below.
+
+Replace `safe` and the credentials path below with your commit and tracked
+file. Make sure encryption is configured for that path before saving.
+History uses a bare Git repository, so use `git update-ref` to move the branch:
+
+```sh
+repo="${MISE_STATE_DIR:-${XDG_STATE_HOME:-$HOME/.local/state}/mise}/history/repo.git"
+git --git-dir="$repo" log --all -- home/.config/app/credentials
+old="$(git --git-dir="$repo" rev-parse refs/heads/main)"
+safe="<commit before plaintext was saved>"
+
+if git --git-dir="$repo" merge-base --is-ancestor "$safe" "$old"; then
+  git --git-dir="$repo" update-ref -m "remove plaintext history" \
+    refs/heads/main "$safe" "$old" &&
+    mise dot save ~/.config/app/credentials \
+      --description "save encrypted credentials" &&
+    mise dot sync
+fi
+```
+
+The ancestry check rejects commits outside the current history. Passing `old`
+to `update-ref` makes it fail if another process has moved the branch. The save
+records the live file with encryption and rebuilds mise's checkpoint index.
+Moving the branch makes the discarded commits unreachable but does not
+immediately erase their plaintext objects from the active repository. After
+verifying the repaired history and deciding that you no longer need those
+objects for recovery, remove them from the active repository with:
+
+```sh
+git --git-dir="$repo" reflog expire --expire=now --all
+git --git-dir="$repo" gc --prune=now
+```
+
+The secure backup still contains the discarded history. Delete it only when
+you no longer need it for recovery.
+
+To keep later checkpoints, use a tool such as
+[git-filter-repo](https://github.com/newren/git-filter-repo) on a separate,
+secure copy. Check that no reachable commit contains plaintext for the
+protected path before replacing the local `refs/heads/main`. Do not filter
+mise's active repository in place.
+
+If the plaintext was already pushed, pause history on every machine using the
+repo. Repair the history, then push the replacement branch with Git's
+`--force-with-lease`; mise does not force-push. On every other machine, move
+its existing history store to a secure backup and run
+`mise bootstrap --adopt <url>` to initialize a fresh store from the reviewed
+replacement. Ordinary `mise dot sync` does not replace existing history. Do
+not restart any watcher until every machine uses the replacement, or an old
+store can bring the plaintext back. The Git host may still retain old objects
+or backups.
+
+Restart the declared watcher once the repair is complete:
+
+```sh
+mise bootstrap services apply
+```

title: fix(pypi): fall back when dependency graphs are unsupported
body:
Ordinary PyPI/pipx installs can work again when dependency graph locking cannot represent the package or its configuration. If a package has a source-only dependency, or uses `uvx_args`/`pipx_args`, `mise install` now warns and falls back to uv's version-only installation path instead of failing before uv gets a chance to install it.

The fallback remains stable on later installs, so the existing version-only installation is reused rather than creating another graph-derived installation directory. Explicit reproducibility requests remain strict: `mise lock` still rejects unsupported free-form installer arguments or dependencies without usable wheels, and `mise install --locked` still requires a valid recorded graph.

For example, configurations such as:

```toml
[tools]
"pipx:example" = { version = "1.0.0", uvx_args = "--prerelease allow" }
```

continue to install normally, while `mise lock` reports that the arguments cannot be represented in a dependency graph.

Fixes the compatibility regressions reported in [Discussion #13168](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13168).

## Validation

- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/backend/test_pypi_lock`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes install and lock satisfaction logic for all pipx/PyPI tools; incorrect fallback or satisfaction checks could affect reproducibility or skip reinstalls, though locked installs remain gated separately.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Ordinary `mise install` for PyPI/pipx tools no longer hard-fails** when mise cannot build or use a uv dependency graph. The installer warns and continues on the existing **version-only** uv/pipx path when `uvx_args`/`pipx_args` are set, graph resolution errors (e.g. no usable wheels), or similar blockers—while reusing an already-installed version-only layout instead of forcing a `~uv~` graph install.
> 
> **Strict paths stay strict:** `mise lock` / `mise install --locked` still require a reproducible graph and reject unsupported `uvx_args`/`pipx_args` or wheel-only lock failures. Automatic lock population gains a **best-effort** mode (e.g. when locking from installed tools) so one bad graph does not abort the whole lockfile; explicit lock generation remains erroring.
> 
> **Related fixes:** `is_install_satisfied` treats satisfied version-only installs correctly when not locked; Python upgrades pass **locked** context into `PIPXBackend::reinstall_all`. Docs and e2e cover fallback messaging and source-only packages via a new test index sdist.

title: fix: suppress missing warnings for lazy tools
body:
Lazy tool declarations are intentionally left uninstalled until one of their commands is invoked, but directory hooks reported them as missing under the normal missing-tool status policy. This caused repeated warnings after entering a project or running a bare `mise install`, even though the lazy tools were behaving as configured.

For example:

```toml
[tools]
jq = { version = "latest", lazy = true }
```

Entering this project no longer emits `missing: jq@...`. The shared missing-version notifier now excludes lazy declarations before applying `status.missing_tools`; ordinary missing tools continue to respect that setting, including `always`.

Addresses discussion #13166.

## Validation

- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_lazy_tools`

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Narrow change to warning filtering only; install, shim, and lazy bootstrap behavior are untouched.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Lazy tools that are intentionally not installed** no longer appear in `missing: …` status messages from `hook-env` and other paths that call `notify_missing_versions`, even when `status.missing_tools` is set to `always`.
>

body:

title: perf(bootstrap): pipeline brew bottle installs
body:
`mise bootstrap packages apply` currently waits for every bottle download to finish before starting any extraction, then waits for every bottle preparation job before linking the first dependency. This change makes each bounded job download and immediately prepare its own bottle, and commits prepared bottles as soon as dependency order permits. Downloads, extraction, relocation, codesigning, and sequential linking can therefore overlap without increasing the existing `jobs` limit.

For 12 alternating fresh-cache, isolated-prefix installs (6 per implementation) of:

```console
mise bootstrap packages apply brew:jq brew:tree brew:wget brew:just brew:shellcheck
```

the median fell from 6.57s on #13152 to 4.04s with the pipeline: 38.6% less wall time, or 1.63x faster. Each run used a fresh bottle and metadata cache, fresh data directory, and fresh Homebrew prefix on Apple silicon; the default remained 8 jobs. All 12 installs succeeded, and the installed `jq`, `tree`, `wget`, `just`, and `shellcheck` binaries were exercised after the initial sanity run.

Source builds remain dependency ordered while concurrently advancing safe bottle download/preparation work. On failure, queued jobs are discarded and only already-active jobs are drained, so staging cleanup completes without starting additional downloads or preparations. The first failure remains authoritative, successfully installed rows remain visible, and Linux runtime setup still runs after a partial install.

Validation:
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise x -- cargo test --locked --bin mise system::packages::brew` (366 passed)
- Optimized release build
- Cold-cache benchmark and installed-binary smoke test described above

Stacked on #13152.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: unavailable/unavailable; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core brew install orchestration (concurrency, dependency-ordered linking, and failure paths) where incorrect ordering or cleanup could leave a partial prefix or mask errors.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Pipelines Homebrew bottle installs** so each bounded job downloads and prepares its own bottle instead of finishing all downloads before any extraction starts. Prepared bottles are linked as soon as dependency order allows, while source builds can overlap bottle work via `tokio::select!` without breaking prefix mutation ordering.
> 
> **Refactors brew concurrency helpers** in `fetch.rs`: `concurrently` now returns a `ConcurrentJobs` handle that streams completions (replacing the old collect-all-at-once helper and the separate `concurrent_jobs` entry point). Tests cover incremental yields and cancel-pending behavior.
> 
> **Tightens failure cleanup**: on error, pending bottle jobs are cancelled, active jobs are drained for staging cleanup, incomplete progress rows are abandoned while keeping successful installs visible, and Linux runtime setup still runs after a partial install before returning the first error.

title: perf(bootstrap): prepare brew bottles concurrently
body:
`mise bootstrap packages apply` currently downloads bottles concurrently but then extracts, relocates, signs, and writes every bottle receipt one at a time. This change prepares independent bottles concurrently using the existing `jobs` limit, while preserving dependency-ordered Cellar commits and prefix linking. It does not change the default job count or add a new setting.

For a warm-cache install of 14 bottles from:

```console
mise bootstrap packages apply brew:jq brew:tree brew:wget brew:just brew:shellcheck
```

8 alternating isolated-prefix runs on Apple silicon improved from a 4.097s median on the metadata-only base branch to 2.893s with concurrent staging: 29.4% less time, or 1.42x faster. The comparison reused downloaded bottles and metadata to isolate extraction, relocation, signing, receipt generation, and linking.

Preparation runs in unique, lock-protected staging directories. On preparation failure, queued work is discarded, active work is drained for cleanup, and successfully prepared earlier dependencies still commit in order before the error returns. A later pour reclaims only unlocked staging created with the current lock protocol, leaving lockless directories from older mise processes untouched.

Final Cellar and shared-prefix mutations use a prefix-local commit lock even when operation history is disabled. Bottle preparation remains concurrent outside it; source builds retain it while writing directly into the final Cellar. The installer rechecks completed state under the lock, and creates `opt/<name>` last so a partial public-link operation cannot look complete after a process is killed.

Validation:
- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise x -- cargo test --locked --bin mise system::packages::brew` (365 passed)
- Installed the benchmark package set into an isolated prefix and ran `jq`, `tree`, `wget`, `just`, and `shellcheck` from that prefix

title: perf(bootstrap): fetch brew metadata concurrently
body:
Fresh `mise bootstrap packages apply` runs previously fetched Homebrew formula metadata one request at a time while discovering a dependency closure. Formulae in the same dependency frontier are independent, so mise now fetches that metadata concurrently using the existing `jobs` limit, then restores deterministic processing order before resolving the next frontier.

This does not change the default job count or add a new concurrency setting. Tap fallback behavior, alias handling, and dependency-first installation order remain unchanged.

## Performance

On an Apple M5 Max, 15 alternating fresh-cache runs of:

```sh
mise bootstrap packages apply --dry-run brew:ffmpeg
```

reduced median dependency-resolution time from 288 ms to 112 ms (2.57x faster). Baseline and changed output were byte-for-byte identical. Network outliers remain possible; this comparison alternated binaries and isolated each run's cache and Homebrew prefix.

## Validation

- 360 Brew-package unit tests passed
- Full repository lint/fix pipeline passed
- Optimized release build passed

title: docs: clarify npm, pypi, and lockfile workflows

Users can install a CLI with `mise use python@3.14 uv pypi:black` or `mise use node@24 npm:prettier`, generate a lockfile with `mise lock`, and install its recorded resolutions with `mise install --locked`.

- The PyPI guide separates package sources, interpreter selection, pipx compatibility, and installer restrictions. Private-index examples distinguish dependency-graph installs from version-only installs.

title: perf(ci): enforce warnings in Windows unit tests
body:
Windows unit CI currently performs a dedicated `cargo check` with unused warnings denied before compiling the unit tests. That redundant build took 3.5–10 minutes on recent runs and made `windows-unit` a critical-path job.

Deny warnings through the x64 MSVC target flags for the existing Windows build and unit-test jobs, retaining the repository's 8 MB stack linker setting. Remove the dedicated check and extend the existing non-default rustls build to `--all-targets`, preserving its feature and target coverage without a separate compilation or additional runner.

The Windows npm backend test now activates its pinned tools in Pester's isolated test project and runs the installed Prettier CLI entrypoint with the selected Node executable. This prevents the repository's active Prettier version from shadowing the version under test and keeps backend installation coverage independent of Windows npm shim lookup.

## Validation

- `mise run lint-fix`
- Parsed `.github/workflows/test-impl.yml` with Ruby's YAML parser
- Verified workflow formatting with Prettier
- Reproduced the isolated project install and direct CLI invocation with fresh data, cache, and config directories
- Windows unit CI passed with warnings denied in 24m9s on the final head

title: feat(lock): store Python and npm dependency graphs in native sidecars
body:
Python CLI tools can lock and replay their dependencies with uv, and both Python and npm dependency graphs now live in native sidecar files instead of expanding `mise.lock` into thousands of nested TOML lines.

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:black" = "24.10.0"
"npm:prettier" = "3.3.3"
```

Run `mise lock` (or `mise lock --upgrade` for an older lockfile), then commit `mise.lock` and the generated sidecars:

```text
.mise/locks/pypi-black/24.10.0/{pyproject.toml,uv.lock}
.mise/locks/npm-prettier/3.3.3/{package.json,aube-lock.yaml}
```

`mise.lock` records each directory's relative path and the SHA-256 of its native graph file. Projects using `.config/mise/` keep their sidecars there; local/environment lockfiles have separate cleanup scopes. Paths remain stable, option variants coexist, and explicit locking or generate-mode saves prune unreferenced sidecars under transaction locks. Merge-mode auto-lock never deletes sidecars. Monorepo graphs follow the root lockfile layout; successful migration removes legacy graph directories. Revision stays **2**, which has not shipped; revisions 0–1 retain their format until explicit upgrade. Unreleased inline revision-2 graphs remain readable and migrate on save.

`pypi:` is the preferred backend name; `pipx:` remains supported without warnings or filesystem migration, including settings and environment compatibility. `pypi:black` and `pipx:black` are distinct tool identities using `pypi-black` and `pipx-black` directories respectively. Changing spelling creates a new installation and lock entry. Settings aliases and backend-level controls still accept both names.

Python graph locking requires an installed **uv >= 0.12.10** and published hashed wheels. Resolution retains universal Python/platform markers, extras, index authentication, and release-age policy without executing source builds or storing credentials. Installation validates the root and interpreter and replays with `uv sync --frozen` and source builds disabled. Standalone pipx and Git sources retain their legacy behavior outside graph locking; unsupported free-form installer arguments are rejected for graph locking.

Ordinary locks reuse graphs; `mise lock --bump pypi:black` refreshes dependencies even when Black's version stays unchanged. Valid external graph edits are accepted by `mise lock` or when an ordinary installation is needed; the actual graph bytes determine the new installation identity and recorded digest. A hot ordinary `mise install` reuses the recorded installation without reading or validating its sidecar, with a metadata-only warning if the graph file is missing. `mise install --locked` rejects digest mismatches. Formatting edits also change identity. Environment resolution and installed-tool lookup use the recorded digest without reading sidecars.

Renovate 44.79.2's local pep621 extractor detected an actual generated sidecar project, its adjacent `uv.lock`, and the pinned fixture dependency. Native aube YAML is preserved byte-for-byte, but

 ---
 
-# pipx Backend
-
-The `pipx` backend installs Python command-line applications in isolated virtual
-environments. Each tool gets its own dependencies. Use a project environment
-and pip or uv for application libraries such as NumPy and requests.
-
-When uv is available, mise uses **`uv tool install`**. Otherwise it uses
-`pipx install`. The `pipx:` prefix names the backend in both cases; the legacy
-`uvx` option names do not mean that mise runs the `uvx` command.
-
-The pipx backend supports the following sources:
-
-- PyPI
-- Git
-- GitHub
-- HTTP
-
-The code for this is inside the mise repository at [`./src/backend/pipx.rs`](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/main/src/backend/pipx.rs).
-
-## Dependencies
-
-Install uv and a Python version suitable for the CLI. For example:
-
-```sh
-mise use python@3.14 uv pipx:black
-mise exec -- black --version
-```
-
-If you need the pipx installer instead, install `python` and `pipx` with
-`mise use python@3.14 pipx`, then set the tool's [`uvx`](#uvx) option to `false`.
-No separately installed pipx is needed for the uv path.
-
-mise forwards [`minimum_release_age`](/configuration/settings.html#minimum_release_age)
-to transitive Python dependency resolution during install. The uv install path uses uv's
-`--exclude-newer` flag and requires `uv >= 0.2.22`. The `pipx` fallback passes pip's
-`--uploaded-prior-to` flag.
-
-## Usage
-
-The command above writes a project configuration like this:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-python = "3.14"
-uv = "latest"
-"pipx:black" = "latest"
-```
-
-Add `-g` for global configuration. `pipx:black` installs the PyPI distribution;
-`pipx:psf/black` installs from its GitHub source. Choose the source intentionally,
-since its releases and installation requirements can differ.
-
-## Choosing Python
-
-The selected installer chooses the interpreter for each tool environment. If a
-CLI must use a particular Python version, pass that requirement explicitly:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-python = "3.14"
-uv = "latest"
-"pipx:black" = {
-  version = "latest",
-  uvx_args = "--python 3.14",
-  pipx_args = "--python 3.14",
-}
-```
-
-Only the arguments for the selected installer apply. uv can also download an
-interpreter according to its own Python discovery and download settings.
-
-## Python upgrades
-
-If a CLI stops working after changing Python, reinstall it under the intended
-Python version. This recreates the tool environment and its dependencies:
-
-```sh
-mise install --force pipx:black
-mise exec -- black --version
-```
-
-Check which Python version is active before reinstalling. Existing virtualenvs
-and native extensions do not necessarily remain usable after their interpreter
-is removed or changed.
-
-### Supported Pipx Syntax
-
-| Description                           | Usage                                                  |
-| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
-| PyPI shorthand latest version         | `pipx:black`                                           |
-| PyPI shorthand for specific version   | `pipx:black@24.3.0`                                    |
-| GitHub shorthand for latest version   | `pipx:psf/black`                                       |
-| GitHub shorthand for specific version | `pipx:psf/black@24.3.0`                                |
-| Git syntax for latest version         | `pipx:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git`            |
-| Git syntax for a branch               | `pipx:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git@main`       |
-| HTTPS with zipfile                    | `pipx:https://github.com/psf/black/archive/18.9b0.zip` |
-
-For GitHub URLs, `latest` resolves to the latest published GitHub Release and falls
-back to default-branch HEAD when there are no releases. For other Git URLs, `latest`
-tracks default-branch HEAD and resolves it to a concrete commit before installation.
-Remote tags are available for explicit version requests.
-
-Other syntax may work but is unsupported and untested.
-
-## Settings
-
-Set these with `mise settings set [VARIABLE]=[VALUE]` or by setting the environment variable listed.
-
-<script setup>
-import Settings from '/components/settings.vue';
-</script>
-<Settings child="pipx" :level="3" />
-
-## Tool Options
-
-The following [tool-options](/dev-tools/#tool-options) are available for the `pipx` backend—these
-go in `[tools]` in `mise.toml`.
-
-### `registry_url`
-
-Set the package registry URL mise uses to resolve versions for this tool. The URL must contain a
-`{}` placeholder for the package name. This overrides the `pipx.registry_url` setting for this
-tool only; registry arguments for installation are still configured separately through `uvx_args` or
-`pipx_args`.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:my-tool" = {
-  version = "latest",
-  registry_url = "https://packages.example.com/pypi/{}/json",
-  uvx_args = "--index-url https://packages.example.com/pypi/simple",
-  pipx_args = "--pip-args='--index-url https://packages.example.com/pypi/simple'"
-}
-```
-
-### `install_env`
-
-Set environment variables for `uv tool install` or `pipx install`. mise still
-sets the tool directory, bin directory, and configured Python package index
-variables after applying `install_env`. For the uv installer, for example:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:black" = { version = "latest", install_env = { UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE = "1" } }
-```
-
-### `extras`
-
-Install additional components.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:harlequin" = { version = "latest", extras = "postgres,s3" }
-# equivalent array form:
-# "pipx:harlequin" = { version = "latest", extras = ["postgres", "s3"] }
-# extras also work with Git sources:
-# "pipx:psf/black" = { version = "latest", extras = ["jupyter"] }
-```
-
-When passing extras inline, use mise's `key=value` tool-option syntax:
-
-```bash
-mise use 'pipx:psf/black[extras=jupyter]@latest'
-```
-
-For Git repositories whose name differs from the Python distribution name, set `package_name` so
-mise can build the requirement used to select extras:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:owner/repository" = { version = "latest", package_name = "distribution", extras = ["feature"] }
-```
-
-### `pipx_args`
-
-Additional arguments to pass to `pipx` when installing the package.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible" = { version = "latest", uvx = false, pipx_args = "--include-deps" }
-```
-
-### `uvx`
-
-Set to `false` to always disable uv for this tool.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible" = { version = "latest", uvx = false, pipx_args = "--include-deps" }
-```
-
-### `uvx_args`
-
-Additional arguments to pass to `uv tool install`. These apply only when uv is
-selected; `pipx_args` applies only to the pipx installer.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible-core" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--with ansible" }
-```

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches the aube-backed package install path and lockfile resolution (including compression deps), so regressions could affect npm/Bun installs and dev tooling sync, though scope is mostly version and lock updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Bumps the embedded **aube** Rust crates and the dev **aube** CLI to **2.2.16**, updating `Cargo.lock`, `mise.lock` (including switching the tool backend to `packslip:github.com/aubepkg/aube` and refreshed per-platform artifacts), and aligning `mise.toml` so `aube` tracks `latest` with **`minimum_release_age = "0s"`** so locks can follow new releases immediately.

title: feat(bootstrap): inspect dotfile sync conflicts
body:
Dotfile sharing conflicts currently report the affected path and require a local-or-remote decision without showing the two stored versions. This adds a read-only conflict inspection command so users can compare the exact saved-local and fetched-remote contents before choosing a resolution.

```sh
mise bootstrap dotfiles conflicts ~/.config/mise/config.toml
mise bootstrap dotfiles conflicts --difftool ~/.config/mise/config.toml
```

The default output is a unified diff. `--difftool` launches the configured Git diff tool and falls back to `merge.tool` when `diff.tool` is not set; `--tool <name>` selects one explicitly. Both output modes report file-mode changes. Encrypted conflict contents are decrypted only into private temporary files for the comparison. Inspection never changes either side or marks the conflict resolved.

The conflict guidance and history documentation now point to the inspection command. The manual merged-content workflow explicitly saves the conflicted path before `--keep-local`, including files tracked with `--no-autosave`.

Secret resolution now follows the same composed bootstrap config maps as dotfile discovery, so root-scoped templates can use secrets declared by their bootstrap root. Identical declarations across roots deduplicate, while conflicting declarations identify both source configs and fail.

The generated command reference links directly to the conflict implementation. Its JSON post-processing capture limit is raised to 10 MiB because this expanded CLI specification exceeds Bun’s 1 MiB default buffer.

Addresses https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13143

## Validation

- `mise run lint-fix`
- `mise run render`
- `mise run docs:build`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_bootstrap_config_root_secrets`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_recovery_journey`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_sync_files_encrypted`

@@ -0,0 +1,47 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+
+secret_root="$PWD/secret-root"
+secret_target="$PWD/root-secret.conf"
+mkdir -p "$secret_root"
+echo '{{ secret(name="root_only_secret") }}' >"$secret_root/secret.tmpl"
+
+cat <<EOF >mise.toml
+[bootstrap]
+config_roots = ["secret-root"]
+EOF
+
+cat <<EOF >"$secret_root/mise.toml"
+[bootstrap.secrets]
+root_only_secret = "MISE_ROOT_ONLY_SECRET"
+
+[dotfiles]
+"$secret_target" = { source = "secret.tmpl", mode = "template" }
+EOF
+
+# Secrets declared only in a selected bootstrap root are available to that
+# root's dotfile templates and appear in aggregate status.
+assert_succeed "MISE_ROOT_ONLY_SECRET=from-root-secret mise bootstrap dotfiles apply --yes"
+assert "cat '$secret_target'" "from-root-secret"
+assert_contains "MISE_ROOT_ONLY_SECRET=from-root-secret mise bootstrap status" "root_only_secret"
+
+# Independent roots may repeat the same declaration, but must reject a secret
+# name that points at a different environment variable.
+second_root="$PWD/second-root"
+mkdir -p "$second_root"
+cat <<EOF >mise.toml
+[bootstrap]
+config_roots = ["secret-root", "second-root"]
+EOF
+cat <<EOF >"$second_root/mise.toml"
+[bootstrap.secrets]
+root_only_secret = "MISE_ROOT_ONLY_SECRET"
+EOF
+assert_succeed "MISE_ROOT_ONLY_SECRET=from-root-secret mise bootstrap status --json | jq -e '[.secrets[] | select(.name == \"root_only_secret\")] | length == 1'"
+
+cat <<EOF >"$second_root/mise.toml"
+[bootstrap.secrets]
+root_only_secret = "MISE_DIFFERENT_SECRET"
+EOF
+assert_fail "mise bootstrap status" "conflicting bootstrap secret declarations for root_only_secret"
+assert_fail "mise bootstrap status" "$secret_root/mise.toml"
+assert_fail "mise bootstrap status" "$second_root/mise.toml"

title: feat(lock): store Python and npm dependency graphs in native sidecars
body:
Python CLI tools can lock and replay their dependencies with uv, and both Python and npm dependency graphs now live in native sidecar files instead of expanding `mise.lock` into thousands of nested TOML lines.

```toml
[tools]
"pypi:black" = "24.10.0"
"npm:prettier" = "3.3.3"
```

Run `mise lock` (or `mise lock --upgrade` for an older lockfile), then commit `mise.lock` and the generated sidecars:

```text
.mise/locks/pipx-black/24.10.0/{pyproject.toml,uv.lock}
.mise/locks/npm-prettier/3.3.3/{package.json,aube-lock.yaml}
```

`mise.lock` records each directory's relative path and the SHA-256 of its native graph file. Projects using `.config/mise/` keep their sidecars there; local/environment lockfiles have separate cleanup scopes. Paths remain stable, option variants coexist, and removing an entry prunes its sidecars. Revision stays **2**, which has not shipped; revisions 0–1 retain their format until explicit upgrade. Unreleased inline revision-2 graphs remain readable and migrate on save.

`pypi:` is the preferred backend name; `pipx:` remains supported without warnings or filesystem migration, including settings and environment compatibility. Existing explicit spellings and registry aliases keep their identities.

Python graph locking requires an installed **uv >= 0.12.10** and published hashed wheels. Resolution retains universal Python/platform markers, extras, index authentication, and release-age policy without executing source builds or storing credentials. Installation validates the root and interpreter and replays with `uv sync --frozen` and source builds disabled. Standalone pipx and Git sources retain their legacy behavior outside graph locking; unsupported free-form installer arguments are rejected for graph locking.

Ordinary locks reuse graphs; `mise lock --bump pypi:black` refreshes dependencies even when Black's version stays unchanged. Valid external graph edits are accepted by ordinary `mise install` or `mise lock`; the actual graph bytes determine the new installation identity and recorded digest. `mise install --locked` rejects digest mismatches. Formatting edits also change identity. Environment resolution and installed-tool lookup use the recorded digest without reading sidecars.

Renovate 44.79.2's local pep621 extractor detected an actual generated sidecar project, its adjacent `uv.lock`, and the pinned fixture dependency. Native aube YAML is preserved byte-for-byte, but scanners that only understand npm lockfiles do not gain transitive aube visibility.

Validation on macOS: 177 lockfile unit tests, 38 Python unit tests, Python/npm fixture e2e tests, lockfile revision and pruning suites, task dry-run and outdated checks, full workspace Clippy, lint fixes, and documentation build passed. The Python/npm fixture tests, revision/rollback tests, 177 lockfile unit tests, 38 Python unit tests, and full Clippy check were repeated successfully after incorporating current main (aube 2.2.16). The 27 CLI lock tests also pass after fix

-# pipx Backend
-
-The `pipx` backend installs Python command-line applications in isolated virtual
-environments. Each tool gets its own dependencies. Use a project environment
-and pip or uv for application libraries such as NumPy and requests.
-
-When uv is available, mise uses **`uv tool install`**. Otherwise it uses
-`pipx install`. The `pipx:` prefix names the backend in both cases; the legacy
-`uvx` option names do not mean that mise runs the `uvx` command.
-
-The pipx backend supports the following sources:
-
-- PyPI
-- Git
-- GitHub
-- HTTP
-
-The code for this is inside the mise repository at [`./src/backend/pipx.rs`](https://github.com/jdx/mise/blob/main/src/backend/pipx.rs).
-
-## Dependencies
-
-Install uv and a Python version suitable for the CLI. For example:
-
-```sh
-mise use python@3.14 uv pipx:black
-mise exec -- black --version
-```
-
-If you need the pipx installer instead, install `python` and `pipx` with
-`mise use python@3.14 pipx`, then set the tool's [`uvx`](#uvx) option to `false`.
-No separately installed pipx is needed for the uv path.
-
-mise forwards [`minimum_release_age`](/configuration/settings.html#minimum_release_age)
-to transitive Python dependency resolution during install. The uv install path uses uv's
-`--exclude-newer` flag and requires `uv >= 0.2.22`. The `pipx` fallback passes pip's
-`--uploaded-prior-to` flag.
-
-## Usage
-
-The command above writes a project configuration like this:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-python = "3.14"
-uv = "latest"
-"pipx:black" = "latest"
-```
-
-Add `-g` for global configuration. `pipx:black` installs the PyPI distribution;
-`pipx:psf/black` installs from its GitHub source. Choose the source intentionally,
-since its releases and installation requirements can differ.
-
-## Choosing Python
-
-The selected installer chooses the interpreter for each tool environment. If a
-CLI must use a particular Python version, pass that requirement explicitly:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-python = "3.14"
-uv = "latest"
-"pipx:black" = {
-  version = "latest",
-  uvx_args = "--python 3.14",
-  pipx_args = "--python 3.14",
-}
-```
-
-Only the arguments for the selected installer apply. uv can also download an
-interpreter according to its own Python discovery and download settings.
-
-## Python upgrades
-
-If a CLI stops working after changing Python, reinstall it under the intended
-Python version. This recreates the tool environment and its dependencies:
-
-```sh
-mise install --force pipx:black
-mise exec -- black --version
-```
-
-Check which Python version is active before reinstalling. Existing virtualenvs
-and native extensions do not necessarily remain usable after their interpreter
-is removed or changed.
-
-### Supported Pipx Syntax
-
-| Description                           | Usage                                                  |
-| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
-| PyPI shorthand latest version         | `pipx:black`                                           |
-| PyPI shorthand for specific version   | `pipx:black@24.3.0`                                    |
-| GitHub shorthand for latest version   | `pipx:psf/black`                                       |
-| GitHub shorthand for specific version | `pipx:psf/black@24.3.0`                                |
-| Git syntax for latest version         | `pipx:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git`            |
-| Git syntax for a branch               | `pipx:git+https://github.com/psf/black.git@main`       |
-| HTTPS with zipfile                    | `pipx:https://github.com/psf/black/archive/18.9b0.zip` |
-
-For GitHub URLs, `latest` resolves to the latest published GitHub Release and falls
-back to default-branch HEAD when there are no releases. For other Git URLs, `latest`
-tracks default-branch HEAD and resolves it to a concrete commit before installation.
-Remote tags are available for explicit version requests.
-
-Other syntax may work but is unsupported and untested.
-
-## Settings
-
-Set these with `mise settings set [VARIABLE]=[VALUE]` or by setting the environment variable listed.
-
-<script setup>
-import Settings from '/components/settings.vue';
-</script>
-<Settings child="pipx" :level="3" />
-
-## Tool Options
-
-The following [tool-options](/dev-tools/#tool-options) are available for the `pipx` backend—these
-go in `[tools]` in `mise.toml`.
-
-### `registry_url`
-
-Set the package registry URL mise uses to resolve versions for this tool. The URL must contain a
-`{}` placeholder for the package name. This overrides the `pipx.registry_url` setting for this
-tool only; registry arguments for installation are still configured separately through `uvx_args` or
-`pipx_args`.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:my-tool" = {
-  version = "latest",
-  registry_url = "https://packages.example.com/pypi/{}/json",
-  uvx_args = "--index-url https://packages.example.com/pypi/simple",
-  pipx_args = "--pip-args='--index-url https://packages.example.com/pypi/simple'"
-}
-```
-
-### `install_env`
-
-Set environment variables for `uv tool install` or `pipx install`. mise still
-sets the tool directory, bin directory, and configured Python package index
-variables after applying `install_env`. For the uv installer, for example:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:black" = { version = "latest", install_env = { UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE = "1" } }
-```
-
-### `extras`
-
-Install additional components.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:harlequin" = { version = "latest", extras = "postgres,s3" }
-# equivalent array form:
-# "pipx:harlequin" = { version = "latest", extras = ["postgres", "s3"] }
-# extras also work with Git sources:
-# "pipx:psf/black" = { version = "latest", extras = ["jupyter"] }
-```
-
-When passing extras inline, use mise's `key=value` tool-option syntax:
-
-```bash
-mise use 'pipx:psf/black[extras=jupyter]@latest'
-```
-
-For Git repositories whose name differs from the Python distribution name, set `package_name` so
-mise can build the requirement used to select extras:
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:owner/repository" = { version = "latest", package_name = "distribution", extras = ["feature"] }
-```
-
-### `pipx_args`
-
-Additional arguments to pass to `pipx` when installing the package.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible" = { version = "latest", uvx = false, pipx_args = "--include-deps" }
-```
-
-### `uvx`
-
-Set to `false` to always disable uv for this tool.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible" = { version = "latest", uvx = false, pipx_args = "--include-deps" }
-```
-
-### `uvx_args`
-
-Additional arguments to pass to `uv tool install`. These apply only when uv is
-selected; `pipx_args` applies only to the pipx installer.
-
-```toml
-[tools]
-"pipx:ansible-core" = { version = "latest", uvx_args = "--with ansible" }
-```

title: fix(dotfiles): support bootstrap secrets in templates
body:
Dotfile templates can now consume values declared in `[bootstrap.secrets]`, matching managed bootstrap file templates. For example:

```toml
[bootstrap.secrets]
api_token = "EXAMPLE_API_TOKEN"

[dotfiles."~/.config/example/credentials"]
source = "dotfiles/credentials.tmpl"
mode = "template"
```

```jinja
token={{ secret(name="api_token") }}
```

Commands that render dotfile templates accept `--prompt-secrets`; without an available value, rendering fails closed. Full bootstrap preflights dotfile templates before any mutation, then rerenders them at apply time while reusing resolved secret values so hooks can update dynamic inputs. `mise bootstrap status` reports secrets used only by dotfiles, and textual dotfile diffs redact resolved secret values from both current and desired content. Both Tera compatibility modes use the same resolver and cover available, missing, and undeclared inputs.

`mise oci build` rejects `secret()` and removes the `env` context, `get_env()`, `exec()`, and `read_file()` from dotfile template rendering so ambient credentials cannot be persisted in a publishable image layer.

This addresses https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13135.

Validation:
- `mise run lint`
- `cargo test --all-features --bin mise system::secrets::tests`
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_dotfiles_files`
- `TEST_ALL=1 mise run test:e2e e2e/oci/test_oci_build_slow`
- `mise run render`

title: fix(brew): support appdir DSL in tap cask metadata evaluation
body:
## What

Define `appdir` on `CaskMetadata` and `CaskFlightSteps` in the tap-cask metadata evaluator, answering Homebrew's default (`/Applications`).

## Why

`brew-cask:` packages from third-party taps hard-fail the packages phase when the cask interpolates `appdir` (e.g. `binary "#{appdir}/..."`): `method_missing` raises `unsupported cask metadata DSL`, and since third-party taps have no published API metadata to fall back on, bootstrap fails entirely. The install-time shim already defines `appdir` (`cask_shim.rb`); it was only missing from `tap_cask_metadata.rb`.

The metadata path never knows the real install location and the installer re-evaluates the cask via the shim, so a default-backed placeholder is sufficient here.

## Test

- Extended `extracts_cask_metadata_without_homebrew` to interpolate `appdir` in both `binary` and a flight-step `run` and assert the resolved path.
- Verified against the real-world failing cask (`umputun/apps/agterm`): baseline raises, this branch evaluates and emits the expected binary artifact.

Fixes #13136

title: security(history): restrict describe commands to global config
body:
`history.describe_command` could previously be supplied by project configuration. After a command such as `mise install` implicitly trusted that project, a later dotfiles history checkpoint could execute the project-controlled command and pass it unencrypted tracked-file diffs.

This restricts the setting to system/global configuration and `MISE_HISTORY_DESCRIBE_COMMAND`. Resolution now also goes through the history-specific configuration path, which never considers project files and verifies trust before honoring command-bearing configuration.

Users who intentionally configure automatic descriptions can continue using global configuration:

```toml
[settings]
history.describe_command = "my-describer"
```

Project values are ignored with a security warning. Focused coverage verifies that an implicitly trusted project cannot execute a description command, while global configuration and the environment override continue to work.

Validation: repository lint-fix/all-feature check, focused settings unit tests, and `e2e/cli/test_history_describe_command_config`.

*AI-assisted — Tool: Codex; model: openai/gpt-5; version: unavailable.*

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes who may configure a command that runs on checkpoints and receives personal dotfile diffs; incorrect resolution or trust handling could re-expose command injection or break legitimate global/env setup.
> 
> **Overview**
> Closes a path where **implicitly trusted project config** could set `history.describe_command` and receive **unencrypted tracked-file diffs** on dotfiles checkpoints.
> 
> The setting is now **`global_only`**: project `.mise.toml` values are stripped at parse time and never used at runtime. Effective command resolution lives in **`history::config::describe_command`**, which considers only **`MISE_HISTORY_DESCRIBE_COMMAND`** (first) and then **trusted system/global** TOML layers—matching other history policy that ignores project files.
> 
> Watcher execution now loads the command through that helper (with warnings on load/trust failures) instead of merged **`Settings`**. Docs note the restriction; new **unit and e2e tests** cover ignored project config plus working global and env overrides.

title: fix(config): accept system in idiomatic version files
body:
A compatibility version file such as `.python-version` can use its native `system` value to select the Python already on `PATH`. Mise honored that selection but also emitted its mise-specific `@system` deprecation warning whenever the tool pathname was evaluated.

With Python idiomatic files enabled:

```toml
[settings]
idiomatic_version_file_enable_tools = ["python"]
```

A `.python-version` containing `system` now continues to select the system Python without printing the deprecation warning. Explicit `@system` requests from mise-owned configuration and command arguments still warn and point users to `MISE_DISABLE_TOOLS`.

This matches the existing compatibility exception for `.tool-versions` and addresses [Discussion #13130](https://github.com/jdx/mise/discussions/13130).

title: feat(lock): preserve aube dependency graphs
body:
Projects using the same npm tool version can resolve different transitive dependency graphs over time. `mise.lock` now records the complete portable dependency graph produced by embedded aube and replays it with a strict frozen install, so those projects receive independent graph-specific installations.

New lockfiles use revision 2. Existing revision 0 and 1 files keep their current behavior until explicitly upgraded:

```console
mise lock --upgrade
mise lock --bump npm:cowsay
```

The first command upgrades the lockfile format and resolves missing embedded-aube graphs. The second refreshes the selected tool's transitive graph even when its top-level version is unchanged. Lock generation uses an isolated temporary project in lockfile-only mode, with lifecycle scripts disabled. Frozen installs preserve aube authentication, integrity and platform filtering, security policy, lifecycle controls, and mise progress reporting.

Graph data and effective npm tool options form a deterministic installation identity. Existing version-only installs do not satisfy graph-locked requests, while `mise ls` continues to display the normal top-level version. Revision 2 locked installs reject missing graphs, integrity failures, incompatible graphs, and attempts to consume embedded-aube metadata through another npm package manager.

No aube release was required: the embedded aube APIs already provide lossless native lockfile import/export, lockfile-only resolution, and strict frozen installation.

Validation:

- `mise run test:unit` (4,030 tests)
- `mise run test:e2e e2e/backend/test_npm_aube`
- `mise run lint-fix`
- Manual revision 1 upgrade, version-only coexistence, frozen execution, inactive listing, and missing-graph checks

Legacy v0/v1 files stay unchanged until an explicit upgrade.
